title: surface-review(reagent-adapter): rethrow the first teardown failure after draining every reaction and root
description:
## Scope

Correct the stock Reagent adapter-wide teardown path, with the shared ratom-spine helper changed only where needed: `implementation/adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs` (`spine-fns`, `dispose-once!`, and the adapter map), `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs` (`dispose-frame-sub-caches!`, `dispose-active-roots-and-caches!`, and `make-ratom-spine`'s `dispose-adapter!`), plus focused stock-Reagent lifecycle tests under `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/`. Keep the one shared drain rather than forking a Reagent-only copy.

## Correctness finding

The stock Reagent adapter does the good half of best-effort teardown—attempting sibling cached-Reaction disposals and sibling root unmounts—but silently discards every failure. `dispose-frame-sub-caches!` catches each disposer throw as `_` and returns `nil`; `dispose-active-roots-and-caches!` does the same for every `unmount-op`. Consequently `rf/destroy-adapter!` reports clean success even though adapter-owned cleanup failed. This directly contradicts Spec 006's current lifecycle rule: attempt all remaining cleanup, preserve and rethrow the first failure, and attach or report later failures as secondary evidence.

This is not a request to stop at the first throw. The required invariant is **drain everything, finalize ownership, then surface the original first failure**.

## Verified evidence

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:1470-1519` documents and implements the frame sub-cache walk. Lines 1517-1518 are `(try (dispose-reaction! r) (catch :default _ nil))`; the exception is irretrievably dropped before the caller can see it.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:1521-1547` is the shared adapter drain. Lines 1542-1544 catch and drop every root-unmount failure, then lines 1545-1546 clear active-root ownership and the emitter and line 1547 returns `nil`.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:3539-3545,3657-3660` shows the stock Reagent ratom spine owns those exact cells and delegates its entire `dispose-adapter!` to that helper.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs:88-113` injects guarded stock `Reaction` construction/disposal and `reagent.dom.client/unmount` into that spine. `dispose-once!` correctly preserves a throw from stock `ratom/dispose!`; the shared outer catch is what erases it.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/adapter.cljc:230-257` already provides the right process boundary: it invokes the adapter disposer in a `try/finally`, clears the claimed generation even if cleanup throws, and naturally rethrows the adapter's exact failure. The Reagent drain prevents that tested/public mechanism from ever seeing its failures.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:2613-2624` publicly promises that `destroy-adapter!` marks the adapter disposed and then rethrows the primary cleanup failure.
- `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:320-337` requires every resource to be attempted, caches/claims to be cleared in a finally-shaped boundary, the first failure to be rethrown, and later failures to be attached or reported.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/dispose_adapter_sub_cache_walk_cljs_test.cljs:144-188` already builds the decisive stock-adapter witness: a poison cached entry throws while real reactions in the same and later frame are still disposed and both caches are cleared. Line 179 currently expects `adapter/dispose-adapter!` to return normally, so the test pins only sibling progress and accidentally codifies disappearance of the primary error.
- `implementation/core/test/re_frame/substrate/spine_dispose_cljs_test.cljs:54-76,185-209` likewise proves sibling drains but never asserts the promised post-drain rethrow. `implementation/core/test/re_frame/boot_test.clj:163-187` separately proves the core preserves exact cleanup-error identity and terminal lifecycle state when an adapter actually lets a failure escape.
- The adapter README recommends Form-3 wrappers for imperative libraries and says cleanup is mandatory (`implementation/adapters/reagent/README.md:23-42,94-101`). Silent teardown failure makes the shutdown/test-fixture boundary claim success precisely when application or host cleanup has malfunctioned.

## Impact / concrete failure scenario

A test or hot-reload fixture installs the stock Reagent adapter, creates subscriptions in multiple frames, and registers a user/framework on-dispose hook that throws. During `rf/destroy-adapter!`, the throwing Reaction is terminally marked and its error reaches `dispose-frame-sub-caches!`; other cached Reactions and roots are still attempted and ownership cells are cleared, but the original exception is dropped. The caller sees `nil`, so the fixture, reload tool, or programmer cannot distinguish clean shutdown from a failed cleanup and may continue after listeners or an imperative host resource failed to release.

The same masking exists when the injected root unmount operation throws. Whether React has already detached some host state is host-specific; the certain defect is that the adapter reports success despite the observed cleanup failure.

## Recommended bounded change

At the existing shared drain chokepoint, capture cleanup failures by **presence**, continue every Reaction and root attempt, clear each sub-cache plus `active-roots-cell` and `emitter-cell` in finally-shaped cleanup, then rethrow the first captured value unchanged. Reuse the spine's existing private `capture-none` identity sentinel (or an equally explicit sentinel), because CLJS may throw `nil` or `false`; a truthiness accumulator would recreate a silent-failure hole. Retain later failures as secondary diagnostic evidence using the project's existing diagnostic/attachment convention without replacing or wrapping the first failure.

Keep the direct zero-argument test seam compatible if it has a distinct caller contract; an optional accumulator/result between `dispose-frame-sub-caches!` and `dispose-active-roots-and-caches!` is preferable to duplicating the walk. Do not retry a consumed Reaction/root and do not add a supervisor, rollback transaction, or root registry.

## Acceptance criteria

- Update the stock-Reagent poison-entry proof so `rf/destroy-adapter!` throws the identical sentinel error **after** the real cached Reactions in the same and later frames have been disposed and every involved sub-cache is `{}`.
- Add a stock-Reagent root proof with one throwing injected `rdc/unmount` and at least one healthy sibling: every snapshot root is attempted exactly once, active-root ownership and the emitter are cleared, and the identical primary failure reaches the caller only after the drain.
- With more than one cleanup failure, the first encountered value stays the thrown primary and later failures are attached or emitted as secondary evidence; `nil`/`false` thrown values are captured by presence rather than lost.
- After either failure, `adapter/current-adapter-spec` is `nil`, `adapter/adapter-disposed?` is true, public delegation reports `:rf.error/adapter-disposed`, and a fresh `rf/init!` can install a new generation.
- Happy teardown still returns `nil`; empty frames/roots remain no-op-safe; existing stock-Reagent exactly-once Reaction disposal and client-root idempotence tests remain green.
- Non-vacuity: on the pre-fix implementation the new primary-error assertion fails because the call returns `nil`, while counters still prove sibling cleanup ran. Record that red control and then restore/apply the fix.
- Run the focused stock-Reagent CLJS adapter lifecycle lane plus the shared spine/core lifecycle tests that cover the helper and process finalization.

## Non-goals

- No change to callback registration order, the landed exactly-once marker (`rf2-rzeko`), or isolation among multiple callbacks inside one native Reagent `Reaction` disposal.
- No retry/recovery protocol for a root or Reaction whose teardown threw, no async-settlement machinery, and no new public API.
- No Reagent 1.x or React 18 compatibility work.
- No redesign of UIx, reagent-slim, Test-React, frame destruction, or application Form-3 lifecycle policy. The shared helper should remain contract-consistent for its existing callers, but this bead's regression proof and reviewed product surface are stock Reagent.

## Posture rationale

This is a small correction at an existing lifecycle chokepoint, not gold plating. Best-effort cleanup and loud failure complement each other: drain siblings for robustness, then trust the programmer with the original error so tests and tools do not claim success falsely. It preserves the minimal adapter API and removes friction from diagnosing real SPA teardown bugs.

## Duplicate and history research

Searched the complete 913-bead corpus across all statuses (title, description, notes, acceptance, and close reason) and repeated final `bd search` checks for `reagent teardown failure`, `dispose active roots`, `sub-cache cleanup error`, and `rethrow first cleanup`; no bead owns this outcome. Exact symbol/phrase searches for `dispose-active-roots-and-caches!`, `dispose-frame-sub-caches!`, `unmount ... swallow`, `cleanup failure`, `first failure`, and `secondary diagnostic` found no matching adapter-drain task. `rf2-rzeko` is closed and distinct: it made one stock Reaction's callbacks exactly-once and explicitly excluded general callback-exception isolation. `rf2-k5r9t` is closed and distinct: it added the reusable client-root lifecycle/idempotent explicit unmount, not adapter-wide failure propagation.

History confirms the defect is still live rather than already repaired: `df8aad1215` introduced per-entry swallow for the unified sub-cache walk; `1ae9c8846c` consolidated root draining with per-root swallow; `2d51830e37` then ratified terminal adapter destruction and the first-failure rule in Spec 006 while retaining both swallow catches. Later stock-Reagent disposal work (`rf2-rzeko`) changed only exactly-once behavior. Current HEAD `1ad17a77fe123bc233a88b89335dcf48196500c1` still contains both catches and the tests above still expect normal return.

## Uncertainties

- React/Reagent may have performed part or all of a particular host teardown before an unmount error escapes; do not claim rollback or infer host settlement. Surface the observed error after local ownership is finalized.
- Spec 006 intentionally permits later failures to be either attached or reported. Choose the smallest established project mechanism; do not invent a new user-facing error taxonomy solely for this fix.
- The active-root set does not promise semantic insertion order. The primary is the first failure in the actual snapshot traversal; tests should avoid depending on a different ordering contract.
notes:
PR #9201 audit reopened this exact owner: the shared Reaction/active-root drain now captures and rethrows correctly, but make-dispose-adapter! still catches and discards an exception from the separately owned singleton after-render driver root at implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:1716-1719. That root is a host-specific resource outside active-roots-cell. If its unmount is the only failure, destroy-adapter! still reports clean nil; if the shared drain already failed, the driver-root failure is not attached as secondary evidence. Both violate Spec 006 lines 320-350 and contradict the PR/README claim that every teardown failure is audible. Keep one teardown transaction across the shared drain and layered cleanup, then rethrow only after the driver-root attempt and ownership resets. Add driver-root-only and shared-primary-plus-driver-secondary witnesses; preserve primary identity and continued finalization.

close_reason:
Both halves are now on a PR. The Reagent half was PR #9201 (merged 2026-09-04): the shared drain in dispose-active-roots-and-caches! got make-teardown-failures / record-teardown-failure! / rethrow-teardown-failure!, presence-keyed on capture-none, with later failures attached to the rethrown primary via the rfAdapterTeardownSecondaryErrors string expando. The previous carrier verified that half is complete and its witnesses non-vacuous, and correctly identified that the live remnant was NOT on the Reagent path at all.

This bead's remnant — the swallowed singleton after-render DRIVER ROOT unmount in make-dispose-adapter! — is PR #9254. That is the UIx half: make-dispose-adapter! is built only by make-react-spine, which serves the UIx adapter and Hicasso's substrate; stock Reagent and reagent-slim use make-ratom-spine, whose whole dispose IS the shared drain (no warn-cache, no driver root). The ratom path is untouched by #9254.

What #9254 does: dispose-active-roots-and-caches! gains a five-arg arity that records into the CALLER's accumulator without rethrowing (the four-arg arity is behaviourally unchanged, so the ratom family keeps exactly what #9201 gave it), and make-dispose-adapter! owns one accumulator across the shared drain and its layered warn-cache / driver-root / set-tick teardown, rethrowing once after every ownership reset. Two nested accumulators would not compose: the inner rethrow attaches its secondaries to the primary and an outer one would overwrite the same expando with only its own, dropping the shared drain's evidence.

The primacy rule the note asked for is explicit in code and PR body, and it is asymmetric: a driver-root failure that is the ONLY failure becomes the PRIMARY and surfaces (a clean nil over a React root that never released is the silent hole Spec 006 MUST (2) forbids), while one arriving after the shared drain already failed becomes a SECONDARY on the primary's expando (the earlier failure names the real fault; attachment never wraps or replaces). The old bare catch got the second case right by accident and the first wrong every time.

No spec change was needed or made: Spec 006's existing "attempt every step under its own boundary, keep the first thrown value by PRESENCE, finalize ownership, and only then rethrow" already covers the driver-root unmount as a teardown step. The code was behind the spec.

Witnesses: three tests in implementation/core/test/re_frame/substrate/spine_dispose_cljs_test.cljs (driver-root-only primary; shared-primary-plus-driver-secondary; falsey throw captured by presence), each separating DRAIN from RETHROW assertions. Proven live by TWO complementary plants: restoring the bare catch gives exit 1 / 5 failures with every DRAIN assertion green and only RETHROW failing; removing the guard so the throw escapes the finally gives exit 1 / 9 failures with test 1's DRAIN failing and its RETHROW green. The halves fail for different reasons in both directions.

Gates: npm run test:cljs exit 0, 11223 tests / 56725 assertions, 0 failures (+3 tests / +17 assertions over the 11220 / 56708 baseline, matching the new deftests exactly), re-run on the final rebased base. npm run build:hicasso-release exit 0, 0 warnings — the :advanced / :infer-externs :auto gate for the .unmount interop, which shadow-cljs.edn records as the only Closure-optimised compile these namespaces get and whose comment names core's spine.cljs. npm run test:hicasso-compile exit 0, 11 namespaces, zero warnings. npm run test:browser does NOT cover these tests and was not claimed: :browser-test binds :ns-regexp ".*-dom-cljs-test$" and this namespace ends -cljs-test; no real React root is needed, since the spine only invokes .unmount on whatever occupies the cell.

title: TRUNK RED: the new require-alias ratchet fails on origin/main itself — two surfaces sit BELOW their baseline floor, and every open PR is blocked
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-04 09:4x AUSEST by the mayor, ON THE MAYOR CHECKOUT AT origin/main WITH NO PR INVOLVED, captured exit 1:

  python scripts/check_require_alias_dialect.py --verbose
  -> 2 surface(s) now BELOW their baseline floor - lower the floor in
     scripts/require-alias-baseline.edn (--write-baseline) so the ratchet holds
     the ground that was won:
       implementation/flows: 155 violation(s), floor 156
       implementation/ssr:   399 violation(s), floor 402

HOW IT GOT HERE. PR #9135 (rf2-ydpr, worker/ratchet-a) merged at a48586caf5 and armed the ratchet as a NEW REQUIRED lint.yml job. Its baseline was captured before two other sweeps landed, so flows is one below its floor and ssr is three below. The ratchet is deliberately two-sided - it refuses when you drop below the floor as well as when you rise above it, so that ground won is held - and that second side is what is firing.

BLAST RADIUS: EVERY OPEN PR. The job is required, and lint.yml's aggregator 'Lint required' consumes it (its log reads 'needs results: success, success, success, skipped, success, failure'), so both go red on any branch whose content is irrelevant to require aliases. Confirmed on PR #9139, a documentation-only change: rebased onto the new trunk it came back 87 checks with exactly these 2 failures. No merge can pass clause 2 of the merge criterion until this is fixed.

THE FIX is small and the tool names it: lower the two floors. scripts/check_require_alias_dialect.py --write-baseline is the affordance the error message points at.

BUT DO NOT RUN --write-baseline BLIND, AND THIS IS THE WHOLE CARE OF THE BEAD. A ratchet floor may only ever go DOWN. If --write-baseline rewrites every row from the current tree, it will also RAISE any row whose count has risen since the baseline was captured - which silently grants permission for a regression that has already happened and destroys the ratchet's purpose on that surface. Read what --write-baseline actually does at source BEFORE running it. Diff the file it produces against HEAD and confirm every changed row moved DOWNWARD; if any row would rise, do not accept that hunk - lower the two failing rows only, and report the rising row as a separate finding with its numbers.

ALSO CHECK, DO NOT ASSUME: whether more than two rows are stale in the downward direction. The tool reported two because two crossed their floor; a row sitting well below its floor without crossing reports nothing at all. Compare every row against a fresh scan and say which rows are slack and by how much.

RELATED, AND NOT YOURS: rf2-ttss covers implementation/http's row, which reads 272 while PR #9142 (unmerged) takes that surface to 0. Do NOT touch the http row - #9142 has not landed, so 272 is still correct at tip, and lowering it now would red the ratchet a second way. Leave it and let rf2-ttss handle it after #9142 merges.

GATE: scripts/check_require_alias_dialect.py itself, captured exit 0 after the fix, plus a planted non-canonical alias in one of the two repaired surfaces proving the tightened floor still bites (a green after tightening proves nothing on its own). Its --self-test if it has one. Read .github/workflows/lint.yml for how CI invokes it and match that invocation.

URGENT: this blocks the whole merge queue.
close_reason: PR #9144 lowers the two crossed floors (implementation/flows 156->155, implementation/ssr 402->399) in scripts/require-alias-baseline.edn. --write-baseline was diffed rather than accepted blind: it changes only those two rows plus :min-edges 9692->9691, and NO surface row would have risen. :min-edges left at 9692 because for that key lower is looser (blind-scanner floor, total<min-edges), not tighter. A --report census confirms no other row is slack — after the change every surface sits exactly at its floor, none under, none OVER. implementation/http untouched at 272 (rf2-ttss owns it post-#9142). Gate: --self-test exit 0 (40 passed) and --verbose exit 0 on the final rebased base; planted non-canonical alias in implementation/flows took it to exit 1 naming 'implementation/flows: 156 violation(s), floor 155', proving the tightened floor still bites.

title: bug(machines-viz): stale ELK settle can overwrite the current topology
description:
## Scope

Correct the `MachineChart` async layout-settle boundary in `tools/machines-viz`. The fix covers every ELK pass owned by one mounted Form-2 chart instance (initial layout and measured relayout) when a newer `:definition`, direction, layout option, density, Context-band row count, or adaptive-mode key supersedes it. Add one deterministic CLJS regression at the existing component seam. No Xray API or selection-flow redesign is required.

## Correctness finding

`MachineChart` starts a new asynchronous ELK pass whenever `this-key` differs from `@layout-key`, but every pass callback later commits its result unconditionally. The callback closes over its own `this-key`; it never checks that this key is still the active `@layout-key` before `reset!`-ing `layout-state` and scheduling `fitView`.

A slow result for topology A can therefore resolve after topology B has already become current and settled, overwrite B's positions, routed edge points, edge-label positions, or layout-error state, and schedule a fit for A. The next render still projects definition B, but against A's layout maps. B node ids absent from A's result fall back to `{x 0, y 0}`, so the visible current machine can collapse at the origin or carry routes from another topology until another real layout invalidation happens. This is a wrong-visualization failure, not a cosmetic timing detail: a developer can be shown topology B with geometry produced for A.

## Evidence

- `tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/chart.cljs:1302-1303` derives the active layout key, and lines 1420-1427 update `layout-key` and launch a new pass while an older Promise may still be pending.
- `chart.cljs:1310-1348` closes each pass over `this-key`, but lines 1331-1348 accept every non-nil callback result, unconditionally `reset! layout-state`, update `:fit-key`, and schedule `fitView`; there is no `= this-key @layout-key` current-generation check.
- `chart.cljs:671-686` maps every ELK Promise resolution or rejection directly to `done-fn`; it provides neither cancellation nor latest-request arbitration.
- `tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/chart/projection.cljc:1384` and lines 1742-1743 default missing position ids to `{x 0, y 0}`. Lines 1709-1711 read routed edge/label maps by the current edge ids. Thus an A result committed while B is current produces observable corrupt B geometry rather than being harmless unused data.
- The public contract explicitly supports changed definitions and keeps previous positions in flight: `tools/machines-viz/spec/API.md:1403-1425`. A stale completion is therefore reachable through normal API use, not an unsupported prop sequence.
- Xray's Static Machines detail keeps the chart at the same unkeyed component position while selection changes: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/static/machines/definition_detail.cljs:213-283` passes the newly selected definition through `topology.cljs:97-133` and `panels/machine_canvas.cljs:329-373` to one `MachineChart` component type. React/Reagent preserves the Form-2 instance and its pending callbacks across that prop change.
- The test suite already models exactly this reuse. `tools/machines-viz/test/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/chart/parse_cache_cljs_test.cljs:2-24` says repeated calls to one Form-2 render function simulate a new definition, but its harness replaces `compute-layout!` with a no-op (`:55-117`), so it cannot exercise completion order. `auto_fit_view_cljs_test.cljs:263-303` mirrors only the synchronous fit-key predicate. No test captures two real layout callbacks and resolves them in reverse order.

## Failure scenario / invariant

Deterministic sequence:

1. Render definition A; capture its pending layout callback `done-A`.
2. Re-render the same `MachineChart` instance with definition B; `@layout-key` becomes B and capture `done-B`.
3. Invoke `done-B` first with B-only sentinel positions/routes. B correctly becomes visible.
4. Invoke `done-A` second with A-only sentinel positions/routes. Current code overwrites `layout-state` with A and schedules an A-key fit even though the current props and `@layout-key` are B.
5. Re-render B. Its nodes read absent positions and fall back to the origin; its current routed geometry has been lost.

Invariant: only the completion whose closed layout key equals the chart instance's current layout key may mutate visible layout state or trigger post-settle fitting. Completion order must not change the final visualization. This applies equally to a stale first pass and a stale measured second pass.

## Steps to Reproduce

Use the existing Node-runnable Form-2 test seam: create one `MachineChart` inner render function, replace `compute-layout!` with a capturing stub, render definition A and then definition B before completing either callback, resolve B's callback with B-only sentinel geometry, then resolve A's callback with A-only geometry. Render B once more and inspect the positions passed to `projection/xyflow-graph` (and the `invoke-fit-view!` spy). On current main, the final projection receives A's stale layout map and the stale callback can schedule another fit; B-only node ids therefore use the origin fallback.

## Recommended minimal fix

At the component-owned callback in `run-layout!`, gate all visible settle side effects on `(= this-key @layout-key)`. An obsolete result should simply be ignored: do not replace `layout-state`, do not update `fit-state`, and do not schedule `fitView`. Keep the current key construction, previous-layout-during-flight behavior, parse/projection caches, ELK instance, and error-result shape unchanged.

Do not add Promise cancellation machinery or serialize all layouts. A one-generation equality check at the single commit boundary is sufficient and also covers measured relayout callbacks because they close over the same `this-key`.

## Non-goals

- Changing which props invalidate layout or changing the layout-key contents.
- Debouncing machine selection, serializing ELK work, terminating/recreating the shared ELK worker, or adding cancellation tokens throughout `compute-layout!`.
- Remounting `MachineChart` per machine id as a workaround; preserving the Form-2 instance and its caches is intentional.
- Changing ELK algorithms, visual styling, topology projection, auto-fit timing, Xray selection UX, or public component props.
- Broad async hardening unrelated to committing the latest layout result.

## Related / duplicate search

All-status title, description, and notes searches for `stale ELK`, `ELK Promise`, `out-of-order layout`, `async layout`, `layout settle`, `stale layout`, `focused-machine change`, `definition switch`, and `layout result` returned no matching bead. A broader all-status `ELK` search found only open `rf2-rc0yh` (skill setup SPA) and `rf2-zq34m` (template SPA), neither about layout arbitration. Open `rf2-sxw06` is the distinct Mermaid-copy workflow. Historical source references `rf2-s5kyp` (focused-machine auto-fit) and `rf2-jl72i` (parse cache); those changes create/test the normal prop-change path but do not arbitrate reversed Promise completion.
acceptance_criteria:
- Add a Node-runnable CLJS component regression that creates one real `MachineChart` Form-2 render function, renders distinct definitions A then B without completing A, and captures the two `compute-layout!` callbacks.
- The regression invokes `done-B` with B-only sentinel positions, routed edge points, and edge-label positions, then invokes `done-A` with different A-only sentinels. A subsequent B render must still project the exact B sentinels and must not expose A's layout-error or geometry.
- Non-vacuity/control: assert exactly two callbacks were captured and explicitly invoked; assert `done-B` visibly changes the projected positions from the pre-layout fallback before `done-A` is invoked. With the current-generation guard locally removed/inverted, the final B assertion must fail.
- A stale completion must not update `:fit-key` or call `invoke-fit-view!`; the current B completion still schedules exactly the existing one post-settle fit when an instance is available.

title: surface-review(conformance-security): strip standardized oncommand from SSR HTML
description:
## Scope Close the current SSR static-markup handler-filter gap for the standardized lowercase `oncommand` attribute in `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/html_helpers.cljc`, with focused coverage in the existing SSR escaping security suite. Keep the existing conservative attribute-name grammar and benign non-handler `on*` behavior. ## Correctness finding `attr-string` strips camelCase/kebab `on*` props structurally and lowercase handler names through a hand-maintained allowlist. The allowlist omits `oncommand`. Because `oncommand` is all lowercase, it misses the structural regex too, passes the attribute-name grammar, and is emitted verbatim into SSR HTML even though current browsers install it as executable inline JavaScript. This violates the documented invariant that server-rendered strings never carry live event-handler attributes. It is not speculative hardening: the current WHATWG HTML Standard names `oncommand` as an event handler content attribute, and the repository's installed Chromium executes it. ## Evidence - `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/html_helpers.cljc:353-413`: the structural matcher catches only `on` plus uppercase or hyphen; lowercase names depend on `event-handler-allowlist`. - `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/html_helpers.cljc:369-397`: the lowercase allowlist contains nearby standardized handlers but no `oncommand`. - `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/html_helpers.cljc:591-621`: a prop not stripped is grammar-validated and serialized as an HTML attribute. - `implementation/security/test/re_frame/security/ssr_escaping_security_cljs_test.cljc:22-174`: generated and named handler corpora do not include `oncommand`; the benign controls explicitly preserve `online`/`once`/`only`/`on`. - Current JVM probe: `(h/attr-string {:oncommand :pwned})` returns `" oncommand=\":pwned\""`. - Current bundled Playwright/Chromium probe: after loading `
`, dispatching `new Event('command')` reports `{"pwned":1,"handler":"function"}`. - WHATWG HTML Standard, GlobalEventHandlers/content-attribute list: `oncommand` is an event handler content attribute: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#global-attributes ## Failure scenario/invariant An SSR app spreads a user-controlled custom-attribute map into hiccup, the exact threat model documented beside `attr-string`. An attacker supplies the grammar-valid key `oncommand` and JavaScript as its value. Server rendering emits the inline handler. When a `command` event reaches that element, the browser executes the attacker's code before or independently of hydration. Invariant: every browser-recognized event-handler prop covered by the shipped SSR contract is absent from static markup in every HTML-equivalent casing, while benign non-handler names such as `online` continue to serialize. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. From `implementation/ssr`, require `re-frame.ssr.html-helpers` and evaluate `(h/attr-string {:oncommand :pwned})`; observe that the returned HTML contains `oncommand` instead of the empty string. 2. Load `
` in the repository's bundled Playwright Chromium. 3. Set `globalThis.pwned=0`, dispatch `new Event('command')` on `#x`, and observe `globalThis.pwned` becomes `1` and `typeof x.oncommand` is `"function"`. ## Recommended minimal fix Add the standardized lowercase `oncommand` spelling to the existing event-handler allowlist and to the named/generated security corpus. Keep the current two-layer matcher and grammar; do not broaden it to all lowercase `on*` names, because the suite deliberately preserves benign attributes such as `online`, `once`, and `only`. ## Acceptance Criteria 1. A focused CLJ+CLJS security regression passes `:oncommand`, `:ONCOMMAND`, and a mixed-case spelling with a string JavaScript payload through `h/attr-string`; each yields the empty string and contains neither the handler name nor payload. 2. An end-to-end `emit/emit-element` case renders a benign sibling attribute/text while omitting `oncommand` and its payload entirely. 3. Non-vacuity: the regression is demonstrated red on the current implementation by asserting the current exact survivor (`oncommand` is present in `attr-string`/emitted HTML); the same payload under a benign attribute is shown serializable so fixture/value omission cannot satisfy the test. 4. The existing `online`/`once`/`only`/`on` non-handler controls remain green, proving the fix did not replace the curated rule with an over-broad lowercase `on*` drop. 5. The focused SSR escaping security namespace passes on both JVM and the shared CLJS Node/security lanes. ## Non-goals - No CSP, sanitizer, DOMPurify, hydration, or renderer redesign. - No blanket rejection of programmer-authored inline script/style content. - No broad `on[a-z]` matcher that drops benign non-handler attributes. - No changes to client event binding or unrelated attribute/value escaping. ## Related/duplicate search Searched all bead statuses by `oncommand`, SSR event handler, event-handler, attribute allowlist, static markup, XSS, HTML, escaping, `ssr-invalid-attribute-name`, `html-helpers`, and description/notes matches. No bead owns this gap. The only in-progress bead is unrelated prose cleanup. `rf2-mocn3` is a distinct open SSR Form-2 arity bug; `rf2-qxg24` is a distinct test-tier changed-surface classifier task.
notes: TRIAGE 2026-08-31 19:38:35 AUSEST (read-only agent at 35402e4322): HOLDS. event-handler-allowlist (html_helpers.cljc :370-399) contains no oncommand (it does carry onbeforetoggle/onpagereveal/onpageswap, so the omission is a curation gap, not policy); the structural regex :353-354 requires uppercase-or-hyphen after on, so all-lowercase oncommand rides through; grammar-valid unstripped names serialize (:591-621 region); grep confirms zero oncommand occurrences under implementation/ssr + implementation/security at tip; WHATWG lists oncommand as an event handler content attribute. One-word allowlist add + security-corpus rows. SURFACES: implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/html_helpers.cljc + implementation/security/test/re_frame/security/ssr_escaping_security_cljs_test.cljc; no hot-zone. COLLISIONS: none live or sibling. GATES: clojure -M:test from implementation/security and from implementation/ssr (JVM, light); npm run test:security --prefix implementation [HEAVY - shadow node compile lane]. AMBIGUITY: none - the bead correctly forbids a broad lowercase on* matcher (keeps online/once/only alive). SHAPE: solo - smallest and most security-relevant of the eleven; dispatch first.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8820: oncommand added to event-handler-allowlist in html_helpers.cljc; security corpus (generated canonical-handlers + named hostile-handler-keys) and two focused regressions added (attr-string all-casings strip + emit-element end-to-end, with non-vacuity benign-payload and online/once/only/on controls). Control demonstrated red on unfixed impl: 13 JVM failures naming oncommand incl exact survivor <div oncommand=...>; restore blob-hash-verified. Gates on final rebased base: JVM security 94/723 0F, JVM ssr 599/2925 0F, CLJS node security lane 95/730 0F, all exit 0.

title: surface-review(reagent-adapter): make stock Reaction disposal exactly-once across shutdown and unmount
description:
## Scope

The stock Reagent adapter's derived-value disposal path: `implementation/adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs`, the ratom-family disposer assembly in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs`, and focused stock-adapter tests under `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/**`. Touch the shared spine only as needed to give one adapter generation one coherent disposal owner.

## Correctness finding

The adapter promises that a derived value's disposal is idempotent and re-entrant safe, but both of its stock-Reagent paths delegate directly to Reagent 2.0.1's `reagent.ratom/dispose!`. That implementation has no disposed guard and does not clear either callback holder before invoking it. A second disposal re-fires every `add-on-dispose!` callback; a callback that defensively re-enters `re-frame.interop/dispose!` on the same Reaction re-enters the same callback array and can recurse until stack overflow.

## Evidence

- `implementation/adapters/reagent/deps.edn` pins `reagent/reagent` 2.0.1.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs:27,35,77,105` injects raw `ratom/make-reaction` and raw `ratom/dispose!` into both `make-ratom-spine` (claimed-generation cleanup) and `make-ratom-adapter` (the routed public disposal hook).
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:3313-3323` (`make-ratom-dispose-dispatch`) adds no exactly-once guard; separate instances are built at `:3400` and `:3635`.
- Reading `reagent-2.0.1.jar!/reagent/ratom.cljs:480-500` shows `Reaction.dispose!` nils `watching` and state, but leaves `on-dispose` and `on-dispose-arr` intact and invokes them on every call. The reading command extracted the source entry from the locally resolved Maven jar; no repository file was modified.
- `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:1062` says Reagent/reagent-slim derived disposal fires callbacks exactly once, makes a second dispose a no-op, and is re-entrant safe.
- The in-tree slim Reaction already implements the required pattern at `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/ratom.cljs:419-448`, with focused repeat/re-entry proofs at `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/reagent2/ratom_cljs_test.cljs:207-245`; stock-adapter tests only prove a single disposal (`implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/dispose_adapter_sub_cache_walk_cljs_test.cljs:86-220`).
- `git show d1cd3ecee3` confirms the earlier exact-once repair covered the shared React spine and reagent-slim Reaction, but not the external stock Reaction now used here.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install `re-frame.adapter.reagent/adapter`, create a source through its `:make-state-container`, and create a real Reaction through its `:make-derived-value`.
2. Register an `add-on-dispose!` callback through `re-frame.interop` that increments a counter and, on its first invocation, calls `re-frame.interop/dispose!` on the same callback argument.
3. Call `re-frame.interop/dispose!` on the Reaction. The callback runs twice (or recurses without a conditional guard) because the routed hook reaches the unchanged callback array in stock `ratom/dispose!`.
4. A second deterministic form is to attach an outward watch, explicitly dispose the Reaction, then remove the final watch. Stock `Reaction.-remove-watch` auto-disposes it again and re-fires the same callbacks.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A mounted Reagent owner watches an adapter-created subscription Reaction. Frame or adapter cleanup explicitly disposes that Reaction, firing its cache/input/user cleanup callbacks, while the Reaction's outward `watches` map can still contain the mounted owner. When the owner later unmounts, stock Reagent removes the last outward watch and its `Reaction.-remove-watch` automatically calls `dispose!` again. Because the callback holders survived the first call, the same cleanup set fires twice, which can double-release input refs or repeat user teardown. More directly, an on-dispose callback that re-disposes the same Reaction through the adapter recursively re-fires itself. The invariant is one callback execution and one source-release pass per adapter-created derived value, regardless of whether explicit adapter cleanup or host auto-disposal arrives first.

## Recommended minimal fix

Give adapter-created stock Reagent Reactions an adapter-owned exactly-once guard. Mark the Reaction before user/framework callbacks run, also mark it when stock Reagent auto-disposes it, and make both the claimed-generation disposer and routed `:adapter/dispose!` consult the same generation-local guard. Keep the native Reaction object and its batching behavior; do not fork Reagent or replace it with a wrapper container. The construction marker must be installed before cache/user callbacks so re-entry from any later callback sees the terminal mark.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A focused stock-adapter test builds a real derived value through `(:make-derived-value reagent-adapter/adapter)`, registers ordered disposal callbacks through the actual routed `re-frame.interop/add-on-dispose!` path, disposes twice through `re-frame.interop/dispose!`, and observes each callback exactly once in registration order.
- A callback conditionally re-enters `re-frame.interop/dispose!` on the same real Reaction; the call returns without recursion, that callback fires once, and a later sibling callback still fires once.
- A host/adapter crossover proof attaches then removes the final stock-Reagent watch (exercising `Reaction.-remove-watch` auto-disposal) and also drives adapter disposal in the opposite order; both orderings leave the callback count at one and release the source wire once.
- The ordinary one-shot path still disposes the Reaction, removes its source watches, and preserves existing sub-cache teardown behavior.
- Non-vacuity: temporarily bypassing the adapter guard (routing the same proofs to raw `ratom/dispose!`) makes the repeat/re-entry assertion red under the pinned Reagent 2.0.1; record that mutation/control command and its nonzero result, then restore the fix.
- Run the focused stock-Reagent CLJS lane containing the new tests and the existing adapter disposal/subscription lifecycle tests; both pass.

## Non-goals

- No fork or patch of the external Reagent artefact, Reagent 1.x/React 18 compatibility, or change to Reaction batching/reactivity semantics.
- No changes to reagent-slim's already guarded Reaction disposal.
- No redesign of the public subscription API, ref-count model, or general callback-exception isolation.
- No reusable client-root API or render unmount-thunk work; that is owned by `rf2-k5r9t`.

## Related / duplicate search

Searched all bead statuses by title and description for `dispose`, `dispose!`, `idempotent`, `re-entrant`, `second dispose`, `double dispose`, `ratom/dispose!`, `Reagent Reaction`, `stock Reagent`, and the adapter path/symbols. No open, in-progress, or closed bead owns stock-Reagent Reaction exact-once disposal. No in-progress bead matched this surface. `rf2-k5r9t` is related but distinct: it owns a reusable adapter client-root lifecycle and the returned root unmount thunk's idempotence, not reactive derived-value callbacks. Historical commit `d1cd3ecee3` / source tag `rf2-1bzlai` is relevant prior art for slim/shared-spine implementations, not an extant bead or a repair of this stock adapter path.
notes: TRIAGE 2026-08-31 19:38:35 AUSEST (read-only agent at 35402e4322): HOLDS. adapter/reagent.cljs injects raw ratom/make-reaction + ratom/dispose! at :27,:35,:77,:105; spine make-ratom-dispose-dispatch :3313-3324 adds no exactly-once guard (instances built at :3400 and :3635); read the pinned reagent-2.0.1 jar (local .m2) reagent/ratom.cljs Reaction dispose! - it nils watching/state/auto-run but leaves on-dispose and on-dispose-arr INTACT and fires them on every call, so a second dispose refires every callback and a re-entrant dispose recurses, exactly as claimed; spec/006 :1062 mandates exactly-once, idempotent, re-entrant-safe disposal for Reagent/reagent-slim; slim reagent2/ratom.cljs already implements the guard pattern with repeat/re-entry proofs - prior art. SURFACES: implementation/adapters/reagent/** + implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs + adapter tests; no hot-zone. COLLISIONS: live websocket-pattern holds a reagent adapter websocket test - different file in the same test tree, keep new test files apart; live interceptor-coords is core interceptor_registry.cljc, disjoint from spine.cljs. GATES: npm run test:cljs --prefix implementation [HEAVY - shadow compile] covering the new + existing adapter disposal suites. AMBIGUITY: guard placement (adapter-owned marker on the Reaction vs spine-level) - follow the bead: adapter-owned generation-local guard consulted by both the claimed-generation disposer and routed :adapter/dispose!, spine change minimal. SHAPE: cluster with rf2-08hx1 (adapter pair, one worker, one heavy lane).
close_reason: Shipped PR #8831 (ready for review): exactly-once, re-entrant-safe disposal for stock-adapter Reactions. Adapter-owned guard in re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs only — zero spine.cljs changes, no hot-zone touch, reagent-slim untouched. install-dispose-guard! arms every adapter-created Reaction (spine :make-reaction and routed :adapter/make-reaction) at construction with a FIRST-registered add-on-dispose! marker that stamps a string-keyed disposed mark and nils both callback holders (stock dispose! iterates a captured local, so the first firing completes in registration order; any later dispose! incl. stock-internal auto-dispose finds empty holders); both the claimed-generation disposer and routed :adapter/dispose! delegate through dispose-once!, which consults the same mark. New suite re-frame.adapter-reaction-dispose-exactly-once-cljs-test: 6 deftests/21 assertions via the actual public paths — double interop/dispose!, conditional re-entrant dispose, host/adapter crossover both orders via add-watch/remove-watch (incl. source-wire release), shutdown+unmount interleave through dispose-adapter! both orders. Gates (captured exits): node-test compile 0 warnings exit 0; focused suite exit 0; existing lifecycle suites (dispose-adapter-sub-cache-walk, sub-dispose-view, standard-epochs-views-subs-lifecycle) 14/111 exit 0; full test:cljs equivalent post-rebase onto ead1d8529c: 11111 tests/54506 assertions, 0 failures, exit 0. Control: one-line #_ on the marker registration routed proofs to raw ratom/dispose! -> focused suite exit 1, 5/6 red (re-fired callbacks, (not (= 1 2))); the one green (unmount-then-shutdown) pins pre-existing cache eviction, expected. Restore verified by blob hash 4d4e6db6132daa901b911eda2e58d9a2cfff10e6 = committed object; re-run exit 0.

title: Incomplete Routing egress correction: declared sensitive current-route params still render raw
description:
PR #10089 (f7effa1ac20acffb26ee471d38be2adbc273cdf7) correctly fixes declared-sensitive current-route query rendering, but the same explicit classification contract remains incomplete for CURRENT ROUTE params. At the audited merge and current origin/main, panels/routing.cljs:689-733 only projects :query; :params is forwarded unchanged from the observed host runtime-db and printed at :248-249 with (pr-str (or params {})). A route declaring :sensitive [[:params :token]] therefore displays that activated token raw in rf-xray-routing-current-params under the normal local-redacted display. The implementation worker identified this residue in rf2-8nyi2 notes, without a separately trackable correction.

The supported route declaration covers the {:query ... :params ...} projection (implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/classification.cljc:30-47), lowered to the current runtime slice at activation. routing/sub_egress.cljc already seeds :rf.route/params, and the newly landed local-render-route-sub-value already accepts that sub. Project the current params through this existing seam with the actual observed frame; preserve ordinary/unclassified params and existing no-route/empty behavior. No new API or blanket scrubbing is needed. This finding concerns explicit declarations on CURRENT ROUTE params, not undeclared values, operator-entered simulator URLs, fragment text, or the separate historical-navigation policy.

Add a real route activation/render-path regression using a sensitive path parameter and an unclassified sibling: the params span must show the sentinel instead of the declared value while retaining the sibling. Include an undeclared control and exercise observed-frame isolation. Evidence for this audit is the merged/current production source chain and existing classification contract; no independent mounted-browser or node-suite run claimed.
notes:
---

## MERGED: MAYOR'S MERGE VERIFICATION (2026-09-20)

PR **#10099** merged by rebase at head `592203f20f2b52006a5d6fe8b6ffd04105aafd27`; merge commit
`caf44fe68e`. Trunk `60f3c4c7a8` -> `caf44fe68e`; `HEAD` == `origin/main` after the fast-forward, two
separate reads. **4 files, 708 insertions / 43 deletions**, including a new test namespace
`routing_params_egress_cljs_test.cljs`.

**Five clauses:** rollup **88** at band; failed **0**, pending **0**, case-folded and status-gated; **4**
runs (portability, docs, lint, tests) all `completed`/`success`, **0** not completed, oid from
`--json headRefOid` at the full 40 characters; matrix control self-derived, `LAST` = `b9220b6dc2`,
**1** then **0**. **Direction test:** merge-base `d672b7f4ce`, trunk-side **5**, branch-side **4**,
overlap **0**, `merge-tree --write-tree` exit **0**.

**Not reopened**; appended.

**THE MAYOR'S FLAGGED PREMISE WAS RESOLVED — AND IT INVERTS. THIS IS THE FINDING OF THE RUN.**

The brief flagged the item's assumption that a route may declare `:sensitive [[:params :token]]`, noted
that `classification.cljc`'s worked example declares `:sensitive` on QUERY paths and `:large` on the
PARAMS path, and required the worker to verify in the validation and lowering code rather than the
docstring — saying that if it were rejected at registration, the item's shape changed.

**It IS supported, measured in the code and not the docstring:** `normalize-axis-paths` never inspects a
path's head, and `apply-route-classification` re-roots every path identically. Measured on the JVM,
`{:sensitive [[:params :token] [:query :token]]}` lowers to BOTH
`[:rf.runtime/routing :current :params :token]` and `[… :query :token]`, each `#{{:source :route}}`.

**THE SURPRISE IS THE DIRECTION, AND IT REVERSES THE RISK THE ITEM DESCRIBED.** **Params are the axis
that CANNOT fail open.** `unpromoted-query-keys` filters `(= :query (first p))` **because path captures
are always keyword-keyed** (`match.cljc:664`), whereas **an unpromoted QUERY key stays a string and
ships raw silently.** So the panel had been projecting the WEAKER axis and leaving the RELIABLE one
raw — the opposite of the reading a careful person takes from the item, which frames params as the

## The dispatch's flagged premise, RESOLVED: :sensitive on a :params path IS supported

The brief flagged this as the single most likely way the item was not what it appeared,
because spec/012's worked example declares :sensitive on QUERY paths and :large on the
PARAMS path — so ":sensitive on a :params path" is a reasonable reading of the
projection-relative rule and is NOT something the example demonstrates. Verified in the
VALIDATION and LOWERING code rather than the docstring:

- `normalize-axis-paths` (classification.cljc) validates each path with
  `rf.path/normalize-concrete` and NEVER inspects its head. There is no :query/:params
  discrimination anywhere in validation; any concrete EDN path is accepted.
- `apply-route-classification` re-roots EVERY path identically:
  `(mapv #(into [:rf.runtime/routing :current] %) ...)`.
- Measured executably on the JVM (new row
  `route-classification-accepts-and-lowers-a-params-path`):
  `{:sensitive [[:params :token] [:query :token]]}` lowers to
  `{[:rf.runtime/routing :current :params :token] #{{:source :route}},
    [:rf.runtime/routing :current :query :token] #{{:source :route}}}`.

PARAMS are in fact the axis that CANNOT fail open, which inverts the expected weakness.
`unpromoted-query-keys` filters on `(= :query (first p))`, and the classification ns says
why: "PARAMS are immune (path captures are always keyword-keyed, match.cljc), so the
advisory is query-axis-only" — confirmed at `re-frame.routing.match:664`,
`[(keyword param-name) value]`. An unpromoted query key stays a STRING and silently fails
open; a path capture never can. So the panel was projecting the WEAKER of the two axes and
leaving the reliable one raw. Pinned by a row whose route declares no :params schema at all.

`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/local_render.cljc` gains
`local-render-route-slice`, composing the existing route-sub arm over the two
classification-covered keys, each named by its routing-owned sub (:rf.route/query /
:rf.route/params) so the seed re-roots the walk to that key's storage position.
`current-route-slice-value` (panels/routing.cljs) delegates to it.

Deliberately NOT `:rf/route` whole-slice seeding, which reads as the tidier call: it would
also walk :fragment, :transition, :error and :nav-token, which the classification contract
does not cover and about which `re-frame.routing.sub-egress` explicitly makes no
sensitivity claim. Projecting the two covered keys individually keeps the blast radius
equal to the contract. Only a key the router actually WROTE is touched, so an absent key
stays absent rather than becoming a sentinel a section would then render.

The arm is .cljc, so the JVM lane grades the algebra and the route lowering; the
view-level regression is node-lane because the panel is .cljs.

title: Incomplete Graph preview budget: nested strings still serialize in full
description: PR #10016 bounds top-level strings and collection breadth/depth in derivation_graph_helpers/bounded-pr-str, but its claim to avoid full serialization for an 80-character Graph preview is incomplete for ordinary nested values. The string truncation only runs when the root v is a string; a sub returning {:body large-string} sends the complete nested string to pr-str because print-length/print-level do not bound string contents. Still present on origin/main. Reproduced by evaluating the exact merged preview definitions with Babashka and observing pr-str output length: a 500,000-character root string serialized 82 characters; {:body same-string} serialized 500,010. Both previews contain 81 characters. Probe exit 0, correct gate root audit-sep20-monitor, artifacts ai/gate-bounded-audit-sep20-monitor-1.log/.exit. This is a source-isolated JVM-compatible probe, not a browser/full-suite run. The Graph refresh repeats this cost for value-bearing fields, so large response bodies nested in normal maps retain the allocation/work the PR is meant to remove. Required correction: bound the actual preview serialization for nested values as well as scalar roots, preserving useful prefix/type/known-size behavior. Prefer a small existing bounded-print mechanism; no new API, policy, preference or broad graph redesign is requested. Add a discriminating nested-string regression that observes work/intermediate output rather than only the final 81-character string. No exact open finding exists.

description:
# Senior review: xray-boot-embedding

Reviewer persona: senior ClojureScript developer who has embedded dev tooling in production apps for years; allergic to boot-order bugs, global mutable state, and tools that leak into release builds.
Tree: xray-review-sep17 worktree, trunk 9555881fe3
Scope read: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/{mount.cljs, install.cljs, preload.cljs, drop_in.cljc, core.cljs, registry.cljs, substrate.cljs, egress.cljs, config.cljc, defaults.cljs, local_storage.cljs, test_support.cljs, open_in_editor.cljs, self_noise.cljc, trace_collector.cljs, epoch.cljs} (8,145 lines), tools/xray/deps.edn, tools/xray/README.md
Owning specs consulted end to end: tools/xray/spec/008-Embedding-Contract.md, 011-Launch-Modes.md, 013-Trace-Consumer.md, 015-Configuration.md, API.md; spec/Tool-Pair.md; spec/009-Instrumentation.md sections 51-60, 147-172, 631-760, 808-1140, 2828-2966, 3028-3078 (listener API, op-type vocabulary, frameless/B3, privacy, retroactive scrub, per-frame rings).

Totals: 7 findings -- 1 high, 3 medium, 3 low. 5 of 7 owning chapters DRIFT.

## Findings, ranked

### 1. Preload boot order inverts the documented settings precedence and strands `:keybinding-enabled?` -- HIGH, correctness + spec-drift, SIZE M, CONFIRMED

WHERE: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/preload.cljs:94-133 (load-time block: `config/load-settings-from-storage!` :98, `keybinding/attach!` :115, `settings-effects/apply-all!` :116); config.cljc:1834-1841 (`configure!` `:rf.xray/settings` branch); config.cljc:1457-1487 (`load-settings-from-storage!`); mount.cljs:1304-1307; core.cljs:145-237 (`init!`).

WHAT: A shadow-cljs `:preloads` namespace's top-level forms run before the app entry namespace, so any host `configure!` written in app code runs AFTER the preload block. Three consequences:
- (a) `configure!` with `:rf.xray/settings` does `(reset! settings (merge-known-sections settings-opt))` (config.cljc:1837-1838). The persisted user Settings that `load-settings-from-storage!` merged in at :1483 are dropped from the live atom on every boot; storage itself is untouched (:1840 writes only when empty), so the next boot repeats the clobber. The documented order is `defaults < configure! < persisted` (config.cljc:1459-1461; 015 "configure! vs init! vs persisted Settings"); the runtime delivers the inverse whenever a host uses this key.
- (b) `keybinding/attach!` reads `config/keybinding-attach-enabled?` at attach time (keybinding.cljs:507-528) and the preload attaches at load time (:115). 015:477-480 says hosts MUST set the flag "BEFORE the Xray preload runs (the preload calls `keybinding/attach!` at adapter-ready time)". Both halves are wrong: attachment is load-time, and ordinary app code cannot run before a preload. `(configure! {:keybinding-enabled? false})` is a no-op on the preload path unless the host also calls `keybinding/detach!` (which keybinding.cljs:530-542 quietly admits).
- (c) The manual path `core/init!` never calls `load-settings-from-storage!` or `settings-effects/apply-all!` -- exactly one production caller of each exists (preload.cljs:98 and :116). Persisted Settings are silently ignored for every `(xray/init! …)` host.

EVIDENCE: The code's own comments contradict each other on the order: config.cljc:1469-1471 "Called from the preload's side-effect block … AFTER any host `configure!` call" vs mount.cljs:1304-1307 "The documented ordering is `configure!` → `rf/init!`, and BOTH run after the preload's load-time block". tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/settings/persistence_cljs_test.cljs:176-228 pins "host `configure!` THEN the preload's `load-settings-from-storage!`" by invoking them in that order by hand -- an order the runtime cannot produce; preload_decoupling_cljs_test.cljs exercises only the manual path.

ACTION: In `configure!`'s `:rf.xray/settings` branch replace the `reset!` with the same three-way merge `load-settings-from-storage!` performs (defaults < seed < persisted) and re-run `settings-effects/apply-all!`; make `keybinding-enabled?` reactive (a `configure!` flip calls `detach!`/`attach!`) so the "before the preload" clause can be deleted from 015:477-480; have `init!` call `load-settings-from-storage!` + `apply-all!` (or document loudly that it does not); reconcile config.cljc:1469-1471 with mount.cljs:1304-1307; add a test that runs the steps in true preload order (load block first, `configure!` second) and asserts persisted wins.

### 2. The preload's require graph writes to the host registrar at load time, ungated -- so "installs nothing in a release build" is false -- MEDIUM, spec-drift + correctness, SIZE S, CONFIRMED

WHERE: 16 top-level `(rf/reg-sub|reg-event|reg-view …)` forms outside any `debug-enabled?` gate: views/edn_inspector_state.cljs:35,38,62,67; views/edn_inspector.cljs:357,360,366,413,416,426,437,4085; views/resizable_table.cljs:793; shell.cljs:2305; panels/machine_canvas.cljs:441. Reached from preload.cljs via registry.cljs:36-41 (which requires `views.edn-inspector` for these top-level forms).

WHAT: `(when rf.interop/debug-enabled? …)` at preload.cljs:94 folds away under `goog.DEBUG=false`, but the required namespaces still load and their top-level `reg-*` calls execute in the release bundle, registering `:rf.xray.edn-inspector/*` handlers (and four views) into the host's global registrar. That is live mutation of production registrar state, not just bundle bytes. Control: everything else Xray registers sits inside `register-xray-handlers!` (registry.cljs:447-1421), a fn the gated block calls.

EVIDENCE: API.md:19-24, 011:768-788, README.md:344-349 and Tool-Pair.md:821 all state that every preload side effect is gated on `interop/debug-enabled?` and stripped by Closure DCE.

ACTION: Move the 16 forms into an `install!` fn invoked from `register-xray-handlers!` (the pattern epoch.cljs:38 already uses), or wrap each in `(when rf.interop/debug-enabled? …)`. Add a bundle-isolation assertion that a `goog.DEBUG=false` build carrying the preload contains no `rf.xray.edn-inspector` registration string.

### 3. Epoch records enter Xray's app-db raw, bypassing the whole-event `:sensitive?` drop and the retroactive scrub -- MEDIUM, privacy + spec-drift, SIZE M, CONFIRMED

WHERE: epoch.cljs:113 and :140 (`(vec (rf/epoch-history target))` assoc'd into `:epoch-history` unfiltered; :176-183 `sync-epoch-history` likewise); panels/epoch/projection.cljc:3902 and panels/issues_ribbon_helpers.cljc:369 walk `(:trace-events epoch-record)`; framework side implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/assembly.cljc:335-337 (record carries raw `:trace-events` and a `:rf.epoch/sensitive?` rollup).

WHAT: The trace path drops the WHOLE event for `:sensitive?` traces (trace_collector.cljs:329 at ingest, :223 at read) -- 013:208-212 argues the envelope itself leaks -- and `retroactive-scrub!` (trace_collector.cljs:376-396) purges the mirror when the egress profile narrows. The identical events also ride each `:rf/epoch-record`'s `:trace-events`, which the epoch pump copies verbatim into `:rf/xray` app-db and the Epoch panel / Issues ribbon project. The record's ready-made `:rf.epoch/sensitive?` rollup -- which Tool-Pair.md:111 calls the "trustworthy off-box-branch signal on the raw ring record" -- is never read. Framework per-slot redaction still applies at capture (Tool-Pair.md:171), so what leaks is the envelope class 013 says Xray closes.

EVIDENCE: `config/suppress-sensitive?` has exactly two call sites, both in trace_collector.cljs (:223, :329); `:rf.epoch/sensitive?` has 0 readers under tools/xray/src (1 mention in tools/xray/spec/004). 013:208-212 whole-event rationale; Tool-Pair.md:110 "every `register-epoch-listener!` listener deliver[s] the raw record".

ACTION: Filter `:trace-events` with `suppress-sensitive?` when seeding `:epoch-history` (both `:rf.xray/epoch-recorded` and `:rf.xray/sync-epoch-history`), gate records whose `:rf.epoch/sensitive?` is true under any non-`local-raw` profile, and extend `retroactive-scrub!` (registered at trace_collector.cljs:410-411) to the epoch slot. Update 013 to say the whole-event drop covers both ingress paths once it does.

### 4. A second, seam-side trace reader bypasses the read gate -- MEDIUM, privacy + spec-drift, SIZE S, CONFIRMED

WHERE: panels/fresco_reads.cljs:125-131 (`trace-windows` reads `(rf.trace.tooling/trace-buffer fid)` per frame; docstring :108 calls itself "a SECOND producer"); consumers panels/fresco.cljs:811 `(advisor/sub-timing windows)`, panels/fresco_advisor.cljc:201 (reads `[:tags :rf.sub/elapsed-ms]`) and :497 (renders `:sub-id` / `:frame-id` / `:elapsed-ms`).

WHAT: 013:200-206 states "Xray has no second, seam-side trace reader" and locates the tool-frame filter (trace_collector.cljs:210-211) and `suppress-sensitive?` (:223) in `snapshot-from-rings`. This reader takes event bundles straight from the framework ring -- and through the home-namespace verb Tool-Pair.md:646 calls an implementation seam, not `rf/trace-buffer` -- so the id of a `:sensitive?` sub can surface in the Fresco advisor under a profile that hides it in every other panel. Self-noise is covered only incidentally: `:rf/xray` is `:rf.trace/frame-no-emit?` so its ring is empty.

ACTION: Expose a `trace-collector/bundles-for-frame` that applies the same read gate and use it here; switch to `rf/trace-buffer`. If a second reader is intended, 013:200 must say so and name the gate it applies.

### 5. Reaches past the Tool-Pair facade: `re-frame.router/dispatch!`, `re-frame.frame/frame`, `re-frame.trace.tooling/trace-buffer` -- LOW, spec-drift + coupling, SIZE S, CONFIRMED

WHERE: panels/shared/coord_link.cljs:39,61-62 (`re-frame.router/dispatch!`; Tool-Pair.md:399 lists `re-frame.router` as off-contract); `(rf.frame/frame defaults/default-frame-id)` as a "frame registered?" probe at install.cljs:124, config.cljc:897,963,971, open_in_editor.cljs:305, trace_collector.cljs:254,392 (7 sites); fresco_reads.cljs:131 (see finding 4).

WHAT: `rf/frame` is not a `re-frame.core` export (control: `frame-ids` and `frame-meta` are, core.cljc:2154/2160, and Tool-Pair.md:306-307 names exactly those as the existence probe). coord_link's stated reason (the `rf/dispatch` macro would capture coord_link itself as the click's source coord) is real, but the fix reaches into a namespace the contract says may change between versions. Legitimate-reach control: 72 `re-frame.core` requires and 34 distinct `re-frame.*` namespaces across tools/xray/src; the other direction holds -- 0 requires of `day8.re-frame2-xray` under implementation/ (prose mentions only).

ACTION: Replace the 7 probes with `(some? (rf/frame-meta id))`; either ask core for a fn-form dispatch that does not capture its own call site or record the `re-frame.router` reach as a sanctioned exception in Tool-Pair §REPL-eval; use `rf/trace-buffer` in fresco_reads.

### 6. `:rf.xray/egress-reveal` is emitted frameless under an uncatalogued op-type and is untested -- LOW, test-gap + spec-drift, SIZE S, PLAUSIBLE

WHERE: config.cljc:768-775 `(rf/emit-trace-event! :rf.xray :rf.xray/egress-reveal {:rf.xray/from prev :rf.xray/to next})` inside try/catch; `rf/emit-trace-event!` aliases `rf.trace/emit!` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:2300), signature `[op operation tags]` (trace.cljc:857-877).

WHAT: The first arg is the op-type, so the event carries `:op-type :rf.xray`, absent from 009's closed `:op-type` set (009:147-167). No `:frame` tag makes it frameless, and per B3 (009 §Frameless; Tool-Pair.md:614) frameless events bypass every ring -- so Xray's own Trace panel, which mirrors rings, never shows the reveal that 015:415-417 and Tool-Pair.md:896 promise is "trace-visible". The try/catch swallows any refusal. PLAUSIBLE because I did not confirm whether `emit!` rejects an unknown op-type; the frameless/untested halves are confirmed.

EVIDENCE: `egress-reveal` appears in config.cljc and spec 015 only -- 0 tests.

ACTION: Emit under `:info` (009:167) with a `:frame` tag for the observed frame, or push it into Xray's frameless secondary ring so the panel shows it; add a test asserting the emit lands.

### 7. localStorage keys split across two prefix families, half unversioned; the spec names a third prefix matching none -- LOW, ergonomics + spec-drift, SIZE S, CONFIRMED

WHERE: versioned `re-frame2.xray.<x>.v1` -- config.cljc:1022 (settings), :1597 (filters; also filters/persistence.cljs:51), frame_switcher.cljs:170, palette/recents.cljs:43, views/resizable_table.cljs:92. Bare `xray.<x>` with no version -- static/persistence.cljs:50, static/machines/persistence.cljs:46,50, spine_filters.cljs:128, panels/machine_canvas.cljs:122. Two independent access layers: local_storage.cljs:2 ("the one place Xray touches localStorage") and config.cljc:1417-1440 (a private duplicate of get/set/remove).

EVIDENCE: 10 distinct keys, 5 per family (grep `"(re-frame2\.)?xray[.\-]…"`; the 11th hit, open_in_editor.cljs:338, is a `data-testid`). 015:1003-1004 says `factory-reset!` "wipes every `day8.re-frame2-xray.*` localStorage key" -- a prefix that matches 0 of the 10.

title: resources: epoch restore clears GC timers, so a restored entry whose owner rides through is never collected after release (split from rf2-omahf)
description:
RULED (iii) — ACCEPT AS A DOCUMENTED DEV-TOOL LIMITATION (Mike corrected the earlier ii ruling). The restore half of rf2-omahf, which that bead's fix worker split out.

REPRODUCED, on the JVM resources lane with the epoch artefact added, through a real rf/restore-epoch!:
- CONTROL, no restore: a load settle arms GC at 300000, a release keeps it armed, and the fire collects the entry.
- RESTORE: an app owner ([:hg/dashboard 1]) rides through. clear-host-transients-on-restore! (implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/ssr.cljc :1841, called at :2232) clears the GC slot. Releasing the owner arms nothing and the fire is a no-op, so the entry persists.
- Result: 2 tests / 6 assertions / 2 failures.
This is the same leak class as hydration, which PR #9857 fixed under ruling D.

WHY THE HYDRATION FIX SHAPE DOES NOT APPLY:
- Restore is not an event, so there is no :fx vector to carry a post-commit rearm.
- Every resources restore seam is consulted from implementation/epoch (perform-restore!). The only post-install seam is :resources/commit-restore-reconcile!, and its contract is trace commit.
- The machines precedent keeps restore CANCELLING ("epoch restore MUST NOT revive host work", Managed-Effects).
- resources_restore_cljs_test pins "no stale/GC timer is armed by restore".

SCOPE OF HARM, as the mayor measured it at source: restore-epoch! is a DEV surface. spec/009-Instrumentation.md :1167 says that with the debug gate off (CLJS :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false, or JVM re-frame.debug=false) the epoch artefact "refuses restore-epoch! / the pair-tool injection surface". So in a production build no restore runs and nothing leaks. In dev, time-travel through Xray or the pair tool can leave restored ride-through entries uncollected for the life of the session.
One caveat to verify before relying on it: spec 005 :2662 lists "restore-epoch! / undo / SSR hydration" as frame reverts. If an undo path in a production build reaches the same resources restore seams, the leak is not dev-only.

OPTIONS:
(i) An epoch-side post-install rearm hook that arms GC for restored entries. It fixes the leak at the source, but it is an epoch change, and it contradicts "restore revives no host work" and the pinned no-timer-on-restore test. Both would need to be rewritten.
(ii) Arm GC on the first owner-free transition when no GC timer is armed. This is fallback A's mechanism, applied to every entry. Restore still arms nothing, and so does hydration's fix beyond what D already does; the release path arms GC only when none is armed. It fixes restore without touching epoch, and it also covers any other path that leaves an owned entry without a GC timer. The cost is a new arm-if-absent timer mode outside the cancel-then-arm precedent, plus a spec 016 sentence adding release as an arming point.
(iii) Accept it as a dev-tool-only limit. Add one spec 016 §Restore sentence recording that restored ride-through entries are not GC-armed until something re-arms them (a later load, a mutation write, or a fresh-skip onto an owner-free entry), and that this is acceptable because restore is refused in production builds. No code change.

MAYOR'S RECOMMENDATION: (iii), PROVIDED the caveat above checks out, meaning no production-build path reaches the resources restore seams. A leak confined to a dev session, which dies with that session, is the minutiae the project stance says not to litigate, and (i) and (ii) each add mechanism to close it. If the caveat fails, recommend (ii).

DISPOSITION: Mike ruled (iii); document the accepted limitation in spec 016, with no runtime change.
