title: resources: a hydrated entry that keeps its ride-through route owner may never arm a GC timer (reproduce first)
description:
CLAIM, unverified. It comes from the rf2-m9uqu worker (PR #9843) reading the hydrated GC path; nobody has run it. Reproduce before fixing.

The chain as read at trunk b174b2ffc8. The mayor spot-checked the second, third and fourth sites:
- SSR hydration installs entries and arms no timer (ssr.cljc hydrate-runtime-db; comments at about :437 and :1500).
- Hydration route owners ride through unchanged: hydration-route-owner-policy is :ride-through (ssr.cljc :1383).
- The client fresh-skip path arms timers only when an owner is newly attached to a previously owner-free entry: was-owner-free? and arm-timers? (events.cljc :510-511), with gc-delay-ms only under arm-timers? (:517-518).
- Releasing the last owner cancels poll timers only, and the stale/GC timers "stay armed" (events.cljc :1910). For this entry, none was ever armed.

The consequence, if the chain holds:
- A hydrated fresh entry still carries its route owner and is ensured on the client by that same owner, so no GC timer is armed.
- A later release arms none either, so the entry is never collected.
- Spec 016 names unbounded owner-free growth as the anti-pattern the finite :gc-after-ms default exists to prevent.

A verified "does not happen", with a run showing a GC timer arming for that entry, is a complete result.

If it reproduces:
- Commit a regression that goes RED first.
- Then make the smallest fix in implementation/resources that is consistent with spec 016: hydration arms no timers, the GC timer arms on client ownership, and a release never restarts an armed timer.

If the only fix changes what spec 016 says, stop and report. That is Mike's call.
notes:
MAYOR DISPATCH NOTE (mayor, 2026-09-15 08:48:09 AUSEST): dispatched to worker/hydgcleak-a (worktree C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/hydgcleak-a), based on b174b2ffc8. Reproduce first; a verified "does not happen" is a complete result.

Sites spot-checked at b174b2ffc8:
- ssr.cljc :1383, the :ride-through policy;
- events.cljc :510-518, the arm-timers? gate;
- events.cljc :1910, the release comment.

Constraints:
- Fix only inside implementation/resources, RED then GREEN.
- If the only fix contradicts spec 016, stop and report for Mike.
- No browser: restutorial2-a holds the exclusive.
- spec 016 is read-only while PR #9843 is open.
WORKER VERDICT (worker/hydgcleak-a, 2026-09-15 09:00:18 AUSEST): REPRODUCED, and wider than the claim. STOPPED at brief step 4: the only fix that covers the realistic SSR boot contradicts spec 016 as merged. No PR opened. This is Mike's call.

PREMISE DIFFERENCES
- PR #9843 is MERGED (trunk commit ae4d682978), not open. Its merged clause says a hydrated entry's GC timer "arms the first time the client's ensure/fresh-skip path re-establishes ownership" and "a later owner release does not restart it". It replaced "a hydrated entry's GC deadline starts counting only once it is owner-free on the client", reasoning from the same fresh-skip gate this bead flags.
- The brief's control (a DIFFERENT owner on the client ensure should arm GC) does not hold. It arms nothing either.

EVIDENCE
Probe namespace re-frame.resources-hydrated-gc-arming-cljs-test, committed on branch worker/hydgcleak-a at 3f3a28d6bf (intentionally RED, not for merge). JVM lane: clojure -M:test -n <that ns>, run from implementation/resources. Two instruments at once: the captured :rf.resource/schedule-timers emissions, and the real host timer side table (the captured fx forwards to the production handler). Resource uses the default :gc-after-ms (300000); entry is fresh :loaded with no :stale-after-ms.
- S1, the claim. Hydrate owners {ssr, route nav-1}; after hydrate {route nav-1}, no GC timer. Client ensure with the SAME owner (fresh-skip): no GC emission, nothing in the timer table. Release: owner-free, still no GC timer. Nothing armed to fire; entry never collected. RED.
- S2, the brief's control. Client ensure with route nav-2: owners {nav-1, nav-2}. owner-newly-attached? is true but was-owner-free? is false, so no GC. Release both: owner-free, no GC, never collected. RED.
- S3, positive instrument control. Hydrated with only an SSR owner, so owner-free after hydrate. Client ensure arms GC 300000; release; fire; collected. GREEN, so the instruments see both arm and collect.
- S4, a real routing round trip. Server navigate + settle, project the payload with the SSR payload policy, reset routing counters and timers, dispatch :rf/hydrate. Routing :current with nav-token nav-1 rides the wire and is installed; the entry is owned by route nav-1. The initial URL sync (handle-url-change to the same URL) is an exact no-op: nav-token stays nav-1 and NO client ensure runs at all. Navigating away releases nav-1: owner-free, no GC timer, never collected. RED.
Run 1 on unfixed code: 4 tests, 8 assertions, 6 failures (S1, S2, S4), exit 1.

DISCRIMINATION (planted fault)
Widened the fresh-skip gate in events.cljc from (and owner-newly-attached? was-owner-free?) to (some? owner), the most permissive fresh-skip arming possible. Run 2: S1, S2, S3 GREEN (armed 300000, collected); S4 still RED; 2 failures, exit 1. So S2 fails on the was-owner-free? conjunct; S1 fails because a ride-through owner re-ensured is not newly attached; and S4 cannot be reached by ANY fresh-skip change, because on the client only the navigate-away release ever touches the entry. Restored from HEAD: default-form blob hash 1fab9eee52 equals the committed blob, git diff --quiet exits 0, and run 3 is back to 6 failures, exit 1.

OTHER PATHS THAT COULD ARM GC LATER (read at source, resources side)
Armed only by: a load/error/abort/page settle, a mutation patch or populate on the key, a GC-skip reschedule (needs an already-armed timer), or a fresh-skip onto an owner-free entry (for example re-entering the route later). Release, release-owner-identities (replan), adopt-owner, hydrate, stale-fired and frame destroy arm nothing. So the leak ends only if the user revisits, refetches or mutates that key; with no :stale-after-ms there is no refetch cadence at all.

OPTIONS FOR MIKE (none implemented)
A. Arm GC on the first owner-free transition when no GC timer is armed: the release path emits a GC arm that the timer fx applies only when that kind is not already armed. Fixes S1, S2 and S4, and likely the restore case below. Keeps "hydration arms no timer" and "a release never restarts an armed timer". But it contradicts the merged #9843 sentence (it adds release as an arming point), and it needs a new arm-if-absent timer mode outside the cancel-then-arm schedule-timers precedent. In effect it restores the pre-#9843 clause.
B. Stay inside the merged sentence: make the first client fresh-skip arm GC for a hydrated entry even when its owner rode through, via a durable "hydrated, GC not yet armed" fact stamped by hydrate-runtime-db, or by re-arming GC on every owned fresh-skip. Fixes S1 and S2 only; S4, the realistic SSR boot, still leaks. The durable fact adds an entry field; re-arming on every hit breaks the pinned fresh-skip-onto-owned-entry-does-not-re-arm contract.
C. Hydration drops ride-through route owners, or arms timers after commit like the machines hydrate-rearm. Contradicts the §Restore part 4 ride-through rule or "hydration itself arms no GC timer". Not recommended.
Recommendation: A, together with a spec 016 edit making "owner-free on the client" the GC clock start for hydrated entries.

RELATED RISK, NOT REPRODUCED
Epoch restore also clears the frame's GC timers (clear-host-transients-on-restore!, which says scheduling "re-arms LAZILY ... the next time the runtime touches each entry"). Restored entries whose owners ride through look like the same class.

Left in_progress for the mayor.
MAYOR NOTE (mayor, 2026-09-15 09:03:39 AUSEST): HOLD — AWAITING MIKE. The worker (worker/hydgcleak-a) REPRODUCED the leak on the JVM lane. It is wider than this bead's claim. The worker stopped at the brief's STOP rule and opened no PR, because the only fix that covers the normal SSR boot contradicts spec 016 as merged in PR #9843.

Reproduction: a fresh :loaded entry was hydrated through :rf/hydrate, with the default :gc-after-ms of 300000. The probe watched both the schedule-timers emissions and the host timer table.
- S1, the client ensures with the same route owner: GC is never armed and the entry is never collected.
- S2, a different client owner: GC is never armed, because was-owner-free? is false. The brief's control did not hold.
- S3, the control, where only an orphaned SSR owner is present: GC arms at 300000 and the entry is collected.
- S4, a real routing round trip: the route and nav-token ride the payload, the client's initial URL sync is an exact no-op, and no client ensure runs. Navigating away leaves the entry owner-free with no GC timer, so it is never collected.

Discrimination: a planted fault widened the fresh-skip gate to (some? owner). S1-S3 went green and S4 stayed red, so no fresh-skip change can fix S4. The restore matched the committed blob by the default hash form. On the ordinary path of an entry's life, nothing arms GC: release, the routing replan release, adopt-owner, hydrate, stale-fired and frame destroy. Only incidental events do: a later load settle, a mutation write, or re-entering the route onto an owner-free entry.

OPTIONS (worker):
- A (worker recommends): arm GC on the first owner-free transition, only when no GC timer is armed yet. It fixes S1, S2 and S4, and keeps "hydration arms no timer" and "release never restarts an armed timer". It needs the PR #9843 sentence edited to add release as an arming point, plus a new arm-if-absent timer mode outside the cancel-then-arm precedent.
- B: the first client fresh-skip arms GC for a hydrated entry. It fits the merged sentence but fixes only S1 and S2, so the real SSR boot still leaks. It also needs a new entry field or a re-arm on every cache hit, which breaks the pinned fresh-skip-onto-owned-entry-does-not-re-arm test.
- C: drop ride-through owners, or arm timers during hydration. Both contradict spec 016. Not recommended.

Risk, not reproduced: epoch restore clears GC timers and says they re-arm "lazily". Restored entries whose owners ride through look like the same leak.

State: worker/hydgcleak-a is pushed at 3f3a28d6bf and holds only the probe test implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_hydrated_gc_arming_cljs_test.cljc. The test is intentionally red, not for merge, and a fix worker should reuse it as the regression. There are no source changes and no PR.

WHAT CLEARS THIS HOLD: Mike rules A, B or C. The fix dispatch then carries the ruling and reuses the branch.
RULING (Mike, in chat, recorded 2026-09-15 13:08:49 AUSEST by the mayor).
Mike's words, verbatim: "rule rf2-omahf as your recomendation". The mayor's recommendation in chat was option D, with A as the fallback. D is not among the worker's A/B/C above; the mayor added it in chat, and it is recorded here so this bead carries it.

HOLD — AWAITING MIKE — CLEARED.

OPTION D (RULED). When the client commits a hydration, arm ONLY the GC timer for each hydrated resource entry: no stale timer, no poll timer. This works because the GC-fired handler re-checks ownership when the timer fires. Still owned: it reschedules and does not collect. Owner-free: it collects.
- S1, S2 and S4 each get a GC timer at hydration, so the entry is collected after its owner releases.
- S3 is unchanged.
- The timer is host-transient, client-side and armed after commit. It never rides the wire, and it is skipped under SSR.
- The implementation shape follows machines' :rf.machine/hydrate-rearm precedent: an fx emitted only after a valid :rf/hydrate.

WHAT D CHANGES IN SPEC 016, authorised by this ruling:
- :1216 says "hydration itself arms no GC timer". That sentence becomes the post-commit client-side arming rule. The server still arms nothing, and nothing rides the wire.
- :1226 says "a hydrated entry's GC timer arms the first time the client's ensure/fresh-skip path re-establishes ownership". That sentence is replaced by the same rule.
Keep "a release never restarts an armed timer".

FALLBACK A applies ONLY if D's premise fails at source. That means the GC-fired handler does not re-check owners and reschedule while owned, or arming after hydration cannot be made SSR- and wire-safe. title: surface-review(mcp-base): preserve metadata-owned data, record keys and EDN kinds through dedup
description:
Repair the shared dedup codec so programmer-owned metadata, record extension keys, and distinct EDN collection kinds cannot change the reported value. Three counterexamples are confirmed on the real Clojure 1.12.0 implementation at the review baseline. Two lose or add data (P2); one changes list/vector representation while preserving Clojure `=` (P3). Keep this bead open for a small local codec repair and focused cross-host regressions.

## Scope, revision and coverage

Slice: `tools_mcp_base`; exactly the 46 tracked paths under `tools/mcp-base/**` listed by `ai/surface-review-20260912/partition.json` for this slice. SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2. WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review). Revision: `1c9ff9697b0fa3a018c7a4371e02983ad2e79b2f` (also HEAD during this review). `git diff --exit-code <revision> -- tools/mcp-base` returned 0 after probing; no source changes, compilation, installs, servers, commits or pushes were made by this worker.

Runtime coverage inspected: all thirteen source namespaces under `tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/`: `args.cljc`, `cap.cljc`, `cursor.cljc`, `dedup.cljc`, `descriptor_manifest.cljc`, `diff_encode.cljc`, `egress.cljc`, `elision.cljc`, `envelope.cljc`, `overflow.cljc`, `section_grouping.cljc`, `sensitive.cljc`, and `vocab.cljc`. Examined argument defaults/finite integer bounds/keyword resolution, cap ResultIO measurement and marker construction, cursor Base64/EDN parsing and recovery, dedup/reference escaping, diff replay and grouping, profile-name mapping, sensitivity filtering, indicator counting, and descriptor serialization. Read relevant per-namespace contracts, spec index and handler-arity boundary, package/dependency/build configuration, and focused test cases/inventories, with deeper attention to dedup, cursor, envelope and CLJS-branch coverage.

Transport, sockets, nREPL connection lifetimes/timeouts, request dispatch and host result adaptation are explicitly consumer-owned and absent from this module. Neighboring Story-MCP `tools/wire_pipeline.cljc:127-161` was inspected to establish that its public `apply-dedup` passes the in-memory `:structuredContent` value to this codec and reprints the transformed EDN; its complete runtime path was not executed. Pair transport and eval-form construction belong to the separate pair review. No claim of exhaustive test execution or external MCP conformance is made.

## Finding 1 — P2: user `:cache-id` metadata becomes encoder authority and replaces real data

Source: `tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/dedup.cljc:503-517`, especially the unconditional `(:cache-id (meta org-element))` lookup at line 515; genuine encoder tagging is at lines 456-470. The escape walk preserves metadata on ordinary maps. A unique subtree returns unchanged from `process-element`, so `outer-fn` cannot assume its metadata was supplied by `check-in-cache`.

Reproduce through the PUBLIC wire wrapper, without any repeated subtree:

```clojure
(require '[re-frame.mcp-base.dedup :as d])
(let [payload {:user (with-meta {:x 1} {:cache-id 7})}
      wire (d/dedup-value payload true)]
  [wire (d/expand (:rf.mcp/dedup-table wire))])
```

Expected: metadata is not wire data and should not cause dedup to change `{:user {:x 1}}`; this no-repeat input should be a passthrough. Actual: the wire contains `{7 {:x 1}, de-dupe.cache/cache-0 {:user 7}}`, and expand returns `{:user 7}`. The encoder manufactures a cache slot outside its own symbol grammar and substitutes literal 7 for the map. A symbol such as `other/id` similarly replaces the map with that literal symbol. Controls: removing the metadata yields an identity-preserving passthrough; `enabled? false` returns the exact original object.

Impact: callers using ordinary map metadata can receive a successful but false view of their data. The caller need not hand-author a malformed cache or use the reserved `de-dupe.cache` namespace; `:cache-id` is an unqualified metadata key. The public codec and Story's in-memory adapter make this relevant beyond a text-reader edge case. No end-to-end Story run is claimed.

Repair: distinguish bookkeeping generated by this encode invocation from input metadata. Prefer threading the cache id separately through the traversal; a call-local private marker with identity checking is also sufficient. Simply checking for any `cache-N`-looking value does not establish ownership, and replacing one unqualified key with a static keyword leaves a collision class. Do not require application callers to strip arbitrary metadata or reserve a new public metadata key.

Acceptance: a `.cljc` regression invokes `dedup-value` on the minimal metadata input and proves the value is unchanged, the no-repeat path does not invent a wrapper, and disabled dedup remains identical. Add an input with a real repeated subtree to prove compression still occurs and expands exactly despite unrelated `:cache-id` metadata. All emitted raw table keys must remain allocator-generated `de-dupe.cache/cache-N` symbols.

## Finding 2 — P2: record key escaping adds a permanent extra entry

Source: `tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/dedup.cljc:384` (record rebuild during escape/count/substitution), `:480` (escape pass), and `:537` (inverse record rebuild). Both record branches reduce transformed entries into the ORIGINAL record. When a dynamic extension key changes spelling, assoc adds the new key without removing the original key.

Reproduce:

```clojure
(defrecord ReviewRecord [x])
(let [shared {:v [1 2 3]}
      payload {:record (assoc (->ReviewRecord shared)
                              :de-dupe.cache/cache-1 77)
               :a shared}
      wire (d/dedup-value payload true)]
  (d/expand (:rf.mcp/dedup-table wire)))
```

Expected: the original record retains exactly `:x` and the dynamic key `:de-dupe.cache/cache-1`. Actual: the expanded record additionally contains `:de-dupe.cache/!cache-1 77`; `=` against the original payload is false. The encoded record already contains BOTH original and escaped spellings, contradicting the codec's promise that all reference-shaped literals are escaped. The inverse similarly keeps the escaped key when adding its unescaped counterpart. The unrelated `shared` subtree forces a real multi-slot wrapper. Control: converting the record to an ordinary map round-trips exactly; disabled dedup is identity-preserving.

Impact: normal persistent records carrying extension-map entries gain data during the default wire transformation. The host-side corruption is proven directly. An additional JSON alias/collision risk follows from the unescaped key left in the table, but the actual Clojure-to-JSON-to-Node seam was not executed in this review and is not counted as an additional confirmed defect.

Repair: rebuild record extension entries with replacement semantics: remove an original extension key when its transformed key differs, then assoc its transformed entry. Apply this in both the forward walk and inverse. Preserve fixed record fields and record identity where currently supported; no generic serialization redesign is needed. Take care to read all original entries before mutations can overwrite a later entry. The existing sorted collection lowering is independent and should remain intact.

Acceptance: add a cross-host record fixture with at least one dynamic colliding symbol/keyword/string key, force a genuine wrapper, and assert exact expanded map entries plus record type. Pin original key removal in the encoded representation and escaped-key removal after expansion. Retain an ordinary-map control and real-repeat/disabled controls. A small real Story `apply-dedup` integration pin should show that text and structured slots preserve the same original data.

## Finding 3 — P3: equality pooling merges list and vector wire representations

Source: `tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/dedup.cljc:411-423`, `:437-445`, and `:456-470`. Candidate counting and slot lookup use only `hash` and `=`. Clojure lists and vectors with the same elements share equality/hash but are distinct EDN forms. `de-dupe-eq` at lines 482-487 promises an exact inverse, and `test/re_frame/mcp_base/dedup_test.cljc:425-449` explicitly describes collection-kind preservation and checks a list remains a list; that test never puts equal lists and vectors next to each other.

Reproduce:

```clojure
(d/expand (d/de-dupe-eq {:list '(1 2 3) :vector [1 2 3]}))
;; => {:list (1 2 3), :vector (1 2 3)}
(d/expand (d/de-dupe-eq (array-map :vector [1 2 3] :list '(1 2 3))))
;; => {:vector [1 2 3], :list [1 2 3]}
```

Expected: a list remains a list and a vector remains a vector, regardless of traversal order. Actual: both occurrences use whichever collection kind was pooled first. Ordinary `=` assertions pass, which hides the changed printed EDN and `list?`/`vector?` results. A same-kind repeated-vector control still round-trips with vector values.

Impact: an agent consuming the EDN view is shown a different collection form, which matters when carrying data back into Clojure code. JSON flattens both to arrays, so no JSON-value corruption is claimed here. This is a narrower fidelity defect than findings 1 and 2, hence P3.

Repair: make the shared pooling equivalence preserve wire-relevant collection kind, consistently across counting, repeat checks and slot lookup. A small kind discriminator distinguishing vector from list/seq is enough; retain equality-based pooling within a kind and the deliberate sorted-to-unsorted policy. Check containing subtrees too: maps containing equal-but-differently-shaped sequences must not be pooled as interchangeable. Alternatively use one wire-shape-aware equality function consistently; do not switch to identity pooling.

Acceptance: `.cljc` tests force a real wrapper with equal list/vector values, exercise both insertion orders, and assert `list?` and `vector?` after expansion in addition to `=`. Include equal containing maps whose child collection kinds differ. Existing same-kind equality pooling remains effective.

## Evidence and validation limits

Executed the unmodified Clojure 1.12.0 sources with Java 21 and already-cached Clojure/spec jars, using an absolute source classpath and a process-local inline/scratch program. Durable review-local evidence (all gitignored):

- `ai/surface-review-20260912/probe-tools_mcp_base-1.clj`
- `ai/surface-review-20260912/probe-tools_mcp_base-1.log`
- `ai/surface-review-20260912/probe-tools_mcp_base-1.exit`

The log identifies the actual loaded source URL in SOURCE_ROOT and prints all three counterexamples and controls. Captured runner exit: 0. That means the observations were reproduced; assertions intentionally establish the present defects and controls, so this is NOT a passing correctness gate or proof of remediation. An initial Babashka attempt could not load `args` because its SCI runtime lacks `find-keyword`; it was replaced by the real JVM and is not evidence of a library defect. No stale compiled CLJS output was used. CLJS behavior, complete Story integration, JSON transport, concurrent execution, release packaging, Malli-present validation and broad gates remain unexecuted.

Additional inspected/probed behavior, not a separate remediation request: deliberately hand-authored cursor/marker text can reproduce the static appended EOF sentinel and close the synthetic wrapper, causing trailing content to be ignored. This is a counterexample to the implementation's strong exhaustion prose, but no evaluation, authorization bypass or changed valid cursor payload was demonstrated. Given opaque cursors, trusted programmers and the stance against speculative hardening, it does not justify expanding this repair into parser security work. Likewise, malformed raw dedup tables with dangling references still yield nil on the Clojure side; that is explicitly recorded as an existing non-goal in rf2-kjv05 and rf2-7wwp, so it is not refiled as new work.

## Existing history and recommendation boundaries

Read current all-status MCP issue summaries, searched exact body/title terms via both `bd search` and the issue export, and examined relevant dedup history. No existing bead was found owning metadata bookkeeping collisions, record extension-key replacement, or mixed list/vector pooling. Closest records:

- `rf2-kjv05` (closed): implements literal-token escaping for symbols/strings/keywords. Its latest closure is the keyword repair; the remaining record rebuild path in finding 2 is different from omitting a scalar type from the escape classifier. Its notes intentionally retain quiet nil for malformed Clojure-side references.
- `rf2-7wwp` (closed): lowers sorted maps/sets before cache placeholders reach their comparator. That repair is present and does not address records, caller metadata or equal sequence kinds.
- `rf2-ntbd1` (closed, rejected as gold-plating): proposed moving the Pair-only diff codec out of base. Do not repeat that relocation; its explicit disposition explains why the existing JVM/Malli lane is retained.
- `rf2-fo4ng` / `rf2-uelji`: existing coordinate/group verification work covers the first-publish concerns. This review found no reason to duplicate it.

Use one focused implementation change to the existing codec and relevant tests/spec wording. Do not change tool names, argument defaults, the public dedup envelope, reference grammar, equality-versus-identity posture, transport ownership or release process. This bead is the complete single deliverable for the slice under `rf2-fzbj`; root owns tracker checkpoint and push.

title: Incomplete: Epoch and Machine Inspector share EDN mount lifecycles
description:
Merged-PR audit #9663, landed 9f103fed31721d9b1583c1e287fa85aa113368ae. The migration replaces thirteen EDN inspector heads in panels/epoch/view.cljs with edn-inspector-view, but each new :mount-id derives only from a logical site/row: line 2036 is the constant epoch/dispatch-event, and the shared cascade transition/start/data sites at 3219, 3299 and 3407 use only a role plus :step. These distinguish roles in one panel, not live mounts in one frame.

Two standalone Epoch panels displaying the same dispatch both emit epoch/dispatch-event. More sharply, an Epoch panel and a Machine Inspector simultaneously displaying the same machine cascade both call machine-cascade-mini-pipeline (Machine Inspector line 387) and emit epoch/machine-cascade-transition-delta/1 for its first transition. panels.cljs:325/394 delegates through zero-argument bridges; both Panel bodies ignore props, so a caller cannot qualify these identities. The facade supports separate mount containers.

views/edn_inspector.cljs:3155 keys mount-state by [frame-id mount-id]. container-ref-for memoizes that key's ref and installs an observer only when none exists. release-mount! disconnects/removes the entry and clears its width when either ref detaches. Thus these simultaneous inspectors share measurement state and one unmount removes the surviving inspector's observer/width state. The landed data flow establishes the collision; this audit did not execute a new two-container browser reproduction. Relevant runtime blobs are unchanged at freshly fetched origin/main. New DOM suites mount one panel at a time and grade boundary subscription counts, not simultaneous inspector lifecycles.

Thread a minimal stable caller-owned instance qualifier through both facades/bridges/boundaries and the shared helper context; qualify the thirteen inspector mount IDs, including the cross-panel shared cascade case. Follow the shipped optional :instance-id pattern and normalize before Reagent interop. Keep intentional logical site/expansion/popup state sharing and existing React row keys distinct from lifecycle/width identity. No general identity framework. rf2-pua3 is literal-open but explicitly owns Trace only; closed rf2-5ykm owns Managed FX only. Neither explicitly records this correction.

title: xray: metadata-carried React keys are invisible to Fresco — class defect, 51 + 9 sites
description:
A CLASS DEFECT, not a site. Discovered by the rf2-vw80 worker while fixing two instances of it, and MEASURED
INDEPENDENTLY BY THE MAYOR at source before filing — the counts below are the mayor's own readings.

THE MECHANISM. Reagent reads a React key from CLOJURE METADATA. Fresco does not. Measured in
`implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/codec.cljs`: `(meta `, `-meta` and a bare `meta` substring
each read **0**, against a control of **88** `defn` in the same file. The codec reads Clojure metadata
NOWHERE. Its own docstring table states the key source for all three head kinds — native tag, boundary
(`defview` head), and host / `[:> Component ...]` — as "literal `:key` in the attr map".

SO `^{:key x} [:div ...]` AND `(with-meta [...] {:key x})` RENDER FINE UNDER REAGENT AND REACH REACT WITH NO
KEY AT ALL UNDER FRESCO. Nothing errors, nothing warns, and the DOM looks correct until React reorders or
reconciles a list — at which point it is a stale-row bug with no stack trace pointing anywhere near the key.

THE POPULATION, measured over `tools/xray/src/` (control: 1899 `defn` under the same root, so the instrument
is alive):
  * `^{:key` — **71 sites across 28 files**
  * `with-meta` lines carrying `:key` — **5**, across a further overlapping set

THE 28 FILES INCLUDE PANELS UNDER ACTIVE MIGRATION, which is why this is filed now rather than after the
migration: `panels/app_db_diff.cljs`, `panels/derivation_graph.cljs`, `panels/reactive_panel_view.cljs`,
`panels/fresco.cljs`, `panels/routing.cljs`, `panels/trace.cljs`, `panels/l2_timeline.cljc`,
`panels/epoch/view.cljs`, `shell.cljs`, `frame_switcher.cljs`, `filters/pills.cljs`, the `static/**` family,
and more. Re-measure rather than trusting this list; it is a snapshot.

TWO SITES ARE ALREADY FIXED and are the worked example: PR #9591 (rf2-vw80) moved two `with-meta` key sites
in `panels/cancellation_cascade.cljs` into the attribute map, keeping the key expressions identical, and
demonstrated red-to-green — before the fix the two abort rows collapsed from two distinct React keys to ONE,
and the teardown rows read `[nil nil]`. That worker also verified at source that Reagent's
`react-key-from-meta-or-props` reads meta THEN props, so **one attribute satisfies both renderers** and the
fix costs no Reagent compatibility.

THE HOLLOW GATE THAT LET IT THROUGH, because the sweep must not recreate it. The test
`cascade-body-rows-carry-key-meta` asserted `(some? (some-> (meta row) :key))` — the row's Clojure metadata,
which `with-meta` genuinely does set. It never rendered through a codec, so it could not see that the key
reaches React as nothing. It proved the thing the code does, not the thing the code is FOR, and it stayed
green across the whole defect. It was REPLACED, not patched. **Any assertion in this sweep must read what
reaches the RENDERER.** The mechanical test: delete the key expression and the row must go red.

SCOPE AND SEQUENCING — THIS IS THE PART THAT DECIDES WHEN IT CAN BE DISPATCHED. Every one of these files is
in `tools/xray/`, and at filing time two live workers hold parts of that tree (the panel migration and the
audit residuals). A tree-wide sweep MUST NOT run concurrently with them. Sequence it after the Xray
migration epic rf2-k97c settles, or scope it to files provably outside any live worker's surface.

NOT ESTABLISHED, and a sweep must establish it per site rather than assuming: whether a given `^{:key ...}`
site sits in a subtree Fresco actually renders. Some may be on Reagent-only paths, and `.cljc` files may be
shared. A blanket rewrite of all 71 without that check would be churn, and would touch files for no reason.
The deliverable is the sites that Fresco renders, fixed, with renderer-level evidence.
notes:
MAYOR CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S OWN FIGURES, 2026-09-10, after PR #9590 merged as 45dbdabbb9. TWO THINGS
ABOVE ARE WRONG. Both were mine, and both were caught by the rf2-k97c.3 worker rather than by me.

=== 1. THE COUNT WAS PROSE-CONTAMINATED, AND SINGLE-AXIS ===

The bead says "71 sites across 28 files". That was a RAW, LINE-ORIENTED grep. It counted comment prose as
evidence — instrument item (g) — and some of the prose it counted was a worker's own comments DESCRIBING the
defect, so the census manufactured findings against a file that had just been repaired.

RE-MEASURED ON TRUNK AT 45dbdabbb9, three axes, control 1904 `defn` under the same root and a nonsense probe
at 0:

    ^{:key   raw line-oriented ...... 59
    ^{:key   CODE-ONLY line-oriented  51   <- the figure to use
    ^{:key   flattened per file ..... 59
    files carrying it, code-only .... 23

    with-meta ... {:key, flattened .. 15 sites across 9 files
    (with-meta occurrences overall ... 27 across 13 files)

The 8-site gap between raw and code-only is prose. Use 51 + 15.

=== 2. THE LINE-ORIENTED PASS IS NOT SUFFICIENT, AND HERE IS THE PROOF ===

Metadata and its call form can sit on ADJACENT LINES. In `panels/derivation_graph.cljs` a line-oriented pass
read 3 and a flattened pass read 5 — a line-oriented census would have called that panel two-fifths clean.
On trunk today raw and flattened both read 59 because that worker fixed the split-line sites, so the
disagreement is currently invisible; the METHOD still stands, because the shape recurs.

AND THE `with-meta` SPELLING DEFEATS A PAREN-BOUNDED REGEX. `with-meta[^)]{0,200}?:key` cannot cross the
wrapped call's own closing paren, so it reads 0 on `(with-meta (row x) {:key k})`. It read 0 on
`panels/cancellation_cascade.cljs` where the truth is 2. Flatten the file and match without a paren-exclusion
class.

=== 3. "TWO SITES ARE ALREADY FIXED" IS TRUE OF A BRANCH, NOT OF TRUNK ===

The bead says the two `cancellation_cascade.cljs` sites are already fixed. They are fixed IN PR #9591, WHICH
HAS NOT MERGED. Verified on trunk at 45dbdabbb9: that file still carries 2 `with-meta ... {:key` sites, and
the hollow test still asserts on `(meta row)`. My wording conflated "landed in a pull request" with "fixed",
which is precisely the kind of premise a worker then has to refute at its own cost. The worked example in
this bead is still the right one — read it as a DEMONSTRATION on a branch, not as trunk state.

=== WHAT IS UNCHANGED AND STILL VERIFIED ===

The mechanism. Re-derived independently by that worker and by me: `codec.cljs` carries 0 occurrences of
`meta` against a control of 88 `defn`. Fresco reads the key from the attribute map only.

AND THE FIX IS PROVEN AT SCALE NOW, which the bead could not say before: PR #9590 moved SEVENTEEN sites
across its own files into attribute maps or keyed fragments, with a new row reading `(:key (props-of node))`
— the attr map, not metadata — proven red-to-green by a planted fault. So the remedy is demonstrated, and
what remains is reach rather than design.

LARGEST REMAINING CONCENTRATIONS, reported by that worker and to be re-derived at sweep start rather than
trusted: `panels/fresco.cljs` (10), `panels/epoch/view.cljs` (7), `views/resizable_table.cljs` (7, the
`with-meta` spelling), `shell.cljs` (5), `settings/view.cljs` (4).
FIGURES SUPERSEDED AGAIN — read THIS block, not the two above it. Measured on trunk c255a4c3d7, after both
PR #9590 and PR #9591 merged, with the census run COMMENT-STRIPPED and then FLATTENED, and a control run
through the identical pipeline (`defn` = 1902, alive).

    ^{:key ................... 51 sites
    with-meta ... {:key .......  9 sites across 4 files:
                                 panels/machine_inspector.cljs 1
                                 panels/trace.cljs             1
                                 static/machines/sim.cljs      2
                                 views/resizable_table.cljs    5

MY PREVIOUS `with-meta` FIGURE OF 15 ACROSS 9 FILES WAS ALSO PROSE-CONTAMINATED. Five of those nine files —
app_db_diff_state, cancellation_cascade, derivation_graph, shell, edn_inspector — no longer carry a code
site: some were repaired by the two merges, and the rest were comments describing the defect. The mayor made
the same error twice in one tick, the second time one command after being corrected on it.

SO THE CENSUS RECIPE IS PART OF THIS BEAD, not an implementation detail: STRIP COMMENTS, THEN FLATTEN, THEN
MATCH, and take the control through the same pipeline. A raw line-oriented grep on this tree is wrong in BOTH
directions at once — it counts prose that is not a defect, and it misses a call form whose metadata sits on
the previous line.

`machine_canvas.cljs` measured 0 in both spellings and needs nothing on this axis; its migration disposition
is rf2-dp64.
CENSUS RECIPE AMENDMENT — STRIP DOCSTRINGS TOO, NOT ONLY COMMENTS.

The recipe above says strip comments, then flatten. That is not sufficient on this tree. A Clojure DOCSTRING
is a string literal, not a comment, so `sed 's/;.*$//'` leaves it entirely intact — and the docstrings here
routinely describe the mechanism being censused.

MEASURED 2026-09-10 on `panels/machine_canvas.cljs` while ruling rf2-dp64: a probe for `subscribe` read 2,
BOTH of them docstring prose at lines 224-225 explaining what the var used to do as a plain fn. The
comment-stripping pass reported the same 2, because it cannot see inside a string. Had that 2 been believed,
the ruling that the panel performs no reads — which is the whole basis for leaving it on Reagent — would have
been reversed on evidence that was documentation.

THIS IS THE THIRD PROSE CONTAMINATION IN ONE HOUR on this tree, after two `;`-comment instances, so treat it
as a property of the CODEBASE rather than an unlucky file: the code here is heavily self-documenting, and the
things worth censusing are exactly the things the prose talks about. A census that counts prose manufactures
findings against the best-documented files, which is instrument item (g) arriving through a third door.

THE GUARD: strip comments AND docstrings before matching, or read the forms rather than the text; then take
the control through the identical pipeline so a broken stripper shows up as a dead control rather than as a
plausible number.
close_reason:
CLOSED BY THE MAYOR WITHOUT DISPATCHING A WORKER, 2026-09-10, on trunk 98f99ad2e1. **THE CLASS IS REAL AND
THE MECHANISM IS CONFIRMED, BUT THERE ARE ZERO LIVE INSTANCES, AND THE FUTURE ONES ALREADY HAVE AN OWNER.**
This bead was mine, it was filed at P2, and the P2 was wrong.

=== THE MEASUREMENT THAT SETTLES IT ===

Census over `tools/xray/src`, stripping STRING LITERALS (docstrings included) and `;` comments before
matching, then splitting each file by whether it carries a Fresco `defview`:

    total code-only metadata-key sites .... 54
    ... in a file with a Fresco defview ...  0      <- LIVE defect surface
    ... in a file with no defview ......... 54      across 21 files
    CONTROL, `(defn ` through the same stripper .... 1008   (instrument alive)

**ZERO.** Reagent reads a React key from Clojure metadata, so every one of those 54 sites works correctly
today. The defect exists only where Fresco renders, and Fresco renders none of these files.

=== WHY THE EARLIER FIGURES WERE ALL WRONG, AND EACH IN A DIFFERENT WAY ===

This bead carried "71 sites across 28 files", then "51 + 9", then a claim of 16 live sites across 3 files.
Every one was an artefact, and the sequence is worth keeping because each failure is a different door:

  * 71/28 — a RAW line-oriented grep. Counted comment prose as evidence, including a worker's own comments
    describing the defect. Instrument item (g).
  * 51 + 9 — comment-stripped but NOT docstring-stripped. A Clojure docstring is a string literal, so
    `sed 's/;.*$//'` leaves it whole, and the docstrings in this tree describe the very mechanism being
    censused.
  * "16 live sites across 3 files" — reached by grepping each file for the string `fresco` and calling a hit
    evidence that Fresco renders it. `panels/fresco.cljs` scored 20 hits and carries ZERO Fresco requires and
    ZERO `defview`: it is the panel ABOUT Fresco, Reagent-rendered. `shell.cljs` scored 1 and has 31
    `reg-view`. The name of a thing is not the thing.
  * `panels/routing.cljs` survived one round longer than the rest, on a single site at line 349 — which is
    the sentence "used to attach it as `^{:key ...}` reader metadata on the CALL FORM", inside a docstring,
    and its only `defview` sits at line 527, AFTER it.

**THE DISCRIMINATOR THAT ACTUALLY WORKS IS `defview` IN STRIPPED CODE**, not the token `fresco` anywhere.
The census script is preserved at the mayor's scratch path for the next attempt; its method is: strip
`"..."` spans, strip `;` to end-of-line, flatten, match, and run a known-present control through the
identical pipeline so a broken stripper reads as a dead control rather than a plausible number.

=== WHY THE FUTURE INSTANCES DO NOT NEED THIS BEAD ===

rf2-k97c.3's own ruling already binds them: *every remaining panel dispatch checks its own panels for this
shape as part of its work*. That is the right place for it — the fix is trivial once you are already editing
the file, the key expression is unchanged, and Reagent's `react-key-from-meta-or-props` reads meta THEN
props, so one attribute satisfies both renderers. Two migrations have already done exactly this: PR #9590
moved 17 sites and PR #9591 moved 2, each with renderer-level evidence.

A STANDING SWEEP WOULD THEREFORE BE DUPLICATED WORK AGAINST FILES THAT ARE CORRECT TODAY, ahead of a
migration that may never reach some of them. "We are not over-engineering or gold plating" settles that.

=== WHAT SURVIVES, AND WHERE ===

The MECHANISM is the durable part and it is recorded where it will be read: Fresco's codec carries zero
occurrences of `meta` against a control of 88 `defn`, and reads `:key` from the attribute map only. That fact
lives in this bead's history, in rf2-vw80's close reason with its red-to-green demonstration, and in
rf2-k97c.3's standing direction to every remaining increment.

**IF A FUTURE READER FINDS METADATA KEYS IN A FRESCO-RENDERED FILE, THAT IS A NEW DEFECT WITH A LIVE
INSTANCE — file it then, with the site.** Do not re-file this bead speculatively; the speculative version is
what produced four wrong numbers in one afternoon.

title: [implementation/resources] Optimistic rollback orphans a newer in-flight refetch
description:
Snapshot: 7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd, dedicated review checkout codex-correctness-20260907. Relevant resources source and Spec 016 unchanged against mayor HEAD 90e9b0008ac96bb59e0e9f6ec03de8e1d650f21d.

Supported sequence: load a resource; start an optimistic mutation that patches it; start a normal refetch while the mutation is pending; receive the mutation's accepted failure before that refetch replies. The optimistic data should roll back without orphaning the newer read. Actual: rollback restores the older whole entry, removing the refetch's current-work/generation. Its later valid reply is suppressed. If that load also attached a new owner, rollback drops that owner and reindexing removes its ownership too.

Exact causal trace:
- implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/state.cljc:958 entry-start-load changes generation, current-work, request-id, attempt/status and can attach an owner, but deliberately does not bump revision.
- mutation_runtime.cljc:414 records the entire pre-apply entry and the applied revision; :492 compares only revision; :512 chooses :restore when it has not moved; :543 restores the whole :before map.
- mutation_events.cljc:615 settle-optimistic-rollback calls that restore at :645 and reindexes at :652. Recovery refetches are only built for conflict/:invalidate dispositions (:660), not this :restore arm. The accepted failure handler uses this settlement path.
- reply_handlers.cljc:93 live-slot-for-reply requires current-work and generation to still match. The read has neither after restoration, and success/failure handlers therefore suppress its reply.

This is a composition defect in two separately written rules, not an objection to the chosen conflict API: docs/EP/EP-0019-optimistic-mutation-rollback.md Decision 2/Open Issue 5 and implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_revision_substrate_cljs_test.cljc:50 explicitly keep read start from moving revision, to avoid false conflicts. The same EP Decision 3 and spec/016-Resources.md optimistic conflict table require whole :before restoration when revision is unchanged. Applied together, those rules lose later live work even though no newer authoritative data has landed. Preserve the settled no-false-conflict rule and :on-conflict API; narrowly clarify which payload/state rollback owns versus newer live-work/ownership facts.

Executed bounded probe (actual CLJC state/mutation/reply primitives, bb classpath implementation/core/src;implementation/resources/src; exit 0, about 0.81s):

```clojure
(require '[re-frame.resources.state :as s]
         '[re-frame.resources.mutation-runtime :as m]
         '[re-frame.resources.reply-handlers :as rh])
(let [key [:rf.scope/global :review/article {}]
      before (-> (s/empty-entry :review/article key)
                 (s/entry-succeeded {:data {:n 1} :loaded-at 100
                                     :stale-at nil :tags #{}})
                 (s/attach-owner [:app :old]))
      inverse (m/record-optimistic-entry key before :patch)
      applied (m/apply-optimistic-patch before #(update % :n inc)
                                      :review/article
                                      {:clock-ms 200 :scoped-key key})
      reading (s/entry-start-load applied
                {:generation 9 :work-id [:review/read 9]
                 :request-id :r9 :owner [:app :new]})
      disposition (m/rollback-entry-disposition reading inverse :invalidate)
      restored (m/restore-before (assoc-in {} (s/entry-path key) reading)
                                disposition)
      after (get-in restored (s/entry-path key))]
  (prn (select-keys disposition [:disposition :conflict?])
       (select-keys reading [:data :generation :current-work :active-owners])
       (select-keys after [:data :generation :current-work :active-owners])
       (boolean (rh/live-slot-for-reply restored :review/frame
                  (fn [_] (s/entry-path key))
                  {:generation 9 :work/id [:review/read 9]}))))
```

Observed :restore/:conflict? false; reading data {:n 2}, generation 9, current-work [:review/read 9], both owners; after data {:n 1}, generation 0, current-work nil, only old owner; final acceptance false. This executes the causal state seam, not a full event/HTTP/browser integration. Event wiring, revision contract and callers were inspected source-only. A realistic caller is examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/mutations.cljs:163 (optimistic favorite); resources also support explicit refetch/revalidation while it is pending.

Smallest repair: reconcile rollback-owned optimistic data/freshness with the current entry's newer live work and owner metadata, including a status coherent with the preserved read. Do not fix by reusing generation as revision or inventing a public API. Update the precise whole-entry normative wording needed for this case, and retain existing no-concurrent-work exact rollback and moved-revision invalidation behavior.

Focused acceptance: public resource/mutation event test loads A, applies optimistic B, starts a refetch, fails the mutation, then settles the read with C. Assert rollback removes B, leaves that read acceptable, and the public subscription eventually shows C. Pair same-owner and newly attached-owner variants; ownership indexes remain coherent. Existing no-work rollback and already-landed-read conflict controls stay unchanged. No full suites, compilation, live HTTP or browser run during review.

Dedupe: active/closed searches optimistic/revision/rollback and relevant optimistic/refetch memories checked. Fully read closed rf2-wcdj4 (tagless moved-revision invalidation/affected-keys; distinct), rf2-6r9j.61 (obsolete revision-helper removal; distinct), rf2-chl2 (example accepted success-writer granularity; distinct). Coordinator explicitly approved filing this demonstrated contract-composition defect without reopening these issues or implementing a normative change.
notes:
Merged-PR audit #9376 (2026-09-07): runtime and focused regression delivery accepted; reopen only the existing owner's requested normative wording correction. At landed 66b53ab80b19fe2dd0fa3935b70b58d20cb78392, docs/EP/EP-0019-optimistic-mutation-rollback.md:284-290 still says the inverse restores the whole entry and an absent snapshot removes it; Decision 3's conflict table at :358 and shipped addendum at :822 still require restoring the before entry verbatim when revision is unchanged. The landed reconcile-restored-entry / restore-before deliberately preserve newer generation/current-work/request-id/attempt/active-owners, reconcile loading status, and retain an empty entry under a live read even for an absent snapshot. These are the demonstrated normal refetch case in this owner's description, which explicitly asks to update the precise whole-entry normative wording. A reader following the unchanged conflict table would reintroduce the orphaned read.

Append a narrow amendment to the normative rollback rule and its shipped carry: rollback owns optimistic payload/freshness, retains current live read and ownership facts with coherent status, and restores absence only when it would not orphan live work. Preserve the original no-concurrent-work exact rollback and moved-revision conflict rules; no new API or broader design work is needed. Preserve historical ruling text where appropriate by identifying the amendment explicitly. No additional runtime defect is claimed. All seven landed paths match the PR head and tested CI merge 19ec0c0dc69b8acb634d9c7ef62e107eee1a991b; actual CI routing, production routing, resources, machines and consolidated Node suites all passed. Existing owner description and criteria remain unchanged.
close_reason: Closing the AUDIT RESIDUAL only (merged-PR audit #9376) — the original deliverable, the runtime fix (reconcile-restored-entry / restore-before) and its focused regression, merged earlier and is UNTOUCHED: no code changed in this work at all. PR #9391, documentation only. EP-0019 still said the inverse restores the whole entry and an absent snapshot removes it, in all three places the audit named: the inverse-snapshot paragraph, Decision 3's conflict table, and the shipped addendum. A reader following that would reintroduce the orphaned read, because entry-start-load deliberately does not bump :revision (Open Issue 5), so a refetch begun while the mutation is pending leaves the revision unmoved, the settle chooses :restore, and a literally-whole restore reinstates the pre-read :generation / :current-work — after which live-slot-for-reply suppresses that read's own valid reply and any owner the load attached is dropped. The documents now describe what shipped: rollback owns the optimistic payload and its freshness; :generation, :current-work, :request-id, :attempt and :active-owners carry forward off the current entry with a coherent :status; an :absent snapshot restores absence only where no read is in flight, otherwise retaining the empty pre-seed entry carrying that read. Original ruling text PRESERVED and the narrowing marked as an explicit Amendment, as the audit asked. ONE FILE BEYOND THE AUDIT NOTE'S CITED LINES: spec/016-Resources.md's optimistic conflict table carried the identical stale sentence and is corrected in the same terms — the audit cited EP line numbers only, but this bead's own description names spec/016's conflict table alongside the EP, and 016 is the normative surface a reader follows. One table row plus a short explanatory note. Gates: python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py exit 0; python -m mkdocs build --strict exit 0 (docs/EP/** is NOT in mkdocs.yml's exclude_docs block — that block holds tools/playground, the two codemod trees and design/freehand|hicasso|retirement — and docs_dir is 'docs', so the strict build DOES cover docs/EP/**; spec/ is covered too via mkdocs_hooks.py's staging).

title: api(views): Hicasso joins the client-root / render! {:hydrate? …} / unmount! grammar; delete h/mount! and h/hydrate!
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from views.md (ref views.4); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

After views.3 the frame lives in the tree on every substrate, and what is left of Hicasso's root door is a fourth spelling of one React-level job: `(h/mount! el opts view)` → handle (Root created at once, so callers wrap it in an atom: `examples/substrates/hicasso/login/core.cljs:255-267`), `(h/hydrate! el opts view)` as a separate verb, `(h/render! handle view)` for hot reload, `(h/unmount! handle)` (`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc:552-681`, impl `impl/mount.cljs:84-96,139-162,247-286,288`). The Reagent/reagent-slim adapters — and UIx after views.1 — spell the same lifecycle as an inert `client-root` handle, a `render!` whose first call creates OR hydrates (`{:hydrate? true}`) and whose later calls update the same Root, and an idempotent `unmount!` (Spec 006 §The client root, `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:244-261`). The transitions are real (create, adopt, update, release) — the disagreement was whether they need four names or one handle with a first-call mode, and both reviewers settled on the handle. Hicasso's `createRoot` at `mount.cljs:157-158` also sits outside the adapter's active-root set (no `active-root` reference anywhere in `impl/mount.cljs`), so `rf/destroy-adapter!` never releases a Hicasso root.

## Evidence (tip 6445d0611b)

- Facade: `mount!` (`hicasso.cljc:552-608`, `(fn mount! [container config hiccup] (impl-mount/root! container (:frame config) hiccup config))`), `hydrate!` (`:610-661` → `impl-mount/hydrate-root!`), `render!` (`:663-674` = `impl-mount/render!`, `(handle hiccup)`, `flushSync`), `unmount!` (`:676-681`). Manifest rows `spec/api-manifest.edn:218,219,222,225` (`:owner "004C"`).
- Impl: `render!` `mount.cljs:84-96` reconciles through `tree` (`:54-82`), which for a hydrated handle wraps the app in the adoption-window Fragment on EVERY render (`:62-67`) — the handle's `:adoption` window is the one fact that says a root is hydrated; `hydrate-root!` `:247-286` returns before adoption finishes and installs the hydration reporter; `root!` `:139-162`; `unmount!` `:288`; `release!` `:310` (fixture door, stays off the facade).
- Consumers: example `login/core.cljs:255-299` (`!root` atom, `re-render!`, `mount!`/`hydrate!` branch); testbeds `hicasso_testbed/core.cljs:888`, `hicasso_hmr_testbed/core.cljs:33,355,454`; Story test `hicasso_substrate_dom_cljs_test.cljs:363,381`; test kit rides `impl.mount/root!` (`mounted.cljs:696-697`) and its own `hm/rerender!` / `hm/unmount!` (`:17,:22`); docs 10 guide pages + `docs/api/re-frame.hicasso.md:125-160` (counts in views.3); skill `skills/reagent-migration/references/catalog-mechanical.md:294-333`; `skills/reagent-migration/tests/fixture/test/reagent_migration/mig23_cold_start_test.cljs:77` names `rf.hicasso/hydrate!` in a message string.
- Codex's ownership facts the handle must retain (from `view-adapter-ergonomics.md` and its Codex Thoughts): synchronous update commits (`flushSync`), a root-specific hydration window, recoverable-error reporting per root, and the stable wrapper tree on every post-hydration render; the `tree` must match the server tree for `useId`.

## Target API

```clojure
(defonce app-root (h/client-root))                            ;=> inert handle; no DOM at load
(h/render! app-root tree el)                                  ;=> nil; first call creates the Root (createRoot) and renders inside flushSync; later calls update the same Root
(h/render! app-root tree el {:hydrate? true :identifier-prefix "main"})  ;=> nil; first call hydrates (hydrateRoot, reporter, adoption window); later calls update — never a second hydration, opts on later calls ignored
(h/unmount! app-root)                                         ;=> nil; idempotent; in the adapter's active-root set, so rf/destroy-adapter! releases it exactly once
```

`opts` keys: `:hydrate?` (boolean; first call only) and `:identifier-prefix` (React's `identifierPrefix`, first call only — it is a `createRoot` / `hydrateRoot` option and belongs on the root call on every React adapter). `tree` is Hicasso hiccup whose root is `[h/frame-root …]` or `[h/frame-provider …]` (views.3). The handle is opaque; the raw Root is reachable through nothing. Liveness is read off the active-root set (the rf2-k5r9t rule, `spine.cljs:3786-3791`), never kept in the handle. Hicasso keeps its own implementation behind the grammar: `impl.mount/root!` / `hydrate-root!` / `render!` / `unmount!` stay as the impl tier (the test kit's `catching-root!` drives `root!` directly — keep a positional impl constructor for it), the adoption-window Fragment still rides every post-hydration render, `flushSync` still wraps updates, and the hydration reporter still installs on the hydrate path only. `h/render!` returning nil (not the handle) matches the Reagent trio; the hmr testbed's `(h/render! handle …)` call needs no return value.

Before / after, the Hicasso boot (after views.3 + this bead):

```clojure
;; before — login/core.cljs:255-299 (post-views.3 shape)
(defonce !root (atom nil))
(defn ^:dev/after-load re-render! [] (when-some [r @!root] (rf.hicasso/render! r [root-view])))
(defn run []
  (rf/init! rf.hicasso.substrate/adapter)
  (let [payload (rf.ssr/read-server-payload) opts {:identifier-prefix identifier-prefix}]
    (if (some? payload)
      (do (rf.ssr/hydrate! {:frame frame-id :payload payload})
          (reset! !root (rf.hicasso/hydrate! el opts [h/frame-provider {:frame frame-id} [root-view]])))
      (reset! !root (rf.hicasso/mount! el opts [h/frame-root (merge {:id frame-id} model/frame-config) [root-view]])))))

;; after — the same file every Reagent and UIx example has
(defonce app-root (rf.hicasso/client-root))
(defn ^:dev/after-load mount! []
  (let [payload (rf.ssr/read-server-payload)]
    (when payload (rf.ssr/hydrate! {:frame frame-id :payload payload}))
    (rf.hicasso/render! app-root
      (if payload
        [h/frame-provider {:frame frame-id} [root-view]]
        [h/frame-root (merge {:id frame-id} model/frame-config) [root-view]])
      el {:hydrate? (some? payload) :identifier-prefix identifier-prefix})))
(defn run [] (rf/init! rf.hicasso.substrate/adapter) (mount!))
```

(`rf.ssr/hydrate!` is idempotent on a reload with a payload still in the document; if it is not, guard it with a `defonce` flag — verify, don't assume.)

## Corroboration

Two-reviewer (fable README: "one root-handle grammar across the React adapters with hydration as a first-render mode … keep the `render!` name"). Codex: "Hicasso can share the public handle grammar without sharing its collector internals … A shared public handle can retain these substrate-specific implementations; replacing them with a generic `.render` path cannot." — so the impl stays Hicasso's. Codex's synthesis §Corrections: "Consistent root names do not make lifecycle differences disappear … preserve their semantics while adopting one handle grammar." Grok: "optional Hicasso mount reshape onto the trio, joining the adapter active-root set so `destroy-adapter!` releases those roots" — ranked after ENSURE/SCOPE (views.3), which is why this bead is sequenced second.

## Deletion list

- `re-frame.hicasso/mount!` and `re-frame.hicasso/hydrate!` (facade vars; manifest rows 218, 219; docs/api sections; api-reference rows :121-122 and §"not symmetric" if any of it survived views.3); the `(handle view)` shape of `h/render!` (becomes `(handle tree el [opts])`); the caller-owned `(atom nil)` around the handle in the example and testbeds; the `re-render!` / `reload!` hot-reload wrappers that only existed because `mount!` and `render!` were different verbs (`00-installation.md:391` §Hot reload teaches the new shape: one `^:dev/after-load mount!` calling `render!`).
- `docs/core/hicasso/api-reference.md:600` (`h/hydrate-root!` → `h/hydrate!` rename row) becomes history: append the second rename to the same row rather than deleting it.

## Consumers to migrate (counts at tip)

- examples: `examples/substrates/hicasso/login/core.cljs` (1) + README (:76-96).
- testbeds: `hicasso_testbed/core.cljs:884-890`, `hicasso_hmr_testbed/core.cljs:33,355,454` (its multi-root-per-frame loop becomes one `client-root` per container).
- tools: `tools/story/test/re_frame/story/ui/hicasso_substrate_dom_cljs_test.cljs:363,381` (1 file).
- implementation tests: facade callers of `h/mount!` / `h/hydrate!` / `h/render!` — re-measure and separate from `hm/*` (test kit) callers as in views.3; `public_root_lifecycle_dom_cljs_test.cljs` (21 matches) is the natural home for the trio's own witnesses.
- test kit: `implementation/hicasso/test_kit/src/re_frame/hicasso/test/mounted.cljs` keeps `hm/mount!` / `hm/rerender!` / `hm/unmount!` (they drive `impl.mount/root!`); only re-point if the impl signature you keep changes.

- docs: 10 guide pages (`00-installation` §Mount a first screen :210, §What `h/mount!` creates :281, §More than one root :348-390, §Hot reload :391; `18-ssr-and-hydration` :75,:148,:274-280,:329,:412-422; `api-reference` :118-181,:390,:600; `cookbook` :506-566; `glossary`; `07`, `09`, `13`, `17`, `20-migration`), `docs/api/re-frame.hicasso.md:125-160`, `docs/core/how-to/boot-and-mount-an-app.md:20-30` (now literally "boot the same way"), `docs/ssr/concepts.md:550` if it shows the Hicasso mount. HD-021 / naming-ledger rows 13 and 20: a second dated supersession note.

## Sequencing and hot-zone

BLOCKED BY views.3 (the frame must already be in the tree, or `render!` would need a Hicasso-only `:frame` root opt, which is exactly the divergence this bead removes). Sequence after views.1 so the three adapters' `render!` opts are settled in one shape (`:hydrate?` first-call mode; `:identifier-prefix` as a root option — add it to the Reagent/UIx `render!` opts too if the ratom spine does not already thread it, so the grammar is one). Hot-zone: `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md`, `spec/002-Frames.md`.

## Risks

Medium, on a two-week-old surface (rf2-7mtcf, PR #8291, ~70 guide mentions) — pre-alpha is the cheap moment, and the doc surface is one guide tree. Behavioural obligations to witness (codex's list): hydration followed by a rerender without remount (the adoption Fragment on every post-hydration render — `mount.cljs:62-67`); matching `:identifier-prefix` between `server/render` and the hydrating `render!`; hot reload preserving DOM and component state (the `render!` update path reconciles the same Root — never `createRoot` twice); adapter destruction releasing owned roots exactly once and a later `render!` mounting afresh; two roots sharing one frame; a Hicasso story under a Reagent adapter. `h/render!`'s synchronous `flushSync` commit is a Hicasso guarantee the guide's witnesses read on the next line — keep it. If the handle grammar cannot carry the adoption window without changing the tree shape the server emits, STOP and report; HS-11 parity is not negotiable.

title: dev:example advertises a live SPA before the first watch build exists
description:
## Scope

Make the default `npm run dev:example -- <build-id>` watch path advertise a runnable SPA only after that run's first browser bundle exists. Keep the current manifest-derived build selection, clean staging, shadow-cljs watch, loopback http-server, ownership-token handshake, and test-free examples policy. The synchronous `--no-watch` path is already ordered correctly and should remain so.

## Finding

The runner announces that an example "is live" after proving only that http-server owns the selected output directory. In the default watch path it has deliberately deleted the previous `main.js`, starts `shadow-cljs watch` asynchronously, and never waits for the first successful compile before printing the URL. On a cold or otherwise slower compile, the printed page therefore serves its host and shared assets while its required `main.js` is still absent. Opening it in that interval requests a missing script and leaves a blank/non-booted app. Because no bundle loaded, no shadow client is present to turn the later compile into recovery; the programmer has to notice the compiler finished and manually reload.

This is a small but high-leverage ergonomics defect in the catalogue's canonical one-command front door. The command's strongest status line says the SPA is live when only the static server is live.

## Independently established evidence

- `examples/scripts/serve-example.cjs:186-202` applies the correct clean-stage boundary and removes the selected output directory, including every prior `main.js`.
- The runner itself records the consequence at `serve-example.cjs:204-210`: in watch mode the cleaned directory has no `main.js` until the first compile lands.
- `serve-example.cjs:222-224` stages `index.html`, `_shared`, and declared static assets; it does not produce the compiled entrypoint.
- `serve-example.cjs:241-264` spawns `shadow-cljs watch` as a long-running asynchronous child. There is no first-build promise, emitted-file wait, or successful-compile signal in this path.
- `serve-example.cjs:275-286` then calls `startLocalHttpServer`; immediately after its `ready` result, lines 288-293 print `serve-example: <build> is live at ... (shadow-cljs watch running - edits recompile live)`.
- `implementation/scripts/lib/local-browser-harness.cjs:636-722` defines that readiness narrowly and correctly for its own purpose: publish and fetch `/.rf-harness-token` to prove the responder serves this run's root. It does not inspect or request `main.js`, so a clean staged root with only HTML/assets is `ready: true`.
- The current example inventory has 33 `index.html` / `*.index.html` host pages that load `<script src="main.js">`; `check-examples-assets.cjs` makes a live `main.js` script reference mandatory but exempts the generated file from source-tree existence checks. Thus host correctness depends on the compile product that server readiness does not cover.
- `examples/README.md:15-23` makes this runner the canonical command and says it "serves the result ... and prints the URL to open"; raw watch is explicitly contrasted with `dev:example` as compiler-only, while `dev:example` is the route to "the running app."
- The `--no-watch` branch at `serve-example.cjs:211-219` runs `shadow-cljs compile` synchronously and rejects nonzero status before staging/server startup, so the defect is confined to the default watch lifecycle.

No application, browser, build, or network operation was run during this review. The race follows from the explicit process ordering. Whether a particular warm-cache launch exposes it depends on scheduling; the cold/slow-compile case is the material witness to add.

## History and why existing coverage misses it

- Commit `a4636f853f` introduced the one-command runner with the current asynchronous watch-before-server shape.
- Commit `1d62730eb1` (`rf2-rg2tze`) fixed a worse stale-output false green by cleaning first. Its commit message and current comments explicitly say `main.js` is now visibly absent until the first compile. That is the right stale-file policy, but it exposes the remaining readiness mismatch rather than resolving it.
- Commit `3686d3ffd0` (`rf2-35lfqo`) made unexpected child failures nonzero; it does not establish first-build success while a healthy watcher is compiling or waiting after a compile error.
- Commit `0b438394dc` centralized local-server readiness around an ownership token. That helper is behaving as designed: server ownership and application-build readiness are different facts. The example runner is the layer that must compose them.
- `implementation/scripts/_examples-staging.test.cjs:411-481` proves stale `main.js` removal and call order. Its lifecycle tests cover child exit classification, not the interval between server readiness and first output. The static asset tests prove the host references `main.js`, not that the dev runner waits until it is served.

## Recommended bounded fix

Keep the existing architecture. In watch mode, distinguish two states in the runner:

1. The local server owns the staged root, but the first build is still pending. If this state is logged at all, call it "waiting for initial build," not live/openable.
2. The current run's `main.js` is present, non-empty, and retrievable from the owned server while the watch child remains alive. Only then print the existing live URL/status.

A small runner-local wait/predicate is sufficient. It may poll the selected output plus the already-owned loopback server; do not parse shadow-cljs's human log format. While waiting, retain the current long-running development behavior: a compile error may be fixed by editing source, and Ctrl+C still tears down the process tree. An unexpected watch exit must abort the wait and remain nonzero.

## Acceptance criteria

- With a fake/delayed watch child and an initially clean output directory, the runner does not emit its `is live`/open-this-URL signal while `main.js` is absent, zero-length, or not served successfully.
- When that same child publishes a valid non-empty `main.js`, the runner emits the live URL once and continues watching/serving as today.
- If the watch child exits before first-build readiness, the runner does not announce the app as live, tears down the server, and exits nonzero with a direct initial-build diagnostic.
- A compile error from a still-running watcher does not require restarting the runner: after the programmer fixes source and the first successful output lands, the URL becomes live.
- The existing ownership-token handshake remains the authority for "this server serves this run's root"; first-build readiness is composed in `serve-example`, not generalized into every local-browser harness consumer.
- `--no-watch` still compiles once before server startup and reports compile failure nonzero. `--list`, build-id normalization, staging, per-example assets, free-port selection, reload caching policy, and cleanup remain unchanged.
- Add focused script-level coverage for delayed artifact, successful first publication, and watch-before-build failure. Demonstrate the new check failing against the current ordering, then run the existing examples staging/script tests.

## Non-goals

- No new launcher, build registry, dev server, compiler wrapper, or shadow-cljs protocol.
- No parsing of compiler console text and no dependence on a particular shadow-cljs log phrase.
- No browser auto-open, page-level smoke for every example, HMR redesign, service worker, retry UI, or generalized file-watching abstraction.
- No change to example application code, public re-frame2 APIs, shared visual assets, or the test-free `examples/` policy.
- No attempt to make every later recompile atomic; this issue owns only the first truthful runnable status after a clean launch.

## Duplicate distinctions

Targeted all-status searches of `.beads/issues.jsonl` covered `serve-example`, `dev:example`, `initial compile`, `first compile`, `main.js` with live/ready/404/blank, and frozen bundle; no bead owns first-build readiness.

- Historical `rf2-rg2tze` removes stale output and intentionally leaves `main.js` absent until the first compile; this finding is the remaining live-status/readiness seam.
- Closed `rf2-iacw2` and `rf2-ujdn0` correct documentation so programmers invoke `dev:example`; they do not change when that command's URL becomes runnable.
- Closed `rf2-y1kbf` requires host HTML to contain a live `<script src="main.js">`; it does not verify the generated script exists at launch time.
- Historical `rf2-35lfqo` handles watcher/server crashes. A healthy but not-yet-successful first compile is not a child-exit outcome.
- The shared ownership-token work (`rf2-slapfs`) prevents a foreign server false green and should not be broadened; it cannot prove application artifacts by design.

## Uncertainty

No cold compile was launched under the review's no-runtime constraint, so the exact user-visible duration is cache and machine dependent. A sufficiently fast warm build can land before http-server readiness and hide the race. The unsynchronized state is nevertheless explicit in source and guaranteed to be reachable whenever initial compilation takes longer than server startup. The implementer should capture that case deterministically with a fake delayed producer rather than relying on machine timing.
notes:
Merged-PR audit 2026-09-05: the readiness probe itself is sound, but the actual child-exit wiring misses a required liveness branch. The watch exit handler sets watchDied and tears down the server only when the watcher exits non-zero (or by an unexpected signal). If the long-running watcher exits with code 0 before publishing main.js, the server remains alive, isAborted stays false, and waitForFirstBuild polls forever. That directly contradicts this issue's acceptance criterion that any watch-child exit before readiness must tear down and exit non-zero.

The new unit witness injects watchDied=true directly, so it does not exercise the handler's code-0 classification; the source-order pins do not cover it either. Bounded repair: before first-build readiness, treat every watcher termination not caused by the runner's own interrupt as terminal, stop the server, and return the direct initial-build failure. Add a handler-level or fake-runner regression for a code-0 watcher exit before publication. Keep the runner-local architecture and unbounded wait for a watcher that is still alive.
Delivery 2026-09-05 (PR #9282, https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9282): the audit's bounded repair is implemented. The watch exit handler no longer carries its own classification; it delegates whole to a new pure, exported watchExitAbortsRun(code, signal, interrupted, firstBuildReady) shaped like the decideRunnerExit beside it. Before first-build readiness EVERY watcher termination the runner did not itself ask for is terminal, a clean code-0 exit included — abort the wait, tear the server down, print a direct initial-build diagnostic naming the entrypoint, exit non-zero. After readiness only an unexpected termination tears down, so the bound the audit set is kept. A firstBuildReady flag is set only after waitForFirstBuild proves the bundle is served, and that ordering is pinned.

The wait stays UNBOUNDED for a healthy watcher, per this note's own instruction; the dispatch brief had asked for a wall-clock timeout and the bead governed. The bound is on watcher liveness rather than the clock, which is the failure mode a timeout was reaching for.

Coverage: five new witnesses in implementation/scripts/_examples-staging.test.cjs — the code-0-before-readiness case alone, an all-outcomes pre-readiness sweep, the after-readiness contrast, the interrupt case in both phases, and a fake-watcher composition driving waitForFirstBuild through the real predicate; plus a source pin that the handler delegates and that the pre-audit inline test is gone. The fake-watcher case carries a probe ceiling ON PURPOSE: the regression's signature is an unbounded poll, so an unbounded witness reproduces it as a HANG rather than a report — measured, the planted pre-audit classification spun the suite past a 300s ceiling with no exit file. Bounded, the same plant gives captured exit 1 and 4 FAILED promptly.

Real runs (examples/counter, cold output dir): cold start printed the waiting line at t+4s with main.js absent and 'is live' at t+88s with a 32MB bundle present — an 84-second window the pre-fix runner advertised as live. A planted reader error left the runner waiting and honest with zero 'is live' lines across 180s while shadow-cljs reported the error for in-place fixing. Killing the watch child mid-wait produced the new diagnostic, the teardown, 'the first build never produced a served main.js', and exit code 1 within two seconds. The code-0 discrimination specifically is carried by the sabotage-verified unit witnesses, not by a real run: shadow-cljs watch cannot be made to exit 0 on demand and the only injection point would be production machinery existing purely for a test.

Gates, captured exits, all 0: examples-staging suite (41 PASS, post-rebase); npm run test:scripts (123/123); the six serve-example-adjacent suites; check_require_alias_dialect.py (2794 files, 10867 edges, every surface at or under floor, post-rebase); check_view_lifetime_residue.py (post-rebase, and separately proved to read this worktree — a planted line returned exit 1 naming file and line); check_readme_links.py --ci; check-examples-assets.cjs (33 pages); check-examples-compile.cjs --list (58 builds). Surfaces armed: cljs_node_test, cljs_browser, examples_compile, cljs_prod, bundle_isolation, reagent_slim_bundle.

Not changed, deliberately: local-browser-harness.cjs (the ownership-token handshake keeps its own meaning and is not in the diff); the --no-watch path; examples/README.md (checked at tip — it already describes the wait accurately, so this change does not make it wrong); no *.spec.cjs under examples/ (rf2-8cevm holds).

Note for a reader of the description above: its line citations describe the PRE-FIX file and no longer resolve at tip. The harness citation 636-722 still holds. And implementation/scripts/check-examples-assets.cjs does not exist — the gate is examples/scripts/check-examples-assets.cjs.
