title: surface-review(examples-real-apps): make offline Conduit writes survive the refetch they cause
description:
## Scope

Make both RealWorld examples honest end-to-end offline SPAs by turning the existing shared in-process Conduit demo backend into a small deterministic stateful model for the API routes the apps already use. Cover `examples/real-apps/realworld_shared/demo_backend.cljs`, the two thin app-local managed-HTTP override seams, the external RealWorld test wrappers, and the two READMEs where they describe offline behavior. Keep the managed-HTTP and Resources application architectures separate and directly readable; the shared backend remains the only comparison seam.

## Findings

The applications themselves exercise a credible breadth of SPA composition: boot and frame scope, URL-owned routing and guards, auth/session restore, schemas, machines, flows, managed HTTP, resources/mutations, pagination, optimistic writes, comments, profiles, settings, editor navigation, and SSR payload policy. They compile as standalone builds and have large headless integration wrappers outside the test-free examples tree.

The production demo backend does not preserve any write. `payload-for-request` is a one-request lookup over immutable `articles`, `favorited`, and `user` values. POST/PUT/DELETE branches manufacture valid response envelopes but never produce a new backend state. Subsequent GETs always read the seed corpus:

- create returns a derived slug but never inserts it; GET of an unknown slug silently falls back to the first article, so create-then-navigate can render `hello-conduit` at the new URL;
- update and delete do not change later detail or list reads;
- post-comment returns a random-id comment while GET comments is always `[]`, and delete changes nothing;
- favorite/unfavorite echo the requested flag but later article/list reads use the original articles and the Favorited tab is a fixed `take-nth` subset;
- follow/unfollow echo a flag but later profile reads always return `following false`, while the feed is permanently empty;
- settings PUT returns the original static user, and tag/author list query params do not filter the corpus.

This is most damaging in the Resources sibling because its headline is the automatic `read -> write -> invalidate -> refetch` loop. Post-comment deliberately does not populate a partial list; it invalidates comments and trusts the refetch as authoritative. The shipped offline backend answers that refetch with `[]`, so a successful comment disappears. Favorite explicitly refetches lists/feed "to truth", but the backend's truth is the pre-write seed. Fixing the client to suppress those refetches would hide the evidence rather than repair it.

The test surface misses the contradiction. `realworld_shared_backend_cljs_test.cljs` calls the pure router once per assertion and checks envelope shape, never write-then-read state. The resources integration wrapper replaces `:rf.http/managed` with a request-capture function and manually supplies every reply; its comment test asserts that a refetch starts but never settles that refetch from the production demo backend. The HTTP wrapper likewise installs bespoke canned stubs. Compile coverage proves buildability, not this user journey, and no current example wrapper mounts the DOM.

History explains the false confidence. Commit `02e6630851` consolidated two drifting fake backends and correctly fixed request routing and response envelopes, but its claim that create/update/delete/favorite/follow/settings "now actually work" was only pinned one request at a time. The shared backend is the right ownership boundary; it needs temporal semantics, not another copy or another abstraction.

## Recommended Action

Keep one shared backend, but express it as ordinary pure data plus one pure transition: seeded backend state + managed-request args -> next state + success/failure reply. Let each launched demo own an explicit, resettable instance of that state and keep `respond` as the thin adapter into the existing canned-success/canned-failure effects and 20 ms deferred reply path. Use deterministic counters/timestamps instead of `rand-int`, and make test/app reset boundaries explicit so hot reload, a fresh mount, and separate frames/tests cannot inherit accidental state.

Implement only the Conduit subset already called by these apps: login/session restore/settings, article CRUD, comments, favorite membership/counts, follow relationships/feed, profiles, tags, current-state list filtering, and limit/offset pagination. Missing article/comment routes should return an explicit Conduit-shaped 4xx failure rather than a plausible first record. Preserve the existing wire schemas, classification, bearer interceptor, frame routing, and offline/no-network default.

Replace the backend's one-shot contract tests with sequential transition tests, then add a focused full-frame receipt for each app-local fx seam using the production demo backend rather than a bespoke canned reply. The Resources receipt should prove a real mutation settles, invalidates, automatically refetches, and leaves the resource at the new server truth. The managed-HTTP receipt should perform the corresponding write and later load through its normal public events. Keep all tests outside `examples/` per repository policy.

Refresh the README claims and give readers one short try-it journey whose result survives refetch/navigation. Do not turn the backend into an example framework; the simple state transition is part of this example's evidence.

## Evidence

- `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/README.md:3,11-13` calls this a complete working blog and names `read -> write -> invalidate -> refetch` as the one idea the example exists to prove.
- `examples/real-apps/realworld_shared/demo_backend.cljs:106-126` defines immutable article/favorite/user data and makes unknown slugs fall back to the first article.
- `examples/real-apps/realworld_shared/demo_backend.cljs:128-134` uses `rand-int` for comment IDs; the same file's POST branches at 190-237 return envelopes without updating any store.
- `examples/real-apps/realworld_shared/demo_backend.cljs:239-255` makes feed/comments fixed empty responses, serves Favorited from a static subset, sends tag/author queries through the full article vector, and always reads profiles as not-following.
- `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/mutations.cljs:163-202` says favorite reconciliation refetches lists/feed to truth; lines 243-271 intentionally make comment writes invalidate and refetch rather than populate a partial collection.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_resources_cljs_test.cljs:90-98,183-186` replaces the live transport with request capture. Its comment case at 1264-1300 hand-injects the write reply and only asserts that refetch began.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_shared_backend_cljs_test.cljs:20-31` explicitly treats the backend as a pure URL/method-to-payload function. Lines 88-139 assert isolated favorite/comment/list envelopes, not any later read.
- `examples/TESTING.md:5,18-23` records the test-free source-tree policy, external headless wrappers, and the distinction between compile coverage and browser behavior.
- Commit `02e6630851` is the backend's entire path history: it centralized the correct seam and added one-shot shape tests, but no state sequence.
- Full title/description searches across open and closed beads for demo/stateful/offline backend, `payload-for-request`, write persistence, mutation refetch, comment disappearance, and favorite reversion found no matching task.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The offline backend has a deterministic seeded state and one canonical transition used by both app-local fx ids; identical fresh-state request sequences produce identical replies and state in both variants.
- Article create -> GET-by-new-slug/list/author-filter, update -> later GET, and delete -> later GET/list are covered sequentially. Unknown/deleted slugs fail explicitly and never return the first seed article.
- Comment POST -> GET includes the exact saved comment and deterministic id; DELETE -> GET removes it. A Resources full-frame test uses the real demo fx and proves the invalidation-triggered comments refetch settles with that new collection.
- Favorite/unfavorite persist through detail, global/tag/author lists, and the acting user's Favorited list with correct counts. Follow/unfollow persist through profile reads and affect the demo feed consistently. Settings changes survive later user/profile reads, and a saved valid demo token can restore the session while invalid/missing credentials fail predictably.
- Tag, author, favorited, feed, limit, and offset query semantics are applied to current backend state, and each `articlesCount` describes the filtered set rather than the seed corpus or page size.
- Backend instances/reset are explicit and isolated for fresh launches and tests; generated values are deterministic; no raw timer replaces the existing `:dispatch-later`-backed canned reply path.
- At least one automated full-frame path per app variant uses its production demo override rather than a bespoke response stub and proves a write remains observable after a later normal read. Tests remain outside `examples/` and include a negative control that fails if the transition result is discarded or reads consult the seed constants.
- Both RealWorld builds compile warning-free, the focused CLJS suites pass, and README claims/try-it steps describe only behavior the served offline apps now retain across refetch and navigation.

## Non-goals

- No full Conduit server, database, network listener, service worker, persistence across browser reload beyond the existing demo-token contract, multi-user authorization system, or production backend replacement.
- No generic mock-server library, request-fixture DSL, compatibility layer, generated client, example framework, or new framework runtime API.
- No sharing of routes, handlers, subscriptions, views, app-db slices, or feature namespaces between the managed-HTTP and Resources variants; their architectural comparison stays explicit.
- No weakening/bypassing resource invalidation, pinning stale optimistic data, or changing cache semantics to accommodate a stateless backend.
- No broad visual redesign, route-id rename, source-layout reorganization, or exhaustive per-page browser suite.
- No duplicate `dev:example` launch-command standardization; the adjacent examples-core/capabilities tasks own that documentation family and this task is about temporal app behavior.

## Related beads

- `rf2-y8jjk` (open) makes active-route resource replanning authoritative; it is complementary. That task repairs which reads are planned after identity changes, while this task makes the backend truth those reads receive reflect prior writes.
- `rf2-8cevm` (closed) established the test-free examples policy; sequential and full-frame receipts stay in the external adapter test tree.
- `rf2-czvc` (closed) fixed RealWorld editor settle races through external production-source wrappers; it is the precedent for testing a real example flow rather than a copied miniature.
- `rf2-0vav5.1` (closed) supplies derived compile coverage for every declared example build; compile remains necessary but cannot prove write/read causality.
- `rf2-iacw2` and `rf2-ujdn0` (open) standardize one-command launch documentation for adjacent example families; they do not cover backend state or this outcome.

TRIAGE 2026-08-31 00:56:58 AUSEST (read-only agent at 5d35356469): premises HOLD (demo_backend.cljs has zero atom/swap!; :125-126, :129, :190-237, :242-255 as cited; seams at realworld_http/http.cljs:209 and realworld_resources/http.cljs:98). Negative control: one deftest that mutates, then asserts the seed vector is unchanged AND the read differs. Do not touch auth.cljs / routing.cljs (y8jjk files). A is DISPATCHABLE now.
CROSS-REFERENCE 2026-09-02 10:28:56 AUSEST (rf2-y8jjk ruling, delegated by Mike): rf2-y8jjk is RULED — APPROVED as [:rf.route/replan-resources {:cause <edn>}], banner struck, now dispatchable — so the part B this close reason parked ('the two full-frame production-seam receipts in realworld_resources_cljs_test.cljs') is no longer waiting on a ruling. The shared demo backend is now a seeded state value plus one pure transition ((transition state args-map) -> [next-state reply]); respond is unchanged as the thin adapter into :rf.http/managed-canned-success / -failure with :after-ms, so the 20 ms reply still rides :dispatch-later and no raw timer was introduced. Each app seam holds its own defonce'd instance, so the two demos never share a world and fresh-state is the explicit reset boundary. The architectures stay separate: the backend is still the only seam, and nothing moved across it.

HOW THE WRITE-SURVIVES-REFETCH BEHAVIOUR WAS DEMONSTRATED (a compile pass is not that proof):

1. Sequential tests, not shape assertions. The one-shot contract suite in implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_shared_backend_cljs_test.cljs is replaced by 15 tests / 115 assertions that each WRITE and then READ BACK through a separate, normal request. The headline test posts a comment and asserts the exact saved comment (id, body, timestamps) is in the collection the next GET returns, and favourites an article and asserts the detail read AND the global list read both still say favourited with the count the write produced -- the two reads that used to revert it. Also covered sequentially: create -> GET-by-new-slug/list/author-filter/tags, update -> later GET, delete -> later GET/list with the deleted slug 404ing, comment DELETE -> GET, favourite through detail/global/tag/author/Favorited-tab with counts, follow -> profile read + feed, settings -> later user/profile reads including a username change moving the byline, and session restore succeeding only for a token that world issued.

Both app fx ids call this one transition, so pinning it pins both.

5. Every reply is Malli-validated against the shared wire schemas, since the canned-success fx never runs :decode and nothing else would catch drift off the Conduit contract.

title: surface-review(testbed-support): retire checkout-root plumbing now the endpoint resolves source files
description:
## Scope

Retire the repository-internal browser-side checkout-root pipeline from `tools/testbed-support/**` and its direct Xray, Story, example, launcher, Shadow, and documentation consumers. Make the already-wired JVM `POST /__rf-open-in-editor` endpoint the one source-file resolver for repository-owned dev testbeds, and return `re-frame.testbed.story-host` to its single job: live-app / Story-shell React-root handoff and hash routing.

Keep the generic public `:rf.story/project-root` / `:rf.xray/project-root` options and the client URI fallback available to external/non-shadow hosts. This is a removal of redundant repository testbed setup, not a redesign of the shipped open-in-editor contract.

## Findings

1. The surface carries two complete paths for the same repository dev workflow. `re-frame.testbed.config` derives an absolute source root in the browser from `RF2_TESTBED_PROJECT_ROOT` or `?checkout-root=`, while `re-frame.testbed.open-in-editor-server` resolves the original relative coordinate against the live JVM classpath at request time. The endpoint is already attached to every dev-http port used by all twelve builds that seed the checkout-root define.
2. The older path makes each new testbed coordinate the same fact in several places: a literal source subdirectory in the CLJS consumer, a per-build Closure define in `shadow-cljs.edn`, the launcher environment export, and related docs/tests. Current consumers repeat seven Xray resolver/configure calls and five Story `:source-subdir` calls even though endpoint resolution needs none of them.
3. The cost is material for a private helper. `config.cljs` is 97 lines and its 41-test suite is 519 lines: 616 of `tools/testbed-support`'s 2,346 tracked lines (26%), before counting Story-host option tests, twelve Closure-define blocks, launcher/static-export checks, and prose across twenty tracked reference files.
4. No live caller was found for the query escape hatch. Repository-wide tracked searches for `checkout-root` find only the resolver, tests, configuration, and explanatory prose; no script emits a `?checkout-root=` URL and no runtime outside this internal support path reads it.
5. This is not a compatibility surface. `tools/testbed-support/deps.edn` and the README explicitly say the tool is dev-only and not published, and `spec/api-manifest.edn` / `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn` contain no `re-frame.testbed.*` row. The private two-arity Story-host option can be deleted rather than shimmed.
6. History explains the overlap. Commit `3b4aed8b4e` (`rf2-5dphw`, 2026-05-31) introduced browser checkout-root plumbing to replace hardcoded personal paths; commit `bc895415b8` (`rf2-wn3bh`, 2026-06-14) later added the zero-config runtime endpoint and wired every testbed port, but did not retire the first mechanism. Five later commits still touched the config source/tests, including malformed-override repair, while endpoint behavior was unaffected.
7. The endpoint suite already owns classpath resolution, cwd fallback, query handling, launch behavior, JSON, and the loopback/method/origin boundary. The useful missing proof is consumer-shaped: real relative Story and Xray coordinates should resolve through that endpoint with both tool project-root atoms unset.

## Recommended Action

- Delete `re-frame.testbed.config` and `config_cljs_test.cljs` outright.
- Remove source-root configuration from `re-frame.testbed.story-host`; keep one `mount-with-hash-routing!` call shape taking only the live root view, and migrate all repository consumers to it without an alias or compatibility arity.
- Remove testbed-only `resolve-source-root` helpers and `xray-config/configure! {:rf.xray/project-root ...}` boot writes from the seven Xray consumers.
- Stop `implementation/scripts/dev-testbed.cjs` from deriving/exporting `RF2_TESTBED_PROJECT_ROOT`, and remove the twelve matching Closure defines plus now-vacuous static-export sentinel checks/prose. Preserve the launcher's explicit-build, de-duplication, process, and URL-printing behavior.
- Keep every affected dev-http entry wired to `re-frame.testbed.open-in-editor-server/handler`. Add one bounded consumer-shaped witness using representative real Story and Xray relative coordinates, with launch stubbed so no editor opens.
- Rewrite the support README around the two remaining responsibilities and show the minimal new-testbed path: wire the handler, call the one-arity host when Story routing is needed, and launch the build. Do not introduce a replacement config layer.

## Evidence

- `tools/testbed-support/src/re_frame/testbed/config.cljs`: 97-line query/define/path resolver whose only public operation is `resolve-source-root`.
- `tools/testbed-support/test/re_frame/testbed/config_cljs_test.cljs`: 519 lines / 41 tests, including private parser and slash-normalisation contracts.
- `tools/testbed-support/src/re_frame/testbed/story_host.cljs:52-77`: optional `:source-subdir` exists only to invoke the config resolver before mounting.
- `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:479-628`: fourteen dev-http entries already use the JVM endpoint handler; lines 1317-1958 separately repeat twelve checkout-root Closure defines for the affected builds.
- `implementation/scripts/dev-testbed.cjs:7-18,261-283`: the launcher exports the root solely for that define; its independently useful build/URL manifest does not need the value.
- `tools/xray/testbeds/{two_frame_isolation,standard_epochs,routes_epochs,machine_epochs,edn_inspector,managed_http,panel_gallery}/core.cljs`: seven identical resolver/configuration gestures.
- `tools/story/testbeds/{counter_with_stories,login_form,hicasso_counter}/core.cljs` and the login/nine-states example hosts: five literal `:source-subdir` options.
- `tools/testbed-support/test/re_frame/testbed/open_in_editor_server_test.clj:17-54`: the server already proves relative classpath files resolve to real on-disk paths; the remainder covers the endpoint boundary and launch result shapes.
- `spec/Tool-Pair.md` open-in-editor launch modes: the endpoint is the preferred zero-config runtime resolver; project-root composition belongs to the generic URI fallback.
- `tools/testbed-support/deps.edn` plus the absent API-manifest rows: local dev/test support, not a published facade.
- Exact current/closed tracker title searches and issue-record scans for testbed-support, checkout-root, `RF2_TESTBED_PROJECT_ROOT`, `resolve-source-root`, source-root resolver, and open-in-editor endpoint found no outcome bead owning this retirement.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. No tracked source, build config, script, test, or current documentation references `re-frame.testbed.config`, `RF2_TESTBED_PROJECT_ROOT`, `?checkout-root=`, or the deleted checkout-root Closure define. The config namespace and its dedicated test namespace are gone.
2. `mount-with-hash-routing!` has one repository-internal call shape and owns only listener/root handoff plus hash selection. All Story/example consumers call it without source-root options; all Xray testbeds boot without testbed-support project-root resolution.
3. `npm run dev -- <build-id>` retains explicit build forwarding, order-preserving de-duplication, URL reporting, cwd, signal, and exit semantics, but no longer computes or exports an absolute checkout path.
4. All twelve formerly seeded builds remain served by dev-http entries using `re-frame.testbed.open-in-editor-server/handler`. With Story and Xray project-root config unset, one real relative Story coordinate and one real relative Xray coordinate reach the handler and resolve to the intended existing file; the test stubs `launch!` and proves the resolved argument without opening an editor.
5. The generic Story/Xray project-root configuration APIs, endpoint-preferred/URI-fallback client rule, endpoint path/query/method/security contract, and `launch-editor` behavior are unchanged. No public facade symbol or API-manifest row is added.
6. The focused testbed-support JVM, Node, and DOM suites plus the launcher/static-build checks pass after deleting the obsolete assertions. A negative witness demonstrates that removing the dev-http handler (not removing checkout-root plumbing) breaks the representative relative-coordinate path.
7. The README and direct consumer comments teach the endpoint-backed one-command workflow and contain no replacement root-discovery convention, generated manifest, compatibility note, or manual absolute-path recipe.

## Non-goals

- Redesigning the endpoint, its loopback security boundary, query grammar, process timeout/drain logic, editor vocabulary, or `launch-editor` dependency.
- Removing or changing the generic `:rf.story/project-root`, `:rf.xray/project-root`, custom editor URI, or URI fallback APIs for external/static/non-shadow hosts.
- Auto-discovering source roots, scanning namespaces, generating Shadow config, or creating a new testbed registry/config DSL.
- Adding a facade namespace, deprecated alias, compatibility arity, environment-variable fallback, warning, or migration mode for this unpublished helper.
- Refactoring unrelated frame boot, testbed application code, port allocation, build IDs, or the `DEV_HTTP` URL manifest.
- Enabling local-editor links in published static Story exports.

## Related beads

- `rf2-in6c4` (closed) owns compile-gate coverage for testbed builds; it does not own developer setup or source resolution.
- `rf2-7dewo` (open) owns Story variant vocabulary convergence; no overlap with Story-host mounting or open-in-editor setup.
- Historical commit-linked `rf2-5dphw` introduced the checkout-root path and `rf2-wn3bh` introduced the endpoint that superseded its repository-dev purpose; neither is present as a current tracker record.
- No matching open, in-progress, deferred, or closed outcome bead was found.

title: surface-review(examples-capabilities): make every capability README launch the real one-command app
description:
## Scope

Make the capabilities catalogue and all eight examples/capabilities/** README launch recipes copyable from a clean checkout. Cover machines/state_machine_walkthrough, routing/routing, resources/{resources,infinite_feed,linearlite}, ssr/{ssr,resources_ssr,ssr_streaming}, and the capabilities entry point in examples/README.md. Keep the existing examples and the existing runner; this is an executable-documentation correction, not a new example framework.

## Findings

- Every capability README still leads with raw "shadow-cljs watch examples/<id>" and then asks the reader to serve or open some combination of source and build output. The root catalogue makes the same blanket claim for every example.
- That is not a complete runnable recipe. Each source index.html references both main.js and _shared assets, while the browser builds emit main.js under implementation/out/examples/<id>. Seven of these examples have no dedicated dev-http root that composes those trees. Linearlite is the lone special case with a hard-coded 8044 dev-http entry, so its README works differently from every sibling.
- The repository already has the canonical solution: "npm run dev:example -- examples/<id>". The runner cleans the selected output, stages that example's real index.html and shared assets, starts watch/compile, serves loopback on a free port, and prints the exact URL.
- The runner derives its standalone-build list from implementation/shadow-cljs.edn. Its current --list output includes all eight capability build ids, and the independent compile gate derives and sweeps the same eight builds.
- History explains the drift. Commit a4636f853f (rf2-pdo5mx, 2026-06-09) introduced the one-command runner and migrated the then-UIx READMEs only. The concept-layout move in 210f812fe2 (2026-06-28) and later capability README rewrites retained the older recipes. The runtime code, mount idioms, and build declarations are already consistent; the learning front door is the stale part.

## Recommended Action

Replace each capability README's primary How to run recipe with the exact npm dev:example command for its declared build id, run from implementation/. Say that the command stages the page, watches it, selects a free local port, and prints the URL; for the three SSR examples, make explicit that the runner stages the checked-in baked SSR index rather than requiring the reader to manually combine it with the bundle. Remove the hard-coded Linearlite-only 8044 path from the primary flow.

Update examples/README.md so its generic launch instruction names the same runner. Raw shadow-cljs watch may remain only as an explicitly advanced compiler-only path that does not pretend to stage or serve a page. Reuse the runner and its manifest derivation as-is unless an actual failing capability build proves a small runner defect.

## Evidence

- examples/README.md:13 currently says any example runs with raw shadow-cljs watch.
- The eight stale commands are at state_machine_walkthrough/README.md:126, routing/README.md:89, resources/README.md:157, infinite_feed/README.md:161, linearlite/README.md:148, ssr/README.md:190, resources_ssr/README.md:171, and ssr_streaming/README.md:167.
- All eight index.html files reference main.js and _shared/css/style.css plus _shared/img/favicon.svg.
- implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1557-1784 declares all eight builds and emits each to implementation/out/examples/<id>; only the top-level dev-http map at lines 603-611 gives Linearlite a composed source/output server.

title: surface-review(hicasso): reduce the clj-kondo export to macro-shape analysis
description:
## Scope

Reduce Hicasso's shipped clj-kondo integration to the part that materially improves ordinary authoring: correct analysis of `h/defview`, `h/event`, and `h/defhost` as macro shapes. The scope is the export under `implementation/hicasso/resources/clj-kondo.exports/day8/re-frame2-hicasso/`, its fixtures/checker under `implementation/hicasso/`, the `test:hicasso-lint` scheduling references, and live package/user/example prose that promises the six custom findings.

Preserve the export's classpath/package delivery. Do not change Hicasso runtime semantics or the public authoring API.

## Findings

The useful editor contract and the accidental apparatus are currently fused in one 847-line hook. The three rewrites make normal clj-kondo analysis understand view names, destructured props, callback bindings/arity, and host option references. That is high-value, general-purpose assistance.

The other half is a bespoke behavioral linter: two custom errors and four custom warnings, plus Hiccup walkers, symbol resolution, a hand-maintained lexical-scope grammar, exact-row fixture matrices, and a mutation-testing gate. Across the hook, README, config, two fixtures, and checker this surface is 2,400 lines. It also owns a required CI lane and a fast-PR step.

That analyzer has already demonstrated the wrong maintenance shape for a trust-the-programmer library. The ERROR-level `direct-view-call` rule repeatedly blocked valid code because a hook has no scope table: parameters and `let` bindings, multi-arity `letfn`, six more binding forms, `areduce`/`amap`, and method-spec grammar each required repair. The same shadowing blindness then spread to the read warnings. The current hook documents a finite roster and still tells authors to rename a legal local or disable the rule for forms outside it.

The payoff remains intrinsically narrow. The direct-call check can see only a view calling itself, not the ordinary cross-view mistake. The function-head check can see literals, not symbols. The key rule deliberately misses the common dynamic-props spelling. The a11y rule cannot see tree-level naming. The deferred-read warning explicitly admits legal synchronous callbacks can trigger it. These limits are honest, but they mean substantial custom machinery protects a small, non-authoritative slice while the actual runtime, React, and Hicasso test kit already own the relevant behavior.

For a pre-alpha surface, carrying this analyzer is worse than teaching the small set of authoring laws clearly and keeping the real failures loud at their execution boundary. It increases contributor and AI context, creates a second grammar that must track Clojure/CLJS binding forms, and turns lint maintenance into product work without making the core SPA API more expressive.

## Recommended Action

Keep the published clj-kondo export, but reduce it to the shortest honest implementation of these three shapes:

- `defview` is analyzed as a definition with its one props vector and body;
- `event` is analyzed as a function with its argument vector and body;
- `defhost` defines its name and analyzes the component/options expressions.

Delete the six `:re-frame.hicasso/*` behavioral findings, their Hiccup/scope walkers, the positive/negative behavioral matrices, and the mutation framework built to keep that custom analyzer correct. Replace the dedicated behavioral gate with one small consumer smoke, preferably folded into an existing package/lint lane, that imports the export through the artifact classpath and proves ordinary clj-kondo analysis sees the three macro shapes. Remove stale live claims and scheduling apparatus. Do not replace the deleted checks with compiler analysis, cache-backed namespace analysis, a new warning framework, or a compatibility layer.

## Evidence

- Current measured surface: hook 847 lines; export README 236; config 46; positive fixture 245; negative fixture 542; checker 484 — 2,400 lines total.
- `hooks/re_frame/hicasso.clj:7-12` describes the valuable macro-shape job; `:14-25` introduces the separate six-finding engine. `config.edn:31-46` couples both jobs.
- The hand-built scope model occupies the `bound-symbols`/`locals-bound-by`/`self-call-nodes` path through `check-direct-view-call!`; its own comments say the binding roster is the price of having no scope table.
- `README.md:48-109` says `direct-view-call` cannot see another view, enumerates the finite binding roster, and asks authors using an unrecognized form to rename the local or switch the check off. `:125-175`, `:188-217`, and `:225-233` document similar blind spots for the warnings and other desired checks.
- `check_lint_export.py:273-455` is a mutation harness largely preserving regressions in that custom grammar. It is scheduled by `implementation/package.json:45`, `.github/workflows/lint.yml:464`, and `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh:1547-1548`.
- The repair history is concrete: `rf2-hic-022` was repeatedly reopened for valid-code false errors; `rf2-ka4d` records the finite binding roster and later method/array-macro defects; `rf2-c6t6` records the same shadowing defect in the read rules. Commits from 2026-08-10 through 2026-08-11 repeatedly repaired the hook before the API had a first tagged release.
- Authoritative downstream behavior remains: bad heads refuse in `impl/codec.cljs`; out-of-render reads refuse in `impl/collector.cljs`; boundary-crossing deferrals refuse in `impl/codec.cljs`; React reports general missing keys; `ht/unnamed-controls` performs tree-level accessibility inspection. Live user docs already teach the corresponding recovery routes.
- Active-bead searches for `clj-kondo`, `lint export`, `direct-view-call`, the hook path, and `check_lint_export.py` found no task owning this reduction. `rf2-6c12m` is the broad dead-weight epic, but none of its children targets this residual.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A consumer importing Hicasso's clj-kondo export from the artifact classpath gets correct ordinary analysis for all documented `defview`, `event`, and `defhost` declaration shapes, including optional docstrings and destructuring.
2. The shipped export defines no `:re-frame.hicasso/*` custom behavioral linters, calls no `api/reg-finding!`, and contains no bespoke Hiccup walker or lexical binding-form roster.
3. The six-finding positive/negative fixture matrices and their mutation machinery are removed. Any remaining gate is a compact packaging/macro-shape consumer smoke, not a second static analyzer.
4. Package scripts, required workflow/fast-PR scheduling, export README, core docs, and live example comments no longer promise or schedule the removed findings. Historical design records need not be rewritten merely to erase history.
5. The normal repository clj-kondo lane remains green on Hicasso code, and a negative control proves the macro-shape smoke fails when one of the three rewrites is unavailable.
6. Runtime behavior, runtime refusal contracts, React behavior, the test-kit accessibility surface, and Hicasso's public API are unchanged.
7. The resulting diff is a material net deletion with no replacement analyzer, compatibility shim, or new dependency.

## Non-goals

- Adding whole-program, cache-backed, compiler, or cross-namespace analysis.
- Recreating any removed finding at warning level or in another tool.
- Weakening or expanding runtime validation and diagnostics.
- Removing ordinary clj-kondo analysis or the artifact's exported macro configuration.
- Changing `defview`, `event`, `defhost`, Hiccup, routing, accessibility, or subscription semantics.
- Broad CI restructuring unrelated to retiring this dedicated behavioral gate.

## Related beads

- `rf2-6c12m` — active Hicasso dead-weight epic; this is a de-duplicated residual not owned by an existing child.
- `rf2-hic-022` — introduced the six bounded findings and records repeated false-ERROR reopenings.
- `rf2-ka4d` — repaired missing binding forms, array macros, and method grammar in `direct-view-call`.
- `rf2-c6t6` — repaired the same lexical-shadowing blindness in the read rules.
- `rf2-zzdg` — repaired drift in the dedicated lint workflow's mutation-count prose.

Triage note: keeping the npm script NAME test:hicasso-lint and its lint.yml step means lint.yml, test-fast-pr.sh and check_fast_pr_gap.py need no edit — hot-zone touch drops to zero; brief will say so. Also delete .clj-kondo/config.edn:49-56 per-namespace :off overrides for the retired findings.
Chronological merged-PR audit (#8808): the reduced macro-shape export is correct, but its shipped README overstates the replacement contract. It says every mistake seen by the six retired checks is now refused at execution with a named :rf.error/hicasso-* id. That is false for at least unkeyed mapped children (React warning), nameless interactive elements (test-kit/tree-level accessibility inspection), and parked reads (documented programmer judgment/undefined conduct); the bead's own evidence distinguishes those owners. Correct this one paragraph to name the split authority without restoring lint checks, changing runtime behavior, sweeping historical records, or adding a gate.

Audit residual fixed by PR #8823: the shipped README's replacement paragraph now names the split authority (runtime :rf.error/hicasso-* refusals for bad heads/out-of-render reads/boundary-crossing deferrals; React's missing-key warning for unkeyed mapped children; test-kit ht/unnamed-controls for nameless interactive elements; parked reads documented judgment, nothing polices). Gates on final base, captured exits: check_readme_links.py --ci exit 0 (planted broken link in the edited file went exit 1 naming file+line, restore blob-hash-verified); npm run test:hicasso-lint exit 0 (self-test PASS incl. behavioral-linter-rides-back-in negative control). No runtime change, no gate added.

title: surface-review(core): remove implementation-only constructors from re-frame.core
description:
## Scope

Make the `re-frame.core` facade expose the supported authoring surfaces, not the implementation-only lowering constructors behind them. Remove `re-frame.core/make-capture-frame`, `re-frame.core/->interceptor`, and `re-frame.core/->interceptor*` from the public facade; relocate or delete their lowering entry points as appropriate, and update the macro/runtime consumers that legitimately need them. Keep `re-frame.core/capture-frame` and `re-frame.core/reg-interceptor` as the app-facing paths.

## Independently verified Findings

- The accepted pre-alpha facade rule says internalising an export must remove it from the facade, manifest, and current API projection; a docstring saying “internal” while `:facade? true` remains is named as the precise failure mode (`spec/Conventions.md`, “Removing or demoting a facade export — delete, don't demote”).
- That exact failure is live. `make-capture-frame` and `->interceptor` are `:tier :implementation` plus `:facade? true`; `->interceptor*` is `:tier :advanced` plus `:facade? true` even though its status and docs say “internal lowering only”. All three appear in generated `docs/api/re-frame.core.md`.
- The exposure is plumbing, not an app capability. `reg-view` expands through `re-frame.core/make-capture-frame`; the interceptor macro expands through `re-frame.core/->interceptor*`; the owned runtime constructor already exists as `re-frame.interceptor/->interceptor*`. A compiler-visible Var need not live on the user facade.
- SCI copies every public runtime Var from `re-frame.core`, so the accidental surface is also presented to playground users and AI-generated examples.
- The earlier API-shrink commit `ca1fa564da` declared `capture-frame` the one public carry primitive but retiered `make-capture-frame` instead of removing it. The same repository conventions explicitly reject annotation as removal.
- The conventions say a public-facade manifest-hygiene CI check enforces this disposition, but `.github/workflows/lint.yml` records that the old check was retired. Current manifest generation accepts the contradictory rows, so the same drift can recur.

## Recommended Action

Move the capture-frame and interceptor lowering seams behind explicitly non-facade implementation namespaces (or delete a wrapper where the owning constructor already suffices). Repoint `reg-view` and interceptor macro expansion, internal/test consumers, and SCI bindings to those owned seams. Remove the three facade Vars and their manifest/API entries without compatibility aliases. Add a small generic manifest invariant that rejects implementation-only rows exported with `:facade? true`, so an internal docstring/status cannot masquerade as surface removal again.

## Evidence

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:1369` — `make-capture-frame` says it is internal and public only for macro expansion; `capture-frame` begins at line 1453.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:2137` — `->interceptor` says it is an internal lowering constructor and directs apps to `reg-interceptor`.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_reg_view_macro.cljc:187` — emitted code calls `re-frame.core/make-capture-frame`.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_call_site_macros.cljc:173-179` — emitted code calls `re-frame.core/->interceptor*`.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/interceptor.cljc:23` — the owned `->interceptor*` constructor already exists.
- `spec/api-manifest.edn:69-70,74,118` — the three internal constructors are facade rows beside the front-porch `capture-frame` row.
- `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:635-668` — metadata acknowledges the internal-only dispositions while retaining facade placement.
- `spec/Conventions.md:1235-1250` — pre-alpha delete-not-demote rule and its stated manifest guardrail.
- `spec/002-Frames.md:1471` — `capture-frame` is the one public carry primitive and `make-capture-frame` is not app API.
- `docs/api/re-frame.core.md:475-483,556-571` — generated public API publishes the internal constructors.
- `docs/tools/playground/sci/src/rf2_playground/sci.cljs:156,165-188` — SCI macro expansion names `make-capture-frame` and `copy-ns` exposes all public core runtime Vars.
- `implementation/core/test/re_frame/reg_view_injection_test.clj:298` and `implementation/core/test/re_frame/interceptor_runtime_complete_cljs_test.cljc` — tests currently pin the facade plumbing rather than its absence.
- `.github/workflows/lint.yml:627-637` — manifest checks remain, but the former facade-hygiene check is explicitly retired.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `re-frame.core` no longer resolves or documents `make-capture-frame`, `->interceptor`, or `->interceptor*` in either CLJ or CLJS, and none has a `:facade? true` manifest row.
2. `reg-view` expansion and internal interceptor construction use owned non-facade symbols; compilation, source-coordinate stamping/elision, and advanced-build behavior remain intact.
3. `capture-frame` remains the single supported carry primitive, preserving frame-incarnation fencing and injected dispatch/subscribe behavior; `reg-interceptor` remains the supported interceptor authoring form.
4. Playground SCI still supports `reg-view`, `capture-frame`, and registered interceptors without copying the removed runtime aliases into `re-frame.core`.
5. Focused tests assert both behavioral preservation and facade absence in CLJ/CLJS. Generated API/manifest projections and affected specs/docs agree with the resulting surface.
6. A generic automated check fails on a planted manifest row that combines an implementation-only disposition with `:facade? true`, and passes after the plant is removed.

## Non-goals

- No broad reclassification of the rest of `re-frame.core`, Story, or Xray.
- No redesign of capture-frame lifecycle semantics, interceptor descriptors, registration, or source-coordinate diagnostics.
- No compatibility aliases, deprecation tier, tombstones, or new public sugar; this is pre-alpha surface correction.
- No change to the public names or signatures of `capture-frame` or `reg-interceptor`.

## Related existing beads

- `rf2-2hpxo` (P3, deferred) is the broad retrospective facade-export classification sweep for external-alpha prep. This task does not duplicate it: these three exports are already classified and documented as implementation-only; the work here is to execute those settled dispositions and restore a regression check.

title: surface-review(uix-adapter): make a real UIx component test copy-pasteable and executable
description:
## Scope

Make the consumer-facing UIx component-testing path runnable from the public docs and easy to copy into a real app. Use the adapter's existing UIx/React primitives; cover the smallest honest real-DOM loop (mount a hook component under `frame-root`, drive an event, settle with `flush-views!`, assert the DOM, and tear everything down). Keep the executable witness close enough to the docs or generated scaffold that drift is caught.

## Verified Findings

- The UIx runtime surface is already substantial and well covered: `spec/api-manifest.edn:60-68` rows all nine public adapter Vars, and the adapter forwards a large shared React regression suite. This is not a request to redesign `use-subscribe`, `use-frame`, or frame scoping.
- The main view-testing guide is not substrate-neutral in practice. `docs/core/testing/views.md:5` says a view is a callable pure function returning hiccup and builds the whole recipe around JVM tree walking. A UIx `defui` that calls `use-subscribe` / `use-frame` is a React hook component and cannot use that recipe. The page's only UIx-relevant escape at line 93 says to use a real DOM and `flush-views!`, but supplies no mount, fixture, event, assertion, or cleanup shape.
- UIx's own public docs stop at the settling primitive: `docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md:178-191`, `docs/core/how-to/use-uix-or-slim.md:263,273`, and `implementation/adapters/uix/README.md:17` show `flush-views!` but no complete component test.
- The generated UIx app does not fill the gap. `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/root/README.md:272-274,309` emits only `events_test.cljs`; `_shared/events_test.cljs:5-7,24` explicitly runs DOM-free against a headless adapter. That is good dataflow coverage, but it teaches nothing about testing the UIx view the scaffold just generated.
- `implementation/adapters/test-react/README.md:3,7,123-128` explicitly makes Test-React local-only, React-free, DOM-free, opaque-tree, and non-reconciling. It therefore cannot execute UIx hooks and is not a missing consumer test kit to point at.
- The desired flow already exists as framework evidence: `implementation/adapters/uix/testbed/adapter_testbed_uix/core.cljs` plus `testbed/spec.cjs` prove frame-root mount -> use-subscribe -> click/dispatch -> DOM rerender in a real browser. Commit `2d2f4aff53` introduced the per-adapter testbed; commit `b924dca1af` introduced the current hiccup-centric Test-a-view recipe. The missing work is to turn those two disconnected bodies of knowledge into one consumer-shaped, executable UIx recipe.

## Recommended Action

Publish one canonical, copy-complete UIx component test using existing APIs only. Put the explanation where a test author looks (`docs/core/testing/views.md` and the UIx adapter docs), point the generated UIx README at it, and back the exact shape with a focused browser-lane test or other named executable witness. Prefer a small fixture/helper local to the example over a new framework abstraction. The recipe should make lifecycle ownership obvious: one mount node/root, `frame-root` (or an explicitly created/scoped frame), a real DOM interaction, `uix-adapter/flush-views!`, an assertion, and guaranteed unmount/runtime cleanup.

## Concrete Evidence

- History: `2d2f4aff53` (adapter testbeds), `b924dca1af` (Test-a-view recipe), `9cf8f2e54c` (generated UIx mount/hot-reload lifecycle)

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A copy-complete CLJS UIx test mounts a `defui` that uses `use-subscribe` and/or `use-frame` under a valid frame boundary, drives a real DOM event, settles through `uix-adapter/flush-views!`, observes the updated DOM, and guarantees unmount plus frame/adapter cleanup.
2. The published command for that test runs successfully in a named browser/DOM-capable lane; a focused executable test protects the recipe from API or lifecycle drift.
3. `docs/core/testing/views.md` explicitly distinguishes its fast hiccup-walk path from UIx hook components and links the runnable UIx recipe rather than implying the hiccup recipe applies.
4. The UIx adapter README/API and generated UIx project README make the first component-test path discoverable; the scaffold's existing DOM-free event/sub tests remain the recommended default for business logic.
5. The solution uses current public primitives. No new public helper namespace/API is added unless implementing the executable recipe demonstrates unavoidable repeated lifecycle machinery.

## Non-goals

- Do not publish or expand the internal Test-React adapter; it deliberately models class-3 lifecycle without React and cannot be made into UIx by adding shims.
- Do not build a Testing Library clone, add speculative compatibility layers, or create a full per-adapter test matrix.
- Do not change UIx hook signatures, frame semantics, adapter installation semantics, or the substrate contract.
- Do not require every generated project to run a browser suite by default if a documented, executable opt-in recipe gives the same low-friction path.

title: mayor loop: sweep open nightly-red issues into beads each merge+dispatch tick (loops.md §2 Dispatch + CLAUDE.md Workflow; alerter unchanged)
description:
Split out of rf2-2ohy's third acceptance item, which asked whether the
rf2-6sg25 alerting failed to surface seven consecutive nightly reds.

MEASURED 2026-08-23 13:36 AUSEST, and the answer is that THE ALERT FIRED
CORRECTLY. Issue #8423 'Nightly `expensive tests` is red' was opened
2026-08-16T16:01:50Z — the first red night — labelled `nightly-red`,
assigned to mike-thompson-day8, and its body named the exact failing step:
`Browser, bundle, examples, Story/Xray gates -> Gate — production elision,
browser (test:browser-prod-elision)`. It was edited every night since and
last updated 2026-08-22T16:02:05Z carrying `reds=7 greens=0`. The
alerting self-test step passed on every one of those runs. So the first
disjunct in rf2-2ohy's premise — 'the alerting did not fire' — is FALSE.
Nothing in .github/scripts/nightly_failure_alert.py is broken, and this
bead is NOT a request to change its signature logic.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED is the second disjunct: the issue went unseen for
seven days, and the alerter's own body says why, in its own words:

  'It is edited in place — which notifies nobody — while the same steps
  keep failing, and comments only when a step that was not failing starts
  to.'

That is a deliberate anti-spam design and it is defensible. The observed
cost of it is that a red lane produces EXACTLY ONE notification, on night
one, and then six nights of silence — and the one notification competes
with normal PR traffic in the same inbox. Seven days later the redness was
found by a manual PR-activity sweep, not by the alert, and no bead existed
until that sweep filed rf2-2ohy.

THE GAP, stated narrowly: nothing escalates a `nightly-red` issue that
stays open, and nothing bridges a GitHub issue into the beads tracker,
which is where work is actually dispatched from in this repo. The alert
lands in a channel the working loop does not read.

NOT PROPOSING A REMEDY — this is an operator call, and there are at least
three shapes with different costs, so it should not be picked by a worker:
  (a) re-notify on an age threshold (comment, not edit, after N reds) —
      cheapest, stays inside the existing script;
  (b) have the mayor loop read open `nightly-red` issues each tick;
  (c) have the alerter file/refresh a bead directly, so nightly redness
      enters the same queue as everything else.
(a) risks the spam the current design avoids. (c) is the most useful and
the most machinery. Mike to rule.

EVIDENCE: gh issue view 8423; gh run list --workflow expensive-tests.yml;
.github/workflows/expensive-tests.yml lines 558-616 (the 'Nightly result ->
tracking issue' job, which succeeded on all seven red runs).

ACCEPTANCE: a ruling on whether nightly redness should escalate past night
one, and if so which shape. If the ruling is 'leave it as is, the mayor
sweep is the backstop', close this — that is a legitimate outcome and the
evidence above is the record of what that choice costs.
notes:
*** AWAITING MIKE — NOT DISPATCHABLE. WHOLLY AN OPERATOR CALL. *** Fence recorded by the mayor's dispatch tick 2026-08-23 13:41 AUSEST at tip e1a1faf9c8, quoting this bead's own description rather than re-reasoning it.

WHY IT IS NOT DISPATCHABLE: the bead states it in terms — 'NOT PROPOSING A REMEDY — this is an operator call, and there are at least three shapes with different costs, so it should not be picked by a worker.' A worker sent here would have to choose between (a) re-notify on an age threshold, (b) the mayor loop reads open nightly-red issues each tick, and (c) the alerter files or refreshes a bead directly. Those differ in cost and in how much machinery they add, which is a judgement rather than a task.

DISCHARGED BY: Mike ruling on whether nightly redness should escalate past night one, and if so which of the three shapes. 'Leave it as is, the mayor sweep is the backstop' is a legitimate ruling and closes this bead — the bead says so itself, and the evidence it carries then stands as the record of what that choice costs.

WHAT IT IS NOT, and this matters because the parent bead's premise said otherwise: the alerting is NOT broken. This bead REFUTED that premise with measurement — issue #8423 opened on the first red night, labelled, assigned, naming the exact failing step, edited every night since, with the alerting self-test passing on all seven runs. Check the exit code of the gh call itself. Exit 0 with `[]` = nothing red, done — the normal tick (the dossier measured the label non-empty on 12 of the last 60 days; at ruling time it is empty). Non-zero exit = "the sweep did not run this tick", retried on the next signal — NEVER read a failed query as "no nightly red" (the reviewer's invariant, adopted).
- DEDUP KEY: the canonical issue URL (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/issues/<n>), carried in the bead's `external_ref` field — a field the tracker already uses this way (15 beads carry PR URLs in it at tip) and which `bd list --json` exposes. description:
The Frames tab is attributed to the RETIRED EP-0013 substrate in two Xray spec chapters, while the same
tree states elsewhere that the tab is the EP-0023 `image -> frame` public model and that EP-0013 was
deleted in full. One of the two chapters contradicts ITSELF.

event-spine chapter are outside that item's fence, so it named them and asked that both be routed as ONE
item rather than fixed singly. That request is correct and is why this bead exists: repairing the
cross-cutting chapter alone would split it from the event-spine chapter, turning one inconsistency into a
different one.

Counts per file (`EP-0013` / `EP-0023`), nonsense-id control 0 across the tree:

    019-Cross-Cutting-Insight.md    2 / 0
    018-Event-Spine.md              2 / 2
    000-Vision.md                   1 / 2
    026-Module-View-Panel.md        4 / 31

**The decisive evidence is the self-contradiction in the event-spine chapter.** Its line 537 says the tab
is "The EP-0023 `image -> frame` PUBLIC model" and, in the same row, that "the retired EP-0013 realm /
app-value / module substrate this tab once also surfaced was deleted in full." Its line 19 nonetheless

title: xray: effects-decomp is dead against the live substrate, and repairing it alone switches on a false 'runtime ignored this effect' accusation (closed-effect-keys 3 vs 7)
description:
Two findings recorded IN CODE by rf2-y8doi.19's worker (PR #9954) and deliberately not fixed, because both
are wider than slice C7. They are filed together because **repairing either one alone makes things worse**,
which is the whole point of this bead.

## (1) `effects-decomp` is DEAD against the live substrate

`:rf.event/fx` is stamped as the fx **vector**, so the `(map? fx)` guard in `effects-decomp` never holds.
Measured live rather than reasoned: `:fx-vec nil`, `:other-effects nil`.

**Synthetic fixtures pass a MAP, which is why nothing caught it** — that is the rf2-y8doi.10 finding-1
drift exactly: a fixture shaped unlike the runtime keeps a dead path looking alive. So any test over this
function is grading a shape the substrate never produces.

## (2) Xray's `closed-effect-keys` has 3 keys; the framework's closed set has 7

The four EP-0025 classification effects are absent from Xray's copy, so each would be reported to the user
as **"an effect the runtime ignored"** — a false accusation against correct framework behaviour.

**(2) is LATENT ONLY BECAUSE OF (1).** The decomposition never runs, so the short key list is never
consulted, so the false accusation never fires. **Repair (1) without (2) and you switch the false
accusation ON** — four legitimate effects start being reported as ignored.

**And the blast radius is not arbitrary: it would land on the very mechanism PR #9954's redaction depends
on.** So the order is not a preference. Either fix both in one change, or fix (2) first and (1) second —
never (1) alone.

## What to do

Re-derive both at source before anything else; all of it is relayed from one worker's report and this
wave's dominant failure is a finding that holds while its prescribed remedy does not.

- For (1), establish what `:rf.event/fx` actually carries at trunk and whether `effects-decomp` has any

- For (2), take the framework's closed set as the authority and say where you read it from. Do not

- Whatever you do, **show the false accusation firing** on a fixture shaped like the runtime — not like

title: Item (s) is INTERMITTENT: the bare grep CR count was measured both 0 and 161 on CLAUDE.md the same day, so 'the determinant is the invocation form' is too strong
description:
Found 2026-09-17 by two workers editing the SAME FILE on the SAME MACHINE within about two hours, who
measured OPPOSITE results and both reported what they actually saw rather than what the catalogue
predicted.

## What item (s) currently claims

CLAUDE.md § "Ways the INSTRUMENTS misreport", item (s), states that a bare
`grep -c $'\r' CLAUDE.md` reads **0** on a file that carries 156 carriage returns, while the identical
command captured by `$( )` reads 156, and concludes in terms: **"THE DETERMINANT IS THE INVOCATION
FORM, NOT THE FILE."** It records eliminations (not stdout destination, not binary classification, not
grep failing to reach the file) and deliberately leaves the precise mechanism open.

## The contradiction, both halves on CLAUDE.md itself

* **rf2-oitjw's worker (PR #9943)** reproduced it exactly as catalogued: bare `grep -c $'\r' CLAUDE.md`
  printed **0** at exit **1**, where Python reading the bytes read **161**.
* **rf2-1hh87's worker (PR #9949)**, roughly two hours later, on the same file at a later trunk, read
  **161 at exit 0** from the bare form — AGREEING with Python. Its brief had predicted 0, per the
  catalogue; it used the three-number Python form regardless and **recorded the disagreement rather
  than quoting the expected result.**

Same file, same machine, same shell tooling, same needle, opposite answers. So the stated determinant —
the invocation form — **does not by itself account for the behaviour.** Something else varies.

## Why this matters even though the guard is unaffected

**The GUARD is untouched and stays exactly as written**: count carriage returns with Python reading the
file in binary, never with `grep` in any form, and take the three numbers (CR, CRLF, bare LF) because
`grep -c` counts LINES MATCHING rather than CR BYTES and so answers a different question even when it
works. Nothing here weakens that, and this bead must not be read as licence to reach for `grep`.

What changes is the **diagnostic value of the zero**. Item (s) is written so a reader meeting a 0 can
recognise it as the known defect. If the behaviour is INTERMITTENT, then:

  * a reader who meets **161** may conclude item (s) is stale or was never real, and drop the Python
    guard — the expensive outcome, because the guard is what makes the standing CR == CRLF check
    non-vacuous, and item (u) shows that check passing vacuously as `0 == 0` under `sed -i` damage;
  * a reader who meets **0** and cannot reproduce it may hunt a file-specific cause that is not there —
    which is exactly the trail item (s) itself records having been sent down once already, since it was
    "first reported as a FILE-dependent oddity and could not be reproduced, because the reproducer
    reached for the `$( )` form."

**An intermittent instrument defect is worse than a consistent one**, because a single negative
reproduction reads as a refutation. Item (s) already warns "a failure to reproduce is not evidence
against it"; that sentence is now load-bearing in the other direction too.

## Required correction

Record that the behaviour has been observed BOTH ways on this file within one day, so the invocation
form is a contributing condition rather than a sufficient one, and that a successful bare read does NOT
license dropping the Python guard. Keep the eliminations, keep the measured numbers, keep the
deliberate refusal to name a mechanism — and do not invent one now.

**Acceptance:** a reader who runs the bare form and gets the RIGHT answer still uses Python, and knows
why. **No new gate, no script, no wrapper.**

## Worker rules

**Re-measure both forms yourself before editing, several times, and report what you get** — including if
it is stable in one direction today. A third data point is worth more than the prose. Take the count
with Python on bytes as the reference in every run, and note the exit status of the bare form each time
(the two accounts differ on that too: exit 1 with the zero, exit 0 with the 161).

**Do not widen this into a hunt for the mechanism.** Two workers have now spent measurements on it; the
guard holds either way, and the stance says we do not litigate every last fine detail. Record the
observation, correct the over-strong sentence, stop.

## Scope and sequencing

- Fence: `CLAUDE.md`, item (s) within § "Ways the INSTRUMENTS misreport", and nothing else.
- Three beads have edited this file today (`rf2-d3l8g`, `rf2-oitjw`, `rf2-1hh87`), all MERGED, so it is
  currently uncontended — but check for a live holder before dispatching.
- `CLAUDE.md` is `i/lf w/crlf`: never `sed -i` (item (u)), build replacement text with the Write tool
  rather than a heredoc (item (o)), and take the three line-ending numbers with Python on bytes — which
  on this item is also the thing being written about.
- The gate for repo-root markdown is `scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci`, NOT `check_doc_slugs.py`,
  whose roots exclude repo-root markdown and which two workers have now separately DEMONSTRATED exits 0
  on a planted broken link there.

Completeness: The item (s) correction records both observed outcomes, limits invocation form to a contributing condition, and explicitly preserves Python byte counting after a successful bare read. Historical figures and the no-mechanism/no-new-gate boundary remain intact.
Correctness: Compared the sole changed physical line with its parent and the source requirement. The prose distinguishes observations from an unestablished cause, accommodates the third measurement without denying either earlier report, and leaves the binary-count guard in force. No contradiction requiring corrective work found; this review does not independently reproduce the machine-dependent shell behavior.
Implementation quality: Bounded documentation correction without runtime, wrapper or gate expansion. Links and headings are unaffected, so green link gates are not treated as proof of the prose; the changed claims were read directly. No actionable new finding.
Evidence: full PR diff and merged source inspected; CI conclusions {'SKIPPED': 67, 'SUCCESS': 21}.

**IT DID NOT OVERSHOOT INTO THE INVERSE, WHICH WAS THE ENTIRE DIFFICULTY OF THIS ITEM.** The brief named

bare readings across five shells read 0 at exit 1 every time against Python's 161 — so the catalogued zero
is live today. The worker then says plainly that a third point landing on one side does not settle between
the two accounts. Reporting a result that favours your own prior and declining to bank it is the behaviour
this project wants.

THE GUIDANCE RESTS ON ASYMMETRIC COST RATHER THAN ON A DIAGNOSIS, exactly as the brief prescribed for the
case where the evidence supports neither side: a reader who meets 161, calls item (s) stale and drops the

by using Python anyway.

**THE GUARD SURVIVED INTACT**, which was the stated non-negotiable: count carriage returns with Python
reading the file in binary, never with `grep` in any form, and take three numbers because `grep -c` counts
LINES MATCHING rather than CR BYTES and so answers a different question even when it works.

IT ALSO WIDENED A SENTENCE IN THE RIGHT DIRECTION WITHOUT BEING ASKED. "A failure to reproduce is not
evidence against it" now runs BOTH ways — under intermittency a SUCCESSFUL bare read is not evidence
against it either. That symmetry is what stops the next reader retiring the item on one lucky run.

MY OWN VERIFICATION AT MERGE, and one of these checks caught me reading the wrong surface. Unicode integrity
on the branch blob against trunk: em-dash U+2014 405 → 409 (the four added by new prose), U+2212 Unicode
minus 0, U+FFFD replacement 0, NBSP 0, and the blob decodes as valid UTF-8 — this file has been damaged by a

as damage**: `git show` returns the committed blob, and `CLAUDE.md` is `i/lf`, so CR=0/CRLF=0 is what a
HEALTHY blob reads — the CR == CRLF test means something only against a WORKING file. Re-taken against the
working file post-merge: `i/lf w/crlf`, CR=161 CRLF=161 bare_LF=0, both conditions true.

title: story: canvas assertion strip renders an :error record like a :fail — ✖ glyph, red band, seed-open, summary and detail from [:error :message]
description:
IMPLEMENTATION BRIEF (for the dispatched worker). Self-contained; the dossier is background, not a prerequisite.

PROVENANCE. Filed 2026-09-17 as discovered-from rf2-20lwk, whose question — should Story's Tests pane and sidebar dot surface a SETUP failure on a variant that declares no tests? — was ruled NO (option A) on 2026-09-17 by delegation from Mike. That bead's close reason carries the ruling and its notes carry the full dossier (two independent reviewers, a JVM probe of the record shape). Both reviewers independently recommended THIS work — the dossier's option E — as the real repair. Trunk when written: 8bb6041d0e; every line number below was read at that revision, and none of the cited files had changed since the dossier's 634b085f12.

THE DEFECT. When a variant's :setup fails — a throwing handler, or (since PR #9878, rf2-0ae7o.13) a dispatch nobody registered, which is exactly what the unfilled "↑ real setup" scaffold `[:dispatch [:your/setup-event {}]]` from view_state.cljc:385-387 does — the per-frame trace listener captures the failure as an assertion record on the frame's :rf.story/assertions (`captured-failure-record`, tools/story/src/re_frame/story/error.cljc:278-313). Its shape, measured on the JVM by the dossier and confirmed by the second reviewer running real variants:

  {:assertion :rf.error/exception  :passed? false          ;; NO :status key
   :event [:your/setup-event {}]   :phase :phase-2-events  :reason nil
   :error {:message "no handler registered for :your/setup-event" :stack nil :data nil}}

`assertion-row` (tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/test_mode/pure.cljc:116-128) projects it to :status :error — through the `(or (:error rec) (:exception rec))` arm, reached BECAUSE the record carries no :status; a record stamped :status :error takes the earlier `verdict/statuses` arm and reads :error too — with :label ":rf.error/exception" and a :detail map carrying :error, :event, :phase and :reason (nil).

The canvas assertion strip (`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/assertion_strip.cljs`; consumed by canvas.cljs:369-377 `render-assertions`, called at canvas.cljs:777, and by every workspace cell at workspace.cljc:471-477) has NO :error arm anywhere. So that row paints as a grey "·" fallback glyph with no summary text, no red band, collapsed — and the one sentence that says what went wrong is never rendered, even after the row is expanded, because `row-detail` does not read :error. The Tests pane's own table DOES render it (view.cljs:312-325 prints `error: <message>`; :343-351 gives :error the glyph ✖) — but the pane short-circuits on a test-less variant, so the canvas is the surface the author is actually looking at.

THE CHANGE — one source file, one spec section, one test file. No new state, no new writer, no new theme token.

1. `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/assertion_strip.cljs` (585 lines):
   a. `summary-line` (:116-141). The `case status` has :fail / :skip / :pass arms and a default "". Add an :error arm: the detail's `[:error :message]` when it is a string; else :reason (as-is when a string, pr-str when non-nil); else "error". Widen the destructuring at :127-128 (`{:keys [reason expected actual]} detail`) to pull `error` too. Extend the docstring's "For failures / For passes / For skips" list.
   b. `status->row-style` (:262-265) and `status->glyph-style` (:267-270): add `:error` entries reusing `(:row-fail styles)` and `(:glyph-fail styles)` (the danger token; styles map :207-208 and :216). This mirrors the pane's own precedent — view.cljs:346-347 gives :fail and :error the SAME `:status-fail` colour and tells them apart by GLYPH — and satisfies spec/018 §12.6 (tools/story/spec/018-Story-UI-North-Star.md:792-809: "fail" and "error" MUST remain distinguishable) by icon and text without inventing a colour token. Do not add a token.
   c. `status-glyph` (:272-275) is `rf.story.predicates/assertion-glyph`, the three-valued SHARED vocabulary (tools/story/src/re_frame/story/predicates.cljc:21-32; also consumed by the test-mode table and the scrubber; its own docstring says consumers supply their own fallback for non-assertion ticks). Do NOT widen `assertion-glyph`. Make the strip's public `status-glyph` `(assoc rf.story.predicates/assertion-glyph :error "✖")` and say so in its docstring; `render-row`'s `(get status-glyph status "·")` at :361 then finds it. ✖ matches the pane (view.cljs:347) rather than reusing ✗, so error stays distinguishable from fail.
   d. `render-row` (:350-398). `fail?` at :370 (`(= :fail status)`) drives the `:summary-fail` style at :388 — widen it to `(contains? #{:fail :error} status)`. `:data-status (name status)` at :372 and the aria-label at :379 already read "error" for free; no change there.
