title: bd history recovery is exposed to a silent 65,535-byte TEXT truncation (upstream #3925) — and the two beads over the ceiling are the two most load-bearing on the board
description:
FOUND 2026-09-16 by the rf2-tm58 bd-1.3.0 evaluation, as a hazard that has NOTHING to do with the upgrade — it is live on the version we run today. Filed separately rather than buried in that bead, because declining the upgrade (which is the recommendation there) does not discharge this.

## THE UPSTREAM DEFECT

Upstream issue **#3925**, OPEN: Dolt `TEXT` columns silently truncate at **65,535 bytes**. Among the affected columns is **`events.new_value`, which stores the full post-mutation issue JSON**. The fix is deferred pending a storage-layer redesign, so there is no version to wait for.

## WHY IT BITES *THIS* PROJECT SPECIFICALLY

`bd history <id> --json` is **one of the two recovery routes CLAUDE.md prescribes** for an erased `close_reason` — the other being a checkpoint commit of `.beads/issues.jsonl` in git history. That matters because this project treats close reasons as NORMATIVE RECORDS: a ruling is frequently the close reason of a closed dependency, which is why `bd gc`'s decay phase is banned outright.

CLAUDE.md's own account of route (2) measures it working — on the throwaway bead `rf2-i834` the per-commit snapshot lengths read `[0,419,0]` newest-first, and four snapshots carried the text for `rf2-dokz`. **Those are small beads.** The route was never exercised against a large one.

## THE EXPOSURE, MEASURED ON THIS BOARD TODAY

Each non-terminal bead's full JSON record, UTF-8 bytes, against the 65,535 ceiling:

    rf2-uelji      201,517 bytes   OVER  (3.1x)
    rf2-kmqx3      142,095 bytes   OVER  (2.2x)
    rf2-hic-063     64,784 bytes         (751 bytes under)
    rf2-8urba       57,816 bytes
    rf2-fo4ng       55,412 bytes
    ...
    2 of 19 non-terminal beads exceed the ceiling.

**THE TWO THAT EXCEED IT ARE THE TWO MOST LOAD-BEARING BEADS ON THE BOARD.** `rf2-uelji` is the critical path — it transitively gates 9 of the 19 non-terminal beads, including the only P1. `rf2-kmqx3` is the first-tag operator gate. And `rf2-hic-063` will cross the line on its next substantial note.

That is the shape worth the filing: the exposure is not spread evenly across a board of small beads, it is concentrated on precisely the items whose accumulated reasoning is least replaceable, because size and importance are the SAME VARIABLE here — a bead gets large by being argued over, and the ones argued over most are the ones that matter most.

## WHAT IS ESTABLISHED AND WHAT IS NOT — READ THIS BEFORE ACTING

**ESTABLISHED:** #3925 is open upstream and names `events.new_value`; the ceiling is 65,535 bytes; two current non-terminal bead records exceed it and one is within 751 bytes.

**NOT ESTABLISHED, and nobody should state otherwise without measuring it:**
  * That `events.new_value` in OUR store actually contains the whole record for these beads rather than a diff or a subset. The column's documented contents say full JSON; our store has not been inspected.
  * That truncation has actually OCCURRED here. Exposure is not damage.
  * Whether `bd history` reconstructs from `events` at all, or from some other table that is not `TEXT`-bound.

So this is a CLAIM about risk, not a report of loss. The next step is one read-only inspection: take a bead known to exceed the ceiling, run `bd history <id> --json`, and check whether the newest snapshot's `.Issue.notes` round-trips to the length `bd show --json` reports. **That is a pure read and safe to do on the live store.** If the lengths agree, the exposure is theoretical and this bead closes cheaply.

## IF IT IS REAL, THE REMEDY IS NOT OBVIOUS AND SHOULD NOT BE GUESSED AT

Do not reflexively propose trimming the large beads. Their size IS their value, the project has already lost ~72,800 characters once to `--notes` replacing a field, and CLAUDE.md's route (1) — the git-history checkpoint export — is UNAFFECTED by a `TEXT` ceiling and remains complete. So the honest framing may simply be: **route (2) is unreliable above 65,535 bytes; prefer route (1) for large beads, and say so in the recovery bullet.** That would be a documentation fix rather than a data migration, which is the cheaper and more likely-correct answer.

## PROVENANCE

Reported by the zero-edit research worker on rf2-tm58 (bd v1.3.0 upgrade evaluation), which flagged it explicitly as pre-existing rather than upgrade-related and noted it is not on CLAUDE.md's instrument catalogue. The byte census above was taken by the mayor on the live tracker the same hour.
notes:
FIRST MEASUREMENT 2026-09-16 (mayor, read-only). THE HAZARD IS REAL BUT IT IS NOT THE ONE THIS BEAD WAS FILED ABOUT, AND THE DIRECTION IS INVERTED. Truncation is still NOT established either way. What IS established is a size hazard that is more immediate and that nearly bit the measurement itself.

MEASURED, four commands, nothing mutated:

    bd show    rf2-uelji --json       200,585 bytes
    bd history rf2-uelji --json   1,590,355,619 bytes     <-- 1.59 GIGABYTES
    bd show    rf2-tezz5 --json        10,557 bytes
    bd history rf2-tezz5 --json        28,718 bytes

The small bead is the control and it behaves: history is 2.7x its record. On rf2-uelji the record is 19x larger and the history is **55,375x larger**. That is grossly superlinear, and it is not explained by pretty-printing.

THE OUTPUT IS WELL-FORMED, NOT GARBAGE. Its first bytes are the documented shape -- an array of objects carrying `CommitHash`, `Committer`, `CommitDate` and a nested `Issue` -- so this is bd doing what it does, at a scale nobody has looked at.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE TRUNCATION QUESTION: **`bd history <id> --json` is CLAUDE.md's recovery route (2)** for an erased `close_reason`, and on this project's single most important bead it returns 1.59 GB. The route is not merely degraded, it is unusable in the idiom everybody writes -- `bd history <id> --json | jq -r ...` -- because the natural move is to pipe it, and a 1.59 GB pipe into a JSON parser inside an agent's context window is not a slow command, it is a dead session. The measurement here survived only because it was redirected to a FILE and sized with `wc -c` before anything read it, which was ordinary caution rather than foresight. **An agent following CLAUDE.md's own recovery instruction verbatim, on the bead most likely to need recovering, would take the damage.**

AND THE EXPOSURE TRACKS IMPORTANCE, exactly as this bead already argues for the truncation case: history size is driven by record size times snapshot count, and both grow with how much a bead has been argued over. rf2-uelji (the critical path, gating 9) and rf2-kmqx3 (the first-tag gate) are the two largest records on the board.

WHAT IS STILL NOT ESTABLISHED, stated plainly so nobody reads this as the bead being answered:
  * WHETHER `events.new_value` TRUNCATES AT 65,535 BYTES HERE. Untested. The 1.59 GB file was DELETED rather than parsed -- parsing it safely is its own exercise and I judged it out of scope for a read-only probe. Note the tension: 1.59 GB is hard to reconcile with every snapshot being truncated to 64 KB, so this measurement is weak evidence AGAINST truncation -- but weak is the right word, and the arithmetic has not been done.
  * WHY it is superlinear. Snapshot count was not read, so "N snapshots x full record" is a hypothesis, not a finding.
  * Whether `bd history` offers a bounded form (a limit, a field selector, a no-payload mode) that would make route (2) usable without parsing gigabytes. **THAT IS THE NEXT THING TO CHECK, and it is cheap** -- `bd history --help`. If such a flag exists, the remedy is a one-line correction to CLAUDE.md's recovery bullet rather than anything structural.

IMMEDIATE, CHEAP AND INDEPENDENT OF THE RULING: CLAUDE.md's recovery bullet should not tell a reader to pipe `bd history <id> --json` without saying to size it first. Route (1) -- the checkpoint export in git history -- is unaffected by any of this and remains complete, so for a large bead it is simply the better route. That is a documentation fix and is the likely whole answer.

DO NOT RUN `bd history` ON A LARGE BEAD INTO A PIPE OR INTO AN AGENT'S CONTEXT. Redirect to a file, `wc -c` it, and decide from the size.
=== PREMISE REFUTED, SAME TICK, BY CHECKING AT SOURCE. THIS BEAD IS NOT ABOUT TRUNCATION. ===

Measured read-only, both fields, same method on both sides so the comparison is not across a seam:

    field         bd show    bd history --limit 1    identical
    notes         191,277    191,277                 TRUE
    description     4,388      4,388                 TRUE

`bd history` returns the notes field BYTE-IDENTICAL to `bd show`, at **2.9x the 65,535-byte ceiling**. So upstream #3925 does NOT truncate `events.new_value` for this field on this store, and the hazard this bead was filed about does not exist here. The filing was honest -- it said plainly that exposure was established and damage was not -- and the check that settles it cost three commands.

WHAT REMAINS IS REAL, AND IT IS THE THING FOUND BY ACCIDENT WHILE TESTING THE THING THAT WAS NOT: **unbounded `bd history` on a large bead returns 1.59 GB.** That stands, and the remedy is now known and trivial.

THE REMEDY: `bd history <id> --json --limit N`. Measured on rf2-uelji -- `--limit 1` 200,683 bytes, `--limit 3` 602,042 bytes -- so it bounds LINEARLY at roughly one 200 KB record per snapshot, against 1,590,355,619 bytes unlimited. The flag has been there all along; CLAUDE.md's recovery bullet simply never used it, because the route was only ever exercised on small beads where it did not matter.

SO THE WHOLE OF THIS BEAD IS NOW A ONE-LINE DOCUMENTATION FIX: CLAUDE.md's recovery route (2) should read `bd history <id> --json --limit N` rather than the unbounded form, with a sentence saying why -- an unbounded history on a large bead is gigabytes, and the idiom everybody writes pipes it straight into a JSON parser. Route (1), the checkpoint export in git history, is unaffected throughout.

AND THE ARITHMETIC NOW EXPLAINS THE SUPERLINEARITY, which the first note left as a hypothesis: 1,590,355,619 / ~200,000 bytes per snapshot is roughly **7,950 snapshots** for this one bead. It is not that each snapshot is bloated; it is that a bead updated this often keeps a full record copy per commit. That also retires the "weak evidence against truncation" hedge in the note above -- the direct comparison settles it and the arithmetic is merely consistent.

ONE MEASUREMENT TRAP MET IN THE COURSE OF THIS, worth recording because it produced two different lengths for one unchanged field. title: CLAUDE.md instrument item: sed -i rewrites a w/crlf working file as ALL-LF, silently, while the edit succeeds
description:
FOUND BY THE rf2-81vnm WORKER (PR #9909) 2026-09-16 and REPRODUCED INDEPENDENTLY BY THE MAYOR the same hour. This is an INSTRUMENT DEFECT of the class CLAUDE.md already catalogues, and its home is that list.

## THE DEFECT

`sed -i` on a CRLF working file REWRITES THE WHOLE FILE AS ALL-LF. It does not merely fail to preserve the endings on the line it edited; every CRLF in the file becomes a bare LF.

Measured by the mayor on a purpose-built fixture, counting bytes with Python (never with `grep -c`, per item (s)):

    fixture before            cr=3  crlf=3  bare_lf=0
    after `sed -i s/bravo/BRAVO/`  cr=0  crlf=0  bare_lf=3
    same edit via Python bytes     cr=3  crlf=3  bare_lf=0

The control both ways is in that table: the Python route preserves the endings on the identical fixture and the identical substitution, so the determinant is `sed -i` and not the edit.

## WHY IT IS DANGEROUS RATHER THAN MERELY WRONG

**It fails in the REASSURING direction.** The substitution SUCCEEDS -- the new text is present, exit status is 0, nothing is printed on stderr, and reading the file back shows exactly the intended change. Every check a careful author would run on the CONTENT passes. Only a byte-level count of the line endings sees it.

**The blast radius is nearly the whole repository.** Measured at trunk: **5082 of 5252 tracked files are `w/crlf`**. `sed -i` is the obvious tool for a one-line correction to a spec page, a doc row or a catalogue entry, which is precisely the kind of edit this project's workers make constantly.

**For most files the COMMITTED BLOB survives and that is what hides it.** 5082 files are `i/lf w/crlf`, so the clean filter normalises on commit and the blob is unaffected -- the damage is working-tree-only and invisible in `git diff`. But it is NOT harmless: git can reclassify the file, and a subsequent editor sees a file whose endings no longer match its siblings. **And for the ONE `i/crlf` file in this tree -- `spec/011-SSR.md` -- the blob itself carries CRLF, so `sed -i` there would change the committed object.**

**It defeats the guard this project already mandates, from a new direction.** CLAUDE.md item (e) tells every editor of a CRLF file to check three numbers afterwards -- total CR, total CRLF, and bare LF -- and to require CR == CRLF and bare LF == 0. Under `sed -i` the file goes to cr=0 crlf=0, which SATISFIES "CR equals CRLF" as 0 == 0 and is caught ONLY by the third number. That is the same vacuous-pass shape item (s) records for a bare `grep -c`, reached through a different tool.

## THE GUARD

Do not use `sed -i` on a file git reports as `w/crlf`. Use the Write/Edit tooling, or read and write the bytes (Python `open(p,'rb')` / `open(p,'wb')`), and then take the three-number check with Python as item (e) already prescribes. Where `sed` is genuinely wanted for its expression language, write to a NEW file and convert the endings back deliberately -- but prefer not to.

`git ls-files --eol <path>` answers whether a file is `w/crlf` before you edit it.

## SCOPE OF THE WORK

One entry in CLAUDE.md's "Ways the INSTRUMENTS misreport on this machine" bullet, in the established shape: the observable, the measurement with both-way controls, why it fails in the reassuring direction, and the guard. It is the same FAMILY as (e), (o) and (s) -- content correct at the source, damaged at the callee, tool reporting success -- and should say so and say how it differs, as those entries do for each other.

**DO NOT USE `sed -i` TO MAKE THIS EDIT.** CLAUDE.md is itself `w/crlf` (measured: cr=159 crlf=159 bare_lf=0 at trunk 516ca86a3a). Use the Write/Edit tooling, and take the three numbers before and after -- the entry would otherwise demonstrate its own defect.

**CLAUDE.md goes through a PR like any other tracked file**; measured, the last several commits touching it each came via exactly one merged PR. Do not commit it to the trunk.

## A SECOND, SMALLER FINDING FROM THE SAME REPORT, recorded so it is not lost

The same worker measured that a naive "is the shadow-cljs lane busy?" process probe returned **4**, and all four were SELF-MATCHES: the search pattern appears in the probe's own command line, so the probe counts itself. That is the same family as the mayor's own reap probe matching its own fence prose, and as item (g)'s census matching a domain term. It is not obviously worth its own CLAUDE.md entry -- the exclusive-lane bullet already tells a coordinator to verify by effect and to filter on the worker's OWN worktree path -- but if this item's author judges it a distinct door, a sentence in that bullet is the place.

title: story-ui: Schema validation panel validates stored args, not the live Controls overrides and modes, and never re-renders on a control change
description:
FENCED: GATED ON PR #9806 MERGING. rf2-fhjke (worker/storyvalid-a) holds tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/schema_validation.cljc. The fence clears when #9806 merges.

Discovered by the rf2-fhjke worker as that bead's symptom 2, with verdict (b): a different defect, NOT the Malli explanation-shape bug #9806 fixes.

THE DEFECT. Controls validates `(rf.story.plan/effective-args variant-id {:active-modes ... :cell-overrides overrides})`. The Schema validation panel calls `(rf.story.plan/effective-args variant-id)` with NO opts (`schema_validation.cljc:473` at trunk e5c6121308). So it sees the stored args, never the live control override, and drops active modes. It also derefs only the trace buffer, not the shell state, so it would not re-render on a control change even with the right opts.

EVIDENCE (measured by the worker; see rf2-fhjke notes):
  * JVM re-enactment: the panel's call resolved `{:heading "Sign in"}` with 0 violations, while Controls' call resolved `{:heading ""}` with `[:heading]`. Handed Controls' args, the panel's own reader also returns `[:heading]`, so the reader is right and its input is wrong.
  * Live, headless, on the login_form testbed: after clearing `:heading`, Controls shows a "1 arg violates" banner while the panel still says "no args violations".

FIX SHAPE (a claim, not a ruling): make the panel resolve args from the same shell state Controls uses (active modes plus cell overrides), and make it subscribe to that state so it re-renders. Reuse Controls' resolution rather than writing a second resolver.

NEIGHBOURS, NOT IN SCOPE UNLESS VERIFIED. Other bare `(rf.story.plan/effective-args variant-id)` calls at trunk e5c6121308: `ui/controls.cljs:279` (resolve-argtypes), `ui/share.cljs:123` (arg-keys), and `story.cljc:1835` (the public arity-1). Check whether each needs overrides before touching it; several may only want the key set.

title: Xray palette: wire Cycle display density to the implemented Settings control
description:
Make the command palette's existing "Cycle display density" action update the implemented Settings density control. It currently closes the palette after writing an unread flag, so the user-visible command has no effect.

Ownership: tools/xray/**, slice tools_xray. Revision 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261. SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2; WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review). Parent rf2-gwye. P3: a broken convenience command with a working Settings alternative.

Evidence:
- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/palette/sources.cljc:209-220 exposes the :density-toggle setting item in both Dynamic and Static modes, labelled "Cycle display density", with action [:palette/cycle-density]. Its hint also promises three tiers (compact / cosy / comfy), while the shipped setting is the two-tier :compact/:cosy control.
- palette/events.cljs:402-407 handles the verb only with {:db (assoc close-db :density-cycle-requested? true)}. The comment says Phase 1 will wire density once the runtime lands.
- That runtime is present: settings/events.cljs:97-122 handles :rf.xray/settings-update, writes config/update-setting!, and applies density font size when section/key are :general/:density. The normal handler also mirrors settings into app-db. settings/effects.cljs:192-236 supplies the density-to-font-size application; settings/subs.cljs:98-104 reads [:settings :general :density] or config/get-setting, not the palette request flag.
- A source search for density-cycle-requested? finds only the palette write. This is corroborated by inspecting the actual density producer/consumer chain, not inferred from grep absence alone.
- tools/xray/spec/015-Configuration.md:543-564 identifies :cosy/:compact as the shipped density setting; :comfy is not a shipped third tier. Settings is already the common density control, so no new feature design is needed to make this existing command honest.

Reproducer:
Open Xray with density :cosy; Cmd/Ctrl+K; find "Cycle display density"; invoke it. Expected: switch to :compact, update the rendered density and persist through the normal Settings path. Actual: the palette closes and :density-cycle-requested? becomes true, while density stays :cosy. Repeating the action makes no further change. The same failure exists when starting :compact or using Static mode.

Validation performed:
The original :palette/cycle-density branch was read from palette/events.cljs and evaluated by Babashka with close-db containing :settings {:general {:density :cosy}}. The exact returned result retained :cosy, set only the request flag, and contained no :fx dispatch. This was a source-expression witness, not execution of the full CLJS registrar/browser. Inspected the actual Settings write, config read, density sub and CSS application paths. Probe exit 0 asserts this counterexample; evidence ai/surface-review-20260913/tools_xray/probe-tools-xray-1.{clj,log,exit}.

Suggested repair:
Resolve the current setting through config/get-setting (the established cold-path source, as the palette theme command already does), toggle :cosy <-> :compact, and emit [:rf.xray/settings-update :general :density next] through the ordinary dispatch effect. Preserve base-fx and palette-close behavior. Remove the orphan request flag and obsolete Phase 1 comment; make the item hint match the two supported tiers. Reuse the existing control rather than introducing new density state or adding :comfy.

Acceptance criteria:
- The real palette event changes :cosy to :compact and back via the Settings handler, with and without first opening Settings.
- The config value, density subscription and applied font size agree; reload restores the chosen value through the existing persistence mechanism.
- The command works in Dynamic and Static, closes the palette, and does not write density-cycle-requested?.
- Source hint lists only the supported tiers. A focused event/fx regression is sufficient; no new application-shaped testbed is warranted.

Deduplication: current tracker queries for palette, density, density-cycle, Cycle display density and exact notes found no dedicated open matching issue. Closed rf2-6r9j.117 concerns unread machines-viz constants, a different owner and behavior. No normative density expansion is proposed. rf2-elrh/B.9 remains unchanged. No production source edits or builds were performed.

title: docs: TESTING.md no longer names three live gates after the dehistoricalisation pass
description:
THREE LIVE GATES ARE NOW UNNAMED IN THE CANONICAL TEST-MATRIX DOCUMENT, as a side effect of the
dehistoricalisation pass that landed in PR #9674 (rf2-9yhv).

`check_doc_slugs.py`, `check_readme_links.py` and `check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py` are all live and
all run on every PR. Before #9674 their ONLY mentions in `TESTING.md` were inside retired narrative —
prose describing how some other gate came to be — so removing that narrative removed the only place the
document named them.

THE WORKER WAS RIGHT NOT TO FIX IT IN PLACE, and that reasoning is why this is a separate item rather
than a defect in #9674: rf2-9yhv was explicitly a SUBTRACTIVE pass, scoped to `TESTING.md` prose, and
adding three roster rows is an additive change requiring a decision about where they belong. Widening a
bounded pass to absorb work it discovered is how a bounded pass stops being bounded.

=== WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN AN ORDINARY DOC GAP ===

`TESTING.md` is the page that answers "which gate covers this surface, and what does it prove?". Three
gates that run unguarded on every PR being absent from it is exactly the question the document exists to
answer, failing silently — and it fails in the direction that causes real harm, because a reader who
cannot find a gate for a surface concludes the surface is ungated and either hand-verifies work already
covered, or files a bead for coverage that exists. Both have happened on this project.

=== WHAT IS ACTUALLY WANTED, AND IT IS A DECISION NOT A TRANSCRIPTION ===

These three were NEVER rostered in any table — they were only ever mentioned in passing — so this is not
restoring a deleted row. It is deciding whether the link/anchor/keyword-drift gates belong in the matrix
at all, and if so under which surface. They are cross-cutting: they grade documentation and vocabulary
across many trees rather than one artefact, which is why they never fitted the existing per-surface rows.

Note the split that makes this non-obvious, and do not collapse it: `check_doc_slugs.py` validates
anchors and repo-relative targets under `docs/`, `spec/`, `skills/`, `migration/` and `tools/*/spec`,
while `check_readme_links.py --ci` covers repo-root markdown and READMEs beside source — DIFFERENT roots,
and the job name `verify-readme-links` runs both, which reads as though it covers only the second. And
NEITHER looks inside a fenced code block. A roster row that says "link checking" without that split will
be wrong the first time somebody relies on it.

=== SCOPE ===

`TESTING.md` only. Do not change a gate, a script or a workflow. If the right answer is that these do not
belong in the matrix, say so with the reasoning and close it — a verified "no row wanted" is a complete
outcome and better than three rows nobody trusts.

=== GATE ===

`scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci` covers repo-root markdown including `TESTING.md`. The docs-slug gate
does NOT — its roots exclude the repo root, so it exits 0 on a broken link here. Neither validates prose,
tables or rendering, so verify table column counts and link targets by hand and say so in the PR body.
The file's line endings must finish with CR count == CRLF count, zero bare LF; count them with Python
reading bytes, never with `grep -c`, which reads 0 on this file and makes the check pass vacuously.
notes:
PROVENANCE: discovered by testmd-a while executing rf2-9yhv (PR #9674, merged a70b04c422). It reported the gap and correctly declined to act on it, since adding rows would have widened a subtractive pass. Recorded here so a later audit reopening rf2-9yhv recognises this as the same finding rather than a second one.

FENCE-STATE: 2026-09-11 18:00 AUSEST — NOT DISPATCHED, NOT FENCED. `TESTING.md` is free (its holder merged). Queued behind six live workers; dispatchable the moment a slot frees.

VERDICT (docsgate-a, PR #9682, awaiting merge): ROWS ARE WANTED — three added to the `Local commands` table.

The bead asked for a decision, not a transcription, and a verified "no row wanted" was an acceptable outcome. It is not the outcome: all three gates are REQUIRED and UNCONDITIONAL, verified at source rather than from the brief. `verify-readme-links` runs `check_readme_links.py --self-test`, `--ci`, and `check_doc_slugs.py --self-test` plus its live scan; `verify-skill-mcp-drift` runs `check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py`. Neither job header carries an `if:` guard, and both are in `all-required-passed`'s `needs:`.

ABSENCE CONFIRMED WITH THREE INSTRUMENTS, not one: line-oriented, whitespace-flattened, and comment-stripped-then-flattened all read 0 for each of the three script names, against a control (`check_fast_pr_gap`) reading 3.

PLACEMENT: the `Local commands` table, beside `check_jvm_lane_rosters.py` and `check_fast_pr_gap.py` — the two sibling `check_*.py` entries that already name their CI job arms there. That is why no new section was minted.

EACH ROW CARRIES THE SPLIT the bead warned a naive "link checking" row would get wrong: different roots (`DEFAULT_ROOTS` = docs/spec/skills/migration plus `tools/*/spec`, versus repo-root markdown + READMEs beside source + since rf2-i4nb2 tracked non-README markdown beside source); different duplicate-heading suffixes (MkDocs `_N` versus GitHub `-N`, the documented reason they are two scripts); the misleading job name; and CI always-on versus the spine's classifier-gated documentation tier, so a green spine is NOT evidence for a diff the classifier did not call documentation.

ONE THING THE BRIEF DID NOT SAY, verified and written into the row: the keyword-drift steps run under `continue-on-error: true`, which reads as advisory. It is not — the job's aggregator reads `outcome` (the honest signal; `conclusion` is laundered by continue-on-error) and fails the job. The `continue-on-error` buys a combined report of every broken invariant.

A closing note after the table records what neither link gate covers: both share one extractor that blanks fenced code blocks before reading a link, outside the two trees in `FENCED_DOC_LINK_TREES`.

HAND VERIFICATION (nothing gates prose or tables): Local commands table = 15 rows, every one exactly 3 pipes / 2 columns, 0 mismatches. Added lines introduce ZERO markdown links, so no new target to resolve. Line endings counted with Python reading bytes (never `grep -c`, which reads 0 here and would pass vacuously as 0 == 0): CR 325 == CRLF 325, 0 bare LF.

GATES: `check_readme_links.py --ci` exit 0 (the gate for repo-root markdown; the docs-slug gate exits 0 on a broken link here, as the bead says). Ratchets over the touched path all exit 0: retired spellings, retired composition vocab, flattened lists, escaped continuations, README inventories, EP status sync. Each nominated gate was proved to read the worker worktree by planting a fault and checking the red named it — `check_readme_links.py` exit 1 on a planted missing target at TESTING.md:121, and `check_retired_spellings.py` exit 1 with `retired-product-name:content: TESTING.md:121`. Plants restored and verified by BLOB hash against the committed object, not by reading a diff.

FINDING RECORDED AND LEFT (second sighting is a finding, not a mandate): TESTING.md line 114 claims `check_jvm_lane_rosters.py` "Runs in the fast spine and in CI's always-on `verify-readme-links` job." Not verified either way here and not touched — a pre-existing claim about a different gate, outside this bead's scope. Worth a look by whoever next holds that file.
close_reason:
Done. PR #9682 merged fe6a4cc950d8a02bf1654e5acef47dd826e580be, at band 87 with nothing
non-terminal and a clean merge-tree against trunk.

The verdict was ROWS ARE WANTED, not the "no row wanted" exit this bead explicitly allowed. The
three gates are now rostered in TESTING.md's Local commands table, beside the two sibling check_*.py
entries that already name their CI arms.

Two things the worker established that neither bead nor brief had. This bead's premise was slightly
narrower than stated: the three SCRIPT names were absent (confirmed by three instruments against a
live control), but TESTING.md still named the verify-readme-links JOB three times, so the hole was
the gates rather than the jobs -- the new rows resolve that mismatch rather than duplicating what
was already there. And the keyword-drift steps carry continue-on-error: true, which reads as
advisory and is not: the job's aggregator reads `outcome`, the honest signal, and fails the job.
That is now written into the row, because a reader who saw only the workflow would conclude the
opposite.

Both link gates and six ratchets exited 0, each proved to read the worker's own worktree by a
planted fault rather than assumed to.

title: Incomplete: metadata-key sweep still leaves the Managed-FX and Trace sites
description:
Merged-PR audit #9649, landing 6097407b967fd78aa072d5d0b60ab60412d592d0. The Epoch slice correctly repairs its six sites. The original eight-site sweep remains incomplete: two metadata React keys survive on that landing and the freshly fetched origin/main.

1. tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/managed_fx_template.cljs:346: paths-touched list emits ^{:key i} on a native [:li {...}] vector. Move i unchanged into the existing li attrs map.
2. tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/trace.cljs:505-506: the db-diff rows loop wraps (db-diff-row parent-row-id triple) with metadata {:key (pr-str path)}. Preserve that exact key on a supported attrs-map carrier or keyed fragment around the returned content.

Both work under Reagent but lose their React identity under Fresco, whose codec reads literal :key from attrs and ignores Clojure metadata. This is the same measured defect the sweep repairs, not a request to migrate additional UI now.

rf2-h100 has now been closed on the Epoch six; the remaining two were delegated in its closure/notes to in-progress implementation rf2-fcy5. Neither is an eligible open exact-defect owner. This new open Bead owns the two residual corrections explicitly; it does not reopen the completed Epoch slice or dispute its scope. Keep the edits with the existing panel migration workers to avoid concurrent edits in their files. Do not close this residual record until BOTH sites are corrected on main, even if they land in separate PRs.
acceptance_criteria: Both exact key expressions survive on a Fresco-supported key carrier, with unchanged component arguments/content. Verify keys at the renderer using raw nodes: Reagent on the full node, Fresco on head+attrs where unmigrated descendants otherwise fail. Confirm expected nonzero sibling counts and a targeted metadata revert makes the Fresco assertion red without reducing test totals. The existing panel migration may carry these fixes; no extra migration or framework is required. Both sites must be landed before this residual record is complete.
notes:
== MAYOR ACCEPTS THIS BEAD'S PREMISE AND ITS CORRECTION OF ME. BOTH SITES VERIFIED AT TRUNK. ==

The audit's judgement — that delegating these two sites into rf2-fcy5's NOTES and rf2-h100's CLOSE
REASON left "neither an eligible open exact-defect owner" — is right, and it is this project's own
rule arriving from the outside: ROUTING DOES NOT CREATE AN OWNER. I routed the two sites to the panel
workers who hold those files and recorded the split in two places, but a note inside a MIGRATION bead
is not an owner for a KEY DEFECT, and a close reason on a CLOSED bead is a record on the wrong object
because nobody reads a closed bead looking for open work. This bead is the owner. Keep it open until
both sites are on main, exactly as it says.

BOTH SITES VERIFIED AT TRUNK, and the shapes differ in a way that matters:

  managed_fx_template.cljs:346   `^{:key i}` directly above `[:li {:style …}]`.
      SHAPE 1 and the easiest kind there is — a NATIVE vector that ALREADY has an attrs map at
      index 1. Move `i` into that existing map. Nothing shifts, nothing reindents.

  trace.cljs:505-506   `(with-meta (db-diff-row parent-row-id triple) {:key (pr-str path)})`.
      NOT metadata on a call FORM — it is `with-meta` applied to the call's RETURN VALUE, so the
      metadata genuinely attaches and the key genuinely reaches React under Reagent. That is why it
      works today and why it is invisible when it breaks: Fresco's codec reads a literal `:key` from
      attrs and ignores Clojure metadata. Preserve `(pr-str path)` EXACTLY on a supported carrier —
      the returned content's attrs map, or a keyed fragment around it.

A CENSUS WARNING FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP, because I hit it while checking the audit's numbers: a
grep for `\^\{:key|with-meta` reads TWO hits in `managed_fx_template.cljs` and THREE in `trace.cljs`,
which looks like more sites than this bead claims. It is not. The extras are all COMMENT lines
(`managed_fx_template.cljs:438`, `trace.cljs:709`, `trace.cljs:826`) that DOCUMENT the hazard in
prose. The audit's one-real-site-per-file is exact. Read the hits rather than the count — this is the
prose-contaminates-a-census hazard, met inside a check of a census.

== OWNERSHIP AND SEQUENCING: DO NOT DISPATCH THIS BEAD ON ITS OWN ==

The audit's own instruction is to keep the edits with the existing panel migration workers to avoid
concurrent edits in their files, and that is also the sequencing this project's funnel forces:

  managed_fx_template.cljs  ->  `mfxmount-a`, LIVE NOW on `worker/mfxmount-a`. Its brief already
      names this site and gives the shape rules. No further message sent — the brief covers it and a
      repeat would be noise.

  trace.cljs                ->  rf2-fcy5's THIRD slice, which is HELD behind `mfxmount-a`. Not for
      concurrency reasons alone: migrating `trace/Panel` edits `mount-trace!` in `panels.cljs`, the
      file `mfxmount-a` holds, and every remaining panel migration funnels through that one file.

SO THIS BEAD CLOSES IN TWO LANDINGS, and it should not be closed on the first. If `mfxmount-a`'s PR
lands the managed-fx site, say so here and leave the bead OPEN for the trace site.

== MANAGED-FX HALF DISCHARGED BY PR #9651 (merged 2026-09-11 01:47Z, trunk cebe6ecc16).
== TRACE HALF REMAINS AND IS NOW THE WHOLE OF THIS BEAD.

`mfxmount-a` carried the managed-fx half inside the mount migration, which is the right place for
it: the key sweep and the boundary move touch the same lines, and separating them would have made
two PRs fight over one file.

WHAT IT FOUND, INCLUDING THE ZEROS -- recorded because a zero is the answer this bead's own premise
would be surprised by, and the worker took controls rather than reporting it bare:

  `managed_fx_template.cljs`  ONE `^{:key ...}` metadata site (`app-db-slice-section`'s path rows),
                              now carried in the `[:li]` attribute map.
                              ZERO `with-meta` sites. ZERO metadata on a call form.
  `panels.cljs`               ZERO of either.

  Live control at that base over `tools/xray/src`: 41 `^{:key` hits across 23 files and 18
  `with-meta` hits -- so the instrument bites, and the zeros above are absence rather than a broken
  pattern.

One of the two sites this bead was filed against had already been moved by rf2-hxfy, into
`record-panel`'s `:section` attrs. So the managed-fx surface was closer to done than the filing
knew, and the residue was a single row.

THE ASYMMETRIC KEY-GRADING PAIR, measured on this file rather than assumed. The new row grades the
key at `(.-key (codec/as-element (subvec node 0 2)))`. `r/as-element` is hollow for this sub-case --
Reagent reads metadata AND props and answers the same key either way -- and the head+attrs form is
taken because the codec lowers children eagerly, so a whole-node call raises HD-016 the moment
anything below it is still a plain fn head. On THIS file the whole-node form does answer today and
reads `[nil nil nil]` under a revert, so the `subvec` is robustness rather than a repair. Do not
carry that as a universal: it is file-dependent, and `sim_cljs_test.cljs:816` works on a whole node.

WHAT IS LEFT: the TRACE sites, and nothing else. `panels/trace.cljs` is the third slice of rf2-fcy5
and has not run. Unassigning rather than reassigning -- the trace half belongs to whoever takes that
slice, and `panels/trace.cljs` is currently held by a live worker on the alias funnel, so it is not
dispatchable as a standalone key sweep today.
Merged-PR audit #9651 independently confirms its Managed FX half is repaired at cebe6ecc1619: the exact formerly metadata-keyed paths-touched li now has :key i in attrs, with a three-row renderer-key assertion. The outstanding exact defect is still the Trace db-diff-row metadata wrapper at trace.cljs:505-506, unchanged by this PR. Reused this literal-open residual owner; no status transition. This audit refers to the paths-touched li, not the different record-panel section site previously repaired by rf2-hxfy. Browser/node CI and landed changed-blob equality verified.
close_reason:
FULLY DISCHARGED ACROSS TWO PRs. The managed-fx half landed in #9651; the Trace half landed in
PR #9661 (tracemig-a), merged 2026-09-11 at trunk 32ec776972.

This bead was filed as "Incomplete: the metadata-key sweep still leaves the Managed-FX and Trace
sites". Both named sites are now done, which is the whole of its scope.

=== THE TRACE HALF, MEASURED

ONE real `with-meta` site (`trace.cljs:505-506`) and ZERO real `^{:key ...}` sites. The key
expression is preserved BYTE-FOR-BYTE on an attrs carrier, with a codec-door gate over it.

THE TWO `^{:key` GREP HITS IN THAT FILE ARE COMMENT LINES DOCUMENTING THE HAZARD — exactly the
prose contamination this bead's own notes predicted. Live tree-wide control taken at the same time
so the zero is not a broken instrument: 33 `^{:key` across 22 files, 19 `with-meta`. The instrument
bites; the file genuinely had one site.

=== THE CODEC PREDICTION WAS CONFIRMED UNDER SABOTAGE

This bead predicted that reverting the key would make the codec read `(nil nil nil)`. Under sabotage
it read exactly that, and the node lane went to exit 1 with 5 failures and 1 error while the totals
stayed identical at 11675/58534 — i.e. the failure was the assertion firing, not a changed test
population.

=== AND THE SABOTAGE CAUGHT A HOLLOW DOOR, WHICH IS THE LESSON WORTH KEEPING

The first version of the codec door compared to the attrs it had just read rather than to the
expected key vector. Under the revert BOTH SIDES WERE NIL, they agreed, and the gate went GREEN ON
THE DEFECT — the precise thing this bead exists to prevent, reintroduced by the check meant to
prevent it. Fixed so each door compares to the LITERAL key vector.

Carry that into any future key gate: a door comparing a value to something derived from the SAME
read it is testing is hollow in the one direction that matters, and only sabotage reveals it.
`subvec` on both doors is fine; comparing the two subvecs TO EACH OTHER is not.

=== WHAT IS NOT IN SCOPE AND IS NOT LEFT UNDONE

The epoch panel's adoption of `resizable-table-view` belongs to that panel's own slice, not to this
sweep. The remaining `^{:key` and `with-meta` sites tree-wide (33 and 19 at the control reading) are
not this bead's — it named two sites and both are discharged.

title: Incomplete: Static Routes migration lacks a browser liveness and teardown witness
description:
Audited PR #9648, landing 606ba24a190ee5b94ef7cb381f4f2d38163ca5de. The Routes Panel now uses Fresco subscriptions, captured frame dispatch and a Reagent child island. Its changed node tests call panel-tree with reproduced rf/subscribe reads and identity instead of running the boundary, so they cannot detect broken boundary observation or island crossing. All four Static siblings have boundary DOM suites; Routes has none. The full feature-matrix Static-mode scenario checks first paint, is absent from PR-smoke, and does not establish this boundary's liveness, frame isolation or teardown. Source rf2-k97c.3 explicitly records this residual only in implementation notes.
Add a small browser witness through the real registered Routes panel: render under an explicit frame; change real route/simulation state and observe the mounted output update and an interaction dispatch to that frame; unmount and verify boundary subscriptions return to baseline. Reuse existing browser helpers or extend a suitable existing suite, rather than copying a large sibling suite. This is a verification gap, not an allegation of a measured runtime leak. Retain the working island; no subtree rewrite is requested.
acceptance_criteria: The registered panel renders and updates from real subscription changes under an explicit frame; interaction preserves that frame; unmount releases the observed subscriptions. A targeted fault in the actual boundary/island makes the witness red without reducing its test count; normal browser lane runs it.
notes:
== ALREADY IN FLIGHT AS `routewit-a` (worker/routewit-a), DISPATCHED ~09:56 AUSEST — DO NOT DISPATCH
== SEPARATELY. BUT IT ASKS FOR MORE THAN MY BRIEF DID, AND I HAVE SENT THE DIFFERENCE ON. ==

Filed by the #9648 merge audit at 00:25Z, about half an hour after a worker was dispatched to add the
missing Routes boundary DOM witness. Independent corroboration of the same gap: all four migrated
Static siblings ship a `panel_fresco_boundary_dom_cljs_test.cljs` and Routes ships none.

WHERE THE AUDIT IS STRICTER THAN MY BRIEF, AND IT IS RIGHT TO BE. I asked for a witness that the
boundary MOUNTS AND PAINTS. This bead asks for four things:

  1. render under an EXPLICIT FRAME;
  2. change real route/simulation state and observe the mounted output UPDATE (liveness);
  3. an interaction DISPATCH reaching that frame (frame isolation);
  4. UNMOUNT and verify boundary subscriptions return to baseline (TEARDOWN).

Only (1) and a weak form of (2) were in my brief. THE TEARDOWN CHECK IS NOT A NEW REQUIREMENT — the
parent rf2-k97c.3's own ACCEPTANCE already says "the teardown check (no retained watches or listeners
after unmount) actually measured rather than assumed". I under-specified the brief against a standard
the bead already carried, and the audit caught it.

SENT TO THE LIVE WORKER mid-flight rather than left for a second dispatch, since it is cheaper to
widen a witness being written than to write a second one later.

THE AUDIT'S OWN SCOPE LIMITS ARE WORTH PRESERVING: it says reuse existing browser helpers or extend a
suitable existing suite rather than copying a large sibling suite; that this is a VERIFICATION GAP and
not an allegation of a measured runtime leak; and that the working Reagent island stays — no subtree
rewrite.

CLOSE THIS WHEN routewit-a's PR LANDS AND THE WITNESS COVERS ALL FOUR POINTS.
close_reason:
DONE in PR #9650 (merged, trunk e4563a126f). All four points this bead asked for are covered, and the
witness is graded by the lane that actually runs it.

WHAT LANDED: `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/static/routes/panel_fresco_boundary_dom_cljs_test.cljs`,
809 lines — the suite the four migrated Static siblings all had and Routes did not.

THE FOUR POINTS, EACH WITNESSED:
  1. rendered under an EXPLICIT frame (W1);
  2. output updates on real route AND simulation state change (W2 — the worker widened this beyond
     what the bead asked, covering both);
  3. an interaction dispatch reaching the named frame (W5);
  4. UNMOUNT to baseline (W4), read through THREE reused kit instruments — `ref-count`,
     `cell-reaction` (the watch) and `cell-readers` (the listener edge), settling on
     `rf.fresco.test.runtime/quiesced!`.

TEARDOWN IS CLEAN AND THAT IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT AN ABSENCE OF EVIDENCE: mounted `[1 1 1 2]` /
4 cells / 4 reader-edges -> unmounted `[0 0 0 0]` / 0 / 0, and reopening reads identical. No leak was
alleged and none was found. The bead's own framing — a verification gap, not an allegation of a
measured runtime leak — was respected exactly.

== THE GATE NOMINATION IN MY BRIEF WAS WRONG AND THE WORKER FOUND IT ==

I nominated `npm run test:cljs` and the full feature gate. NEITHER RUNS A DOM SUITE. A
`*_dom_cljs_test.cljs` namespace belongs to shadow-cljs' `:browser-test` build and is graded by
`npm run test:browser` (CI's `cljs-browser` job); under `test:cljs` it merely LOADS and every row
short-circuits on `(browser?)`. TESTING.md line 28 states this outright and line 196 documents this
exact failure as a "stated green skip" — the tree had the answer and I did not look. Relayed to the
other live workers and recorded as a standing merge-time check on rf2-k97c.3.

== THE HOLLOW-GATE PROOF IS THE STRONGEST PART, AND IT WAS RUN TWICE ==

Plant 1, the naive migration (`r/as-element` -> `identity`): baseline exit 0 at 930 tests / 5141
assertions; planted exit 1 at 930 / 5136, all five rows red, first failure
`expected: (some? (testid container "rf-xray-static-routes"))` — the tab paints nothing, matching the
feature gate's own `(last=null)`.

Plant 2, a DELIBERATE TEARDOWN LEAK (first `teardown!` skipped), run precisely because a passing
teardown row is the kind that passes vacuously: exit 1, W4 red on all three instruments printing
`Residue: {:ref-counts [1 1 1 2], :live-cells [all four], :reader-edges 4}`.

TEST COUNT IDENTICAL AT 930 EITHER SIDE OF BOTH PLANTS — a genuine runtime failure, not a load error
running nothing. Both plants existed only in the worker's tree, so the red is itself proof the gate
read that tree. Restores verified by `git hash-object` against the committed object plus
`git diff --quiet HEAD`.

== TWO FINDINGS CARRIED FORWARD ==

`static/routes/panel.cljs` DID need one change, flagged rather than made silently: `panel-tree`'s
docstring census said eight plain-fn heads where there are nine. The missed one, `browse_list.cljs:71`,
has its head at END OF LINE — invisible to a pattern anchored on a following space, which is the
instrument hazard CLAUDE.md catalogues, met inside a census whose own docstring bills itself
re-runnable. Line numbers were dropped rather than re-pinned, and the hazard recorded.

The stale prose was wrong for ALL FIVE Static panels, not just Routes, so the worker corrected the
Static inventory WHOLE — correcting one row of five would have made Routes read as the odd one out.
It deliberately did NOT touch the Dynamic tables, which are stale for six of ten; that is rf2-u68x.

title: spec(xray): mount-fn contract step 2 names (rf/make-frame ...), which no mount fn calls — and omits the hook-table seeding
description:
THE MOUNT-FN CONTRACT'S STEP 2 NAMES A CALL NO MOUNT FN MAKES, AND OMITS THE HALF THAT MATTERS.

`tools/xray/spec/007-UX-IA.md` §`The mount-fn contract`, step 2, under the universal
"Every `mount-<panel>!` fn:", reads:

    2. Calls `(rf/make-frame {:id :rf/xray})` — idempotent register of
       Xray's state-isolation frame.

MAYOR-VERIFIED AT SOURCE, trunk bad36b747c, nonsense control zero:

  - NO mount fn calls `rf/make-frame`. The only occurrence of that symbol in `panels.cljs` is
    at :197, inside a comment explaining why a direct call would be WRONG.
  - The real path is `panels.cljs`'s private `ensure-xray-handlers-installed!` routing through
    `mount/ensure-xray-frame!` (`mount.cljs:380`).

`panels.cljs:193-206` states the reason in terms, and it is the substance this bead is about:

    "Routes through `mount/ensure-xray-frame!` so the frame is not just registered but ALSO
     seeded via the first-mount hook table -- `::seed-trace-and-target-frame`,
     `::reset-transient-filters`, `::seed-configured-filters`, `::hydrate-static-mode`,
     `::auto-open-watcher`. A direct `(rf/make-frame {:id :rf/xray})` here would register the
     frame but skip the hook table, leaving Xray's trace-buffer slot empty + `:target-frame`
     pinned to `defaults/default-target-frame` ... That misalignment is the
     EMPTY-XRAY-ON-STORY-RHS class of bug -- Story embeds a panel via `mount-<panel>!`, the
     panel renders against a frame the hooks never populated, and the user sees blank inputs
     even though the host has been dispatching events."

title: SSR strip-prop?'s JSX source-coord class has no test at all — including the upstream-of-grammar-gate ordering property
description:
THE JSX SOURCE-COORD STRIP CLASS HAS NO SSR TEST AT ALL — MEASURED, NOT INFERRED. Filed from rf2-twyh, whose brief asked whether `ssr_emit_test.clj` reading ZERO for the three newer strip classes was two files owning different halves of the surface, or an assertion set that never grew. The answer is BOTH, split by class — and the split exposes one genuine hole. === WHAT WAS MEASURED (trunk e9d90444a40c6f759e3f0b2569ce3cae495e89ba) === `strip-prop?` in implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/html_helpers.cljc drops six classes. Test coverage in the SSR lane, by class: 1. `on*` event-handler props COVERED — unit + end-to-end 2. function-valued props COVERED — unit + end-to-end 3. prototype-pollution keys COVERED — unit + end-to-end 4. JSX source-coord props ** NOT COVERED ANYWHERE ** 5. structural slots `:key` `:ref` COVERED — unit + all four emitter surfaces 6. content channels COVERED — unit + all four emitter surfaces Classes 5 and 6 are NOT a gap: `ssr_attr_filter_test.clj` absorbed their end-to-end obligation itself, in `structural-slots-drop-on-every-emitter-that-shares-the-roster` (line 175) and `content-channels-drop-on-every-emitter-that-shares-the-roster` (line 305), each exercising the hiccup body emitter, the streaming shell walker and the byte-for-byte agreement between them. So `ssr_emit_test.clj`'s zero for those two is the two files owning different halves, exactly as the alternative hypothesis said. Class 4 is a real hole. Census over the WHOLE implementation/ssr subtree, case-insensitive on `jsx`: 13 hits, ALL of them in html_helpers.cljc, i.e. the source. ZERO in implementation/ssr/test/. A fixed-string census on `_jsxFileName` across implementation/ returns four files — html_helpers.cljc, core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs, and two reagent adapter devtools tests — so the pattern demonstrably bites, and none of the three non-SSR hits exercises the SSR stripper. === WHY IT HAPPENED, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING === `git log -S` says the class was added in exactly one commit: `62d5b57e75` (2026-05-27), "feat(framework): reg-view React DevTools quick wins — displayName + JSX source-coord props + Context label (rf2-fa4ly)". Its stat under implementation/ssr is ONE FILE, 23 insertions, 2 deletions — source only, no test. The SSR-side stripper was a defensive rider on a commit whose subject was a DevTools feature elsewhere, and it shipped untested and stayed untested for about three and a half months. That is the same commit and the same date on which the spec enumerations went short (rf2-2fes), so one rider produced both a documentation drift and a coverage hole. === WHAT THE TEST SHOULD ASSERT === The class is not merely "drops three names" — it has a documented ORDERING property that nothing pins. Per `jsx-source-prop-names`' own comment and the `attr-string` docstring, the stripper sits UPSTREAM of the attribute-name grammar gate specifically so a user-carried JSX source-coord prop passes through cleanly instead of surfacing as an `:rf.error/ssr-invalid-attribute-name` throw — the leading underscore fails the conservative HTML5 grammar `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_:-]*`. So the valuable assertions are: * `[:div {:_jsxFileName "app.cljs" :_jsxLineNumber 12 :_jsxColumnNumber 3}]` emits `
` and does NOT throw — the ordering property, which is the one that would regress silently if the filter ever moved below the grammar gate. * surviving attributes on the same element are untouched. * matched CASE-SENSITIVELY against exactly those three names — the comment says the matcher deliberately pins the three documented names rather than a broad underscore prefix, so an app's own underscore-prefixed prop STILL surfaces the grammar error. That negative is the half that pins the design decision. `ssr_attr_filter_test.clj` is the right home — it is the roster's owner and already carries one deftest per class. Whether to add the four-surface sweep the two 2026-09-10 classes got is a judgement call; the ordering property is the part with real value, and it is reachable at the `attr-string` unit level. === NOT A REGRESSION, AND NOT URGENT === The behaviour is CORRECT today — the SSR JVM suite is green (672 tests / 4454 assertions), and the stripper does what its comment says. This is missing coverage on a defensive path, not a live defect, which is why it is filed separately rather than folded into rf2-twyh's prose change. Sizing: one deftest, roughly the shape of `attr-string-drops-prototype-pollution-keys` next door.

title: docs: three sites say clojure -P enforces Xray's release ordering; release-xray.yml has no such step (clein pom does it)
description:
Found while writing the tools-tier recovery cascade for rf2-yskb (PR #9549). Verified at
source at f12d8c310d, with a working control.

THE CLAIM, IN THREE PLACES: that `clojure -P` resolving the rewritten graph from Clojars is
what enforces Xray's release ordering.

  - docs/release-process.md:158 -- "After each workflow rewrites :local/root -> :mvn/version,
    `clojure -P` resolves the rewritten graph from Clojars, so a coordinate that has not
    published yet fails the job at classpath resolution".
  - docs/release-process.md:162 -- the closed rf2-5dut1 note, "enforced by `clojure -P`
    resolving the rewritten graph from Clojars".
  - .github/workflows/release-xray.yml:60 -- the workflow's own header comment repeats it.

IT IS TRUE FOR machines-viz AND story, AND FALSE FOR XRAY. release-xray.yml contains no
executable `clojure -P` at all: the only occurrence in that file is the prose comment at :60.
Its deploy job runs exactly three steps after the cache -- rewrite (:239-261), preflight
(:284-288), deploy (:290-295).

WHAT ACTUALLY ENFORCES IT: preflight-xray-package.sh:135 runs `clojure -M:clein pom`, which
forces the cold resolve as a SIDE EFFECT of building the pom. The script's own assertions are
pom-CONTENT checks -- it reads the pristine committed deps.edn via `git show HEAD:...`, derives
the required coordinate set with the Clojure reader, refuses a vacuous zero count, then parses
the generated pom and asserts presence, completeness and exact-VERSION pinning.

CONTROL (the search is live, so the xray zero is a real negative): the same fixed-string search
returns real executable hits in release-story.yml at :373 and :512, and in
release-machines-viz.yml at :278.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING PEDANTRY: the effect is the same today -- both commands fail
before `clein deploy` touches Clojars -- so nothing is broken. The cost is to the reader
DEBUGGING a failed xray tag, who is told to look for a resolution step that does not exist in
that workflow, and to anyone reasoning about whether the gate still holds if the preflight is
reordered or its pom build is replaced. The two mechanisms have different failure surfaces:
`clojure -P` is a dedicated resolve step, while xray's resolve is incidental to pom generation
and would vanish if that step were ever swapped for one that does not resolve.

SCOPE: three prose sites, one of them a workflow comment. Deliberately NOT fixed in PR #9549 --
that lane's surface was docs/release-process.md and docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md only, and a
correct fix touches .github/workflows/release-xray.yml, which was outside it. The new cascade
paragraphs in that PR sidestep the issue by saying "fails at dependency resolution" without
naming a command, so they are correct for all three workflows and this bead is not a
prerequisite for anything.

Sequencing note: release-xray.yml is a workflow file, so this is hot-zone by the
.github/workflows/* rule -- do not run it in parallel with another worker touching workflows.

## THE RESIDUAL WAS REAL AND THE FIXTURE WAS A FALSE GREEN FOR ITS OWN CRITERIA

The audit established, and I verified both load-bearing claims at source before dispatching: `check-trace-emissions` is an **order-preserving SUBSET** matcher whose own docstring says "Extras between matches are tolerated", so asserting a `scheduled` trace does not exclude a later cancellation; and `:fixture/calls` are "pure-function assertions, run AFTER dispatches", so the fixture's tail fed a hard-coded snapshot to pure `machine-transition`, disconnected from the timer `:rf/hydrate` actually armed. Neither *exactly one armed timer* nor *expiry of that timer* was graded.

## THE HARNESS AFFORDANCE, AND WHY ITS SHAPE IS THE RIGHT ONE

`:fixture/clock` in `conformance_runner.cljc`. A fixture carrying the key runs its dispatches with the **Spec 005 §Clock-abstraction primitives** (`rf.interop/schedule-after!` / `cancel-scheduled!`) replaced by a recording realisation, then runs three orthogonal steps: `:assert-timers` (live cardinality + delays), `:assert-runtime-db` (mid-run submap), `:fire` (invoke a live timer's own callback). Two choices carry the whole design:

* **It observes at the clock boundary the spec already names**, not a port-internal timer table — so the assertion is about a normative seam rather than an implementation detail.
* **It counts LIVE timers (armed minus cancelled)**, which is precisely what makes cancel-after-arm detectable. A count of *armed* would have reproduced the original false green.

--- DECISION 2026-09-08 22:59:16 AUSEST — DECLINED. Region-sourced cross-region transitions stay rejected; record the divergence, teach three coordination spellings. ---

THE DECISION. re-frame2 will NOT support a region-sourced cross-region transition (a `:target` declared inside region `:a` whose head names sibling region `:b`). The registration rejection that landed in PR #9404 (`:rf.error/machine-unresolved-target`) is now a RULED position, not an open question. The deliverable is PROSE IN `spec/005-StateMachines.md` PLUS ONE SMALL REGRESSION FIXTURE — no engine change, no new public primitive, no conflict-resolution framework. Two independent reviews (the dossier author and Codex, the latter running executable probes against XState `6.0.0-alpha.17`/`.52` and against this checkout) reached the same disposition by different routes.

WHY, COMPRESSED. Keeping each region responsible for its own transitions gives authors — and their AI — ONE selection rule to learn. A cross-region target hands one region authority to override another region's locally selected response; that is an additional public semantic commitment, and today it is unreachable, so no conflict policy exists or is needed. Region transition domains are disjoint by construction (`parallel.cljc:256` `build-region-machine` hands the engine one region's body alone), the only contest that exists is region-versus-root, and it is settled by a one-sentence rule (`parallel.cljc:1496` — the root fires only when NO region handled the event). Adopting the v6 form creates region-versus-region for the first time. This is a judgment about the resulting programming model, NOT a claim that the implementation is hard: `apply-root-region-target` (`parallel.cljc:1068`) is a plausible reusable target-region cascade, and Codex is right that adoption is technically viable.

WHERE THE REVIEWERS DISAGREED — CODEX WON EVERY CONFLICT, AND THREE OF THE CORRECTIONS CHANGE WHAT GETS WRITTEN.

(1) THE BIG ONE — "Spelling A is behaviourally identical to v6" IS FALSE. The dossier's §3.2 (write the transition on the TARGET region's own root `:on`, guarded on the source region's `:all-state`) was claimed as an exact match. It is not, and the counterexample is one line: add a targetless `:on {:help {}}` to `:helper`'s `:closed` state. Under XState native cross-region, the wizard still targets `:helper/:hint` — the targetless helper transition exits no state and does not conflict. Under the re-frame2 rewrite, the helper's LEAF handler suppresses its own region-root fallback and the hint STAYS CLOSED. Codex executed both configurations under `6.0.0-alpha.17` and `.52` and executed the re-frame2 rewrite; the difference is observed, not hypothetical. VERIFIED AT SOURCE FOR THIS RULING at `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc:1470` — `pick-transition` walks leaf->root over the active state-path nodes FIRST and consults the machine root's own `:on` fallback "only when no state-path node handled the event"; inside a region's synthetic machine that root IS the region root. GENERAL FORM OF THE TRAP: moving a rule from source to target also changes WHICH SOURCE-SIDE DESCENDANTS CAN OVERRIDE IT. Codex's measurement beats the dossier's derivation, which its own §8 admits was never run. THE SPEC MUST STATE THIS LIMIT; a worked example that promises universal equivalence would be teaching a falsehood that an expert with the source open already fell for.

(2) "v6's cross-region form cannot move source and sibling atomically" IS FALSE. The dossier §3.3/§3.4 claimed re-frame2's root multi-target `[[:a :x] [:b :y]]` is strictly beyond v6. Codex ran a transition on `wizard.step2` with `target: ['#wizardStep3','#helperHint']` and BOTH regions moved, in both tested alphas; the single-target domain-narrowing example does not prohibit a multi-target transition (primary source: https://stately.ai/docs/transitions#multiple-transitions-in-parallel-states). So DO NOT write "re-frame2 can do something v6 cannot" on this axis. What SURVIVES unrefuted is the OTHER root-form capability: a multi-region default that is ATOMICALLY SUPPRESSED the moment any region competes (`parallel_root_on_test.clj:125-141` — root `{:reset {:target [[:a :initial] [:b :initial]]}}` with `:a` declaring its own `:reset`, dispatch from `{:a :initial :b :resting}` yields `{:a :special :b :resting}`, NOT `{:a :special :b :initial}`; a broadcast decomposition cannot express this). That one is real and is the honest root-form selling point.

(3) "Adopting requires importing SCXML optimal-enablement-set and document-order preemption" IS OVERSTATED. Some conflict policy is necessary; document-order preemption is only one choice, and simply REJECTING conflicting selected targets is another (with its own ergonomic cost). Also: the v6 domain change is NOT a move toward SCXML — SCXML says transitions crossing parallel children EXIT the parallel ancestor and its overlapping exit sets drive preemption (https://www.w3.org/TR/scxml/#removeConflictingTransitions), whereas XState now NARROWS the domain to the targeted region; XState's own code separates target-domain narrowing from exit-set conflict filtering. So do NOT cite "the standard requires it" in either direction. THE SURVIVING ARGUMENT, and the one to write down, is the narrower one: a NEW CONFLICT CLASS with no precedent in this codebase, requiring a new normative rule. A note that stands regardless: re-frame2 states TWICE (`spec/005:1632`, `:1708`; guaranteed by `parallel.cljc:873-880`'s frozen SELECT pass) that region declaration order governs ONLY apply ordering, NEVER which sibling transitions are selected — a document-order preemption rule would invert that contract, so if adoption is ever revisited, that spelling of the conflict policy is the one to avoid.

(4) THE RECONSIDERATION TRIGGER IS LOWER THAN THE DOSSIER PROPOSED. The dossier wanted "v6 stable release AND a concrete authoring case neither spelling expresses". Codex: do not demand an impossibility proof or a stable v6 release — PROGRAMMER FRICTION IS SUFFICIENT EVIDENCE IN A PRE-ALPHA PROJECT. Codex wins; that matches the posture (trust the programmer, no ceremony). TRIGGER AS RULED: a real machine where the sanctioned spellings are substantially more cumbersome, or lose required ordering. Release status is explicitly NOT the reason for this decline and must not be written as one (dist-tags re-read for both reviews: `latest` 5.32.6, `beta` 5.0.0-beta.54, `alpha` 6.0.0-alpha.52, zero stable v6 — cited as context only). EP-0029 C17's rejected "don't chase alpha churn" stance is consistent with the decline but is NOT load-bearing for it; if v6 shipped stable tomorrow this ruling would be unchanged.

title: hygiene: the §5 branch sweep's 'is this branch owned?' check misses every retained-record ruling, because bd search defaults to OPEN
description:
ROOT CAUSE of rf2-jojz, which was the THIRD re-filing of the same settled question (rf2-fuuqd 2026-08-15 -> rf2-7ngc 2026-09-02 -> rf2-jojz 2026-09-06).

The bd memory 'hygiene-cannot-tell-a-strand-from-a-retained-record' prescribes the discriminator: 'search the tracker for the branch name before calling anything stranded. A retained record says so in the bead that closed it.' That instruction is correct and the check is cheap. It is also BROKEN AS WRITTEN, and it fails in the reassuring direction.

MEASURED 2026-09-07 09:1x AUSEST:
  bd search 'receipts-hic081'                  -> 1 hit: rf2-jojz, the sweep's OWN filing
  bd search 'receipts-hic081' --status closed  -> rf2-7ngc, rf2-pi2p (the rulings)

bd search DEFAULTS TO OPEN ISSUES. A retained-record ruling lives, by definition, on a CLOSED bead — the bead that closed with 'retained as the experiment's record' is the whole artefact being looked for. So the prescribed check can never find one, and returns either nothing or the sweep's own prior filing. rf2-jojz's description says 'none has a bead' in exactly those terms; that sentence is the false zero speaking.

Compaction makes it worse but is NOT the cause. rf2-hic-081, rf2-fuuqd and rf2-lafmr have all left the live tracker (bd show: no issue found), so even a closed-inclusive title search finds them only via rf2-7ngc, which quotes them. The defect would bite with all three still present, because they are closed.

THE FIX, in the sweep step itself:
  bd search <branch-name> --status closed
  bd memories <branch-name>
both, before a branch is filed as orphaned or stranded. Neither is expensive; the second is what actually holds the standing rule here.

Also update the memory 'hygiene-cannot-tell-a-strand-from-a-retained-record' so its prescribed command carries --status closed. As written it sends the next reader down the same path.

WHERE THE SWEEP STEP LIVES: docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md, the branch/hygiene section (the '§5' the rf2-jojz description cites). Confirm the exact heading before editing; the doc is the normative copy and CLAUDE.md points at it rather than restating it.

ACCEPTANCE: a sweep run against worker/receipts-hic081 reports it as a retained record with the owning ruling cited, rather than filing it. That branch is the standing test case and must NOT be deleted to test this.
acceptance_criteria: A §5 sweep over worker/receipts-hic081 identifies it as a deliberately retained spike record citing rf2-7ngc, instead of filing it as orphaned. Memory text updated to carry --status closed.
notes:
WORKER gates-a, 2026-09-07. Implemented on worker/gates-a, PR #9364 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9364). Bead left OPEN for the mayor.

WHERE THE BROKEN CHECK WAS WRITTEN DOWN, and there was MORE THAN ONE COPY.
Not in a script -- no branch-sweep script exists (scripts/ has none; checked the whole directory).
NOT in docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md either, which is the bead's stated location. Confirmed the
heading before editing, as the bead asked: section 5 "Hygiene" -> "### Branches" reasons at length
about CONTAINMENT (patch-equivalence, why `+` is only absence of proof) and says NOTHING about
OWNERSHIP. It carries no tracker check at all, and loops.md is deliberately tracker-agnostic
("your tracker CLI"); `bd search` appears nowhere in any tracked file.

The check existed only in bd memories, in TWO copies:
  1. hygiene-cannot-tell-a-strand-from-a-retained-record -- "search the tracker for the branch name
     before calling anything stranded"
  2. absent-remote-branch-is-the-signature-of-a-merge -- "Search the tracker for the branch name
     before filing a branch for decision"
Correcting (1) and leaving (2) is exactly this bead family's failure mode, so BOTH were corrected.
A third, worker-receipts-hic081-is-a-retained-spike-record, was already correct on the status axis
("check whether a CLOSED bead retained it on purpose") and was left alone.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE BEAD'S PRESCRIBED FIX, both measured on worker/receipts-hic081.
(a) USE --status all, NOT --status closed. Measured: default 1 hit, --status closed 3, --status all 4.
    --status closed DROPS rf2-xcqk -- the OPEN bead carrying the standing KEEP and its release
    condition. It swaps one blind spot for another, which is the same species as the original defect.
(b) NO STATUS FLAG IS SUFFICIENT. `bd search` matches TITLES AND IDS ONLY (its own --help says so),
    so a retention recorded in a CLOSE REASON -- which is where retentions are written -- is invisible
    at every status. Measured: `bd search "retained as the experiment" --status all` returns 0 while
    the export carries that phrase in 4 records. Control sharing the shape (two-word phrase, but
    present in a TITLE): `bd search "stranded sweep" --status all` returns 1. So the four hits in (a)
    are luck -- they are beads whose TITLES happen to name the branch. Grepping .beads/issues.jsonl
    finds 7 carriers of "receipts-hic081" against bd search's 4.
The memory bd-search-matches-titles-only-and-excludes-closed (2026-08-22) already recorded (b) and
was not cross-referenced from either copy; both corrections now point at it.

WHAT LANDED.
  * docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md section 5 "Branches": one new two-paragraph block, in that doc's
    tracker-agnostic voice, covering the retained-record case, the closed-by-default failure, the
    --status closed trap and the title-only trap. This is the durable fix: a memory is not what the
    loop reads, the doc is.
  * Both memories corrected in place. `bd remember --key <existing>` REPLACES, so each was re-sent as
    full original text + appended correction; verified afterwards that the original opening survives
    and lengths grew (2633->4757 and 3033->3953).

ACCEPTANCE DEMONSTRATED. The corrected check over worker/receipts-hic081 returns:
`bd search --status all` -> rf2-7ngc (KEEP, citing rf2-lafmr), rf2-pi2p, rf2-xcqk (open, standing
KEEP + release condition), rf2-jojz; export grep -> those plus rf2-4228y, rf2-wx9z, rf2-94l1;
`bd memories` -> worker-receipts-hic081-is-a-retained-spike-record. It is identified as a
deliberately retained spike record citing rf2-7ngc, not filed as orphaned.
THE BRANCH WAS NOT TOUCHED -- no delete, no tag, no push to it.

ONE MEASUREMENT IN THE BEAD HAS MOVED. The description records `bd search 'receipts-hic081'`
returning "rf2-jojz, the sweep's OWN filing". Today it returns rf2-xcqk instead, because rf2-jojz has
since closed and the default hides it. The defect is unchanged; only which bead the false zero
happens to surface has changed.
close_reason: PR #9364 merged. The fix did NOT land where the bead said it would, and that correction is the finding: worker gates-a established the broken 'is this branch owned?' check exists in NO script and NOT in loops.md — it lived ONLY in two bd memories, 'hygiene-cannot-tell-a-strand-from-a-retained-record' and 'absent-remote-branch-is-the-signature-of-a-merge'. Fixing one and leaving the other is this bead family's exact failure mode, so both were corrected, and the durable rule was added to loops.md §5 because a memory is not what the loop reads. TWO MEASURED CORRECTIONS TO THE BEAD'S OWN PRESCRIPTION: (1) the fix is '--status all', not '--status closed' — the latter drops rf2-xcqk, the OPEN bead carrying the standing KEEP for worker/receipts-hic081; (2) NO status flag suffices, because bd search matches titles and IDs only, so a ruling recorded in a CLOSE REASON is invisible at every status ('retained as the experiment' returns 0 hits against 4 in the export; shape-matched control returns 1). MAYOR'S CORROBORATING MEASUREMENT from this session's §5 hygiene loop: the discriminator WORKED for worker/receipts-hic081 — but only because that KEEP had been re-carried onto an open bead. When the same ruling lived solely in the closed rf2-jojz, the identical search returned nothing and the branch read as unowned and deletable. The defect reproducing and not reproducing on ONE branch depending purely on where the ruling happened to sit.

title: docs(xray): mount-control.md says load-theme is 'not yet wired' and emits a warning that no longer exists -- a live test asserts the opposite
description:
FOUND 2026-09-05 by the rulings-a triage pass while verifying rf2-7nk1's premise. Split out of rf2-7nk1 because it is INDEPENDENT of that bead's spelling ruling: whichever way `load-theme` / `load-theme!` is settled, this doc page is wrong today, and if rf2-7nk1 is ruled "leave it", the defect stays buried in a closed ruling bead.

THE DEFECT, measured at tip aa3c616e46.

docs/xray/api/mount-control.md:120 reads:
  "Programmatically swap the Xray shell's CSS theme. The theme module exists (`day8.re-frame2-xray.theme/*`) but the runtime CSS-swap surface is not yet wired. Calling emits `:rf.warning/xray-load-theme-not-yet-implemented` so the gap is visible in the trace stream. Forward-compatible -- host code may call with a CSS string today and expect the impl to land later."

Every clause of that is false at tip:
  - IT IS WIRED. tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/core.cljs:259 defines `load-theme`; :270 calls `global-styles/set-host-theme-css!`, defined at tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/theme/global_styles.cljs:1656. Wired by rf2-ee38b.2.
  - THE WARNING DOES NOT EXIST. `grep -rn "xray-load-theme-not-yet-implemented" tools/xray/src` returns nothing.
  - A LIVE TEST ASSERTS ITS ABSENCE. tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/core_cljs_test.cljs:123-140, deftest `load-theme-is-safe-without-document`, filters the trace stream for that exact warning keyword and asserts the result is empty: "no not-yet-implemented warning -- the stub is gone". So the published doc contradicts a green test in the same repository.

CONTROL for the two zero-returning searches above, so neither is an honest-looking zero from a broken instrument: the same grep over tools/xray/src DOES find `set-host-theme-css!` (two hits, the call site and the definition), and the same warning keyword IS found in the test file. The instrument works; the absence is real.

THE REPAIR. Rewrite mount-control.md:120's Description to say what `load-theme` actually does: it installs or replaces a dedicated <style> block appended last to <head> via `set-host-theme-css!`, returns nil, and is a safe no-op with no DOM and on an empty or nil argument (all three pinned by the test above). Delete the "not yet wired", the warning-id sentence and the forward-compatible caveat.

SPELLING: use whatever spelling rf2-7nk1's ruling lands. If this bead is dispatched FIRST, write `load-theme` (the name at tip) and let rf2-7nk1's rename sweep this page — that page is already on rf2-7nk1's own blast-radius list.

NOT IN SCOPE, and deliberately: the PRODUCTION-ELISION claims on the same page (:5, :135, :196-205) and in docs/skills/re-frame2-xray.md:7 and docs/xray/01-installation.md:136. Those belong to rf2-qqn9, which already carries them in an audit note and cannot be repaired until its (A)/(B) ruling lands. This bead is the load-theme paragraph only, so the two do not collide on the same lines.

GATES BY PATH. docs/ is inside `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`'s roots, and docs/xray/ is inside `docs_dir`, so `mkdocs build --strict` builds this page -- but note it grades a missing heading ANCHOR at INFO and `--strict` does not promote INFO, so `check_doc_slugs.py` is the anchor gate. No code change, so no CLJS suite is implicated; run `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` and `mkdocs build --strict`.
