title: ssr-node: two remaining error-text paths onto public refusals — pool.cjs ISOLATE_LOST boot diagnostics, service.cjs last-resort String(error)
description:
FILED BY THE MAYOR 2026-09-05 from the ssrnode-b worker's report on PR #9278 (rf2-c38b, merged 5e7acf5a4e). Both were found while closing the exception-door leak, both were judged outside that bead's non-goals fence, and both were reported rather than changed. That judgement was right; this bead is the ruling they need.

THE TWO SITES. Verify each at tip — these are the worker's claims, and line numbers move.

1. src/pool.cjs:178 interpolates err.message into an ISOLATE_LOST refusal handed to WAITING CALLERS when a REPLACEMENT isolate fails to boot. So boot diagnostics reach a caller at runtime. rf2-c38b's non-goals fenced boot off, which is why it was left.

2. src/service.cjs:108 puts String(error) on a public refusal in a last-resort arm. The worker judged this NOT worth changing and gave a reason worth preserving: it is unreachable today (every isolate.render() path rejects with a Refusal) and would carry only THIS PACKAGE's own error text, unlike the analogous worker.cjs arm that PR #9258 hardened, which is application-adjacent.

WHY THIS IS ONE BEAD AND NOT TWO. They differ on both axes that decide the answer — reachability and whose text they carry — and ruling them together is what makes the boundary legible. The question is not "is any error text on a refusal bad" but "which side of the trust boundary authored it, and can a caller reach it". A ruling that answers only site 1 leaves the next reader re-litigating site 2 from scratch.

THE RULING NEEDED, and the stance bears on it directly. Under 'trust the programmer' and 'don't litigate the minutiae', an unreachable last-resort arm carrying the package's own text may simply be correct as written, and a bead can die with its reasoning recorded instead of consuming a worker. Under 'fail closed' and the response-egress law the package states in its own README, a refusal that can carry ANY interpolated text is a door that will be walked through eventually. Both readings are honest. Pick one per site, with the reason, and if the answer is 'leave it', say so ON the code so the next audit does not re-raise it.

WHAT WOULD MAKE SITE 1 ACTIONABLE WITHOUT A RULING, if a worker takes this: the same shape rf2-c38b landed — the diagnostic goes to the sidecar's own stderr where the operator running it can see it, and the public refusal carries the closed-taxonomy code and a fixed message. If that shape applies cleanly to pool.cjs, this is implementation rather than a decision, and the ruling is only needed for site 2.

CHECK BEFORE ACTING: this brief's premises are the worker's claims. Confirm site 2 is genuinely unreachable today (the worker's basis was that every isolate.render() path rejects with a Refusal — prove it with a control, not a bare grep), and confirm site 1's refusal really does reach waiting callers rather than only the log.

FENCE if dispatched: implementation/ssr-node/** only. spec/Conventions.md catalogues the :rf.ssr-node/* code MEMBERS and is hot-zone — if a member changes, that is a separate sequenced edit, not part of this.

  serializer row) is a string on the first read and unclonable on the
  second. postMessage then throws DataCloneError SYNCHRONOUSLY INSIDE
  render()'s promise executor — which is why it appears in no enumeration
  of that method's reject() calls.

synchronous throw, which is not a reject() call and so is invisible to any

title: flows: direct reg-flow does not materialize a new flow's initial output until an unrelated drain
description:
Sibling of the fixed rf2-g1zb, found while fixing it. NOT yet reproduced with a live probe — the evidence below is source-level, so the first task is to measure it.

CLAIM (verify at source): `re-frame.flows/reg-flow` called as a plain function OUTSIDE an event drain registers the flow and returns without running a flow pass, so the new flow's INITIAL output is not materialized until some later, unrelated drain. Source evidence: `implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/registry.cljc` `reg-flow` writes output marks, mutates the registry, drops the dirty-check row and emits traces — it contains no call to `run-flows-on-db` and no settle. That is the same shape as the clear-flow defect rf2-g1zb fixed. Its own comments note the asymmetry: a DIRECT cold `reg-flow` does not inherit the router's exact-owner predicate that the `:rf.fx/reg-flow` route does.

WHY IT IS FILED SEPARATELY AND NOT FIXED IN PR #9204: rf2-g1zb's scope and bounded recommendation were explicitly clear-flow-only, and its acceptance criteria named no reg-flow arm. PR #9204's spec wording therefore says in terms that the new Spec 013 subsection governs clear-flow only and that reg-flow's direct path is out of scope, so symmetry is NOT read into it — see spec/013-Flows.md, the subsection 'The same boundary for a direct clear-flow'. That sentence is what this bead would revisit.

WHAT IS ALREADY SPECIFIED: Spec 013 §Sequencing is NORMATIVE that a flow registered by `:rf.fx/reg-flow` has its initial output materialised, and every dependent recomputed, by the time the dispatching event settles. It is silent on the direct function, exactly as it was for clear-flow before rf2-g1zb.

FIRST STEP: reproduce. Seed app-db FIRST, then `reg-flow` a flow whose inputs are already present, then read app-db with no dispatch in between — the trap is that a probe which registers against an EMPTY db proves nothing, because there is no value to derive. Use the witness harness from `implementation/flows/test/re_frame/flows_direct_clear_settle_cljs_test.cljc`, which already carries the machinery: adjacency, a derive counter, a whole-stream :rf.event trace recorder with its own in-run positive control, and a drain-equivalence assertion. If the premise does not hold, that finding with its evidence is the deliverable.

IF IT REPRODUCES: the fix is likely one line reusing the seam PR #9204 added — `registry/set-settle-fn!` publishes an exact-owner settle installed by the facade, and `reg-flow` could call it under the same three fences clear-flow uses (inside the registration's exact-owner postcheck, out-of-drain only, inside the serialized region). Note the docs promise to reconcile: docs/core/flows.md currently states in prose that reg-flow's direct form does NOT make the matching promise about initial output and points readers at `:rf.fx/reg-flow`; docs/api/re-frame.flows.md documents the settle boundary on clear-flow only. Both would need updating alongside the spec subsection.

Consider also whether reg-flow's error surface changes: reg-flow already throws `:rf.error/flow-frame-not-live`, so a settling derive throw propagating to the direct caller is less of a departure there than it was for clear-flow.
notes:
Post-merge audit — PR #9222 (correctness + completeness): the new rationale overclaims the safety of the effect route. `spec/013-Flows.md` and `flows_direct_reg_deferral_cljs_test.cljc` say `:rf.fx/reg-flow` runs inside a drain “where app-db is by construction the application's live seeded state, so the hazard cannot arise.” A drain does not guarantee that a new flow's declared inputs exist. On merged commit `fc306b82b6434b676e34e70d1e4036e063732adb`, a fresh default frame with `{}` app-db and an event whose only effect is `[:rf.fx/reg-flow [:audit/double {:inputs [[:n]] :output-path [:out]} (fn [n] (* 2 n))]]` calls the derive once with nil, leaves db `{}`, keeps the flow registered, and emits `{:error :rf.error/flow-eval-exception, :event [:rf/settle-flows], :flow-id :audit/double, :phase :derive}`. Thus the very absent-input hazard used to justify direct-call deferral can arise through the effect route; it is merely surfaced at the effect's explicit settle boundary. The main direct-reg-flow contract and its three new behavior tests remain sound. Bounded fix: correct the false sentence in the normative spec and test docstring (and user guide if needed) to explain the actual distinction: an effect registration requests immediate evaluation, so its event must establish/precede the inputs or can fail normally; a direct registration deliberately waits for the caller's next drain. A focused effect-before-seed witness would keep that caveat executable, but no lifecycle redesign or removal of effect settling is implied.
Resolved on PR #9257 (branch worker/flowsettle-a) as the AUDIT note directs, not as the description does. The description's premise — that a direct reg-flow's missing initial-output settle is a defect to fix by symmetry with clear-flow — is superseded: PR #9222 already ruled the opposite way and landed it as NORMATIVE (Spec 013 'Why a direct reg-flow does not settle': a direct reg-flow registers without evaluating and MUST NOT settle). Nothing in that ruling was disturbed.

MEASUREMENT of the audit's claim: it REPRODUCES. The sentence ':rf.fx/reg-flow ... runs inside a drain, where app-db is by construction the application's live seeded state, so the hazard cannot arise' is false. A drain evaluates against the EVENT'S OWN pending app-db, which may be empty. Witness effect-reg-flow-evaluates-immediately-even-against-an-unseeded-db: default frame, app-db {}, one event whose only effect is [:rf.fx/reg-flow [:audit/double {:inputs [[:n]] :output-path [:out]} derive]] -> derive called exactly once with nil, app-db still {}, flow still registered, always-on record :rf.error/flow-eval-exception with :flow-id :audit/double and :phase :derive. Paired witness effect-reg-flow-succeeds-when-its-own-event-seeds-first shows the other half: the same registration on an event that seeds first yields {:n 21 :out 42} by the time the dispatch returns.

Note for any port or re-measurement: the derive is spelled with an explicit refusal on nil, not arithmetic. (* 2 nil) throws on the JVM but evaluates to 0 in CLJS, so the arithmetic form would go green on one host for the wrong reason.

FIX is prose only, three sites in one commit: the normative sentence in spec/013-Flows.md, the same reasoning in the witness file's docstring, and the user guide parenthetical in docs/core/flows.md (which now says the effect evaluates right then, so that event needs its inputs present or must seed them). The rule is unchanged; only its justification moves — from safety to RESPONSIBILITY: an effect registration is issued from inside an event, so that event is the place to establish the inputs and it requests evaluation now, a failure being an ordinary event failure at the effect's explicit settle boundary; a direct registration has no such event to be responsible for, so it declares and waits. docs/api/re-frame.flows.md documents the settle boundary on clear-flow only and needed no change. No lifecycle change, no removal of effect settling.

title: spec/009's frame-destroyed row describes the RETIRED ui (frame) bundle in the present tense, and contradicts on_error_cljs_test on whether :op is public
description:
FOUND 2026-09-04 by the rf2-xtqs worker (PR #9179), which deliberately did not widen into either of these. Both VERIFIED AT SOURCE by the mayor before filing; they are findings, not claims, but re-check them at tip because #9179 moves lines in both files.

DEFECT 1 — spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2159 describes a REMOVED surface in the present tense.

The :rf.error/frame-destroyed catalogue row narrates the retired implementation/ui (frame) operation bundle as a live throwing surface. Verbatim, at tip: "A substrate's (frame) operation bundle (rf2-vxgfnd.230) is a further throwing surface for the SAME category ... The incarnation fence emits at the ui source BEFORE delegating to core's dispatch/subscribe, so the same failure is never ALSO fanned by the router/subs recover-and-emit path ... all four bundle arms route through one ui-frame emit-and-throw helper so their two-channel contract cannot drift."

implementation/ui was RETIRED AND REMOVED (rf2-0yp7w, executed by PR #8322 on 2026-08-16); git ls-files returns nothing under it. So there is no ui source emitting anything, no incarnation fence, and no four bundle arms. A reader takes this row as a description of live behaviour because every verb in it is present tense.

SCOPE AGAINST #9179, and this is the part to get right: #9179 removes the :capture enum value and the clauses that attribute it to the ui surface. IT DOES NOT TOUCH THE REST OF THE PASSAGE. So do not read a merged #9179 as having fixed this — check what survives, then decide per sentence whether it is (a) live behaviour that outlived the ui and should be re-attributed to router/subs, (b) retirement bookkeeping that should be past-tensed and dated to rf2-0yp7w, or (c) a claim about a surface that no longer exists and describes nothing, which is rf2-63t1i's rule and the ground #9179 stood on.

CLAUDE.md's Architecture Overview is the governing distinction: a donor reference is either retirement bookkeeping or the reserved-kind contract, and is never a surface to build on. Neither exemption obviously covers a present-tense operational narration, but read both before deleting anything.

DEFECT 2 — the tree contradicts itself on whether :op is PUBLIC or PRIVATE.

  spec/Spec-Schemas.md:1201            ";; enum ratified PUBLIC on this category (per the 009 catalogue row)"
  spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2159     ":op (the failing operation realm ... a small closed-enum public realm attribution"
  implementation/core/test/re_frame/on_error_cljs_test.cljc:823
                                       ";; PRIVATE steering input (read from the record's attribution, never promoted to"

Two normative documents say PUBLIC; a test header says PRIVATE and never-promoted. One of the three is wrong. This matters beyond tidiness because :op's publicness is what licenses consumers to switch on it, and a test header is exactly where an implementer looks to learn whether a slot is contractual.

DETERMINE WHICH IS AUTHORITATIVE RATHER THAN HARMONISING THE WORDING. The spec is the artefact and the code is downstream, so the presumption is that the two spec documents govern and the test header is stale — but check whether the header is describing something narrower and true (:op as a steering input to error-source-coord's realm-exact resolution, which IS an internal use) that has merely been worded as a global claim. If so the fix is to narrow the header, not to invert it.

FENCE — DO NOT DISPATCH UNTIL PR #9179 MERGES. Both spec/Spec-Schemas.md and spec/009-Instrumentation.md are HOT ZONE and #9179 edits BOTH in one commit. The hazard is the stale-copy revert: a branch cut before #9179 lands silently undoes its :capture removal while passing every gate, because a revert of a merged change is well-formed and every checker reads it as clean. RE-READ BOTH FILES AT TIP AFTER IT MERGES; the line numbers above will have moved.

GATES. The cross-file gate is tags-column-keys-are-documented, a JVM deftest at implementation/core/test/re_frame/error_catalogue_channel_conformance_test.clj:1483 — it REDS if 009 and Spec-Schemas disagree, so both files move in ONE commit. NEITHER DOC GATE COVERS THE SCHEMA HALF: check_doc_slugs.py and mkdocs build --strict share one extractor that strips fences before reading a link, and the FrameDestroyedTags schema lives inside a fence. Run them for the 009 prose row, but hand-check the fenced block and the row's pipe count (7, matching its siblings) and say so in the PR body. mkdocs is not on PATH here; use python -m mkdocs.
notes:

title: Clarify SSR Ring HTTP metadata helper roles
description:
## Finding

The internal cookie/header/trust helpers use generic names that hide which HTTP value is being validated or accumulated. In cookie.clj, private url-encode and validate-attribute-string! do cookie-specific work while parameters such as s, v, and n erase that context. In headers.clj, the folds use m/k/v, v*, key*, and existing across case-folding and multi-value promotion. trust.clj similarly validates k/v. These names make security-sensitive wire code harder to audit.

## Evidence

- implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/cookie.clj:37-112: url-encode is specifically a cookie-value encoder; validate-attribute-string! is specifically the Set-Cookie attribute injection gate.
- implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/headers.clj:17-122: m/k/v and starred temporaries cover the Ring header map, logical header name/value, wire-coerced value, emitted key, and existing value.
- implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/trust.clj:81-102: k/v are trusted-shell option key/value.
- API-manifest configuration classifies these sub-namespaces as internal. The public facade name cookie->set-cookie-header and every header/error/wire key remain contracts.
- History shows these helpers were extracted as implementation plumbing; repository-wide searches find no external call to the private cookie helpers.
- Phase-1 beads rf2-6r9j.47/.50 own removal/lint residue, not these surviving names.

## Recommendation

Rename only private helpers, parameters, and locals to their domain roles: encode-cookie-value, validate-cookie-attribute!, cookie-name/attribute-value, ring-headers/header-name/header-value, wire-value/emitted-key/existing-value, and option-key/option-value. Update internal docstrings and all callers. Preserve public function names, facade arglists, error ids, ex-data keys, warning tags, ordering, coercion, casing, and Set-Cookie bytes.

## Risks / contracts

No serialized key, header spelling, error id, protocol vocabulary, public facade var, or behavior may change. Parameter-name changes in internal namespace arglists are documentation-only, but all direct tests must continue to compile.

## Acceptance criteria

- The generic helper/local names above are replaced consistently and exact old-name searches leave no stale implementation references beyond unrelated prose.
- Public names and wire/error shapes are unchanged.
- Cookie/header materialiser and trusted-shell tests pass.
- Focused lint is clean apart from independently-owned Phase-1 findings.
close_reason: Implemented scoped internal/private/local clarity renames; preserved public and wire contracts; clj-kondo, 231-test default lane, 9-test JVM-Node crossing lane, exact searches, and diff-check all pass.

title: Core trace tooling: name deferred-fanout queue accessors by returned carrier
description:
Partition: implementation/core trace, listener, and post-drain delivery tooling.

Evidence:
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace/tooling.cljc defines private deferral-pending, set-deferral-pending!, and clear-deferral-pending!.
- deferral-pending returns the current host-specific volatile FIFO queue or nil; pending is a value carrier, not a predicate. The accessor is consulted by call-with-deferred-fanout and deliver-to-tooling!, while pending is also used as the opaque parameter in drain-deferred-batch! and flush-deferred-fanout!.
- Targeted history shows this vocabulary entered with the CLJS post-drain parity fix 7c3275d47e. All affected helpers are private; the public no-doc call-with-deferred-fanout name and late-bind key are separate contracts and remain unchanged.
- Exact all-status bead searches by symbols and deferred-fanout queue concept found no duplicate.

Ambiguity cost:
The noun pending does not say what value is carried and resembles predicate vocabulary. In the concurrency-sensitive deferral seam, a reader has to repeatedly recover that the object is a volatile queue of deferred fan-out entries, not a boolean or a batch value.

Recommendation:
Rename the accessor family to current-deferred-fanout-queue, set-current-deferred-fanout-queue!, and clear-current-deferred-fanout-queue!. Rename local/parameter carriers from pending to deferred-queue in the accessor, drain, flush, call wrapper, and delivery branches.

Risks/contracts:
Preserve the ThreadLocal-versus-CLJS-volatile storage, scope nesting, listener snapshot, FIFO order, monitor boundaries, production elision, public call-with-deferred-fanout symbol, and :trace.tooling/call-with-deferred-fanout late-bind key.
acceptance_criteria:

- The queue bindings in drain-deferred-batch!, flush-deferred-fanout!, call-with-deferred-fanout, and deliver-to-tooling! identify the carrier as deferred-queue.
- Exact search finds no code reference to deferral-pending, set-deferral-pending!, clear-deferral-pending!, or a bare pending binding in this seam.
- Focused JVM trace-listener deferral/serialization tests and CLJS compilation/lint coverage pass, and git diff --check passes.
- Public symbols, late-bind keys, trace operation IDs, ordering, synchronization, and elision behaviour are unchanged.

title: Give local Test-React changes a precise CI surface instead of the shipped-adapter fan-out
description:
## Finding

`.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh:915-931` sends every path under `implementation/adapters/*` through the shipped-adapter fan-out. Test-React is the documented exception to that population: it is a local-only CLJC fixture, has no Maven coordinate or production consumer, and owns no browser testbed.

Measured commands at the audited tip:

```
bash .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh implementation/adapters/test-react/src/re_frame/adapter/test_react.cljc
bash .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh implementation/adapters/test-react/test/re_frame/adapter/test_react_cljs_test.cljc
bash .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh implementation/adapters/test-react/deps.edn
bash .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh implementation/adapters/test-react/README.md
```

All four produce the same twelve true outputs: `implementation_jvm`, `cljs_node_test`, `adapter_diagnostic`, `cljs_browser`, `examples_compile`, `cljs_prod`, `bundle_isolation`, `adapter_testbed_smokes`, `tools_jvm`, `template_expensive`, `mcp_conformance`, and `mcp_live`. Those outputs occur in 45 job-level conditions in `test.yml` (21 JVM artefact jobs, four adapter jobs, five production jobs, four tools-JVM jobs, four MCP-conformance jobs, and seven other Node/browser/example/isolation/smoke/template/live jobs).

Only two owning jobs can reach a Test-React source/test change:

- `jvm-adapters-test-react` runs this artefact's own `clojure -M:test` alias.
- `cljs` runs Shadow's consolidated `:node-test`, whose `cljs-test$` selector discovers both Test-React `.cljc` test namespaces because `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:79-90` lists their source/test roots.

Repository-wide code search finds no require/call of `re-frame.adapter.test-react` outside its own tests. The only non-test source mention is the quoted producer roster in `re-frame.late-bind.directory`; production/example/tool entry points do not require the namespace. The adapter-smoke gate explicitly drives two testbeds at `adapters/<reagent|uix>/testbed` (`report-changed-surfaces.sh:915-920`); Test-React has no testbed. Per-artifact JVM jobs use their own deps files and cannot see this local fixture. Shadow source-path presence does not make an unrequired namespace part of an example, browser, or release build. Even a prose-only Test-React README edit currently schedules the same full fan-out.

## Impact

A local fixture edit queues 43 surface-gated jobs that cannot compile, load, or exercise the changed file, in addition to the two real host lanes. The false targets consume CI time and give a misleading wall of green results while adding no evidence about Test-React. The README case demonstrates this is stale path classification rather than conservative behavioral coverage.

## Disposition

Carve `implementation/adapters/test-react/**` out before the generic shipped-adapter arm and route it by the files each lane actually consumes. Introduce a dedicated Test-React JVM signal/job condition (or an equivalently precise mechanism) so its own JVM suite can run without opening the other three adapter jobs or all 21 `implementation_jvm` jobs. Source/test changes should retain the Test-React JVM and Node lanes; `deps.edn` must retain the JVM lane; prose should not open code lanes absent a real pin. Keep the existing reverse edge from `implementation/core/**` to Test-React's JVM suite, because the fixture depends on core.

## Risks and boundaries

Do not "optimize" away either real host: this is CLJC specifically to run under JVM and Node. `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh` currently uses `implementation_jvm` plus its artefact selector, so a new dedicated signal must be consumed there (or otherwise preserve local Test-React JVM selection). Core changes must continue to test every adapter. Do not change the generic arm for Reagent/UIx or their real browser/testbed/production consumers.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. From the repository root, run `.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh` once for each of these paths: `implementation/adapters/test-react/src/re_frame/adapter/test_react.cljc`, `implementation/adapters/test-react/test/re_frame/adapter/test_react_cljs_test.cljc`, `implementation/adapters/test-react/deps.edn`, and `implementation/adapters/test-react/README.md`.
2. Observe that all four paths set the same broad shipped-adapter outputs, including browser, examples, production, bundle-isolation, testbed, tools, template, and MCP lanes, although Test-React has no consumer in those surfaces.
3. Trace those outputs through `.github/workflows/test.yml` and confirm they fan out to unrelated jobs; separately confirm only the Test-React JVM job and consolidated Node suite consume Test-React source/test code.
4. Check `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh`: removing the broad `implementation_jvm` signal without adding a dedicated Test-React JVM signal makes a Test-React-only local diff skip its JVM suite, which is the required negative control for the proposed classifier change.
5. Preserve the `implementation/core/**` reverse edge to the Test-React JVM job while reproducing or fixing the local-path fan-out.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Representative Test-React source and test paths schedule its own JVM suite and the consolidated Node suite, while no longer scheduling Reagent/UIx testbed smokes, browser DOM, examples, production, bundle-isolation, tools, template, or MCP jobs that cannot reach the fixture.
2. `implementation/adapters/test-react/deps.edn` schedules the Test-React JVM suite; `implementation/adapters/test-react/README.md` schedules no executable lane unless a documented byte/content pin genuinely consumes it.
3. A Test-React-specific signal/job condition does not fire the other adapter JVM jobs or unrelated implementation JVM artefacts, and `implementation/core/**` still schedules `jvm-adapters-test-react`.
4. `implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs` pins source, test, deps, README, and core reverse-edge cases including explicit false assertions for the retired outputs.
5. `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh` still selects `implementation/adapters/test-react` for a Test-React code diff; changed-surface, JVM-roster, test-lane-bijection, fast-PR-gap, and gate-scheduling self-tests pass.
6. Both `clojure -M:test` in the Test-React artefact and the CLJS `:node-test` coverage remain green; no published-adapter gate is narrowed.
notes:
ANALYSIS ONLY — bead deliberately LEFT OPEN (2026-09-03). rf2-6r9j.85/.83/.81 landed as
PR #9100; .87 was fenced out of that worker because .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh
and its mirror implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs are one-toucher by
construction for any change that alters what the classifier OUTPUTS (this is exactly such a
change) and PRs #9091/#9092/#9093 were contending for that pair at the time. Neither file was
touched. Below is the change list to apply verbatim once that pair is free.

== PREMISE RE-MEASURED AND HOLDS, at commit 061d3560e4 ==

All four representative paths still produce the SAME twelve true outputs, README.md included:

  implementation_jvm cljs_node_test adapter_diagnostic cljs_browser examples_compile
  cljs_prod bundle_isolation adapter_testbed_smokes tools_jvm template_expensive
  mcp_conformance mcp_live

Measured with: bash .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh <path>  on
test-react/src/re_frame/adapter/test_react.cljc, test/.../test_react_cljs_test.cljc,
deps.edn and README.md.

== THE TRAP THE DISPOSITION DOES NOT NAME: THERE ARE TWO case STATEMENTS ==

examples_compile is NOT set by the generic adapter arm. It comes from a DIFFERENT, EARLIER
case "$file" in block:

  * case #1 opens at :602, closes esac at :657. Its arm at :612 is a long alternation
    listing implementation/adapters/* among many, and sets examples_compile=true.
  * case #2 opens at :732 and holds every adapter arm: reagent-slim at :878,
    implementation/adapters/scripts/* at :899, the generic implementation/adapters/* at :915.

A carve-out added only to case #2 leaves examples_compile=true firing on a README edit and
silently fails acceptance criterion 1. BOTH cases need an arm. Shell case is first-match, so
each new arm must sit ABOVE the generic pattern it is narrowing.

== CHANGE LIST — .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh ==

C1. Declare the new output. After  adapter_diagnostic=false  (:153) add:

      test_react_jvm=false

C2. mark_all() (opens :224). After its  adapter_diagnostic=true  (:227) add:

      test_react_jvm=true

    Not optional: force_all / the workflow-file arms rely on mark_all being total, and a

C3. Emit it. In the emit block (~:2508) after  emit adapter_diagnostic "$adapter_diagnostic"
    (:2510) add:

      emit test_react_jvm "$test_react_jvm"

C4. CASE #1 (:602-:657) — carve test-react out of the examples_compile alternation. IMMEDIATELY
    ABOVE the  examples/*|implementation/adapters/*|...  arm at :612 insert:

      implementation/adapters/test-react/*)
        # rf2-6r9j.87 — local-test-only CLJC fixture. No Maven coordinate, no
        # production/example consumer, no testbed. Nothing under examples/ requires
        # re-frame.adapter.test-react, so it cannot appear in a compiled example
        # closure. Deliberately falls through with NO output set here; case #2 below

        ;;

C5. CASE #2 (:732-) — carve it out of the adapter fan-out. IMMEDIATELY ABOVE the generic
    implementation/adapters/*)  arm at :915 (i.e. after the implementation/adapters/scripts/*
    arm that ends at :913) insert:

      implementation/adapters/test-react/src/*|implementation/adapters/test-react/test/*|implementation/adapters/test-react/deps.edn)
        # rf2-6r9j.87 — route by the files each lane actually consumes.
        # Two owning lanes only:
        #   * jvm-adapters-test-react — this artefact's own clojure -M:test.
        #   * cljs — Shadow's consolidated :node-test, whose cljs-test$ selector
        #     discovers both .cljc test namespaces because shadow-cljs.edn:79-90

        # Everything the broad arm below adds (browser DOM, examples, prod, bundle
        # isolation, the reagent|uix testbed smokes, tools JVM, template, MCP) has no

        # re-frame.adapter.test-react, and it owns no testbed.
        test_react_jvm=true

    adapter_diagnostic=true is at :805) must keep firing adapter_diagnostic, which is what

C7. jvm-adapters-test-react (job key at :1753) currently reads

title: Remove Root Descriptor key inventories stranded by re-frame.ui retirement
description:
## Finding

`re-frame.ssr.manifest/descriptor-keys` and `extension-keys` are production data inventories whose only stated purpose was to make the Root Descriptor -> Root Manifest subset property mechanically checkable. The sole descriptor producer and the compiler-backed subset suite were retired with `re-frame.ui`, but both inventories and prose claiming that suite still pins the property remain.

## Evidence

- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/manifest.cljc:94-116` defines the two sets. A repository-wide exact-symbol search across `implementation/`, `tools/`, `examples/`, `skills/`, `spec/`, and `docs/` finds no reads; each name occurs only at its definition.
- The namespace docstring at lines 23-24 and `problems` docstring at line 155 still say "the subset-property test" pins the invariant. `spec/011-SSR.md:474-475` likewise claims the reference suite checks the real compiler output.
- `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/root_manifest_cljs_test.cljc:11-21` now explicitly records that the subset-property suite was deleted because `re-frame.ui` was retired and no remaining substrate emits a Root Descriptor.
- Commit `b24c6ab015` introduced the sets and compiler-backed suite together. Commit `a3e5e17e73` removed the producer, its test dependency, and the 11 descriptor-coupled tests, but left the production inventories and stale claims.
- `implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/gen.clj` classifies `re-frame.ssr.manifest` as an internal namespace. Spec 011's artefact roster names `problems`, `valid?`, `validate!`, `manifest`, `script-html`, `read-manifest`, and `discover`; it does not expose either key-set Var.

Duplicate searches for `descriptor-keys`, `extension-keys`, "root manifest subset", "retired descriptor inventory", `a3e5e17`, and `rf2-0yp7w` found no owning bead.

## Impact

The two dead Vars carry a retired compiler model in the shipped SSR artefact and can drift independently from the live validator. The stale prose falsely suggests a real-producer integration check still exists, obscuring the deliberate coverage gap documented by the surviving test namespace.

## Proposed disposition

Delete `descriptor-keys` and `extension-keys`. Update the three stale subset-suite claims in the manifest source and Spec 011 to describe the current hand-built validator coverage and the absence of a live descriptor producer. Preserve the normative rule that only `:rf.root/schema-version` is required and extension keys are optional. Keep `schema-version`, `dev-only-keys`, validation, assembly, wire, discovery, and late-bind behavior unchanged.

## Risks

Do not turn this cleanup into a schema contraction: unknown keys must remain accepted, every extension key must remain optional, and descriptor-shaped maps must still validate. The removed Vars are internal and have no repository consumers, but the implementation should still run the API-manifest check so an accidental public-surface change elsewhere is caught.
acceptance_criteria:
- `descriptor-keys` and `extension-keys` are absent, with no replacement duplicate inventory.
- Source and Spec 011 no longer claim a deleted real-compiler subset-property suite is running; the documented absence of a descriptor producer remains explicit.
- `problems` still accepts `{:rf.root/schema-version 1}`, ignores unknown keys, and shape-checks optional extension keys only when present.
- Existing Root Manifest JVM and CLJS tests pass, including schema-version-only validity, assembly, exact EDN round-trip, and discovery coverage.
- The API-manifest gate still classifies `re-frame.ssr.manifest` as internal and passes.
close_reason: Landed in PR #9107 (27108c7b56). Premise held: descriptor-keys and extension-keys each occurred exactly once in the tracked corpus, at their own definition. DONOR-REFERENCE CATEGORY CALL, per item. descriptor-keys: NOT retirement bookkeeping (no dated statement naming rf2-0yp7w, no struck-through catalogue row - its docstring asserts a LIVE checkable property) and NOT the reserved-kind contract (it rosters :rf.root/* descriptor keys, not :rf.adapter/ui or :rf.adapter/freehand reserved values that tooling refuses defensively against a stale co-loaded build); genuinely unreachable inventory, removed. extension-keys: same two calls, same verdict - and specifically NOT a reserved-value roster, because the live validator problems already encodes all six keys in its own destructure and contains? checks, and the namespace docstring's markdown table is the documentation; the set was a duplicate with no reader. dev-only-keys: RETAINED - it has a live consumer on the emit path (manifest.cljc:421, apply dissoc). The three stale claims that a real-compiler subset-property suite still pins the invariant were corrected rather than deleted, so the RECORD survives: the ns docstring and problems docstring now say validation is checked over hand-built manifests because re-frame.ui was retired (rf2-0yp7w) and no remaining substrate emits a Root Descriptor, pointing at re-frame.ssr.root-manifest-cljs-test which already records the deliberate gap; spec/011-SSR.md:473-475 likewise. No schema contraction: :rf.root/schema-version still the only required key, unknown keys still ignored, every extension key still optional and shape-checked only when present, descriptor-shaped maps still validate. Two instruments with a control that fires: fixed-string census (control: dev-only-keys run the same way returns its consumer) and clj-kondo over implementation + tools reporting no unresolved var. ssr JVM suite 623 tests / 3172 assertions / 0 failures / 0 errors; api-manifest gen --check exit 0, in sync at 528 public vars, re-frame.ssr.manifest still on the internal roster; check_doc_slugs.py exit 0. spec/011 edit is prose inside an existing paragraph - no headings, links, anchors or tables touched.

title: http reply: remove the never-consumed duplicate transport-request-id helper
description:
## Finding

`re-frame.http.reply/transport-request-id` is a never-consumed duplicate constructor for `[:rf.req frame-id work-id]`. The only shipped producer of that token is the Resources work-ledger’s separate `managed-request-id` implementation.

## Evidence

- Fixed-string and resolved-var searches across implementation, tools, examples, skills, docs, and specs find no production call to `http-reply/transport-request-id` (`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/reply.cljc:99-107`). Its only calls are shape assertions in `http_reply_lowering_test.clj:138-140` and `http_reply_lowering_cljs_test.cljc:38-40`; the remaining hit is its own namespace prose.
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/work_ledger.cljc:148-169` defines the byte-for-byte equivalent `managed-request-id` and is the actual runtime authority. Resources transport/teardown code and multiple Resources tests use that function to issue, supersede, and abort managed HTTP work.
- History makes the duplication explicit: Resources added `managed-request-id` in `450cdd44a1` at 11:53 on 2026-06-11. HTTP added the identical helper later that day in `b6789084b2` while introducing reply lowering, but no runtime call edge was ever added; `git log -S` shows creation only.
- The HTTP artifact accepts a caller-chosen `:request-id` and does not itself know when a caller needs frame qualification. The frame-local Resources owner is therefore the layer that has both identities and constructs the transport token.
- The helper is absent from the generated API manifest and HTTP user facade/docs. Specs require the token shape, not this unused constructor. Exact-symbol, title, description, and broader transport-correlation bead searches found no existing issue.

## Impact

Two implementations claim authority for a security-relevant process-global correlation identity, while HTTP’s copy has no consumer. Its focused tests can stay green if the real Resources constructor or lowering path changes, overstating coverage and inviting tuple-shape drift.

## Proposed disposition

Remove `re-frame.http.reply/transport-request-id`, its two direct shape assertions, and the namespace sentence claiming it builds the identity. Keep the canonical token shape documented and tested through the live `re-frame.resources.work-ledger/managed-request-id` path. Do not add an HTTP -> Resources dependency. If a second production owner emerges, extract one genuinely shared lower-layer constructor rather than retaining parallel copies.

## Risks / retained contracts

The var is public at the namespace level but is unmanifested and has never had an in-repo production caller, so an unknown downstream direct-require is the only compatibility risk. Preserve `http-reply/work-id` and all reply correlation behavior; this finding concerns only the unused frame-qualification helper, not the `:request-id` accepted by managed HTTP.
acceptance_criteria:
1. HTTP reply code no longer ships an unconsumed duplicate `transport-request-id`, or a concrete production caller and ownership rationale is added.
2. The `[:rf.req frame-id work-id]` contract remains implemented once on the live Resources lowering/teardown path (or in a truly shared dependency-safe owner) and is covered on JVM/CLJS as applicable.
3. HTTP reply-lowering tests continue to cover HTTP work IDs and canonical replies without asserting a helper the runtime never invokes.
4. Resources managed-HTTP issuance, cross-frame isolation, supersession, and opportunistic-abort tests pass; HTTP JVM/CLJS suites pass.
5. Repo-wide searches show no stale HTTP helper/doc reference and no new HTTP -> Resources dependency cycle.
close_reason: PR #9115. Removed re-frame.http.reply/transport-request-id, its two shape assertions (http_reply_lowering_test.clj:138-140, http_reply_lowering_cljs_test.cljc:38-40) and the namespace sentence claiming it builds the identity. Proven unconsumed with two instruments plus firing controls: repo-wide git grep -F over tracked files returned only its own defn, its own prose and the two test assertions (control 'success-reply' hit 24 files); clj-kondo var-usage analysis over implementation/ returned 3 usage records, all test namespaces, 0 from src (controls: success-reply 21, work-id 33). Surviving original named and verified equivalent: re-frame.resources.work-ledger/managed-request-id at work_ledger.cljc:148, identical body [frame-id work-id] -> [:rf.req frame-id work-id], with four production callers (resources/events.cljc 653/977/1149, resources/mutation_events.cljc 1271). Namespace prose now names that constructor so the token shape stays documented; no HTTP -> Resources dependency added. CLJS deftest work-id-and-transport-id renamed work-id-head (no other reference existed). Gates: http JVM 506 tests/3882 assertions exit 0; npm run test:cljs 11169 tests/55740 assertions exit 0.

title: reagent-slim StrictMode test still says the fixed bug fails by design
description:
## Finding

The live StrictMode regression test still tells contributors that its assertions fail by design and that the production bug is unfixed, although the fix landed immediately afterward and the test is now a required green regression.

## Evidence

- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/re_frame/adapter/reagent_slim_strict_mode_dom_cljs_test.cljs:6-12` says assertions `(a)` and `(b)` `FAIL BY DESIGN`, the substrate does not honor the contract, and the fix belongs to a separate bead.
- Its `FINDING` block at lines 29-51 speaks in present tense: StrictMode leaves every slim component reactively dead and a production fix is still needed.
- Commit `2c4a87e3df` (`fix(adapters/reagent-slim): re-establish render Reaction after StrictMode remount (rf2-6b6pex)`) landed the repair after test commit `66e9e2af0e`.
- Current production code at `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/component.cljs:389-415,432-442` installs a remount marker, queues a render on the second `componentDidMount`, and documents the fixed sequence.
- The test remains discovered by both browser and node selectors, so this is live test guidance rather than archived design history.

## Impact

The header normalizes red output from a required acceptance test and directs maintainers to file/fix work that is already complete. During a genuine regression, a reader could dismiss the failure as expected.

## Proposed disposition

Rewrite the header as regression history: state the former failure, name the fixing commit/bead, and describe the invariants the now-green test protects. Remove all present-tense `FAIL BY DESIGN`, `not yet honour`, and separate-fix instructions. Do not weaken the assertions or erase the useful explanation of the StrictMode lifecycle sequence.

## Risks

The historical diagnosis is valuable and should remain clearly marked as past behavior. Avoid turning the header into a terse comment that loses the reason for the remount marker or the two non-vacuous assertions.

## Duplicate search

Searched all bead states/fields for `StrictMode`, `a07937`, `6b6pex`, `FAIL BY DESIGN`, the test filename, and `reagent-slim`. StrictMode matches concern Hicasso or unrelated surfaces; the historical IDs are no longer live bead records. No current bead owns this stale header.
acceptance_criteria:
- The live test file contains no present-tense claim that its assertions are expected to fail or that production lacks the repair.
- The header records the former failure and fixing commit/bead as history, then states the current green invariants: post-remount reactive update and watch-count cleanup.
- The production/test explanation agrees on the remount marker and forced re-render path.
- The StrictMode DOM test remains enrolled and passes; a focused negative control that disables the reattach behavior makes its reactive-update assertion fail.
- Any now-unused `cljs.test/testing` import may be removed, but no assertion or browser gating is weakened.
close_reason: Confirmed at tip: the STATUS block still read FAIL BY DESIGN and directed maintainers to file work already complete, and the FINDING block was present tense. Verified 2c4a87e3df (rf2-6b6pex) exists and landed 2026-07-12, the same day as the test's own commit 66e9e2af0e. Header rewritten as dated history rather than erased, per the standing rule on retired states: STATUS now says the file is a required green regression, then records what it used to say and when that ended; the FINDING block is retitled FORMER BUG, moved to past tense and KEPT because it is the diagnosis the remount marker was built from; a new section describes the fix (cljsRemountReattach set by the transient componentWillUnmount, read by the now-unconditional componentDidMount, which queues a render so make-render-method recreates the Reaction) and states what each assertion fails on. Those claims were verified rather than asserted: disabling the reattach reds the test with exactly (not (= 'n=2' 'n=1')) for (a) and (not (= 1 0)) twice for (b) -- the two failure modes the new prose names; restore verified by blob hash. No assertion or browser gating weakened; the now-unused cljs.test/testing refer removed as the acceptance criteria permit. PR #9077.

title: pair-mcp: remove four zero-consumer helper definitions
description:
## Finding
Four public Pair-MCP helper definitions have no production, test, build, or repository consumer and expose misleading or obsolete surface:
- `roots_discovery.cljs`: `project-home->candidate` and `candidates-from-edns`
- `tools/wire.cljs`: `structured-content` and `arg-keyword`

## Evidence and reachability proof
- Whole-repository symbol searches find each name only at its definition/docstring/comment; no invocation exists.
- `clj-kondo` var-usage analysis across Pair-MCP source and tests reports zero source uses and zero test uses for all four definitions.
- Production root discovery calls `discover-via-roots*` with concrete dependencies, and that seam calls `candidates-from-edns*`; tests also call the starred seams directly. The two unstarred wrappers are bypassed. The docstring for `project-home->candidate*` nevertheless claims production callers use the dead wrapper.
- All structured response envelopes call `wire/result`, whose implementation uses private `structured-of`; `structured-content` has had no client since it was introduced alongside `result` in commit `834af6cdd9`.
- `arg-keyword` was used by the progress-stream/list-streams operations removed in commit `89bb4d49f1`; no current frame parser calls it.
- `package.json` publishes compiled `out/server.js`, README, and LICENSE—not these CLJS namespaces as a supported library API.
- Dynamic zero-static-use entrypoints such as `server/main` and `descriptor-manifest-gen/-main` were explicitly excluded because `shadow-cljs.edn` proves their build reachability.

## Impact
The dead definitions enlarge an apparent API, retain stream-era residue, and leave a false production-call claim in a root-discovery docstring. Future maintainers can mistakenly preserve or test paths the server cannot take.

## Proposed disposition
Delete the four zero-consumer definitions and correct the starred root-discovery seam documentation to describe the actual production path. Keep the live starred injection seams, `wire/result`, and private `structured-of` unchanged.

## Risks / retained contracts
Re-run whole-repository searches before deletion to catch concurrent clients. Do not classify build entrypoints or deliberate test seams as dead merely because ordinary static call analysis cannot see them. Do not change response envelope shape or root candidate ordering.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The four listed zero-consumer definitions are removed (or a newly discovered concrete consumer is documented and the applicable definition retained).
2. Root-discovery docstrings accurately describe the real production and test call paths.
3. Whole-repository searches show no dangling references to the removed symbols.
4. Pair-MCP build and tests pass; descriptor generation/check and registry fixture checks remain unchanged/green.
5. Public MCP response envelopes and roots-discovery behavior are unchanged.
close_reason: Done in PR #9076. Reachability premise re-verified at tip and HELD for all four. Two independent instruments, each run against live controls in the same files: (a) line-oriented fixed-string search over tracked files, (b) a whitespace-flattened per-file census over 4810 tracked files. Both returned ZERO call heads for project-home->candidate, candidates-from-edns, structured-content and arg-keyword; controls wire/result, wire/arg, rd/project-home->candidate*, candidates-from-edns* and rd/discover-via-roots* all fired non-zero. Production path confirmed at source: discover-via-roots -> discover-via-roots* -> candidates-from-edns* -> project-home->candidate*, bypassing both unstarred wrappers. structured-content's docstring named server.cljs, cache.cljs and cap.cljs as its consumers; checked each — all three call wire/result instead (cache.cljs:283, server.cljs:586/626, cap.cljs:145). The sibling unstarred walk-for-shadow-edns is LIVE (passed to discover-via-roots* at roots_discovery.cljs:303) and was deliberately left alone — the audit was right to name only two of the three wrappers. Docstring trap fixed: project-home->candidate*'s 'production callers use [[project-home->candidate]]' was false and pointed at a deleted var; it now describes the real call path. Two comments in dispatch.cljs and trace_window.cljs cited wire/arg-keyword as the coercion NOT to use and would have dangled; they now say (keyword ...) directly. No dangling references remain. Envelope shape and root candidate ordering unchanged. Suite green: 1120 tests, 4070 assertions, 0 failures (captured exit 0).

title: gate(check_skill_migration_contract_drift): remediation advice names register-error-listener!, a facade fn that does not exist
description:
scripts/check_skill_migration_contract_drift.py prints remediation advice that
names a facade fn which does not exist.

SITES: the module docstring (~line 35) and the M13-FRAME-ONERROR problem message
(~line 731) both read: "Error observability is `register-error-listener!`
(always-on) / `register-listener!` (dev-only)."

TRUTH AT TIP, confirmed by EVALUATION on the JVM for PR #9039 (rf2-qbgy1), not by
reading: re-frame.core exports ONE stream-parameterised pair --
(:arglists (meta #'rf/register-listener!)) => ([stream id f]) and
(:arglists (meta #'rf/unregister-listener!)) => ([stream id]). There is no
rf/register-error-listener!; that name survives only as an INTERNAL error-emit
alias the facade delegates to for the :errors stream. The dev/prod axis is carried
by the STREAM, not by two different verbs: :errors and :events are always-on,
:trace is dev-only.

IMPACT is narrow but real and inverted: this text is what the gate prints to tell
an author how to FIX a drift it just caught, so an author who follows the
remediation writes (rf/register-error-listener! ...) -- an unresolved-symbol
compile error. A gate that steers toward a non-existent symbol is worse than
silence.

FIX SHAPE: both strings become the stream-first form, e.g. "Observability is
`(register-listener! :errors ...)` (always-on) / `(register-listener! :trace ...)`
(dev-only)." This is advice text only -- it is NOT a content pin, so no document
moves with it and no gate output changes shape.

OUT OF FENCE for rf2-qbgy1's dispatch (scripts/ was barred), hence filed rather
than fixed. Same class as rf2-qbgy1: the collapsed listener API stated in its
pre-collapse spelling.
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-09-03, worker/skillgates-a, PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9042 (base 70f6cea39b). bd history walked to the item's beginning: zero text-bearing changes since creation, so the description was the live instruction.

THE CHECK ITSELF IS CORRECT, established SEPARATELY from its advice and at source rather than by reading the bead. Rule 2 fires on M13_ERROR_HANDLER_RE AND M13_MOVED_TO_ONERROR_RE AND NOT M13_NEGATION_RE, and the claim it refutes is genuinely false at tip: spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2946 records the removed surface as "the :on-error frame-config slot, the {:swallow | :replacement | :default} return vocabulary" and states "The v1 process-wide reg-event-error-handler remains dropped"; :2682 states there is "no app-steering recovery policy"; reg-event-error-handler appears in no implementation/*/src. Exercised in both directions by evaluation: line_problems() returns exactly 1 problem on the stale claim and 0 on a clean sentence. No change was made to the check.

THE ADVICE WAS WRONG, at both sites the bead names -- the module docstring (~:35) and the M13-FRAME-ONERROR message (~:731). VERIFIED AT SOURCE rather than copied from the brief: implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc defines register-listener! at :2126 with arglist [stream id f] and unregister-listener! at :2161 with [stream id]; register-error-listener! exists ONLY as error-emit/register-error-listener!, the internal delegate the facade calls for the :errors stream (:2157). So an author who tripped the gate and followed its advice wrote an unresolved symbol.

The advice also inverted the AXIS, which is the part worth fixing rather than just the spelling: the dev/prod distinction is carried by the STREAM, not by two different verbs. listener-streams (:2098) is the closed set #{:trace :events :errors :epoch}; the register-listener! docstring marks :trace dev-only (DCE'd under goog.DEBUG gating) and :events / :errors always-on (surviving :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false), with :epoch the epoch-record stream. An unknown stream throws :rf.error/unknown-listener-stream.

FIX. Both strings now read "(register-listener! :errors id f) (always-on) / (register-listener! :trace id f) (dev-only)", naming the closed vocabulary and stating that the axis is the stream rather than two verbs. Advice text only -- no content pin moves and no gate output changes shape, exactly as the bead predicted. Corroboration that this is the house spelling: spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2682 already directs readers to "the :errors stream of register-listener!" for production observation and the :trace stream for dev.

VERIFIED. Zero occurrences of register-error-listener! remain in the gate (control: register-listener! still present 4x, so the search instrument bit). Gate self-test exit 0; the M13 rule re-exercised after the edit and confirmed to emit the corrected text. check_skill_migration_contract_drift.py --self-test 0 and --ci 0 on the final rebased base; scripts/test-fast-pr.sh 0.
close_reason: PR #9042 corrects both advice sites to the stream-first form (register-listener! :errors id f) / (register-listener! :trace id f), naming the closed vocabulary #{:trace :events :errors :epoch}. Verified at source: core.cljc:2126 defines register-listener! [stream id f], :2161 unregister-listener! [stream id], and register-error-listener! exists only as the internal error-emit delegate at :2157 — so the old advice steered authors at an unresolved symbol and also inverted the axis (the dev/prod split is the stream, not the verb). The CHECK itself was established correct separately and left unchanged: it fires exactly once on the stale claim and zero times on a clean line, and spec/009:2946 confirms the :on-error slot was removed.

notes:
BACKLOG REREAD 2026-09-03 (mayor) — COSTING THE HOLD, and adding a recommendation the bead deliberately did not make.

WHY THE HOLD EXISTS: the bead says "Mike rules" and I am respecting that. It is not a technical judgement — it is what nine published packages PROMISE a reader who installs one from a tarball. That is a product call.

WHAT IT COSTS TODAY: nothing is blocked, and no bead waits on it. The 398 links resolve fine for the monorepo reader, who is every reader this project actually has right now, because the packages are not published yet — rf2-8arzr.8 established that this repo has no npm publishing path at all (package.json is private:true, no NPM_TOKEN, no registry.npmjs anywhere under .github/ or scripts/). SO THE COST IS ZERO UNTIL THE PACKAGES SHIP, and it becomes real on the same day the first one does. That timing is the useful thing to know: this is not urgent, and it must not be forgotten, which is a bad combination for a bead with no dependency edge. Recorded here so a later reader does not have to re-derive it.

MY RECOMMENDATION, offered because "none costed here" left four options equally weighted and that is how a bead sits still. Option (iii) — rewrite the escaping links as absolute GitHub URLs. Reasons, in order:
  - It resolves for BOTH readers, where (i) serves only the monorepo reader and (ii) serves only the package reader by telling them the link is not for them.
  - 398 markers of prose is a lot of noise for a mechanism (ii) designed to excuse the occasional line; the three improver links show it working at the scale it was built for.
  - There is precedent IN THIS TREE for exactly this rewrite: mkdocs_hooks.py already rewrites references to implementation/ into GitHub URLs when a doc leaves its context, for the same reason.
  - Under the stance it is the low-friction answer: it is mechanical, the gate is already ready for it (the check resolves every link and knows which side of the package root it lands on), and it needs no ongoing discipline from authors.
  Option (iv) — ship the referenced trees — is the one I would not take: it makes every skill package carry the monorepo.

STILL MIKE CALL. This is a recommendation, not a ruling, and no work goes out on it.
FENCED — DO NOT DISPATCH UNTIL: (a) Mike rules between options (i)-(iv), AND (b) PR from worker/isolation-a merges.

FENCE (b) MEASURED THIS TICK 2026-09-03 07:2x AUSEST, and it is new since the last note. isolation-a holds skills/re-frame-migration/references/auto-cross-cutting.md live (rf2-phtp, 23 lines changed, unpushed at read time). That file carries 14 escaping ../ links, so ANY of options (ii), (iii) or (iv) touches it and collides with a live peer. Per-skill escaping-link counts measured at tip for whoever takes this: re-frame-migration 173, re-frame2 130, re-frame2-improver 78, re-frame2-xray 68, re-frame2-pair 43, re-frame2-implementor 29, re-frame2-setup 24, reagent-migration 16, re-frame2-pair-retro 6. Total 567 ../-shaped links, of which the bead's classification says 398 escape the package root — RE-RUN THE CLASSIFICATION rather than subtracting, the two censuses count different things.

FENCE (a) UNCHANGED AND STILL MIKE'S. I am not overriding the previous mayor's read that this is a product call. I agree with it: what nine published packages promise a tarball reader is not a technical judgement.

TWO MAYORS HAVE NOW INDEPENDENTLY LANDED ON OPTION (iii) — rewrite the escaping links as absolute GitHub URLs. I am recording my concurrence rather than a new argument, because the previous mayor's reasoning is complete and I checked its load-bearing claim: mkdocs_hooks.py does carry a _REWRITES table that turns references to implementation/ into GitHub URLs when a doc leaves its context, so the precedent in this tree is real and this is the idiomatic spelling here rather than an invention.

WHAT I ADD, which is only a scheduling observation: the previous mayor established the cost is ZERO until the packages ship, and that remains true. But (iii) is MECHANICAL and the gate is already ready for it. So this is cheap now and cheap later, which means the argument for holding it is purely that Mike has not ruled — not that it is expensive to do. That is worth saying plainly, because "not urgent" and "not yet decided" read the same on a board and only one of them is a reason to wait.

SURFACED TO MIKE IN CHAT THIS TICK.

RE-MEASURED AT TIP 2026-09-04 (worker/skilllinks-a, base 3c67c6834a). NO CODE CHANGE MADE: fence (a) is still live, and every available fix IS the ruling. Evidence below so the ruling is a one-word answer.

MY RE-COUNT, both instruments. 408 escaping links on the gate's own scan surface (SKILL.md + README.md + references/**) against the bead's 398 - drifted +10 since 2026-09-02. 427 across every doc the package.json files allow-lists actually ship. Line-oriented and whitespace-collapsed censuses agree EXACTLY at both figures; the flatten instrument was controlled against a link deliberately wrapped at the parenthesis, which it finds and the line instrument cannot see, so "no wrapped links in this corpus" is a measured result and not an unexercised instrument.

notes:

title: docs/core/hicasso/15-testing.md: the published :local/root test-kit route (:extra-paths to ../re-frame2/implementation/hicasso/test_kit/src) prints a Clojure CLI deprecation warning on every build
description:

  WARNING: Use of :paths external to the project has been deprecated, please remove: ../re-frame2/implementation/hicasso/test_kit/src
tools.deps has deprecated paths that escape the project root. Nothing fails today, but (a) a pilot following the published chapter meets a deprecation warning on the first build, which the friction log will (correctly) record against the published docs; (b) a future Clojure CLI may refuse it, at which point the published route breaks. The chapter is outside rf2-xkhul's fence (docs/core/hicasso is the published guide), so this is filed rather than fixed.

prints. worker/docsdrift-a, commit edc0a3606e.

title: skills: six of nine SKILL.md descriptions exceed the Agent Skills 1,024-char description cap — verify runtime truncation and trim so the tail disqualifier survives
description:
CLAIM. The Agent Skills spec caps the frontmatter description at 1,024 characters. Measured at tip: re-frame2-xray 1,712; reagent-migration 1,486; re-frame2 1,243; re-frame2-improver 1,149; re-frame2-pair-retro 1,137; re-frame2-setup 1,062. No repo gate checks it.
IMPACT. If the loader truncates, the clause at the END of each description is what is cut — in xray that tail is the Xray-vs-pair disqualifier the family README treats as the routing rule; in setup it is the greenfield-only disqualifier.
FIX SHAPE. First verify (do not assume) whether Claude Code truncates or refuses; then either trim the six descriptions to the cap with the disqualifier moved to the front, or record in skills/README.md that the cap does not apply and why. Do not add a gate unless truncation is confirmed.

NOTHING TO RE-DECIDE HERE. rf2-w9p2 owns the gate; this bead owns the six descriptions. Read rf2-w9p2 before working either, and take the measured truncation behaviour from it rather than re-establishing it.

title: skill(re-frame2-implementor): the harness fail-loud floors and derivation greps omit the top-level :fixture/* key set — 8 live keys are undocumented in the corpus README
description:
IMPLEMENTOR-REVIEW-7f2c-B4

CLAIM
- skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/conformance.md:28-33 — "Four fail-loud floors the harness owes": spec version, unknown capability, unknown op (handler-DSL or Mode-B `:call`), non-vacuous run.
- conformance.md:12-20 — "Derive, never transcribe" greps: fixture count, Mode-B call ops, one family's live tags, dynamic-host-only set, spec versions in play.
- conformance.md:26 — harness shape: "read every fixture; filter …; bootstrap the registry; realise handler bodies via the DSL; create the frame; run the dispatches or calls; capture observables and compare; report".
- conformance.md:3 — "the **full contract is [`spec/conformance/README.md`]** — fixture format, the handler-body DSL op table, capability tagging, versioning, the harness steps."

TRUTH AT TIP
- The 245 fixtures carry 20 distinct top-level `:fixture/*` keys (`grep -rhoE ':fixture/[a-z?-]+' spec/conformance/fixtures/ | sort | uniq -c`). Beyond the keys the README §Fixture format describes, live fixtures use: `:fixture/frames` (13 fixtures), `:fixture/interceptor-fired` (11), `:fixture/flow-bodies` (6), `:fixture/clear-interceptor` (5), `:fixture/wire-order` (2), `:fixture/render-after-hydrate` (2), `:fixture/runtime` (1), `:fixture/compute-subs` (1). None of those eight strings occurs anywhere in spec/conformance/README.md, nor in spec/Spec-Schemas.md §`:rf/fixture-file` (line 4476). `:fixture/classification-effects` (17 fixtures; 6 of them `:data-classification/*`, i.e. gate-1 v1-required) is documented in the README's harness-step section but not in Spec-Schemas. `:fixture/dynamic-host-only?` is likewise README-absent.
- The README's own contract for silent skips: "a harness that silently skips unknown capabilities is the shape the spec forbids" (§Capability tagging). No floor — in the README or the skill — extends that to an unknown top-level key.

IMPACT
The skill's derive-at-the-pin posture rests on "the README is the contract"; on the fixture-file shape the README demonstrably lags the fixtures by eight keys. A port harness built from README + skill supports registry / handlers / frame-config / dispatches / expect / calls and none of the four floors fires when a fixture arrives with `:fixture/interceptor-fired` or `:fixture/frames`: the setup or expectation is ignored and the fixture can pass vacuously (an interceptor-fired expectation never checked) — the exact silent-skip shape the floors exist to forbid. On `:data-classification/*` (gate 1) a harness that has not implemented the classification-effects step fails loudly, which is fine; the eight undocumented keys are the quiet ones.

FIX SHAPE (one PR, skill side)
1. conformance.md §The harness: add a fifth floor — "**Unknown fixture key.** A top-level `:fixture/*` key the harness does not implement fails the run naming it — the corpus adds setup/expectation keys ahead of the README."
2. conformance.md §Derive, never transcribe: add the key-enumeration grep above beside the existing five.
3. phase-2-impl-order.md:11 (Step 0) lists the fail-loud set ("unknown spec version, capability, DSL op, call op") — add the key. SKILL.md:36 and README.md:20 carry the same four-item list; keep them in step (the order guard does not pin this list — hand check).
Spec side (report, not this bead): document the eight keys in spec/conformance/README.md §Fixture format and in Spec-Schemas §`:rf/fixture-file`; that is a corpus README gap and belongs to spec/.

GATE
No gate — verify by hand: run the new grep at tip and confirm it lists 20 keys; check_skill_implementor_order.py --verbose stays green (it scans conformance.md for the family roots only).

ACCEPTANCE
conformance.md names five floors including unknown top-level fixture keys and ships the key-enumeration grep; phase-2 Step 0, SKILL.md and README.md list the same five.

acceptance_criteria: conformance.md lists five floors including unknown top-level fixture keys plus the key-enumeration grep; phase-2 Step 0, SKILL.md and README.md carry the same list
notes: DISPATCHED 2026-09-02 20:25:38 AUSEST by the mayor as CLUSTER implskill-a (order r5u9t → weshq → 9vbg3 → jjk3v, one PR, worktree worker/implskill-a off origin/main 9ebddf1425). close_reason: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9001 (draft), commit 141107d53b548eea9e0e669c8c82b71b932b0b3f. DERIVED KEY SET (not transcribed): 247 fixtures at tip carry EIGHTEEN distinct top-level :fixture/* keys. Derived by two independent methods that agree exactly on membership and on every per-key count: (1) a bracket-depth scan of every fixture that skips strings and ';;' comments and counts a keyword only at depth 1; (2) a line-start heuristic. The eighteen: capabilities, doc, id, spec-version (247 each), registry 237, handlers 218, expect 150, dispatches 148, frame-config 120, calls 108, frames 9, classification-effects 8, dynamic-host-only? 7, flow-bodies 6, render-after-hydrate 2, wire-order 2, compute-subs 1, runtime 1. Eleven are named in spec/conformance/README.md; SEVEN are not -- frames, flow-bodies, wire-order, render-after-hydrate, runtime, compute-subs, dynamic-host-only?. NINE are absent from spec/Spec-Schemas.md section :rf/fixture-file (line 4498 at tip, not 4476): those seven plus capabilities and classification-effects. DELTA AGAINST THE BEAD'S EIGHT: it is seven, and membership differs at three points. REMOVED (2): :fixture/interceptor-fired and :fixture/clear-interceptor are NOT top-level keys -- they are EVENT IDS in the :fixture/ namespace, registered under :fixture/registry :event, dispatched from a :before hook and handled by ordinary handler bodies, in http-interceptor-before-transforms.edn and http-interceptor-clear.edn. They entered the bead's list because an unanchored grep ':fixture/[a-z?-]+' cannot distinguish a map key from a value; the same grep also counts mentions inside :fixture/doc strings and ';;' commentary, which accounts for the rest of its count inflation (e.g. classification-effects reads 17 unanchored, 8 structurally; registry 241 vs 237). THIS MATTERED TO THE FIX, not just the report: building the new floor off the naive grep would make a harness REJECT A CONFORMING FIXTURE, failing :fixture/interceptor-fired as an unknown key when it is an ordinary event id. The shipped derivation grep is therefore line-anchored, controlled in both directions (it finds the rarest key, compute-subs at 1 fixture, and excludes the event id), and the leaf explains why the anchor is load-bearing and that a harness which has parsed the fixture should take the key set from the parsed map rather than from any text search. That is the corpus README lagging the fixtures, and it belongs to spec/. title: skill(re-frame2-pair): README "Watch events as they fire" example starts a signal `record` (no signals, a required arg) to observe events — the route is a watch-epochs poll with event-id-prefix + since-id
description:
CLAIM

skills/re-frame2-pair/README.md:96-100, §Examples "Watch events as they fire":
> **You**: Tell me about every `:checkout/*` event as I click through.
> **Claude**: *(starts a recorder, then reads it back between your clicks — every observation arrives as a completed tool result)* — I'll `record` now; after each step I'll `read-recording` and pull the matching epochs with `watch-epochs` (pred `:event-id-prefix ":checkout"`, `since-id` from the last pull), narrating each one with its effect cascade.

This is the line the rf2-ahjbc purge rewrote (e1a95e7135 changed exactly one README line) to replace the retired `subscribe` example, and it replaced a push-stream with the wrong pull tool.

TRUTH AT TIP

- `record` observes SIGNALS, not events: its `signals` arg is REQUIRED (tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/tool-descriptors.edn `:required ["signals"]`) and the SIGNAL vocabulary is `{:app-db [path]}` / `{:sub [q]}` / `{:dom "sel"}` / `{:focus true}` (references/ops.md §Signal recording). A `record` call "for every `:checkout/*` event" has no signal to name — issued as written it fails on the missing arg, and with any signal it records value changes, not event epochs.
- The event-observation route is `watch-epochs {pred: {"event-id-prefix": ":checkout/"}}` polled with the previous `:head-id` as `since-id` — references/ops.md §Live watch and references/recipes.md §"Watch for X while I interact" both teach exactly that, with no recorder in the loop. The server's own routing rule 5 (get_re_frame2_pair_instructions.cljs:80-85) separates the two: `record` + `read-recording` "to sample while a human drives the UI", `watch-epochs` for "what already happened".
- README.md:165 (§How the connection works) states the correct route one screen later: "Live-watch is the pull-mode `watch-epochs` poll loop".

IMPACT

The README is the human-facing catalogue (skills/README.md names it "the shipped tool catalogue") and its Examples are what a developer pattern-matches their first prompts against. This one models a three-tool dance whose first call cannot succeed, for a gesture one tool answers. It is also the retired stream use-case's replacement example — the one place the purge should have shown the new route cleanly.

FIX SHAPE

One PR, one file, ~2 lines: rewrite the Claude reply as a `watch-epochs` poll — e.g. "*(polls between your clicks — every observation arrives as a completed tool result)* — after each step I'll call `watch-epochs` with pred `:event-id-prefix ":checkout/"` and the previous `:head-id` as `since-id`, narrating each new epoch with its effect cascade." Optionally keep a one-clause pointer that `record` + `read-recording` is the route when what you want is a VALUE (a path, a sub, a DOM node, focus) sampled while the human interacts.

GATE

No gate covers README prose — verify by hand; `python scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci` is the README's link gate (repo-root and beside-source READMEs), run it if any link is touched.

ACCEPTANCE

The §"Watch events as they fire" example names `watch-epochs` (with `event-id-prefix` + `since-id`) as the tool that observes the events and does not start a `record` without a signal; `grep -n 'record' skills/re-frame2-pair/README.md` shows `record` only where a signal is named.

title: skill(reagent-migration): three leftover-Reagent failures, three ids — the render-time refusal seam (:rf.error/ambient-frame-refused) and the complaint shape are untaught
description:
## CLAIM

- `skills/reagent-migration/references/catalog-judgment.md:306-325` (MIG-26): "Under Hicasso an `h/sub` from an ordinary `defn` **is legal** ... What fails is a read or a dispatch with **no active render**: a timer, a callback the browser invokes later, a foreign listener." and "An ambient `rf/dispatch` from a callback raises `:rf.error/no-frame-context` — **core's id, not a `hicasso-*` one** — at click time."
- `skills/reagent-migration/SKILL.md:104` (cardinal rule 2): "A converted `h/defview` has no ambient `subscribe`/`dispatch`, so a body with some sites rewritten and some not does not work." — states the law, never the diagnostic.
- `skills/reagent-migration/references/gotchas.md:7-31`: only the click-time closure trap is taught. Every diagnostic id the skill names anywhere (grep over the package): `:rf.error/no-frame-context` x9, `:rf.error/no-adapter-installed` x9, `hicasso-intent-needs-the-event`, `hicasso-intent-outside-boundary`, `hicasso-malformed-prevent`, `:rf.warning/hicasso-entity-key`, `:rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch`. Neither `:rf.error/ambient-frame-refused` nor `:rf.error/hicasso-sub-outside-render` appears in any file.
- Nothing in the skill says what a Hicasso complaint IS (the four ex-data slots) or where the index lives.

## TRUTH AT TIP

- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/intent.cljs:64-118` — `with-frame` binds `frame/*ambient-frame-refusal*` for the whole render extent "so ambient `rf/subscribe` and `rf/dispatch` refuse for the extent (HD-002 clause (a))"; the substrate's `:reason` names the recovery verbatim: "Read through the boundary's own collector (`sub`) ... and dispatch through an intent at a handler position ...".
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:595-601, 637-640` — that refusal surfaces as **`:rf.error/ambient-frame-refused`**, "rather than the generic `:rf.error/no-frame-context` — a refused ambient read and a genuinely frameless one are different mistakes and must not share a diagnostic". `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:1991` rows it; firing case "a Hicasso boundary body".
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/collector.cljs:584` — `h/sub` invoked outside a body raises **`:rf.error/hicasso-sub-outside-render`** (`implementation/hicasso/spec/complaints.md:102`; guide `docs/core/hicasso/02-views-and-reads.md:241`, `16-diagnostics.md:158`).
- `implementation/hicasso/spec/complaints.md:27-42` — every complaint is an `ex-info` whose `ex-data` carries four required slots: `:rf.error/id` (branch on this), `:where`, `:reason` (names the fix), `:recovery`; `:view`/`:source` are dev-only context. That file is the index; meaning per id is Spec 009 §Hicasso.

So the three commonest leftovers in a converted Reagent view map to three DIFFERENT ids at three DIFFERENT times:

| leftover | fails when | id |
|---|---|---|
| `@(rf/subscribe ...)` or `(rf/dispatch ...)` in a converted body, or in a helper `defn` it calls | at RENDER | `:rf.error/ambient-frame-refused` |
| `#(rf/dispatch ...)` closure surviving at an `:on-*` | at CLICK | `:rf.error/no-frame-context` |
| an `(h/sub ...)` moved into a callback / timer / promise | at FIRE | `:rf.error/hicasso-sub-outside-render` |

## IMPACT

The skill teaches only row 2. An author who converts a view whose helper `defn` still derefs `rf/subscribe` — the most common shape in a Reagent codebase — gets `:rf.error/ambient-frame-refused` at FIRST RENDER, and the skill's text points them at a click-time / frameless problem with the wrong id. MIG-26's "if it runs during render, leave it in the helper — that is the supported shape" is true only once the helper reads through `h/sub`; the skill never says the helper is ALSO deref-dropped (MIG-02 reaches helpers). And the complaint catalogue with stable ids is a headline Hicasso feature; the skill hands the author no way to read one, so the `:reason` that names the fix goes unread.
