title: ci(http): no lane runs a solo-namespace ordering, so latent load-order hook dependencies are ungated
description:
DISCOVERED-FROM rf2-zvbm9 (PR #8889), reported by that worker as an observation it deliberately did not file itself.

THE FINDING (verify at source before acting): the jvm-http CI job runs a bare "clojure -M:test", i.e. the full-suite ordering only. rf2-zvbm9 was a namespace that passed in that ordering and failed when run ALONE, because it depended on a late-bind hook published by a namespace load that an alphabetically earlier test namespace happened to perform. No gate would have caught it, and none will catch the next namespace that acquires the same kind of latent dependency.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE ONE BUG: the failure is silent and it accumulates. A namespace acquires an unnoticed dependency on somebody else load-ordering before it, the suite stays green, and the defect only surfaces when someone runs that namespace alone — which is exactly what a developer does when iterating, so the cost lands on the person least equipped to explain it. The specific hook here fails OPEN too: extract-paths returns an empty map when unbound rather than erroring, so the classification silently does nothing.

SCOPE IS A JUDGEMENT AND NOT OBVIOUS — this is filed to be RULED ON as much as fixed. Running every namespace solo multiplies the lane cost; running none leaves the hole. Candidate shapes worth weighing before building anything: a nightly rather than per-PR solo sweep; solo runs for a named set of namespaces with known late-bind dependencies; or making the hook fail LOUD when unbound, which converts a silent misclassification into an error and may remove the need for a solo lane at all. The last one is the smallest change and may be the right one — the stance prefers it over new CI machinery.

NOT URGENT: the specific instance is fixed by #8889, which requires the schemas namespace in the fixture that needed it.
notes:
MAYOR RULING, 2026-09-01: make the hook fail LOUD when unbound. Do NOT build a solo-namespace lane, nightly or per-PR, and do not add a named-set sweep.

The bead names three shapes and already leans at the right one. Confirming it as the ruling: extract-paths returning an empty map when unbound is a fail-OPEN, and that is the actual defect - the silent misclassification, not the absence of a lane. Convert it to an error. A namespace that has acquired a latent load-order dependency then fails immediately and says so, on the developer's own solo run, which is where the cost currently lands and where the message is most useful.

This is the smallest change, it removes a silent failure mode rather than adding machinery to detect one, and it may make a solo lane unnecessary - which is the point. New CI machinery to catch a class of bug that a two-line fail-loud converts into an ordinary error is exactly the over-engineering the stance rejects, and it would put a recurring toll on every PR forever.

If, having made the hook loud, you find a case it cannot reach, file that as its own bead with the case - do not widen this one into a lane.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #8943 (branch worker/cilanes). Followed the ruling exactly: the hook now fails LOUD when unbound, and NO CI machinery was added — no solo lane, no nightly, no named-set sweep.

THE DEFECT. privacy-body/extract-paths (implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/privacy_body.cljc) returned an empty marks map when the late-bind schema-walker hook was unbound. An unbound hook means the marks are UNKNOWN, not EMPTY, and answering {} for it is the fail-OPEN the ruling names: a :decode schema marking a slot :sensitive? classified nothing and the secret rode the trace verbatim, green either side of it. rf2-zvbm9 was exactly that — four assertions reading their own secret back, visible only in a solo-namespace run because the full-suite ordering happened to load re-frame.schemas first.

THE LOUDNESS IS GATED ON WHETHER A MARK IS DECLARED, AND THAT MATTERS — an unconditional throw would have been wrong in both directions, checked at source rather than assumed. (1) day8/re-frame2-schemas is a TEST-ONLY dep of the http artefact, and the artefact resolves malli.core directly (decode.cljc, which WARNS rather than throws when Malli is absent), so an app can legitimately use a Malli :decode with no schemas artefact at all; an unconditional throw breaks every such app on every successful response, and on the production accept-failure path (transport.cljc, not debug-gated) too. (2) In-tree, http-decode-test, http-managed-test and http-empty-body-parity all use vector :decode schemas WITHOUT requiring re-frame.schemas, so an unconditional throw reddens all three on a solo run for schemas carrying no marks at all.

So extract-paths separates the two cases with declares-marks?, a presence probe asking only whether the schema's EDN form writes a :sensitive? / :large? PROP anywhere — a MAP KEY, so a field merely named :sensitive? is not a mark. It reads no Malli semantics, resolves no registry, derives no paths: not a second walker (the ns doc forbids one), it only decides whether the shared walker is REQUIRED. Declares no mark → {} as before, and a schemas-less app is untouched. Declares a mark with the hook unbound → throws :rf.error/schemas-artefact-missing via the canonical error/throw-error! builder, naming the require that fixes it. Probe and walker agree on the opaque cases (keyword registry ref, compiled m/schema object): both read them as markless leaves, so neither throws.

REUSING THE EXISTING ERROR ID leaves spec/009-Instrumentation.md — hot-zone — untouched; the id is already catalogued there. The contract is recorded in its owning tracked record, spec/014-HTTPRequests.md §Privacy, as a new rule 5 (old rule 5 Composition becomes 6; nothing in the repo references these by number, checked).

GATES, captured exits on the final rebased base: implementation/http 'clojure -M:test' exit 0, 514 tests / 3901 assertions (was 508 / 3883 — the six new tests are §7 of http_privacy_body_test, pinning the throw for both mark axes and the four no-throw cases); scripts/check_doc_slugs.py exit 0 for the spec edit. Both gates were exercised against a planted fault and came back red naming what was planted; restores verified by git BLOB hash against the committed object.

NO CASE FOUND THAT THE LOUDNESS CANNOT REACH, so no follow-up bead was filed. One adjacent surface was checked and deliberately LEFT: resources/classification.cljc's validation-failure-params-marks has the same {}-when-unbound shape but is not a live fail-open — it runs only on a validation failure, which requires the schemas artefact to have validated in the first place, so the unbound branch is unreachable, and its surrounding comment states that posture deliberately.

title: hicasso guide ch04: the owned-literal alternate-spelling claim is not delivered by the taught plain merge
description: docs/core/hicasso/04-controlled-inputs.md §Forward caller attributes safely (lines ~116-119 at 1af79839db) claims: 'A caller cannot replace the field's value, checked state, handler, key, or revision by supplying an alternative spelling such as :onInput or "value"; the controlled contract binds to the React slot reached by the authored literal.' The taught spelling — a plain merge with owned keys last — never delivered it: {:onInput f :on-input [...]} survives the merge as two map keys, both land on React's one onInput slot in convert-entry, and which wins is map iteration order. rf2-6c12m.12 removed :& (so no spelling delivers it now) and chose NOT to add a slot-collision refusal in convert-props — the epic's direction is fewer refusals and trust the programmer, and ch02 §Forward attributes with owned keys last already says 'Forward maps should use the same kebab-keyword spelling as Hiccup; a foreign props object's "className" string is a different merge key.' DO: bring ch04's sentence in line with ch02 — the owned literal wins by presence when the caller forwards the SAME key; an alternate spelling of the same slot is a different key, so forward maps in the same kebab spelling (or dissoc the alternates). title: ambient-frame-refused records still depend on nonexistent rf2-k0rbk
description:
FOUND while fixing rf2-0d1w. That bead named TWO sites carrying the same stale PROVISIONAL claim and said they should move together; bench/** was outside the dispatch's write surface, so only the docs/design/hicasso/ half was fixed. This is the other half.

SITE: bench/hicasso/src/re_frame/bench/hicasso/arm1/ambient_refusal_cljs_test.cljs:315

  ';; THE ERROR ID IS NOT REPEATED IN THESE ROWS, deliberately.
   ;; :rf.error/ambient-frame-refused is PROVISIONAL (rf2-k0rbk may rename
   ;; it), so a carry's refusal is pinned as *the same id an ambient read
   ;; gets*, taken live from [[refusal-id]].'

WHY IT IS STALE, verified at source:

1. rf2-k0rbk is not a bead. bd show rf2-k0rbk -> 'no issue found' (exit 1) against a control that resolves; absent from all 511 issue ids in the export. It is cited only in prose, by rf2-0d1w and by the two sites it complains about.
2. The id is settled, not provisional. It is fully rowed in spec/009-Instrumentation.md:1991 and raised by re-frame.frame/emit-ambient-frame-refused! (implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:1035).
3. The rename it anticipates is forbidden. implementation/hicasso/spec/complaints.md §The stability rule: 'An id is stable: it names one refusal, and it is never re-spelled or reused.'

NOTE THE MECHANISM IS SOUND AND SHOULD SURVIVE. Taking the id live from [[refusal-id]] and anchoring the literal ONCE in the file is good test design for its own reasons - it keeps a rename to one row and keeps these rows about the interesting property (that a carry and a read agree). Only the JUSTIFICATION is stale. So this is a comment fix: drop the PROVISIONAL claim and the dead bead id, keep the indirection and say plainly why it is there.

NOTHING IS RED - comment only, which is why it is P4. The docs/design/hicasso/studio/hframe-design.md site was corrected under rf2-0d1w.
notes:
MAYOR NOTE, 2026-09-03 04:1x AUSEST — THIS IS ONE OF THREE, AND THE CLASS IS NARROWER THAN IT FIRST LOOKS. Three open beads now report the same shape: a marker in the tree gated on a bead id that does not exist. rf2-fgwf cites rf2-k0rbk, rf2-rn3u cites rf2-mxkq7, and rf2-0d1w reports an ambient-frame-refused PROVISIONAL note citing a nonexistent bead. All three ids confirmed absent by bd show.

I TRIED TO CENSUS THE CLASS AND THE CENSUS WAS INVALID — recording that here so nobody repeats it. Matching every rf2-* token in implementation/, tools/, docs/, spec/ and examples/ against the tracker export returns 5,179 distinct cited ids of which 4,997 are absent. That number is meaningless: this repo deliberately keeps historical bead citations in prose as provenance, and the tracker holds only ~516 issues, so essentially every citation older than the current tracker reads as absent. CLAUDE.md itself cites rf2-0yp7w as the authoritative ui/freehand retirement disposition, and rf2-0yp7w.4 — its own child — is likewise absent. A scan returning EVERYTHING is not corroboration; it means the comparison set was wrong.

THE REAL CLASS IS NOT 'A CITATION TO A DEAD BEAD', WHICH IS NORMAL HERE. It is A LIVE CONDITIONAL GATED ON NOTHING — a PROVISIONAL marker, a pending-on annotation, a 'revisit when X lands' note whose X cannot be found. A historical citation records why something is the way it is and ages harmlessly; a pending marker is a promise to revisit that nobody can ever discharge, and it will sit in the tree forever looking like live tracking.

SO A SWEEP HERE IS WORTH DOING AND MUST BE SCOPED TO PENDING MARKERS, NOT TO CITATIONS. Search for the marker vocabulary (PROVISIONAL, pending, 'until rf2-', 'when rf2-', 'blocked on rf2-', 'revisit') and resolve only the ids those markers gate. Exercise the instrument in both directions: a marker citing a REAL open bead must be found and left alone, and one citing a real CLOSED bead is a third case — the promise was discharged and the marker is stale, which is a different fix from a phantom.

Whoever takes this bead: do the scoped sweep as part of it and report the count. Two siblings (rf2-rn3u, rf2-0d1w) are the other known instances.
PR #9041 AUDIT FOLLOW-UP (merged 2026-09-02T16:56:03Z). The PR correctly settles item 2 in docs/design/hicasso/studio/hframe-design.md, but two earlier sentences in that same record still depend on the phantom rename owner it disproves: lines 266-269 say "rf2-k0rbk's rename" will touch the anchor, and lines 311-314 say rf2-e28wl is "to sequence with rf2-k0rbk". Because rf2-k0rbk does not exist and item 2 now says the id is settled and cannot be respelled, both are live contradictions, not harmless historical citations.

This open bead already owns the exact pending-marker class and the remaining bench carrier, so do not open another issue. Minimal finish: update those two hframe sentences plus the known bench comment to state the settled contract while preserving the useful live-id indirection; no general cleanup of historical bead citations is needed.
BENCH HALF DONE, 2026-09-03 (phantom-a worker). The docs/design/hicasso/ half is NOT done and is NOT mine to do - see REMAINS below.

WHAT CHANGED. bench/hicasso/src/re_frame/bench/hicasso/arm1/ambient_refusal_cljs_test.cljs: the PROVISIONAL claim and the bead id are gone. The comment now states the id is SETTLED on the same three grounds the docs/design/hicasso/studio/hframe-design.md half was corrected to (verified at source at tip, not copied from a note): the row at spec/009-Instrumentation.md:1991, the emitter re-frame.frame/emit-ambient-frame-refused! at implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:1035, and "The stability rule" at implementation/hicasso/spec/complaints.md:57-59.

THE INDIRECTION IS KEPT, and the justification is REWRITTEN rather than deleted. The old reason was rename economy ("a rename touches one row rather than five"), which dies with the rename. The real reason survives it: these rows assert that a carry and a read refuse IDENTICALLY, so taking the id live from [[refusal-id]] is what makes the agreement the property under test - two independent literals would assert two constants and could not see them drift apart. That is the bead's own reasoning ("keeps these rows about the interesting property").

ONE STALE CLAIM IN THE OLD COMMENT, CORRECTED IN PASSING. It said the literal is "anchored ONCE in this file". It is not: :rf.error/ambient-frame-refused appears at lines 19, 136, 153 and 186. The new wording says the rows above pin the spelling BY NAME (which is their job - two are named ...-refuses-by-name) and does not make a count claim.

THE "PHANTOM" FRAMING IS WRONG, AND THE CORRECTION MATTERS FOR THE FIX. rf2-k0rbk is not an id that never existed. It was a real bead - "rf2-2rtt6.122 follow-up: confirm or rename the provisional error id, and confirm the always-on elision call" - CLOSED 2026-08-06, and its close_reason reads: "Confirmed-as-implemented ... :rf.error/ambient-frame-refused stands; always-on stands. No code change needed per the bead's own terms. Remaining touch: the provisional stamps' removal is a one-line comment/docs touch the mayor folds i[n]". It was later garbage-collected out of the tracker (539 rows live today, 14,551 ids ever exported). So this marker is the DISCHARGED-PROMISE case, not the phantom case: the confirm-or-rename question was ASKED, ANSWERED "confirmed", and the marker simply outlived the answer. Full evidence and method on rf2-cu5h.

GATES. No local tier covers bench/hicasso - `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh --plan` arms docs + JVM implementation/core + node/CLJS + clj-kondo and no browser/bundle lane. Proved the change moves no code instead of asserting it: read both versions with the Clojure reader (which drops `;;` comments) - 32 top-level forms and 22 deftests before and after, printed-form sequences IDENTICAL. Controls both ways (self-equality holds; an altered copy is unequal).

REMAINS, and it is why this bead stays OPEN. docs/design/hicasso/studio/hframe-design.md:268 ("so `rf2-k0rbk`'s rename touches the one pre-existing anchor") and :313-314 ("Filed as `rf2-e28wl`, to sequence with `rf2-k0rbk`") still stand, and :268 contradicts item 2 of that same document, which now says the id is SETTLED. Both cited beads are real-and-closed (rf2-e28wl closed 2026-08-05, fixed in PR #7533), so both are discharged promises. docs/** was outside this dispatch's write surface - the same fence that split this bead off rf2-0d1w in the first place - so the two halves have now failed to move together TWICE. Whoever takes the remainder needs docs/design/hicasso/ in scope.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #9055 — the docs/design/hicasso/ half is done, so both halves of this bead have now moved and the fence that split them twice is discharged.

THE DESCRIPTION'S PREMISE IS REFUTED, and I re-verified it at source rather than taking the phantom-a note on report. rf2-k0rbk is NOT a phantom: it is 'rf2-2rtt6.122 follow-up: confirm or rename the provisional error id, and confirm the always-on elision call', closed_at 2026-08-06T01:22:51Z, close reason 'Confirmed-as-implemented ... :rf.error/ambient-frame-refused stands ... Remaining touch: the provisional stamps' removal is a one-line comment/docs touch.' rf2-e28wl is likewise real, closed_at 2026-08-05T06:26:01Z, 'Fixed in PR #7533.' METHOD, which is the durable lesson: the tracker is garbage-collected, so absence from bd show proves nothing at all; existence is decidable in the git history of .beads/issues.jsonl. Read a 3148-row export dated 2026-08-06 out of git and searched it fixed-string for each id, with BOTH controls — a known-present id (rf2-so3io) returns 1 and a known-absent one (rf2-ZZZZZ) returns 0 — so the instrument was shown to discriminate in both directions before its answer was believed.

SO THESE WERE DISCHARGED PROMISES, and the citations are KEPT as provenance with the resolution recorded beside each. THREE sites, one more than this bead's REMAINS note named:
- :266 — the rename-economy argument is marked discharged and the indirection re-justified on the reason that outlives the rename (a carry and a read must refuse IDENTICALLY, so reading the id live is what makes the agreement the property under test; two literals would assert two constants and could not see them drift apart).
- :311 — records that rf2-e28wl landed in PR #7533, VERIFIED AT SOURCE: the spec/009 row no longer enumerates :operation as (:dispatch / :subscribe) (0 matches) and now states the rule — the category is defined by the DOOR and :operation is documented as an OPEN set.
- :343 — THE SITE THE NOTE DID NOT NAME, and the one that most needed it: section 9 item 2's parenthetical positively asserted 'no such bead exists in the tracker'. That is the refuted claim standing in the tracked record as a statement of fact. It now records that the bead was real, that it closed answering 'confirm', that it was later garbage-collected, and that existence is decidable in the export's git history rather than in the tracker.

GATE: scripts/check_provenance_pins.py, the gate for this page — exit 0, 153 pages inspected, 821 cited pins, 696 landed / 112 stranded / 10 unresolvable / 3 foreign, 122 accompanied in scope, 0 findings. The scoped pending-marker sweep the MAYOR NOTE asked for was not run — it is a separate, larger piece of work than this bead's remainder, and the two known siblings (rf2-rn3u, rf2-0d1w) are its natural home. Worth noting for whoever picks it up that the note's own framing needs adjusting: it classes 'a marker citing a real CLOSED bead' as a third case, and this bead turned out to BE that case rather than the phantom case it was filed as — so the sweep should expect discharged promises to be the common finding, and GC means a phantom cannot be diagnosed from bd show alone.

## 4. `nine-states.md` footer pin predates material example changes

CLAIM (footer L304): "Derived from `examples/patterns/nine_states/core.cljs` @ main `89bd9c3`" (2026-05-12) and L202 "Lifted from `examples/patterns/nine_states/core.cljs`". Whether a user simulating a machine with timeouts in Xray's Static Sim should be able to fire a timer edge, and if so whether that is done by making machines-viz's `:after` event-nodes clickable (a public-contract change in a separately published artefact, `day8/re-frame2-machines-viz`, `tools/machines-viz/deps.edn:220`) — or, as this dossier shows is possible, entirely inside Xray's sim rail using data the engine already hands the sim on every step.

## The problem, carefully

**What machines-viz promises today.** `tools/machines-viz/spec/API.md:62` (§Props, `:on-edge-click`): *"Called with a JavaScript object carrying `eventId`, `fromPath` and `toPath` when a fireable event-node label is clicked … `:after` / `:always` nodes remain inert."* The component docstring says it again at `chart.cljs:880-884` ("Only edges with a fireable event (plain `:on` transitions) are clickable; `:after` / `:always` auto edges stay inert"), and the table at `API.md:400` marks the wildcard row `(:eventId nil, not user-fireable)`.

**Where the code enforces it.** `chart/projection.cljc:1694-1699`:

```clojure
fireable?    (and (nil? (:after e)) (not (:always? e)) (not (:on-done? e))
                  (keyword? (:event e)) (not= :* (:event e)))
event-id     (when fireable? (:event e))
```

emitted as `:eventId event-id` at `:1833`, beside `:fromPath`/`:toPath` (`:1834-1835`) and `:afterMs` (the raw `:after` map key, `chart/layout.cljc:376-384`). The renderer, `chart/nodes/event_node.cljs:210`, gates `clickable? (and (fn? on-click) (some? event-id))`; when false there is no `:role "button"`, no `:title`, no `:on-click` (`:272-278`) and the cursor is `"default"` (`:300`). So a click on an `:after` node never reaches any host — not even as a no-op callback. Two tests pin the nil: `chart/projection_cljs_test.cljc:1239-1256` ("not user-fireable") and `:2404-2406` (wildcard).

**The worker's finding, and the half of it that is true.** The C9 worker (bead note, "WORKER VERDICT", PR #10059) measured that firing a timer needs three values — the delay key, the node's current epoch, and the declaring path (region-prefixed inside a parallel region) — and that the chart payload carries the delay key (`:afterMs`) and the in-region path but not the epoch or the region. Correct as far as it goes: `spec/005-StateMachines.md:2481-2490` makes the timer a synthetic ordinary event `[:rf.machine.timer/after-elapsed <delay-key> <epoch> <decl-path>]`, `transition.cljc:1473` special-cases it into `pick-after-transition`, which fires only when `(= carried-epoch cur-epoch)` (`:1075-1082`), and the epoch is runtime state in the snapshot (`node-epoch`, `:937-951`, absent reads 0). The bead's framing — "the epoch can never be chart data" — is right. **But it does not need to be chart data**, and this is the fact the bead's notes do not carry:

**The sim already receives all three values on every step.** `re-frame.machines/machine-transition` returns `{:status :ok :snapshot … :fx […]}` (`implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines.cljc:138-164`), and for every entered `:after`-bearing node the `:fx` vector carries

```clojure
[:rf.machine/after-schedule {:rf/parent-id … :rf/invoke-id (vec prefix)   ; the decl-path
                             :state leaf :delay-key delay-key :epoch epoch :server? …}]
```

(`transition.cljc:2198-2204`), and for a parallel region the pure side has ALREADY prefixed `:rf/invoke-id` with the region name before the result leaves the engine (`parallel.cljc:758` and `:1116`, `prefix-region-invoke-id`). The sim stores that `:fx` on every audit row today — `sim_helpers.cljc:383` `:fx (:fx result)` — and its docstring says so ("The `:fx` ride into the audit-trail row but are NOT executed"). I ran a read-only probe from `implementation/machines` (`clojure -M <scratch>/after-probe.clj`, exit 0) assembling the timer event from nothing but those fx values:

```
step 1: :idle --:start--> :loading      status :ok  after-epoch {[:loading] 1}
  fx: [:rf.machine/after-schedule {:rf/invoke-id [:loading] :delay-key 5000 :epoch 1 …}]
step 2: [:rf.machine.timer/after-elapsed 5000 1 [:loading]]   status :ok  state :timeout
step 3: same with epoch 99                                     status :ok  state :loading  unchanged? true  fx []
seed:   build-initial-snapshot stamps no epoch; [… 5000 0 [:loading]] against the seed -> state :timeout
parallel: after [:go] fx carries :rf/invoke-id [:net :busy]; echoing it -> {:net :busy} becomes {:net :idle}
```

So: the timer fires from fx values; a wrong epoch is the silent no-change `step-sim` already reports (`sim_helpers.cljc:361-367`); the seed state (no fx yet) fires at epoch 0 because `node-epoch` reads an absent node as 0; and the parallel case needs no re-derivation of the engine's region rules. Every one of the worker's three "missing" values is in the sim's own hands, on the pure side, with no reach into `re-frame.machines.transition` internals.

**Who consumes the click payload.** Grep for `on-edge-click` across the tree (13 files, `.beads` excluded): the only FUNCTIONAL host is Xray's Static Sim, `static/machines/sim.cljs:793-802`, via the wrapper `panels/machine_canvas.cljs:417`; the live Machine Inspector passes nothing (`machine_inspector_helpers.cljc:312` is a docstring line); the machines-viz viewer page sets `:read-only? true` and never enables callbacks (`page/…/viewer.cljs:20,34`); `docs/` carries 0 mentions of `on-edge-click`/`eventId`/"remain inert" (control: `API.md` 1). So "every host" is, inside this repo, one host — but the artefact is published on its own (`:clein/build :lib day8/re-frame2-machines-viz`, `deps.edn:219-220`), so the promise is to hosts we cannot see.

**Xray's own spec already documents the inert click** — `tools/xray/spec/003-Machine-Inspector.md:1584-1586`: *"`:after` and `:always` auto edges are inert on click: the chart hands the sim no event id for them, so the click is a no-op."* And the rail's "Available from current state" list surfaces only direct `:on` transitions by design (`sim_helpers.cljc:144-152`: "`:always` / `:after` / parent-state inheritance are not listed in the picker").

## Make it tangible

Take the machine in the probe:

```clojure
{:initial :idle
 :states {:idle    {:on {:start :loading}}
          :loading {:after {5000 :timeout} :on {:loaded :ready}}
          :timeout {} :ready {}}}
```

**Today, in Static → Sim, after clicking `:start`:** the chart shows `:loading` amber with two event-nodes hanging off it — `:loaded` and `⌚ 5000ms` (`event_node.cljs:56`). Hover `:loaded`: pointer cursor, tooltip "Send :loaded"; click it and audit row `#1 :loading → :ready [:loaded]` appears. Hover `⌚ 5000ms`: default cursor, no tooltip, click does nothing at all — not even the "No change" diagnostic, because no callback fires. The rail's "Available from current state" lists `:loaded → :ready` only. The rail DOES print `:data {:rf/after-epoch {[:loading] 1}}` (`sim.cljs:366`, `pr-str` of the snapshot data), so a user who knows the internal event shape can type `[:rf.machine.timer/after-elapsed 5000 1 [:loading]]` into the event input (`parse-event-vector` accepts any vector headed by a keyword, `sim_helpers.cljc:282-320`) and press Step — and it works. Nobody will discover that; it is the gap.

**Under YES (B):** `⌚ 5000ms` gets a pointer cursor and a "Send" tooltip; clicking it delivers a payload to the host. The payload alone cannot carry the epoch, so Xray still has to resolve the click against the fx it stored — which is the same fold C needs. Every other host of `MachineChart` that passed `:on-edge-click` starts receiving clicks for `:after` nodes it was told would never arrive; `API.md:62`, `chart.cljs:884`, `API.md:400`'s neighbour rows and two projection tests change.

**Under the Xray-only middle path (C):** the chart is untouched — `⌚ 5000ms` stays inert, as the spec promises. The rail's list grows one row per armed timer on the active path, rendered like the existing rows (`sim.cljs:517-548`):

```
Available from current state
  :loaded            → :ready
  ⌚ 5000ms           → :timeout        (timer)
```

Clicking the timer row does what the `:on` rows do — fills the event input (`sim-set-pending-event`, an existing registration) with `[:rf.machine.timer/after-elapsed 5000 1 [:loading]]`, or steps directly through `sim-step` (also existing); Step yields audit row `#2 :loading → :timeout [:rf.machine.timer/after-elapsed 5000 1 [:loading]]` and the chart animates the `⌚` edge exactly as it animates a fired `:on` edge (the focused-event lens is driven from the audit row, `sim_helpers.cljc:396-410`). A guarded timer whose guard declines reads as today's "No change — … a guard declined …" diagnostic. Nothing new is registered, so the `registry_cljs_test.cljs` roster (the structural constraint recorded on this bead) is untouched.

## Options

### A. NO — close as not worth building
- What changes: nothing. Close reason records that the chart promise stands, that the engine honours a hand-typed timer event today, and that the fx-fold route (C) is the cheap path if anyone reopens.
- Consequences: a user simulating a machine with timeouts cannot get past a timeout without knowing an internal event shape and reading an epoch out of a `pr-str`'d map. `spec/003:1584-1586` already tells them the click is inert, so nothing is misdocumented.
- Cost: zero.
- Risk: the gap recurs as a review finding (it was found once by a senior-developer review wave and is a real ergonomic hole in the one surface whose whole point is "what happens next").

### B. YES — make `:after` event-nodes clickable in machines-viz (the bead's YES)
- What changes: `chart/projection.cljc:1694` (`fireable?` admits `:after`; payload grows `region`, or hosts read `:afterMs`), `chart/nodes/event_node.cljs:210,278` (clickable gate + payload), `chart.cljs:880-884` docstring, `spec/API.md:62` (rewrite the promise; §Events-as-nodes table `:400` context), `projection_cljs_test.cljc:1239-1256` (flip the pin) and probably `edges_cljs_test.cljs`; THEN in Xray `sim_helpers.cljc:419` `edge-click->event` widens to build the timer vector from the stored fx (the payload cannot carry the epoch, per the probe), `sim.cljs:793-802` reads the new keys, `sim_cljs_test.cljs:453` (`nil-event-is-noop`) and `spec/003:1584-1586` change.
- Consequences: a public behaviour change for every `:on-edge-click` host of a published artefact; hosts that assumed "inert" now receive clicks carrying a nil-or-new `eventId` shape. Also lossy at the seam the worker noted: xyflow `clj->js`-es node `:data`, so a Spec 005 function-valued delay key (`005:2364`) cannot round-trip through the payload — the host must match the click back to its own fx anyway.
- Cost: ~2 worker-mornings across TWO PRs in TWO artefacts, sequenced (machines-viz first; its test lane `test:tools-machines-viz` is the machine-wide shadow-cljs exclusive per this bead's lane notes; then the Xray node-lane PR). No CLAUDE.md hot-zone files, but `tools/machines-viz/spec/API.md` is that artefact's public contract.
- Risk: the chart-click half buys only what C buys (a way to fire a timer) at the price of a contract change; and the semantics are slightly off — an `:after` node is not an event the user "sends", it is the clock, and clicking it is really "advance the clock past this timer".

### B'. YES, additive (mine) — an opt-in prop, default off
- What changes: as B on the machines-viz side but behind a new optional prop (e.g. `:on-timer-click` receiving `{afterMs fromPath toPath}`), so `:on-edge-click`'s "remain inert" sentence stays literally true and existing hosts see no change; `API.md` gains a row rather than rewriting one.
- Consequences: no host breaks; the API surface grows by one prop for one host's one mode.
- Cost: same two-artefact, two-PR shape as B, ~2 mornings.
- Risk: it is still a cross-artefact public-surface addition for a Static-mode nicety, and Xray still needs the fx fold to supply the epoch — so B' = C + a chart affordance + an API row.

### C. Xray-only (mine; the brief asked for it) — fire timers from the sim RAIL, fed by the engine's own fx
- What changes: `static/machines/sim_helpers.cljc` gains two pure fns — `available-after-transitions` (walk the active path's nodes for `:after` entries, the same walk `available-transitions` does for `:on` at `:144-172`) and `after-elapsed-event` (look the `[invoke-id delay-key]` up in the after-schedule fx folded from the audit rows, default epoch 0 for the seed, build `[:rf.machine.timer/after-elapsed delay-key epoch invoke-id]`); `sim.cljs` renders one extra row kind in the "Available from current state" list (`:517-584`) and hands its click to the existing `sim-set-pending-event` / `sim-step` registrations; `sim_helpers_cljs_test.cljc` (JVM-runnable, three tests: flat, seed, parallel — the probe above is already the fixture) and one `sim_cljs_test.cljs` row test; `tools/xray/spec/003-Machine-Inspector.md:1576-1586` rail bullet gains a clause ("…and each armed `:after` timer as a `⌚` row that fires its timer event"); the sentence at `:1584-1586` stays TRUE and stays.
- Consequences: programmer gets the timer step where the sim's controls already are; machines-viz, its spec and its promise untouched; no new registration; the chart's `⌚` node keeps its cursor and its inertness, exactly as documented in both artefacts.
- Cost: ~0.5-1 worker-morning, one PR, one artefact, no hot-zone file. Gates: `clojure -M:test` from `tools/xray` for the helpers, the node lane (`npm run test:cljs`, shadow-cljs exclusive) for `sim.cljs`, clj-kondo. Fence: the four Xray files above plus one spec paragraph.
- Risk: low. The one design choice is whether the row lists every declared `:after` on the active path (simplest; a not-yet-armed or stale one just reads "No change") or only timers whose fx has been seen (stricter; misses the seed state unless epoch 0 is special-cased). Recommend the first — the engine is the arbiter and already answers honestly.

## Recommendation

**C**, with **A** as the acceptable fallback if even half a morning is more than this deserves right now. Not B or B'.

From the stance: the gap is real and it sits in the one surface built for "what happens next" — a machine with a 5-second timeout cannot be walked past its timeout today without typing an internal event shape and reading an epoch off a `pr-str`. That is a friction the sim exists to remove, and the remedy is small and confined. But the bead framed it as a CHART question, and the chart is the wrong place: an `:after` node is not an event a user sends, so machines-viz's "remain inert" is not a limitation to break, it is the correct semantics of a click-to-send affordance — and rewriting a published artefact's public contract, across two PRs and two lanes, to add a second way of doing what one rail row does, is precisely the over-engineering the second half of the stance resists. The C9 worker was right that its fence could not reach the data; what nobody had checked is that the engine already hands the sim the data on every step (`transition.cljc:2198-2204`, stored at `sim_helpers.cljc:383`), which collapses the cross-artefact change into an Xray-local one. "Trust the programmer" also cuts C's way: no new diagnostic, no chart mode, no prop — one row that does what the other rows do.

What would change my mind toward B': if Mike wants on-chart click parity for timers as a product stance (the chart as the sole control surface, the rail as read-only). Even then, do B' (additive prop) rather than B, and only after C has landed, since B' cannot fire anything without C's fold.

## Codex Recommendation

**Choose C in spirit: give Static Sim an explicit “Trigger timeout” action in its rail. Keep this increment in Xray, and refine C's implementation brief before dispatch.** Walking a loading state through success and timeout is ordinary SPA development; requiring an internal event vector undermines the tool's purpose. title: CLAUDE.md item (k)'s guard prescribes 'bd show --json | jq -r' — the same item, further down, records that idiom carrying the carriage return the guard exists to defeat
description:
CLAUDE.md instrument item **(k)** prescribes an extraction idiom as THE GUARD, and **the same item, 1,272 characters later, records that idiom carrying the very defect the guard exists to prevent.** The guard is incomplete rather than wrong, and it fails silently in the reassuring direction.

## The two sentences, both in item (k), verbatim at trunk `fb33e3d60c`

**The guard (char 97,146):**

> **The guard: probe the FIELD, not the rendering — `bd show <id> --json | jq -r '.[0].notes'`**

**The refutation (char 98,418, same item):**

> flattening the line breaks alone still read **0**, because the field had come through `jq -r` and
> the surviving carriage return sits inside the joined phrase, so stripping the carriage returns
> FIRST and flattening second is what reads **1**

So item (k) knows. What it never does is fold that back into the guard sentence, which is the line every reader copies.

## The measurement

Measured 2026-09-21 on `rf2-z0pma`, whose notes are large enough that the effect is unmissable:

| extraction | size | carriage returns |
|---|---|---|
| `bd show <id> --json \| jq -r '.[0].notes'` | 54,318 bytes | **315** |
| the raw `--json` output read with Python's `json` module | 53,794 chars | **0** |

**Found by a worker that had been instructed to use the jq form by its own dispatch brief** — and the brief got it from here. So the defect propagates: the coordinator prescribing the guard was prescribing the defect, on every dispatch, because it was copying this file.

## Why it matters more than an ordinary item (e) instance

Item (k) exists to escape a REAL trap: `bd show`'s renderer hard-wraps to its own width and strips backticks, so a probe of the RENDERING reads 0 on text that landed perfectly. **That diagnosis is correct and the rule — probe the field, not the rendering — must not be weakened.**

But the prescribed SPELLING of the remedy swaps one silent under-match for another. A probe spanning a line boundary now fails on the `\r` instead of on the wrap, and it fails in the same direction, with the same reassuring zero. **The reader who follows the guard most carefully is the one who lands in it**, because they only reach for the field extraction after being warned about the rendering.

This is also the exact shape item (k) already warns about one level up — a guard whose own instrument is broken — arriving through the guard's own prescribed command.

## The edit wanted

**Amend item (k)'s guard sentence so the extraction it names does not inject the carriage return.** The
cheapest correct form redirects the raw JSON and reads it with a JSON parser:

    bd show <id> --json > <file>.json
    # then, in Python:  json.load(open(path, encoding='utf-8'))[0]['notes']

**Keep the `encoding='utf-8'`** — native Python on Windows defaults to cp1252 and dies
`UnicodeDecodeError: 'charmap' codec can't decode byte 0x9d` on any bead carrying a curly quote or
an em dash, which is nearly all of them here. Measured twice on 2026-09-21.

Where a shell pipeline is genuinely wanted, `tr -d '\r'` after the `jq` restores it — but the parser
is preferable, because it removes a second failure mode in the same act: a `jq` filter carrying
nested quotes is easy to malform, and a malformed filter exits non-zero with a compile error rather
than answering (met twice on 2026-09-21).

**Do NOT weaken "probe the FIELD, not the rendering".** That rule is right and is not what is at
fault. **Do not delete the later refutation sentence either** — it carries its own measurement about
a different sub-case (flatten-then-strip versus strip-then-flatten) and stays useful.

**Do not add a gate.** There is nothing mechanically checkable that would not also flag every
legitimate `jq` use in the file.

## Fence and lane

**`CLAUDE.md` only**, and item (k) only. **It is a HOT-ZONE file and this item is SERIAL behind
`rf2-u6igq`**, which widens item (o) and is itself queued behind `rf2-z0pma`'s PR #10134. Second
waits for the first's PR to merge; no exceptions.

**Item (k) sits inside the single physical `Ways the INSTRUMENTS misreport` line**, which measured
76,477 characters / 76,953 bytes before `rf2-z0pma` appended 418 to it. An Edit against that line
needs a uniquely anchored short `old_string`; confirm uniqueness before editing.

Gate is `python scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci` (repo-root markdown is its surface, NOT
`check_doc_slugs.py`). **Expect a green that inspected nothing of the change** unless a markdown
link is added — prove the gate live with a planted broken link on the edited line, then say plainly
what its green did and did not inspect.

`CLAUDE.md` is `i/lf w/crlf`: never `sed -i`; take the three numbers with Python on the raw bytes —
total CR, total CRLF, bare LF — requiring CR == CRLF and **bare LF == 0**, because the two-number
form passes vacuously as `0 == 0` on a flattened file.

The report prescribed a sentence saying a `reg-cofx` `:schema` mismatch *"skips the handler, which is the silent-boot failure below"*. It found the sharper true route and wrote that instead: `validate-recordable-value!` skips only on an ABSENT key — there is no `nil` exemption — so the `nil` this generator returns for its absent/unusable cases is itself validated, and `:schema Session` would hard-error on **every cold boot**. Two plants, both red, both restored and verified by BLOB hash with `git diff --quiet HEAD` exit 0 as a second instrument:
1. **A4 identity-uniqueness** — duplicate id in `evals.json`, match count 1 as predicted → exit **1**, `ERROR: [re-frame2-improver] A4 uniqueness: id 33 is shared by 2 evals`. Restored to blob `7fd35bded64b53b324a004747c1ae6509d9cc34a`.

## THE WORKER CAUGHT ITS OWN DRAFT ERROR

It first wrote that `article_lifecycle_test.clj` pins `manual-retry-loops.md`; it pins `schemaless-events.md`. Caught by hand-verification before the PR, not by a gate — nothing in this repo validates that sentence.

## A MAYOR INSTRUMENT NOTE FROM THE MERGE ITSELF

Searching the rollup for `skills-structural` returned NO row, which read as "the structural job never ran" — the very job that loops this skill's two tests. It ran. The job KEY is `skills-structural`; its DISPLAY NAME is `Skills structural tests (changed skill paths only)`, COMPLETED/SUCCESS. ## The decision in one sentence

Whether `skills/re-frame2-improver/spec/inputs.md` §5 gets a one-line carve-out naming `docs/core/fresco/11-ephemeral-state.md` as the sanctioned source of leaf 6's three Fresco citations (A), or leaf 6's three citations move off `docs/core` to some other home that owns the same rule (B) — the rule itself, the merged PR, and what the improver's runtime reader sees stay the same either way.

## The problem, carefully

**The two sides, quoted at trunk.** `skills/re-frame2-improver/spec/inputs.md` opens (:3) "Skill-internal meta-doc … Not loaded during normal skill operation; exists to re-author the skill from inputs", and its §5 "What the skill does NOT consume" ends (:51):

> - **`docs/core/**`** — the narrative tutorial is for learners; the improver works one level up, on existing code.

`skills/re-frame2-improver/references/view-side-hook-state.md` cites that tree three times, all to one page:

- :13 (Detection rules) — "**Under Fresco**, a hook (`use-state` / `useState` / `useReducer`) or an `r/atom` inside an `h/defview` body is a finding whatever it holds. Fresco has no component-local reactive cell, and hooks in a body that branches on data make hook order data-dependent ([`docs/core/fresco/11-ephemeral-state.md`](…))."
- :33 (The canonical fix) — "Sources: [`docs/core/fresco/11-ephemeral-state.md` §Why one owner matters](…#why-one-owner-matters) (each fact has one owner — no second reactive store beside `app-db`) and [`spec/000-Vision.md` §Pointers to per-area Specs](…) (views as pure projections)."
- :84 (Edge cases) — "**Under Fresco the render-local exemption does not reach an `h/defview` body** — every fact still has an owner, just not a hook in the view. Hover and focus belong to CSS and the browser; high-rate mechanics … to a React island or declared host; anything another view, a test or Xray reads to `app-db`, where `h/reg-state` mints the per-instance sub + setter pair … ([§Common state and its owner](…#common-state-and-its-owner))."

All three are absolute `https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/blob/main/…` URLs, the form `scripts/check_skill_package_refs.py` prescribes for anything a shipped doc cites outside its package (its docstring :15-17). The review's cites (:13, :33, :84) are still exact at 155ff6871c.

**What the cited page contains.** `docs/core/fresco/11-ephemeral-state.md` is chapter 11 of the published Fresco guide (`mkdocs.yml:279` puts it in the nav). Its opening (:7-13) states the rule the leaf's :13 paraphrases — "Fresco has no component-local reactive cell. There is no Fresco equivalent of Reagent's `r/atom`, and `useState` does not belong in a `defview` body … That gives each fact one owner and keeps a second reactive store out of the application." §Why one owner matters (:15-33) gives the three properties the leaf's :33 cite leans on (data-driven tests, complete Xray cause chain, frame isolation) and the line "A host may still keep React state … It must not keep an invisible duplicate of an application fact" (:32-33). §3 (:160-162) carries the hook-order clause: "Hooks belong in the island. A `defview` body may branch and loop dynamically, so putting hooks there makes hook order depend on data". §Common state and its owner (:194-205) is the eight-row placement table the leaf's :84 summarises (hover/focus to CSS and the browser, drag to native host state, selected tab to app-db, `h/reg-state` in §1 :41-66).

**How the contradiction arose — it was ruled in, not drifted in.** The exclusion line is old: `git log -S 'narrative tutorial is for learners'` lands on `3d43fbb09a` (2026-05-23), months before Fresco existed in this leaf. The three citations landed together in `975273f918` (2026-09-13, PR #9736) under rf2-fi12: its F2 finding read "the leaf mentions fresco / reg-state / h/ zero times … Fix: one 'Under Fresco' clause in Detection rules and one in Edge cases with an absolute link to 11-ephemeral-state.md", and its close reason records F7 as "re-pointed to docs/core/fresco/11-ephemeral-state.md section Why one owner matters. The bead named docs/core/views.md:274-276 as a second home; those lines are the reg-view house rule, not single-owner text, so it is not cited." Before that commit the leaf's :32 read "Spec source: `spec/Principles.md` (single source of truth for application state) and `spec/000-Vision.md` …" — and `spec/Principles.md` carries **0** lines matching `single source of truth` today (control: the phrase reads 5 in `spec/README.md`), so the pre-September source was already a dangling pointer. The mayor chose the guide because it is where the rule is actually written down; nobody re-read `inputs.md` §5 at the time.

**Who it affects — a re-author, and nobody else.** At runtime the improver loads `SKILL.md` and only the matching leaves (`SKILL.md:51`, :61-63); `package.json:29-35` ships `SKILL.md`, `README.md`, `LICENSE`, `references/`, `.claude-plugin/` and not `spec/`. So a programmer using the skill, and the AI running it, read the leaf as it stands under every option. The reader who meets the contradiction is the one `spec/authoring-prompt.md` addresses — a full re-author (:16 "read `inputs.md` — the canonical inputs"; :28 "each … footering to the spec owner `inputs.md` §3 verifies") or a maintainer following `inputs.md` §6.

**Where else the same content lives — the search B needs, done.**

| Candidate home | What it says | Status as an input |
|---|---|---|
| root `spec/` | Nothing. `git ls-files 'spec/*resco*' 'spec/**/*resco*'` returns 0 paths; `spec/000-Vision.md` reads 0 for `fresco`; `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` names Fresco at :254 and :737-741 for root mounting and `data-rf-view` annotation only; `spec/009` hits on `hook` are late-bind hooks (:255, :268). | The allowed tertiary input (`inputs.md` §3) — and it has no Fresco page to point at. |

The linearlite example declares `:decode :json` on every request but only works because its canned stub hands Clojure keywords through undecoded; a real JSON backend returns `"backlog"` strings and every board column silently empties — so do we add a comment at the `:decode` site saying so (A), make the example survive a real JSON boundary (B), or leave it (C)?

One sentence of history: the review filed this against a README sentence ("the same reply shape a live server would produce") that does not exist at any revision (`live server` and `reply shape` each read 0 in `README.md` and `core.cljs` at trunk and at the review tree `b60a20abca`, per the bead), so the "README makes a false promise" framing is refuted; what survives is the mechanism, which the worker then MEASURED on the JVM rather than reasoned about, and which I re-measured today (below).

## The problem, carefully

**The example.** `examples/capabilities/resources/linearlite/` is "the write-side flagship" (`examples/README.md:121`) for optimistic mutations and is now indexed from `docs/resources/examples.md:10` (that row landed in PR #10176). Its domain is keyword-based end to end:

- columns are keywords — `examples/capabilities/resources/linearlite/core.cljs:97-102`: `[{:id :backlog …} {:id :in-progress …} {:id :done …}]`;
- the change-status mutation's params schema is `[:map [:id :string] [:status :keyword]]` (`core.cljs:323`), its optimistic patch writes that keyword (`:325-326`), and its request body carries it (`:339-341`);
- the picker turns the `<select>` value back into a keyword (`core.cljs:587-588`, `(keyword (.. % -target -value))`) and renders with `(name status)` (`:585`);
- the seed board the stub serves is keyword-valued (`core.cljs:372-375`) and a create mints `:status :backlog` (`:412`; optimistic twin at `:271`);
- the board view partitions issues by `(filterv #(= (:id status) (:status %)) issues)` (`core.cljs:687`).

**Every request declares `:decode :json`** — four sites: the board read (`core.cljs:146`) and the three mutations (`:292`, `:317`, `:342`).

**What `:decode :json` actually does.** Spec 014 is explicit: an explicit content-type decode has "No Malli step. The user gets the raw decoded value" (`spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:245-255`). The implementation's `:json` arm is `rf.http.json/json-parse` (`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/decode.cljc:266-273`), which keywordizes object KEYS only — on the JVM via a Cheshire `key-fn` that calls `keyword` on each key (`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/json.cljc:93-101`), on CLJS via `js->clj parsed :keywordize-keys true` (`json.cljc:109-133`). A JSON string VALUE stays a string on both hosts.

**What the demo stub actually does.** The example overrides `:rf.http/managed` with `:linearlite.demo/http-stub` (`core.cljs:429-473`), which builds a Clojure payload and hands it to the framework's `:rf.http/managed-canned-success` as `:value` (`:469-473`). That fx delivers `{:status :ok :value value}` verbatim — `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/test_support.cljc:202` reads `:value` off the args and `:219` builds the reply from it; no decode, no `:accept` (a search for `decode-response-body|run-accept|:decode` over `test_support.cljc` reads 0 matches, against 11 lines naming `keywordize-keys`/`json-transformer` under `implementation/http/src`). Spec 014 says the same at `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:1038` and `:1041` ("a minimal canonical reply — `{:status :ok :value v}`"). The resources layer then installs `(:value reply)` as the entry's `:data` unchanged (`implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/events.cljc:2502-2506`) and hands a mutation's `(:value reply)` to its `:patches` fn as `result` (`implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/mutation_events.cljc:1720-1724`; the call is `(patch-fn old mutation-result)` at `mutation_runtime.cljc:267-272`).

So the board's keywords never cross a codec. The `:decode :json` the example declares four times is preparation for a boundary the shipped demo never reaches.

**Who it affects.** Not the demo as shipped (nothing is wrong on screen; the README's own section is headed "No backend ships with the example", `README.md:149-164`). It affects the programmer — or the AI — who copies this flagship into a real app and does the one obvious next thing: point it at a JSON server. They get a loaded board with three empty columns and no error. The README makes no value-type promise, so nothing is FALSE; it is a latent trap one sentence away from being disarmed.

**Measured versus asserted.** The worker executed the JVM branch of `decode-response-body` over the stub's board and the example's own filter (bead description): canned `{:backlog 1 :in-progress 1 :done 1}`, real JSON `{0 0 0}`, controls both ways. I re-ran an equivalent probe today from `implementation/http` (JVM, malli added via `-Sdeps`, script in my scratchpad `zw6nf-probe.clj`) and extended it to the option-B routes — figures in the next section. The concurrent Codex pass (appendix) additionally executed the example's pure patch functions on the JVM and read the mutation-side vanishing described below. **The CLJS branch was READ, not executed**, by all three: the example is `.cljs`, and executing its branch needs the shadow-cljs lane. `js->clj :keywordize-keys true` is a ClojureScript core contract and `json.cljc`'s own docstring pins both hosts to behave identically (`json.cljc:102-108`), so an asymmetry is unlikely but is stated as unexecuted.

The owning spec for the Resources capability is `spec/016-Resources.md` (`spec/Ownership.md:63-64`); the decode pipeline is Spec 014's (`spec/Ownership.md`'s managed-HTTP row).

```clojure
          {:id "srv-2" :title "Render the three status columns" :status :done}
          {:id "srv-3" :title "Add the create-issue form"       :status :backlog}]}
```

**What a real JSON backend returns for `GET /api/board`** — this is `json-stringify` of that same board, taken from my probe, byte-for-byte what a server would have to send to be "the same data":

```json
{"issues":[{"id":"srv-1","title":"Wire up the optimistic board","status":"in-progress"},
           {"id":"srv-2","title":"Render the three status columns","status":"done"},
           {"id":"srv-3","title":"Add the create-issue form","status":"backlog"}]}
```

**What `:decode :json` makes of it** (probe, JVM branch): `{:id "srv-1", :title "Wire up the optimistic board", :status "in-progress"}` — keys keywordized, `:title` byte-identical, `:status` a `java.lang.String`.

**Probe results, column counts in Backlog / In Progress / Done order** (my measurement, 2026-09-22, exit 0):

| Path | Columns | `:status` type |
|---|---|---|
| 1. canned (what the demo runs) | 1 / 1 / 1 | Keyword |
| 2. `:decode :json` over the wire JSON | **0 / 0 / 0** | String |
| 3. Malli schema `:decode` with `[:status :keyword]` over the same JSON | 1 / 1 / 1 | Keyword |
| 4. `:json` then `(update i :status keyword)` per issue | 1 / 1 / 1 | Keyword |

**Exactly which board expression breaks first, and how it presents.** With a real backend the read succeeds: `:rf/resource` settles `:loaded`, `:rf.resource/data` hands the view `{:issues [...]}` (`core.cljs:659-662`). In the `cond` at `:673-688`, `(:loading? state)` is false and `(:error state)` is nil, so the `:else` branch renders `[:div.board]` and, for each of the three statuses, `(filterv #(= :backlog "backlog") issues)` at `:687` returns `[]`. `board-column` (`:645-650`) then renders its `<h2>` and an empty `<ul.issue-list>`. **Presentation: three headed, empty columns. No skeleton, no "Could not load the board", no exception, no console warning, no trace warning** — the resource reports data present and loaded, and Xray would show a populated entry. It fails in the reassuring direction.

**It is not only the first load — the writes commit the same way.** A create paints its optimistic card in Backlog (`:271`, keyword), then the server's row `{"id":"srv-4","status":"backlog"}` replaces it at commit (`:278-285`) and the card vanishes from every column. A status move paints the card in its new column (`:325-326`, keyword from the picker), then the commit assoc's `(:status saved)` — a string — at `:335` and the card vanishes. Retitle commits only `:title` (`:310`) and is unaffected. I inferred this from the patch functions; the Codex pass executed those pure functions on the JVM and read a canned move as `[0 1 2]` against `[0 1 1]` for the same move committed from a JSON reply, and a canned create `[2 1 1]` against `[1 1 1]` (appendix, its measurement). The optimistic phase looks right and the commit undoes it — the inverse of the lesson the example teaches. The request BODY is fine either way: `{:status :in-progress}` serialises to `"in-progress"`.

**What the Resources / HTTP capability offers for reply coercion (option B priced against the API).** Spec 016 puts response shape-validation on the request's `:decode` and nowhere else: `:data-schema` is a static tooling fact that "does not drive runtime validation … runtime shape-validation of a response … rides the `:request`'s `:decode`" (`spec/016-Resources.md:767`, `:795`); the registration example is `:decode :app/article` (`:780`); there is deliberately no `:select` key (`:814-816`); a request fn "describes the domain request only (method, url, params, body, `:decode`)" (`:1157`). Spec 014's schema-driven path JSON-parses then runs Malli `decode` with the `json-transformer` (`spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:226-241`; `decode.cljc:305-337`), and the artefact's own test pins that a string `"active"` under `[:status :keyword]` comes out as `:active` (`implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_decode_test.clj:104-115`). Malli is on the examples' browser build (`implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:464-465`, `[metosin/malli "0.20.1"]` under `:dependencies`; the `:examples/linearlite` build is at `:1890-1894`), and `realworld_http` already uses schema `:decode` everywhere (`examples/real-apps/realworld_http/tags.cljs:169`, `auth.cljs:387`, …) with a `[:status :keyword]` slot in its schemas (`examples/real-apps/realworld_http/schema.cljs:200`). The docs teach it in one line: "Pass a Malli schema instead of `:json` to validate the reply shape" (`docs/resources/tutorial/03-auth-and-forms.md:231`). Control: no example under `examples/capabilities/` uses a schema `:decode` (the `:decode` search over `examples/` returns only `realworld_http`/`realworld_shared` for non-`:json` forms), while `:decode :json` reads 19 occurrences across 11 example files, 4 of them linearlite's.

The other in-API seam, `:accept` (`spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:322-345`, `(decoded → {:ok v} | {:failure m})`), could carry a keywordise step in its `{:ok v}` — but it is **parked** with "zero shipped consumers" as of 2026-09-08 (`:324`, rf2-kuky.13), so using it in a flagship example would un-park it by accident. And a custom `:decode` fn receives raw `body-text` (`decode.cljc:263-264`) and would have to re-implement `json-parse` minus its key-interning cap (`json.cljc:26-30`). Neither is the B spelling to price; the schema is.

**Option A's comment, and where.** One comment at the board read's `:decode` (`core.cljs:144-146`), naming the three writes rather than repeating itself there:

```clojure
  (fn [_params _ctx]
    {:request {:method :get :url "/api/board"}
     ;; `:json` keywordizes object KEYS, not values. The demo stub below hands
     ;; this board through undecoded, so `:status` arrives as the keyword the
     ;; domain uses (`:backlog`). A real JSON backend returns "backlog", and the
     ;; column filter (`(= (:id status) (:status %))`) would then match nothing
     ;; — three empty columns, no error — and each write's commit would put the
     ;; server's string back over your keyword. Pointing this at a server: swap
     ;; `:json` for a Malli schema carrying `[:status :keyword]`, here and on
     ;; the three writes below, and the runtime coerces it at the boundary.
     :decode  :json}))
```

That is the long form; the bead's two-line minimum is the first sentence and the last. Both Codex passes insist the comment name the write replies as well as the read (appendix); the text above does.

**What a programmer copying this example into a real app hits, per option.**

- A: reads the resource declaration first (it is the first thing a copier changes), sees the comment, swaps `:json` for a schema on four lines, done. If they skip the comment they hit C's outcome, but the explanation is at the exact line they were editing.
- B (schema): copies a board that already survives JSON; the cost is that the schema's validation is a new failure mode (`:rf.http/decode-failure` on a shape mismatch) they now own, in an example that is not about that.
- B (strings): copies a string-valued domain; nothing to swap, and the Clojure enum idiom is gone from the flagship.
- C: three empty columns, `:loaded`, no error, and the diagnosis is `(= :backlog "backlog")` somewhere in a 741-line file.

## Options

The bead's letters are used below; note that the PR #10176 body priced the same choices under DIFFERENT letters (there A = strings end-to-end, B = keywordize at the boundary, C = comment), so a worker briefed from the PR body would implement the wrong letter — the ruling should name the option by content as well as letter.

### A. A comment at the `:decode :json` site (no behaviour change)
- What changes: the comment above at `core.cljs:144-146` (optionally one pointer line at the change-status commit, `:335`). Nothing else.
- Consequences: programmer — the trap is disarmed at the line they will edit first; AI — a comment beside the declaration is exactly what a model copying the example reads; tools/production — none; spec — none.
- Cost: minutes, one file (`examples/capabilities/resources/linearlite/core.cljs`, not hot-zone), no spec sentence. Examples are test-free (rf2-8cevm), so no test; the CI `cljs-examples-compile` job compiles it on the `examples_compile` surface (armed by `examples/*`), so no local shadow-cljs run is required for a comment-only diff.
- Risk: essentially none; the worst case is a comment that goes stale if the decode contract changes, and it names the contract by its spec behaviour rather than a line number.

### B. Normalise in the example so the board survives a real JSON backend
Two honest spellings (a third, hand-rolled `:decode` fn, is rejected above):

**B-schema — keep keywords, coerce at the boundary with the API's own seam.** Replace `:decode :json` at `:146`, `:292`, `:317`, `:342` with a Malli schema, e.g. `(def ^:private board-schema [:map [:issues [:vector [:map [:id :string] [:title :string] [:status :keyword]]]]])` (writes reply in the same envelope, `:427`), optionally mirrored into `:data-schema` for tooling (`spec/016:767`).
- Consequences: programmer — the copied board is JSON-ready and the domain stays idiomatic; the example now also teaches schema-driven decode, which is real but is not its lesson, and a malformed reply now classifies as `:rf.http/decode-failure` (`spec/014:241`), a failure path the example never explains. AI — sees the repo's real pattern (as `realworld_http`) in the focused example. Tools — Xray gets a `:schema` fact. Production — none. Spec — none.
- **The shipped demo cannot demonstrate it**: the canned stub bypasses decode entirely (`test_support.cljc:219`), so the schema is dormant code in the demo and live only for the copier. Nothing on screen changes.
- Cost: ~30 minutes plus one shadow-cljs compile (it is a code change; the CLJS decode branch stays read-not-executed unless someone also runs `dev:example` against a JSON server, which the example does not ship). One file, not hot-zone.
- Risk: low; Malli is on the build. The design risk is scope creep in a teaching artefact whose whole pitch is how little machinery optimistic writes need (`core.cljs:2-11`).

**B-strings — strings end to end.** `"backlog"` / `"in-progress"` / `"done"` at the eight keyword-literal sites (`:100-102`, `:271`, `:373-375`, `:412`); `:status :string` at `:323` (the one params schema carrying it — the PR body's "two schemas" over-counts); drop `(keyword …)` at `:588` and `(name status)` at `:585`. The `data-testid` at `:646` goes from `column-:backlog` to `column-backlog`; nothing in the tree reads it (`column-` has one code site, `:646`; examples are test-free), so that is cosmetic.
DOSSIER (continued, part 2 of 2; same canonical record, preserved verbatim from ai/decisions/rf2-zw6nf.linearlite-json-values.md)

- Consequences: survives any JSON boundary with no codec at all, and the shipped demo then exercises exactly the data shape a server would send; costs the example its keyword enum, in a Clojure teaching artefact, to guard against a backend that does not ship. This is the second Codex pass's preference (appendix).
- Cost: ~20 minutes plus a compile and a manual create / move / retitle / rollback check in the browser; one file.
- Risk: low mechanically; it is the least idiomatic of the three and moves the domain model to suit a transport.

### C. Leave it
- What changes: nothing.
- Consequences: defensible — the README promises no backend and no value types, so nothing is false. The cost lands on the first copier, as the empty-board scenario above, with no clue in the file.
- Cost: zero.
- Risk: a flagship example that quietly fails the first realistic thing done with it.

## Recommendation

**A.** Argued from the stance: nothing is wrong on screen, the example is honest about shipping no backend, and the trap is one sentence away from being disarmed at exactly the line a copier edits first. "Trust the programmer" says a sentence beside the declaration is enough — not a schema they did not ask for, not a domain model bent to a transport. "Don't litigate the minutiae" says a JSON-codec lesson does not belong in the optimistic-writes flagship. B-schema is the elegant, in-API answer and is what the comment should POINT AT, but as a change to the example it adds machinery that the shipped demo cannot even exercise (the stub bypasses decode), so it would be code that exists to be read rather than run. B-strings is the one spelling where the demo genuinely runs on server-shaped data, which is a real point in its favour; against it, the enum idiom is what a Clojure programmer expects to see in a flagship, and swapping it for strings to satisfy a transport the example does not ship is the kind of pre-emptive change the second half of the stance tells us to stop at. C is defensible but leaves a reassuring-direction failure in the flagship for the price of a comment. The worker and the mayor both landed on A (bead description); the two Codex passes split, one for A and one for B-strings (appendix).

What would change my mind: a decision that examples should be backend-swappable by construction — then B-schema, and as a policy across the 19 `:decode :json` example sites rather than this one; or a planned real backend / backend-integration tutorial for linearlite, in which case B-schema lands with that work and the comment is redundant.

### Method

1. Traced every verdict and exit-code path of the JVM runner and the CLJS node runner against the nine scenarios in the brief. Tracker searches for prior rulings: `test-quiet`, `test_quiet`, `spec-resource`, `spec_resource`, `slurp-resource`, `conformance`, `vacuous`, `graph egress`, `sensitive? stamp`, `contains-secret`, `project-graph`, `opaque-handle`, `embeds-raw`.

3. Read the security and conformance corpora for assertions that cannot fail, and confirmed every candidate with a bounded JVM probe.

| bead | P | title |
|---|---|---|
| rf2-3x7nj.20.1 | 3 | derivation graph-egress leak predicate matches only a leaf EQUAL to the secret, so a projection that embeds it stays green (executed: `opaque-handle` regressed to ship the canonical token, section (g) 58/58 still green, secret on the wire as a substring) |

**test-quiet: zero findings. spec-resource: zero findings.**

### Considered and rejected (do not re-litigate)

1. **A test calling System/exit or js/process.exit.** The process exits with that code, possibly 0, with no summary, and there is no guard. Rejected because nothing live does it: 11 `src` files carry `System/exit`, all of them CLI mains, and the only test `-main` calls are test-quiet's own `-H` subprocess fixtures. A halt-on-exit guard is the speculative hardening that "trust the programmer" rejects.
2. **An error outside any deftest.** A namespace-load throw or a fixture throw propagates through cognitect `-main`, then clojure.main's catch-Throwable exits 1 (`main.clj:663-667`). Pinned by `namespace-load-throw-exits-nonzero` and `once-fixture-throw-exits-nonzero`. CLJS: an uncaught throw exits non-zero, and `exitCode` is seeded to 1 anyway.
3. **Zero tests.** `(apply run-tests ())` falls through to `(run-tests *ns*)`, which is `user`, so `:test` is 0 and the floor reds the run. Pinned by `zero-test-discovery-is-red`. CLJS: the pre-run floor counts discovered vars, and an unmatched `--test=` selector is refused.
4. **A var filter matching nothing.** An unresolvable `-v` throws (exit 1). `-i`, `-e` or `-v` matching nothing leaves 0 tests, which the floor catches.
5. **stderr ring overflow.** It changes only the red-replay content, never the verdict. The front-trim is O(cap) per append past the cap, which is not pathological.
6. **Warning-as-failure.** Neither runner has such a rule, so there is nothing to lie.
7. **Output after the summary.** stdout passes through. stderr written after a red run's replay is dropped. That loses diagnostics only; the exit code is unaffected.
8. **Exit code vs printed summary.** Cognitect exits from the same summary map the reporter prints. The runner's own reds (floor, uncallable fixture, probe) print a clean tally and then exit 1, which disagrees only in the safe direction.
9. **Reporter overrides.** test-quiet's `:fail` and `:error` overrides delegate to the captured library defaults, which increment the counters, so failures are counted.
10. **Nested run-tests.** A nested `run-tests` inside a test fires the `:summary` hook mid-suite. That can only false-red, and there is no live instance.
11. **Tests cognitect never discovers.**
   - Default ns-filter (`.*-test$`) skipping a deftest-bearing namespace: census over all 31 test-quiet lanes found 0 such files, against a control of 941 matching files.
   - Deftests outside the discovery dirs: only the top-level `implementation/deps.edn` REPL-convenience `:test` alias puts them there. That alias discovers a nonexistent `test/`, so the floor reds it rather than greening it.
12. **A test namespace redefining `clojure.test/report :summary`** would silently remove the floor. There are 0 live instances outside test-quiet's lifecycle fixtures.
13. **CLJS `parse-min-tests`** accepts hex and exponent notation through `js/Number` where the JVM side rejects them. This cannot disable the gate.
14. **spec-resource contracts hold.**
   - `(:ns env)` refuses a JVM macro `&env`, which is a locals map.
   - `resolve-after-require` takes `RT/REQUIRE_LOCK` before resolving.
   - `shadow.resource/slurp-resource` records `::resource-refs path` against the last-modified time (`resource.clj:47-49`), so a data edit invalidates the consumer.
   - The directory-listing consumer does not see an ADDED file. That was ruled an accepted bounded tradeoff in rf2-1tlr4's close.
15. **spec-resource race control.** In principle `::blocked` could be an unrelated monitor, but the `requiring-resolve` control reproduces `:unbound`, so the harness is not vacuous.
16. **Restoring `default-schema-fns` after the throwing-validator test** does not soft-pass later tests, because `default-malli-validate` late-binds to Malli.
17. **Security generators that look shape-irrelevant still bite.** Whole-slot elision of sensitive machine ex-data, and grammar-breakout suffixes that already carry a breakout char, do not make those properties vacuous.
18. **The generated-cofx test's part (a)** is vacuous by design (the op may be absent), but its part (d) checks the whole trace stream.
19. **The framed reply-envelope security tests** scan only the four wire slots. That is narrower, not vacuous: the frameless test scans the whole summary.
20. **The flows sensitive-`:explain` leak** is already open as rf2-3x7nj.18.1 (flows slice). It is a different case: registration-classified, not schema-classified.
21. **The completeness of the SSR event-handler allowlist** belongs to the SSR slice.

No tracked file was edited and no git write was made.

title: machines-lifecycle: join resolution cancels a child that already finished but whose carrier has not folded (completed, cancelled and suppressed terminals for one attempt)
description:
## Defect

At join resolution `build-resolution-fx` treats every child not in `:done ∪ :failed` as a SURVIVOR. Those sets record carriers already FOLDED, not actors already FINISHED. A child that reached `:final?` (published its `:completed` terminal, auto-destroyed with `:reason :rf.machine/finished`) but whose carrier is still queued behind the decisive one is therefore also stamped `:rf.machine.spawn/cancelled-on-join-resolution` with `:rf.reply/work-status :cancelled`. Its carrier then lands as `late-completion :suppressed`. One child attempt publishes three contradictory terminals (completed → cancelled → suppressed), which breaks Spec 005:4017 ("each child attempt has exactly ONE terminal authority") and 005:4058 (a `:rf.machine/finished` actor "already closed its attempt … carries no cancelled reply facts"). The work-ledger / Xray reply rows show a child that finished as cancelled. The trigger is ordinary: any `:any` (or `:on-any-failed`) join whose children can finish in the same drain, for example children that complete on `:start`.

## Where

- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/join.cljc:486-539`: `survivors` = `:children` minus `(:done ∪ :failed)`. For each one, `:rf.machine.spawn/cancelled-on-join-resolution` is emitted with a `cancelled-actor-reply` and a `[:rf.machine/destroy id]` (a silent no-op for the already-gone actor).
- Public entry: a declarative `:spawn-all` whose join resolves while another child's completion carrier is still queued.

## Failure scenario

`:racing {:spawn-all {:children [{:id :a :machine-id :pd/child :start [:go]} {:id :b :machine-id :pd/child :start [:go]}] :join :any :on-some-complete [:race/won]}}` with a child that goes `:running` → `[:go]` → `:done {:final? true}`. Dispatch `[:pd/parent [:start]]`. Both children finish before either carrier folds. :a's carrier resolves the join. :b, already finished and gone, is "cancelled".

## Evidence

Executed with a bounded JVM probe (`probe_d.clj`, frozen tree `034d0c8fc8`). Terminal evidence for `:b`, in order:
`[:rf.machine/done :completed]`, `[:rf.machine/destroyed :rf.machine/finished]`, `[:rf.machine.spawn/cancelled-on-join-resolution :cancelled]`, `[:rf.machine.spawn-all/late-completion :suppressed]`.

Control (only :a started, :b genuinely live): `[:cancelled-on-join-resolution :cancelled]`, `[:rf.machine/destroyed :cancelled :explicit]`, which is correct.

Provenance: this exact defect was raised by the merged-PR audit #9353 in rf2-kuky.14's notes ("B therefore gets contradictory completed/cancelled terminal evidence … Classify cancellation/destruction against live exact-attempt ownership"). That audit reopened the bead, but it was re-closed at 18:00 2026-09-07 with a close reason that does not mention the defect, and the code at `034d0c8fc8` is unchanged. No open bead tracks it.

## Smallest fix

Classify survivors against LIVE ownership rather than fold state. Emit the cancellation trace and destroy fx only for a child whose snapshot is still present and whose `:rf/join-child` authenticates against this attempt (the same `authenticated-join-child` test `destroy.cljc:387-408` uses). A finished-but-unfolded child gets neither, and its later carrier stays `late-completion`. Fence: `lifecycle_fx/join.cljc` (it already holds `runtime-db`), plus one test. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

`.cljc` shared code, no reader conditional: `scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh` (`implementation/machines`) and `npm run test:cljs`.

## Decision needed

no
