title: resources-queries: an invalidation landing during an entry's first in-flight load is lost; the pre-mutation reply settles fresh and is fresh-skipped thereafter
description:
## Defect

An invalidation that lands while an entry's FIRST load is in flight is lost. The entry's tags come from the resource's `:tags` fn at success time, so until the first success the entry carries `:tags #{}`. `match-invalidation-keys` matches only on `(:tags entry)`, so it never matches the in-flight entry. Nothing is marked, no follow-up refetch is scheduled, and the mutation-settlement path reports the key as not invalidated.

The request was served before the write, so its reply carries pre-mutation data. That reply then settles as `:loaded` and fresh, with `:invalidated-at nil`. Every later `:rf.resource/ensure` fresh-skips it and serves the pre-mutation data. With the default registration (no `:stale-after-ms`) the entry never goes stale, so it stays wrong until GC or a manual refetch.

This contradicts spec/016-Resources.md:1211 (Race and in-flight semantics, normative): "Invalidation while a request is in flight marks the entry stale and records the invalidation. If the in-flight request is for the current generation, its success may satisfy the invalidation only when policy says the request covered the invalidated identity; otherwise schedule a follow-up refetch."

A second path has the same root. A loaded, owner-free entry with a refresh in flight DOES get `:invalidated-at` set, but the pre-invalidation success then clears it unconditionally, so the invalidation is lost again. An owned entry is safe, because invalidation arms a force-new refetch that supersedes the in-flight attempt. The previous review, rf2-pk4i6.1, listed this owner-free sub-case under "Considered, left alone". That reviewer read the spec as leaving "did the request cover the invalidated identity" to policy. But no coverage policy exists in the code, so the success always counts as covering, and the sentence's default branch is "otherwise schedule a follow-up refetch". It was never ruled on, and it is the same defect.

## Where

At 034d0c8fc8:
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/events.cljc:1558-1602`: `match-invalidation-keys`. Its `tags-hit?` intersects `(set (:tags entry))` with the requested tags.
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/events.cljc:1604-1881`: `invalidate-tags-handler`, the only consumer of that match set for the stale mark and the refetch arm.
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/state.cljc:999-1037`: `entry-succeeded`. It sets `:invalidated-at nil` unconditionally (line 1028) and only then installs the tags from data (line 1033).

Public entry points:
- `[:rf.resource/invalidate-tags {:scope ... :tags ...}]`
- a mutation's `:invalidates` descriptor, whose settlement dispatches that event and computes its reported match set with the same predicate
- `[:rf.resource/ensure ...]`, which starts the first load

## Failure scenario

1. A route enters `/articles` and ensures `:app/articles` (tags `#{[:article-list]}`). The GET is in flight.
2. Before it returns, the user completes a "create article" mutation declaring `:invalidates [{:tags #{[:article-list]}}]`. The server committed the write after it had already answered the list GET.
3. The invalidation matches nothing, because the entry's tags are still empty.
4. The list GET's reply (without the new article) settles as `:loaded`, fresh, with `:invalidated-at nil`.
5. The new article never appears. Re-entering the route fresh-skips. Only a manual refetch, GC, or a later unrelated invalidation shows it.

## Evidence

EXECUTED with a bounded JVM probe (plain-atom substrate, capturing `:rf.http/managed` fx) against the frozen tree `review-sep23` at 034d0c8fc8, run from a scratch directory with `CLJ_CACHE` in scratch. The tree's `git status --porcelain` read 0 lines afterwards.

- Control, loaded owned tagged entry `:pa/list2`: invalidating `[:item-list2]` took the request count from 1 to 2, set `:invalidated-at`, and moved the entry to `:fetching`. The instrument sees a working invalidation.
- Subject `:pa/list`, first load in flight: status `:loading`, `:tags #{}`.
- Invalidating `[:item-list]`: the request count stayed at 3, and `:invalidated-at` stayed nil.
- The pre-invalidation reply `[:pre-mutation-data]` landed: status `:loaded`, `:invalidated-at nil`, and `entry-stale?` false.
- A route re-ensure issued no request and served `[:pre-mutation-data]`.

Tracker searched over a full `bd export` (all statuses; title, description, notes and close_reason) for `invalidation while`, `in-flight invalidat`, `first-load invalidat` and `covered the invalidated`: no existing bead. Control: the pattern `invalidat.{0,40}in.flight` returned 3 unrelated hits, so the search can see body text.

## Smallest fix

Record the invalidation against in-flight work, and let the settle honour it. Either:
- (a) keep a per-scope tag-invalidation time, bounded or pruned on settle, and have the success handler compare it with the work record's `:started-at` for the tags it has just computed from data; or
- (b) when `invalidate-tags` runs, stamp in-scope in-flight entries whose tags are not yet known with the invalidation time, and have the settle keep it.

In both cases, the success handler must not clear an `:invalidated-at` that is later than the attempt's `:started-at`. For an owned entry it should also dispatch the follow-up refetch that spec 016:1211 requires.

Fence: `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/events.cljc`, `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/state.cljc`, plus one new test under `implementation/resources/test/`. No hot-zone files. The spec sentence is already correct.

## Gates

- `clojure -M:test` from `implementation/resources`. The change is in plain `.cljc` code, not a `#?(:cljs ...)` branch, so the JVM lane compiles it.
- The resources `.cljc` tests also run in CI's CLJS node lane (`npm run test:cljs`).

## Decision needed

Yes: which detection mechanism, (a) or (b), and whether an owned in-flight first load gets an automatic follow-up refetch or only the stale mark.
notes:
== DOSSIER WRITTEN 2026-09-23 22:56:16 AUSEST (analysis only — no status change, no dispatch, no edit) ==

Dossier: ai/decisions/rf2-3x7nj.10.1.inflight-invalidation-lost.md (ai/ is local-only and gitignored, so this path is a convenience that can rot; the decisive findings are inline below). Read at trunk bed2f4f65e (= origin/main); `git diff 034d0c8fc8 bed2f4f65e -- implementation/resources implementation/core spec` = 0 lines, so the bead's cites hold.

RECOMMENDATION: option (b), refined. Stamp an in-flight, tag-unknown in-scope entry with the invalidation's time AND its tag set. The settle keeps the entry stale when the tags produced from the reply's data intersect the stamped tags, and discards the stamp otherwise. An OWNED entry then gets one automatic follow-up :rf.resource/refetch; an owner-free one gets the stale mark only. Separately, no settle (entry-succeeded, entry-append-page, entry-replace-page) may clear an :invalidated-at that landed during its own attempt. Decide "during" by attempt identity (current-work or generation), not by ms timestamps: a same-ms tie or a pinned test clock would read as "covered". The owned-entry half is already answered by spec/016-Resources.md:1211 ("otherwise schedule a follow-up refetch") and 016 §Invalidation step 3; no coverage policy exists in the code.

DECISIVE FINDINGS:
1. TWO paths, one root, both EXECUTED (JVM, frozen tree = trunk for resources). Path 1: an owned first load in flight is invalidated → 0 new requests, :invalidated-at nil; the pre-invalidation reply settles :loaded with stale? false. Path 2: a loaded OWNER-FREE entry with a refresh in flight gets :invalidated-at set, then the pre-invalidation reply clears it; a route re-ensure issues 0 requests and serves the pre-mutation data. Control: a loaded owned tagged entry → 1 new request, mark set.
2. Causes at source: events.cljc:1582 `tags-hit?` intersects only (:tags entry), which is #{} until the first success computes tags from data (events.cljc:2526). state.cljc:1028 (entry-succeeded), :1223 (entry-append-page) and :1298 (entry-replace-page) all write :invalidated-at nil unconditionally.
3. No earlier ruling. rf2-ifzg4 (PR #9890) moved the clear from load start to success, which leaves path 2 open. rf2-pk4i6.1 listed path 2 as a reviewer's "Considered, left alone" note, not among its six ruled findings. The tag-blind (b) as written would cost one extra GET per first load that races ANY in-scope mutation. Option (a), a per-scope log, needs pruning plus an SSR/epoch serialisation decision.

Fence for the fix: resources events.cljc + state.cljc + one test ns; no hot zone; no spec edit. Sequence with rf2-3x7nj.10.3 (same events.cljc). Lane: clojure -M:test from implementation/resources (plain .cljc), plus npm run test:cljs in CI.
== RULING (delegated by Mike; mayor-dispatched ruling agent, 2026-09-23 23:35:15 AUSEST) ==

RULING: option (b), refined twice. (1) An invalidation records its tag set against EVERY in-scope in-flight attempt it does not already match (not only tag-unknown first loads), and that attempt's success resolves the record against the tags its reply produces. (2) No success settle may clear an :invalidated-at written DURING the attempt being settled, judged by attempt identity (work id), never by comparing milliseconds. A success that leaves the entry stale dispatches ONE follow-up :rf.resource/refetch when the entry has active owners AT SETTLE; an owner-free entry keeps the stale mark only. Rejected: (a) per-scope log, tag-blind (b), eager tags at ensure, and "stale mark only" for owned entries.

--- WHY ---
- Axis 2 is already answered by the spec. spec/016-Resources.md §Race and in-flight semantics (normative): "Invalidation while a request is in flight marks the entry stale and records the invalidation. If the in-flight request is for the current generation, its success may satisfy the invalidation only when policy says the request covered the invalidated identity; otherwise schedule a follow-up refetch." No coverage policy exists in the code, so the follow-up is the rule. §Invalidation step 3 "refetch entries with active owners" and step 4 "leave inactive entries stale" agree. "Stale mark only" for an owned entry contradicts both sentences.
- (a) per-scope tag-invalidation log loses: a second home for invalidation state in runtime-db, beside the entries. It would need a pruning rule and an SSR/epoch serialisation decision. That is the same "side table kept in step" class that rf2-3x7nj.10.2 removes.
- (b) as the bead writes it (stamp every tag-unknown in-flight entry in scope) loses: it is tag-blind. Any in-scope invalidation during a first load would stale that load, costing one extra GET per first load that races any unrelated mutation in the scope.
- (c) evaluating :tags eagerly at ensure with nil data loses. Tags are a function of data (016 §Invalidation: "the tag index for that scoped resource key is replaced with the tags produced by the new data"), so a tag fn that destructures its data yields the wrong set. Nor can it see tags that the reply newly produces. The optimistic seed already calls (tags-fn rparams nil) at mutation_events.cljc:554 for a freshly seeded entry. That precedent does not rescue (c), for the second reason.
- The dossier stamped only in-flight entries with no known tags; Codex argued for every in-flight attempt the invalidation does not match. The source and a measurement decided it, not a compromise. Data-dependent tags are an established, tested feature: `successful-load-replaces-tag-index` in resources_invalidation_gc_cljs_test.cljc registers tags #{[:article slug] [:rev (:rev data)]} and asserts that a refetch REPLACES them. An entry's current tags therefore describe its OLD data, not the reply in flight. Codex executed the case: an owned refresh started with tags #{[:item 1]}, [:item 2] was invalidated mid-flight, and the reply produced #{[:item 2]}. It settled fresh with 0 follow-up requests. Dropping the "tags unknown" condition makes the rule shorter, not longer.
- The two recommendations AGREED on the rest, which stands. Attempt identity, not ms: a same-millisecond tie or a pinned test clock would read as "covered". A tentative match must NOT write :invalidated-at at invalidation time, so an unrelated mutation never makes an unrelated resource observably stale. A definite mark must survive its attempt's success. Owned entries get one follow-up through the existing refetch machinery; owner-free entries stay stale. No new public API, coverage policy or diagnostic field. RTK Query delays invalidation globally until pending queries settle and documents the risk of indefinite delay under continuous activity (Codex's external check). That argues for entry-local bookkeeping over a global barrier.

--- EVIDENCE (executed twice, independently, on resources code byte-identical to trunk) ---
- Drift: `git diff --stat 034d0c8fc8 950a0cba74 -- implementation/resources spec/016-Resources.md spec/Spec-Schemas.md docs/EP/EP-0019-optimistic-mutation-rollback.md docs/EP/EP-0021-infinite-resources.md examples/real-apps/realworld_resources tools/xray/spec/024-Resources-Panel.md docs/resources` read 0 lines, against 19 commits in that range. Every review-tree cite holds at trunk 950a0cba74.
- Dossier JVM probe (plain-atom substrate, :rf.http/managed captured, no-op timers; tags (fn [_ _] #{tag})):
  - Control C.1, a loaded owned tagged entry, invalidated: 1 new request, :fetching, :invalidated-at set.
  - PATH 1, owned first load in flight (:tags #{}), invalidated: 0 new requests, :invalidated-at nil. The pre-invalidation reply then settled :loaded, stale? false.
  - PATH 2, loaded OWNER-FREE entry with a refresh in flight, invalidated: 0 requests (correct), :invalidated-at set. The pre-invalidation reply then CLEARED the mark (stale? false). A route re-ensure issued 0 requests and served the pre-mutation data.
- Codex's independent JVM probe (exit 0) read the same 1 / 0 / 0, plus the data-dependent-tag case above.
- Source at trunk:
  - events.cljc:1582 `tags-hit?` intersects only (:tags entry). events.cljc:2526 produces tags from the reply's data at success.
  - state.cljc:1028 (entry-succeeded), :1223 (entry-append-page) and :1298 (entry-replace-page) all write :invalidated-at nil unconditionally.
  - entry-start-load (state.cljc:954) deliberately does not touch it (rf2-ifzg4).
  - The dossier's `rg -i "covered|coverage|cover the"` over implementation/resources/src found only unrelated prose, against a control of 73 "invalidat" hits in events.cljc, so there is no coverage policy.
- History: rf2-ifzg4 (PR #9890) moved the clear from load start to success, and this bead is its unfinished half. rf2-pk4i6.1 listed path 2 as "considered, left alone", which was a reviewer's note rather than one of its ruled findings.

--- WHAT TO BUILD (trunk 950a0cba74) ---
1. DEFINITE marks survive their own attempt. rf.resources.state/entry-invalidate (state.cljc:867) is already the single home of the durable stale mark: invalidate-tags-handler writes through it (events.cljc:1833-1837), and so do the EP-0019 conflict rollback (mutation_events.cljc settle-optimistic-rollback) and the restore dangle.
   - Make entry-invalidate also record the attempt it landed during, e.g. :invalidated-during (:current-work entry), which is nil when no read is in flight.
   - The three success settles (entry-succeeded, entry-append-page, entry-replace-page) keep :invalidated-at when that stamp equals the entry's :current-work at settle. live-slot-for-reply guarantees that is the settling attempt. Otherwise they clear the mark and the stamp.
   - This one choke point also covers a rollback-driven mark landing during a read, which covers both the EP-0019 :on-conflict :invalidate case and rf2-3x7nj.11.2's new restore-then-stale. rf2-3x7nj.11.2 depends on it.
2. TENTATIVE records resolve at success.
   - In invalidate-tags-handler, select each entry that is in scope, NOT exempt, has a live :current-work, and was NOT matched. For the scope and exemption tests, reuse the exact predicates of match-invalidation-keys (in-scope?, the Rider-1 exempt-ids), minus the tag test.
   - Record the invalidated tag set against each selected attempt. Union repeated invalidations, and keep the latest invalidation event's :rf/time-ms. Do NOT write :invalidated-at or bump :revision for it.
   - At that attempt's success, intersect the recorded tags with the tags just produced. That happens in the scalar success handler (events.cljc ~2523-2529) and in page-succeeded-handler (~2964-2971, whose tags are computed over the accumulated (:data swept)). A non-empty intersection settles the entry stale, with :invalidated-at set to the recorded time.
   - A failure, abort or supersession of the attempt drops the record with it. A definite mark already survives those (rf2-ifzg4).
   - CARRIER: recommended on the attempt's work-ledger record (rf.resources.work-ledger/update-record; both success handlers already read `record` via get-record). The record IS the attempt, dies with it, and is immune to an optimistic snapshot/restore landing on the entry mid-attempt. restore-before seats the snapshot's non-live-work keys, so a tentative record written onto the ENTRY after a snapshot would be silently dropped by a no-conflict rollback. The entry keyed by work id is acceptable if the implementer handles that case; say which in the PR.
3. FOLLOW-UP. When a success settle leaves the entry stale by either route AND the settled entry has active owners, add one fx: [:dispatch [:rf.resource/refetch {:resource :scope :params :cause [:invalidate {:tags <recorded tags>}]}]]. For a definite mark, use the entry's pre-settle tags in the cause. Owner-free entries get nothing. One race is known and benign: an owned entry's definite match already armed a refetch, but the old reply was queued ahead of it. Then both refetches run and the first is superseded, costing one extra GET that is thrown away. Do not add machinery for it.
4. LEAVE ALONE:
   - the mutation settlement's :affected-keys report (at that moment the in-flight entry genuinely is not matched);

- C2: an invalidation in another scope has no effect.

title: pair-mcp: tail-build evaluates the caller's :probe CLJS with no --no-eval check, under read-only/idempotent annotations
description:
## Defect

`tail-build` evaluates its `:probe` argument, which is arbitrary caller-supplied ClojureScript source, in the browser runtime through `nrepl/cljs-eval-value`, with no check of the `--no-eval` gate. So on a server launched with `--no-eval`, where `eval-cljs` correctly refuses with `:rf.error/eval-cljs-disabled`, `tail-build` still runs any form it is given. It runs that form repeatedly: once, then on every poll until `wait-ms`. The descriptor also carries `idempotent-read-only-annotations` (`readOnlyHint true`, `idempotentHint true`). That is the annotation set whose own docstring says "safe to auto-approve", so an MCP host that auto-approves read-only tools will approve arbitrary code execution without asking.

The contract being broken: spec/Tool-Pair.md:915 defines the arbitrary-eval authority class as "Tools that accept arbitrary host-language source and execute it in the runtime process (e.g., `eval-cljs`, or the host's equivalent eval surface)" and gives it the `--no-eval` opt-out. spec/Tool-Pair.md:923 says a "true read-only debug session" is `--no-eval` with `--allow-writes` absent. The tool's own spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md:672 says "`--no-eval` additionally removes eval-driven writes". `tail-build`'s `:probe` belongs to that class, and nothing gates it.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`, under `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/`:

- `tools/tail_build.cljs:177` evaluates the first sample with `(nrepl/cljs-eval-value conn build-id probe)`, and `:219` evaluates every poll the same way. Nothing in `tail-build-tool` (`:125`) reads `eval-cljs/eval-allowed?`.
- The only gate is in `tools/eval_cljs.cljs:258` (`(not @eval-allowed?)`), and it is local to `eval-cljs-tool`.
- In `server.cljs:479-515`, `handle-call` refuses only unknown tools and the `--allow-writes` pair (`tools/writes.cljs`, `gated-write-tools #{"restore-epoch" "replace-app-db"}`). It has no eval gate.
- `tools/descriptors_data.cljs:853` sets `:annotations idempotent-read-only-annotations`, defined at `:115-123`, whose docstring at `:108-111` says "safe to auto-approve".

Entry point: MCP `tools/call` `tail-build`.

## Failure scenario

1. The operator launches with `--no-eval` for a CI or shared-environment session. The boot log prints "eval-cljs: DISABLED (--no-eval)" (`server.cljs:1015`).
2. The agent calls `eval-cljs {:form "(re-frame.core/dispatch-sync [:account/delete] {:frame :rf/default})"}`, which is correctly refused.
3. The agent calls `tail-build {:probe "(do (re-frame.core/dispatch-sync [:account/delete] {:frame :rf/default}) 1)" :baseline "1" :wait-ms 5000}`.
4. The form runs in the browser once, and again on every poll that still matches the baseline, until 5000 ms pass. Every run fires the event. The host treated the call as read-only.

The same call exfiltrates raw state past the privacy gate. `tail-build {:probe "(re-frame2-pair.runtime/snapshot :rf/default)" :baseline "x"}` returns the unprojected app-db under `:probe-values :initial`, including declared-`:sensitive?` slots, with `--allow-sensitive-reads` OFF. That is exactly the read the operator's `--no-eval` was meant to take away.

## Evidence

Inspected only; `tail_build.cljs` is `.cljs` and shadow-cljs is off-limits in this wave. I traced the full path: `handle-call`, then `tools/invoke` (`tools.cljs:327`), then `tail-build-tool`, then `nrepl/cljs-eval-value` (`nrepl.cljs:780`, which calls `cljs-eval` at `:753-763` and wraps the source in `shadow.cljs.devtools.api/cljs-eval`). No function on that path consults the eval gate. As a control, the eval gate does exist and fires for `eval-cljs` (`eval_cljs.cljs:258-262`, pinned by the conformance fixture `:eval-cljs/disabled-via-no-eval`, `test/re_frame2_pair_mcp/conformance_test.cljs:384`), so the gate works and `tail-build` simply never consults it. A Grep of the pair-mcp tree for `eval-allowed` finds hits only in `eval_cljs.cljs` and `server.cljs`, and none in `tail_build.cljs`. The tool's spec (003:1899-1943) documents the probe as "a CLJS form" and says its baseline is captured "with `eval-cljs`". Under `--no-eval` that capture step is refused, which shows the tool was designed on the assumption that eval is available.

Tracker: there are no prior beads on tail-build and `--no-eval`. The only tail-build bead, rf2-1f60u (closed), is the baseline race.

## Smallest fix

Refuse a supplied `:probe` with the existing `:rf.error/eval-cljs-disabled` envelope when `(eval-cljs/eval-allowed?)` is false. The no-probe soft-delay form can stay available. title: examples-real-apps: realworld_resources pagination renders every li.page-item OUTSIDE an empty ul.pagination — (into [:nav [:ul ...]] ...) appends to the nav
description:
## Defect

`realworld_resources`' `pagination` view builds its markup with `(into [:nav [:ul.pagination {...}]] (for ...))`. `into` appends to the OUTER vector, so every `[:li.page-item ...]` becomes a child of `<nav>`, a sibling AFTER an EMPTY `<ul class="pagination">`. What ships is:

- stray `<li>` elements outside any list, which is invalid HTML;
- a `.pagination` container that holds nothing, so the Conduit/Bootstrap `.pagination` flex row never lays out the page links: they fall out as a vertical run of bare list items;
- a `data-testid="pagination"` hook that locates the empty `<ul>` and not the links.

That breaks the official "Conduit" pagination markup the app claims to follow (README section on RealWorld contract conformance: "the selectors"). The managed-HTTP twin renders the same control correctly.

## Where

- `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/views.cljs:314-328`, the `pagination` reg-view. The offending form is at `:322`.
- Used by `list-view` at `:373` (home, tag, profile tabs, feed).
- Correct twin: `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/articles.cljs:483-494`, which is `[:nav [:ul.pagination (for ...)]]`: the seq nested INSIDE the `ul`.

## Failure scenario

EXECUTED for the data shape. Babashka evaluated the identical `into` expression with `total-pages 3` and `current-page 2`:

```
[:nav [:ul.pagination {:data-testid "pagination"}] [:li.page-item {:class nil} [:a.page-link {:href "#"} 1]] [:li.page-item {:class "active"} [:a.page-link {:href "#"} 2]] [:li.page-item {:class nil} [:a.page-link {:href "#"} 3]]]
```

The control is the corrected form, `(into [:ul.pagination {...}] (for ...))`. It yields `[:ul.pagination {:data-testid "pagination"} [:li ...] [:li ...] [:li ...]]`, with the items inside the list.

INSPECTED ONLY for the rendered DOM and CSS consequence. That needs a browser, which this review may not run.

Reachable on any list with more than one page. The demo backend seeds enough articles for the home Global Feed to paginate: README step 5 and the `page->limit-offset` section describe paging.

## Evidence

- Source read at the lines above. The probe is `probe_pagination.clj` in the reviewer's scratch directory.
- Introduced by `da70c190e8` (2026-06-11, "realworld_resources favorited tab + paginated resources"). It is unchanged since, apart from `f3acd10051`'s namespace refactor.
- No test pins the pagination markup. A search of the implementation, tools and testbeds trees for `"pagination"` / `page-2` in realworld tests finds nothing relevant.
- Tracker: a full-text search for `ul.pagination|page-item` over a `bd export` (2316 issues) reads 0. Neither rf2-fn0kx.9 nor its follow-ups mention it.

## Smallest fix

`views.cljs:322`: `(into [:nav [:ul.pagination {:data-testid "pagination"}]] (for ...))` becomes `[:nav (into [:ul.pagination {:data-testid "pagination"}] (for ...))]`. Alternatively, copy the http twin's `[:nav [:ul.pagination (for ...)]]` shape.

Examples stay test-free (rf2-8cevm). No hot-zone file is touched.

## Gates

- CI's `cljs-examples-compile` sweep (the `examples_compile` surface) for compilation.
- `npm run test:cljs` for the resources app suite that loads `realworld-resources.core`.

Neither asserts the pagination markup, so the worker verifies the corrected hiccup shape by evaluating it, as above, and says so in the PR body.

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
## WORKER VERDICT: FIXED in PR #10316 (commit 5745ddb8dd on worker/realworld-3x7nj), 2026-09-24 08:23 AUSEST

The premise was re-verified at trunk `51fe95a7fb`. The `pagination` reg-view in `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/views.cljs` still read `(into [:nav [:ul.pagination {...}]] (for ...))`.

Fix: `[:nav (into [:ul.pagination {:data-testid "pagination"}] (for ...))]`. The items now go into the list.

Control: a JVM probe (bb), deleted afterwards. It lifted the SHIPPED `pagination` reg-view body out of the source, evaluated it with 25 articles (3 pages) and current page 2, and read where the `li.page-item`s landed.
- Before the fix: 3 `li` were direct children of `nav`, and 0 were inside `ul.pagination`.
- After the fix: 0 were direct children of `nav`, 3 were inside `ul.pagination`, and exactly 1 was `.active`. A one-page list still renders nil.
- Sabotage: the one line was planted to `(into [:nav [:ul.pagination ...]]` (match count 1), and 0 `li` were inside `ul.pagination`. The restore was verified by the default-form blob hash equal to the committed blob `6e590d13d2`.

The rendered DOM/CSS consequence needs a browser and was not run, as in the review. No test pins the markup, and the examples compile sweep in CI grades compilation.
Merged-PR audit #10316 (423809164fa372d16aa3144a59baf41ba58f615b; merged 2026-09-23T23:33:22Z). Completeness: The four scoped example fixes land: correct token path, pagination nesting, route-gated settings navigation in both twins and resources draft reset. The acknowledged HTTP-twin principal crossing has an exact in_progress Bead, which cannot be reused under the open-only instruction; a separate open audit finding points to that existing work. Correctness: Read all five changed example files and framework test adjustments. Accepted shipped-form probes/negative controls, CI node 12668/63846 and 58 example builds. Route-id rather than nav-token gating and same-slug draft retention match the chosen scope. Implementation quality: Small changes follow the existing twin patterns and keep examples free of test infrastructure. The HTTP follow-up needs only session-boundary cleanup, not a new draft storage abstraction. Actionable findings: rf2-qtbeb. Existing finding updates: none.

title: story-execution: runner-events run!/re-run!/run-play! (the toolbar Re-run, banner Re-run and Run play) set no fresh-run boundary, so Re-run fails a correct variant and dispatched? reads the previous run
description:
## Defect

`runner-events/run!` is the play engine's public driver. It sits behind `re-run!` (documented as the one-call API for the toolbar's `[Re-run]`), `run-play!` and `run-plays-sequentially!`. It drives the script against the variant frame AS IT STANDS and establishes no fresh-run boundary, which only the runtime path (`run-variant` / `prepare-run!` + `resume-run!`) provides:

- app-db is not reset;
- the stub-call log is not cleared;
- the run epoch baseline is not re-stamped. That baseline is what rf2-3okc introduced so that the tape-projected assertions `:rf.assert/dispatched?`, `:effect-emitted` and `:no-warnings` read only the current run, and it is stamped only in `runtime/run-phase-0!`.

Every Re-run the UI offers is therefore graded against the PREVIOUS run's leftovers, in two directions:

- a correct stateful variant reads FAIL on Re-run, because its dispatches apply on top of the prior run's end state;
- a tape assertion reads the prior run's epochs, so a Re-run whose script stopped dispatching an event still passes `dispatched?`. This is exactly the false green rf2-3okc fixed, reached through the engine's other entry point.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:

- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/play/runner_events.cljc`:
  - `run!` (1889-1981): resets the run-state and settle boundaries only.
  - `re-run!` (1983-1995): documented as "so the toolbar's `[Re-run]` button has a one-call API".
  - `run-play!` (1997-2005) and `run-plays-sequentially!`.
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/assertions.cljc:145-182`: `run-epoch-baselines`, `set-run-epoch-baseline!`, `frame-tape`.
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/runtime.cljc`:
  - 819-828, `stamp-epoch-baseline!`: the only writer of the baseline, called from phase 0;
  - 800-817, `ensure-fresh-frame!`: the only app-db and stub-log reset.
- Callers:
  - `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/play_status.cljs`: the chip's `[Re-run]` at :344, the PLAY FAIL banner's `[Re-run]` at :384, and the dropdown's per-play run at :268;
  - `ui/recorder_export_dialog.cljs:160`, through `recorder/play_export_events.cljc:62-80`.
- The canvas's own runs do go through `prepare-run!` / `resume-run!` (`ui/canvas.cljs:462-520`), but only when the run-key changes, which a Re-run click does not do.

## Failure scenario

```clojure
(rf/reg-event :p/inc (fn [{:keys [db]} _] {:db (update db :n (fnil inc 0))}))
(rf/reg-event :p/first-time
  (fn [{:keys [db]} _] (if (:greeted? db) {:db db}
                          {:db (assoc db :greeted? true) :fx [[:dispatch [:p/greet]]]})))
(rf/reg-event :p/greet (fn [{:keys [db]} _] {:db (update db :greets (fnil inc 0))}))
(reg-variant :story.p/counter {:script {:script [[:dispatch [:p/inc]]
                                                [:assert [:rf.assert/path-equals [:n] 1]]]}})
(reg-variant :story.p/greet   {:script {:script [[:dispatch [:p/first-time]]
                                                [:assert [:rf.assert/dispatched? [:p/greet]]]]}})
```

Both variants PASS on selection, the fresh runtime run. Pressing `[Re-run]` then gives:

- `:story.p/counter` reads FAIL, with `:n` at 2. This is a false red on a correct variant.
- `:story.p/greet` reads PASS although `:p/greet` was NOT dispatched in that run (`:greets` stays 1). `dispatched?` answered from the first run's epoch, a false green.

## Evidence

- EXECUTED. A process-local JVM probe against the frozen tree (`:local/root` deps, `re-frame.epoch` loaded, plain-atom adapter) first ran each variant through `run-variant`, then through `runner-events/re-run!` with a `done-cb`:
  - counter: fresh `:status :pass` with app-db `{:n 1}`; re-run run-state `:status :fail :failures 1` with app-db `{:n 2}`;
  - greet: fresh `:status :pass` with `{:greets 1}`; re-run run-state `:status :pass :failures 0` with `{:greets 1}`, so `:p/greet` was not dispatched and the assertion still passed.
- CONTROL. The same greet assertion is exactly the rf2-3okc shape, whose regression proves that the RUNTIME path now reads only the current run (`story_assertions_test.clj` `dispatched-assertion-reads-only-the-current-run`).
- INSPECTED. The browser wiring: the play-status chip and the banner call `re-run!` / `run-play!` directly (`play_status.cljs:268,344,384`), and the canvas does not re-prepare on those clicks.
- Tracker: `re-run!` is not exercised by any test. rf2-3x7nj.29.4 (story-ui-evidence) reports the export dialog's "replay in this story" instance of the app-db half, and its suggested fix, "reset app-db", would still leave this bead's baseline half (the false green) open.

## Smallest fix

Give the engine's standalone drivers the fresh-run boundary the runtime path has. The cleanest route is to have the UI's Re-run / Run play / Replay call the runtime (`prepare-run!` with a fresh run-key, then `resume-run!`, or `run-variant`) instead of `runner-events/run!`. `runner-events` cannot require `runtime`, so the alternative is to have `run!` re-stamp `set-run-epoch-baseline!` itself when called standalone and document that it drives the live frame.

Fence:
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/play_status.cljs` (story-ui-evidence scope);
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/play/runner_events.cljc`;
- possibly `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/recorder/play_export_events.cljc`.

Coordinate with rf2-3x7nj.29.4 so the export Replay takes the same route. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

- The engine half: `cd tools/story && clojure -M:test` (runner_events.cljc is cljc), with the probe's two cases as a JVM regression.
- The `play_status.cljs` change is compiled only by the CLJS lane: `npm run test:cljs` / `npm run test:browser`.

## Decision needed

Yes, in two lines. Should `[Re-run]` / "Run play" re-run the variant FRESH, as Test mode's Re-run does (spec 009 §Read-only contract: "re-allocates the variant frame")? Or is re-driving the live frame intended, in which case the chip must at least stop grading tape assertions against the previous run? Recommend fresh.
notes:
== DOSSIER WRITTEN 2026-09-24 01:06:08 AUSEST (analysis only — no status change, no dispatch, no edit) ==

Dossier: ai/decisions/rf2-3x7nj.30.3.play-rerun-fresh-or-live.md (ai/ is local-only and gitignored, so this path is a convenience that can rot; the decisive findings are restated here). Read at trunk a61f903c5c (= origin/main); git diff --quiet 034d0c8fc8 HEAD -- tools/story exits 0 (control implementation/core/src exits 1), so the bead's citations hold unchanged.

RECOMMENDATION: FRESH. The chip [Re-run], the PLAY FAIL banner [Re-run], a dropdown play row and the dropdown's Run all should reset the frame IN PLACE to the variant's declared start (phases 0-2 with the shell's current args/overrides/modes/substrate, i.e. runtime/prepare-variant) and then play; Run all resets once and then sequences, as the selection run's auto-play sequencer already does. Closer to a fix than a ruling: no Story spec page promises keep-live-state.

Decisive findings:
1. No spec defines the chip's Re-run; every page that defines a re-run says fresh: 009-Test-Mode.md:109-111 ("dispatches a fresh run-variant call against the variant, re-allocates the frame"), :212-214 (Read-only contract, "re-allocates the variant frame"), 002-Runtime.md:852-858 (fresh-run boundary, evidence scoped to this run's epoch baseline); runtime.cljc:813-814 ensure-fresh-frame! docstring: "an intentionally-persistent mode would be an explicit opt, not the default". Census over tools/story/spec for live-frame phrasings: 0 normative hits (control: re-allocates 4).
2. EXECUTED JVM probe at trunk (author pokes the canvas with two :p/inc, then presses Re-run): counter variant TODAY :fail at {:n 4}; live-with-baseline-restamped (option B) :fail at {:n 7}; fresh (prepare-variant then re-run!) :pass at {:n 1}, twice. A variant whose play never dispatches :p/greet reads :pass on TODAY's Re-run after the author's own click dispatched it (false green); fresh reads :fail (control holds).
3. Traps for the fixing worker: never route through reset-variant (its destroy! under a mounted canvas freezes the DOM, closed rf2-insd's positive control); pass the shell run opts (ui/sidebar.cljs:675 run-opts-for-variant) or Controls edits vanish; the in-place reset evicts the dropdown's active play (measured "second" -> nil), so capture the play key first. One pin changes: play/runner_events_cljs_test.cljc:1209 run-play-keys-state-per-play asserts the second play sees [:n] 2, which holds only by accumulation (measured :fail, :n 1, through the fresh route); :1267 run-all-plays-sequences-runs stays green under reset-once-then-sequence.

Interactions: one fresh-route fix also closes rf2-3x7nj.29.4 (export "replay in this story", play_export_events.cljc:80, same runner-events/run! call). It does NOT cover rf2-3x7nj.28.1 (Run all/watch already run fresh via run-variant; defect is sidebar.cljs:711-715 dropping :status) or rf2-3x7nj.28.3 (plan read without :run-args in docs.cljc/view_args.cljc). No hot-zone file.
== RULING (delegated by Mike; mayor-dispatched ruling agent, 2026-09-24 01:31:00 AUSEST) ==

RULING: FRESH. The chip [Re-run], the PLAY FAIL banner [Re-run], a dropdown play row and the dropdown's "Run all (N)" each reset the variant frame IN PLACE to its declared start (phases 0-2 with the shell's CURRENT Controls overrides, modes and substrate) and then run the chosen play, taken from the SAME compiled plan the preparation used. "Run all" resets ONCE, then sequences every play in declared order. The same operation serves the recorder export's "replay in this story" (rf2-3x7nj.29.4) and the CI hook `runPlay`. Freshness belongs to this author-facing operation, which EXTENDS the existing one run owner (`runtime/prepare-run!` + `runtime/resume-run!`) with an explicit play selection. The low-level engine (`runner-events/run!`, `run-play!`, `run-all-plays!`) is NOT changed to reset, and no second lifecycle is created.

Decision needed (the description's two-line question): answered, fresh. Option B (drive the live frame, re-stamp the baseline) and option C (leave it) are rejected. No hot-zone file is involved (tools/story/spec is not on the hot-zone list).

--- WHY ---

1. Today's buttons are wrong in BOTH directions, measured at trunk (table below). A correct variant goes red after any canvas interaction. A variant whose play never dispatches the event it asserts goes GREEN on the author's own click. The false green is rf2-3okc's defect again, reached through the engine's other entry point: rf2-3okc scoped the tape to a per-run epoch baseline, but only `runtime/run-phase-0!` stamps it.
2. The spec gives one meaning for a re-run, and it is fresh. No Story spec page defines the chip's Re-run at all: `010-Toolbar.md:53` shows only `[Play]` in the DATA cluster, and `003-Render-Shell.md:450` points there. Every page that does define a re-run says fresh:
   - `009-Test-Mode.md:109-111`: Test mode's Re-run "dispatches a fresh `run-variant` call ... re-allocates the frame".
   - `009-Test-Mode.md:196-199` and `:212-214` (§Read-only contract).
   - `002-Runtime.md:852-858` (§Fresh-run boundary: reset in place, and "Evidence is scoped to this run's epoch baseline").
   - The runtime's own docstring (`runtime.cljc:813-814`, `ensure-fresh-frame!`): "Determinism by default; an intentionally-persistent mode would be an explicit opt, not the default."
   - Census, re-run by this ruling over the 32 `.md` pages under tools/story/spec (findings/ excluded), each pattern both line-oriented and whitespace-flattened. Six live-frame phrasings (`without (a )?reset`, `on top of (the )?(current|live|previous)`, `from (the )?current state`, `(play|run) from here`, `re-?run.{0,40}(live|current) frame`, `keeps? (the )?(live|current|author)`) read 0 hits each. Controls taken from the same pages: `re-allocates` 4 and `fresh-run boundary` 1.
3. B loses on the measurements. Re-stamping the baseline fixes the false green and nothing else. It turns BOTH correct probe variants red after an interaction: counter at {:n 7}, and a first-time-guard variant because its guard is already spent. It also makes the most prominent run button disagree, by design, with selection, Test mode and Run all. It is exactly the "intentionally-persistent mode" the runtime says must be an explicit opt. If a "play from here" button is ever wanted, add it later as a separately labelled opt. C is a correctness defect and is ruled out.
4. What an author gives up: hand-built canvas state is gone when they press Re-run, and loaders and :setup run again. That is what "run again" means. The sanctioned ways to keep a state already exist: "Save current state as variant" (019-Story-UI-Controls-And-View-States.md §3) and the Dispatch Console. Controls, modes and substrate ARE preserved, because they are the run's inputs.

--- WHERE THE TWO RECOMMENDATIONS AGREED AND DIFFERED ---

Both (the dossier author's and Codex's) recommended fresh, and both recommended "a single play starts from :setup, and only Run all chains". They differed on two points. Each was resolved at source rather than split.

(a) THE ROUTE: Codex is right. The dossier proposed `prepare-variant` followed by `runner-events/run-play!` / `re-run!`. That resets the frame but runs the WRONG PROGRAM.
- The engine resolves a play from the RAW registered body: `runner_events.cljc:410-439`, `variant-plays` -> `handler-meta` -> `rf.story.play.runner/variant-body->plays`.
- Phase 4 executes the COMPILED plan's `[:world :scripts]` (`runtime.cljc:1072`). In that plan:
  - `[:arg k]` placeholders are substituted against the effective args, including the run's cell overrides and modes (`plan.cljc:1436`, `scripts*`);
  - a `:compose`d fragment's `:script` is prepended to the primary play (`plan.cljc:1365-1383`, rf2-k23efg);
  - every step is shape-validated (`normalize-scripts`).
- Codex measured the `[:arg]` half. This ruling re-measured it and found the `:compose` half as well (table rows args-* and compose-*). The rule for the implementer: the executed play(s) MUST come from the prepared ctx's `(get-in ctx [:plan :world :scripts])`. Never from `runner-events/variant-plays` / `resolve-play` / `variant-play-script`.

(b) THE `:1209` PIN: Codex is right, and it stays unchanged. `play/runner_events_cljs_test.cljc:1209`, `run-play-keys-state-per-play`, calls `runner-events/run-play!` directly on one frame and pins per-play state keying. Under this ruling the engine keeps its semantics, so that test stays green and correct as written. The dossier's measurement (the second play reads :fail at {:n 1}) is what happens if that test is re-routed through the new operation, which is not what the test is for. `:1267`, `run-all-plays-sequences-runs` (a/b/c -> 1/2/3), also stays green. The new semantics get their OWN pins, below.

--- MEASUREMENTS (this ruling, trunk ba2c41a767 = origin/main; tools/story byte-identical to the frozen review tree 034d0c8fc8: `git diff --quiet 034d0c8fc8 origin/main -- tools/story` exit 0, control `-- implementation/core/src` exit 1) ---

Method: a bounded, process-local JVM probe (`clojure -M -i`, :local/root deps on tools/story and implementation/epoch, plain-atom adapter, re-frame.epoch loaded), captured exit 0. title: impl-scripts: splint shim --fail-on-errors turns Splint's own failure exit into 0 (multi-value .splint.edn or bad argv lints nothing, gate green)
description:
## Defect

`re-frame.splint-main`, the shim behind the CI Splint gate, throws away Splint's own non-zero exit whenever `--fail-on-errors` is passed. In that mode it computes its exit code only from error-class DIAGNOSTICS (`splint_main.clj:82-90`). But Splint has three early-return failure paths that return `{:exit 1}` with NO `:diagnostics` key, having linted nothing:

1. a `.splint.edn` that holds more than one top-level value (`:type :config`, which Splint catches);
2. an unknown CLI option, or an option placed after the paths;
3. an empty path list.

On all three the shim sees `error-count` 0 and exits 0. The Splint job then goes green while checking zero files, and that includes files that do not parse, which are exactly what the gate exists to catch. The workflow says in so many words that a `.splint.edn`-only change must run this gate "so the Splint gate validates the new config" (`lint.yml:104-108`, `lint.yml:249-255`). For this class of broken config, the gate validates nothing and passes.

## Where

- `implementation/scripts/splint/re_frame/splint_main.clj:77-91`: `-main`. The docstring (`:26-39`) says that without the flag the shim passes Splint's exit through. With the flag, only `error-count` is consulted, and `exit` is dropped.
- `.github/workflows/lint.yml:553-560`: the `splint` job runs `clojure -M:splint --fail-on-errors ../implementation ../tools ../examples ../testbeds`.
- `.github/workflows/lint.yml:104-108` and `:249-255`: `.splint.edn` is armed as a lint surface specifically so a config change "including broken syntax" is validated.
- `.splint.edn:15`: the file's own header offers `style/eq-zero {:enabled false}` as the shape of a per-rule suppression. The existing single map is at `:39`.
- Upstream, inside `io.github.noahtheduke/splint 1.24.0` (the pinned version, `implementation/deps.edn:154`):
  - `noahtheduke/splint/runner.clj`, `run`: the `:type :config` catch returns `{:exit 1}`; the `exit-message` branch returns `{:exit (if ok 0 1) ...}`; empty paths returns `{:exit 1}`. None of the three carries `:diagnostics`.
  - `noahtheduke/splint/config.clj` `slurp-edn`: throws `ex-info ... {:type :config}` on more than one value.

Reached from CI on every PR that arms `lint_surface`, and by anyone running `clojure -M:splint --fail-on-errors ...` locally.

## Failure scenario

A PR adds a rule suppression by appending `style/eq-zero {:enabled false}` below the closing `}` of the existing `{global ...}` map, which is the spelling `.splint.edn:15` shows. The file now holds three top-level values. Splint prints `Error reading .../.splint.edn` / `edn file has more than 1 value` and returns `{:exit 1}` before loading a single source file. The shim exits 0, and the `Splint (fail on errors, warnings informational)` job is green.

The gate stays green on every later PR until someone notices, and meanwhile a planted parse error anywhere in `implementation/`, `tools/`, `examples/` or `testbeds/` is not reported.

The same thing happens with a future edit to the job's argv that adds a misspelt or misplaced Splint option, for example a flag after the paths.

## Evidence

EXECUTED. This was a bounded JVM probe run from scratch directories, never from the tree. It used the pinned splint 1.24.0 jar from `~/.m2` and put the frozen tree's `implementation/scripts/splint` on the classpath, so the shim under test is the one at `034d0c8fc8`. Each fixture dir has its own `.splint.edn`, a clean `clean_ns.clj`, and a `broken_ns.clj` missing its closing paren.

| probe | `.splint.edn` | args | exit | output |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | one map | `--fail-on-errors src/clean_ns.clj` | 0 | `checked 1 files, 1 style warnings` (baseline) |
| D | one map | `--fail-on-errors src` | **1** | `[splint/parsing-error] ... EOF while reading`: positive control, the gate bites on a parse error |
| E | two maps | `--fail-on-errors src` | **0** | `Error reading ...\.splint.edn` / `edn file has more than 1 value`: no file checked, and the same broken file D caught is now passed |
| C | two maps | `src` (no flag) | **1** | same message: Splint itself reports the failure, and only the shim's flag hides it |
| F | one map | `--fail-on-errors --no-such-flag src` | **0** | `splint errors:` / `Unknown option: "--no-such-flag"` |
| G | unbalanced `{` | `--fail-on-errors src` | 1 | uncaught `edamame` `ExceptionInfo`: an unreadable config fails closed, because Splint rethrows non-`:config` exceptions |

So the defect is bounded exactly as described. An unreadable config (G) and a parse error in a source file (D) both go red. A multi-value config (E) and an argv error (F) go green. C is the control showing the green is the shim's doing.

INSPECTED:
- the shim in full;
- Splint's `runner.clj` `run` / `build-result-map` / `run-impl`, `config.clj` `slurp-edn` / `find-local-config` / `load-config`, and `cli.clj` `validate-opts` / `print-errors`, extracted from the jar to scratch;
- the `lint.yml` splint job and its path and classifier arming.

Consumers of the shim: `rg '-M:splint|splint-main|splint_main'` over the tree finds only the shim, `implementation/deps.edn` and `lint.yml`, plus prose in `.beads/issues.jsonl`. No test exercises the shim.

Tracker checked before filing:
- `bd search "splint"` and `bd search "Splint"` (all statuses) return `[]`.
- The beads the workflow comments cite (rf2-4v147, rf2-ps9u9, rf2-nlnd9y.3) no longer resolve.
- The export carries 10 records mentioning `--fail-on-errors`. All are gate-run receipts reading "splint --fail-on-errors exit 0", and none rules on this behaviour. Those receipts are themselves only as good as this exit code.

## Smallest fix

In `-main`, keep Splint's own failure when the run never reached linting. A real lint run always returns a map carrying `:diagnostics` (`build-result-map`); every early return does not. So in fail-on-errors mode, exit non-zero when `error-count` is positive OR when the result has no `:diagnostics` key and Splint's `exit` is non-zero. That is roughly three lines.

Fence: `implementation/scripts/splint/re_frame/splint_main.clj` only. No hot-zone file. The `lint.yml` job needs no change.

## Gates

- The `lint.yml` `splint` job (`Splint (fail on errors, warnings informational)`) runs the fixed shim over the tree. That proves only that the normal path is unchanged, because a green there cannot tell the fix from the bug.
- The discriminating check is to re-run probes E and F above and see exit 1, with D still 1 and A still 0. It is a plain JVM run, with no shadow-cljs lane involved.

## Decision needed

No.

title: test-infra: two security 'no :sensitive? stamp' assertions read :tags, which the trace builder always strips, so they cannot fail
description:
## Defect

Two security-corpus assertions claim a NON-sensitive validation failure carries no `:sensitive?` stamp, but they read the flag off the trace's `:tags` map. The trace builder always strips `:sensitive?` from `:tags` and hoists it to the envelope's TOP LEVEL: `re-frame.trace/build-event` does `(dissoc tags :recovery :sensitive?)`, and `hoist-projected-sensitive` does `(update :tags dissoc :sensitive?)`. So `(contains? (:tags trace) :sensitive?)` is false on EVERY delivered trace, stamped or not, and the two assertions cannot fail. The behaviour they claim to guard is real. It is the "the seam is precise, not a blanket scrub" half of the redaction contract: a trace wrongly stamped sensitive is dropped whole by default MCP egress (`strip-sensitive` reads the top-level flag). A sibling test in the same corpus does it right, reading `(contains? v :sensitive?)` on the trace itself (`schema_redaction_security_cljs_test.cljc:275`).

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:
- `implementation/security/test/re_frame/security/validation_redaction_invariant_security_cljs_test.cljc:769`, in `non-sensitive-failure-not-over-redacted`: `(is (not (contains? (:tags event-trace) :sensitive?)) ...)`.
- `implementation/security/test/re_frame/security/error_slot_egress_security_cljs_test.cljc:318`, in `navigate-error-verbatim-for-plain-route`: `(is (not (contains? tags :sensitive?)) ...)`, where `tags` is `(:tags trace)` (`:313`).
- The stripping is at `implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace.cljc:690` (`build-event`) and `:828-833` (`hoist-projected-sensitive`). The public entry points are `rf.schemas/validate-event!` and `rf.routing.navigate/navigate-handler`, both of which emit through `rf.trace/emit-error!`.
- The same corpus already pins the stripping as a contract: `error_slot_egress_security_cljs_test.cljc:106-107` asserts ":sensitive? stripped from :tags after the hoist (no double-stamp)" on a trace that IS stamped.

## Failure scenario

A regression makes `redact-validation-tags`, or `compute-sensitive?`, stamp every validation failure sensitive. Non-sensitive `:event` and `:machine-data` failures, and plain-route navigate failures, now carry top-level `:sensitive? true` and are silently dropped from AI/MCP egress. Both tests stay green, because their values still ride unredacted and the stamp they look for is never in `:tags`.

## Evidence

EXECUTED as a bounded JVM probe from `implementation/security` on its own `:test` classpath (CLJ_CACHE redirected to scratch, frozen tree left clean):
- Baseline observation: a SENSITIVE-schema `validate-event!` failure gives top-level `:sensitive? true` and `(contains? (:tags t) :sensitive?)` `false`. A plain-schema failure gives `nil` and `false`. The key is absent from `:tags` whether or not the trace is stamped.
- The two target tests, baseline: `{:test 2, :pass 9, :fail 0, :error 0}`.
- With `re-frame.trace/compute-sensitive?` redefined to always return true (every trace force-stamped; observed top-level `:sensitive? true` on the plain failure): the targets are still `{:test 2, :pass 9, :fail 0, :error 0}`.
- Control, which bites under the same redef: `schema-redaction-security-cljs-test/non-sensitive-collection-failure-not-over-redacted` reads the top-level flag and went RED (`{:test 1, :pass 2, :fail 1}`, FAIL at `:275`). So the redef is live and the correct spelling of the assertion catches the over-stamp.
- Census of `:sensitive?)` assertions in the security and conformance corpora: 4 sites. Two read `:tags` (these two), one reads `:tags` on a stamped trace deliberately (`:106`, the hoist pin), and one reads top-level (`schema_redaction...:275`, the control).

## Smallest fix

Read the envelope rather than its tags: at `validation_redaction_invariant...:769` use `(is (not (contains? event-trace :sensitive?)))`, and at `error_slot_egress...:318` use `(is (not (contains? trace :sensitive?)))`. That is two lines in two files under `implementation/security/test/`. No hot-zone file is involved.

## Gates

Both files are `.cljc`, and the lines sit outside any reader conditional. Two lanes grade them: the JVM lane `clojure -M:test` from `implementation/security` (in `scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh`), and the CLJS lanes `npm run test:cljs` / `npm run test:security`.

## Decision needed

No.

title: story-authoring-data: determinism ->artifact drops a plan's force-fx-stub decorators and :db-seed, so assert-deterministic / capture-golden on a variant plan fire the stubbed real effect and replay an unseeded run
notes:
== DOSSIER WRITTEN 2026-09-24 01:33:21 AUSEST (analysis only — no status change, no dispatch, no edit) ==

Dossier: ai/decisions/rf2-3x7nj.31.2.determinism-gate-on-variant-plans.md in the mayor checkout. ai/ is local-only and gitignored, so that path is a convenience that can rot; the findings below stand on their own.

Read at trunk 805612eef6 (= local origin/main; HEAD 4fe0cbe915 is one beads-only checkpoint ahead). git diff --quiet 034d0c8fc8 HEAD -- tools/story exits 0 (not fixed since the review tree); control over implementation/core/src exits 1.

RECOMMENDATION: B. Refuse a plan whose world carries run-shaping slots the artifact cannot hold (:db-seed, non-hiccup decorators incl. force-fx-stub, loaders, [:frame :interceptor-overrides]): :cannot-run from assert-deterministic, a structured throw from the golden family, naming the slots and the two doors that already work. Do NOT grow ->artifact into a second run engine (option A).

Decisive findings, inline:
1. determinism.cljc:101-108 (->artifact plan branch) reads only [:world :setup], :script, [:world :frame :fx-overrides] and [:world :network]; run-variant additionally applies force-fx-stub stubs (frames.cljc:163-197), :db-seed with schema validation (runtime.cljc:926-963), frame-setup decorators (frames.cljc:296-348), loaders, interceptor overrides and classification. Spec 017:3510-3513 specifies exactly that lossy fold and is silent on the rest; spec 005 says NOTHING about determinism/golden/property (it only says force-fx-stub is "per-frame and per-variant", 005:101-105). Spec 017:356-362 and :3966 say fx mocking for tests is the first-class :fx-overrides slot, which the artifact does carry.
2. EXECUTED bounded JVM probe at ba2c41a767: force-fx-stub variant run-variant [:pass, 0 real calls]; assert-deterministic over its plan [:non-deterministic [:fail :fail], 2 real calls]; capture-golden over its plan froze :fail with 1 real call; :db-seed variant 11 vs replay 1; frame-setup decorator variant 6 vs replay 1. Controls: a plan using first-class :fx-overrides plus a :setup seed reads :deterministic with 0 real calls and app-db 11.
3. The doors B points at already work, EXECUTED: two run-variant runs of the stubbed variant give equal :run-hash with 0 real calls; capture-golden of a run-variant run-result then golden-match? against a second run reads true. No caller outside tests passes a variant plan to assert-deterministic/capture-golden (examples, testbeds, docs, skills: 0). Option A would repeat the rf2-tymyh (:network added to the artifact) / rf2-shx4 (same bug in the runtime inline path) pattern for every world slot.
== RULING (delegated by Mike; mayor-dispatched ruling agent, 2026-09-24 05:03:27 AUSEST) ==

RULING: B, with the boundary drawn at the GATE and the GOLDEN FAMILY, and covering EVERY normalized plan, not a subset. `assert-deterministic` handed a normalized variant plan (a map carrying `:world`) returns `{:status :cannot-run :reason :determinism-plan-target ...}` before any replay; `capture-golden` / `golden-match?` / `compare-golden` handed one throw the existing `:rf.error/golden-bad-target` with a plan-specific reason. Both messages name the one recovery: run the VARIANT and judge its run-result. `determinism/->artifact` KEEPS its plan branch, because it is the specified promotion API route, and gets an honest docstring instead.

Decision needed (the description's A-or-B question): answered, B. A (fold the whole world into the artifact) and C (route plans through `story/run` inside the gate) are rejected. No hot-zone file is involved.

--- WHY ---

1. The artifact path judges a run the variant never makes, and at trunk it does so with a GREEN verdict. Measured by this ruling (bounded JVM probe, tools/story `:test` classpath, plain-atom adapter, trunk 779281870b, determinism.cljc and promotion.cljc loaded from the mayor checkout; tools/story is byte-identical to the review tree: `git diff --quiet 034d0c8fc8 <tip> -- tools/story` exit 0, control `-- implementation/core/src` exit 1), with a real fx that counts its calls and returns normally:
   - A0 `run-variant` of a `force-fx-stub` variant: `[:pass 0]`, 0 real calls.
   - A1 `assert-deterministic (variant-plan id)`: `[:deterministic 2]`. The gate reports DETERMINISTIC while calling the stubbed real effect twice. (The dossier's `:non-deterministic` came from a probe fx that threw; with a normal fx the answer is a false green, which is worse.)
   - A2 `capture-golden (variant-plan id)`: froze a `:pass` run, 1 real call.
   - B0/B1/B2, a variant whose terminal `:assertions` expect `[:count] 99` after one increment: `run-variant` `[:fail 1-assertion]`; replay of `->artifact` `[:pass 0-assertions]`; gate `:deterministic`. The plan's `:expect` never reaches the artifact.
   - C1/C2, `:db-seed {:count 10}` then one increment: `run-variant` app-db count 11; replay of `->artifact` count 1.
   Probe attempt 1 was not a valid witness (its fx had the wrong arity, `(fn [_] ...)`; reg-fx handlers take `(ctx args)`), so it counted 0 while the effect errored. Attempt 2 fixed that and is the one quoted.

2. Why every plan, not the dossier's "artifact-shaped subset" (this is where the dossier and Codex differed; Codex is right on the boundary). What `->artifact` drops is wider than the world slots the dossier listed. It reads only `[:world :setup]`, the top-level `:script` (the FIRST play only), `[:world :frame :fx-overrides]` and `[:world :network]` (determinism.cljc `->artifact`, plan branch). It also drops the plan's `:expect` (terminal `:assertions` / `:checks`, measured B above) and every non-primary auto-run play in `[:world :scripts]` (plan.cljc `normalize-scripts` returns `{:script (first play) :scripts plays}`; Codex measured two auto plays giving 2 in the real run and 1 in replay). And `[:world :decorators]` carries the FULL stack, globals and story included (plan.cljc, `(seq full-decos) (assoc :decorators full-decos)`), so hiccup theme decorators are on almost every plan and a subset predicate would have to classify decorator kinds. A correct subset test would therefore be a slot-and-kind classification framework over `:world`, `:expect` and `:scripts`, maintained for ever against a runtime that keeps growing slots (the rf2-tymyh `:network` repair to this very fold is the precedent). Refusing every plan uses the `(contains? target :world)` test both call sites already dispatch on, deletes a branch instead of adding a classifier, and cannot fail open when a new slot lands. What it costs is two lines for the author: run the variant instead.

3. Why the refusal is NOT at `->artifact` (this is where this ruling departs from Codex, who said "share the rejection at the conversion boundary so direct callers cannot bypass it"). `determinism/->artifact` of `variant-plan` is the SPECIFIED promotion API route: tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md §Promotion ("The capture boundary": "The API route, an artifact built from the compiled plan (`determinism/->artifact` of `variant-plan`) ..."), both skills teach it (skills/re-frame2/references/tooling/story-mcp-loop.md §Promote a failing run; skills/re-frame2-pair/references/stories.md §Three recipes), tools/story/spec/023-Parity-Test.md's probe6c names it as the API route, and it is the materialize seam in promotion_cljs_test.cljc (:320, :435, :525, :975), ui/promotion_cljs_test.cljc:302 and artifact_test.cljc:468. Refusing there breaks promotion. An explicit `(assert-deterministic (->artifact plan))` is not a bypass worth guarding: the caller asked for the artifact, and the artifact is exactly what is judged. Trust the programmer.

4. Why not A: it builds a second run engine inside replay (stub registration is a process-global `reg-fx`, so the fold cannot stay pure; `:db-seed` needs schema validation; frame-setup needs its teardown walk; loaders are async with a completion predicate), and every future runtime slot must be mirrored or the gate silently diverges again. That has already happened once (rf2-tymyh added `:network` to the artifact; rf2-shx4 fixed the same bug separately in the inline path). There are no callers to serve: outside tests and the facade, `assert-deterministic` / `capture-golden` / `golden-match?` / `compare-golden` are called nowhere in examples/, testbeds/, docs/ or skills/ (the testbed hit at tools/story/testbeds/counter_with_stories/stories.cljs:800 is a comment).

5. Why not C: `story/run` returns a Promise on CLJS (a CompletableFuture on the JVM), so the gate would become async for one target kind, or need a new verb (an API-manifest touch). The two-line recovery below already gives C's answer with no new surface.

6. The recovery is measured, and one tempting recovery is a trap (Codex's point, re-measured):
   - C4: two `(story/run :variant-id)` runs of the seeded variant: both `:pass`, app-db count 11, `(determinism/compare-runs [r1 r2])` `:deterministic? true`, run-hash equal.
   - C5: `capture-golden` of a `story/run` run-result, then `golden-match?` against a second run: `true`.
   - C3 TRAP: `(story/run (story/variant-plan :variant-id))` ends at count 1, not 11. `story/run`'s map branch treats the map as an authoring body and recompiles it (runtime `run-inline-plan` calls `plan/variant-plan` on it), so a normalized plan's `:world` is silently ignored. NEVER teach that form. Filed as rf2-nt9f1 (see FOLLOW-UPS).
   - Codex: teach `compare-runs` (canonical equality is the authority), not bare hash equality; and surface a run that itself returned `:error` / `:cannot-run` separately rather than calling two identical errors "deterministic".

--- WHAT TO BUILD (verified at trunk 7fc78b7b72; tools/story unchanged since 034d0c8fc8) ---

1. tools/story/src/re_frame/story/determinism.cljc
   - A small pure refusal builder beside `cannot-run-wait-refusal`, e.g. `plan-target-refusal`, returning `{:status :cannot-run :reason :determinism-plan-target :detail "..."}`. The detail says: the gate judges an artifact or an event program; a variant plan's run depends on world the artifact does not carry (decorator stubs such as force-fx-stub, :db-seed, frame-setup, loaders, terminal :assertions/:checks, extra plays); to ask whether a VARIANT is deterministic, run it twice with `story/run` on its id (not on its compiled plan) and compare the two run-results with `re-frame.story.determinism/compare-runs`.
   - `assert-deterministic`: check `(and (map? x) (contains? x :world) (not (rf.story.artifact/run-artifact? x)))` BEFORE calling `->artifact`, and return the refusal. Pure pre-flight, zero replays, zero effects.
   - `->artifact`: keep all three branches. Rewrite its docstring: the plan branch is a PROGRAM projection used by promotion (`[:world :setup]` ++ the primary `:script`, frame `:fx-overrides`, `:network`, `:source`), NOT a reproduction of the variant's run, and it lists what is not carried. Drop the "determinism-gate target" framing from its first line. After this ruling the plan branch serves promotion alone, and rf2-hyheo may reshape it for promotion. Whichever lands second makes the docstring describe the branch as it then stands. Do not change the branch's behaviour here.
   - Update the ns docstring and the `assert-deterministic` docstring ("a normalized variant plan" is no longer an accepted target; name the refusal).
2. tools/story/src/re_frame/story/golden.cljc `->run-result`: replace the plan branch (`(and (map? target) (contains? target :world)) (replay-run-artifact (->artifact target) opts)`) with a throw of `:rf.error/golden-bad-target` whose `:reason` names the plan case and the recovery (capture from the run-result of `story/run` on the variant id). Keep the branch ahead of the `:status` branch so a plan is never mistaken for a run-result. Reuse the existing error id: it is uncatalogued in any spec, so no catalogue edit follows. Update the `->run-result` and `capture-golden` docstrings (the facade's `capture-golden` docstring already names only run-result and artifact, so it needs no change).
3. tools/story/src/re_frame/story.cljc facade `assert-deterministic` docstring: stop saying `plan-or-artifact`. Renaming the parameter is harmless: spec/api-manifest.edn carries no arglists (its `assert-deterministic` row has no parameter names), so no manifest regeneration and no hot-zone touch.
4. Spec (neither file is hot-zone):
   - tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md §Determinism gate (:3491 on): the opening question becomes "does this artifact / event program produce the same run every time?"; the `plan-or-artifact` paragraph (:3510-3513) becomes the artifact / `:setup`/`:script`/`:event-program` body list plus one sentence: a normalized variant plan is refused with `:cannot-run :reason :determinism-plan-target`, and a variant's determinism is judged by running it twice and comparing the run-results with `compare-runs`. Add the new refusal to the result-shape fence beside `:determinism-wall-clock-wait`.
   - 017 §Golden slices / §Capture / compare contract (:3844 on): add that a normalized plan target is refused with `:rf.error/golden-bad-target`, and capture from a run-result instead.
   - spec/008-Testing.md:893: the fence line `(assert-deterministic plan-or-artifact opts)` becomes `artifact-or-program`.
5. Tests:
   - determinism_test.cljc `gate-accepts-a-normalized-plan` (:267-276) becomes the refusal pin: the same hand-built plan returns `:cannot-run` with `:reason :determinism-plan-target`. Keep a both-ways control in the same file: the same `:setup` / `:script` passed as a BODY map (no `:world`) still reads `:deterministic` (probe E0 measured exactly that at trunk).
   - golden_test.cljc `capture-golden-from-plan-replays-not-frozen` (:425) becomes a refusal pin for capture AND for compare/match; `capture-golden-rejects-bad-target` (:343) stops listing the plan as an accepted shape.
   - The RED the new pins must show before the fix: a registered `force-fx-stub` variant over a COUNTING fx (a two-arg `reg-fx` handler that returns normally, per the arity trap above), then `(assert-deterministic (variant-plan id))` reads `:deterministic` with 2 real calls today; after the fix, `:cannot-run` and 0 real calls. Likewise `capture-golden (variant-plan id)` makes 1 real call today and must throw with 0 after. Pin the zero-real-call count explicitly, through gate, capture and compare (Codex).
   - Controls that must stay green, untouched: artifact_test.cljc:468 (`->artifact` threads `:network`), every promotion test that materializes through `->artifact` of a plan, and the explicit-artifact gate/golden tests.
6. Lanes: all changed source is `.cljc` with no `#?(:cljs` branch in the changed forms, so `cd tools/story && clojure -M:test` grades it; determinism_test / golden_test also run in the node lane (`npm run test:cljs`), a shadow-cljs lane: take it from the mayor or declare reliance on CI.

--- TRAPS ---

- A probe or regression fx must take two args, `(fn [ctx args] ...)`. A one-arg handler throws on every call, counts nothing, and makes a real-effect witness read 0 exactly where the defect lives.
- Do not recommend `(story/run (story/variant-plan id))` anywhere (C3 above).
- `[:world :decorators]` is present on nearly every plan (the full global + story + variant stack), so "has decorators" is not a usable signal for anything.

--- INTERACTIONS ---

- rf2-3x7nj.31.1 (replay drops non-dispatch steps): independent. It fixes what replay EXECUTES for an artifact; this ruling only stops plans reaching replay. Land in either order.
- rf2-3x7nj.31.3 (canonicalize keeps `:error-trace`): still needed for genuine fx-error artifacts; no longer reachable through a plan target.
- rf2-3x7nj.30.4 (canonicalize over-strips `:source` / `:elapsed-ms` / `:runner`): this ruling makes run-result comparison the sanctioned route for a variant, so 30.4's fix must keep the C4/C5 shape green: two `story/run` results of one variant compare `:deterministic? true` through `compare-runs` and a golden captured from one run matches the second. A pointer note is appended there.
- rf2-3x7nj.31.4 (force-fx-stub spec): independent; its corrected spec points test-shaped mocking at first-class `:fx-overrides` / `:network`, which artifacts DO carry.
- rf2-3x7nj.30.3 (ruled): same principle, one run engine, no second path.

--- FOLLOW-UPS FILED ---

- Promotion API route loses the source's world: measured by this ruling (probe D, same run as above).
