title: INCOMPLETE: inline declarative spawn crashes when optional address fields are omitted
description:
PR #10296 promises inline :definition validation at spawn, but a legal-looking declarative inline child without :id-prefix or :fixed-actor-id fails earlier in actor-address allocation, before the new validator can run. This is a pre-existing residual found while auditing that claim.

At merge 779281870b7b8fbe5d5d7a83999d1815994287e7, register a parent {:initial :working :data {} :states {:working {:spawn {:definition {:initial :wait :states {:wait {}}}}}} and dispatch an event to boot it. Registration accepts it. Runtime emits :rf.error/handler-exception caused by NullPointerException from clojure.core/namespace in transition/format-spawn-id; parent snapshot remains nil. The child definition is valid. Same path with a registered :machine-id runs; the merged regression's explicit :fixed-actor-id also bypasses the defective allocator.

Cause: transition.cljc spawn-id-prefix at 2384-2386 returns (or (:id-prefix spawn-spec) (:machine-id spawn-spec)), hence nil for an unaddressed inline definition. allocate-one at 2388-2399 passes nil through allocate-spawned-id to format-spawn-id at 563-567. No default or typed rejection covers the inline arm. The new spawn-fx inline-definition-error gate is later and cannot intercept this crash.

Spec 005 Declarative :spawn table around lines 2997-3003 permits exactly one of :machine-id/:definition and labels BOTH :id-prefix and :fixed-actor-id optional. The address requirement therefore cannot be inferred by the caller.

Correction: settle the inline arm using the existing address grammar: make an accepted inline spawn allocate a deterministic address, or require an existing prefix/address explicitly with an early typed diagnostic and matching docs. Do not add a new API. Cover absent-address valid and invalid inline definitions plus fixed/prefix controls, including spawn-all where applicable.

Evidence: ai/gate-entry-cofx-10296-audit-sep23-monitor-2.log/.exit, exit 1: intended control failed before its transition because the valid inline child reached format-spawn-id with nil; full trace and loaded worktree path captured. Trial 3 replacing that inline child with a registered :machine-id booted and reached :errored. No exact open duplicate among 66 open Beads; searched inline and id-prefix descriptions. Baseline PR tests 40/83 green only cover explicitly addressed inline children.
notes:
== RULING (mayor, 2026-09-24, under the project stance; small call, not escalated) ==

OPTION (b): an inline `:definition` spawn must carry an address — `:id-prefix` or `:fixed-actor-id` — and one that carries neither is refused EARLY, typed and fail-closed. No default address is invented.

WHY (b), not (a):
- The existing grammar already says where the default comes from, and an inline definition has none of it. Spec 005 §Spec-spec keys reads `:id-prefix` "optional; defaults to `:machine-id`". `spawn-id-prefix` in `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc` (~:2394 at trunk 63e118215c) is exactly `(or (:id-prefix spawn-spec) (:machine-id spawn-spec))`. So the inline arm needs a THIRD source of default, and that is new grammar, which this bead forbids ("Do not add a new API").
- A default is not cosmetic here. `spawn-id-prefix`'s own docstring records that since rf2-1sip option (f), a generated address held by a live actor fails closed, and `:id-prefix` is the author's only namespacing escape from that collision. Any shared inline default (a reserved keyword, or the parent's id) sequences every unaddressed inline child in the tree under one prefix, drawn from per-parent snapshot-local counters. That manufactures exactly the collision the escape exists to avoid. A parent-derived default would also mint addresses that read like instances of the PARENT's type.
- Requiring the address costs the author one keyword, and it gives Xray a meaningful actor name in place of an opaque one. That fits "trust the programmer" and low friction: one clear error at authoring time, never a crash deep in allocation.
- Nothing that works today changes. The unaddressed inline path crashes with an NPE in `format-spawn-id` at trunk, and the bead records that the only green inline tests are explicitly addressed.

BUILD:
1. Refuse at the EARLIEST existing validation point that sees the spawn spec:
   - If `reg-machine`'s registration-time validation already walks `:spawn` / `:spawn-all` specs, refuse there, so the machine never registers.
   - Otherwise refuse in the spawn path BEFORE `allocate-one`, with the existing fail-closed reject shape: no snapshot, no slot, no allocation, no `:start`, as `reject-unregistered-spawn!` in `lifecycle_fx/spawn.cljc` does.
   - Cover the declarative `:spawn`, each `:spawn-all` child spec, and a hand-emitted `:rf.machine/spawn` fx carrying `:definition` alone. Check each reaches the same NPE today before claiming it.
2. Reuse an existing `:rf.error/*` id if one already names malformed spawn args (look at what the spawn-args validator and PR #10296's `inline-definition-error` emit). Mint a new id only if none fits; in that case STOP and ask the mayor for `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` (hot-zone) before adding its catalogue row.
3. `spec/005-StateMachines.md` (hot-zone, granted to this bead's worker):
   - In the §Spec-spec keys table, the `:id-prefix` row's required? cell becomes "optional with `:machine-id` (defaults to it); REQUIRED with `:definition` unless `:fixed-actor-id` is given".
   - Make the same one-clause correction in §Spawn-spec keys (~:2825) if that table carries the inline arm too.
   - Add no new prose section.
4. Tests (the bead's list): an absent-address VALID inline definition is refused with the typed error and nothing installs; an absent-address INVALID inline definition is refused too, by whichever gate fires first; `:id-prefix` and `:fixed-actor-id` controls run; `:spawn-all` covered.

If building this shows the ruling rests on a false premise (for example, a working in-tree caller of an unaddressed inline spawn), stop and report with the evidence.
== WORKER VERDICT (2026-09-24 10:14:08 AUSEST, PR #10325, branch worker/machines-inc) — FIXED per the ruling (option b) ==

Premise check at trunk 63e118215c, through the real router. Two of the three shapes the ruling names reach the NPE; the hand-emitted one does NOT.
- Declarative :spawn {:definition valid} (no address): registration accepted it, then booting raised :rf.error/handler-exception ("Cannot invoke Named.getNamespace() because x is null") and left no parent snapshot.
- :spawn-all child {:id :c1 :definition valid} (no address): the same outcome.
- Hand-emitted [:rf.machine/spawn {:definition valid}]: NO NPE and no error at all. spawn-fx allocated nothing, INSTALLED an actor snapshot at address nil, and emitted :rf.machine.spawn/spawned with :spawned-id nil. It is still an unaddressed inline spawn under the ruling, and the Spawn-spec keys table (the hand-emitted args) is one of the two cells the ruling corrects, so it is refused too.

Ruling premises checked:
- No in-tree caller uses an unaddressed inline spawn. A scan of every tracked .md/.clj/.cljs/.cljc/.edn found each inline :definition spawn carrying :id-prefix or :fixed-actor-id, apart from two registration-only tests in spawn_all_test.clj. Those asserted that the unaddressed shape registers (it crashed on boot), and now carry an address.
- reg-machine registration already walks :spawn / :spawn-all (validate-spawn!, validate-spawn-all!), so the refusal lives there.

Build:
- Error ids REUSED, none minted, so spec/009 is untouched. :rf.error/machine-spawn-bad-shape covers a single :spawn and :rf.error/machine-spawn-all-bad-shape covers a :spawn-all child. The new inline-spawn-address-error runs right after the existing XOR check, so the machine never registers.
- For the hand-emitted fx, spawn.cljc's new inline-address-error throws :rf.error/machine-spawn-bad-shape before anything installs. It sits just ahead of #10296's inline-definition-error on that gate's own path, which the fx runner surfaces as :rf.error/fx-handler-exception.
- spec/005-StateMachines.md: the :id-prefix required? cell in both §Spawn-spec keys and §Spec-spec keys now reads "optional with :machine-id (defaults to it); REQUIRED with :definition unless :fixed-actor-id is given". No other prose was touched.

Tests, in the new machine_spawn_inline_address_test.clj:
- For each of declarative :spawn, :spawn-all child and hand-emitted fx: an absent-address VALID definition is refused with the typed id and nothing installs. An absent-address INVALID definition is refused by the address gate, which fires first. :id-prefix controls install at <prefix>#1, and :fixed-actor-id controls install at their address.
- Fix removed (both gates disarmed): exit 1, 11 failures, every one a CASE assertion. The controls stayed green.
- Restored against the committed blobs: exit 0, 19 tests / 114 assertions with spawn-all-test.

Two follow-ups outside this fence:
(1) tools/machines-viz's grammar definition-defect still returns nil (accepts) for {:spawn {:definition ...}} with no address, and the engine now refuses it. The parity corpus has no such entry, so nothing reds. It needs either a documented divergence or a mirror update.
(2) The Spec 009 rows for machine-spawn-bad-shape / -all-bad-shape describe only the XOR / shape triggers. A one-clause amendment would name the address rule if 009 is granted.
Merged-PR audit #10325 (82dbed92a73e63e65c8ac5690f4f52cecaa4f5ff; merged 2026-09-24T00:40:46Z). Completeness: Both prior audit defects are corrected: synthetic/root transition targets ensure initial-descent entry coeffects, and unaddressed inline spawn is refused at registration and hand-emitted fx ingress. Read specification address cells. Sources already closed by implementation; no status changes. title: examples-substrates: the Fresco login's SSR route hydrates the draft password as :rf/redacted, so the password field arrives pre-filled with 'redacted' and a correct password is refused - and the README teaches it as intended
description:
## Defect

On the Fresco login's server-rendered route, the password field arrives PRE-FILLED with the text `redacted`, so a user who types the correct password into it submits `redacted` + password and is refused (four such attempts lock the account). The host ships `:payload [:auth]`; the shared model classifies `[:auth :login-form :draft :password]` `:sensitive`; the hydration projection therefore puts the keyword `:rf/redacted` at that leaf; `:rf/hydrate` REPLACES the client's app-db with the payload's, so the controlled password input's `:value` becomes `:rf/redacted`, which Fresco's prop codec renders as `(name v)` = `"redacted"`. The server half renders the same value from its render-state projection, so there is no hydration mismatch to warn anyone. The README presents this as the intended "third case" of the two policies ("the input comes back reading `redacted` on a server-rendered page"), so the example TEACHES a login page whose SSR form cannot be submitted as-is. The client-only route is unaffected (no payload, draft password seeded to `""`).

## Where

Cited at `034d0c8fc8` (frozen tree):
- `examples/substrates/fresco/login/host.clj:153` — `:payload [:auth]` (the whole form slice, draft password included).
- `examples/core/login/model.cljc:493-505` — `:auth.login/initialise-form` seeds `{:email "" :password ""}` (`:450`) and returns `:sensitive [[:auth :login-form :draft :password]]`.
- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/payload_policy.cljc:308-326` — `project-app-db-egress` runs the allowlisted slice through `project-egress` under `:rf.egress/ssr-hydration`, so a classified leaf becomes `:rf/redacted` whatever its value (an empty string included).
- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/hydrate.cljc:233-260` — `hydrate-event-handler` "Replaces app-db with `(:rf/app-db payload)`".
- `examples/substrates/fresco/login/core.cljs:313-335` — the SSR branch of `run`: make-frame (initial-events seed `""`), then `rf.ssr/hydrate!` overwrites it; `:137-144` — the password input's `:value (:password draft)`.
- `implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/codec.cljs:298-313` — `convert-prop-value`: a keyword prop value becomes `(name v)`.
- `examples/core/login/model.cljc:135` (`[:password [:string {:min 8}]]`), `:276` (stub accepts only `(= good-password (:password body))`).
- The teaching sites: `examples/substrates/fresco/login/README.md:234-237` and `examples/substrates/fresco/login/policy.cljc:25-32`.
- Public entry: the README's "Build it and run it" route (`host/init!` + `host/app` on Jetty, `fresco.login.core/run` in the browser).

## Failure scenario

Follow the README's SSR recipe and open `http://localhost:3000`. The server document carries `__rf_payload` with `:draft {:email "", :password :rf/redacted}`; the browser hydrates it; the password input shows eight masked characters. Click into it and type `correct-horse`: the caret lands after the existing text, the edit event carries `"redactedcorrect-horse"`, validation passes (a string of 8+), the demo stub compares against `correct-horse` and fails, and `:error-shown` appears. Leave the field untouched and submit: the draft password is the keyword `:rf/redacted`, and the `[:string {:min 8}]` validator refuses it. The correct password succeeds only if the user first notices and clears the field. A developer copying this recipe ships a login page that does the same.

## Evidence

EXECUTED (bounded JVM probe, scratch deps.edn with `:local/root` onto the frozen tree's core/ssr/ssr-ring/schemas/machines/http and both examples roots; nothing written into the tree, `git status --porcelain` empty afterwards): after `(host/init!)`, an `rf.ssr.ring/ssr-handler` built with exactly `make-handler`'s opts except a stub `:renderer` returned status 200; the stub read the LIVE post-drain frame's draft as `{:email "", :password ""}` (control: the value really is an empty string), while the emitted `__rf_payload` read `{:draft {:email "", :password :rf/redacted}, …}`. The shipped crossing test pins the same redaction on the render-state side (`implementation/ssr-ring/test/re_frame/ssr/ring/login_host_crossing_test.clj:448`).
INSPECTED only (CLJS, no shadow-cljs in this review): the hydrate replacement and the codec's `(name v)` are read at the cites above; the README itself states the outcome ("the input comes back reading `redacted`").
Tracker: no bead covers it — searched the full export for `rf/redacted` with `draft|password` and `hydrat|payload` (2 hits, rf2-8arzr.5 and rf2-bv1p, both only recording the redaction as a pass); `comes back reading` 0 hits. The three prior reviews of this slice (rf2-fzbj.36, rf2-fn0kx.8, rf2-8k6br) exercised the CLIENT-only login in a browser and the SSR host with a synthetic renderer; none looked at the hydrated form.

## Smallest fix

Keep the secret out of what the browser adopts. Example-local options: (a) after `rf.ssr/hydrate!` in the SSR branch of `run`, put the draft password back to its default before the first render (one small event in `core.cljs`, or a model event the three arms can share), and change README:234-237 / `policy.cljc:25-32` to say the redacted slot is re-seeded on the client; or (b) move the transient draft password out of the `:auth` slice the payload ships (the model owns the path). Fence: `examples/substrates/fresco/login/{core.cljs,README.md,policy.cljc}`, possibly `examples/core/login/model.cljc`. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

`core.cljs` is CLJS: `npm run test:examples-compile` (`:examples/login-fresco`) grades compilation only; the behaviour is graded by the CLJS witness `implementation/fresco/test/re_frame/fresco/login_server_crossing_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs` (its namespace ends `-dom-cljs-test`, which `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` routes to BOTH `:browser-test` and `:node-test` — `npm run test:browser` / `npm run test:cljs`) if an arm is added there, and by hand in a browser. A JVM green says nothing about the client half. Examples stay test-free (rf2-8cevm).

## Decision needed

Yes, one line: is this example-local (a or b above), or should the framework own it — e.g. `:rf/hydrate` keeping the client's own value at a leaf the payload carries as `:rf/redacted` (a Spec 011 / 015 change)? The example fix is cheap either way; the framework option is Mike's call.
notes:
== DOSSIER WRITTEN 2026-09-24 04:24:32 AUSEST (analysis only — no status change, no dispatch, no edit) ==

Dossier: ai/decisions/rf2-3x7nj.43.1.hydrated-sentinel-example-or-framework.md. The ai/ tree is local-only and gitignored, so this path is a convenience that can rot; the decisive findings are restated below. Read at trunk a3d19d9826 (= origin/main as last fetched). The example, model, hydrate.cljc, payload_policy.cljc, boot.cljc, the witness and the crossing test are unchanged since 034d0c8fc8.

RECOMMENDATION: example-local, option (a). Leave :rf/hydrate unchanged. The login re-seeds its empty draft password right after rf.ssr/hydrate! and before render!. Use a small model-owned event, not :auth.login/edit-password, which would mark :touched. Route the step through one public core.cljs helper that both run and the witness's hydrate-row! call. README.md:234-237 and policy.cljc:25-32 then teach the step instead of "comes back reading redacted". File the framework findings below as ONE separate bead.

DECISIVE FINDINGS (inline, so this note stands alone):
1. Spec 011 already rules on this. spec/011-SSR.md:1874 (Resolved decisions) rejected a merge because "a merge policy makes 'did the server's value win?' undecidable at every key. Apps that want client-only seeded state run it after the hydration event, not before." Option (a) is exactly that. The framework alternative (keep the client's value at sentinel leaves) cannot honour a server-side clear, because classification does not depend on the value: a blanked leaf still ships :rf/redacted. The alternative helps only client-originated leaves.
2. The class is framework-wide, and :large is the worse half. JVM probe at trunk with local roots on core and ssr, exit 0, controls both ways: payload-policy/apply-policy + project-app-db-egress, then [:rf/hydrate], on a client frame seeded like the example. Results: [:auth :draft :password] "" became :rf/redacted (a Keyword); a server-held [:session :csrf] "csrf-abc-123" became :rf/redacted; a :large [:catalog :items] [1 2 3] became {:rf.size/large-elided {...}}, no longer a vector. Unclassified siblings were unchanged. The client's elision registry survived, via elision.cljc:287-328 reconcile-runtime-db-effect. :rf.egress/ssr-hydration sets include-large? false (implementation/core/src/re_frame/projection.cljc:154-157).
3. The hiccup tier diverges by construction. Second JVM probe: the JVM render-to-string reads the live frame, so the HTML carried value="csrf-abc-123" and value="" while the payload carried :rf/redacted. The client's first-render hash was 68e5f961 against the server's 6a1aa453, so :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch fires. The Fresco/sidecar path projects the render-state too, so both halves print "redacted" and nothing is reported. That is why this example shipped unnoticed.

FOR THE SEPARATE FRAMEWORK BEAD (the mayor should file it; the dossier filed nothing):
(i) :large elision on the hydration wire destroys data the page needs.
(ii) The hiccup render is raw while the payload is projected.
(iii) boot.cljc:163-172: hydrate! verifies synchronously right after :rf/hydrate, so there is no seam for the ruled post-hydration seed on the hiccup tier.
(iv) Spec drift, three items:
   - the "unless SSR policy explicitly permits it" door (015:404, EP-0015 §14, keep-secrets-out-of-traces.md:343) does not exist: 0 matches of include-sensitive/include-large in the ssr, ssr-ring and fresco src trees, against 17 matches of project-app-db-egress in the same trees;
   - 011:67/396/398/1630 say the payload runtime-db carries "elision declarations", but the code omits them (payload_policy.cljc:466/500/587, rf2-ybn1yb);
   - 015:401/545 and Privacy.md:159 teach :ssr {:hydrate {:include-app-db ...}}, which exists nowhere in implementation/.

ACCEPTANCE BAR (option a), in the Fresco witness login_server_crossing_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs:
- Non-DOM row: RED reads :rf/redacted, GREEN reads "". Controls: the payload still carries :rf/redacted, the email keeps the payload's "ada@example.com", and project-egress of the client's app-db still redacts.
- DOM row on the form page: the input's .value is "" and there are no mismatches.
Lanes are npm run test:cljs and npm run test:browser, the shadow-cljs lane (exclusive). A JVM green says nothing about core.cljs.
== RULING (delegated by Mike; mayor-dispatched ruling agent, 2026-09-24 05:02:32 AUSEST) ==

RULING: The fix is local to the example; `:rf/hydrate` does not change. Two small edits make the two halves agree by construction:
(1) STATE: right after `rf.ssr/hydrate!` and before the first render, the client re-seeds ONLY the draft password to `""`, through one public boot helper that `run` and the witness both call.
(2) MARKUP: the password input renders the exact sentinel `:rf/redacted` as `""`, so the server HTML carries an empty field rather than the eight masked characters of "redacted".
The README and the policy comment then teach this instead of "comes back reading `redacted`". No hot-zone file, no public API, no spec change. The framework half is ALREADY filed as rf2-hjz4r (discovered-from this bead); no new bead is needed.

WHY

The dossier and the independent Codex review both chose example-local. I re-verified the chain at trunk 7fc78b7b72:
- `examples/substrates/fresco/login/host.clj:153` ships `:payload [:auth]`, the whole form slice.
- The shared model seeds `{:email "" :password ""}` (`examples/core/login/model.cljc:450`), and `:auth.login/initialise-form` (:493-505) classifies `[:auth :login-form :draft :password]` `:sensitive`.
- The payload runs through `project-app-db-egress` under `:rf.egress/ssr-hydration`. Classification does not look at the value, so even `""` ships as `:rf/redacted`.
- `hydrate!` dispatch-syncs `[:rf/hydrate payload]`, which REPLACES app-db (implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/boot.cljc, `hydrate!` docstring step 2).
- The view binds `:value (:password draft)` (`examples/substrates/fresco/login/core.cljs:137-144`), and Fresco's `convert-prop-value` renders a keyword as `(name v)` (`implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/codec.cljs:312`), giving "redacted".
- The only drift since the review tree is `codec.cljs` (4da30826a2, frame-boundary routing), which leaves that line as cited.

What the user sees: typing `correct-horse` into the pre-filled field submits "redactedcorrect-horse". That passes `[:string {:min 8}]` and fails the stub, and the flow locks after the fourth failure (`:under-retry-limit` is `(< attempts 3)`). Submitting untouched sends the keyword, which the validator refuses.

The framework cannot fix this generically, and should not try in this bead:
- Spec 011 already rules on the shape. spec/011-SSR.md:1874 (Resolved decisions) rejected a merge policy because it "makes 'did the server's value win?' undecidable at every key. Apps that want client-only seeded state run it after the hydration event, not before." Edit (1) is exactly that.
- The rejected framework option — `:rf/hydrate` keeps the client's pre-hydrate value at any sentinel leaf — fails three ways. It cannot honour a deliberate server-side clear (a blanked classified leaf still ships `:rf/redacted`). It helps only client-originated leaves; a server-held CSRF token or `:large` list gets nil or a stale seed, which is quieter and worse. And it would create adoption mismatches that do not happen today.
- A dev warning when a sentinel is installed would fire on every correct app that ships a classified leaf it never reads, which is the nagging diagnostic "trust the programmer" rejects.
- Dropping the leaf instead of stamping the sentinel loses the "withheld" signal and moves a conformance fixture (spec/conformance/fixtures/data-classification-ssr-hydration-allowlist-first.edn pins `:token :rf/redacted`).
- The sentinel IN THE PAYLOAD is correct defence-in-depth (spec/015:404). The defect is only that this client ADOPTS it.

WHERE THE TWO REVIEWS DIFFERED: Codex added edit (2), rendering the sentinel as "" in this one view, and I ADOPT it. The decider is that the dossier's state-only fix leaves the server HTML carrying `value="redacted"` while the client renders `""`. That leaves three problems:
- The user sees a fabricated password until JavaScript runs.
- Anyone who types before hydration types after it, and React does not overwrite a dirty field.
- Whether the field ends up empty depends on a React-internal detail. The dossier read react-dom 19.3.0's `initInput` (react-dom-client.development.js:1911-1912): when hydrating it sets `.defaultValue`, not `.value`. That was inspected, never run. React's hydration contract expects matching output and gives no guarantee that it repairs attribute differences.
Edit (2) makes both halves print `""`, so nothing depends on it. Codex's second reason also holds: matching exactly `:rf/redacted` in the credential view, rather than a global codec rule, keeps the meaning local. A generic codec cannot know what a redacted balance, list or label should display. (The how-to's "handlers MUST see real values" is served by edit (1). Edit (2) touches only what the SERVER render prints, since the client's state never holds the sentinel at render time.) I also take Codex's qualification that spec/015:416/422/500 do not by themselves forbid a sentinel in hydrated state. There is a documentation and composition gap, and it belongs to rf2-hjz4r.

WHAT TO BUILD (trunk 7fc78b7b72)
- examples/core/login/model.cljc: one small model-owned event, for example `:auth.login/reseed-draft-password`, that writes `""` at `[:auth :login-form :draft :password]` and NOTHING else. Do not touch `:touched`, `:errors`, `:submit-attempted?` or the email. Traps:
  - Do NOT reuse `:auth.login/edit-password {:value ""}`, which adds `:password` to `:touched` although the user never touched it.
  - Do NOT reuse `:auth.login/reset-form` (:681) or re-run `:auth.login/initialise-form`, which would wipe the server's email and validation state.
  - The event carries no value, so it needs no `:sensitive` meta. The model's classification comment (:483-492) may gain one clause: on a hydrated client the draft password is re-seeded after hydration.
- examples/substrates/fresco/login/core.cljs: one PUBLIC fn, for example `(hydrate-client! frame-id payload)`, that calls `(rf.ssr/hydrate! {:frame frame-id :payload payload})` and then `(rf/dispatch-sync [:auth.login/reseed-draft-password] {:frame frame-id})`. `run`'s SSR branch (:313-335) calls it in place of the bare `hydrate!`, still after `make-frame` and before `render!`.
  - The witness's `hydrate-row!` currently copies `run` by hand (`rf.ssr/hydrate!` at login_server_crossing_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs:454). It must call the SAME helper, or the step goes ungraded.
  - This example passes no `:render-tree-fn`, so `hydrate!` runs no synchronous verify before the re-seed. That is correct and needs no seam.
- core.cljs view (:137-144): the password `:value` renders the exact sentinel `:rf/redacted` as `""` and every other value unchanged. Keep it to this field.
- Teaching text: `examples/substrates/fresco/login/README.md:234-237` and `policy.cljc:25-32`. Replace "comes back reading `redacted`" with the rule: "A classified leaf in a slice you ship arrives as its sentinel. The render cannot print a secret it was never handed, so this field renders it empty. The client owns this value, so it sets it after hydrating (Spec 011's post-hydration rule)."

REGRESSION: rows in implementation/fresco/test/re_frame/fresco/login_server_crossing_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs. Examples stay test-free (rf2-8cevm), so the rows go in the witness. To get a real RED for the state row, first land the helper as a bare `hydrate!` (no re-seed) and watch the row go red, then add the re-seed.
- STATE row (non-DOM, both lanes). Server frame with `idle-events` (:275-278, which types email `ada@example.com` and password `correct-horse`), then `payload-of` (:145, pure, runs in both lanes). Then a fresh client frame from `model/frame-config`, then `views/hydrate-client!`.
  - Assert the draft password reads `""`. RED without the re-seed: `:rf/redacted`.
  - Controls in the same row:
    - the payload still carries `:rf/redacted` at that leaf (wire and privacy unchanged);
    - the email reads the payload's "ada@example.com";
    - `:touched` equals the payload's (the re-seed touched nothing else);
    - an egress projection of the client's app-db still redacts the password. The client's classification registry survives hydration via `reconcile-runtime-db-effect`, per the dossier's JVM probe.
- MARKUP row (both lanes, via `rendered!`, :252). The idle-form server HTML's password input carries an empty value and no `value="redacted"`. RED today. This is the row a state-only fix fails; the state row is the one a view-only fix fails, so each edit has its own red.
- DOM row (browser lane). Adopt the IDLE FORM page through `hydrate-row!`. Today §6 (:471) uses `authed-events`, the Welcome page, so it never renders the field.
  - Assert `seen` is `[]`, no uncaught error (`swallow-uncaught? false`), and the adopted password input's live `.value` is `""`.
  - `:adopted-html` is innerHTML, which shows the value ATTRIBUTE, not the `.value` property. So extend `hydrate-row!` to read the input node's `.value` BEFORE `unmount!` (React empties the container on unmount, as the helper's own docstring warns).
  - §6 and its control (:490) must stay green unchanged. The re-seed does not alter the Welcome page's markup.
- Must stay green unchanged: `a-classified-secret-reaches-neither-wire` (:374) and implementation/ssr-ring/test/re_frame/ssr/ring/login_host_crossing_test.clj:448 (the render-state carries `:rf/redacted`). Edit (2) is in the view, not the projection.
- Typing and submitting through the real form is checked BY HAND in a browser on the README route: the field arrives empty, and `correct-horse` signs in without clearing anything. Neither review ran a browser.

LANES:
- core.cljs and the witness are CLJS: `npm run test:cljs` (state and markup rows) and `npm run test:browser` (DOM row). Both take the shadow-cljs build lane, which is machine-wide exclusive, so take it by grant.
- `npm run test:examples-compile` grades compiling `:examples/login-fresco`.
- model.cljc also loads on the JVM through the ssr-ring host tests, so run `clojure -M:test` in implementation/ssr-ring as the unchanged-control lane.
- A JVM green says nothing about the client half.

SEQUENCING: no hot zone, no overlap with rf2-3x7nj.13.3 (numeric payload walk, in flight), which edits payload_policy/streaming rather than the example. It can run in parallel with anything outside examples/substrates/fresco/login/, examples/core/login/model.cljc and the witness file.

FRAMEWORK HALF: tracked in rf2-hjz4r. It covers `:large` elision destroying hydrated data, the hiccup tier rendering raw values while the payload is projected (hash mismatch on a correct app), the missing "unless SSR policy explicitly permits it" door (spec/015:404, EP-0015 §14; `include-sensitive|include-large` 0 matches in ssr/ssr-ring/fresco src against 17 for `project-app-db-egress`), and the spec drift around `:include-app-db` and elision declarations. This ruling stands whatever rf2-hjz4r decides: the draft password is client-originated, so there is no server value to permit, and the re-seed stays right. At worst it becomes a harmless no-op.
== RULING ADDENDUM: carried from the dossier before it was deleted (2026-09-24 05:02:32 AUSEST) ==

Uncertain, and not settled by this ruling:
- The exact DOM behaviour of the adopted field. The DOM row measures it.
- Whether STREAMING deltas carrying sentinels overwrite live client state. They are projected under the same profile (implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/streaming.cljc:222-245) and land on a live frame. This is framework territory: rf2-hjz4r.
- examples/real-apps/realworld_http/ssr.cljc:56-65 comments that "the client puts [:auth :token] back on hydrate via `:auth/initialise`". That is an in-tree instance of this same put-it-back-after-hydration idiom. Its bootstrap `hydrate-client!` is not wired into `run`, so it was never exercised. Whoever works rf2-hjz4r should read it.

Related records, for rf2-hjz4r and not this bead:
- rf2-3x7nj.40.1: the flagship ssr example builds its payload by hand and ships raw runtime-db.
- rf2-3x7nj.32.6: edits the same `profile->size-opts` table (implementation/core/src/re_frame/projection.cljc:123-162) that the `:large` fix would touch.
- rf2-fc84b (closed): "projection never mutates committed state". Hydration is the one place an egress projection BECOMES committed state.
- rf2-3x7nj.17.1's "deleting the payload beats guarding it" favours the rejected option A′: move the password out of every shipped slice. A′ stays a sound alternative for a larger app, but it splits the shared form draft that build-a-form.md teaches as one map, across three arms, for an SSR-only concern.

Tier contrast, measured by the dossier's second JVM probe:
- On the HICCUP tier the server HTML carried the raw value while the payload carried the sentinel, so a correct app raised a hash mismatch (server 6a1aa453, client 68e5f961).
- On the Fresco adoption tier both halves print the projection, which is why this example shipped unnoticed.
== WORKER VERDICT (examples-3x7nj, PR #10329, 2026-09-24 AUSEST): FIXED per the RULING ==

This follows the ruling as written; :rf/hydrate is unchanged.

- examples/core/login/model.cljc gains :auth.login/reseed-draft-password. It writes "" at [:auth :login-form :draft :password] and nothing else, with no :sensitive meta. The classification comment gains one clause.
- examples/substrates/fresco/login/core.cljs gains the public (hydrate-client! frame-id payload). It runs rf.ssr/hydrate! and then dispatch-syncs the re-seed, and returns what hydrate! returned. run's SSR branch calls it.
- The password input renders the exact sentinel :rf/redacted as "".
- README.md and policy.cljc teach the ruling's rule.

The witness login_server_crossing_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs changes as follows:

- New STATE row (both lanes), with controls: the payload still carries :rf/redacted; the email is ada@example.com; :touched equals the payload's; the client's project-app-db-egress still redacts the field.

title: story: the add-expectations snippet drops the source's :compose (same defect as rf2-3x7nj.29.1 for :script/:plays)
description:
## Defect

`:compose` is not inherited through `:extends`, so the Story add-expectations snippet has the same defect rf2-3x7nj.29.1 fixed for `:script`/`:play`. A source variant that composes a setup fragment passes. The expectations test the dialog builds for it (`:extends` the source) FAILS, because the extending variant never receives the source's `:compose`.

Measured by the rf2-3x7nj.29.1 worker (PR #10326): the source composing a setup fragment passes with `:submits 1`, and its add-expectations test fails with `:submits nil`.

## Where

- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/author_expectations.cljc`: `build-snippet` and its body reader. After PR #10326 (merged at trunk ed48977d96), these carry the source's `:script` and `:plays` word for word, and they now live outside the CLJS-only branch, so a JVM test runs the exact function the dialog calls.
- Pin: `tools/story/test/re_frame/story/dialog_output_paste_test.clj`, the JVM test #10326 added. It requires `re-frame.epoch`, because without it `:rf.assert/dispatched?` sees an empty tape when that namespace runs alone.

## Correction

Carry the source's `:compose` into the snippet the same way #10326 carries `:script`/`:plays`: a one-line carry.

Before choosing that, check whether `:extends` itself should inherit `:compose` in the plan compiler (`plan.cljc`). If the registry's `:extends` semantics deliberately exclude `:compose`, the snippet carry is the fix. If `:extends` is meant to inherit it, that is a different, wider change: stop and report it rather than choosing.

## Control

A dialog-built snippet for a composing source passes (`:submits 1`) with the carry. It fails with `:submits nil` when the carry is removed.

## Decision needed

No for the snippet carry. See the `:extends` check above.
notes:
## Worker verdict (story-ui2-3x7nj, PR #10335): FIXED (snippet carry, as specified)

- The `:extends` check came first, as the item asks. `:extends` is deliberately NOT meant to inherit `:compose`:
  - spec/017 §`:compose` says it is a "child-only directive — like `:extends`, it is not itself inherited down an `:extends` chain";
  - `plan/compile-body` reads `(:compose child)` only, with a comment saying the same.
  - So no wider change is hiding here, and the snippet carry is the fix.
- The fix:
  - `re-frame.story.author-expectations/gen-expectations-snippet` takes `:compose` and emits it verbatim;
  - `re-frame.story.ui.author-expectations/build-snippet` passes the source body's own `:compose`, beside `:script` / `:plays`.
- Regression: `tools/story/test/re_frame/story/dialog_output_paste_test.clj` `add-expectations-to-a-composing-story-carries-its-compose`.
  - The source composes a fragment whose `:setup` dispatches `:paste/submit`. The source passes with `:submits 1`.
  - The dialog-built snippet is pasted, and the new variant now composes the fragment and passes with `:submits 1`.
  - With the carry removed it is red: exit 1, 3 failures, `:compose` nil, `:fail`, `:submits nil`.
  - Restored, it is green. The restore was verified by blob hash.
Merged-PR audit #10335 (456160cc4fd68cbdae69bb160f19f80e0893d64a; merged 2026-09-24T02:05:30Z). Completeness: All four scoped fixes land: compiled maps refuse at the common compiler ingress; add-expectations preserves child-only compose as well as script/plays; sidebar fidelity/world inputs fold inherited/composed context without compiling; text-copy error rows and EDN fallback become visible. Source Beads and updated inline-plan contract match. Correctness: Accepted author full Story JVM 2080 tests, seeded-plan red 8 failures and 22/107 green, snippet red 3 failures, sidebar red 7 and 7/76 green, node 12706/64032 and 9 copy-render control failures, final CI 38 successes. Read all production changes and source constraints. No redundant rerun or actionable defect found. Implementation quality: Refuses ambiguous misuse with recovery rather than adding a second compiled-plan execution API. Snippet uses existing composition semantics, sidebar reuses the ancestor walk with a bounded slot fold, and clipboard recovery is a plain read-only field. Actionable findings: none. Existing finding updates: none.

title: xray test: the derivation-graph redaction test's contains-secret? still matches only an EQUAL leaf (port the rf2-3x7nj.20.1 predicate)
description:
## Defect

Xray carries its own copy of the derivation-egress leak predicate, and it still has the weakness rf2-3x7nj.20.1 fixed in the derivation conformance suite. `contains-secret?` in `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/derivation_graph_redaction_cljs_test.cljc` (~:354-361 at trunk 84fedecee4) matches only a leaf EQUAL to the secret. A redaction that shipped the raw token EMBEDDED in a larger string, keyword or symbol, such as an opaque handle built from the token, would pass it green.

## Where

- The weak copy: `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/derivation_graph_redaction_cljs_test.cljc`, `contains-secret?` and its two uses (~:375-376).
- The fixed original to mirror: `contains-secret?` in `implementation/derivation-conformance/test/re_frame/derivation_algebra_conformance_cljs_test.cljc`, from PR #10324, commit bbb81d347a. It matches a string leaf with `str/includes?`, walks the keys and values of maps and the elements of collections, and for every other leaf (keyword, symbol, ...) falls back to `(str/includes? (pr-str v) secret)`.

## Correction

Port the fixed predicate into the Xray test. Add one adversarial assertion there: a value that embeds the secret without any leaf EQUAL to it, for example a string containing the secret or a keyword built from it, trips the predicate. Test-only; no source change.

## Control

With the old equality-only predicate restored, the new adversarial assertion goes red. The existing sanity and redaction assertions stay green either way.

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
## Fixed — PR #10334 (worker xshell-3x7nj, 2026-09-24)

Ported the rf2-3x7nj.20.1 `contains-secret?` into `panels/derivation_graph_redaction_cljs_test.cljc`: a string leaf matches by `str/includes?`, maps walk keys and values, collections walk elements, and every other leaf falls back to `(str/includes? (pr-str v) secret)`. Test-only.

The adversarial row is `leak-predicate-catches-an-embedded-secret-rf2-413u0`. It checks the CEDN-1 token from `re-frame.identity/canonical-bytes` of the secret scope (the token the egress mints handles from), plus a keyword built from the secret, with a sanity row showing that no leaf EQUALS the secret.

Control: with the old equality-only predicate, the local JVM run (`clojure -M:test -n` on the namespace) exited 1 with exactly 2 failures, both on the new row. With the port it exited 0. Both runs covered 6 tests and 48 assertions, so the existing sanity and redaction assertions stayed green either way. CI agreed at the tests-only head b5561d4640: JVM tools/xray had 2 failures over 1406 tests, and node-test had the same 2 in this namespace.
Merged-PR audit #10334 (11a2287c93e9fe43f505602b185b22be15228254; merged 2026-09-24T01:52:48Z). title: story: a recorded :dispatch-later child may double-fire on browser replay (timer children carry no parent id in CLJS) — reproduce first
description:
Residue from rf2-3x7nj.30.2 (PR #10315, merged at 43bf4ee37c). It was found by READING the code and has NOT been reproduced. Reproduce first.

## Claim

In the browser, a recorded `:dispatch-later` child may fire twice on replay:
1. The replayed root re-arms its timer, which fires the child during a recorded `[:wait]` step.
2. The recording also holds the child as its own step, which fires it again.

#10315 drops only children dispatched synchronously inside a root's handler, identified by `:rf.trace/parent-dispatch-id`. In the browser, timer children carry no parent id. On the JVM, `set-timeout!` wraps its callback in `bound-fn`, so there they carry it and are already dropped.

## First step (the deliverable if it does not reproduce)

Record a root that dispatches a `:dispatch-later` child through the real recorder in a CLJS test. Replay it, and count the child's handler runs. If the count is 1, close as 'premise does not hold', with the measurement.

## If it reproduces

The implementing worker noted that the obvious fix (drop timer children at record time) breaks an auto-assert that runs straight after the root. Candidate directions: stamp a parent id on browser timer callbacks, the same way the JVM does; or skip a recorded step whose event a replayed root has already re-armed. Pick the smallest change that makes browser replay match the JVM, and say which you took.

Fence: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/recorder.cljc (plus recorder/** if needed) and Story CLJS tests. No implementation/ change unless the stamp approach needs core's timer. In that case stop and report.

## Decision needed

No for the reproduction. If it reproduces and neither direction fits, report back and the mayor rules.
notes:
WORKER (story-doc-3x7nj, 2026-09-24): REPRODUCED and FIXED in PR #10331. The direction taken was "skip the recorded step", done in the recorder. Stamping a parent id on browser timers was not taken, because it needs core's timer.

REPRODUCTION. The test is tools/story/test/re_frame/story/recorder_timer_child_cljs_test.cljs, run in the node lane under a mayor-granted slot at trunk 982fb2ce41.
- Setup: a root's :fx arms [:dispatch-later {:ms 80 :event [:tbik1/child]}]. The root is recorded through the real trace listener on a live variant frame, and the timer fires while recording.
- The recording is exported with recording->script-body, with auto-assert on against the recording's :seed-db, then replayed as a registered variant.
- Before the fix the export was [:dispatch root] [:wait 85] [:dispatch child] [:assert-db [:roots] 1] [:assert-db [:children] 1].
- Replaying it ran the child handler 2 times, and the run's :status was :fail because [:children] read 2. The run exited 1.
- Controls passed: the recorded session ran the child once, and the export carried the auto-assert.

FIX (recorder.cljc + recorder/play_export.cljc).
- The trace listener recognises a :dispatch-later child by :rf.event/source-detail {:ms ...}. That stamp is written only by the :dispatch-later seam in re-frame.fx, for fx- and machine-emitted children alike.
- It records a payload-free {:kind :event/timer-child :t ms} marker on :entries. The marker never reaches :events, so gen-play-snippet and :cofx alignment are unaffected.
- entries->steps turns the marker into [:wait dt] whatever the 50ms threshold, and emits no dispatch. The step after it (the auto-assert) therefore runs once the timer re-armed by the replayed root has fired.
- The JVM is unchanged: its bound-fn-wrapped timer child carries :rf.trace/parent-dispatch-id and the rf2-3x7nj.30.2 rule skips it first.

RESULTS.
- With the fix: run exit 0 (1 test, 5 assertions, 0 failures).
- Control, with only the play_export half reverted: run exit 1. The child ran once, but the export had no wait, so the auto-assert read [:children] before the timer fired. This is the "obvious fix breaks the auto-assert" failure this bead predicted. The file was restored and its blob hash verified.
- A pure JVM probe covers the threshold rule: a timer child 12ms after its root emits [:wait 12], while a plain dispatch 12ms after its root emits no wait.

KNOWN RESIDUAL, shared with the JVM and not fixed. A :dispatch-later child whose root was dispatched BEFORE recording started is also skipped, so the replay never runs it. On the JVM the parent-id rule drops such a child the same way. In CLJS the child carries no lineage, so nothing in the recorder can tell whether its root was recorded without a core change.

title: examples-patterns: websocket clean :ws/disconnect from :active keeps the retry count, so the next manual :ws/connect inherits the abandoned run's budget (example and spec sample)
description:
## Defect

A clean `:ws/disconnect` taken from `:active` does not reset the retry counter, and neither does the later manual `:ws/connect` from `:disconnected`. Both go through `:fail-in-flight` and `:record-connection-opts`, and neither touches `:retries`. So a user who gives up during a reconnect attempt, while the connection is in `[:active :connecting]` or `[:active :authenticating]` with `:retries` N>0, and later clicks Connect, starts the new connection with the abandoned run's count.

The pattern states the opposite rule for the two sibling doors. `:reset-retries` exists "so the next manual `:ws/connect` gets a full budget rather than inheriting the abandoned run's" (Pattern-WebSocket.md:305-313), and a manual connect out of `:reconnecting` / `:failed` "zero[es] the retry counter" (`:record-and-reset`). The third door, out of `:active`, was missed. During a real outage most of a reconnect cycle's wall-clock time is spent in `:connecting`, waiting for the open to fail, not in `:reconnecting`'s short backoff. So that is the door a user most often takes.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:
- `examples/patterns/websocket/connection.cljs`:
  - `:active`'s `:ws/disconnect` is at `:626-627` (`:fail-in-flight`, whose action at `:313-325` has no retry reset).
  - `:disconnected`'s `:ws/connect` is at `:579-580` (`:record-connection-opts`, `:271-278`, likewise).
  - Compare `:reconnecting` / `:failed` `:ws/disconnect` → `:reset-retries` at `:722-723` and `:742-743`, and their `:ws/connect` → `:record-and-reset` at `:280-290`.
  - Retries are otherwise zeroed only on `:connected` entry (`:373-374`).
- `spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md`: the same shape in the worked example, `:record-connection-opts` at `:205-211`, `:fail-in-flight` at `:235-243`, `:active` `:ws/disconnect` at `:451-452`. The stated rule is at `:305-313`.
- Public entry: `[:ws/connection [:ws/disconnect]]` while a reconnect attempt is in `:active`, then `[:ws/connection [:ws/connect ...]]`.

## Failure scenario

The server goes down. The machine walks drop → `:reconnecting` → `:after` → `[:active :connecting]`, and each failed open bumps `:retries`. At `:retries` 6 the user clicks Disconnect; an app would dispatch it on logout or on an "offline mode" toggle. Later they click Connect while the server is still down.

The new connection gets 2 attempts (`:max-retries` 8), with its first backoff at `min(100*2^7, 5000)` = 5 s, before landing in `:failed`. A fresh budget would give 8 attempts starting at 200 ms. It recovers only once a connect actually succeeds, because `:connected` entry zeroes the count.

## Evidence

**Executed.** The probe loaded `connection.cljs` VERBATIM with `load-file` on the JVM, with a stub socket actor. Output is in the review scratch dir at `probe/ws.out`.
- connected, retries 0.
- drop → `:reconnecting` 1.
- The real `:after` backoff fires → `[:active :connecting]` 1.
- drop → `:reconnecting` 2 → backoff → `[:active :connecting]` 2.
- `:ws/disconnect` → `:disconnected`, **retries=2**.
- manual `:ws/connect` → `[:active :connecting]`, **retries=2**.
- **Control, the same disconnect taken from `:reconnecting`:** retries 3 → `:disconnected`, **retries=0**.

The demo UI never takes this door, because Disconnect is disabled during `:connecting` / `:authenticating` (`views.cljs:106-108`, noted as harmless by rf2-fn0kx.5). The machine is the recipe, and the spec sample has the same hole.

**Tracker.** An all-status search found 0 hits for `reset-retries`, `record-connection-opts` near retries, and "retry budget".

## Smallest fix

Zero `:retries` on every manual connect: add `(assoc :retries 0)` to `:record-connection-opts`, or route `:disconnected`'s `:ws/connect` through `:record-and-reset`. Apply the identical one-line change to the spec sample's `:record-connection-opts`, and reword `:reset-retries`' comment, which then covers belt and braces.

Files: `examples/patterns/websocket/connection.cljs` and `spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md`. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

`npm run test:cljs` (`websocket_cljs_test.cljs` could pin disconnect-from-`:active`-then-connect). The spec page needs a hand check of the sample.

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
## Fix in PR #10347 (worker wsretry-3x7nj, 2026-09-24), head b741c4db79

Premise verified at trunk 2d7bcf9b84: the defect reproduced.

Fix: took the bead's second option, which the dispatch brief also named ("reuse :record-and-reset").
- `examples/patterns/websocket/connection.cljs` and spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md's worked machine:
  - `:disconnected`'s `:ws/connect` now runs `:record-and-reset`.
  - `:record-connection-opts` became unbound and is removed.
- spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md prose:
  - §Parameters names `:record-and-reset`.
  - The `:reset-retries` comment says the disconnect-side reset is belt and braces, because the connect guarantees the budget whichever door led to `:disconnected`.
- The `:active` `:ws/disconnect` door still runs only `:fail-in-flight`, so `:retries` can read N while `:disconnected` until the next manual connect zeroes it. That is deliberate: action slots are single (005), and the bead's correction is connect-side.

The skills sketch has sibling send, subscribe, disconnect and reset handling, plus connected record-and-send; omitted request registration is explicit. The earlier open audit companion was already closed by its owner after this fix; no statuses changed. Correctness: Read all source, sketch and test changes. The reset action retains connection options while zeroing retries; automatic backoff does not reset them. Accepted author reported example/spec 5-of-6 red then 6-of-6 green, test-form 15 assertions with two-failure control, leaf 9-of-25 red then 33-of-33 green with retained send/subscription and connected-behavior controls, and CI node exact +1 test/+15 assertions. title: story promotion: the API route (promote-run-artifact! over determinism/->artifact of variant-plan) drops the source's force-fx-stub decorators and :db-seed, and :extends doubles its :setup, so no spelling reproduces the source run
description:
## Defect

The promotion API route does not reproduce its source variant's run when the source's behaviour depends on world the run artifact does not carry. The route is `(story/promote-run-artifact! (determinism/->artifact (story/variant-plan src {:run-args ...})) {:variant/id new})`, specified in tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md §Promotion ("The capture boundary": "The API route, an artifact built from the compiled plan (`determinism/->artifact` of `variant-plan`), carries every source shape") and taught by both skills (skills/re-frame2/references/tooling/story-mcp-loop.md §Promote a failing run; skills/re-frame2-pair/references/stories.md §Three recipes). `->artifact` carries only `[:world :setup]` ++ the primary `:script`, the frame `:fx-overrides` and `:network`, so the promoted body loses the source's `force-fx-stub` decorators, `:db-seed`, frame-setup decorators and loaders:

- without `:extends`, the promoted variant runs UNSEEDED and fires the effect its source stubbed;
- with `:extends src` (the Test-mode dialog's default draft), the world is inherited, but the source's `:setup` then runs TWICE, because `->artifact` already folded setup into the program that becomes the promoted `:script`.

So neither spelling reproduces a source that has both `:setup` and world-shaping slots, and the spec's "carries every source shape" is false for world slots. The Test-mode dialog route is not affected in the same way: its capture deliberately excludes `[:world :setup]` and its default draft `:extends` the source (spec 017 §Promotion).

## Evidence (EXECUTED)

Bounded JVM probe by the rf2-3x7nj.31.2 ruling agent, tools/story `:test` classpath, plain-atom adapter, trunk 779281870b (tools/story byte-identical to 034d0c8fc8 and to trunk 7fc78b7b72). The probe fx is a two-arg counting `reg-fx` handler that returns normally.

Source A: `{:decorators [[:rf.story/force-fx-stub :probe.fx/http {:status 200}]] :db-seed {:count 10} :script [[:dispatch [:probe/load]] [:dispatch [:probe/inc]]]}`:
- `run-variant` source: `:pass`, count 11, 0 real calls.
- promoted with no `:extends`: body keys `(:doc :run-artifact :script)`; run `:pass`, count 1, **1 real call**.
- promoted with `:extends src`: `:pass`, count 11, 0 real calls.

Source B: as A plus `:setup [[:dispatch [:probe/inc]]]`:
- `run-variant` source: `:pass`, count 12, 0 real calls.
- `->artifact` `:event-program`: `[[:dispatch [:probe/inc]] [:dispatch [:probe/load]] [:dispatch [:probe/inc]]]` (setup folded in).
- promoted with no `:extends`: `:pass`, count 2, **1 real call**.
- promoted with `:extends src`: `:pass`, count **13** (setup twice), 0 real calls.

The promotion acceptance both skills prescribe (fails under the fault, passes when fixed, fails again) can still pass on a promoted variant that fired a real effect, because nothing in it counts effects.

## Where (trunk 7fc78b7b72)

- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/determinism.cljc `->artifact`, plan branch.
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/promotion.cljc `artifact->variant-body` (lifts `:network` and `:fx-decisions` only; `:extends` only when the caller passes it).
- tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md §Promotion, "The capture boundary" paragraph.
- The two skill recipes named above.

## Options (for the ruling)

- (a) Make the API route mirror the dialog: the plan projection used for promotion leaves `[:world :setup]` out of the program, and promotion defaults `:extends` to the recorded source when that source is registered and no `:extends` is given. Then `:extends` supplies setup and world once. Watch `source-expectations`' `extends-source?` path, which changes which checks are carried.
- (b) Keep the program fold and lift the source's world-shaping slots onto the promoted body (its own `:decorators`, `:db-seed`, loaders ...), as rf2-vf8es did for `:network` / `:fx-overrides`. This grows a per-slot mirror, the pattern the rf2-3x7nj.31.2 ruling declined for the gate.
- (c) Docs only: correct spec 017's "carries every source shape" and teach the recipe's limits. Leaves the trap armed.

Context: under the rf2-3x7nj.31.2 ruling the determinism gate and the golden family no longer accept plans, so `->artifact`'s plan branch now serves promotion alone and can be reshaped for it without affecting the gate.

## Gates

- `cd tools/story && clojure -M:test` (promotion.cljc and determinism.cljc are `.cljc`); promotion_cljs_test.cljc also runs in the node lane (`npm run test:cljs`, a shadow-cljs lane).
- Regression: the two sources above, promoted by the documented API recipe, must reproduce the source's count with 0 real calls; show RED first (count 1 / 2 with 1 real call, or 13).
- Skills and spec edits: link gates (`scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` for skills/ and tools/*/spec); the recipe code sits in fences no gate reads, so verify by a probe run and say so.

## Decision needed

Yes: choose (a), (b) or (c). (a) is the smallest change that makes the documented recipe true, but it changes what the API route's promoted body looks like.
notes:
== RULING (mayor, 2026-09-24, under the project stance; small call, not escalated) ==

DECISION: which of the bead's three options fixes the promotion API route?

RULING: (a). The API route mirrors the Test-mode dialog.
- The plan projection used for promotion leaves [:world :setup] OUT of the promoted program.
- Promotion defaults :extends to the recorded source when that source is registered and the caller gives no :extends.
- :extends then supplies setup and world exactly once.

WHY:
- (a) is the smallest change that makes the documented recipe (spec 017 §Promotion; skills story-mcp-loop.md §Promote a failing run and re-frame2-pair stories.md §Three recipes) TRUE, and it gives ONE promotion behaviour for both routes. That is elegance.
- (b) grows the per-slot mirror the rf2-3x7nj.31.2 ruling already declined.
- (c) leaves the trap armed.
- The changed shape of the API route's promoted body is not a cost here: pre-alpha, no back-compat.
- Under the 31.2 ruling, ->artifact's plan branch now serves promotion alone, so reshaping it cannot affect the determinism gate or the golden family.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES for the worker:
- The files are those named under Where:
  - determinism.cljc ->artifact, plan branch;
  - promotion.cljc artifact->variant-body;
  - spec 017's "The capture boundary" paragraph, whose "carries every source shape" must become true or be reworded to what is carried;
  - the two skill recipes.
- Watch source-expectations' extends-source? path, which changes which checks are carried. Say in the report what moved.
- A promotion from an UNREGISTERED source (an inline plan) has nothing to extend. Keep today's behaviour there and say so; do not invent a new mechanism.
- Regression, per the bead's Gates: the two sources in the bead's evidence, promoted by the documented API recipe, reproduce the source's count with 0 real calls. Show it RED first (count 1 / 2 with 1 real call, or 13).
- The recipe code sits in fences no link gate reads, so verify it by a probe run and say so.
== IMPLEMENTED (worker promo-3x7nj, 2026-09-24, PR #10355) — option (a) as ruled ==

CHANGE
- determinism/->artifact, plan branch: for a plan whose :variant/id is REGISTERED, [:world :setup] stays out of the event program (as in a Test-mode capture). A plan naming no registered variant (inline plan) keeps today's setup-first fold, since it has nothing to extend. The predicate is rf.story.registrar/registered? :variant, the same fact promotion uses for its default.
- promotion/artifact->variant-body: :extends defaults to the registered source the artifact records ([:source :variant/id] or [:result :variant/id]) when the caller gives none. An explicit :extends wins. An artifact with no registered source gets no default and is promoted exactly as before.
- Producer census at trunk 46ef83f136: only two in-tree producers record a source variant id, ->artifact of a plan and the Test-mode capture (ui.promotion/result->artifact). Replay results carry no :variant/id. Both producers now exclude setup for a registered source, so the default :extends cannot double a setup.
- Spec 017 §Promotion "The capture boundary" no longer says the API route "carries every source shape". It says an artifact carries a program, :fx-decisions and :network but not the rest of the source's world, and that a registered source's setup and world arrive through :extends exactly once on both routes. Both skill recipes say the same, and warn that an explicit :extends drops the source's own setup and world.

WHAT MOVED in source-expectations (extends-source?): an API-route promotion given no :extends now counts as extending its source. It therefore carries only the source's own plus composed :checks, and the inherited ones arrive via :extends. Remove, don't add.

title: INCOMPLETE: Xray region transition actions omit the region from their source key
description:
Audit of PR #10442 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/10442), merge 993afa1f904f95e8fb472d109d701ede4ee7f180. The macro now stamps parallel-region transition source, but Xray cannot address it for inline transition actions. This is the distinct downstream gap disclosed by the PR.

transition.cljc:2093-2102 emits :region separately from the region-relative :transition-slot discriminator; action-cascade-row in projection.cljc:923-940 preserves both. format.cljc:390-405 builds transition-slot->spec-prefix solely from :decl-path and slot keys. cascade-row-source-key at :519-532 appends :action to that result without prefixing the row's :region (only lifecycle-source-key handles regions).

For an action row {:kind :action :phase :transition :region :r1 :action-id <inline-fn> :transition-slot {:slot :on :event-key :go :decl-path [:x]}}, the resulting key is [:states :x :on :go :action]. The newly captured code/coord is at [:regions :r1 :states :x :on :go ...]. The row therefore still has no matching source, despite complete metadata. The new Xray tests exercise region lifecycle rows, not a region transition action.

Required correction: compose the region prefix into region-relative transition source keys using the existing row/discriminator data; preserve exact carried :spec-path and named actions, and retain candidate-index and after-delay discrimination. Add a producer-derived parallel transition assertion through the production source lookup, with two regions sharing state names to prove the correct region is selected. No new source API is needed.

FIXED by PR #10447 (rf2-o03wl), merged at trunk c3d02a688c. This audit ran on PR #10442's merge, 993afa1f90, which is BEFORE #10447.

Checked by the mayor at trunk c3d02a688c:
- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/format.cljc now builds a region transition's action key with the row's [:regions <region>] prefix (about :521-525, `(into (if (some? region) [:regions region] []))`).
- The new test tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/region_transition_action_key_cljs_test.cljc registers a literal parallel reg-machine with an inline :on :go :action. It asserts the key is [:regions :r1 :states :x :on :go :action], that the inline source resolves, and (on CLJS) that proj/state-node-source-coords resolves the macro-stamped coordinate through the production reader.
- Worker evidence: with the fix removed, the key reverted to [:states :x :on :go :action] and the test went red.

Mayor's disposition on the one scope point not taken: the test's two regions do not share a state name. The region prefix is what separates same-named states, so this is recorded here rather than dispatched (stance: don't litigate the minutiae).

title: Save Variant follow-ups: sub-overrides/network/viewport rows from the compiled plan, fx-overrides fork, saved variant loses :compose fragments
description:
## What

Worker seedshot-u9tq5 reported these after fixing rf2-u9tq5 (PR #10450, merged at trunk 4e79c7a546). That PR made Story's Save Variant report the DB seed and setup a saved variant actually carries. It does this by compiling the saved body `{:extends source :args snapshot}` with the existing plan compiler (`rf.story.plan/variant-plan`), so no second resolver is needed. Re-verify each at your trunk.

1. **The other capture rows still read the raw source body.** The `:sub-overrides`, `:network` and `:viewport` rows do not use the compiled plan, so a value inherited through `:extends` still reports as not captured.
2. **`:fx-overrides` has a fork.** The plan's `[:world :frame :fx-overrides]` also folds in `:network`'s managed-stub lowering, so reading it would report network stubs as fx overrides.
3. **The saved variant loses the source's `:compose` fragments.** `:compose` is child-only in `compile-body`: it is not inherited through `:extends`. So `{:extends source :args snapshot}` renders WITHOUT the fragments the source composes. The saved variant does not look like what the user saved. The report is honest about it since #10450, but the loss is real.

## Ruling (mayor, 2026-09-26, under the stance)

- **Item 1.** Read `:sub-overrides`, `:network` and `:viewport` from the same compiled plan #10450 already builds for the DB seed and setup. That is one mechanism for every row, with no second resolver.
- **Item 2.** The row reports what the AUTHOR declared or inherited, never the lowered world value.
  - If the plan exposes the merged `:fx-overrides` BEFORE network lowering, use that.
  - If it does not, keep the row reading the declared slot, and say in the row's note that inherited fx overrides are not shown.
  - Do not restructure plan.cljc for it.
- **Item 3.** Carry the source's `:compose` into the saved body, so the saved variant renders what the user saved.
  - It is a SAVE-FIDELITY fix: `:compose` is simply copied, because `:extends` does not inherit it. No new inheritance semantics.
  - If copying it is ambiguous (for example, the source composes AND overrides the same slot), stop and report that case rather than choosing.
- Move the spec/019 rows and tests that describe these rows in the same commit.
- Each fix needs a regression that fails with the fix removed.

## Surface

`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/save_variant.cljc`, `tools/story/test/**` (new tests), and the affected rows of `tools/story/spec/019-Story-UI-Controls-And-View-States.md`. `plan.cljc` is read-only unless item 2 needs an existing accessor exposed.

## Gates

- `cd tools/story && clojure -M:test`, with the deltas.
- clj-kondo, plain.
- `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` for the spec edit.
- CLJS via CI.
- CLAUDE.md item (e).
notes:
== WORKER REPORT: PR #10458 (branch worker/savevar2-5kxbq), 2026-09-26 AUSEST ==

Reproduced at trunk d9b007be62 before any edit, through save-current-as-variant!:
- Item 1: a child that only :extends a parent carrying :sub-overrides, :network and :viewport got :not-wired on all three rows.
- Item 2: for a source with only :network, [:world :frame :fx-overrides] of {:extends src :args ...} is exactly {:rf.http/managed :rf.http/managed-test-stub}. [:explain :network :lowered-to] carries the same map. The plan exposes no merged fx value from before the lowering.
- Item 3: the source composes a fragment with :db-seed {[:count] 7}. The saved form {:extends src :args ...} re-registered with [:world :db-seed] nil and [:world :network] nil. The snippet carried no :compose.

Item 1: FIXED. carried-source-body now compiles the saved body and reads :sub-overrides (from [:world :render :sub-overrides], not-empty), :network and :viewport off the plan's :world, next to :db-seed and :setup.

Item 2: FIXED, by the ruling's second branch. The plan does not expose the merged value before the lowering, so the row keeps reading the declared slot. Its note, in both statuses, now ends ":fx-overrides the source inherits or composes are not shown." plan.cljc is untouched.

Item 3: FIXED, except for one case STOPPED FOR A RULING.
- New public fn save-variant/saved-variant-body builds {:extends src :args snap} plus the source's own :compose.
- The capture report compiles that body. ui/save_variant.cljs prints it: the snippet call site there is the only place the snippet is built, which is outside the brief's fence and held by nobody.
- gen-variant-snippet gained a :compose opt, documented in spec/005.
- Map-shaped slots cannot collide. :sub-overrides, :db-seed, :network, :fx-overrides, :interceptor-overrides, loaders and decorators compile identically, because the source stays in the :extends chain and so still owns every key it sets. The args snapshot wins over fragment args exactly as the source's own args did.
- THE STOPPED CASE is order-folded slots. :compose runs a fragment's :setup and script BEFORE the composing body's own. In the saved variant the source is the :extends parent, so its own :setup runs FIRST and its own script not at all.
- Measured on a fragment with :setup [[:frag/boot]] composed by a source with its own :setup [[:own/boot]]. The source's plan runs [:frag/boot] [:own/boot]. The copied-compose body runs [:own/boot] [:frag/boot].
- Script has the same shape, measured. A source with :plays [{:auto-run? false :script [[:own/click]]}] composing a fragment with :script [[:frag/click]] compiles to one play: auto-run? false, [frag own]. The copied-compose body compiles to auto-run? true, [frag]. So the copy makes the fragment's script auto-run where the source never auto-runs it. With an auto-run source the copy gives auto-run [frag] against the source's [frag own]; the own script's absence comes from :extends, not from the copy.
- Shipped behaviour in the stopped case: when the source's own body and a composed fragment both carry :setup, or both carry a script, :compose is NOT copied. That is the behaviour before this change, and the capture report does not flag it. Pinned by saved-variant-body-leaves-out-a-compose-whose-order-it-cannot-keep.
- RULING WANTED: copy anyway, accepting the reordering; keep leaving it out; or leave it out and warn in the report.

- tools/story clojure -M:test: 2104 tests / 8002 assertions / 0 failures, captured exit 0. Baseline 2100/7968/0, so the delta is +4/+34, as predicted.

So :compose is left out there, as before.

title: Spec prose describes a non-existent co-located :rf/reply default (AI-Audit.md, Pattern-NineStates.md)
description:

title: docs/api re-frame.resources: load-more says the feed stays :loaded, but the runtime moves it to :fetching
description:
From GitHub issue #10489 (closed into this bead). Original text:

**Type:** bug (reference docs) · **Priority:** P2 · **Size:** small, one file

## Gap

`docs/api/re-frame.resources.md`, the `[:rf.resource/load-more {…}]` entry (line ~410 at `92c6b29960`), says:

> The feed stays `:loaded` and its pages stay visible; the in-flight load shows as the `:rf.resource/fetching-next?` subscription, separate from a whole-feed `:fetching?` refresh.

The implementation moves the feed to `:fetching`. In `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/events.cljc`:
- The load-more section header (~line 894) reads: "a `load-more` on a `:loaded` feed transitions to `:fetching` (the refresh-class transition — the feed has data, so `entry-start-load` chooses `:fetching` and the accumulated pages stay visible)".
- The call site (~lines 1024-1034) calls `rf.resources.state/entry-start-load` on the feed entry, with the comment "transition the FEED to its in-flight status … chooses `:fetching`".

The half about pages staying visible is correct. The half about status is wrong: a reader who branches on status `:loaded` during a load-more will see `:fetching`.

## What to do

1. Confirm the observable status during a load-more: read `entry-start-load` in `resources/state.cljc` and the load-more reply handlers in `events.cljc`.
2. Check whether the whole-feed `:fetching?` subscription is masked during a load-more while `:fetching-next?` is true. The earlier review believed it is, but that was not measured here.
3. Rewrite the sentence to match. For example: "The feed moves to `:fetching` and its pages stay visible. Use `:rf.resource/fetching-next?` to show the load-more spinner, not a whole-feed refresh."
4. Check whether `docs/resources/how-to/paginate-a-feed.md` or `spec/016-Resources.md` §Causal event — load-more make the same `:loaded` claim, and fix it the same way.

## Acceptance

- The API entry states the status the implementation produces, with `events.cljc` as the source of truth.
- `python3 scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` and `python3 -m mkdocs build --strict` exit 0.

## Context

Found during the `docs/resources` correctness pass (day8/re-frame2#10480), and left out of it because the file is outside `docs/resources`. `spec/API.md` is a hot-zone file and is not expected to change for this.
notes:
== CONFIRMED (mayor, 2026-09-26): the docs/resources review measured it. docs/api/re-frame.resources.md:410 says 'The feed stays :loaded', but load-more gives :status :fetching, with :fetching-next? true in the infinite-state sub and :fetching? true in the :rf/resource sub.

== FIXED (worker/apirev12-elnoo, PR #10549, commit f1383e553f, 2026-09-26 20:3x AUSEST)
Verified at source: events.cljc's load-more calls rf.resources.state/entry-start-load on the feed entry, which picks :fetching because the feed has data (next-status :start-load had-data?). subs.cljc: state-sub-fn (:rf/resource) and fetching?-sub-fn (:rf.resource/fetching?) both read (= :fetching status), so they report :fetching? true during a load-more; infinite-state-sub-fn sets :fetching? (and fetching (not next?)) and :fetching-next? next?, so the feed view-model keeps :fetching? false and reports :fetching-next? true. This agrees with the mayor's measurement above.
docs/api/re-frame.resources.md, the load-more entry, now reads: the feed moves to :fetching and its pages stay visible; show the load-more spinner from :rf.resource/fetching-next?; the :rf/resource view-model and :rf.resource/fetching? read :fetching? true during a load-more or a whole-feed refresh alike, while :rf.resource/infinite-state reports :fetching-next? and keeps its own :fetching? false.
Step 4 (the two other files): the premise does not hold for either. docs/resources/how-to/paginate-a-feed.md already says "A load-more moves the feed to :fetching with the loaded pages still visible", and spec/016-Resources.md §Causal event — load-more already says it "transitions the feed to :fetching (the refresh-class transition)". Neither makes the stays-:loaded claim, so neither changed.
