title: Fresco residue: a modal applies the popover-only :anchor/:placement; overlay docstring cites a missing checker; four test-level findings
description:
Found by the docs-residue worker (PR #10574, rf2-qyw01 item 5) and the fresco pruning worker (PR #10569, rf2-98kzs.2), both merged 2026-09-27. Each is a CLAIM; verify at tip.

1. CODE DEFECT: implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/overlay.cljs uses one render fn for modal and popover. So a modal claims the :anchor trigger, applies :placement, and raises :rf.error/fresco-overlay-anchor-missing. The module docstring says the two options are popover-only and "a modal takes none"; guide ch13 teaches them for popovers only; no test anchors a modal. docs/api/re-frame.fresco.overlay.md was left unchanged and describes the popover options.
   MAYOR RULING (2026-09-27): make the code match the docstring, so the modal render path never reads :anchor or :placement. If the overlay already refuses option keys a kind does not take (a per-kind option check with an error id), refuse these two on a modal the same way. Otherwise a modal simply ignores them, with no new diagnostic (trust the programmer). Add one regression showing a modal given :anchor renders as a modal (no anchor trigger, no anchor-missing error), and show it red with the fix removed. If the docs/api page or ch13 then says something untrue, correct that one sentence.
2. implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/overlay.cljs's namespace docstring cites check_complaint_catalogue.py, which does not exist. Point it at the real checker, or drop the citation.
3. Test-level findings from the pruning (no production defect):
   a. forms/l2 the-subject-field-is-value-revision-and-three-intents never checks the revision its name promises. Make it check the revision, or rename it to what it checks.
   b. view_annotation_slot's docstring is stale about which spellings the DOM rows use. Correct it.
   c. No test covers revision_dom §5c (distinct revision objects with equal values). Add one row only if the spec states §5c as a contract; otherwise record why none is needed.
   d. The forms and grid L2 rows that built a literal form instead of reading the view were removed in the pruning, so "the view carries no reset trigger" is not checked at L2 for those two examples. If a retained test covers that contract, record which. If none does, add one row per example that reads the view.
Gates: the fresco JVM suite; CLJS via CI (the node and browser lanes; ask the mayor for the shadow-cljs lane before any local run); clj-kondo WITHOUT --fail-level, per CLAUDE.md item (w); present_tense.py verify on changed docstrings.
notes:
== VERDICT (worker frescores-rki3d, PR #10575) ==

All three items fixed; one PR, one commit per item. Left open for the mayor to close after merge.

1. FIXED. Premise held: impl/overlay.cljs `body` served modal and popover alike, reading (:anchor props) into the cell and (:placement props) into position-area for both. Which ruling case applies: the overlay has NO per-kind option refusal (its only error id is :rf.error/fresco-overlay-anchor-missing; `own-keys` is one shared list and every other key passes through as an attribute), so per the ruling a modal simply ignores the two keys, no new diagnostic. `popover-ops` carries `:anchored? true` and `body` reads :anchor/:placement only then; the modal still strips both from its attributes and still spends the same three hooks. Regression `overlay-dom-cljs-test/a-modal-given-an-anchor-renders-as-a-modal-and-claims-nothing` (resolving anchor: dialog opens :modal, trigger keeps its author anchor-name, no position-anchor, no position-area; dangling anchor: no refusal, boundary child still rendered, dialog open). Shown red in CI with the fix removed (`:anchored? true` planted into modal-ops): 6 failures in that row, trigger claimed `--rf-overlay-34`, position-area `block-end span-inline-end`, anchor-missing raised. docs/api/re-frame.fresco.overlay.md and guide ch13 already give both options as popover-only; no sentence became untrue, no docs edit.

2. FIXED. overlay.cljs namespace docstring now names scripts/check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py, which holds the emitter and the Spec 009 row in step (it does not read complaints.md, so the sentence no longer says "both rows").

3. a FIXED: forms/l2 the-subject-field-is-value-revision-and-three-intents now asserts `(= 2 (::rf.fresco/revision attrs))` off the view tree. b FIXED: view_annotation_slot docstring now says the DOM rows use two spellings (keyword; string in a hash map). c ROW ADDED: the condition holds, revision-prop-spec.md §3.2 states "Equal-but-fresh revision values are inert, by =" and HD-019 repeats it; revision_dom equal-but-fresh-revision-values-are-inert uses a MAP revision through a memoized Fresco boundary (codec/memoize-boundary!, = over props), because the pruned row used strings, which Object.is already equates, so it only restated §5b. d ROWS ADDED: no retained test read "no reset trigger" off the forms or grid views (grep over forms/grid tests: only the subject field's revision is exercised), so forms/l2 the-two-form-fields-carry-no-reset-trigger and grid/l2 a-cell-carries-no-reset-trigger read it off the view, each with a present-trigger control.

Controls: a DO NOT MERGE sabotage head (24dca45e5d, since force-pushed away; restore verified by blob hash on all 4 planted files) removed each property. CI browser lane 8 failures (6 modal row, 1 equal-but-fresh row, 1 forms flow_dom collateral of the 3a plant); node lane 12906 tests / 66993 assertions / 4 failures, all four the new 3a/3d assertions.

Gates: fresco JVM suite exit 0 (3 tests, 92 assertions; compiles no .cljs, so no evidence about these changes); CLJS node+browser relied on CI, green on head 7649559234 (88 checks settled, 52 success / 36 skipped; node 12906 tests / 66993 assertions / 0 failures, browser 1156 / 6347 / 0 — exactly the predicted +4/+10 and +2/+12 over main's run at base b45d9fa083, node 12902/66983, browser 1154/6335); pinned clj-kondo 2026.04.15 without --fail-level over the 7 changed files 0 errors 0 warnings (planted unresolved symbol -> exit 2, restored by blob hash); present_tense.py verify on the two docstring-only files ok; static ratchets (retired spellings, thrown messages, ambient reads, require-alias dialect, test-lane bijection, keyword drift, residue gates, fresco reachability/guide-samples/lint-export) all exit 0; all 7 changed files w/crlf with CR=CRLF, bare LF 0.

Other defect for the mayor to file (outside this fence): implementation/fresco/test/re_frame/fresco/codec_cljs_test.cljs:448 comment also cites the nonexistent check_complaint_catalogue.py.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #10575, merged 2026-09-27 at trunk 05d4535ef5.
(1) The premise held: impl/overlay.cljs's body read :anchor and :placement for both kinds. The overlay has no per-kind option refusal (its only error id is fresco-overlay-anchor-missing, and own-keys is one shared list), so under the ruling a modal simply ignores both keys, with no new diagnostic. popover-ops carries :anchored? true, and only then are the keys read. Regression: a-modal-given-an-anchor-renders-as-a-modal-and-claims-nothing. With the fix removed, all 6 of its checks failed (trigger claimed, position-anchor/position-area written, anchor-missing raised). The docs/api page and ch13 already say popover-only, so no docs edit was needed.
(2) The overlay.cljs docstring names scripts/check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py, and says what it actually checks.
(3) a: the row checks the revision its name promises. b: the docstring names the two spellings the DOM rows use. c: added; the spec states the contract (§3.2 "Equal-but-fresh revision values are inert, by =", and HD-019), and the new row uses a map revision through a memoized view and fails with the memo removed. d: added; one row each for forms and grid reads "no reset trigger" off the view, with a positive control.
CI measured node +4 tests / +10 assertions and browser +2 / +12, exactly as predicted. Each new row was shown red in CI on a throwaway sabotage commit, which was then removed and every restored file checked by blob hash. PR CI 88/88.

title: Redo docs/story: four serial steps (completeness, correctness, quality, holistic structure) with annotated Playwright screenshots; Story<->testing and Story<->Xray tie-ins
description:
Mike asked (2026-09-26) to REDO the re-frame2 Story guide, docs/story/ (16 pages: index, the nine numbered tutorial parts 01-09, and api/ with index, mcp-surface, reference, registration, runtime, script).

Keep in mind (Mike's words):
- It is rendered into a GitHub-hosted website via MkDocs (mkdocs.yml nav "Story", about lines 406-415).
- Ensure best practices in tutorials and didactics.
- This is a tutorial for human engineers, not AIs. Abide by docs/AUTHORING.md.
- Ensure it explains the tie-in between Story and testing, and between Story and Xray.
- Include helpful, explanatory ANNOTATED screenshots, which the agent obtains via Playwright.

Proceed in FOUR SERIAL steps. Each step reviews the tree the previous step left. It produces a read-only report, which is triaged, and then its accepted findings are applied as one commit.

1. COMPLETENESS: compare what is taught with the UI AND the API.
   - Are the happy path and the unhappy paths discussed?
   - Are errors explained?
   - Are values fully enumerated, with the explanation they need?
   - Are the likely use cases covered?
   The sources of truth are tools/story/src (the Story tool and its UI), tools/story/spec (225 files, spec 000-Vision onward; second to the code) and the running Story shell itself.
2. CORRECTNESS: check every factual claim, every code sample and every screenshot against the implementation and the running UI. A screenshot that shows a UI which no longer exists counts as a correctness defect.
3. QUALITY: review for a human senior developer, against docs/AUTHORING.md.
   - Do the docs make a good tutorial, with progressive disclosure?
   - Are they cohesive and consistent?
   - Are they human-friendly?
   - Do they use good, simple examples that build progressively?
4. HOLISTIC QUALITY: repeat step 3, taking a view of the guide as a whole.
   - Is the current set of pages the right way to teach Story?
   - Do they have the right structure? Should the tutorial structure be improved?
   - Should new pages be created, content be moved between pages, or pages be removed?
   Because this is a REDO, step 4 has licence for substantial restructuring. Its structural proposals, with their reasons, come to the mayor for a ruling before pages are created, moved, split or removed. Keep or update every inbound anchor: grep the repo, including example sources and tools/story, for links into a page before moving or removing it, and update the mkdocs.yml nav to match.

SCREENSHOTS (all steps; step 3/4 decide which ones earn their place):
- Existing machinery: docs/scripts/generate-story-tutorial-screenshots.cjs captures the Story shell with Playwright, from compiled example bundles (:examples/login-form, :examples/counter-with-stories, :examples/nine-states-with-stories, served from implementation/out). Nine PNGs are committed in docs/images/story/ (story-tutorial-00-shell ... 08-nine-states), because the MkDocs site renders without Playwright at build time. Extend that script rather than writing a second one, and keep generated images committed.
- ANNOTATED means the image itself explains: callouts, numbered markers or highlight boxes that the surrounding prose refers to, e.g. "(1) the variant list, (2) the fidelity control". The annotation should be done by the script (e.g. overlaying DOM-positioned markers before capture, or post-processing), so that screenshots are REGENERATED, not hand-edited, when the UI changes. Every image gets meaningful alt text.
- Building the bundles uses shadow-cljs, which is the machine-wide EXCLUSIVE build lane (CLAUDE.md § Workflow). The dispatch must carry an explicit lane grant, and the worker announces TAKING and RELEASED.
- Mind repository size: prefer a sensible viewport and PNG optimisation, and don't commit a large image set nobody reads.

THE TIE-INS Mike names are required content, not optional:
- Story <-> testing: a variant is a test (Part 4 today), plus assertions, test mode, CI use, and how a Story variant relates to the project's test runners.
- Story <-> Xray: Xray embedded in Story, and when and why a developer reaches for it (Part 6 today, "earned at failure").
Both must read as one coherent workflow, not as feature lists.

How it runs: one worktree, with one worker per step or one worker running the steps in order, and one commit per step. Given the size, the mayor may dispatch steps 1-2 and steps 3-4 as two dispatches, as with rf2-e4zsm. Gates:
- check_doc_slugs.py (links, anchors, any HANDBOOK_COMPAT_ANCHORS pins);
- mkdocs build --strict (docs/story is inside docs_dir);
- the fenced-block and zero-link caveats of CLAUDE.md § Build & Test;
- the screenshot script runs clean end to end under the lane grant.
Verify anchors and table column counts by hand, and say so. Prose follows AUTHORING.md and the present-tense rule. Spec or implementation defects found along the way go to the mayor as a list for filing, not fixed here.

Related: this is the Story sibling of the per-folder docs reviews Mike requested the same day (rf2-elnoo api, rf2-cmmdq async, rf2-3gnll core, rf2-yeg4c machines, rf2-e4zsm resources, rf2-niyml routing, rf2-311li skills). Unlike those, it is a REDO, with the screenshot requirement on top.
notes:
== NOTE (mayor, 2026-09-26): use the EXISTING annotation mechanism, and sequencing
The Xray side already has a data-driven annotation pipeline. docs/scripts/generate-tutorial-screenshots.cjs resolves per-scene regions (DOM selectors or xy boxes, labels, colours, optional arrows) declared in docs/scripts/tutorial-annotation-spec.json. The Story screenshot script (generate-story-tutorial-screenshots.cjs) should REUSE that mechanism, sharing the annotation code, with scene entries in that spec file or a sibling spec, rather than inventing a second annotation system.
SEQUENCING: NEVER run this concurrently with the docs/xray redo bead (filed the same day). They share the exclusive shadow-cljs build lane, the docs/scripts screenshot tooling, and cross-linked tie-in pages. Dispatch one after the other; the second reads the first's merged tree for the tie-in wording.
The docs/xray redo bead is rf2-km1dh.

== ROUTED (mayor, 2026-09-26) from rf2-wogka: docs/story/02-every-state-side-by-side.md:79 links a reader into spec/002-Frames.md by absolute GitHub URL ("Spec 002 §What lives in a frame"). docs/AUTHORING.md forbids sending readers into spec/ to learn usage. In step 2 or 3, rewrite the idea for the reader, or point at the guide page that covers it.

== STEPS 1-2 DONE (worker storyredo12-yzdus, 2026-09-26 20:47 AUSEST) — PR #10553, branch worker/storyredo12-yzdus
Two commits, one per step, touching docs/story/** and docs/images/story/** only. The screenshot script is unchanged.

STEP 1, completeness (commit "docs(story): completeness pass"): 63 findings (counted per topic from the change list), 63 accepted, 63 applied, 0 deferred.
Sources were tools/story/src and the running shell. It added the shell regions, sidebar chips and keys, id shapes and closed bodies (with a per-kind body table in api/registration.md), the Controls and argtypes controls, Test mode's sections, the failure, promotion and Tests-widget flows, test setup (the fixture plus a re-frame.epoch require), the recorder UI with a real recorded form, the :script shapes and :plays, the step table, the verdict order and the capability-token ladder, the Xray target frame, :xray-panel and the :xray preset, the Story-to-Xray failure walkthrough, the Docs mode sections, the workspace layouts, modes, viewports and backgrounds, decorators and the built-ins, tags, the Dispatch console and Inspect, the share URL parameters and embed=1, UIx substrate registration, and on the API pages the execution verbs, run results, evidence/hashing and testing primitives, and how to run story-mcp. The Story-to-testing and Story-to-Xray tie-ins are now explicit in chapters 4 and 6.

STEP 2, correctness (commit "docs(story): correctness pass"): 92 findings, 92 accepted, 92 applied, 0 deferred.
Every sample was run on the JVM through throwaway probes against the login testbed.
- Tutorial: the args precedence is global < story < mode < variant < live override; the extends, fragment and compose samples now run; the inheritance table follows the compiler's :merge (decorators REPLACE, script and assertions child-only, checks inherited); compose conflict is :rf.error/story-compose-conflict, and a nested fragment gives :rf.error/fragment-shape; bad step arity gives :rf.error/story-bad-step; wait-until is a one-shot check after settle; dispatched? sees setup too; the share labels drop instead of "warning"; the Docs mode list is labelled Contents.

- ROUTED item: 02's absolute spec/002 URL now points to docs/core/frames.md#what-a-frame-is.
- CI's check_escaped_continuations flagged step 1's run options table at 2 columns. It now nests at 4.
Screenshots: all 9 regenerated with docs/scripts/generate-story-tutorial-screenshots.cjs, against bundles compiled from the rebased tree (lane taken and released per protocol). All were stale: the shell chrome had moved, and 08 now shows the subject text-style reset.

GATES (exit captured in each log): check_doc_slugs 0, with a planted broken anchor giving 1 (restore verified by blob hash); mkdocs build --strict 0, with a planted missing page giving 1 (restore verified by blob hash); check_escaped_continuations 0; check_flattened_lists 0; check_readme_links --ci 0; api-manifest doc-api-check 0 (462 references); check_retired_spellings, check_require_alias_dialect, check_retired_composition_vocab and check_retired_image_keys 0. present_tense census skips docs/story as out of scope; its verify gates heading preservation for rewrite-only PRs, so it does not apply here, and a manual sweep found no bead ids, dates or provenance. title: Claim incomplete: sentinel fallback test accepts a CLJS protocol error instead of the derived-write guard
description:
Audit of merged PR #10642 (6f0a36bc3c7d978a555a79abeb852e02286c7cf2), source rf2-98kzs.9. The retained no-opinion-falls-back-to-atom-marker-heuristic test claims the sentinel fallback rejects a derived container through the library guard on both hosts, but its CLJS assertion cannot establish that claim.

Required correction: strengthen this existing assertion to inspect ex-data and require :rf.error/id :rf.error/derived-container-replaced on both hosts (and, if useful, observe that the adapter write was not reached). Keep the valid base-write assertions. Verify the CLJS row rejects a sentinel-fallback mutation that delegates the derived write. No new public API or additional test namespace is needed.

LESSONS FROM rf2-zbnoc.9-.15 (the core, machines and fresco workers):
- Census for name citations, and for FILE names, before cutting or deleting a file. In machines, every blocked fold was blocked by a filename citation (a spec, a fixture, a workflow comment), and in core a docstring in another file forced a restore.
- Predict from per-case counter rows, not from reading the code: helper assertions count (machines: a helper's own `is`; fresco: assert-clean!'s own pass report).
- Read-only review subagents surface candidates fast, but every candidate still needs reading against its cover before acting.
- Run the lint and `git diff --check` after every batch: deletions leave unused requires, helpers and trailing blank lines.
- A source-grep test can be satisfied by the function's own docstring, so plant the behaviour, not the text.
- The Bash tool halves runs of backslashes even inside quoted heredocs (CLAUDE.md instrument hazard (o)), so write scripts and plant patches with the Write tool.
- Run bd from the worktree root: from the scratchpad it read a different database.
- scripts/check-beads-pr-boundary.sh and scripts/check-commit-attribution.sh fail closed without a base ref; pass origin/main.
- Instrument hazard (v): the classifier takes PATHS. Any plant or probe of it must hand it paths, with a control path known to arm a surface.

LESSONS FROM rf2-zbnoc.1-.8: a negative-control plant shows a test is vacuous; a removal relying on "the higher-level path covers it" needs a plant; read each plant's anchor match count before running, because CRLF files make an anchor match 0.

title: Playground: the first TOC or heading-anchor click after page load may refetch the page and re-run every live cell
description:
## Symptom (read at source, NOT yet measured)

This was found while fixing rf2-r1en5 (PR #10805), by reading mkdocs-material 9.5.44's instant-navigation source through its source map. The theme starts its location stream empty. So the FIRST click after a full page load on a same-page fragment link in the prose counts as a new pathname, the page is fetched again, and every live cell on it re-runs. That covers a table-of-contents entry, a heading permalink, or any `[text](#anchor)`. A reader who edited a cell and then clicked the TOC loses the edit.

PR #10805 fixed the same mechanism for links INSIDE a cell's result area: `keepFragmentLinksInCell` in docs/tools/playground/src/playground.mjs. That fix deliberately leaves prose links alone.

## Want

1. Measure it first, headless against `mkdocs serve`, on a page with a live cell: edit the cell, click a TOC entry, and check whether the page was fetched again. If it does not reproduce, close this bead with the measurement.
2. If it reproduces, fix it in the playground bootstrap, so a same-page fragment link on a page that has live cells scrolls without a refetch. The fix must keep Material's own behaviour: the URL hash updates, the target scrolls into view, the TOC highlight follows, and back/forward work. The rf2-r1en5 worker found that pre-filling Material's location stream breaks the scroll on the first anchor click, so that route is known bad.
3. If only a theme-level change would do (mkdocs.yml, e.g. turning `navigation.instant` off), make NO change. Report the options and their costs to the mayor; that one is Mike's call.

## Verify

Run it headless. Control: with the fix removed, the cell's edit is lost after a TOC click; with it restored, the edit survives and the TOC still works. Blob-hash the restore. The playground's `npm run smoke` stays green.
close_reason:
Reproduced and fixed in PR #10808, in the bootstrap only, with no engine change.

Measured headless against mkdocs serve before the change. On a fresh load of core/views/, after an edit to a cell, the first TOC click re-fetched the page once, replaced the cell's wrapper and lost the edit.
Cause, in Material 9.5.44's instant/index.ts: location$ is a plain Subject, and document$ is location$.pipe(distinctUntilKeyChanged("pathname"), requestHTML ...). So the first emission after a full load always re-fetches, whether it comes from a click or a popstate.

Fix: carryCellsOver in docs/tools/playground/src/playground.mjs. loadPlayground first checks whether the injected page is the one already mounted: the same pathname, the old wrappers detached, and the fresh <pre>s matching the mounted cells by source and kind. If it is, the bootstrap moves the mounted wrappers in place of the fresh <pre>s and skips disposePage and the re-mount. It then redoes Material's scroll rule (the offset saved in history.state, otherwise the hash target), because Material scrolled against the shorter page. The re-fetch still happens on the first same-page navigation, but nothing re-runs.

Rejected route, measured. Stopping the click at the container, before Material's body listener, does work. But the browser's own fragment navigation then fires popstate, and Material's popstate listener on window ran before a capture listener the bootstrap registered later: Material's location emission was logged first. So the re-fetch still happens. Material's first-anchor scroll also comes from the re-fetch, which is why seeding location$ breaks it (rf2-r1en5).

CONTROL:
- With "if (carryCellsOver()) return;" removed, the check exits 1: the edit is lost and the wrapper replaced.
- Restored, it exits 0. The edit survives in the same wrapper node, and the TOC target is in view 68px from the top. The TOC highlight is on the clicked entry, Back restores the earlier fragment at 68px, and a link to another page still navigates instantly with the window state kept.
- core/fresco/03-events-as-data/ also exits 0.
- The restore was checked by blob hash for src/playground.mjs and docs/cljs/playground.js; a fresh build:bootstrap reproduces the committed bundle.
- Smoke: exit 1 with the line removed and exit 0 with it. The new pin checks that a same-page re-injection keeps the cell node and its state.

Not addressed, because it is Material's own theme-level behaviour and the mayor ruled to leave it. In 9.5.44 the first fragment click after ANY page injection does not scroll: that is the second TOC click on a fresh page, or the first click on a page reached by instant navigation. It was measured on a page with no cells too, and behaves the same before and after this change.

title: re-frame-migration: distinguish mechanical M71 input vectors from intent-dependent cases (GH #10811)
description:
M71 is labelled Type B as a whole, while the guided recipe (skills/re-frame-migration/references/guided-interceptors-subs.md) calls its vector case mechanical and then demands author confirmation, so the skill's cardinal rules disagree at a fixed-order vector site. Split M71 the way M42 already is: a fixed-order vector producer is mechanical once its input membership and order, pure dependence on the outer query, absence of state reads, lifecycle and side effects, and value-shape preservation are shown. Map-order choices, app-db-dependent topology and lifecycle/effect ownership stay Type B; classify scalar (bare single signal) and extra-argument cases explicitly; unknown or custom reaction behaviour stays held. Keep the M71 and M75 obligations (metadata move plus runtime materialisation; a compile proves neither) and the batch announcement for genuinely intent-dependent sites. Surfaces: migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md M-71 (HOT ZONE), the guided recipe, SKILL.md cardinal rules/routing. Acceptance: corpus, recipe and skill routing agree per case; the fixed-vector example needs no invented decision; map and state-dependent examples still require a concrete author decision.

Filed from a consumer migration run. The full body, with evidence links and suggested fix, is on the GitHub issue. Close the GH issue when the PR merges (PR body carries `Closes #10811`). Posture: a proportionate clarification of the skill and corpus text, not a rewrite; trust the programmer, don't litigate minutiae.

GH issue: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/issues/10811
notes:
== RESULT (PR #10820, commit "classify M-71 per site") ==
Corpus M-71 type line now: Type A for a vector-returning or single-signal signal fn meeting four conditions (fixed input membership/order from the fn's own code; query vectors from outer query-v + constants only; no state reads, lifecycle or side effects; same values in the same positions to the computation fn), Type B for map return, app-db-dependent topology, a read extra argument, lifecycle/effect/custom-reaction bodies. New corpus cases 5 (extra args: unread dropped, read = Type B) and 6 (lifecycle/effects = Type B, routed like reg-sub-raw); Type-tag summary lists the split on both lines. Guided recipe: cases 1/3 Type A once proven, case 2 Type B, new subsection "Classify each site — the case decides the type" carrying the :example/sum fixed-vector example as needing no author decision. Routing aligned: SKILL.md cardinal rule 2 (classify each site, not the rule), breaking-changes.md index row A/B and both at-a-glance lines, sequencing.md sweep row + batch item, silent-runtime-failures.md row 1. M-75 move + materialized check kept for every site. No gate pins the changed content (three-way phrase search); TYPE-DRIFT pin keeps M-71 on both Type-B lines, red-on-removal control shown in the PR. Issue closes on merge.
close_reason: Merged as PR #10820 (a4a889b6ee); GH #10811 closed by the merge. M-71 is classified per site: a vector-returning or single-signal signal function is Type A once its inputs and order are fixed by its own code, its query vectors use only the outer query and constants, it reads no state and has no lifecycle or effects, and the computation receives the same values in the same positions. Map returns, app-db-dependent inputs, a used extra argument and lifecycle/effect/custom-reaction bodies stay Type B. The corpus M-71 rule, the guided recipe (new 'Classify each site' subsection with the issue's fixed-vector example), SKILL.md cardinal rule 2, breaking-changes.md and sequencing.md agree; check_skill_migration_cites TYPE-DRIFT still pins M-71 on the Type-B line (shown red when removed).

title: M73 codemod: skip reader-discarded #_ forms in scan and rewrite, preserving their bytes (GH #10852)
description:
GitHub #10852. The M73 traversal (~L1389) walks every zipper node, so it descends into #_ reader-discarded forms: #_(rf/reg-event-fx :demo/discarded ...) counts as a finding and is rewritten to rf/reg-event, though the reader retains no active registration. A mixed input (one active plus one discarded) reports two findings and two renames; the active-only control reports one. The census then disagrees with the code the reader keeps, and a preserved inactive form keeps reappearing in every dry run.

Ask: by default skip a reader-discarded subtree in scanning and rewriting, preserving every original byte inside it; the M73 recipe's census refers to ACTIVE registrations; rewriting retained historical examples, if supported at all, is an explicit opt-in.

Acceptance: discarded-only input gives zero active findings and no write; mixed input changes only the active call and counts it once; a discarded Type B shape raises no active author decision; nested discarded containers stay byte-identical; ordinary qualified and bare registrations stay discoverable; comments and newline conventions preserved; verify the filesystem dry-run/write counts as well as the source-string API.

Mayor triage 2026-10-04: valid, action it. The issue carries an executed source-text reproduction at a592708a84 (trunk is a592708a84, no codemod change since), with its own positive control. Fix in the codemod source with codemod tests, and update the M73 recipe and the codemod README to state the behaviour. Clustered with its sibling M73 issue into one worker and one PR. The GitHub issue closes when the PR merges (`Fixes #N` in the body); the mayor closes this bead at merge and verifies the issue reads CLOSED.
notes:
== RESULT (worker, PR #10854, commit 15a172f34f on worker/m73codemod) ==
Fixed in the codemod: the walk skips a `#_` subtree whole (any depth, stacked `#_ #_` included), returning its bytes untouched, and `sig-children` drops `#_` children so a site's own analysis reads past a discarded middle slot or handler form as the reader does. Findings and the filesystem dry-run/write counts cover active registrations only. No opt-in to rewrite discarded source; no separate inactive-source report (both stated in the recipe and README).
Acceptance met by reg_event_codemod_test.clj: `discarded-forms-not-scanned-or-rewritten` (discarded only -> zero findings, byte-identical; active beside discarded -> one :rename, comments kept; discarded Type B (ctx, custom interceptor + nil-capable db) -> no finding; nested and stacked discards -> byte-identical; discarded slot inside an active call; bare + qualified active sites beside discards; each row checks scan-string AND rewrite-string), `write-keeps-line-endings` discarded source (LF+CRLF byte-identical, CLI dry run `4 file(s) would change (dry run); summary: {:total 6, :rewrite 0, :rename 4, :flag 2}`, write `4 file(s) rewritten`).
Controls: commit-2 tests vs commit-1 source overlay -> exit 1, 22 failures, all discard rows; removing only the walk skip -> 19 failures; removing only the sig-children #_ filter -> 3 failures (in-call discard row); green at head. Issue repro at base: discarded-only scan 1 finding and rewritten; mixed 2 findings/2 renames. At head: 0 findings and byte-identical; mixed 1 finding/1 rename with the discarded form verbatim.
Gates: clojure -M:test 61 tests / 324 assertions exit 0; clj-kondo v2026.04.15 0 errors; doc gates exit 0.

Tests: discarded-forms-not-scanned-or-rewritten (6 rows, each checking scan and rewrite); write-keeps-line-endings gained a discarded source plus a CLI dry-run check reading "4 file(s) would change (dry run); summary: {:total 6, :rewrite 0, :rename 4, :flag 2}" and the write count. title: Fresco codemod fixer: refuse r/as-element inside a #(...) anonymous fn in a foreign prop (same list-only blind spot as #10943)
description:
Reported by the rf2-cy0xy worker on PR #10945 (merged at e5efe4f1a7), and checked at source.

Defect: the reagent-to-fresco FIXER's refusal walk has the same list-only blind spot that #10943 fixed in the census. `[:> Foo {:x #(r/as-element [:div])}]` gets no `:as-element-island` refusal, while `(fn [] (r/as-element [:div]))` in the same position does. The cause is that the refusal walk uses `bound-call?` in migration/reagent-to-fresco/codemod/src/re_frame/migration/fresco/rewrite.clj (about L648), which accepts only list nodes. A `#(...)` reader fn is a `:fn` node whose children are the body's items, with no list around them.

#10945 added `rewrite/call-form`, `(if (tag= nd :fn) (n/list-node (n/children nd)) nd)`, which reads a `#(...)` node as the call it writes. It applied it to `inert?` and the census, and deliberately left `head-symbol` and `bound-call?` untouched, because the fixer's SITE and adapt-def detection must not treat `[#(r/adapt-react-class X) ...]` as an adapt site.

Ask: apply `call-form` in the fixer's REFUSAL walk only, wherever it asks whether a value position holds a refused call (`r/as-element` and any sibling refusals that read through `bound-call?`). Leave site and adapt-def detection unchanged. Tests, red at base: `#(r/as-element [:div])` in a foreign prop is refused exactly like the expanded `fn` form; `#(quote (r/as-element ...))` and `#(comment ...)` are not refused, because they are inert; `[#(r/adapt-react-class X) ...]` is still not an adapt site. Show the fixer's corpus output byte-identical apart from the newly refused sites, and list them. JVM-only (the codemod's own clojure -M:test). Mayor-filed 2026-10-05.

title: xray: two comments still call the <html> width write a host write, and 011 misstates which cascade override beats a persisted drag width
description:
Follow-up to rf2-b37ch (PR #10981), found by its worker. Its fence left these out.

STALE AT TIP. Each still describes Xray's <html> width write as a write to the host:
- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/registry.cljs comments, about L586-593;
- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/shell.cljs comment, about L3282.
apply-panel-width! writes --rf-xray-inline-width only on <html>, never on the host element. resize_handle_dom_cljs_test.cljs pins that.

WRONG CLAIM. tools/xray/spec/011-Launch-Modes.md §User-draggable resize says a reload restores the persisted width "unless a fresh override up the cascade has shifted the default". For a :root override that is false: the inline value Xray writes on <html> outranks a stylesheet declaration on :root. Only a declaration on an element below <html> (the host itself, for example) beats it, and then the drag cannot move that width. PR #10981's xray.md says this in its added sentence.

ASK. Make the two comments present-tense true (comment-only, no code change), and correct 011's sentence to the actual cascade behaviour. Small; P4.
notes:
== RESULT (worker xrayfollow, 2026-10-06 AUSEST): PR #10982, one commit b2d320245b on trunk 4ba53943ca. Comment and prose only.

Verified at source: apply-panel-width! (settings/effects.cljs) calls .setProperty on <html> only for a non-default clamped width and .removeProperty on <html> for the default; it never writes the host element. Cascade rule, cited: CSS Cascade 5 §6.1 ranks Element-Attached Styles (style attribute) above Specificity, and :root matches <html> (Selectors 4), so the inline <html> value beats a normal :root rule; custom properties inherit (Custom Properties 1 §2), and Cascade 5 §7 / §7.2 use the inherited value only when the element's own cascade yields none, so a declaration on the host or an ancestor below <html> wins for that subtree.

registry.cljs :rf.xray/set-panel-width-px comment. OLD: "AND applies the CSS var to the host immediately via `settings-effects/apply-panel-width!`." NEW: "AND sets the CSS var on `<html>` immediately via `settings-effects/apply-panel-width!`, and the host inherits it from there."

011-Launch-Modes.md §User-draggable resize. OLD: "reload restores the persisted width unless a fresh `--rf-xray-inline-width` override up the cascade has shifted the default." NEW: "a reload restores the persisted width. A `:root` override does not shift that width, because Xray's inline value on `<html>` outranks a stylesheet declaration on the same element; a declaration on the host itself, or on any ancestor of it below `<html>`, does beat the drag, and the handle then cannot move that width."

title: api-manifest generator accepts a misspelt tier or blank owner/status, silently dropping the var from docs coverage
description:
## Bug

The API manifest generator copies each var's curated `:tier`, `:owner` and `:status` from `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn` without checking them. A misspelt tier, a blank owner or a missing status therefore regenerates cleanly, and `--check` then agrees with the regenerated file. A misspelt tier also silently removes the var from the `docs/api/` coverage check, which selects four exact tiers.

## Evidence

All file:line references are at trunk 475bdcaacf (unchanged at b375cd0e42).

- `implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/gen.clj`:
  - `build-rows` (`:844-886`) copies `(:tier c)`, `(:owner c)` and `(:status c)` straight through, for JVM rows (`:852-860`) and for `:cljs-only` rows (`:867-883`).
  - `build-manifest` (`:993-1107`) refuses missing, stale, duplicate, implementation-facade, unjustified-facade and bad-action rows. It never inspects tier, owner or status.
  - `:tier-vocab` (`:1103-1105`) is emitted metadata. Nothing validates against it; the only other tier set in the tooling is `doc_api_check`'s coverage filter.
- `doc_api_check.clj:157-161`: `eligible-tiers` is `#{:front-porch :advanced :adapter :testing}`. It decides which vars must have a `docs/api/` page and member heading (`:263-277`).
- Repro (*probed*, JVM, from `implementation/scripts/api-manifest`):

  ```clojure
  (let [sidecar (gen/read-sidecar)
        k       ["re-frame.core" "dispatch"]
        bad     (update-in sidecar [:classification k] assoc :tier :front-proch :owner "" :status nil)]
    (gen/build-manifest bad))
  ;; returns normally; the emitted row is
  ;; {:namespace "re-frame.core" :var "dispatch" :tier :front-proch :owner "" :status nil}
  ;; and (contains? #{:front-porch :advanced :adapter :testing} :front-proch) => false
  ```

- The safety net is partial. `api_md_check` would catch a tier mismatch only for a var that has a `spec/API.md` var row, and 314 of the 488 manifest rows have none (*probed*).
- Trunk is clean (*probed*): 0 rows with a tier outside the vocabulary, 0 blank owners, 0 blank statuses. A new refusal reds nothing today.

## Expected

Generation and `--check` refuse a row whose tier is outside the closed vocabulary, or whose owner or status is blank or absent. The error names each `namespace/var`.

## Fix direction

- Define the tier vocabulary once in `gen.clj` and use it for both the emitted `:tier-vocab` and a new `build-manifest` refusal, which covers JVM-derived and `:cljs-only` rows alike.
- Require only a non-blank status. Status is free text such as `"v1 (preserved + extended)"`.
- Optionally, point `api_md_check`'s `tier-tokens` at the same definition.

## Acceptance

- `gen_test`: `build-manifest` throws, naming the pair, for each of:
  - one misspelt tier;
  - a blank owner;
  - a nil status;
  - the same faults on a `:cljs-only` row.
- `clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen --check` stays green on trunk.

## Notes

- **Origin:** Sol review (surface 35, insight 1), adopted by the Opus tooling cross-review (D10, action 2c).
- **Related:** rf2-mn2ht.58 and rf2-mn2ht.59 are in the same artefact, with no file overlap.
- **Hot-zone files:** none. Neither the generated `spec/api-manifest.edn` nor the sidecar changes, because trunk carries no invalid rows.
- **Supporting detail:** `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/tooling.md` §D10; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/35-api-manifest-spec-resource.md` §1.
notes:
== WORKER SUMMARY (2026-10-10, PR #11083, commit 48ac2f61db) ==
FIXED. The premise held at the branch base (753addc602): build-manifest graded no tier, owner or status. Live: 486 rows, 0 tiers outside the vocabulary, 0 blank owners/statuses, and every owner and status is a String, so the new refusal reds nothing on trunk.

Fix (gen.clj):
- `tier-vocab` defines the closed tier vocabulary once. `:meta :tier-vocab` emits it, so the regenerated manifest is byte-identical and `gen --check` stays OK.

title: Classification: index-free matching rides a :map-of key as the durable walker does (land parked d3c23bfe55, re-pin the epoch precision test, keep the machine SSR :data anchor, state the rule in Spec 015)
description:
Found by the rf2-mn2ht.48 worker and probed at that branch's tip (PR #11056, merged at d5e10f5d4b). A CLAIM to re-check at tip.

DEFECT: re-frame.classification/redact-with-paths (implementation/core/src/re_frame/classification.cljc) can skip a collection INDEX ({:index-free? true}) but has no way to skip a :map-of KEY. The schemas walker reports a mark under a :map-of value at the path WITHOUT the key, so the mark never matches the data.

REPRO (probed): an HTTP decode schema [:map [:accounts [:map-of :string [:map [:id :int] [:token {:sensitive? true} :string]]]]]. The walker marks {[:accounts :token]}; schema-has-opaque-child? is false; the off-box disposition is :classify; classify-decoded leaves {:accounts {"a" {:id 1 :token "SECRET"}}} unredacted. Control: a [:set [:map ...]] element mark does redact.

REACH: every caller that feeds walker marks to redact-with-paths: HTTP's classify-decoded; probably resources' classification (which already passes :index-free?) and SSR's machine-snapshot projection (rf2-mn2ht.50 is changing that call site now; check after it merges). Probe each before claiming it.

DIRECTION (smallest): let the matcher treat a :map-of value position as a wildcard key, in the same way :index-free? treats a vector index. The walker would need to tell it where a :map-of sits (for example a marker segment in the path), or the matcher accepts any key at that depth. Alternatively, fail closed: the walker reports a mark under :map-of as opaque, so HTTP stamps :omit. Fail-closed is the smaller change if the matcher change spreads.

ACCEPTANCE: the repro's token is redacted on the off-box trace (or the body is omitted), red at base and red again with the fix reverted; the :set control still redacts; no other redaction changes.

Fence when dispatched: implementation/core classification.cljc is core; check which core files are in flight first. Not a hot zone unless spec/015 needs a row (not hot).
notes:
== A SECOND CALLER WITH THE SAME GAP (mayor, 2026-10-10 20:15 AUSEST) == From the rf2-mn2ht.50 worker (PR #11062, merged at b8ba6dc98f): SSR's machine-snapshot hydration projection now passes {:index-free? true} to redact-with-paths, which closes vectors but not keyed collections. Example: a machine :data {:by-id {"a" {:token ...}}} with the declaration [:data :by-id :token] still ships the token in the hydration payload while the trace redacts it. That is this bead's map-key matching gap, reached through SSR. When this bead is fixed, fix it at the shared matcher (or fail closed in the walker) so HTTP, resources and SSR all pick it up, and add an SSR row to the Acceptance. The .50 bead's own primary direction (route the snapshot through elide-wire-value) is the alternative for SSR alone.
== WORKER: NOT FIXED. The shared-matcher key skip breaks a pinned precision property, so this needs a ruling (classif-mapof worker, 2026-10-10 21:07 AUSEST, trunk a8b1edb553) ==

PREMISE HOLDS AT TIP. For the decode schema [:map [:accounts [:map-of :string [:map [:id :int] [:token {:sensitive? true} :string]]]]] the walker marks [[:accounts :token]], and (redact-with-paths v marks [] {:index-free? true}) leaves {:accounts {"a" {:id 1 :token "SECRET-A"}}} unredacted. The SSR reach holds too: a spawned machine declaring :sensitive [[:data :by-id :token]] with :data {:by-id {"a" {...}}} ships both tokens through re-frame.ssr.payload-policy/project-runtime-db, while elide-wire-value (the trace's durable walker) redacts them. The [:set [:map ...]] control redacts.

WHAT WAS TRIED: the mayor's direction. In :index-free? mode a candidate already inside a declaration also rides a map key unchanged; this is re-frame.elision's fork-decl-paths device, and the empty root candidate never skips. The acceptance test (4 tests, 9 assertions: HTTP repro, set control, exact-mode and root-float controls, SSR by-id row) ran red at base (exit 1, 4 failures), green with the fix (exit 0), and red again with the src alone reverted (exit 1); the restore matched the committed blob. JVM lanes with the fix: core 0 (1232 tests), schemas 0, http 0, resources 0, ssr 0, machines 0, core prod gate 0, and EPOCH 1. The epoch failure is re-frame.epoch-egress-resource-trace-test/fx-carrier-index-free-fork-does-not-reach-an-undeclared-nested-slot. It pins that a feed's [:data :email] redacts each item's :email but leaves an :email one NAMED slot deeper alone: item {:email .. :meta {:email nested}} must keep :meta :email. A matcher that cannot tell a :map-of key from a named slot has to ride every key, so it reaches :meta :email. That breaks the pin, and it breaks this bead's own acceptance clause "no other redaction changes".

WHY NO SMALLER VARIANT EXISTS:
- A walker marker segment (the walker writes [:accounts <any-key> :token]) is precise. But it changes the {path declaration} output of re-frame.schemas/extract-sensitive-paths-from-schema, an implementation-tier fn whose shape spec/010 section Walker documents and which schemas validation redaction, HTTP, resource params marks and Story all read. It also cannot reach SSR, because machine :sensitive declarations are written by hand and never pass through the walker.
- A data heuristic (skip only non-keyword keys, or only in a map lacking the next declared slot) is fragile, and it makes the result depend on which sibling keys happen to be present.

OPTIONS FOR A RULING:
(1) Accept the blanket key skip in :index-free? mode and re-pin the epoch test. That over-redacts a same-named nested slot (the safe direction), and it matches re-frame.elision's durable walker. The fix and its acceptance test are parked on origin branch worker/classif-mapof-keyskip, commit d3c23bfe55.
(2) A walker marker for schema-derived marks (HTTP, resource params), plus SSR handled separately by rf2-mn2ht.50's own alternative: route the snapshot :data through elide-wire-value in implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/ssr.cljc.
(3) Make the key skip an opt-in beside :index-free?, and have HTTP's classify-decoded and machines SSR opt in. Those files belong to other owners.

SIDE FINDING: a ROOT-level :map-of decode ([:map-of :string [:map [:token {:sensitive? true} :string]]], mark [:token]) stays unredacted under options (1) and (3), because the root candidate never skips a key. Only a marker reaches it.

PR #11075 does not carry this bead. It stays open pending the ruling.
== [MIKE DECISION] HELD (mayor, 2026-10-10 21:05 AUSEST) == The defect is real at tip, confirmed by the classif-mapof worker. The mayor's chosen fix, a key skip in the shared matcher, works: red at base exit 1 (4 failures), green exit 0, and red again exit 1 with the fix alone reverted. It is parked, unmerged, on branch worker/classif-mapof-keyskip at d3c23bfe55, pushed to origin. Do NOT delete that branch.

Why it is held: it also turns one deliberately pinned epoch test red, re-frame.epoch-egress-resource-trace-test/fx-carrier-index-free-fork-does-not-reach-an-undeclared-nested-slot. That test pins that a declaration [:data :email] redacts each feed item's :email but NOT an :email one named slot deeper. The matcher cannot tell a :map-of key from a named slot, so a key skip also reaches the deeper :email (over-redaction). That changes what a path declaration means, which is a semantics call, not a mechanical fix.

OPTIONS:
1. Accept the key skip, and re-pin the epoch test to the new, wider meaning. This is the smallest change and fails safe: it can only over-redact. Cost: a same-named key one level deeper also redacts. An HTTP decode schema whose ROOT is a :map-of stays unredacted.
2. Precise. The walker marks where a :map-of sits, so the matcher skips exactly those keys. SSR is fixed separately by routing the machine snapshot through elide-wire-value in machines/ssr.cljc, which was rf2-mn2ht.50's own primary direction, because hand-written machine declarations never pass through the walker. Cost: it changes the walker's output, which spec/010 documents and four other consumers read. Larger. It touches the same walker-completeness area as rf2-mn2ht.49 (also yours).
3. An opt-in key skip, with HTTP and machines SSR opting in. This adds a mode, which the posture argues against.

MAYOR'S RECOMMENDATION: option 1. It closes the leak with one small change, it fails safe, and it matches the fail-closed direction already taken for opaque schemas (rf2-mn2ht.48, rf2-ulu3a). Option 2 is the masterpiece-grade answer if declaration precision matters more than the size of the change. If you choose option 2, it is worth deciding together with rf2-mn2ht.49.

On a ruling: dispatch from the parked branch for option 1, or fresh for option 2. Strike this marker in the same words when discharged.
== RULING (delegated by Mike; decided 2026-10-10 23:50:42 AUSEST at HEAD 200a67df2d) ==

DECISION: Option 1, amended. In `:index-free?` mode, `re-frame.classification/redact-with-paths` lets a candidate that has already matched at least one declared segment ride a map key unchanged; the empty root candidate never does. That is exactly the `re-frame.elision/fork-decl-paths` rule the durable trace walker already applies to every declaration. Land the parked fix (`d3c23bfe55`), deliberately re-pin the epoch precision test to the wider meaning, make the machine SSR projector keep its `:data` anchor so a `:data` keyed at its root matches as the durable walker does, and state the matching rule once in Spec 015 (plus a `:map-of` clause in Spec 014 rule 1). Keyed collections with NO named anchor before them (a root `:map-of` HTTP decode, a root-keyed `:params-schema`) and resources' anchor-stripped data walks go to the new follow-up rf2-mn2ht.72, which fails closed where no anchor exists and keeps the anchor where one does.

WHY:
- One meaning everywhere. `elide-wire-value` already reads every declaration this way, on every trace and tool egress of app-db, runtime-db and machine snapshots: `fork-decl-paths` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc:879-916`) is called unconditionally (`:1068`, `:1155`). So option 1 adds no new meaning. It brings the index-free carriers (HTTP decoded body, machine SSR hydration, resources replies / params / keys / sub projections, epoch's recorded-registry pass) into line with the meaning durable entries already have. A programmer learns one rule for what `[:x :y]` reaches.
- The pinned precision is carrier-only, and its durable twin already contradicts it. For the enveloped `:declared/feed`, the durable walker reaches `[:data <page> :items <item> :email]` only by riding the `:items` key, and that same ride reaches `:meta :email`. The pin therefore protects a disagreement between a durable entry and its continuation echo, which is the disagreement rf2-zaopo set out to remove. Any fix for keyed resource `:data` has to ride keys, so the pin could not survive a resources fix anyway.
- It fails safe. The worst case of option 1 is a predictable, documented over-redaction; the worst case today is a declared secret shipped silently under a `:classify` stamp.
- The cost is accepted explicitly, not waved away. Once a declaration's leading segment has matched, a same-named slot nested under an intermediate map also matches. That applies to `:large` as well as `:sensitive`, and in SSR hydration it can blank data the hydrated client would otherwise receive (a machine `[:data :user :email]` also blanks `[:data :user :manager :email]`). The remedy is a documented rule the programmer can reason about (Spec 015), not "rename your field". Trusting the programmer means giving them one clear rule.
- Smallest. The code is written, verified red/green/red, and applies cleanly to HEAD. The SSR anchor is a one-function change, and without it the same declaration redacts on the trace but ships in hydration.

REJECTED:
- Option 2 (the walker writes a marker segment where a `:map-of` sits; SSR routes through `elide-wire-value`): precise only for schema-derived marks. Hand-written resource and machine declarations never pass through the walker, so they still need the key ride or a new wildcard grammar, which rf2-zaopo declined. It also changes the walker's `{path declaration}` output, which four consumers and Spec 010 §Walker read. Too much machinery to protect one visibility nicety. Revisit only if an app demonstrably needs the precision; the route then is to preserve schema collection coordinates internally.
- Option 3 (an opt-in key skip; HTTP and machines SSR opt in): adds a mode to a core primitive, so every future caller has to choose. Resources replies would keep leaking keyed `:data` while their durable entry redacts it, and the epoch pin would stay green only because of that leak. The day resources are fixed, it becomes option 1 with a flag.
- Change nothing / document: a silent leak of a declared secret under `:classify`. It contradicts the natural reading of Spec 014 rule 1 and Spec 015's rule that hydration slices are projected as the registry projects them.
- Dropping the root guard in index-free mode (raised in this ruling, since it would close the root cases with no per-caller change): it turns declarations into name-matching at any depth (`[:email]` would redact every `:email` anywhere), diverges from the durable walker, and contradicts Spec 015's "classification covers exactly the paths and payload shapes you declare". Both reviews keep the guard; the probe's root-guard row pins it.
- Folding the no-anchor fail-closed cases into this bead's acceptance (Codex's preference): it is a different mechanism (the walker's completeness answer, plus anchoring in resources' own walks), it touches files other workers own and the completeness area rf2-mn2ht.49 also touches, and the resources part is unprobed. A separate bead keeps this worker on the parked branch and lets both move.

WHERE THE REVIEWS AGREED / DISAGREED:
- Agreed (mayor, dossier author, Codex): option 1; no wildcard grammar; no new mode; the root guard stays; the epoch re-pin is an intentional policy change; the HTTP root `:map-of` case is real and should fail closed.
- Codex added four points, all accepted. (a) The machine SSR projector strips the `:data` anchor, so a machine whose `:data` is keyed at its root still leaks after the parked fix; this ruling's probe confirms it (rows "SSR stripped" and "SSR anchored" below). (b) The fork serves `:large` too; probed and accepted, and it gets an acceptance row. (c) The over-redaction reaches SSR hydration data, not only tool visibility; accepted. (d) Document the behaviour in Spec 015 as conservative collection matching rather than offering "rename the field"; accepted.
- Disagreed on one point. Codex wanted root-shaped HTTP and invalid-params fail-closed inside this repair's acceptance; the dossier author proposed a follow-up bead. Ruled: follow-up bead (rf2-mn2ht.72), extended with resources' anchor-stripped walks, which this ruling found while checking the root guard's reach.
- One dossier fact is stale at this HEAD: "neither file it touches has changed since its base". `classification.cljc` moved once, in `45960a05c8` (marker idempotence in `large-marker`; a new `project-sub-value`). Those regions are unrelated: `git apply --check` of `git diff a8b1edb553 d3c23bfe55` against HEAD 200a67df2d exits 0, every hunk applying at offset +6.

It calls `(redact-with-paths v s l {:index-free? true})` at HEAD, then `load-file`s `d3c23bfe55`'s `classification.cljc` over the live namespace and reruns. HEAD result, then parked result:

Any index-free caller that strips the leading declared segment before walking puts a keyed collection at the walk's root, where the guard stops the ride. Machine SSR is fixed here. Resources' data-relative walks are rf2-mn2ht.72. Depends on / feeds: discovered from rf2-fn0kx.7 (closed, PR #10149) finding 5 and rf2-fn0kx.9 (closed, PR #10152) finding 7 / held item 2. Gates nothing; unlocks one cross-twin PR.

## The decision in one sentence

Both RealWorld flagships declare a deployment sub-path on the router (`with-base-path … "/realworld"` and `"/realworld-resources"`) that nothing in the repo serves, while their host pages pin `<base href="/">`; rule whether they are ORIGIN-ROOT apps (A: drop the combinator and the sub-path prose in both twins) or SUB-PATH apps (B: set `<base href="/realworld/">` / `"/realworld-resources/"` and make the dev runner mount them there).

## The problem, carefully

**What each twin declares today (all at trunk 155ff6871c).**

- Host pages: `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/index.html:13` and `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/index.html:13` both read `<base href="/">`, under a comment (`:5-12`) explaining that Conduit routes three segments deep, so relative asset URLs must resolve against `/` or a refresh on `/profile/bob/favorites` loads no stylesheet and no `main.js`.
- Routers: `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/routing.cljs:253-254` — `(def url-strategy (rf.routing/with-base-path rf.routing/history-url-strategy "/realworld"))`; `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/routing.cljs:366-367` — the same with `"/realworld-resources"`. Each is handed to the URL-owning frame as `:url-strategy routing/url-strategy` (`realworld_http/core.cljs:417`, `realworld_resources/core.cljs:407`).
- Prose that asserts a sub-path is real: the http twin's namespace docstring says "this example is served from a sub-path" (`realworld_http/routing.cljs:18-20`); its frame comment says "the orchestrator serves this example under `/realworld/`" (`realworld_http/core.cljs:361-362`) — the same false claim PR #10152 removed from the resources twin (`realworld_resources/core.cljs:383-386` now says the repo's own runner serves one build at the server ROOT). The resources wiring block still says "Each entry is served from its OWN deployment sub-path … `core.cljs` … mounts under `/realworld-resources`" (`realworld_resources/routing.cljs:352-365`), and the http block hedges to "might be served from a sub-path" (`realworld_http/routing.cljs:242-244`).
- The rule the pair breaks is stated by two other examples' host pages and by the docs: "Under a sub-path deployment this becomes `<base href="/my-app/">`, with `rf.routing/with-base-path` on the frame's `:url-strategy` so the two agree" (`examples/capabilities/routing/routing/index.html:12-13`, `examples/capabilities/resources/resources/index.html:13-14`, `docs/core/fresco/07-routing-and-navigation.md:426-429`). The twins have one line from each half of that recipe.

**How the twins are actually served (measured by reading the runner).**

- The only runner is `npm run dev:example -- <build-id>` (`implementation/package.json:54` → `examples/scripts/serve-example.cjs`; both READMEs say so, `realworld_http/README.md:83`, `realworld_resources/README.md:204`; `examples/README.md:18`). It stages ONE build's `index.html` + `examples/_shared/` into that build's `:output-dir` (`examples/scripts/examples-staging.cjs:211-219`; `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1787-1791` and `:1801-1805`, both `:asset-path "."`), then serves that directory as the server ROOT on `http://127.0.0.1:PORT/` (`serve-example.cjs:496-510`, banner at `:549-551`). The URL it prints ends at `/`. Nothing mounts either build at a prefix: ripgrep `realworld|basePath|base path|prefix` over `examples/scripts/` hits only a comment in `serve-example.cjs:229`, avatar-staging comments (`examples-staging.cjs:86`, `examples-asset-manifest.cjs:98-117`) and — the control — `serve-and-run-story-play-scripts.cjs:579 basePathFor(testbed)`, which DOES mount Story testbeds under base paths, so a prefixed mount is a thing this scripts tree knows how to do and neither RealWorld build is on that roster. shadow-cljs's own `:dev-http` map serves Xray/Story testbeds only (`implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:541-560`; `examples/README.md:23` names the three example builds that have one — RealWorld is not among them).
- Behind the static server sits a history-route DOCUMENT FALLBACK (`serve-example.cjs:225-316`, wired at `:483-486` and `:506-509`): a GET that accepts `text/html` and names no file extension gets the staged `index.html` with 200; everything else 404s (`isDocumentNavigationRequest`, `:264-270`).

**Why the mismatch has not bitten locally — the combinator fails safe on ingress and always prefixes on egress.** From `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/strategy.cljc`: `strip-base-path` returns a URL unchanged when it is not under the base (`:260-281`, "fails safe rather than mis-slicing"); the wrapped `:encode` unconditionally prepends the base (`:373`); a blank base returns the inner strategy untouched (`:362-364`). I confirmed this with a JVM probe from `implementation/routing` (`clojure -M -e …`, exit 0):

```clojure
{:encode-profile      "/realworld/profile/bob"   ; (:encode w) "/profile/bob"
 :encode-root         "/realworld/"              ; (:encode w) "/"
 :strip-root          "/"                        ; strip "/realworld" from "/"           → unchanged
 :strip-unprefixed    "/profile/bob"             ; strip from "/profile/bob"             → unchanged
 :strip-prefixed      "/profile/bob"             ; strip from "/realworld/profile/bob"
 :strip-sibling       "/realworld-resources/profile/bob" ; prefix-sharing sibling: untouched
 :blank-base-encode   "/profile/bob"             ; with-base-path … ""  → no prefix
 :blank-base-is-inner true}                      ; … and it IS history-url-strategy
```

So the app boots at `/`, and the first in-app navigation writes `/realworld/…` into the address bar; the dev fallback then answers a reload of that URL with the host page, and `<base href="/">` still finds `main.js` at `/main.js`. ## Codex Recommendation

**Recommend A: make origin-root deployment the deliberate convention for both RealWorld examples.** Keep `<base href="/">`, use the default history URL strategy, and remove the subpath wrappers and contradictory explanations together. This is a recommendation for Mike's ruling, not an implementation authorization or a recorded decision.

I independently inspected source revision `155ff6871c341637081bdf4024715ff039e81214` and read the live `rf2-67vjf` record. The runner, HTML and build configuration already agree about where assets live. Both HTML files set the root base (`examples/real-apps/realworld_http/index.html:13` and `realworld_resources/index.html:13`); the builds use relative `:asset-path "."` (`implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1787–1805`). `examples/scripts/examples-staging.cjs:211–218` copies the host page, shared assets and declared avatar into the selected output directory. `serve-example.cjs:483–509` serves that directory as the HTTP root, and its advertised URL ends at `/` (`:549–550`). Neither build name is a URL mount directive. The adapter orchestrator does serve a shared parent directory, but its actual roster is the Reagent and UIx adapter testbeds (`implementation/adapters/scripts/adapter-smoke-filter.cjs:77–87`); it does not establish the RealWorld mounting claim in the HTTP example's `core.cljs:361–367`.

**The mismatch is real, but it does not establish that today's examples cannot navigate.** The current strategies (`realworld_http/routing.cljs:254`, `realworld_resources/routing.cljs:367`) always prefix outgoing hrefs, while `strip-base-path` deliberately leaves unrelated incoming paths unchanged (`implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/strategy.cljc:260–281,362–389`). Thus an initial `/` can become `/realworld/profile/bob/favorites` after navigation, with assets still fetched from `/`. The resources example's comment that root ingress works is accurate but incomplete: accepting root ingress does not make its outgoing URLs root based.

Two bounded controls substantiate that distinction. First, I evaluated the production history encoder and base-path functions with controlled incoming URLs: both configured prefixes emitted prefixed profile URLs; `/`, unprefixed profile URLs, and the corresponding prefixed URLs decoded as expected. A prefix-sharing sibling stayed unchanged, and an empty-base control emitted the unprefixed URL. Second, I staged each real host page and assets into a private temporary directory using the production staging helper, added an explicitly synthetic `main.js`, and served it through the same HTTP-server harness and document fallback used by the runner. For both examples, `/`, an unprefixed deep route and its prefixed counterpart returned the real HTML with status 200. Root script, stylesheet and avatar requests returned 200; prefixed script requests and a missing-script control returned 404. The runner's HTML fallback explains why prefixed deep links can work without a genuine subpath asset mount. Merely changing `<base>` to the configured prefix would instead request the script path that returned 404. These were source-function and HTTP/asset measurements, not a compiled-app or browser result.

Root deployment is the smallest coherent teaching example. Subpath deployment is a legitimate application requirement, but choosing it here would also require deliberate mounting/staging and advertised-URL behavior, plus verification that HTML, routes and assets share the same base. A runtime base detector or configurable runner extension adds machinery without a demonstrated requirement. The framework already demonstrates subpath configuration in the routing example (`examples/capabilities/routing/routing/index.html:12–14`); these flagship examples can focus on their HTTP/resources comparison.

After a ruling, make one coordinated correction: remove each frame's explicit `:url-strategy routing/url-strategy` and its now-unused wrapper/require, retain `:url-bound? true`, and update the routing/core explanations and any affected launch instructions. Keep the root HTML bases and current server behavior. Verify each app by opening `/`, following a profile/article link, changing a query, using Back/Forward, and directly reloading a deep route; confirm script, stylesheet and fallback avatar requests still resolve. Keep that verification within the existing policy that examples remain test-free.

The meaningful compatibility cost is that previously generated prefixed bookmarks would no longer be normal app routes. For these pre-alpha local examples I would accept that without a compatibility layer. Evidence of an actively supported deployment or published links depending on the prefixes would change the migration plan and could justify B. This review did not compile either app, run its browser UI, inspect an external deployment, or validate arbitrary production-server rewrite rules; the bounded results do not make those claims.

The implementation scope also includes an existing consumer outside `examples/`: `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_resources_cljs_test.cljs:2306–2314` directly uses `app-routing/url-strategy` and expects `/realworld-resources/login`. I independently re-read that test at the same revision. Removing the example's strategy variable requires addressing this reference in the same change. Under A, retire this specific mount assertion and its now-obsolete explanatory block (`:2286–2304`), while retaining the routing library's general base-path coverage. Include compilation/execution of the affected existing test namespace in verification; checking only the example builds would miss this consumer. This adds one test-file adjustment to A's scope and does not change the recommendation or require a new example test suite.
