description:
Filed from the review wave under epic rf2-fn0kx (report patterns.md). The report below is the reviewer's, verbatim.

## Project stance (verbatim, from CLAUDE.md)

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every
> last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.

## Worker rules

- Every path:line below was read at the FROZEN review tree named in the report header. Re-verify each cite at the current trunk before editing; the review wave's earlier beads found premises that had moved.
- Act on the findings under the stance: a finding you would not spend a morning on yourself is not one to implement. Where a finding says "decide: A or B", it is Mike's call; hold it and say so in the PR body rather than choosing.
- Fences are full repo-relative paths. Hot-zone files (CLAUDE.md § Workflow) are sequential; if a finding lands in one, say so and wait for the mayor's sequencing.
- The shadow-cljs build lane is a machine-wide exclusive granted by the mayor: ask before any build, and prefer static checks and the JVM lanes.
- Examples stay test-free (rf2-8cevm). Skills gates live in scripts/check_skill_*.py; run the ones that name your surface and say which.
- No AI attribution trailers; the PR body carries a "## Quality gates" section naming what ran and its exit codes.

---

# Senior review: examples/patterns (boot, long_running_work, nine_states, websocket)

Reviewer persona: read-only senior reviewer on the pattern-spec fidelity axis — is each example a faithful, current rendering of its `spec/Pattern-*.md`, with every promised state, transition, failure and cancellation path reachable and wired.
Tree: skills-review-sep21 worktree, trunk b60a20abca
Scope read: all 25 tracked files under `examples/patterns/` (`git ls-files examples/patterns`), 6086 lines — every `.cljs`, every `index.html` / `stories.index.html`, every README, read in full; plus `examples/README.md` and `examples/TESTING.md`.
Surfaces the examples teach, consulted: `spec/Pattern-Boot.md`, `spec/Pattern-LongRunningWork.md`, `spec/Pattern-NineStates.md`, `spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md`, `spec/Pattern-StaleDetection.md` (each end to end); `spec/005-StateMachines.md` §Declarative `:spawn` / §Spawn-and-join via `:spawn-all` / §Final states / §Synthetic creation marker (targeted); `docs/machines/examples.md` rows; `skills/re-frame2/examples-map.md` rows; `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_reg_view_macro.cljc` (how `reg-view` binds `dispatch`), `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/test_support.cljc` (canned stubs, `:after-ms`), `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` (the five build defs + preloads), `examples/scripts/examples-staging.cjs` + `serve-example.cjs` (which host page a build stages), `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/{preload,mount,keybinding}.cljs`, `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/xray_embed.cljs`, `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/boot_cljs_test.cljs` (targeted).
Checks run: `node implementation/scripts/check-examples-compile.cjs --list` → exit 0, 58 entries, all five slice ids present (`examples/boot`, `examples/long-running-work`, `examples/nine-states`, `examples/nine-states-with-stories`, `examples/websocket`); `node examples/scripts/check-examples-assets.cjs` → exit 0, 33 host pages clean (scanner verified static: 0 `child_process`/`http`/`fetch` references before running); `diff examples/core/login/stories.index.html examples/patterns/nine_states/stories.index.html` → 3 hunks, all `<title>`/meta. No browser, no build, no edits.

## Findings, ranked

### 1. boot: the `:failed` → Retry branch the README headlines cannot be reached in the running example  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: ergonomics] [size: S]
- Where: `examples/patterns/boot/core.cljs:75-82` and `:90-119`; `examples/patterns/boot/README.md:7-8`, `:55-62`, `:131-139`
- What: the demo stub always delegates to `:rf.http/managed-canned-success` (even the `:else {}` fallthrough is a success), so no click, URL or toggle ever routes the boot to `:failed`, and the error screen + `[:app/boot [:boot/restart]]` retry that the README calls "the failure branch, a retry" is code a reader running the example can never see.
- Evidence: `core.cljs:75-82` picks a payload by substring with `:else {}`; `:108-119` unconditionally calls the canned-SUCCESS handler. The `:failed` machinery is real and correct (`boot.cljs:241-244` `:on-error`, `:300-305` `:on-any-failed`, `:313-335` `:boot/restart` clearing every folded payload so `:config-loaded?` cannot short-circuit), and the wrapper test reaches it only by installing a blanket canned-FAILURE override of its own (`boot_cljs_test.cljs:85-91`, `:211-226`). Control: `examples/core/managed_http_counter/` and `examples/capabilities/resources/linearlite/` both ship an in-page failure trigger (README table rows at `examples/README.md:88`, `:121`), so the corpus convention is that a taught failure path is clickable.
- Action: add a one-boolean "Fail next load" toggle to the demo stub (route one URL — `/user.json` is the natural one, it fails inside the `:spawn-all` and so also shows `:on-any-failed` cancelling siblings — to `:rf.http/managed-canned-failure` while set), surfaced as a checkbox on the `main-app` screen with a "Re-run boot" button; one file plus one README sentence.

### 2. Pattern-Boot.md's own Retry snippet dispatches `[:app/boot [:rf.machine/start]]` at a live machine, which Spec 005 says does nothing — the example is right and the spec sample is the stale side  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: teaching-drift] [size: S]
- Where: `spec/Pattern-Boot.md:396` (Retry button) and `:438` ("or an explicit `[:app/boot [:rf.machine/start]]` re-entry event"); contrast `examples/patterns/boot/boot.cljs:313-335`, `views.cljs:65-67`, `README.md:55-62`
- What: an AI (or programmer) who reads the spec first copies a Retry button that is a silent no-op, and even a corrected event would have nowhere to land because the sample's error states carry no `:on` (`Pattern-Boot.md:197-200`).
- Evidence: `spec/005-StateMachines.md:1500`: "a redundant `[:rf.machine/start]` on an already-alive machine runs no cascade and emits nothing"; `Pattern-Boot.md:247` says the marker "then stops; it is never re-fed as a transition trigger" — the spec contradicts itself two pages apart. The example's README (`:59-62`) and `boot.cljs:315-319` spell out exactly this and use an ordinary `:boot/restart` transition out of `:failed`.
- Action: in `spec/Pattern-Boot.md` change the button at `:396` to dispatch `[:app/boot [:boot/restart]]`, add `:on {:boot/restart {:target :configuring :action :reset-boot}}` to the three error states at `:198-200` (clearing folded `:data` as the example does), and rewrite `:438`'s clause to name an ordinary re-entry event. Cite the example as the worked shape.

### 3. nine-states-with-stories: README promises Xray via Ctrl+Shift+C on "either surface", but the page has no `[data-rf-xray-host]`, and the `stories.index.html` it names is not the page the runner stages  [CONFIRMED (code-traced, no browser run)] [severity: medium] [kind: readme-drift] [size: S]
- Where: `examples/patterns/nine_states/README.md:162`, `:166-171`, `:194-198`; `examples/patterns/nine_states/index.html:18`; `examples/patterns/nine_states/stories.index.html:18`; `examples/scripts/examples-staging.cjs:367`
- What: on the live `#/` surface of `npm run dev:example -- examples/nine-states-with-stories`, the first Ctrl+Shift+C logs a `console.error` and mounts nothing, because Xray's inline mount requires an app-provided `[data-rf-xray-host]` element and neither nine_states host page carries one; separately, the README's "host page for the Story-showcase build" (`stories.index.html`) is never served by the documented command — the stager derives `htmlSrc` as `<init-fn folder>/index.html`.
- Evidence: `keybinding.cljs:404` routes Ctrl+Shift+C to `mount/toggle!`; `mount.cljs:1136-1140` sends a first-ever toggle to `open!`; `open!` calls `create-inline-mount-node!` (`mount.cljs:306-322`), which returns nil and `report-diagnostic!`s `:missing-layout-host` when `(.querySelector js/document "[data-rf-xray-host]")` finds nothing; `preload.cljs` docstring confirms "Missing host is reported via console.error ... startup is not blocked". `grep -c data-rf-xray-host` reads 0 on both nine_states pages; control: `examples/core/counter/index.html:27` carries `<aside data-rf-xray-host></aside>` and its build (`shadow-cljs.edn:1282-1309`) carries the identical preload the with-stories build declares at `:1988-1989`. Staging: `serve-example.cjs:352` enumerates through `listStandaloneExamples`, whose `htmlSrc = path.join(srcDir, 'index.html')` (`examples-staging.cjs:367`); repo-wide, `stories.index.html` is referenced only by the two READMEs and the asset scanner's `*.index.html` enumeration — no runner or stager names it. The `#/stories` surface is a different case: the Story shell hosts Xray as a per-panel embed (`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/xray_embed.cljs:1-12`), so "either surface" is half right.
- Action: add `<aside data-rf-xray-host></aside>` (counter's shape, with its flex CSS) to `examples/patterns/nine_states/index.html`, the page actually staged; then decide: A) delete `stories.index.html` (it differs from `index.html` in `<title>`/meta only) and fix README `:162`/`:166`, or B) teach `listStandaloneExamples` to prefer `<prefix>.index.html` when the init-fn namespace is a `*.stories-host` — A is one file, B touches a shared script. A sibling reviewer found the same shape on another `*-with-stories` host page; cited once here for nine_states.

### 4. nine_states: a valid submit while a load is in flight silently discards that load's reply on a real transport  [PLAUSIBLE] [severity: medium] [kind: correctness] [size: S]
- Where: `examples/patterns/nine_states/core.cljs:617-632` (the valid-submit branch); `:381-402` (`:loading`); `:414-437` (the cardinality buckets); `:112-142` (the "newest intent wins" docstring)
- What: the submit path impersonates a fetch — it dispatches `:fetch-started` then `:fetch-succeeded {:items (conj current new)}` — so if a real load is in flight, `:loading` consumes the synthetic `:fetch-succeeded` and moves to a bucket; when the genuine reply lands, no bucket state handles `:fetch-succeeded`, the event is an unhandled no-op, and the user's "5. Some" click has silently done nothing while the page shows "✓ Todo added." over the old list. The `data-load-request-id` supersession the docstring relies on does not cover this, because the competing writer is not a second request.
- Evidence: traced `:new-todo/submit` → `[:ui/nine-states [:fetch-started]]` (unhandled in `:loading`, `:388-396` says so deliberately) → `[:fetch-succeeded …]` (handled at `:398-399` → `:resolving` → bucket) → the later `:nine-states.demo/loaded` → `[:fetch-succeeded …]` against `:empty`/`:one`/`:some`/`:too-many`, none of which lists it (`:414-432`). Not demo-reachable: the in-page stub calls the canned-success handler with no `:after-ms`, which lands the reply in the same drain (`test_support.cljc:306-313`: "absent / 0 → reply lands immediately"), and `core.cljs:236-244` already notes the stub bypasses the in-flight registry — so this only bites the reader who does the copy-and-adapt step the example "exists to guide" (`:242-244`). `spec/Pattern-NineStates.md:239` prescribes broadcasting `:submit-valid`/`:submit-invalid` from the `:new-todo/*` events and never prescribes routing an append through `:fetch-*`; the detour is the example's own. What would confirm it: drive the wrapper with a stub carrying `:after-ms`, dispatch `load {:n 4}`, submit "Buy milk", advance the clock — `(count items)` reads 5 if sound, 1 if the race is real.
- Action: give the machine a real `:items-appended` event (guard-free, handled on `:nothing`, every bucket AND `:loading`, target `:resolving`, action `:conj-item`) and have `:new-todo/submit` dispatch that instead of the fetch pair — the cardinality cascade still decides the bucket, which is the property `:617-621` wants to keep. Or decide to leave it and say so in one sentence beside the `data-load-request-id` docstring; the fix is smaller than the sentence.

### 5. boot: the child loader still carries the retired staging-slot vocabulary, and one docstring describes the hand-off route the code removed  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: ergonomics] [size: S]
- Where: `examples/patterns/boot/schema.cljs:102-110` (LoaderData docstring), `:116-118`; `examples/patterns/boot/boot.cljs:101-106`, `:230-234`, `:266-269`, `:281-284`, `:289-293`; `schema.cljs:89-96` (`:phase`)
- What: `schema.cljs:103-105` says each loader "reports `:boot/asset-loaded` (or `:boot/asset-failed`) back to its parent" and names a `:staging-key`, while `boot.cljs:47-63` and `README.md:108-122` teach the opposite (completion is finality, the child dispatches nothing, there is no staging slot); `:staging-key`, `:parent-id` and `:child-id` are written into every loader's `:data` and read nowhere, so a copier cannot tell which of the two idioms is current.
- Evidence: Grep over `examples/patterns/boot` — `:boot/asset-loaded|:boot/asset-failed` 2 hits, both inside that docstring; `staging-key` 8 hits, every one a write or comment, 0 reads; control `:boot/deps-ready` 2 hits (`boot.cljs:300`, `:302`, declared and consumed). `BootData`'s `:phase` is set once (`boot.cljs:209`) and read by nothing (control: `:app.boot/error` read at `views.cljs:56`). `skills/re-frame2/examples-map.md:30` still says ":hydrating applies the staged payloads" — same stale idiom, another slice.
- Action: drop `:parent-id`/`:child-id`/`:staging-key` from `LoaderData` and the four `:data` fns (keep `:url`), rewrite `schema.cljs:102-110` to say "reaches a `:final?` leaf; `:output-key` names the result", and either delete `:phase` or have `boot-progress` read it. Purely subtractive.

### 6. websocket: the example and the spec's worked example have drifted apart in three places, and the README points the wrong way on one of them  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: teaching-drift] [size: S]
- Where: `spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md:554-557` vs `examples/patterns/websocket/connection.cljs:725-743`; `Pattern-WebSocket.md:532-552` vs `connection.cljs:722-723`; `examples/patterns/websocket/README.md:176` vs `Pattern-WebSocket.md:70-78`, `:134-136`
- What: (a) the spec's `:failed` state handles only `:ws/connect`/`:ws/rotate-cred`, so a `:ws/send` or `:ws/request` issued after giving up is unhandled and dropped — the example's own comment (`connection.cljs:729-738`) names that "user-visible message loss" and adds the enqueue transitions; (b) the spec's `:reconnecting` and `:failed` offer no clean `:ws/disconnect`, the example does (`:722-723`, `:742-743`) and its Disconnect button depends on it (`views.cljs:106-108`); (c) the README says the spec hand-records a `:socket-id` where the example reads `:rf/spawned` — the spec has already moved to `:rf/spawned` (`:78`, "No :socket-id field" at `:134-136`), so the README describes a spec that no longer exists.
- Evidence: read both machines state by state; the example is the more complete one on (a) and (b), and `README.md:11` says the spec "describes the same state machine". Minor fourth: the spec's `:record-connection-opts` (`:206-207`) does not clear `:error`; the example's does (`:278`).
- Action: port the example's `:failed`/`:reconnecting` `:on` maps (enqueue + disconnect) into the spec sample, and delete the `:socket-id` clause from README `:176`. One PR, spec + README.

### 7. long_running_work: `:complete` declares `:meta {:terminal? false}` beside a `:flow/terminal` tag  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: ergonomics] [size: S]
- Where: `examples/patterns/long_running_work/worker.cljs:337-339`
- What: the state's own metadata says "not terminal" while its tag says "terminal" and its two siblings (`:cancelled`, `:error`) carry no `:meta` at all; a copier replicates a self-contradiction with no comment explaining it.
- Evidence: read `:336-349`; `spec/005-StateMachines.md:222` and `:2294` define per-state `:meta` as tooling-visible static metadata, so nothing at runtime resolves the contradiction for the reader. Everything else in this example traced clean: the `with-let` `finally` dispatch is sound because `reg-view` binds `dispatch` to a render-time `make-capture-frame` handle (`core_reg_view_macro.cljc:188-195`), the `:progress` internal self-transition has no `:target` as the README says, and `:on-any-failed` sibling cancellation matches Spec 005 `:3843`/`:3885`.
- Action: delete the `:meta` line (the tag already carries the intent) — one line.

## Per-example census
- boot (examples/patterns/boot): 3 findings above (#1, #2 on its spec, #5); README MATCHES (the failure branch it describes exists — it just cannot be triggered); roster: listed
- long-running-work (examples/patterns/long_running_work): 1 finding above (#7); README MATCHES; roster: listed
- nine-states (examples/patterns/nine_states): 1 finding above (#4); README MATCHES; roster: listed
- nine-states-with-stories (examples/patterns/nine_states stories trio): 1 finding above (#3); README DRIFTS; roster: listed
- websocket (examples/patterns/websocket): 1 finding above (#6); README DRIFTS; roster: listed

## Considered, left alone
- nine_states `view-too-many` (`core.cljs:763`) renders a search `<input>` with no handler — a visual placeholder the spec's "needs search / pagination" row invites; not a morning's work.
- long_running_work accepts `:start` from `:cancelled`/`:error` (README diagram `:131-132` says so) while `controls` disables Start unless `:idle` (`views.cljs:117-119`) — UI stricter than machine; harmless.
- websocket "Disconnect (clean)" is disabled during `:connecting`/`:authenticating` (`views.cljs:106-108`) although `:active` accepts `:ws/disconnect` from every leaf — same shape; harmless.
- boot `:failed` carries `:meta {:terminal? true}` with an outgoing `:boot/restart` — `boot.cljs:319-322` explains the choice and Spec 005 treats `:meta` as tooling-only.
- `skills/re-frame2/examples-map.md:94` lists `:after` as an exit path of `:working` (there is none) — skills tree, another slice; noted for its owner.

## Instruments and controls
- Grep (ripgrep) `staging-key|:boot/asset-loaded|:boot/asset-failed|:boot/deps-ready` over `examples/patterns/boot`: 8 / 2 / 2 hits; control `:boot/deps-ready` found where declared and consumed (`boot.cljs:300`, `:302`).
- Grep `data-rf-xray-host` over `examples/**/*.html` + `tools/xray/src/.../mount.cljs`: hits in counter, flows, realworld_resources; `grep -c` on the two login and two nine_states host pages reads 0 each, `examples/core/counter/index.html` reads 1 (control).
- Grep `rf.machine/start` with already/inert/no-op context in `spec/005-StateMachines.md`: line 1500 is the ruling; the bare token appears on 8 further lines (control that the file is searchable).
- Grep `canned-failure|:failed|boot/restart|deps-failed` in `boot_cljs_test.cljs`: 85-91 and 211-226 (failure reached only via a blanket override); control `hydrat` hits at 154, 179.
- Grep `stories\.index\.html` repo-wide: READMEs, `examples/README.md:165`, `check-examples-assets.cjs:326/356` and its tests only; 0 hits in `serve-example.cjs` / `examples-staging.cjs` (control: `index.html` 40+ hits there).
- Grep `listStandaloneExamples|htmlSrc` in `serve-example.cjs`: lines 75, 352 — the runner enumerates through the function whose `htmlSrc` is `<srcDir>/index.html` (`examples-staging.cjs:367`).
- Grep `defn-? canned-success-handler` in `test_support.cljc`: 273-289; `:after-ms` semantics at 306-313 (absent → immediate).
- Grep `dispatch` in `core_reg_view_macro.cljc`: 188-195 — injected `dispatch` is `(:dispatch handle#)` from a render-time capture, so the `with-let` `finally` path is sound (no finding).
- `node implementation/scripts/check-examples-compile.cjs --list` → 58 lines, exit 0; the five slice ids present.
- `node examples/scripts/check-examples-assets.cjs` → 33 pages, exit 0; scanner static (0 `child_process`/`http`/`fetch` references).

`re-frame.hicasso/route-link` (`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc:477` → `hicasso/impl/route_link.cljs:140-168`) ACCEPTS `:prefetch :intent` and does nothing with it. `:prefetch` is in its `control-keys` (`route_link.cljs:103`) so it is stripped off the anchor; the value is validated on both hosts through the `:routing/link-model` seam (`routing/link.cljc:504 (validate-prefetch! target)`), so `:prefetch :render` throws `:rf.error/route-link-bad-prefetch` — but `:intent`, the ONE accepted value, installs no handler. The result is precisely the failure `validate-prefetch!`'s own docstring names as the one a prefetch can least afford (`link.cljc:58-63`): "a passive link looks identical to a working one until you measure". `rf/route-link` on the same props warms the destination on hover / focus / touch-start (`link.cljc:43 prefetch-intent-keys`, `prefetch-intent-attrs`); the two link surfaces Spec 012 declares behaviourally identical disagree on the one behaviour key they share.

The tree carries two contradictory records of intent. Spec 012:653-662, `docs/core/hicasso/07-routing-and-navigation.md:198-215` + `:412`, `glossary.md:553` and `route_link.cljs:57-63` all say v0 DECLINES `:prefetch` ("deliberate v0 decline rather than an oversight … an author spells the warm-up directly"). But the shipped design record says the opposite: `docs/design/hicasso/product/naming-ledger.md:71` row 36 — "`:prefetch :intent` accepted on `route-link` … **keep as taught** — routing's own `:rf.route/prefetch` event and its `:intent` value are attested, so only the link-side acceptance is new, and **it is the designed end state**. The prototype's v0 decline id `:rf.error/hicasso-route-link-prefetch-declined` is retired and must not be reused" (applied, rf2-hic-065 / rf2-hic-093), and Spec 009:2547 records that retirement (rf2-6c12m.11, PR #8772). rf2-g8pf (closed 2026-09-04) then KEPT `rf.routing.link/prefetch-on-intent!` with no caller on exactly this argument: "Retiring it would leave a link-model seam consumer able to validate and ACCEPT `:prefetch :intent` — with no published way to honour it. That is the exact fail-open shape both files exist to refuse." So the designed end state is WIRED; what shipped is the prototype's decline minus its refusal. This bead wires it.

Two pieces of doc drift ride along: `docs/core/hicasso/troubleshooting.md:532` names `:rf.error/hicasso-route-link-bad-prefetch`, an id that appears NOWHERE in Spec 009 (neither live nor struck — `grep -n hicasso-route-link-bad-prefetch spec/009-Instrumentation.md` is empty); `implementation/hicasso/spec/server-policy.md:68` (HS-40) says "the declined-`:prefetch` refusal fires during the server render" — no refusal exists on either host.

## Target API

```clojure
;; re-frame.routing.link/link-model — one more key; PURE, both hosts, same validation
(link-model target render-frame)
;; => {:href     <strategy-encoded href>
;;     :payload  [:rf.route/url-requested {…}]
;;     :native?  <bool>
;;     :prefetch <[:rf.route/prefetch {:to … ?:params ?:query}] | nil>}    ;; (prefetch-payload target)

;; re-frame.hicasso/route-link — data, no hook, no boundary, no new seam
(h/route-link {:to :app/article :params {:id "intro"} :prefetch :intent} "Read more")
;; renders
[:a {:href           "/articles/intro"
     :on-click       [intent/navigate-head {…}]
     :on-mouse-enter [:rf.route/prefetch {:to :app/article :params {:id "intro"}}]
     :on-focus       [:rf.route/prefetch {:to :app/article :params {:id "intro"}}]
     :on-touch-start [:rf.route/prefetch {:to :app/article :params {:id "intro"}}]}
 "Read more"]
;; :prefetch absent → none of the three positions is touched (passive by construction, as today)
```

The three positions are `rf.routing.link/prefetch-intent-keys` (`link.cljc:43`) — read them off routing rather than restating the list; if the seam needs to carry them, add a `:prefetch-keys` entry to the same `link-model` map rather than a second hook.

**One closed rule for a caller value at a claimed position.** `:prefetch :intent` CLAIMS the three intent positions; a caller-supplied `:on-mouse-enter` / `:on-focus` / `:on-touch-start` alongside `:prefetch :intent` is refused AT RENDER, fail-loud, naming the position — the same shape and the same law as `on-click-roster!` (`route_link.cljs:105-125`: "the click already produces the one routing intent"); here the hover already produces the one prefetch intent, and Hicasso's in-band grammar carries one intent per position. An author who needs both spells the prefetch by hand at that position (the guide's existing form) and omits the sugar. The refusal needs a catalogued id: add ONE row to `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` §Hicasso rows beside `:2545-2546` (**hot-zone**; suggested `:rf.error/hicasso-route-link-claimed-intent-position`) and its `docs/core/hicasso/troubleshooting.md` entry. Do NOT reuse `:rf.error/hicasso-route-link-prefetch-declined` (struck at 009:2547; naming-ledger row 36 forbids it) and do NOT emit routing's `:rf.error/route-link-bad-prefetch` for it (that id means "bad value"; `:intent` is the good value). No silent-skip and no partial fill is admissible — either every claimed position carries the prefetch intent or the render throws.

Server: event props are data the server render drops with every other `on-*`; `link-model` already validates `:prefetch` on the JVM, so the SSR shell rejects what the client rejects and emits what the client emits minus handlers — HS-40 restates that.

## Corroboration

One-reviewer on the fable side; codex INDEPENDENTLY called this "the most concrete user-visible defect here … Prefer wiring the existing routing-owned intent behavior if the published option remains supported; otherwise reject it clearly. A silent no-op is poor ergonomics even for trusted programmers. Verify focus, pointer intent, existing user handlers, navigation cancellation, and frame capture; do not build another prefetch policy subsystem." Wiring is chosen over rejection because (a) naming-ledger row 36 rules acceptance the designed end state and retired the decline id, (b) rf2-g8pf's KEEP verdict presumes the seam consumer can honour the value, (c) rejection would also need a 009 row and would make the two link surfaces disagree on a key Spec 012:640 calls "a routing control key on every link surface". Codex's checklist maps to the acceptance: focus + pointer + touch = the three positions; existing user handlers = the closed rule; navigation cancellation = untouched (`:on-click` / `::h/prevent` path is not read by this change); frame capture = the intent vector lowers on the boundary's ambient frame, the same frame `require-frame!` pinned the click to.

title: Retrospective facade-export classification sweep (re-frame.core slice + the manifest :justification/:action axes; Story = rf2-i6kh, Xray = rf2-ar67) - external-alpha prep CALLED 2026-09-04; gates the first v0.0.1.alpha tag
description:
EXTERNAL-ALPHA PREP CALLED 2026-09-04 21:05 AUSEST by delegated ruling (Mike delegated the call on 2026-09-04; operator-reversible; full ruling, reviewer analysis and implementation guidance in the notes). This bead is now SLICE 1 of the three-slice retrospective facade-export sweep and is a dispatchable single-worker task. It GATES the first v0.0.1.alpha tag: rf2-kmqx3 depends on this bead and on the two slices split out of it, rf2-i6kh (Story) and rf2-ar67 (Xray). Nothing here waits for the tag.

## What it is

spec/Conventions.md lines 1199-1250 define the facade-export audit in two halves. The FORWARD half is active since commit 037d7b2029 (2026-06-04): every new facade export records tier, owner spec, facade-placement justification and recommended action in its PR (lines 1211-1216). The RETROSPECTIVE half is "the full retrospective sweep of every existing non-front-porch export - and the manifest table it produces", deferred to API-freeze / external-alpha prep (line 1218) - which is now called. The deadline is Conventions' own (line 1228): before the first meaningful external alpha/beta, explicitly NOT before v1, because the moment real users copy examples a namespace move becomes a breaking change, and Conventions lines 1234-1244 forbid a retained-for-migration tier after that.

## Scope of THIS bead (slice 1)

1. The two missing manifest axes. spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn carries tier/owner/status only; :justification and :action appear 0 times in it and in the generated spec/api-manifest.edn. Add both as curated axes on every :facade? true row (:action one of :keep :rename :move :internal-public), carry them through implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/gen.clj into the generated rows, and make clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen --check refuse a :facade? true row missing :justification or carrying an unknown :action, with tests. Not required on :facade? false rows.
2. The re-frame.core table. 103 manifest rows, all :facade? true: 17 front-porch (quick keeps), 86 non-front-porch (55 advanced, 27 tooling, 4 testing) each given a disposition and justification. Consumer counts and the counting loop are in the notes (4082 in-repo file-refs across the 86; top: make-frame 687, app-db-value 301, reg-machine 276, register-listener! 235; 18 names with five or fewer files; group-by-event-with-events has zero non-test consumers).
3. Execution of the clear moves: small ones (under ~10 consumer files) in this PR; larger ones as one bead per owning subsystem, --deps discovered-from:rf2-2hpxo, with bd dep add rf2-kmqx3 <new-id> so the tag waits on the move.

Slices 2 and 3 (NOT this bead): rf2-i6kh widens the manifest's facade? predicate (gen.clj:748-753, currently re-frame.core only) to re-frame.story and reconciles its 55 :implementation facade rows, which the invariant at gen.clj:845-863 has never reached; rf2-ar67 enrols day8.re-frame2-xray.core, which has zero manifest rows against 16 public vars. Each dispatches only after the previous slice's PR has MERGED (shared files: gen.clj, the sidecar, spec/API.md).

## Discriminator (bounded freeze pass, not a carve-up)

KEEP when one import supports a coherent ordinary app-authoring workflow even if the tier is advanced/tooling (Conventions lines 1222-1226: single-import product facades stay coherent on purpose). MOVE only when an existing owning namespace is already a clearer door and ordinary facade users do not need the name; never invent a namespace to tidy a column. RENAME only for a concrete lifecycle-verb-law or vocabulary violation. INTERNAL-PUBLIC only for a deliberate supported host/tool embed seam; a var used solely by repository internals leaves the facade at :implementation. Consumer counts are evidence, never the verdict. CONTESTED (tier ambiguity, or a move on anything over ~100 consumer files): record keep with the uncertainty in :justification, list the name on this bead for Mike, and do not hold the PR or the tag on it.

## Hot zone and sequencing

spec/API.md is a one-toucher file (and spec/Conventions.md if the two fields get a sentence there; optional - the sidecar header can carry the vocabulary). This PR runs alone against any other toucher of those files. implementation/scripts/api-manifest/** and spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn are otherwise isolated surfaces.

## Gates, by path, foreground to completion

From implementation/scripts/api-manifest: clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen --check; clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.api-md-check; clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.story-spec-check; clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.xray-spec-check; clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.skills-check; clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.doc-guide-check; clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.doc-api-check; clojure -M:test (the api-manifest job, .github/workflows/lint.yml lines 609-700). For any executed move: the substrate suites its consumers live in, scripts/check_doc_slugs.py for docs/ and spec/ pages, scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci for READMEs beside source. Nothing validates prose or table columns; say in the PR body they were checked by hand.

## Acceptance

1. :justification and :action exist in the sidecar and the generated manifest, required and validated on every :facade? true row, with unit tests in implementation/scripts/api-manifest/test/.
2. All 103 re-frame.core rows carry both fields (tier and owner confirmed while there).
3. Every ruled move or rename is executed, or has a bead that rf2-kmqx3 depends on.
4. Contested names, if any, are listed on this bead with the reason.
5. The api-manifest lint job is green.

## History

Surfaced 2026-07-25 while processing the rf2-fby7o api-freeze dossier (that bead and its coupling no longer exist; nothing to strike). Deferred 2026-07-25 behind S7 (rf2-vxgfnd.99), whose 2026-07-31 closure carried the substrate removal but not the tag. Edged behind rf2-kmqx3 on 2026-08-22; edge reversed by the 2026-09-04 ruling. The former "NOT a Freehand audit" paragraph is deleted: implementation/freehand was removed by PR #8322 (rf2-0yp7w) and the manifest carries no Freehand rows.

RULING 2026-09-04 21:05:49 AUSEST (delegated by Mike 2026-09-04, operator-reversible; dossier ai/decisions/rf2-2hpxo.call-external-alpha-prep.md and its Codex Recommendation section folded here and deleted). THE RULING. External-alpha prep is CALLED: release condition 2 of the 2026-07-25 defer note is met as a delegated, operator-reversible call, and the retrospective facade-export sweep dispatches now, AHEAD of the first v0.0.1.alpha tag. The dependency edge is REVERSED, not merely removed: rf2-2hpxo no longer depends on rf2-kmqx3; rf2-kmqx3 (cut the first tag) now depends on rf2-2hpxo and on the two slice beads split out below (rf2-i6kh Story, rf2-ar67 Xray). The sweep is bounded, not a carve-up: a durable disposition (keep / rename / move / internal-public) with a justification for every export on the three facades, recorded as two new curated axes in spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn and gated by the existing drift-check; only the clear moves and renames execute before the tag; contested names are recorded keep-with-uncertainty and held for the operator without holding the tag. The work is three serialised slices, each one worker, each a green PR: (1) rf2-2hpxo itself = the :justification/:action schema and gate plus the re-frame.core table (103 rows, 86 non-front-porch); (2) rf2-i6kh = widen facade? to re-frame.story and reconcile its 55 :implementation facade rows, classify 117; (3) rf2-ar67 = enrol day8.re-frame2-xray.core (16 vars, zero rows today) and classify. Any move or rename a slice does not execute gets its own bead per owning subsystem, and rf2-kmqx3 is made to depend on each, so the tag waits on the actual moves rather than on a promise. If Mike wants the publish-proof tag before the sweep completes, striking the rf2-kmqx3 -> rf2-2hpxo edges is the visible act of taking that exception, and it needs a written exception to spec/Conventions.md line 1228 because the tree gives no other reading (see below).

WHY BEFORE THE TAG (the one point the two reviewers differed on, decided from the tree). Conventions line 1228 sets the deadline at the first meaningful external alpha/beta, explicitly not v1, because the moment real users copy examples a namespace move becomes a breaking change. Verified: .github/workflows/release.yml lines 162-165 triggers on any v* tag, runs the deploy jobs and creates a GitHub Release (prerelease-flagged); docs/release-process.md policy 3 (line 17) calls v0.0.1.alpha the first publish, all 14 framework artefacts; Clojars cannot yank (policy 4); rf2-kmqx3's own dependents are consumers of that artefact on day one (rf2-hic-063 pilots on the PUBLISHED artefact, rf2-8urba template :hicasso variant unblocking at the first v* tag, rf2-lb566 clean-workspace migration reporter, rf2-59bgn cold-repo install gate); and the migration guide and skills already teach the facade spellings. Nothing in the tree distinguishes a publish-proof tag from the meaningful alpha; the only place that reading exists is rf2-kmqx3's 2026-09-04 dossier note, which itself says the current edge direction is consistent ONLY under that reading. Cost of the reversal in calendar terms is nil: rf2-kmqx3 is already behind rf2-uelji (deferred 2026-09-16, operator act) and rf2-fo4ng (deferred 2026-09-16), and the sweep is dispatchable today. Cost of the alternative is permanent: every move ruled after the tag is a hard Unknown var or a throwing stub for whoever copied the alpha (Conventions lines 1234-1244 forbid a retained-for-migration tier).

OPTIONS REJECTED.
- B, leave it gated on the tag (status quo): converts the one cheap window into consumer breakage on an unyankable registry; the tag chain has no date, so it also has no release event.
- C, classify now and execute when the tag is imminent: a second trigger of the exact shape that already misfired once (condition 1's proxy closed on 2026-07-31 without its substance), and a table that ages against a live facade needs a re-read before use.
- D, strike the sweep and grandfather everything: rewrites Conventions lines 1218 and 1228 (hot-zone) and leaves 55 Story :implementation facade rows and 16 unrowed Xray vars unexamined, a standing contradiction with Conventions line 1249.
- Remove the edge without reversing it (the dossier's step 1): leaves the tag free to land mid-sweep, which is B by another route.
- One bead per ruled move (the dossier's step 4): process overhead; moves group by owning subsystem so related docs and tests move together, and a subsystem PR is still one worker.
- Landing a Story facade? widening as an isolated mechanical prerequisite (the dossier's step 2b): red on main by construction, because the invariant at gen.clj 845-863 / 915-929 would fire on 55 rows; the widening lands with, or after, the reconciliation.
- Making gen --check refuse :action :move on a :facade? true row: the table must be able to RECORD a move before it executes; the tracker edge to rf2-kmqx3 is the gate, and no new workflow gate is added (release.yml is hot-zone and the pre-release test job already covers what it covers).
- Requiring the new fields on every row in the manifest (all 528): the obligation in Conventions lines 1211-1216 is on FACADE exports; gating :facade? true rows only keeps the schema change proportionate and the intermediate states green.

REVIEWER POSITIONS. Both reviewers recommended calling external-alpha prep now (dossier Option A; Codex: call now, activate, and make the sweep a prerequisite of the tag). They concur on the substance and differ on the edge (dossier: remove; Codex: reverse) and on execution granularity (dossier: one PR per ruled move; Codex: one bead per coherent owner/workflow slice). Nothing about the audit's obligation has been discharged; the acceptance criteria in the audit note above stand in full.

HOW I GOT IT WRONG. I discriminated "audit reopen" from "status revert" with a case-sensitive grep for a fixed marker set — AUDIT-REOPEN, "REOPENED THIS EXACT", REOPENED, "still owed", "residual" — plus a check that the notes length was unchanged across the newest few snapshots. Both halves failed, and each failed in the reassuring direction.

THE GREP: this bead's audit text opens "AUDIT 2026-09-04 — MERGED PR #NNNN: reopened because ..." — LOWERCASE "reopened", under a header matching none of my patterns. I ran a control ("external-alpha prep", 1 hit) and concluded the instrument was live. IT WAS: the grep ran fine. A CONTROL PROVES THE INSTRUMENT EXECUTES; IT DOES NOT PROVE THE PATTERN SET IS COMPLETE. To test a pattern set you must control against a POSITIVE INSTANCE OF THE THING THE PATTERNS ARE MEANT TO CATCH — here, a bead known to carry an audit note — not against arbitrary text known to be present.

THE LENGTH TEST: I compared the notes length across the immediately-adjacent snapshot pair at the reopen boundary. That assumes the status change and the note are ONE mutation. They are not: an audit commonly appends its note in a SEPARATE, LATER mutation, so the adjacent pair reads unchanged on a genuine audit. The corrected probe compares the notes length AT THE LAST CLOSE against the NEWEST notes length: growth means text was written while the bead was closed, which is exactly what an audit does and what a bare status revert never does. On this bead that probe reads a clear growth.

WHAT EXPOSED IT: running the corrected probe against a CONTROL BEAD I already believed was a genuine audit reopen. It reported "revert" for that bead, which could not be true — and that contradiction, not any new evidence about this bead, is what falsified the method. A probe that disagrees with a case you are confident about is telling you the probe is wrong.

TWO BEADS WERE WRONGLY RE-CLOSED BY THE OLD METHOD (this one and its sibling) and both are now reopened. Two others re-closed in the same session were re-checked with the corrected probe and confirmed genuine reverts: their notes did not grow while closed. Those closes stand.

WHY, on three grounds.

1. THE RECORD IS APPEND-ONLY BY DESIGN, AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES IT TRUSTWORTHY. A tracker note that can be silently rewritten is not evidence. This project's whole audit chain rests on being able to read what a carrier actually claimed at the time, then read the correction beside it. Excising the claim would leave the correction referring to something no longer present, and would erase the fact that a carrier once believed it — which is exactly the provenance a third carrier needs. The same principle already governs the design corpus: corrections restate a passage with an italic note giving its former wording, the reason and the date, rather than overwriting it.

2. THE MECHANICAL RISK IS REAL AND ASYMMETRIC. `notes` on this bead is ~43,000 characters. `bd update --notes` REPLACES the field, and CLAUDE.md records ~72,800 characters lost across five beads in one session by exactly that mistake, with rf2-9wmqd going 46,569 -> 3,294. A true excision means the documented chunked rewrite — split at line boundaries into ~18,000-character chunks, `--notes` for the first and `--append-notes` for the rest, then probe for known content from the start, middle and end rather than comparing lengths, because chunking shifts them by a byte or two. That is a multi-step destructive operation on a 43KB field to delete one sentence that is already marked false in the same field. The downside of getting it wrong dwarfs the upside of getting it right.

3. THE STATED GOAL IS ALREADY MET. The audit's acceptance wanted the false claim not to mislead. The withdrawal quotes the offending sentence verbatim and gives the corrected figure — 24 of the 30 raise, 6 degrade silently — so a reader who reaches the claim reaches its correction from the same field, in the same read. Nothing further is owed.

THE GENERAL RULE THIS SETS, for any future carrier facing the same shape: WITHDRAW BY APPENDING, NEVER BY DELETING. Quote the sentence you are withdrawing, state what is true instead, and date it. Treat an instruction to "remove" a claim from a tracker note as an instruction to NEGATE it in place unless the operator explicitly asks for excision — and say that you have, as this carrier did.

comments.text:
MAYOR, BACKLOG-REREAD LOOP 2026-08-15 21:52 AUSEST — STAYS DEFERRED. Its release condition READS as met and is NOT met, so I am recording the discrimination rather than leaving the next reread to re-derive it.

THE CONDITION, as written on this bead: "reopen when EITHER holds: 1. rf2-vxgfnd.99 (S7 + alpha tag) closes, or 2. Mike calls api-freeze / external-alpha prep explicitly."

CONDITION 1'S PROXY HAS FIRED. rf2-vxgfnd.99 is CLOSED — "EPIC S7 — Helix-removal wave + alpha tag", closed 2026-07-31. A literal read of the condition releases this bead today.

*** DO NOT RELEASE IT ON THAT READING. *** The condition names "S7 + ALPHA TAG", and the alpha tag never happened. `git ls-remote --tags origin` returns ZERO tags at this tick — nothing has ever been published from this repository. The epic closed carrying the S7 half and not the tag half, so the proxy moved while the thing it was standing for did not.

AND THE TAG IS NOT MERELY LATE — IT IS BLOCKED. rf2-uelji records that Clojars' verified-group policy refuses the FIRST publish of every day8/re-frame2-* coordinate: a new project may not be created in an unverified group, and day8 is not reverse-domain so it cannot be verified. That is an operator-only action, and it gates all 13 implementation artefacts and 5 tool jars. So "published artefact" is still exactly the moving target this bead deferred itself against.

THIS IS THE INVERSE OF THE USUAL FINDING. The loop normally catches a dependency that outlived what it was enforcing — the blocker shipped and the bead stayed blocked. Here the blocker's RECORD closed while its SUBSTANCE did not ship, so the bead reads releasable and is not. Both cases are found the same way, by testing the substance rather than the status field.

THE OPERATIVE GATE IS THEREFORE NOW: rf2-uelji clearing (which yields the tag, satisfying condition 1 in substance), OR condition 2 — the operator calling api-freeze / external-alpha prep explicitly, which needs no tag at all and remains available at any time.

Not a rejection. Conventions mandates the work; this is sequencing only, unchanged from the original disposition.

title: reagent-migration: qualify the closure and ^{:key} checks by dispatch binding and by the renderer that lowers the Hiccup (GH #10942)

- references/gotchas.md (about L24-28).
But references/catalog-mechanical.md's queued escape (about L125-131) deliberately captures the frame during render and closes a plain callback over its queued dispatcher, and it is passed by identity on purpose. Metadata inside an explicitly retained Reagent island (`r/as-element`) is lowered by Reagent, which does read `(:key (meta v))`. Mayor verified all the cited passages at trunk 279fd6d193.

Apply the same qualification to Step 3, gotchas.md and SKILL.md's gotchas and done checklist. ## What C2 learned the hard way, because it will save you the same two CI round-trips

C2's FIRST cut did exactly what its bead prescribed — project `:db-before` and `:db-after`, then diff
the projected pair — and that **reproduced the disease it was curing**. Once both sides are the same
sentinel, `diff-paths` classifies them EQUAL and emits no triple, so a changed secret renders as
**NOTHING**, indistinguishable from "nothing changed". Eighteen assertions went red and **every one was
"the row vanished"** — section, row, glyph, `:data-op`, React key, count — **not one asserted a value**.
A panel whose rows disappear while no value assertion notices has gone silent.

The shape that works, and the one that leaks, both measured on the JVM lane with a plain-frame control
on every arm:

    A. declared [:auth :token], value at [:auth :token]  -> :rf/redacted   (control: "secret")
    C. declared [:auth],        value at [:auth :token]  -> "secret"       <-- LEAKS
    D. declared [:auth],        whole-db projection      -> {:auth :rf/redacted, ...}

So: take the path SET from the RAW pair, so equality stays honest, and re-seat each triple's VALUES on
the WHOLE-DB projection. Never project each triple at its own path — `[:auth]`-shaped declarations are
ordinary and `diff-paths` descends to the leaf, so case (C) recurs constantly.

**And walk rather than `get-in`**: under a redacted ancestor `get-in` answers `nil`, and **nil reads as
a value**. C2 shipped a `projected-at` that walks, plus a regression guard for case (C).

**Fail-closed must be fail-VISIBLE**: an unresolvable frame should withhold every value and KEEP every
row. Silence is the one failure a diff panel cannot afford.

title: story: snapshot identity does not cover render inputs inherited through :extends (follow-up to rf2-pt0d1)
description:
FOLLOW-UP from rf2-pt0d1 (PR #9860). The worker left this residue unfixed and did not file it. It is a CLAIM; verify it at tip before acting.

THE CLAIM: render inputs that a variant inherits through :extends do not reach snapshot identity. Examples are a parent's :db-seed or :setup, and the post-merge decorators that Story spec 007 names. Identity resolves only args and tags through the chain. Since PR #9860, watch mode does re-run on these edits, because the watch hash covers every :extends ancestor. What stays unsound is the identity itself: an edit to a parent's render input changes what the child renders, yet leaves the child's identity unchanged.

THE CONTRACT, as the rf2-pt0d1 worker read it:
- Story spec 002 defines snapshot identity as a fingerprint of declared render inputs.
- identity.cljc admits a slot if and only if editing it changes the settled rendered state.
- Spec 017 says :extends inherits the context/world.
PR #9860 widened identity for :compose on exactly this reading, adding a :composed slot that is absent unless a fragment carries a render input. Every other variant kept its identity byte for byte.

WHAT TO DO:
1. Measure on the JVM that a parent render-input edit changes the child's settled app-db and verdict but not its identity.
2. If it holds, widen identity through the :extends chain on the #9860 precedent. The slot is present only when an ancestor carries a render input, it costs one lookup per ancestor, and it needs no plan compile. Commit a RED regression first, then the control.
3. State plainly in the PR that every variant extending such a parent gets a new content hash once.
4. If widening would contradict what spec 002 or spec 017 says identity is, STOP and report.

The docs/story/08 note for this change belongs with the rf2-mc87a worker's docs/story/08 edit after PR #9856 merges; write the sentence into the report.

CLAIM: HELD. Measured on the JVM at base. Parent carries :db-seed {:count 1}, :setup [[:set-n 5]], :decorators [[:centered]]; child extends it with only assertions; grandchild extends the child. Parent :db-seed to {:count 2}: child app-db count 1 to 2, verdict pass to fail, child and grandchild identity unchanged. The agent loop was the research's row C3 (DIVERGENT) and grok's "one agent loop split across two skills": the JVM story-mcp server (tools/story-mcp; 19 tools; fail-closed; list-substrates and read-a11y-violations answer capability-unavailable by design because that host has no browser) and the browser route through re-frame2-pair (the human's live frame; eval-cljs into the running registry) are two hosts, and an agent found out which one it needed by getting an error. Chapter 09 now names the two hosts on its first screen (#9801, rf2-b7o66). The skill leaves are where an AGENT reads, and they still describe the split as an ownership boundary (story-mcp-loop.md lines 3-28 "AUTHOR / REFINE (this skill) vs RUN / SELF-HEAL (re-frame2-pair)"; the headless section at ~:170-172; pair stories.md ~:17-19, :96, :157-158) without one rule an agent can apply before it starts, and without the three transformations the research proved (promotion, fidelity upgrade, explain) as recipes. Journey 3 of the measurement child (rf2-a1v8a: human state -> agent -> verified revision; count host switches) will measure the result, so this child precedes it.

== WHAT TO WRITE ==
1. THE RULE, identical in both leaves and in tools/story-mcp/README.md, four lines: no browser in the loop -> story-mcp over stdio (registry + run + explain + register; anything that needs a rendered substrate or a live a11y engine answers capability-unavailable — that is the verdict, not a failure); a human's live workshop in the loop -> re-frame2-pair (eval into the browser registry; drive the live frame; read the a11y panel); NEVER both for one edit; when in doubt, start on the JVM and move only when a tool says capability-unavailable. Say which skill owns which half in the same breath and link the other.
2. RECIPE: promote a failing run. Both routes as they are at trunk — from Test mode (the dialog captures the run's dispatches and, since #9804, carries the registered source's :assertions/:checks and replaces a dispatch-only capture with the source's full program; until rf2-vgthk lands, a variant whose :script has no dispatch step shows no promote row — say so and give the API route as the fallback) and from the API (`determinism/->artifact` of the compiled plan + `promote-run-artifact!` with a :variant/id; or over MCP: run -> register-variant carrying the source's assertions). The acceptance an agent should apply: the promoted variant FAILS under the fault with the same assertion count, PASSES when the app is fixed, FAILS when the fault returns — an agent that edits the expected value instead of the app has not repaired anything (the research's own MCP transcript did exactly that and the siblings called it out; write that warning).
3. RECIPE: upgrade fidelity. `upgrade-snippet` (ui/view_state.cljc) now reads back as one form and drops the pin by walking the :extends chain (#9803); caveat until rf2-yt6ak: pins composed from fragments may survive — check the compiled child's :fidelity (`story/explain` -> :fidelity must not contain :sub-overrides unless the author kept the pin). Include the JVM one-liner.
4. RECIPE: explain before running. `story/explain` now reports story-level :args and :effective-args (#9799) — read them before editing a declaration; the pure `plan/explain` folds ambient layers only when handed :run-args, so an agent calling the pure compiler sees the variant layer alone by design.
5. story-recorder.md: align its capture vocabulary with (2) (the recorder emits data; capture-or-warn) — no new content, consistency only.
6. tools/story-mcp/README.md: the same rule, and correct or confirm the register-variant parent-story wording (rf2-bf12o closed by correcting the skill leaf: a parentless variant is legitimate; make the README and both leaves say the same thing).
7. docs/story/09-multi-substrate-and-agent-loop.md: cross-link both leaves from the first screen (one sentence; the chapter already names the hosts).

== TESTS AND GATES ==
scripts/check_doc_slugs.py covers skills/ and docs/; scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci covers tools/story-mcp/README.md; if any tool DESCRIPTION text in tools/story-mcp's tool-descriptors.edn changes, the story-mcp conformance suite must stay green (do not change descriptions unless the README wording forces it). Prose has no gate: the worker executes each recipe once (JVM for 2-4; the MCP loop with ai/findings/Story/fable/probes/mcp-prelude.clj + mcp-requests.jsonl for the stdio path) and pastes the transcript in the PR body. NOT a hot zone.

== DO NOT ==
Merge the two skills into one, add a third host, add an in-process MCP, or promise anything about browser capabilities from the JVM host. The split is deliberate; the fix is that choosing is easy. Blocks rf2-a1v8a (journey 3 uses these recipes).

(B) fault: preview-variant source :fail 1 assertion; register-variant promoted body; preview-variant promoted :fail 1; control body with only :extends previews :pass with no assertions. title: Ratchet: retire the hicasso spelling so it cannot return
description:
CONTEXT IS ON THE PARENT EPIC rf2-d1nr. Read it first — it is the durable record.

AFTER child .2. Make `hicasso` unable to come back.

THE MACHINERY ALREADY EXISTS AND IS THE RIGHT HOME: scripts/check_retired_spellings.py. It
already retires spellings and coordinates in exactly this shape — it carries a COORD arm with
COORD_SCAN_PATHS / COORD_EXCLUDE_PATHS and its own fixture tree under
scripts/_test_fixtures/check_retired_spellings/coord/. It runs in .github/workflows/test.yml
AND in scripts/test-fast-pr.sh, so an entry there is graded on every PR.

DO NOT BUILD A NEW GATE. Adding a rule to the existing one is the whole job.

== WHAT TO RETIRE ==
  `hicasso` in all four case forms (hicasso, Hicasso, HICASSO, hicasso_)
  `re-frame2-hicasso` as a coordinate
  `:rf.adapter/hicasso` as a keyword value

== THE EXEMPTION THAT MUST EXIST, AND IT IS NOT OPTIONAL ==
docs/design/fresco/decisions.md legitimately quotes the old name FOREVER: child .3 supersedes
HD-001 rather than deleting it, and the superseding block quotes the original ruling verbatim
including the word Hicasso and the Picasso derivation. Any retirement rule that cannot express
that exemption will either fail CI permanently or force the deletion of a decisions-log entry
this project deliberately preserves.
The existing COORD arm already models this distinction — its fixture tree has negative cases
named bare_comment_provenance, refusal_message_prose and spec_boundary_cases, i.e. prose that
MENTIONS a retired spelling without USING it. Follow that existing pattern; do not invent a
second mechanism.

== FIXTURES, BOTH DIRECTIONS ==
Add fixtures under scripts/_test_fixtures/check_retired_spellings/ that pin BOTH:
  POSITIVE — a source file using `re-frame.hicasso` is REFUSED.
  NEGATIVE — the decisions-log supersession block quoting the old name PASSES.
A gate that cannot fail is not a gate, and a gate that cannot pass the one legitimate use is a
gate that will be disabled the first time it fires.

== ACCEPTANCE ==
Run scripts/check_retired_spellings.py against the post-.2 tree: it must be GREEN (nothing
left to catch) while its own fixtures prove it would catch a reintroduction. Then plant one
`re-frame.hicasso` reference in a scratch file, confirm the gate goes red naming file and
line, and remove it. Report both results. Do not report a green without having seen it go red.

Do not use `grep -iF` anywhere in this work — it ABORTS on this box (SIGABRT, exit 134, silent
stdout), and a false zero is precisely the failure this bead exists to prevent.
notes:
--- SEQUENCING FENCE, mayor 2026-09-09. Recorded when rf2-d1nr.2 merged and this bead became tracker-unblocked. ---

*** THIS BEAD IS TRACKER-UNBLOCKED AND MUST NOT BE DISPATCHED YET. HELD BEHIND rf2-d1nr.3. Release when that PR MERGES. ***

WHY, and it is a content dependency rather than a file collision: this bead's own description says the exemption for `docs/design/fresco/decisions.md` "MUST EXIST" and "is not optional", because rf2-d1nr.3 supersedes HD-001 rather than deleting it, and the superseding block quotes the original ruling VERBATIM — including the retired product name and the Picasso derivation. A retirement rule that cannot express that exemption "will either fail CI permanently or force the deletion of a decisions-log entry this project deliberately preserves".

THE TRAP IF THIS RUNS FIRST, and it is quiet: at trunk today the retired spelling reads ZERO everywhere, so a ratchet added now PASSES with a permitted count of zero and no exemption. Then rf2-d1nr.3 lands, writes the verbatim quote into `decisions.md`, and the ratchet goes red on a change that is correct — and the reflex repair is to widen the floor, which inverts the gate. Running .3 first means the exemption is written against text that actually exists.

WHAT TO DO WHEN THE FENCE RELEASES: read rf2-d1nr.3's landed `docs/design/fresco/decisions.md` and its PR body/notes, which are briefed to state EXACTLY which file and which construct carries the surviving occurrences and how many. Build the exemption against that, as narrowly as the existing COORD arm's fixture tree models (`bare_comment_provenance`, `refusal_message_prose`, `spec_boundary_cases`). Do NOT widen it to the whole file or the whole directory if a construct-scoped rule will do.

UNCHANGED: add the rule to the EXISTING `scripts/check_retired_spellings.py`, which already runs in `.github/workflows/test.yml` AND `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh` so an entry there is graded on every PR. DO NOT BUILD A NEW GATE — the bead says so and it is right.
--- MAYOR FENCE AMENDED 2026-09-09 22:26 AUSEST. THIS BEAD NOW WAITS ON TWO SIBLINGS, NOT ONE. ---

*** THE SECOND FENCE: rf2-d1nr.2 WAS REOPENED BY THE MERGED-PR AUDIT OF #9568 AND ITS REPAIR WILL DELIBERATELY PUT THE STRING `hicasso` BACK INTO `bench/fresco/**`. Your exemption list cannot be built until that PR merges, because you would be ratcheting against a tree that is about to gain legitimate occurrences. ***

WHY THEY ARE LEGITIMATE, and why no amount of care in .2 removes them. The audit reproduced two residuals, both the same shape: a mechanical rename moved a POINTER while its REFERENT stayed immutable.

  (1) `data_archive.cjs` advertises `git restore --source=7b492b98cb -- bench/fresco/src/re_frame/bench/fresco/data`. That exits 1 — pathspec did not match. Commit `7b492b98cb` predates the rename, so its tree carries the corpus at `bench/hicasso/src/re_frame/bench/hicasso/data`, 237 entries, sentinel `alloc-0gjqi/paired-run1.json` resolving there. A directory rename on main cannot rename a path inside an older commit. The working recovery operation MUST name the old path, so the old spelling is load-bearing.

  (2) `alloc_pass_position.cjs:170-176` pins FAMILIES to `lad/fresco`, but the archived `paired-run1.json` carries `lad/hicasso` keys and always will. Measured on that same unmodified record at R0/R3/R7: base reader 55 cells (lad/hicasso 28, lad/reagent 14, lad/uix 13); landed reader 27, with all 28 native-arm cells silently dropped and every published median moving with them. Reagent and UIx unchanged is the positive control. Any reader that consumes the archive must spell `lad/hicasso` to see it.

So these are not residue awaiting deletion and not a miss by the sweep. They are historical facts that must be spelled correctly to work at all — the same category as a git SHA. A ratchet that refuses them breaks the recovery of the corpus the Fresco programme's published numbers were taken from.

WHAT TO DO WHEN THE FENCE LIFTS, and it is cheap because the list is being handed to you. The rf2-d1nr.2 brief REQUIRES its worker to publish, in the PR body and in a bead note, the exact `file:line` of every surviving `hicasso` occurrence its change introduces, with a one-line reason each. Build the exemption from THAT list, at source, re-measured against the merged tree — not from this note, which is an account of why the list will exist rather than the list itself.

ONE THING THAT MAKES THIS LESS URGENT THAN IT LOOKS, recorded so nobody manufactures an emergency: `scripts/check_retired_spellings.py` does NOT scan `bench/`. Its own text says so at :246 — `bench/fresco` is a hand-run project that no per-PR lane covers — and the classifier agrees: the `bench/*` arm of `.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh` sets NO surface at all, by ruling, and `implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs` pins every output false there. So nothing goes red today. The fence exists because THIS BEAD widens the ratchet, and the widening is what would meet them.

THE FIRST FENCE STANDS UNCHANGED: still held behind rf2-d1nr.3, whose exemption must quote the verbatim HD-001 passage that bead writes. Release requires BOTH PRs merged. Read .3's landed `docs/design/fresco/decisions.md` and .2's landed `bench/fresco/**` and build one exemption set against both.
--- WORKER REPORT, rf2-d1nr.4. PR #9572, branch worker/ratchet-a, worktree ratchet-a, base b248076e2f. 2026-09-09. ---

FENCE STATUS. The two mayor fences above are SUPERSEDED by the dispatching mayor, not by me.
The first (held behind rf2-d1nr.3) is discharged: .3 merged as PR #9570 and its landed
`decisions.md` is what the exemption was written against. The second (held behind rf2-d1nr.2)
was RELEASED and INVERTED: .2 is still in flight in another worktree, and the ratchet was built
against the tree in front of it instead of waiting. That inversion is deliberate and its cost is
paid by a documented extension procedure, below.

== WHAT LANDED ==

Rule (g) of `scripts/check_retired_spellings.py`, plus 5 fixtures and 2 self-test phases. No new
gate, as the description required. 523 insertions in the gate, 94 in fixtures.

Two carriers: a file's CONTENT and a file's PATH (reported at line 0). The path carrier is not
redundant — a directory of JSON records or image assets reintroduces the name in hundreds of
places with no scannable line, and the rename moved 741 paths.

WHY WIDE. Rules (a)-(f) are narrow because their retired spellings collide with sanctioned
vocabulary; a coined product name collides with nothing, so the substring IS the violation and
what the rule needs instead is REACH. It scans the whole repo with NO SUFFIX FILTER — the rename
moved .md, .edn, .json, .cjs, .yml, .html as well as .clj* — and states its surface as
SUBTRACTIONS rather than a roster, because a subtraction has to justify itself where an omission
is invisible. Five subtractions: generated trees carrying zero tracked files, the two staged
mkdocs copies, the local-only `ai/` tree, this gate's own fixtures, and this gate's own source
(closed by construction, the same carve-out rule (f) makes for the parser that refuses the arrow).

MEASURED SURVIVING POPULATION, verified rather than taken from the brief. On b248076e2f, tracked,
`.beads/` excluded, case-insensitive: 1 file, 2 lines, 3 occurrences — `docs/design/fresco/
decisions.md:48-49`. Positive control 1005 files carrying `fresco` (the brief said 911; that
figure was almost certainly case-sensitive — no other discrepancy). Negative control 0 on a
nonsense token.

== THE EXEMPTION, AND THE PREMISE THAT HELD ==

`PRODUCT_EXEMPTIONS` pairs a PATH (matched exactly) with a LINE CONSTRUCT (a regex) and a reason.
The standing entry is `docs/design/fresco/decisions.md` + `^> > `.

The `> > `-uniqueness premise HELD and was verified two ways, not assumed: `^> > ` matches 8 lines
in that file, contiguous at 48-55, all of them the one HD-001 supersession quotation; a looser
pattern admitting leading whitespace and variable spacing finds the same 8. So a construct-scoped
exemption is available and no narrower shape (line range, quoted text) is needed. It is
deliberately NOT a file exemption — new prose in that file is still graded — and deliberately not
a line range, which would move silently under an edit above it.

== bench/ IS IN SCOPE, DECIDED RATHER THAN DEFAULTED ==

The note above is right that `check_retired_spellings.py` did not scan `bench/` and that the
classifier gives `bench/*` no surface. That is precisely the argument for INCLUDING it: rule (f)
already reaches `bench/` on the ground that a reintroduction there goes SILENT rather than red,
and silent is the worse shape. A hole cut through the tree that most needs the ratchet is not a
smaller decision than an exemption entry; it is a bigger one, and an invisible one.

So .2's legitimate occurrences will meet this gate, and NOTHING has been pre-written for them —
guessing at their shape is how a ratchet acquires a hole. The extension procedure is in the PR
body and inline on the constant: add (path, construct-regex, reason), then add the file's real
content as a fixture and TWO rows in `_PRODUCT_SELF_TEST_CASES` — one at the real path with the
expected count, one attributing the SAME fixture to a different path with a non-zero expectation.

_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from machines.md (ref machines.2); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

A spawned actor IS an event handler whose id is its address (005:2600), and every real consumer already holds that id (`:rf/spawned` on the parent, `:rf/self-id` / `:rf/parent-id` on the child) and sends with the one verb `[:dispatch [id ev]]`. Beside that story the tree carries three surfaces with zero consumers:

1. **The `:system-id` family** — a per-frame reverse index consulted at send time: `:system-id` spawn key, `re-frame.machines/machine-by-system-id` (2 arities, `machines.cljc:197-230`), the `[:rf.machine/dispatch-to-system [sid ev]]` fx + `dispatch-to-system-fx` (`machines.cljc:254-290`, reg :374-376; **no-op when the name is unbound** :282 — "the caller sees success, the value vanishes", Principles §No silent swallow), the `[:rf.runtime/machines :system-ids]` runtime-db slot (`paths.cljc:74-81`), traces `:rf.machine/system-id-bound` (`spawn.cljc:582`) / `-released` (`traces.cljc:155-163`), error `:rf.error/system-id-collision` (`spawn.cljc:478-530`; 009:2040), the `:system-id` tag on the spawned/destroyed traces, D8 (005:3202), 153 source lines across 12 `implementation/machines/src` files plus core touchpoints, 30 test files, 4 dedicated conformance fixtures, 55 lines of 005.
2. **`:on-spawn`** — a callback whose one plausible output (the id) the runtime discards and then warns about (`transition.cljc:2320-2380` `apply-on-spawn`, `:rf.warning/on-spawn-return-ignored` :2367), with a root-level `:on-spawn-actions` registration slot (Spec-Schemas:2619), a `MachineElementEntry` schema row, source-coord stamping in the macros (`core_reg_macros.cljc:343-548`, `source_coords.cljc` 9 sites), an action-ref id `:rf.machine.spawn/on-spawn` on the exception path, a conformance DSL arm (`conformance.cljc:668-683` `realise-on-spawn-handler`), and 005 §Recording the spawned id user-side (:2982-3000) — a four-mechanism preference list that exists only because the hook invites the wrong one.
3. **`:child-machine`** — a spec key with no implementation: API.md:952 row ("post-v1 lib"), 005:4591-4600 "Declarative state-scoped child machines" + :4635 bullet. 005:4046 already says the thing it describes is `:spawn`.

Wave 2 (July) parked the fx "until the facade audit"; that audit (rf2-2hpxo, closed 2026-09-04) scoped `re-frame.core` rows only and never had this surface in scope, so the park has lapsed. Parked surfaces become permanent unless ruled.

## Evidence (tip `6445d0611b`)

- Real call sites of `:system-id` / `machine-by-system-id` / `dispatch-to-system` in `examples/`, `testbeds/`, `tools/*/src` (non-test): **none**. The hits are `tools/machines-viz/.../grammar.cljc:560` (the closed spawn-key vocabulary) and Xray's app-db diff panel, which lists the runtime-db SLOT as a diff area (`app_db_diff_helpers.cljc:288,336,355,484`, `app_db_diff.cljs:20`, `app_db_diff_state.cljs:16,340`, docstring `machine_inspector_helpers.cljc:223`). Docs teach it in `docs/machines/actors.md:143,196-225,253,299`, `docs/api/re-frame.machines.md:15,17,203-372`; skills in `api-cheatsheet.md:52-53`, `spawn.md:36,76,188`, `frames.md:195`, `re-frame-migration/SKILL.md:109,124`, `breaking-changes.md:174`, `guided-handlers-state.md:185`; the migration README carries opt-in rule O-9 (:2950-2974). More teaching than use, two months after the July count of zero.
- `:on-spawn` sites: **none** — the two example hits (`connection.cljs:69`, `websocket/core.cljs:42`) are prose saying "no `:on-spawn`". 73 source mentions across 12 files, 17 test files, fixture `spawn-on-spawn-callback.edn` + edits in three more.
- `:child-machine`: zero code.
- 005:2705 heads "Spawning from inside an action (the common case)" with an example that reaches the child via `:system-id`; measured: 0 hand-emitted `[:rf.machine/spawn]` sites in app or tool code against 4 declarative example sites + 3 testbed sites. The heading is false.
- The addressing that IS used: `:rf/spawned` 19 example mentions, `:rf/parent-id` / `:rf/self-id` 8 + 15, `[:dispatch [id ev]]` dozens (websocket, long_running_work, deep_machine).

## Options (codex's three, carried verbatim)

- **A. Retain named addressing as a small advanced capability.** Keeps XState `systemId` as a surface. Cost: everything in the deletion list stays, with its silent no-op, its second registry and its teaching burden, for no consumer.
- **B. De-scope it because it has no named application consumer** (the demand bar, Principles:124: "a public surface ships only for a named consumer … a capability with no consumer today is parked"). `:fixed-actor-id :primary-request` gives the BEHAVIOUR XState `systemId` exists for — a stable address any sibling can reach — and a dispatch to a dead one is `:rf.error/no-such-handler` (loud).
- **C. Require applications to carry identities and own any rebinding they need.** Same deletion as B, stated as the app's responsibility; B and C differ only in what the spec says about rebinding.

**Recommendation: B**, ruling all three families together, with the teaching flip at 005:2705 and the `:rf/spawned`-only id story as the replacement text. Rationale: identity is carried, not found (002's frame rule; a send-time reverse index is ambient lookup creeping back); no silent swallow; one protocol for one fact; the phantom row makes the spec describe what does not exist; XState parity is behavioural, not surface (Mike, 2026-06-22) — an addressing mode nobody addresses with is not parity.

**The counter, which a port MUST carry (codex; fable agrees):** `:system-id` and `:fixed-actor-id` are not behaviourally equivalent. `spawn.cljc` allocates actor identity separately from the reverse-index binding: a `:system-id` collision REBINDS the name to the new actor (last-write-wins, `:rf.error/system-id-collision`, `spawn.cljc:478-530`) while the earlier actor keeps its own identity; `:fixed-actor-id` REUSES the identity itself on re-entry (`spawn.cljc:1184`), and two live children sharing a fixed literal are a spawn error (:165-205). The `:work-generation` stamp (`spawn.cljc:313`) disambiguates incarnations for the lifecycle machinery, but that does not mean every ordinary application dispatch carries incarnation information. So under B/C the spec must say plainly: the name IS the address; a re-entered `:fixed-actor-id` child is a new incarnation at the same address; an app that needs "a fresh actor while the old one lingers" allocates (`:id-prefix`) and holds the id. No shim, no compatibility layer.

**Codex caution (fable-synthesis §Corrections, verbatim in spirit):** "Zero observed calls is evidence, not a deletion algorithm" — strong for a convenience already covered by data (this is that case for `:on-spawn` and the phantom), weaker for a lifecycle capability with its own timing (the rebind semantics above are the one real difference). Codex "neither verified nor refuted" the `:system-id` deletion and recommends not making @machines.1 depend on it — honoured: @machines.1 is ruling-free and this decision follows it.

**Surfaces:** `:spawn` / `:spawn-all` (state-node keys) · `[:rf.machine/spawn spawn-spec]` (fx) · `:child-machine` (API.md:952, phantom) · `[:rf.machine/destroy id]` (fx) · `:final?` auto-destroy · `:spawn` exit cascade · frame-destroy cascade · `:rf/spawned` / `:rf/self-id` / `:rf/parent-id` (carried ids) · `:fixed-actor-id` · `:system-id` + `re-frame.machines/machine-by-system-id` (fn, 2 arities, shape-discriminated) + `[:rf.machine/dispatch-to-system [sid ev]]` (fx) + `[:rf.runtime/machines :system-ids]` slot + 2 traces + 1 error · `:on-spawn` (+ root `:on-spawn-actions`, + `:rf.warning/on-spawn-return-ignored`) · `:on-done` / `:on-error` / `:output-key` / `:error?` (single-child completion) · `:on-child-done` / `:on-child-error` (spawn-all completion) · `:raise` · registration: `reg-machine` (M) / `defmachine`+`reg-machine` / `reg-machine*` / `make-machine-handler`+`reg-event`.

## The problem

A machine IS an event handler, a spawned actor IS an event handler whose id is its address (005:2600), and dispatch already reaches both. That single elegant fact is then surrounded by parallel spellings for each lifecycle question:

Corpus = `examples/` (app), `tools/*/src` (tool), `testbeds/` + `tools/*/testbeds` (app-shaped), `docs/` + `skills/` (secondary), `implementation/**/test` (tertiary).
