title: The Render-on-Node recipe drops :url-strategy, so Node-rendered route-link hrefs ignore a base path although the docs promise they match
description:
The Render-on-Node recipe drops the handler's `:url-strategy`. Links rendered on Node therefore ignore a base path, while the docs promise that server and client hrefs match.

## Where

`re-frame.ssr.ring.node/renderer` sends Node only protocol, entry, state, runtime, buildId, timeoutMs and requestId, plus args (`implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/node.clj`). The `:url-strategy` that `ssr-handler` threads into the JVM frame (`pipeline.clj` ~L325-330) never reaches Node; Fresco's `render-body` builds its frame from the entry's own `:frame-opts`.

The docs get this wrong in two ways:
- `docs/ssr/concepts.md` §Render on Node, step 2, calls `server/render-body` with `:hiccup`, `:render-state` and `:identifier-prefix`, and no `:frame-opts`. Nothing on that page says frame config does not cross.

The login example already gets it right: `examples/substrates/fresco/login/server.cljs` (~L138) passes `:frame-opts model/frame-config`.

## Change

- Make the step-2 sample pass the shared frame config as `:frame-opts`.
- Add one sentence saying that only projected state crosses to Node.
- Qualify both rows for the Node case.

Do not serialise frame config onto the wire, and add no check.

title: Unit-test pruning: security
description:
Apply the exact requested pruning prompt recursively to implementation/security/test. This is a distinct worker cluster under rf2-0wcq5. Production code remains unchanged except temporary hash-verified fault plants. Push a draft test-only PR, babysit all latest-head checks to green, then mark ready. A measured no-op or unexecuted-file report is valid; do not manufacture changes.

Simplify the unit tests under implementation/security/test. Do not change the code under test. LLMs tend to
write too many low-value unit tests, and this suite was largely written by them.

Assume the suite has more tests than it needs, and that many of its tests are longer
than they need to be. Every test costs CI time, reading time and refactoring friction,
and the low-value ones hide the tests that matter. I want a lean suite: each test earns
its place by guarding a behaviour a caller relies on, against a regression that could
plausibly happen and would matter. Each surviving test should be as short as the thing
it proves.

Stay inside implementation/security/test. Do not edit tests elsewhere. If a deletion relies on a test outside
implementation/security/test to keep covering something, name that test in your report.

Work in this order:
1. Run the suite and record the result: tests, assertions, failures, lines. Confirm a
   runner actually executes each file in implementation/security/test; a file nothing runs cannot be pruned on
   evidence, so report it.
2. Read the code under test and list what it promises its callers: normal results, each
   boundary that takes its own path, each promised failure, and any past bug the tests
   refer to.
3. Map every test to the promise it checks. Most of the work shows up in this map:
   promises with five tests, tests with no promise, and tests of something no caller
   relies on.
4. Decide each test: keep, simplify, merge or delete.
5. Run the suite again and prove the pruned suite still guards every promise.

Work in small batches by contract group, and commit as you go. Before each batch,
predict the change in test and assertion counts; after it, confirm the counts moved by
exactly that much. If helper agents are available, use read-only ones for the mapping
step. If implementation/security/test plainly will not finish in about four hours, stop at a group boundary,
ship what is done, and list the files you did not reach.

Decide each test with two questions:
- If this test were deleted, what bug could ship that no remaining test would catch?
  If you cannot name one, delete it.
- If you can name one: is that bug plausible in this code, would a caller notice it,
  and would nothing else surface it at once (a compile or load error, a boot-time
  validation, most of the suite going red)? If the bug is implausible, harmless, or
  loud anyway, delete the test.

Delete:
- A test another test implies. If A cannot pass while B fails, drop B.
- Extra examples of one behaviour that take the same path through the code.
- Existence and smoke checks: a function exists, a var resolves, something "is
  registered", a result is non-nil, a call "does not throw", when another test
  exercises the same call with a real assertion.
- Change detectors: a test that copies a constant, a data table, a default config, a
  roster or a string out of the source and asserts equality. It fails on every intended
  change and catches no bug. The exception is a value callers depend on exactly, such as
  a public id or a documented default, that nothing else pins: keep one test for it.
- Absence checks for things nothing produces, and negative-input tests for inputs no
  caller passes and the contract does not mention.
- Exhaustive enumeration: one row per enum member, keyword or field when they all take
  one path. Keep one representative plus the members that take a different path.
- Tests of the language, a library or the framework: a constructor sets a field, a
  getter returns it, a map holds the key just put in it.
- Tests that pin how the code works instead of what it does: private helpers already
  exercised through the public path, call order, internal data shapes, greps of the
  implementation's own source, and log, trace or error wording that is not part of the
  contract.
- Tests whose expected value is computed by the same logic as the code under test.
- Assertions that a mock returned what it was told to return, and tests whose mock setup
  is most of the test while the assertion checks the mock.
- Separate per-platform test files asserting the same thing about platform-neutral code.
  A single shared test that runs on both platforms is one test, not two: keep it.
- Tests of test helpers and fixtures.
- Tests of code that has no logic in it, and tests whose only subject is production code
  that no production caller uses.

Simplify every test you keep:
- Assert the whole result with one equality instead of one assertion per field. Drop an
  assertion that a later one in the same test implies.
- Cut setup, fixtures and data to what the assertion needs. Remove unused bindings,
  requires, helpers and fixtures.
- Tests that vary one input become one table-driven test. Keep the boundary rows and
  drop the mid-range ones.
- Tests that repeat the same setup for one assertion each become one test.
- Delete comments and docstrings that restate the code or narrate history. Keep a
  one-line why where a test's purpose is not obvious from its name and body.

- The only test of a promise a caller relies on: a normal result, a boundary that takes
  a different path (empty, one, many; zero; the limit and one past it), a promised
  failure.
- A regression test for a bug that actually happened, unless a stronger test now covers
  it.
- The last guard of a security, privacy or redaction promise.
- The last test that keeps a gate able to fail, and the last test holding a published
  doc or spec claim to the code.
When a weak test and a strong test overlap, keep the strong one: the one that would fail
on more bugs.

Do not:
- Weaken an assertion, or swap an exact check for a looser one, to make a merge or a
  simplification easier.
- Delete a test because it fails, is slow or is flaky. Report it.
- Leave unused helpers, fixtures or requires behind.
- Add new tests. If you find a promise with no test, report it.
- Change production code. Dead code and stale docs or spec text go in your report as a
  list, not into your change.
If anything pins test counts or names, such as a count floor or a roster, update it in
the same change. Commit one file or module at a time.

Prove it:
- The suite passes before and after. Report both sets of counts.
- For each group of deletions that rests on a surviving cover, break the code in a place
  the deleted tests guarded and confirm a surviving test fails. Then restore the code and
  confirm it matches the committed file. One plant per group sharing a cover is enough.
  If nothing fails, you removed real coverage: put the tests back.
- A cover must actually run. A skipped test, a fixture the runner never loads, or a test
  on a lane nothing executes covers nothing. Confirm the runner executes a cover before
  resting a deletion on it.
- Run each test file you touched on its own at least once. Deleting a file can break a
  sibling that relied on it loading something first; give such a file its own require.
- A deletion made under the second question needs no plant. Give its one-line reason in
  the report instead.
- A simplification must not change what a test can catch. Where you removed an
  assertion, name the assertion that implies it.

Report:
- Before and after: tests, assertions, lines.
- Deleted tests, grouped by reason. For each, the surviving cover, or the one-line
  reason it was not worth keeping.
- Merges and simplifications: what went into what, and the lines each file lost.
- Notable keeps: tests you considered deleting but kept, and why.
- Plants, and which test caught each.
- Tests outside implementation/adapters/reagent/test that your deletions rely on.
- Dead code, stale docs or spec text, and gaps (promises with no test). One line each.

If you are unsure whether a promise a caller relies on is still covered, keep the test
and say so. Losing the only guard of a real promise is still the one mistake that matters
more than leaving an extra test in. But being unsure whether a test is worth keeping is
not a reason to keep it. If you cannot say in one line what plausible regression it
catches that a caller would notice, delete it.

title: EPIC ssr-node crossing: make the bounded Node renderer a first-class ssr-ring path (RULED 2026-09-02 — six children rf2-8arzr.1..6; do not dispatch this bead)
description:
## Scope

Make the bounded Node/React renderer a supported opt-in renderer for the non-streaming re-frame.ssr.ring request path. The outcome includes the smallest useful Ring render seam, the JVM side of the v1 crossing, an explicit post-drain render-state projection, a supported Node package/launcher entry point, and one canonical runnable native-Hicasso example with its tests and documentation. The existing JVM/Reagent renderer remains the default.

## Findings

- The three components are individually substantial and well tested, but they do not compose into a public product path. re-frame.ssr.ring owns request frames, event/resource drain, head, hydration payload, shell, response and teardown; implementation/ssr-node owns a bounded React render service; no caller joins them.
- build-full-response* resolves a JVM hiccup root and directly invokes ssr/render-to-string. That API shape cannot name a native JavaScript root which exists only in the application bundle.
- The Node request already has a stable entry, EDN root args, build identity, and allowlisted state, but its state shape is only top-level app-db key -> EDN value text. The JVM does not produce that projection, and route/machine/runtime facts needed by a real SPA have no inbound door.
- Render visibility and hydration egress are different policies. The server must be able to render from state that is intentionally absent from __rf_payload; deriving one projection from the other would either leak server-only state or silently render nil.
- The documented consumer API imports implementation/ssr-node/src/*.cjs directly. implementation/ssr-node has README.md, src/ and test/ but no package manifest/export or supported launch command of its own.
- Existing JVM and Node suites are broad but disjoint. The Node lane proves the service in isolation; there is no JVM -> Node -> JVM witness, runnable example, or generated recipe.

## Recommended Action

Add one explicit render-body boundary at the full-response body decision, selected when constructing the Ring handler. Its input should describe the post-drain request frame plus a stable render entry and serialized root arguments; it should not require a JVM hiccup value. Keep a tiny local adapter as the default so the current JVM/Reagent path and output remain unchanged.

Implement the concrete JVM-to-Node adapter for the existing bounded service. Let applications supply one render-state projector; define the serialization domain and carry the render-visible app-db and runtime/route/machine facts a native root needs. Revise the pre-alpha v1 request directly if necessary rather than adding compatibility layers. Keep the ownership line crisp: Node returns body markup only; the JVM continues to own boot-event drain, head, hydration payload, shell, status/headers/cookies/redirects, error projection, and frame teardown.

Give ssr-node a supported package entry point and runnable server command, then exercise the path in one small native-Hicasso reference app. Document that recipe at the public Ring/SSR surface and reflect any new public symbols or artifacts in the API and distribution manifests.

## Evidence

- implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj:533-557 pins the frame, resolves root-view to hiccup, and hard-calls ssr/render-to-string at line 548.
- git blame attributes that call to 185c149a537 on 2026-06-09. The Node service landed later in commits b2b35bf6e9 through aa413ab092 and subsequent fixes; history contains no crossing implementation.
- implementation/ssr-node/README.md:17-21 says there is no caller; lines 509-512 and 540-543 name build-full-response* as unwritten separate work.
- implementation/ssr-node/README.md:434-465 teaches imports from implementation/ssr-node/src/service.cjs and src/http.cjs. A top-level listing contains only README.md, src/ and test/.
- implementation/ssr-node/src/protocol.cjs:106-113 declares the v1 request fields; lines 226-280 require a per-entry stateAllowlist; lines 370-415 constrain state to top-level app-db keys and EDN-text values.
- docs/design/hicasso/production-server-arm.md:35-40 records the Node-sidecar ruling and the hard-wired host; lines 77-98 say the Node half alone landed and identify the state projector and end-to-end witness as the two undischarged crossing gates; lines 673-688 define the intended ownership arrows.
- implementation/package.json:63 and .github/workflows/test.yml:5079 gate ssr-node itself, but an executable-source search for ssr-node, createService, or x-rf-ssr across implementation/ssr, implementation/ssr-ring, examples/capabilities/ssr and tools/template returns no match.
- Deep tracker searches for ssr-ring, Node sidecar, render seam, state projector, and no caller found no open owner. The matching records are closed and describe either the decision, the Node half, isolated CI/absence checks, or documentation drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A documented Ring handler option selects either the existing local renderer (the unchanged default) or the concrete Node adapter through one narrow render-body contract; no renderer registry or protocol hierarchy is introduced.
- On the Node path, the JVM drains initial events and blocking resources first, then sends a stable entry id, EDN root args, expected build id, request identity/deadline, and an application-projected render snapshot from the live request frame.
- The render snapshot can faithfully seed both app-db and the route/machine/runtime facts used by the reference native view. Its serialization rules have a round-trip corpus and one clear negative fixture for an unsupported value.
- Render-state projection is independent of hydration payload projection. An end-to-end fixture renders from a server-only value while proving that value is absent from the JVM-written __rf_payload.
- A real JVM -> Node -> JVM test launches the supported Node entry point, renders a native application entry, and proves that Node body bytes are inserted into a complete JVM-owned Ring response with JVM-owned head and payload.
- The same crossing test covers one representative refusal or deadline, shows it reaches the existing Ring error/on-error semantics without a partial success page, and proves request-frame/isolate cleanup on success and failure.
- Application authors can import and start ssr-node through a declared package export/command without reaching into implementation/ssr-node/src.
- One runnable example and one canonical documentation recipe cover build, entry-table declaration, renderer selection, state projection, startup, hydration, and build-id skew. Spec 011, public API docs/API manifest, and package/release manifests agree with the shipped surface.
- Existing SSR, Ring, and Node test lanes stay green, and CI runs the new crossing witness.

## Non-goals

- Moving HTTP request, head, payload, shell, cookies, redirects, or response ownership into Node.
- Node streaming, React Server Components, islands, or a general RPC/renderer plugin framework.
- Multi-version protocol negotiation or compatibility scaffolding; this is a pre-alpha v1 contract and may be changed coherently.
- Replacing or changing the default JVM/Reagent renderer.
- Platform-specific supervisor, container, autoscaling, or deployment automation.

## Related beads

- rf2-2rtt6.88 - ruled the production server arm as the Node sidecar and defined the crossing gates.
- rf2-hic-056 - built the bounded Node/React service (the Node half).
- rf2-n8vp - added the dedicated Node test script and CI job.
- rf2-6ovv - hardened the service absence/coupling witness.
- rf2-a8c5 - corrected status documentation and explicitly recorded the still-missing JVM half.

Every premise below was re-verified at tip by the ruling agent, not taken from the dossier.

BANNER STRUCK — the *** AWAITING MIKE *** banner above is discharged by this ruling.

== DECISION ==

AXIS 1 — GO, now, at P2, queued at normal cadence behind Causa/Story (go does not mean jump the queue). Not hold, not reject.

AXIS 2 — SIX sequenced slices, not one programme and not the four both reviewers proposed. Children rf2-8arzr.1 through rf2-8arzr.6 carry the full per-slice briefs as their descriptions (the same text is repeated in this note under IMPLEMENTATION BRIEF); this bead is their parent and stays OPEN until all six land.
  A/6 rf2-8arzr.1 — render-body seam + byte-identical local default. Fence: implementation/ssr-ring; one stanza each in spec/011-SSR.md and spec/API.md (hot-zone).
  B/6 rf2-8arzr.2 — ssr-node package.json exports + `serve` launcher + absence witness rewritten. Fence: implementation/ssr-node only.
  C/6 rf2-8arzr.3 — render-state contract: `re-frame.ssr.render-state` project (JVM) / restore! (CLJS) over two partitions + protocol v1 revision. Fence: implementation/ssr (new cljc + tests), implementation/ssr-node/src/protocol.cjs + tests + fixtures + one README section.
  D/6 rf2-8arzr.4 — JVM->Node adapter `re-frame.ssr.ring.node` + the JVM->Node->JVM CI witness on a plain fixture module. Fence: implementation/ssr-ring (+ deps.edn data.json), test.yml new job (hot-zone), spec/011 stanza (hot-zone), classifier pair only if a new output is genuinely needed.
  E/6 rf2-8arzr.5 — native-Hicasso product witness: `re-frame.hicasso.server` body-only entry + the login example's server bundle. Fence: implementation/hicasso, examples/substrates/hicasso/login, ONE build in shadow-cljs.edn (hot-zone).
  F/6 rf2-8arzr.6 — docs recipe + spec 011 / API.md / api-manifest / release-roster reconciliation. P3; dispatches only after E MERGES.
  ORDER: A, B, C in PARALLEL (three disjoint artefacts; B and C share ssr-node's README in different sections — rebase, don't fight). D after A, B and C merge. E after D merges. F after E merges. D and E each queue behind any in-flight toucher of their hot-zone file. The edges are on the tracker (D blocked by A, B, C; E by D; F by E; this parent by all six), so `bd ready` surfaces exactly A, B and C today and never this parent.
  WHY SIX, NOT FOUR: each four-slice cut on record hid one 5-6-criterion bundle — the dossier's C (adapter + projector + serialization domain + corpus + protocol revision + witness with refusal and cleanup arms) and Codex's A (snapshot contract + projector + Node restore + body-only Hicasso module + fixtures + hydration parity) — which is exactly the shape the split-bundles rule exists for: a worker times out and strands uncommitted work in a worktree. Six is the honest single-worker sizing; two extra dispatches are cheaper than one stranded worktree.

AXIS 3 — WITNESS: native Hicasso is the product witness (slice E). The existing Reagent SSR example (examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr) does NOT substitute — a Reagent root already renders on the JVM, so Reagent-over-Node proves machinery nobody would ship and quietly weakens acceptance criterion five ("renders a native application entry") into what it was written to exclude. The early MECHANICAL crossing proof rides slice D on a plain fixture render module (the eight-line `{protocol, buildId, entries, render}` shape ssr-node's own eleven fixtures already use — no React, no CLJS build), which is what dissolves the schedule pressure the Reagent shortcut was reaching for. "Both" is rejected: the Reagent module would be throwaway.

== HOW THE OPINIONS WERE WEIGHED ==

The dossier author (sections: Summary; The problem, carefully and fully; What is waiting on this; Options — Axis 1/2/3; Recommendation) and the Codex reviewer (sections: Codex Recommendation; Independent findings; Delivery slices; Trade-offs and stop conditions) AGREE at the headline on all three axes: go now at P2, four slices, native Hicasso required, Reagent not a substitute, a plain module for the early mechanical test. That agreement is adopted.

They DISAGREE on what slice A is, and that is the substantive disagreement:
  - Dossier, Options/Axis 2: A = the render-body seam with the byte-identical local default, landed first as a safe refactor.
  - Codex, Delivery slices (1) and the closing paragraph of Trade-offs: A = the snapshot/projector/restore contract plus a body-only Hicasso module, with "no public seam yet" — "it earns public shape only after A proves what the non-local implementation actually needs".
  RULING: the dossier's A stands, and Codex's ordering concern is answered on the merits rather than by sequencing. The seam's INPUT is maximal — the live post-drain frame by id, the handler opts and the Ring request, i.e. everything the JVM knows — and its OUTPUT is fixed by the ownership line the bead already locks (body markup, plus an optional locally-derived render hash, which is Codex's own Independent-findings refinement, adopted). A contract with maximal input and ownership-fixed output cannot turn out too narrow for the Node adapter, so there is nothing for the contract work to discover that would reshape it. == SHARED CONTRACT (every slice cites these by number) ==

S1 THE SEAM. `ssr-handler` gains ONE construction opt, `:renderer` — a plain fn, no protocol, no registry, no multimethod: `(fn [{:keys [frame-id request opts]}] -> {:body-html <string> :render-hash <string-or-nil>})`, called by `build-full-response*` at today's hard call (pipeline.clj:564) INSIDE the existing `rf/with-frame` scope, AFTER `drain-blocking-resources!` and the boot-event drain, BEFORE head resolution and the payload build consume its result. Input: the live post-drain frame by id (everything the JVM knows is reachable from it), the handler opts and the Ring request — NEVER a JVM hiccup value. Output: body markup plus an optional LOCALLY-derived render hash; nil hash => no `data-rf-render-hash` marker and no payload `:rf/render-hash`, exactly today's unresolved-root behaviour (rf2-q1b96). The default renderer wraps today's resolve-root-view -> render-document-hash -> render-to-string; the default path's bytes and errors are unchanged, and that is slice A's acceptance floor. `:root-view` is required iff the renderer is the default. `stream-handler` refuses `:renderer` at construction with `:rf.error/ssr-streaming-unsupported-opt` (the `:html-shell` precedent, spec/011-SSR.md:1695-1703); streaming over a non-local renderer is a programme non-goal.

S2 OWNERSHIP LINE (the bead's, restated because every slice cites it). Node returns body markup and nothing else. The JVM owns the request frame, boot-event drain, blocking-resource settle, head, hydration payload (`__rf_payload`), shell, status/headers/cookies/redirects, error projection and frame teardown. The sidecar's HTTP status is never copied to the browser response.

S3 RENDER STATE. The render-visible projection is DISTINCT IN POLICY from the hydration payload's but SHARES ITS ENVELOPE: the partition shape `{:rf/app-db {...} :rf/runtime-db {...}}` the payload already uses (payload.clj:5-13) and the client's `:rf/hydrate` already installs (hydrate.cljc). It is declared like `:payload` — a fail-closed allowlist per partition (top-level app-db keys; top-level runtime-db keys such as the route slice and machine snapshots) — as a new handler opt `:render-state`, with a `(fn [frame-id] -> partition-map)` escape hatch for a projector the allowlist vocabulary cannot express. The FRAMEWORK does the projecting, in a new `re-frame.ssr.render-state` cljc namespace reusing payload_policy.cljc's apply/project machinery. The serialization domain is the payload's existing EDN domain — reuse it, never invent a second one; slice C supplies the round-trip corpus and the negative fixture. The Node-side restore seeds a FRESH per-request frame with both partitions WITHOUT replaying boot events (the JVM drained them), reusing hydrate.cljc's partition-install path minus verification and DOM. This is the "second install door" the ssr-node README (:355-365) declined to invent in a sidecar; the framework decides it here, by ruling.

S4 PROTOCOL v1 REVISION (slice C; pre-alpha — revise protocol.cjs directly, no compatibility layer, `protocol` stays 1). The request carries the runtime partition beside `state`, per-key EDN text, gated by an ENTRY-owned allowlist for that partition too (absence = unrenderable, mirroring stateAllowlist at :264-273). The service still never decodes application data; allowlists stay entry-owned so a caller cannot widen its own allowance — the fail-closed guarantee is KEPT in Node, not moved to the JVM. The wire spelling (`runtime` + `runtimeAllowlist`, or one two-partition `snapshot` object) is the worker's call within those invariants. `initialEvents` / `payloadPolicy` / `head` stay refused for the reasons already in REFUSED_FIELDS.

S5 ERRORS ON THE NODE PATH route through the EXISTING render-failure projection — the `:error-view` side of spec/011's division (:1428-1450). A transport failure (connection refused, JVM read timeout), a sidecar refusal (`x-rf-ssr-refusal`; 4xx/503/504/500) and a sidecar render failure are ALL throws at the render call site with a live frame the projector can see, so all become a projected 5xx via `ssr/project-render-exception!` — with DISTINCT codes (e.g. `:rf.error/ssr-node-unreachable`, `:rf.error/ssr-node-refused` carrying the refusal code in ex-data, `:rf.error/ssr-node-deadline`) so operators can tell them apart in the trace stream. `:on-error` keeps its meaning (the net for when the projector cannot run). No partial success page is possible: the body render fails before any shell is assembled.

S6 JVM HTTP/JSON. The adapter lives in ssr-ring as ONE namespace, `re-frame.ssr.ring.node`, required only by consumers who select it. JDK `java.net.http.HttpClient`: ONE client per renderer, built at construction and reused (per-operation clients defeat pooling); EVERY request carries an explicit timeout = the request's `timeoutMs` + the sidecar's admission budget + a wire margin, derived by the adapter (a separate knob only if the worker finds one necessary). JSON via `org.clojure/data.json` added to implementation/ssr-ring/deps.edn — ACCEPTED as ssr-ring's one new dependency (first-party, zero transitive deps; consumers of the default local renderer pay one small jar, which is acceptable). Rejected: a separate adapter artefact; cheshire (Jackson's transitive weight for a flat request); hand-rolled JSON.

S7 DEPLOYMENT POSTURE. Default endpoint http://127.0.0.1:8148. The adapter accepts any URL and does NOT refuse a non-loopback one (trust the programmer); the recipe states that render state may carry server-only values, so a remote sidecar is the operator's network and transport to secure. `engines: {node: ">=24"}` in ssr-node's package.json, matching CI. Build skew: the sidecar refuses on `buildId` mismatch already; the adapter additionally checks `x-rf-ssr-build` on success and throws a distinct code if it differs.

Construction validation: entry, args, render-state policy, build id, endpoint and timeouts are required for the Node renderer; `:root-view` is not (A made it conditional).

Transport (S6): ONE `java.net.http.HttpClient` per renderer, built at construction and reused; EVERY request carries an explicit timeout = `timeoutMs` + the sidecar's admission budget + a wire margin, derived by the adapter (add a knob only if you find one necessary). JSON via `org.clojure/data.json` — accepted by the ruling as ssr-ring's one new dependency. Build skew: the sidecar already refuses on `buildId` mismatch; additionally compare `x-rf-ssr-build` on success defensively and throw a distinct code if it differs.

Errors (S5): a transport failure (connection refused, read timeout), a sidecar refusal (`x-rf-ssr-refusal` present; 4xx/503/504/500) and a sidecar render failure ALL throw at the render call site with a live frame, so ALL route through the EXISTING render-failure projection (`ssr/project-render-exception!` -> the `:error-view` side of spec/011's division, ~:1428-1450) as a projected 5xx — with DISTINCT codes (e.g. `:rf.error/ssr-node-unreachable`, `:rf.error/ssr-node-refused` carrying the refusal code in ex-data, `:rf.error/ssr-node-deadline`). NEVER copy the sidecar's HTTP status to the browser response. `:on-error` keeps its existing meaning. No partial success page is possible: the body render fails before any shell is assembled.

## The crossing witness (a new test.yml job, named for what it is: the JVM -> Node -> JVM crossing)

A dedicated ssr-ring test alias (`:crossing-test`, so the default `:test` alias stays Node-free) that: spawns slice B's `serve` launcher via `ProcessBuilder` with the fixture module on port 0, parses B's ready line, constructs `ssr-handler` with the Node renderer, and proves —
(a) the JVM drains `:initial-events` FIRST and the fixture receives the drained value through the state partition (the fixture echoes a state value into its markup);
(b) the response is a complete JVM-owned document — JVM head, `__rf_payload` built from the JVM app-db, JVM shell/status/headers — with Node's body bytes inserted verbatim;
(c) render-state != payload: a server-only key is rendered by the fixture and ABSENT from `__rf_payload`;
(d) ONE refusal-or-deadline arm: a fixture entry that sleeps past `timeoutMs` -> sidecar 504 -> projected 5xx through `:error-view`, distinct code, no partial page (a refusal arm — a key the entry does not allowlist — is an acceptable substitute if the deadline arm proves flaky under CI load);
(e) cleanup on success AND on failure: the JVM request frame is destroyed (frame registry empty) and the sidecar's `/health` shows no in-flight work;
(f) ONE observational complete-crossing timing printed to the job log — a number, not a threshold.
Kill the launcher in a `finally`. The job needs `setup-node` 24 and the JVM toolchain; copy the shape of the existing JVM jobs.

## Acceptance

Everything above; existing ssr-ring, ssr and ssr-node lanes green; the spec/011 stanza; and while in `test.yml`, correct the stale comment at ~:5123 ("73 rows across 7 suites" — 8 suites since before this programme; slice B raised it to 9).

title: Machines: a keyword-form [:rf.machine/destroy id] cancel row for a declarative child carries work-bearing-path [], so it never matches the child's reply
description:
rf2-fuxeq (c74bd45930) and rf2-m1vuu (PR #11383) made a fixed-id single `:spawn`'s replies and its explicit-destroy cancel row carry the attempt's work-id generation, so the cancel row matches the attempt's done/error reply (`[:rf.work/machine actor-id work-bearing-path generation]`). rf2-m1vuu's worker found one destroy path that still cannot match: the keyword form `[:rf.machine/destroy <id>]` passes nil `parent-id` / `invoke-id`, so for a declarative child its cancel row's work-bearing-path is `[]`, not the spawn's path, and the row does not correlate with the child's done reply. This predates both fixes.

No sentence states capability implications (e.g. "`:fsm/history` implies `:fsm/hierarchical`") or says that registration-error rows are graded as if every capability were claimed. All 66 `:machine-transition` rows are consistent; only `:reg-machine` rows drift. | My stage-2 claim includes `:fsm/hierarchical`, so the drift did not bite in the claimed subset. | Pass for claimed fixtures; would FAIL a flat-only port claiming `:fsm/eventless-always :fsm/registration-validation`.

> G14. machine-reg-error-timeout.edn control (3) — instance of G9 | machine-reg-error-timeout.edn | A `:spawn {:machine-id :child :timeout 10000 :on-timeout …}` control row in a fixture tagged only `#{:fsm/timeout :fsm/registration-validation}`; my claim does not include `:actor/declarative-spawn`, so per 005 §Capability gating `:spawn` must throw `:rf.error/machine-grammar-not-in-v1`. | Kept the spec-normative gating. | FAIL (call[2]: threw `:rf.error/machine-grammar-not-in-v1`, expected no throw). This is the one stage-2 failure; it is a fixture-tagging defect, not an engine defect.
>
> G14 (update). Resolved once `:actor/declarative-spawn` joined the stage-2 claim (run-stage2-6.log): the row now passes. The fixture-tagging defect stands (it is G9).

Includes G14, which the probe's own log marks as an instance of this entry: machine-reg-error-timeout.edn's control row 3 uses :spawn while the fixture's tags declare only #{:fsm/timeout :fsm/registration-validation}, so a port with the declared claim must throw :rf.error/machine-grammar-not-in-v1 there. title: Xray trace row shows no message for a :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch adoption trace
description:
The `:rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch` adoption trace carries React's message in `:tags :error`, plus `:where` and `:recovery`. Xray's trace-row target text comes from tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/trace_helpers.cljc (around line 551), which reads only `:reason` / `:exception-message`. So a hydration-mismatch row in the Trace tab shows no message until it is expanded.

Fix: let the row target fall back to `(:error tags)` when it is a string, and add a trace_helpers test row for the adoption trace's shape.

This was found while doing rf2-qyjv2, where the file was outside the fence.
notes:
== WORKER SUMMARY (PR #11451, commit 476acaf29e, branch worker/ssr-followups)
tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/trace_helpers.cljc target-detail, (:error :warning) arm: after :reason and :exception-message it now takes (:error tags) when that is a string, ahead of the :rf.error/operation fallback. The adoption trace is (rf.trace/emit! :warning :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch {:error <React message or nil> :where ... :recovery :warned-and-replaced}), so its row now shows React's message; a nil :error still renders nothing. With the fix it exited 0 across every tools lane (tools/xray 590 tests, 1567 assertions, 0 failures). Both runs printed this worktree's gate root. clj-kondo on both files: 0 errors, 0 warnings. The CLJS side runs in CI's `cljs` job, "CLJS (shadow-cljs :node-test)".

title: Implement static flows: registrar reg-flow, make-frame :flows activation, delete the toggle and lifecycle-settle machinery, migrate every consumer
description:
## Ruling

Flows stay, as static definitions activated per frame. `reg-flow` becomes an ordinary top-level registration into the registrar's `:flow` kind, with no `:frame` and no live-frame requirement. Each frame names the flows it runs with a new `:flows [ids]` frame-config key on `make-frame` / `frame-root`, defaulting to none. Runtime toggling goes: the reserved effects `:rf.fx/reg-flow` / `:rf.fx/clear-flow`, the lifecycle settle they trigger, the direct-clear settle, and the side read API. A feature gate becomes ordinary data in app-db that a flow reads as an input. The evaluator stays, and so does the state-write settle. This bead is the IMPLEMENTATION and CONSUMER half. The spec half is rf2-yl9dt, which this bead depends on; it carries the same ruling, and its §Activation text is the contract to build.

Decided 2026-10-16: Mike directed that every dossier recommendation an independent Codex review agreed with be actioned. His instruction, verbatim:

> review all decisions. They now have a "Codex Recomendation" section.  Where the original recomendation matches the Code Recomendation, create a bead to action the decision.  And then remove the file.  Leave behind cases where the two differ materially.

Both the dossier and the Codex review chose this option (dossier option B).

**Decisive facts (read in source at trunk 89517e8f54):**

1. **The live-frame rule forces workarounds at every flow site.**
   - `reg-flow` refuses a frame that is not live: `implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/registry.cljc:634-647` throws `:rf.error/flow-frame-not-live`.
   - Definitions sit in the per-frame side store `flows-by-frame` (`registry.cljc:26-30`), outside the registrar. The registrar's `:flow` kind throws `:rf.error/registrar-kind-not-queryable` when queried (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:2131`).
   - The cart works around this with `install-flows!` (`examples/core/flows/core.cljs:80`), a strict boot order (`:327-341`) and a hand-written `^:dev/after-load reload!` (`:323`). So does every other flow site in the repository.
2. **The runtime toggle re-applies after an epoch restore.** This is a live defect, and it is one of the reasons for the ruling.
   - Flow definitions live in the process atom `flows-by-frame`, and an epoch restore resets only the dirty-check rows (`implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc:873`, `reset-flows-dirty-check!`).
   - So after the cart registers `:cart/discount-rate` through `:rf.fx/reg-flow` (`examples/core/flows/core.cljs:163-175`), restoring the epoch from before the click rewinds app-db to 9,700 but leaves the flow registered.
   - The next event writes 0.1 again, and the discount reappears. This was read from the code, not run.
   - **The defect goes away with the toggle.** The gate becomes a value in app-db, which rewinds with app-db, so `tool_pair.cljc` needs no fix. Acceptance criterion 7 pins it.
3. **The toggle is the expensive part, and the corpus barely uses it.**
   - The two effects (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:1016-1041`) run after the flow pass, so they request a head-inserted `[:rf/settle-flows]` event (`fx.cljc:812-868`; `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:4413`).
   - The settle has two triggers (`fx.cljc:862-863`): the lifecycle request flag, and `walk-changed-flowed-frame-state?` (`fx.cljc:784-810`) for effects that write frame state after the pass. Only the first goes.
   - The only toggle in the repository derives a constant (`examples/core/flows/core.cljs:175`).

**Same id, different derive per frame.** The bespoke per-frame definition store goes; only `flow-frame-scoped.edn` exercises it. Do not add a prohibition in its place. A frame made with explicit `:images` resolves `:flows` ids through its sealed generation, so two image compositions can select different namespace-authored definitions of one id. That comes from image semantics, not from a flows mechanism. In one live process, two derives means two ids.

**Rejected options:**

- **A, leave as is:** the boot and reload workarounds stay, tools keep the side door, ports inherit the toggle machinery, and the epoch-restore defect stays.
- **C, retire flows** in favour of subs, a shared pure function and a registered frame interceptor: it loses the declared graph (queryable inputs and outputs, ordering across features, refusal of two writers to one path, per-write Xray attribution) for no correctness gain.
- **D, retire and park:** the same loss now.

**Supersedes:**

- Spec 013's per-frame single store and frame-divergent-per-id rule (`spec/013-Flows.md:123-143`), and the `:rf.error/flow-frame-not-live` rule (`013:156-158`).
- §Dynamic toggle and its settle sections (`013:427-514`), and the Resolved section "Lifecycle effects settle" (`013:619-627`), which is reduced to the state-write trigger.
- The lifecycle-settle design from rf2-kh73v, and the direct-settle fixes under rf2-3x7nj.18.2, rf2-3x7nj.18.3 and rf2-gwye.63.
- In part, EP-0014's mid-event `:rf.fx/reg-flow` passage (`docs/EP/EP-0014-derivation-and-process-algebra.md:941-944`).
- EP-0002 R7 is applied, not overturned: `reg-flow` is "classified as genuinely global".
- The atomic-abort ruling (Mike, 2026-05-24, `013:609-613`) is not reopened.

## Work

Every path is at trunk 89517e8f54.

**Registration.**

- `reg-flow` (`registry.cljc:592-818`) writes the registrar, keeping its shape validation. Its `:frame` handling and live-frame gate go.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc` drops the `:flow` not-queryable carve-out (`core.cljc:1744-1921`, `:2075`, `:2131`).
- `(rf/clear :flow id)` becomes the ordinary registrar clear.
- The reload sweep (rf2-konlg) and the live default (rf2-bmrh9) then give hot reload with no extra code.

**Activation.**

- `make-frame` and `frame-root` accept `:flows [ids]`, defaulting to none.
- Validate at construction. An unknown id fails the way an unregistered interceptor reference does.
- Run the cycle and output-overlap checks (`implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/topo.cljc`) over the frame's active set at construction, and again when a re-registration reaches the frame.
- The flows stage (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:1653`) reads the active set through the frame's own view: live without `:images`, the sealed generation with explicit `:images`. Use that view's existing refresh semantics.
- The settle guard `:flows/frame-has-flows?` (`registry.cljc:115`) becomes "the frame has active flows".

**Per-frame state is the evaluation memo only.**

- `flows-by-frame` stops holding authoritative definitions. Don't rebuild a frame-scoped side table under another name.
- Each memo row records the definition identity and output path it was computed with. A re-registration then recomputes on the next event, and a moved output path is vacated on the next pass.
- A flow the reload sweep deletes vacates its output, with a warning that `:flows` names an unregistered id.
- Frame destroy drops the frame's memo rows.

**Delete:**

- the `:rf.fx/reg-flow` and `:rf.fx/clear-flow` handlers (`fx.cljc:1016-1041`) and their reserved-fx table entries (`fx.cljc:537-538`);
- the lifecycle request flag `*flow-settle-requested*` and its setter (`fx.cljc:745-782`);
- the direct-clear settle (`implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows.cljc:575-641`) and `clear-flow*` (`registry.cljc:886-1060`);
- `*pass-caller*` (`flows.cljc:261-294`);
- `first-evaluation-deferred?` (`flows.cljc:489`);
- the live-frame gate and `:rf.error/flow-frame-not-live` (`registry.cljc:634-647`);
- the side read API `re-frame.flows/flows-snapshot`, `flows` and `flow-meta` (`registry.cljc:59`, `:97`, `:107`) and their facade re-exports.

Estimate: roughly 600-800 source lines leave, and activation adds roughly 150-250. The estimate is unmeasured.

**Keep:**

- the state-write trigger `walk-changed-flowed-frame-state?` (`fx.cljc:784-810`) and `[:rf/settle-flows]`;
- the evaluator: the outermost `:after` position, topological order, the dirty check, output reassertion, rollback bookkeeping and the atomic abort;
- `tool_pair.cljc:873` `reset-flows-dirty-check!`, which resets the memo after a tool write.

**Tests** under `implementation/flows/test/`:

- Delete the toggle, direct-settle and registration-versus-destroy race suites: the `direct_clear_settle*`, `direct_reg_deferral`, `reg_flow_destroy_linearization`, `clear_reg_watch_incarnation`, `lifecycle_drain_race` and `*_trace_incarnation` files. That is about 750 of 2,725 lines, an estimate.
- Keep `flows_output_reassert_cljs_test.cljc`, `flows_rollback_dirty_check_test.clj`, and the state-write cases of `flows_user_fx_lifecycle_settle_cljs_test.cljc` (`:64-71`).
- Add the tests the acceptance criteria name.

**Conformance fixtures** (`spec/conformance/fixtures/flow-*.edn`):

- `flow-frame-scoped.edn` becomes two ids.
- `flow-toggle-via-fx.edn` becomes a data gate.
- Rewrite `flow-lifecycle-emits-traces.edn`, `flow-frame-destroy-teardown.edn` and `flow-hot-reload-preserves-output.edn`.

**Spec rows that gates grade against source** move here, with the code:

- The Spec 009 error and warning catalogue rows for every deleted emitter. `scripts/check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py` checks both directions.
- `spec/API.md` and `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn` (`:866`, `:939`, `:1703-1711`): hand-edit both, then regenerate `spec/api-manifest.edn` with `generate!` in `implementation/scripts/api-manifest`. Never hand-edit the generated file.

**Consumers.** At trunk, 37 files under `skills/`, `docs/`, `tools/`, `examples/` and `testbeds/` name `:rf.fx/reg-flow`, `:rf.fx/clear-flow`, `flows-snapshot`, `flow-frame-not-live` or `re-frame.flows/flows`. Re-run that census rather than trusting this list.

- **The cart** (`examples/core/flows/core.cljs`, plus its README):
  - top-level `reg-flow`s, and `:flows` on its `frame-root`;
  - the discount as a data gate, with the events setting and dissoc-ing `[:cart :discount-rate]`;
  - `install-flows!` (`:80`) and `reload!` (`:323`) deleted, so `run` is init plus mount.
- **The realworld editors** (`examples/real-apps/realworld_http/article_editor.cljs:144-183`, `:284-310`; `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/article_editor.cljs:163-183`, `:268-281`):
  - Prefer a shared pure `can-submit?` plus a `reg-sub`. The submit handler already re-validates (`realworld_http/article_editor.cljs:412-413`). Don't manufacture flow consumers.
  - Delete the boot one-shot registration events and their commentary.
- **Testbeds:**
  - `testbeds/long_flow_w_failure/core.cljs:163-181`;
  - `testbeds/deliberate_throw/core.cljs:90-103`;
  - `tools/xray/testbeds/standard_epochs/core.cljs:281-301`;
  - `tools/xray/testbeds/two_frame_isolation/core.cljs:255-273`, where the re-seed workaround goes.
- **Xray** (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/static/flows/panel.cljs`, `registry.cljs`, its tests and its `spec/` pages): the flows panel reads the registrar and `frame-meta`, not `flows-snapshot`.
- **Pair MCP:** drop the "NOT flow" carve-out from `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/descriptors_data.cljs:1767` and `:1840`, and update `tool-descriptors.edn`, `handler_meta.cljs`, the README and `spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md` to match.
- **Docs:**
  - `docs/core/flows.md`, including the setup at `:65-75`, the frame-binding troubleshooting rows at `:232-234` and the hot-reload section at `:301-312`;
  - the docs playground smoke cell;
  - `docs/api/re-frame.flows.md`, `docs/core/25-from-re-frame-v1.md` and the other `docs/` hits.
- **Skills:** `skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/flows.md` and `fx.md`, the `skills/re-frame-migration/references/` hits, and `skills/re-frame2-pair/references/ops.md`. Their drift gates (`scripts/check_skill_*_drift.py`) will name what they pin.

**If it doesn't simplify, stop.** The implementation must not need a new frame-scoped side table of definitions, and it must remove the cart's installer and reload hook. If it cannot do both, stop and report back for a ruling rather than shipping part of the design.

**Out of scope, and not decided here:**

- Q4: whether machine and resource writes join the pending commit, and so whether `[:rf/settle-flows]` survives;
- the optional "settle only when an active input changed" refinement;
- the flow's own `:schema`;
- publishing memo rows at install;
- fencing at the pass boundary;
- map-keyed `:inputs`.

## Sequencing

- **Depends on** rf2-yl9dt, the spec bead, which carries the spec half of this ruling. Its §Activation text is the contract.
- **Hot-zone files touched:** `spec/API.md` with `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn` and `spec/api-manifest.edn` (one holding, graded together by `lint.yml`'s api-manifest job), and `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` (catalogue rows). It should not need `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn`, `implementation/deps.edn` or `.github/workflows/*`, because the flows artefact stays. If a new testbed or build is added, those become hot.
- **Cross-dossier:**
  - **conformance-fixture-grammar.** It moves the flows runner's observations (`implementation/flows/test/re_frame/flows_conformance_test.clj`) into a shared runner, and this bead rewrites five flow fixtures. Sequence the two, either order.
  - **durable-app-db-classification-static-or-runtime.** It changes flow-output classification declarations, which `reg-flow` stamps today. Sequence them.
  - **one-registry-top-level-reg.** Its frame-config activation item for HTTP interceptors (`:http-interceptors [ids]`) should share this bead's activation and validation code path, or follow it.
- **`spec/011-SSR.md`** is the one i/crlf file. If you touch it, edit it with the Edit tool or Python bytes, never `sed -i`.

## Evidence

**Read in source at trunk 89517e8f54:**

- `registry.cljc:26-30`, `:59`, `:97`, `:107`, `:115` and `:634-647`;
- `flows.cljc:261`, `:489` and `:664`;
- `fx.cljc:745`, `:784-810`, `:812-868` and `:1016-1041`;
- `tool_pair.cljc:873-880`;
- `router.cljc:4413`;
- `core.cljc:2131`;
- the cart at `:80`, `:163-183`, `:323` and `:338`;
- `flows_user_fx_lifecycle_settle_cljs_test.cljc:64-71`;
- `descriptors_data.cljs:1767` and `:1840`;
- the 37-file consumer census.

**Still needs a run:**

- the epoch-restore defect, reconstructed from the code; criterion 7 turns it into a test;
- the SSR client round trip, untested today (`implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/flows_integration_test.clj:114-126` covers server rendering only);
- all line-count estimates.

Gates are named in the acceptance criteria.

**Before believing a green**, predict the test and assertion-count delta from the diff. Then compare it against a baseline taken on the trunk this branch sits on after its final rebase.

title: SSR: delete ssr-handler's :version override, which can only cause version mismatches
description:
## Defect

`ssr-handler` takes a `:version` opt (`implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring.clj` ~166). `coerce-version` parses it tolerantly, so `"7"` is accepted (`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/payload_policy.cljc` ~721-790, with `resolve-version`). The client compares it against the compiled-in protocol version, so any host value other than that constant draws `:rf.ssr/version-mismatch` on every page (`check-version-fx`, `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/hydrate.cljc` ~518-541). The opt can only cause harm.

## Change

- Delete the opt, `coerce-version` and the resolution path, so the payload always carries the compiled-in `:rf/version`.
- Keep `:rf/version` and `:rf.ssr/check-version` (`ssr.cljc` ~193), because a cached old bundle meeting a new server is the case the check exists for.
- Update Spec 011 and the `ssr-handler` docs.

## Acceptance

- `git grep -n coerce-version` finds nothing.
- A hydration test still detects a real protocol mismatch.
- The ssr and ssr-ring suites stay green.

If `spec/API.md` or the manifest lists `ssr-handler`'s opts, update them; that holding is a hot zone.

title: Router diagnostics: a cyclic :rf.cofx or :rf/time-ms value overflows pr-str; use the content-free value summary
description:
## Defect

`implementation/core/src/re_frame/error.cljc` already has content-free summaries (`diag-value-summary` ~302, `type-of-value` ~357). The SSR cycle tests (`implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/diagnostic_cycle_cljs_test.cljs`) show the pattern.

## Change

Use the existing summary in both messages; a map-shape or integer-shape rejection does not need the contents. Ex-data keeps the raw value, since holding it prints nothing. Add no traversal machinery.

## Acceptance

title: Spec 010 and schemas docstring hygiene: abort wording, a nonexistent strict mode, the digest's same-host limit, Spec-Schemas registration, post-commit
description:
## Current

- `spec/010-Schemas.md:186` says "A failure at any step aborts the dispatch", but its own fx and sub rows skip the effect or substitute a value.
- `010:197` says "Strict mode re-raises". No strict mode exists.
- 010 §Digest states the cross-host limits but not the same-host one:
  - The function token is name-derived (`implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validator.cljc` ~81-120), so two closures from one function site with different captured bounds print the same token.
  - A registry-keyword reference keeps its bytes when the registry's definition changes.
  - So equal digests mean "equal serialised declarations", not equal validation behaviour, and `010:515`'s "Catches deploy-drift bugs" needs that qualification.
- `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:48` says spec-internal schemas are registered through `reg-app-schema` and read with a `{:frame f}` form. Nothing registers them.
- The facade docstring (`implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas.cljc:6`) calls candidate validation "post-commit". It runs before the candidate is installed.

## Change

Correct each sentence in the present tense. For the digest, put the same-host limit beside the cross-host warning; add no function-code hashing or schema versioning.

## Acceptance

Each sentence matches the code, and the docs gates stay green.

Hot zone: `spec/Spec-Schemas.md`.

Checked at trunk f4e5adad0a.
notes:
== WORKER epoch-schemas-contract, 2026-10-19 02:00:34 AUSEST — done, PR #11506 (commit b442cca21b)
Every cited site re-derived at tip 0b46c53541; each premise held as filed (no delta against the bead).
- spec/010-Schemas.md Validation order: "aborts the dispatch" replaced. A failure emits a structured error; steps 1 to 4a stop the event, an fx-args failure skips only that effect, a sub return-value failure replaces only that sub's value with nil (per Per-step recovery).

title: Story stepper: read the epoch restore cursor, not the ring's newest record, so a second step-back restores the right state
description:

title: Machines: timeout transitions skip required coeffects
description:
Audited merged PR #11499 at 0b46c53541ded29bb804e0680fd17d10f889fdf4. Its explicitly deferred normalization work records this existing behavior gap in rf2-i674g. This separate open bug tracks the user-visible failure; it is not a regression introduced by the documentation/smoke changes.

A registered state with :timeout / :on-timeout does not ensure the named timeout guard/action's :rf.cofx/requires, or the destination state's entry-action requirements. The same machine expressed with :after ensures them. A required generated fact therefore silently becomes nil: a guard can reject a valid timeout, and an action can commit incorrect durable data.

Concrete reproduction under the shipped plain-atom reset-runtime fixture:
- Register :audit/required as a recordable generator returning 42.
- Register a machine with initial :idle; :idle handles :go -> :waiting; :waiting has :timeout 500000 and :on-timeout {:target :done :guard :check}; named guard :check declares :rf.cofx/requires [:audit/required] and checks (= 42 (:audit/required (:rf.cofx ctx))).
- Dispatch [machine-id [:go]], then the timer's [machine-id [:rf.machine.timer/after-elapsed 500000 1 [:waiting]]].
Expected :done and one generator call. Actual :waiting and zero calls. Replacing the waiting node with :after {500000 {:target :done :guard :check}} reaches :done with one call.
The same paired probe for an :on-timeout action or :done entry action reaches :done but records :captured nil and calls the generator zero times; the :after controls capture 42 and call it once.

Evidence: cofx_attach.cljc:655 after-diet-for-event reads [:after delay-key] from the as-written machine. registration.cljc:953 indexes that machine, ignores validate-machine!'s return, and closes over it; validation.cljc:2553 lowers only its local copy. parallel's transition/birth normalization runs later, so it cannot repair the earlier coeffect ensure-set.

Focused JVM probe against an isolated archive of this exact merge: ai/pr-audit/pr-audit-sol-oct11-11499-timeout-cofx-1.clj; 4 tests, 22 assertions, 6 failures, 0 errors, process exit 3. All three direct-:after controls pass. No shadow-cljs run.

Small correction: derive coeffect requirements from the same lowered definition used by transition selection. The approved normalize-once route in rf2-i674g can supply that common definition; no second timer mechanism or new public API is needed. Add regression coverage for the timeout guard, action and target-entry cases, with :after controls.
close_reason: Already fixed on trunk by #11507 (rf2-i674g, 7b250470c6). This bead was filed against #11499 before that merge. Registration now lowers :timeout/:on-timeout onto :after once (parallel/normalise-definition), and the registrar entry, the handler and the ensure-set index all hold that one normalised value. So a timeout transition takes the same ensure path as the :after control in this bead's own reproduction: the :on-timeout guard's and action's :rf.cofx/requires and the destination's entry-action requirements are all ensured. #11507 added red-before tests showing the :on-timeout facts are ensured. #11512 (rf2-g09gm) later made the as-written refusal name :on-timeout. Nothing remains.

title: SSR: move realworld_http's hand-rolled payload (and, if clean, ssr-ring's build-payload) onto re-frame.ssr/hydration-payload
description:
#11518 (rf2-a1plt, a9541bc356) added the public re-frame.ssr/hydration-payload, (hydration-payload frame opts). It takes ssr-handler's payload options and wraps the payload-policy projection: allowlist, then :sensitive redaction, then the runtime-db projection under the explicit frame, plus :client-frame-id and :schema-digest. Both capability SSR examples and the tutorial now call it. Two callers still assemble the payload by hand.

1. examples/real-apps/realworld_http/ssr.cljc. It requires re-frame.ssr.payload-policy only for pattern-protocol-version, and builds its own payload: select-keys over ssr-app-slice-keys, a hand dissoc of [:auth :token], and select-keys over [:rf.runtime/routing :rf.runtime/machines]. So it ships routing and machines runtime-db children without the framework's serializable-durable projection, and its token redaction sits outside the :sensitive mechanism. The real-app example teaches the hand-rolled route rather than the public helper.

2. implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/payload.clj build-payload repeats the projection calls the helper now makes (apply-policy, then project-runtime-db under the explicit frame, then assemble).

Change. Move (1) onto rf.ssr/hydration-payload. Declare the payload allowlist as the {:payload [...]} option. Express the token drop through the framework's :sensitive declaration if realworld already declares or can naturally declare [:auth :token] sensitive; otherwise keep the one hand dissoc on top and say why in a comment. Keep the namespace docstring's point: this file is where a real app draws its payload boundary. For (2), make build-payload delegate to the helper only if that is a clean fit for the ssr-ring artefact's dependencies and its handler-construction validation. If not, leave it and record why in the close reason.

Acceptance. The realworld_http SSR path still hydrates. Its existing tests and the example compile sweep stay green. A server-rendered page's payload still carries no :auth :token: show this with a check that goes red if the redaction is removed. The ssr-ring JVM tests stay green if (2) changes.

The framework's projection now decides which runtime-db slices ship.

The token drop stays as ONE hand dissoc on top, with a comment saying why. realworld does classify [:auth :token] :sensitive (:auth/classify-token), but a classification REDACTS: the payload carries :rf/redacted in the token's place. Under :replace-frame-state that keyword becomes the client's [:auth :token], which fails AuthSlice's [:maybe :string], and the bearer interceptor would send it. Measured: in the planted run, with the dissoc neutralised, the classified pass shipped :token :rf/redacted and hydrate! installed it into the client app-db.

(2) ssr-ring build-payload: LEFT AS IS. Delegating is not a clean fit. build-payload takes VALUES (frame id + app-db + runtime-db), while the helper reads the LIVE frame. title: HTTP: parse JSON-typed 4xx/5xx bodies best-effort into :body, keeping the raw text at :body-text
description:
## Problem

Measured at trunk 3959d2a5bf.

Managed HTTP classifies by status before decode, so a 4xx or 5xx carries the raw response text at `[:error :body]` (`spec/014-HTTPRequests.md` § the classification order: "the caller decodes the raw `:body` themselves in the failure-handling branch"). So structured validation errors are parsed by hand, with host code:

- `docs/core/how-to/build-a-form.md`: `(js->clj (js/JSON.parse body) :keywordize-keys true)`;
- `docs/resources/tutorial/03-auth-and-forms.md`: a reader-conditional `JSON.parse` / Cheshire parse inside `failure->form-errors`.

Nearly every app with a server-validated form writes this.

## Change

When a 4xx or 5xx response's Content-Type is JSON-eligible (the same RFC 6839 rule the schema decode path uses, 014 § decode step 2), `:body` holds the parsed, keyword-keyed value. When parsing fails, `:body` holds the raw string. `:body-text` always holds the raw text.

- Classification is unchanged: still `:rf.http/http-4xx` / `:rf.http/http-5xx`, never `:rf.http/decode-failure`. An HTML 404 stays a string.
- The `:rf.http/max-decoded-keys` interning cap applies to the parse.
- Off-box, both `[:error :body]` and `[:error :body-text]` stay unconditionally omitted, as raw error bodies are today (the off-box disposition stamp in `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc`).

**Breaking:** the type of `:body` for JSON error responses.

## Spec and docs that move with it

- `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md`: the classification order, the failure-category table's 4xx/5xx rows, and the paragraph quoted above.
- The HTTP failure shape in `spec/Spec-Schemas.md`, if it types `:body`. **Hot zone.**
- `docs/api/re-frame.http.md`, `docs/async/http.md`, and the two docs pages above, whose examples lose their host parsing.

## Acceptance

- A 422 with `application/json` delivers a map at `:body` and the raw string at `:body-text`.
- Malformed JSON under a JSON Content-Type delivers the raw string at `:body`, still classified by status.
- An HTML 404 delivers a string.
- The key cap is respected.
- Off-box egress omits both slots.
- HTTP suites (JVM and `npm run test:cljs`) green, and the docs examples run without host parsing.

## Sequencing

Hot zone: `spec/Spec-Schemas.md`, only if it types the slot. Effort S.

Malformed JSON, a blank body, a cap overflow, any other Content-Type and an ABSENT Content-Type all leave the raw string at :body. title: Keep frame initialization handlers on their target during a Reagent render
description: Merged-PR audit #11535, merge 3c2550942e5e331f214257227baafaa8a21aa707. Reagent's new re-frame.views.provider/current-frame always tries the rendering component's tree-frame before rf.frame/*current-frame*. The router binds *current-frame* to the envelope's target for the handler chain (router.cljc:2843-2861,2891), but it does not end the enclosing Reagent render. Consequently creating a child frame with :initial-events while a parent-scoped view sets up runs the child's initialization handler synchronously under that still-rendering parent component. The handler's ambient resolver returns the parent's frame despite the child's handler binding. This is reachable through make-frame's supported construction-time setup path, without a view directly issuing dispatch-sync: frame.cljc/run-setup-events! explicitly dispatches each setup step synchronously with :frame forced to the new id. Concrete measurement: reused the views-flush-frame worker's existing compiled Node runtime, with the test-runner entry removed and test namespaces excluded; no shadow-cljs command ran. A real reagent.dom.server/render-to-string of a view under :audit/parent creates :audit/child with one initial event. Inside that event the dynamic binding is :audit/child but (rf/current-frame-id) is :audit/parent; the render succeeds as created child. The focused probe exits 1 on the assertion that the initializer must resolve :audit/child. A positive control creating :audit/control outside a render resolves :audit/control by both reads. The merge and the compiled worker head 22ef1defe76344ef604aa32e047b967d6d094fd9 have identical blobs for provider.cljs, frame.cljc, router.cljc and the Reagent adapter; the compiled current-frame function was inspected for the new tree-first order. Supporting log: ai/pr-audit/pr-audit-sol-oct11-11535-init-frame-2.log (the first, broader loader attempt timed out and is not a behavioral verdict). The same scope reader drives ambient subscribe, dispatch and capture-frame, so initialization code can read or address the parent. Small correction: at the in-flight event-handler boundary, preserve the envelope's carried frame ahead of any enclosing rendering component (for example using the existing event-ownership scope); keep provider-first lookup for ordinary view renders. Pin the child-frame :initial-events case with two distinct frame ids and an ambient read/child dispatch. No new public option is needed.
close_reason:
Merged in PR #11543 (rebase merge, commit 44b370995d). An event handler that a Reagent render runs synchronously, such as a make-frame :initial-events step called from a view, now resolves the frame its envelope targets, not the rendering component's tree.

How it works: frame.cljc's existing event-ownership scope (call-with-event-owner-token) records :render-host, the component rendering when the handler started, through the Reagent-only :adapter/current-component hook. provider.cljs's current-frame skips the tree lookup for exactly that component. A component that starts rendering inside the handler still reads its own tree, and ordinary renders keep #11535's tree-first order. There is no new public option, and router.cljc is untouched.

Spec 006 § One frame-resolution rule for React hooks gains one sentence. The matching spec/002 sentence was routed to machines-data-spawn, which holds 002.

Evidence: the new handler_frame_in_render_dom_cljs_test went red at trunk; inside the child's step, both reads returned the parent and the dispatch missed the child. It is green with the fix (4 tests / 9 assertions). test:cljs ran 6196 tests, test:browser 779 (+4 tests / +11 assertions, as predicted), core JVM 1195, and the fast-PR spine passed. CI was green at 84 checks.

UIx and Fresco already resolve the dynamic frame before the tree, so they were unaffected.

title: SSR: a custom :html-shell receives the escaped payload tag prebuilt in its opts
description:
## Problem

Measured at trunk 8fc6369484.

`ssr-handler` takes `:html-shell`, a `(body-html payload-edn opts) → string` that replaces the default envelope (`implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring.clj`, docstring around line 191; default `re-frame.ssr.ring.shell/default-html-shell`).

A custom shell receives the payload as raw `pr-str`'d EDN. It must re-emit the hydration `<script>` itself:
- under the id `"__rf_payload"` (`re-frame.ssr.constants/payload-script-id`);
- with the EDN-aware script-body escaping, so string content cannot close the element and unsafe token-position breakouts fail loudly.

`shell.clj`'s docstring says custom overrides "MUST emit the payload `<script>` under this id". Getting either the id or the escaping wrong breaks hydration or opens an injection. `:html-shell` appears 25 times across 13 files.

The shared helpers already build the right tag (`re-frame.ssr.html-helpers/payload-script-tag`, used by the default shell and by Fresco's server `document`).

## Change

- Pass prebuilt parts to a custom shell in its `opts`: at least `:payload-tag`, the finished escaped `<script id="__rf_payload">` element. Add the rendered `<html>` / `<body>` attribute strings only if they remove the same class of mistake.
- A custom shell splices `(:payload-tag opts)` instead of re-emitting the script.
- Keep `:html-shell` and the trusted-content contract as they are. No sanitizer, no validation grammar.
- The default shell uses the same part, so there is one builder.

This also settles the question of whether `:html-shell` stays beside the four trusted hooks and `reg-head`: it stays, and it is given parts.

## Spec and docs that move with it

- `spec/011-SSR.md` §Trusted shell hook contract, and the passage under §Client-side hydration boot helper that names the `__rf_payload` id. Use the Write/Edit tools or Python bytes on this file: it is the one `i/crlf` file in the tree, so never `sed -i` it.
- `ssr-handler`'s and `default-html-shell`'s docstrings.
- The SSR guide's custom-shell example in `docs/ssr/`.

## Acceptance

- A custom shell that only splices `(:payload-tag opts)` hydrates.
- A payload containing `</script>` inside a string round-trips safely through that tag.
- The default shell's output is byte-identical to today.
- `ssr-ring` and SSR suites green.

## Sequencing

`ssr-handler`'s docstring and Spec 011's options text are also edited by rf2-bkrwd (one `:frame` option) and rf2-0gkvv (redirect), so sequence after both have merged.

Effort S. Additive.
notes:

== WORKER SUMMARY (ssr-debug-gate-shell, branch worker/ssr-debug-gate-shell): https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/11560

Disposition: done.

What changed:
- The pipeline builds (re-frame.ssr.html-helpers/payload-script-tag payload-edn) once and passes it to every shell as :payload-tag in its opts.
- default-html-shell splices it. Called directly without :payload-tag, the shell builds the same tag, so payload-script-tag stays the one builder.
- :html-shell and the trusted-content contract are unchanged.
- No attribute strings were added. A shell that ignores the attribute bags still hydrates, while every shell must ship the payload, so only the payload tag removes a mandatory hand-rolled step.

Evidence: re-frame.ssr.ring.custom-shell-payload-tag-test, written first.
- A shell that splices only :payload-tag hydrates a client frame to exactly the shipped slice, including the title "</script><script>alert(1)</script>".
- No literal breakout reaches the body, and :payload-tag equals the helper's output.

Docs that moved with it: the ssr-handler and default-html-shell docstrings, docs/api/re-frame.ssr.ring.md, Spec 011 §Trusted shell hook contract and §Client-side hydration boot helper, and docs/ssr/concepts.md §The page shell (which gains a splicing example).

title: Routing: one spelling for don't scroll (:scroll false); retire :preserve and the bespoke scroll error
description:
## Problem

Measured at trunk 8fc6369484. Paths are under `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/`.

"Don't scroll" has two spellings:
- **`:scroll false`** on a route or a navigation. `resolve-scroll-strategy` (`scroll.cljc:150`) turns it into `::suppress`, so the `:rf.nav/scroll` fx is not emitted. It appears 20 times in 10 files.
- **`:scroll :preserve`**, a strategy value. The fx receives it and does nothing (the `:preserve nil` arm, `scroll.cljc` around line 524). It appears 8 times in 5 files.

The `:rf.nav/scroll` fx also carries a bespoke always-on error, `:rf.error/unsupported-scroll-strategy`. It is made of `supported-scroll-strategies`, `unsupported-strategy-reason` and `emit-unsupported-strategy!` (`scroll.cljc:316-440`), plus a docstring defending it. The error fires only when an app emits `:rf.nav/scroll` itself with a bad `:strategy`, because `reg-route` and the navigate gate already check `:scroll` where it is written. It appears 26 times in 12 files.

## Change

- **One spelling.** `:scroll false` means don't scroll. Retire `:preserve`, so the strategy vocabulary is `:top` / `:restore` (`rf.routing.address/scroll-strategies` and the fx schema `rf.routing.nav-fx-schemas/scroll-args`). A `:preserve` reaching `reg-route` or the navigate gate is refused there with a message naming `false`.
- **Ordinary error.** An unknown `:strategy` at the fx throws, so it surfaces through the ordinary always-on `:rf.error/fx-handler-exception`. Delete `:rf.error/unsupported-scroll-strategy` and its three supporting definitions.
- **Keep the fx's argument `:schema`**, because `:rf.nav/scroll` is a public fx id user code can emit directly.

## Spec and docs that move with it

- `spec/012-Routing.md` §Scroll restoration.
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md`: the error catalogue row for `:rf.error/unsupported-scroll-strategy` goes. **Hot zone.**
- `spec/Conventions.md`, if it reserves the error id. **Hot zone.**
- The routing guide pages that show `:preserve`.

## Acceptance

- `:scroll false` on a route and on a navigation emits no scroll fx.
- `:scroll :preserve` is refused at `reg-route` and at the navigate gate, naming `false`.
- `[:rf.nav/scroll {:strategy :bogus}]` emitted directly yields one `:rf.error/fx-handler-exception`, on a schemas-less production build too.
- No `unsupported-scroll-strategy` reference remains outside history.
- Routing suites, JVM suite and `npm run test:cljs` green.

## Sequencing

Hot zone: `spec/009-Instrumentation.md`. Otherwise isolated to `implementation/routing/`.

Effort S, about 100 lines and one error id gone. Breaking for apps spelling `:preserve`.

title: Schemas: teach one sensitivity declaration for an app-db path (classification), not a second schema prop
description:
## Ruling

Mike ruled on 2026-10-20 that an app-db path is declared sensitive once, by classification, and that one declaration covers both egress and validation-failure traces.

The code already does this. What remains is to stop teaching the second declaration, and to fix the comments and spec text that still describe two routes. A schema's `:sensitive?` prop stays the route for transient values that no path declaration can reach: events, coeffects, HTTP bodies and machine `:data`.

## Problem

Measured at trunk cb9cb3c074.

**App-db failure traces already read the frame's classification.** `project-through-registry` (`implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc:273-312`, called at `:1217-1225`) does this, and Spec 010:404 says so. It adds that "the schema prop stays an additional way to mark a slot".

**Yet the double declaration is still taught:**
- `docs/core/how-to/validate-with-schemas.md:290-302`;
- `spec/010-Schemas.md:400` and `:422-423`;
- `spec/015-Data-Classification.md:365`, which gives a schema ownership of "a slot's own validation-failure-trace redaction";
- `implementation/schemas/test/re_frame/schemas_failure_paths_test.clj:43`.

**The examples already declare once.** RealWorld classifies `[:auth :token]` by effect only (`examples/real-apps/realworld_http/core.cljs:149-153`), and login classifies its draft password by effect (`examples/core/login/model.cljc:465-473`).

**Stale comments** still say failure traces "read the schema directly, not this registry": `implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc:575-587` and `implementation/core/src/re_frame/privacy.cljc:15-18`.

## Change

**Teach one route for app-db.** A sensitive app-db path is a classification, and its failure traces follow it.
- **Docs:** rewrite the how-to section and the Spec 010 passages to that.
- **Spec 015:365:** narrow it to transient values and machine `:data`.
- **Existing app-db schemas:** a `:sensitive?` prop on one keeps working as an additional mark. Remove it from the teaching. Add no warning: it is legal code.

**Fix the two stale comments.**

**Point at the test's primary route.** Keep `schemas_failure_paths_test.clj:43` as the test of the additional route, and add one test showing a classification-only path redacted in a failure trace, if none exists.

**Stay coherent with static classification.** rf2-o5rtr's stage 2 deletes the elision registry that `project-through-registry` walks. When that lands, the failure-trace route has to move to the static declarations with it. That is rf2-o5rtr's work; this bead only states it in Spec 010 so the dependency is visible.

## Spec and docs that move with it

- `spec/010-Schemas.md` (`:400-423`) and `spec/015-Data-Classification.md:365`. Neither is a hot zone.
- `docs/core/how-to/validate-with-schemas.md:290-302`.
- If any wording in `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` or `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` says app-db failure-trace redaction comes from the schema, fix it. **Hot zones**, so touch them only if a sentence is wrong.

## Acceptance

- No doc or spec teaches declaring an app-db path sensitive twice.
- A failure trace on a classification-only path shows `:rf/redacted`.
- The two comments describe the registry route.
- `mkdocs build --strict`, `check_doc_slugs.py` and the schemas JVM suite green.
