title: Bundle isolation reads require-graph claims from each build's manifest.edn; grep stays for elision claims
description:
## Ruling

Mike approved on 2026-10-21 that `implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs` answers require-graph questions ("core must not require a feature", "nothing may require `tools/`") from each browser build's `manifest.edn` (`:sources` per module). Emitted-byte grep scans, with their paired on/off controls, stay for dead-code-elimination claims.

## Problem

Measured at trunk c383c6a92e.

- The gate greps sentinel strings in the counter release (`check-bundle-isolation.cjs:24-30`, `main` at `:1470`). It never reads `manifest.edn`: the word does not occur in the file, while `implementation/scripts/lib/read-release-bundle.cjs`'s own test plants one beside a bundle (`_read-release-bundle.test.cjs:52`).
- `ARTEFACTS` (`:88-671`) has 22 entries. 21 are namespace-level claims: the artefact's namespaces must not be in the counter build at all. One, `trace-tooling` (`:339`), is var-level: core requires `re-frame.trace.tooling` statically, and only Closure drops the bodies (`:326-332`). The three consumer allow-list budgets (`flows` `:154`, `http` `:184`, `epoch` `:220`) count emitted strings.
- A grep can only prove absence of a literal that is live, so each entry needs a positive control (`POSITIVE_CONTROL`, `:715-751`). 18 of them read a module of the `:bundle-isolation-positive-control` release (`implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1136-1182`), one source file each under `implementation/scripts/bundle-isolation-positive-control/src/` (18 files). Four read an example bundle; `realworld-resources` is released in `test:bundle-isolation` (`implementation/package.json:42`) only for the `resources` control.
- shadow-cljs 3.4.10 (`package.json:21`) writes `manifest.edn` into every `:target :browser` output dir: one map per module with `:sources`, the classpath-relative source paths compiled into it. That answers a namespace-level claim exactly. `implementation/scripts/lib/edn.cjs` already reads EDN as structure.

## Change

- Each namespace-level entry names its forbidden sources: classpath-relative prefixes such as `re_frame/flows.cljc`, `re_frame/story/` and `node_modules/@xyflow/react/`. The gate reads `out/examples/counter/manifest.edn` through `edn.cjs` and fails on any `:sources` entry matching a forbidden prefix.
- The liveness signal moves too: each forbidden prefix must name a real file or directory in its artefact's source tree (or in `node_modules`), so a rename fails loud rather than passing vacuously.
- Keep one positive control: a test in `check-bundle-isolation.test.cjs` copies a real manifest to a temp dir, injects one forbidden source, and expects red.
- Keep grep for `trace-tooling` and the three allow-list budgets, with the `trace-tooling` module as their on-control.
- Delete a file under `bundle-isolation-positive-control/` only once the entry it controls reads the manifest. Remove its module from `:bundle-isolation-positive-control` in the same commit. Drop `realworld-resources` from the release list once `resources` no longer uses it.
- Keep `assertPositiveControlComplete`'s fail-closed idea: every entry declares a manifest claim or a grep claim with its control.
- Node targets write no `manifest.edn`, so a node-target isolation claim keeps grep. This gate reads none today.
- `check-uix-reagent-free.cjs` and `check-login-bundle-isolation.cjs` are out of scope.

## Spec and docs that move with it

- `spec/Conventions.md:1792` and `:1865` both end "The check is a grep over the advanced-compile output". Say the graph claim is read from the build manifest and the elision claim from the emitted output. **Hot zone.**
- `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1136-1182` (the control modules). **Hot zone.**
- `TESTING.md:29` ("grepping for symbols").
- The gate's header comment (`check-bundle-isolation.cjs:1-50`) and the `POSITIVE_CONTROL` commentary (`:673-714`).

## Acceptance

- The real counter manifest passes. The mutation test goes red on an injected `re_frame/flows.cljc`, and on an injected `re_frame/story/registrar.cljc`.
- A planted `[re-frame.flows]` require in `examples/core/counter/core.cljs` turns the real gate red (planted-fault control; revert before merge).
- A forbidden prefix that names no real source fails the gate.
- `trace-tooling` and the allow-list budgets still grep and still fail on their own plants.
- Every deleted control file had its entry moved to the manifest first.
- `npm run test:bundle-isolation` green.
notes:
== DISPATCHED (mayor), 2026-10-21 20:07:10 AUSEST: worktree bundle-isolation-manifest, branch worker/bundle-isolation-manifest, clustered with rf2-5c7vd, holding implementation/shadow-cljs.edn (the positive-control build) and the classifier pair. HELD FOR THE MAYOR: the two spec/Conventions.md sentences (:1792, :1865) wait until the resources-work-on-owner worker (rf2-w9wec) merges and releases Conventions.md; the worker writes them in its PR body. RE-DISPATCH FENCE: do not put a second worker on this bead or branch until that worker reports.
== WORKER SUMMARY (bundle-isolation-manifest), 2026-10-21 20:49 AUSEST: done, PR #11616.
WHAT CHANGED. check-bundle-isolation.cjs reads out/examples/counter/manifest.edn through lib/edn.cjs (new readBuildManifest in lib/read-release-bundle.cjs, which refuses any shape it cannot read as a module list). 21 of 22 entries are graph claims over 30 forbidden classpath-relative sources: a plain path names one file, a trailing `/` a directory, matched by whole path. Each must resolve on the classpath shadow-cljs.edn declares (a :source-paths root, node_modules, or a :dependencies jar in the local Maven repository, read from the zip central directory); a dead one fails the gate by name. A manifest not listing re_frame/core.cljc is refused. trace-tooling stays the one elision claim (grep "trace-events"); the flows/http/epoch allow-list budgets stay grep. assertPositiveControlComplete stays fail-closed: exactly one claim per entry, a control module for every elision claim and nothing else, well-formed sources, no module/sentinel/source with two owners. 17 of 18 control files and modules deleted, one family per commit, each with its entry: (1) schemas, machines, http, resources (bundle-controlled, no files; realworld-resources left the release list); (2) the seven tooling siblings and derivation composers; (3) routing, flows, epoch, ssr, fresco; (4) story; (5) xyflow, elkjs, zprint, editscript.

At baseline it carried 2 hits only because seventeen sibling modules depended on it and Closure hoists a constant several modules share into their common base module. Elision sentinel drifted to trace-eventz: exit 1, on-control 0/1.

title: Artefacts register lifecycle contributions; Spec 002's destroy order becomes a pre-/post-dead phase contract
description:
## Ruling

Mike approved on 2026-10-21 that core's hard-coded lifecycle rosters give way to a minimal internal ordered list of per-artefact contributions, e.g. `{:id :phase #{:pre-dead :post-dead} :preflight-config :on-frame-registered :on-frame-destroyed :test-reset :config-keys}`. `destroy-frame!` and `upsert-frame!` iterate it; `:config-keys` takes over the `rf.frame/add-config-keys!` calls.

Spec 002's cross-port MUST on the internal teardown order becomes an observable phase contract: pre-dead and post-dead hooks plus three constraints. Machine exits run against a live container. URL ownership precedes routing teardown. Epoch terminal evidence is captured after dissoc (today it is snapshotted before the dissoc and published after it). Delete Spec 002 §Two destroy-hook verbs. The `spec/Runtime-Subsystems.md` host-transient descriptor becomes exactly this list. No capability, dependency or plugin framework.

## Problem

Measured at trunk c383c6a92e. Paths are under `implementation/core/src/re_frame/` unless stated.

**Core names every artefact's hooks in four rosters:**
- **Teardown:** `run-destroy-recipe!` (`frame.cljc:4597-4851`, restated in `destroy-frame!`'s docstring, `:4382-4562`). One hook runs before the dead flip (`:4644`), ten after it in a fixed order (`:4671-4771`), then the epoch snapshot (`:4788`) and publish (`:4816`) around the dissoc.
- **Registration:** `frame-registered-hook-keys` (`:3030-3041`).
- **Preflight:** `:routing/preflight-frame-config!` and the `:revalidate-on` check (`:3343-3402`).
- **Test reset:** `reset-hook-table` (`test_support.cljc:302-419`), 13 rows.

`add-config-keys!` (`frame.cljc:2994`) has five artefact callers.

**28 of the 183 keys in `late_bind/directory.cljc` exist for these rosters:** 13 destroy, 2 registration, 1 preflight, 12 test-reset (the chained adapter reset is the 13th row). Their verbs follow no rule, which §Two destroy-hook verbs (`spec/002-Frames.md:877-889`) explains.

**The spec pins the internal order** ("a conformant port MUST mirror it", `002:781-784`). `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:4196-4204` gives the descriptor "Status: None".

**One more order is load-bearing:** Spec 014:811 runs http's frame sweep after resources' ledger cleanup. resources requires `re-frame.http.managed` (`resources.cljc:25`), so a load-ordered list runs http first.

## Change

- **The list:** one `^:no-doc` vector in `frame.cljc`, appended at artefact load and replaced by `:id` on reload. A second namespace may merge into its artefact's entry (resources publishes its reset from `resources/test_support.cljc:38`). Fns are called directly.
- **Destroy:** core keeps its own steps (claim, `:on-destroy`, dead flip, sub-cache and projection disposal, `:rf.frame/destroyed`, ring release, dissoc, failure report). It calls `(on-frame-destroyed id phase)` for `:pre-dead` members before the flip and `:post-dead` members after disposal, in list order, under today's best-effort boundary.
  - Machines joins both phases: its `:exit` cascade is pre-dead, its timer cleanup post-dead. Pre-dead members run inside the frame's own resolution, as machines does today (`frame.cljc:4145-4148`). The machines-absent fallback (`:4149-4165`) stays in core.
  - Routing is post-dead, so the dying frame no longer resolves as URL owner when it reconciles the listener (`routing/.../history.cljc:192-197`).
  - A post-dead fn may return a fn that core calls after the dissoc. Epoch snapshots in the first and publishes from the second.
  - Make http's sweep correct in either order (both paths suppress replies). Drop the resources half of 014:811.
- **Registration:** iterate `:on-frame-registered`. Resources reads only `:revalidate-on` (`resources.cljc:365-374`), so routing-first is no constraint.
- **Preflight:** call each `:preflight-config` at today's point. The artefact-missing refusals stay in core, probing `rf.features/feature-registry`, because a contribution cannot speak for an absent artefact.
- **Test reset:** the fixture iterates `:test-reset` and keeps its two dispose phases. The chained adapter row stays a fixture step.
- **Config keys:** the unknown-key warning reads the union of `:config-keys`. Delete `add-config-keys!`.
- A teardown failure's `:hook` names the contribution `:id` and phase.

## Spec and docs that move with it

- `spec/002-Frames.md`: `:776` and `:781-850` become the phase contract; delete `:877-889` and re-point its links (`spec/011-SSR.md:1373`, `:1377`; `spec/012-Routing.md:1925`); `:656`. **Hot zone.**
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2024-2025`. **Hot zone.**
- `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:4196-4204` gains the shape. **Hot zone.**
- `spec/Runtime-Subsystems.md:297-311` and its grading column `:313-326`.
- Hook names: `spec/011-SSR.md:745`, `:1412`; `spec/012-Routing.md:1924-1926`; `spec/013-Flows.md:143`; `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:811`; `spec/016-Resources.md:534`, `:631`; `docs/core/how-to/report-errors-in-production.md:212-213`.

## Acceptance

- A new artefact's teardown touches no core file. A test registers a throwaway contribution; its destroy, registration, preflight, reset and config-key members all take effect.
- The 28 keys go unless another reader keeps one (`:flows/reset-flows!`, `test_support.cljc:533`). `late_bind_drift_test.clj` green.
- Still green: `destroy-frame-runs-exit-cascades-in-reverse-creation-order` (`frame_lifecycle_test.clj:104`), the CLJS URL-listener teardown tests, the `:halted-destroy` tests in `frame_destroy_incarnation_jvm_test.clj`.

title: conformance: a :fixture/transport harness seam so the :rf.http/managed fixtures run the real Spec-014 fx (decode, :accept, retry on the controlled clock, abort)
description:
## Problem

The 11 `spec/conformance/fixtures/http-managed-*.edn` fixtures stub the effect they are named for. Each registers its own `:rf.http/managed [[:noop]]` body and its own canned-reply body, and routes one to the other with `:fx-overrides`; the runner installs those bodies over the framework's registrations (`implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_runner.cljc:441-457`). So no Spec 014 code runs, and a port with no managed-HTTP code passes all 11. That was probed twice, independently, at trunk 9b51da3393 through the real `re-frame.conformance-runner/run-fixture` with the JVM host map: 11/11 pass with every `:rf.http/*` fx unregistered.

rf2-mn2ht.62 (ruled 2026-10-10, option A) relabels Checklist Q8, the conformance README, the implementor skill and the 11 fixture headers so they say this honestly. **This bead is the real fix that ruling deferred**: make the corpus grade the Spec 014 lifecycle, so that "AI-implementable from the spec alone" (the corpus's stated purpose, `spec/conformance/README.md:4`) holds for managed HTTP.

**Deferred on purpose.** Pick it up when certifying a Q8 port becomes a concrete goal: a second port, or the implementor skill being used against HTTP. The reference implementation's HTTP is already graded by its own lane (`implementation/http/test/`: 54 test files at 200a67df2d, 16 of which drive the real transport against an in-process `HttpServer` on the JVM), so nothing is at risk meanwhile.

## Why a seam, not a deletion

Running the real `:rf.http/managed` with no stub and no override fails today (probe row E at 9b51da3393: `:final-db {}`), because the fx has no server to reach. The fixtures need a substitute WIRE, not a substitute fx.

The counterpart is `:fixture/clock` (rf2-bmqv), which replaces the Spec 005 §Clock-abstraction primitives with a recording realisation. rf2-bmqv's bar: "It observes at the clock boundary the spec already names, not a port-internal timer table — so the assertion is about a normative seam rather than an implementation detail." **Spec 014 names no such boundary today**: a ripgrep over `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md` for `seam|transport abstraction|schedule-after|Clock abstraction` hits only line 484 (the internal `:aborted?`-cell abort-precedence "implementation seam") and incidental mentions. So this bead must CREATE a named boundary before it can observe at one.

## Design direction (settle in a short design pass before coding)

- **The contract lives with the harness, not the app API.** The fixture key specifies portable inputs and observations: per-attempt canned wire responses (status, status text, headers, and a text OR binary body), timeout and network-failure steps, abort/cancellation, and observations of attempt count and request shape. A port's conformance harness adapter realises them with its own internals; it need not expose the reference's functions or its promise/future representation. No new public var, no `spec/API.md` or manifest row. Spec 014 gains at most a short paragraph, probably in §Testing, naming the boundary: one request attempt in, one normalised wire response out, plus abort.
- **Reference realisation.** Route `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc` through that boundary between `prepare-body!` (`:1703`) and the host fetch (`transport_cljs.cljc` / `transport_jvm.cljc`), above `handle-response!` (`:1522`). Its result destructure is `{:keys [ok? status status-text headers body-text body-binary]}` (`:1534`). **A text-only response map is not enough**: `:body-binary` is consumed (`:1534`, `:1579`).
- **The async shape is the real design risk**: a JVM `CompletableFuture` against a Fetch promise. The seam must allow a CONTROLLED completion, not only an immediate return, or abort-before-completion and timeout cannot be expressed.
- **HTTP backoff must move onto the Spec 005 clock primitive, or `:fixture/clock` cannot reach retry.** At trunk 200a67df2d, backoff arms with `rf.interop/set-timeout!` (`transport.cljc:1352`) and cancels with `rf.interop/clear-timeout!` (`:1247`, `:1396`, `:1408`). `:fixture/clock` redefines only `rf.interop/schedule-after!` / `cancel-scheduled!` (`conformance_runner.cljc:1607-1608`). Those two are `def` aliases holding the same fn values (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/interop.clj:189-190`, `interop.cljs:164-165`): separate vars, so a `with-redefs` on the alias never reaches a direct `set-timeout!` caller. Switch backoff, both arm and cancel, to `schedule-after!` / `cancel-scheduled!`, and have Spec 014 §Retry and backoff say backoff rides the Spec 005 clock abstraction (it does not mention it today). That also makes Implementor-Checklist H2's "CLJS schedules on the same timer seam the machine `:after` implementation uses" true at the var level, not only at runtime. Check separately whether the per-attempt `:timeout-ms` timer needs the same move on each host.
- **Sequence after rf2-mn2ht.61** (the runner ignores unknown top-level fixture keys; in progress on 2026-10-10). Before it lands, a new `:fixture/transport` key is silently ignored and a mis-wired fixture passes vacuously. After it lands, the runner's known-key set must include `:fixture/transport`, or every rewritten fixture fails loudly. Document the key in `spec/conformance/README.md`'s top-level key list. If `FixtureFile` in `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` gains the key, that file is a HOT ZONE, so sequence it; `:fixture/clock` never added itself there, so follow that precedent unless there is a reason not to.
- **Sequence after rf2-mn2ht.62.** It rewrites the same 11 fixture headers and the Q8/README prose to say managed HTTP is "not yet corpus-graded"; this bead reverses that prose as its last step.

## Fixture rewrite

- The 11 fixtures drop their `:rf.http/managed` and canned-stub bodies and their `:fx-overrides`, and declare wire responses instead. Their `:fixture/expect` blocks (final app-db, reply envelopes) largely survive.
- `abort-by-request-id` becomes a real cancellation test: issue, hold the attempt open, abort, then assert exactly one `:status :cancelled` reply carrying `{:kind :rf.http/aborted :reason :user :request-id <id>}`, and no success reply even if the wire later completes (Spec 014 §Abort precedence). rf2-mn2ht.62 has already fixed that fixture's impossible order, in which the cancelled reply ran before the abort was dispatched.
- `retry-exhaustion` and `retry-recover` run on `:fixture/clock`: `:assert-timers` on the backoff timer, `:fire` it, count attempts.
- **Both runner matchers are order-preserving SUBSET matchers**: `check-trace-emissions` and `check-effects-routed` (`conformance_runner.cljc:655-678`, "Extras are tolerated"). Where the contract is "exactly one reply" or "exactly N attempts", assert the count or the absence explicitly. That is rf2-bmqv's lesson: count LIVE timers rather than armed ones, because a subset match does not exclude a later cancellation.

## What it lets the corpus witness

Classification order (status before decode), decode and `:accept`, retry count on a controlled clock, abort precedence and envelope synthesis. It also covers two bug classes no stubbed fixture can see:

- failure-path privacy (rf2-kiepc: denylisted headers on the `:rf.http/replied` trace for a 4xx). Its close reason records that the canned stub "never reaches `dispatch-failure!` or `emit-reply-trace!`", so a dual-host pin of the real failure path is blocked until a seam exists;
- `:after` reclassification routing (rf2-mn2ht.12).

## Acceptance

title: skill(re-frame-migration): inventory Step 3 M-11 row still says subscribing plain defn views throw at first render, contradicting guided-views-m11 and SKILL.md since rf2-vqe4f
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 2a6fd908a6. Priority 2: the skill contradicts itself, and following the stale text leads a migration into an unrequested whole-tree rewrite.

## Skill file and section

skills/re-frame-migration/references/inventory-and-plan.md, the Step 3 table's M-11 row (line 94). Also SKILL.md:129, the leaf-routing row for guided-views-m11.md.

## What it says

inventory-and-plan.md:94:

> Reagent view components that `subscribe` / `dispatch` **in their render** but are registered as plain `(defn …)`, not `reg-view` — **count them to SIZE the M-11 `defn` → `reg-view` sweep**, often the largest single conversion in the app (one per subscribing component). COMPILE-SILENT: each compiles 0/0 and throws `:rf.error/no-frame-context` at first render ...

Against this:

- guided-views-m11.md:11, "What already works": "While a view renders, its ambient `subscribe` / `dispatch` resolve the frame from the component tree — the closest enclosing `frame-provider` (SCOPE) or `frame-root` (ENSURE) — for a `reg-view` and a plain `(defn …)` Reagent fn alike".
- SKILL.md:159, in the anti-patterns: "Converting plain Reagent fns to `reg-view` reflexively. That is O-2, opt-in: a plain `defn` under a provider reads its frame already."
- SKILL.md:87, breaking-changes.md:39 (the M-11 row) and guided-views-m11.md:236 ("fix the call sites, do not over-convert") say the same.
- SKILL.md:129 still describes the leaf as "M-11 — subscribing plain `defn` views → `reg-view`".

## What happened (generic)

On a ~170-file app, a first inventory run followed the row. It sized M-11 as a whole-tree `defn` → `reg-view` conversion and planned it that way. A second run read guided-views-m11 and re-sized M-11 to about 200 deferred callbacks across 38 files, fixed by capturing the frame at render time, with no blanket conversion. Following the row produces an unrequested O-2 conversion, which breaks cardinal rule 3 (smallest correct diff) and brings in the function-position call-site hazard that guided-views-m11.md:240 describes.

## Evidence

- `git log -S'throws `:rf.error/no-frame-context` at first render' -- skills/re-frame-migration/references/inventory-and-plan.md` shows the row was added by d7ee14aaf8 on 2026-06-28.

- `git grep -n -i 'first render' origin/main -- skills/re-frame-migration/`, filtered for defn, plain or M-11, has exactly one hit: inventory-and-plan.md:94.

title: skill(re-frame-migration): floor-gate Check 5 cites an unsourced React 19 browser floor, and mechanically bumps a CI browser pin that may mirror a supported host floor
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 2a6fd908a6.

## Skill file and section

skills/re-frame-migration/references/floor-gate.md, Check 5 "Runtime-host floor" (line 97, with the host-inventory bullets at lines 103-107), and Check 6 GO / NO-GO (lines 117-118).

## What it says

Line 97:

> re-frame2's modern runtime targets React 19, and **re-frame2 inherits React 19's minimum-browser floor** (~Chrome 90+ / current stable): the bundle relies on modern JS that an older browser does not have. **Audit your CI test-runner's PINNED browser version** ... **and bump it to one React 19 supports** — current stable is the safe target. This is ... a mechanical version bump in the CI config (the skill flags the stale pin and edits the CI config to the target; CI's next run is what proves it), **not** a NO-GO blocker.

Line 107:

> A host whose declared floor sits below React 19's is not bumped like the CI browser: its acceptance item shows whether it runs the migrated bundle with the providers it loads, and raising that floor is the author's decision.

## What happened (generic)

Two problems surfaced at the floor gate of a ~170-file v1 app:

1. **The floor number has no source.** Nothing names the API, the compiler output level or the artefact that sets "~Chrome 90+", so a migrator cannot check it against a host, or say whether a given old host is in or out.
2. **The CI pin can be a host's coverage.** That app's CI test browser was pinned on purpose to match the floor of a supported host. Check 5 calls the CI pin a mechanical bump to current stable. Line 107 says a below-floor host is the author's decision. The leaf does not say which rule wins when the CI pin is that host's only automated coverage. A mechanical bump would silently remove that coverage, and nothing would report it.

## Evidence

- `git grep -n -i -E 'chrome ?(8|9)[0-9]|minimum-browser|browser floor|browser-capability floor|minimum browser' origin/main -- . ':!.beads'` gives floor-gate.md:97, its field case at :99, and one unrelated Fresco design note on timer resolution. Nothing in spec/, migration/ or docs/ states a browser floor. (Control: the same grep finds :97 itself.)
- The close reason of rf2-cbao5, the change that added the host inventory to Check 5, records: "The corpus never states the browser floor, so it got no change."
- A token scan of the non-test sources under implementation/ finds no API that would put the floor at Chrome 90: structuredClone, Object.hasOwn, WeakRef and FinalizationRegistry are each in 0 files, queueMicrotask (Chrome 71) is in 5 and AbortController (Chrome 66) is in 2, and no `:output-feature-set` is set. (Control: `reg-event` matches 553 files.) This does not show that the number is wrong, because React or the Closure output level may set the floor. It shows that nothing in the tree says what sets it.

## Suggested change

1. Name what sets the floor and cite it. That could be React 19's stated browser support, the Closure output feature set that re-frame2's build emits, or a specific API that the runtime calls. If none can be cited, drop the number and say: "the floor is whatever the optimized migrated bundle needs; establish it by running that bundle on the host".
2. In Check 5, before the bump instruction, add this rule: if the CI test-browser pin was chosen to match a supported host's floor, it is that host's coverage, so do not bump it mechanically. Handle it under the host-inventory bullets (lines 103-107), and leave any change to that floor to the author. Make the same exception in Check 6's GO wording and NO-GO note, both of which now call a stale CI pin a mechanical bump.

Related: rf2-cbao5 (closed). It added the host inventory but did not source the floor or cover a CI pin that matches a host's floor.

The "~Chrome 90+" floor CANNOT BE SOURCED (checked at origin/main 2a6fd908a6):

They feature-detect their newer APIs with fallbacks: queueMicrotask ('"function" === typeof queueMicrotask ? queueMicrotask : ...'), reportError (reportGlobalError fallback), WeakMap (PossiblyWeakMap = ... : Map), MessageChannel / setImmediate in the scheduler. Unguarded needs are ES2015 built-ins (Symbol.for, Map, Set, Object.assign, Promise).

- No runtime API sets it: a census of every js/ global across the 263 non-test implementation/**/src .cljs/.cljc files finds nothing newer than about Chrome 71 used unguarded (globalThis, queueMicrotask, AbortController, TextEncoder, URL, fetch). The two js/reportError calls are guarded by (fn? (.-reportError js/globalThis)) at implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:1165-1166 and implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/mount.cljs:314-315. A method census for .at / replaceAll / randomUUID / findLast / toSorted / hasOwn / allSettled / structuredClone / WeakRef / FinalizationRegistry / AggregateError found 0 (control: the same expression found (.getRandomValues js/crypto ...) at implementation/core/src/re_frame/derivation/egress.cljc:207). The commit that introduced Check 5 claimed Array.prototype.at, Object.hasOwn and structuredClone; none is in today's runtime.

So Check 5 now takes the bead's fallback: the floor has no published version number; it is whatever the optimized migrated bundle needs (the language level the project's build emits, its shadow-cljs :output-feature-set, and the APIs the bundle calls), established by running that bundle on the host. title: skill(re-frame-migration): SKILL.md Boot and init says keep an intended override of a library id "in a later image" with no recipe for a single-frame image-less target and no fold-into-the-ported-library route
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 0783705626.

## Skill file and section

- skills/re-frame-migration/SKILL.md §Boot and init, line 112 ("One v1 habit stops an id working").
- Its two outbound routes: docs/core/images.md §When two registrations collide (lines 51-70) and §Composing images: the later one wins (lines 312-330); and skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/images.md §Composing patterns (line 51).

## What it says

- SKILL.md:112: "v1 let a later registration of an id replace an earlier one, so an application namespace could override a library's. A single-frame target names no image and resolves the registrar live ... So inventory duplicates before boot: fix an accidental one at its source, and keep an intended override — the definition v1 actually ran, the last one loaded — in a later image."
- docs/core/images.md:61-63: "You have three ways out ...: rename one id, narrow each frame to its own slice with an explicit image, or compose a later image that overrides the other."
- docs/core/images.md:327-328: "A collision within one image is still an error: an image must resolve to one registration per `(kind, id)`. To override, compose a later image."

## What happened (generic)

The case is a v1 app that customises a library's fx (or event, or sub) by re-registering the library's id in an app namespace. In v1, last load wins. In v2 it raises `:rf.error/ambiguous-registration` at use. For this case the migration skill gives one destination, "in a later image", and no recipe. On a single-frame, image-less target, the three ways out cost more than the skill suggests:

- Rename is not available: the library itself emits or dispatches the id.
- A later image means moving the whole app frame onto explicit `:images`, from live-store resolution to a sealed generation. Every other cross-namespace duplicate then fails assembly with `:rf.error/image-duplicate-id`, not at use. The base image must also exclude the overriding namespace, because one image cannot hold both registrations, so the override has to move out of whatever feature namespace it sits in (or into an inline-registration image).

Nothing in the migration skill walks through that conversion, says what it changes for the rest of the app, or offers the cheaper route that a migration usually has to hand. The overridden library is often a v1-era library the migration already ports or overlays under its library decisions. In that case the app's behaviour can be folded into that single ported or overlaid registration, and the frame stays image-less.

## Evidence

- SKILL.md:112 and the docs sections above are the only override guidance in skills/re-frame-migration and migration/from-re-frame-v1. A grep for "later image" there finds only SKILL.md:112.
- spec/008-Testing.md:233 confirms that only the test fixture's frame lets the latest registration win; every `make-frame` frame raises the ambiguity.
- Observed on a ~170-file app: its duplicate census (rf2-soqmk) found app overrides of library fx ids among 19 duplicate (kind, id) pairs, and the migration needed a destination for each.

## Suggested change

Under SKILL.md:112 (or in a reference it links), add a short decision for an intended override of a LIBRARY id:

1. If the migration ports, overlays or replaces the library, fold the app's behaviour into that one registration and delete the app's re-registration. The frame stays image-less.
2. Otherwise, adopt explicit images. Give the recipe: base image `{:select-ns {:include [...] :exclude [<override ns>]}}`, then an override image after it (or inline `:registrations`), and assert the override in `:rf.gen/shadows`. State the cost: the frame becomes sealed, so every other cross-namespace duplicate fails assembly.
3. Name the census cross-check that finds these pairs: `rf/ambiguous-registrations`.

Related: rf2-soqmk (the duplicate-registration census whose "intended override" disposition this recipe would serve).
close_reason: Changed in PR #11658 (commit 158dbe40f2), taken into the rf2-soqmk cluster because it edits the same sentence. Premises verified. docs/core/images.md:58 says an explicit image selecting both namespaces fails with :rf.error/image-duplicate-id, and :327 says a collision within one image is an error and the fix is to compose a later image. spec/008-Testing.md:233 says only the fixture frame lets the latest registration win. 'later image' appeared only at SKILL.md:112 across the skill and the corpus. The census's intended-override disposition now gives two routes. (1) If the plan already ports or patches the library, fold the app's behaviour into that one registration; the frame keeps no explicit images. (2) Otherwise, use a base image whose :select-ns :excludes the overriding namespace, then a later image (or inline :registrations) carrying the override, asserted in :rf.gen/shadows. The note says the override moves to its own namespace first, and that assembly then refuses any other pair one image selects, so the census must be settled first. SKILL.md Boot and init names both routes. Gates exit 0.

## What it says

The table covers two `sub` shapes only:

    (sub <vector>)                       → (subscribe <vector>)   ; EXCEPT inside a reg-sub signal/input fn, per M-71 (below)
    (sub {:re-frame/q ::id :param 1})    → (subscribe [::id 1])   ; vectorize the query-map

## What happened (generic)

v1's `re-frame.alpha/sub` also accepts a bare keyword, and a 2-arity id plus params map. Neither shape has a row. A worker who reads the table as a rename ("just switch the namespace", as the corpus row for vectors says) turns `(sub :kw)` into `(subscribe :kw)`. That is wrong: v2's `subscribe` takes a query vector, and its 2-arity is `[query-v opts]`. So the correct rewrite is `(subscribe [:kw])`, and a renamed `(sub ::id {:param 1})` would pass the params map as `opts`. Observed on a ~170-file app that used the keyword shorthand for no-parameter subs.

## Evidence

* v1 source, re-frame 1.4.3 jar, re_frame/subs/alpha.cljc:21-31:

      (defn sub
        ([q]
         (if (keyword? q)
           (sub q {})
           ...))
        ([id q]
         (sub (assoc q ::rf/q id))))

  So `(sub :kw)` is `{:re-frame/q :kw}`, and `(sub ::id {:param 1})` is `{:re-frame/q ::id :param 1}`, the query-map the existing row already handles.
* v2 source, implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc:1998 onward: `subscribe` is `([query-v] ...)` (reads `(first query-v)` for its error payload) and `([query-v opts] ...)`, described there as "The 2-arity is `[query-v opts]` ONLY — no `vector?` shape-discrimination on the first arg".

Control: the same scope finds the existing map row at auto-call-site-rewrites.md:142 and README.md:1217/:1233.

## Suggested change

Add two rows to the leaf's M-23 table, and the same two to the corpus §M-23 table:

    (sub ::id)                           → (subscribe [::id])     ; keyword shorthand = {:re-frame/q ::id}
    (sub ::id {:param 1})                → (subscribe [::id 1])   ; 2-arity id + params = the query-map row

Add a note that neither is a rename: v2's 2-arity `subscribe` is `[query-v opts]`, so a renamed 2-arity alpha call silently treats the params as opts. The M-71 signal-fn carve-out applies to these rows as it does to the vector row.

title: skill(re-frame-migration): M-21/M-70 say author with reg-interceptor but give no recipe for a v1 interceptor constructor fn; the skill never names {:factory f} or [id arg] refs
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 0783705626.

## Skill file and section

- skills/re-frame-migration/references/breaking-changes.md, the `->interceptor` façade row (line 132).
- auto-cross-cutting.md M-70 step 2 ("Read each value's own `:id` where the value is defined, or at the constructor call that builds it").
- guided-interceptors-subs.md §M-21.

## What it says

breaking-changes :132: "Author the before/after work with `(rf/reg-interceptor id descriptor)` and reference it by **id** in the event/frame `:interceptors` chain."

## What happened (generic)

v1 apps define interceptor **constructors**, for example `(defn with-timeout [ms] (->interceptor :id :with-timeout :before …))`, used in chains as `(with-timeout 500)` and `(with-timeout 30000)`. The recipe above leaves two bad choices:

- one registered id per call site, which loses the shared definition;
- one id with a fixed descriptor, which loses the argument.

re-frame2 already has the right shape: a `{:factory f}` descriptor plus `[id arg]` chain refs (spec/001-Registration.md:507-511; docs/core/interceptors.md §Parameterized interceptors). The corpus lists `{:factory f}` once in passing (README:1143), but the migration skill never names it, nor the `[id arg]` ref.

- A fixed-string search for `:factory` in skills/re-frame-migration finds 0 hits, and `factory` or "returns an interceptor" in auto-cross-cutting.md and guided-interceptors-subs.md also finds 0. Control: `reg-interceptor` hits twice in each of those two files.
- spec/001-Registration.md:511: "The `:factory` form defines a parameterized interceptor family: `factory-fn` receives one argument (the ref's `arg`…)".
- Observed on a ~170-file app's shared-interceptors unit.

Add a row to M-21 / M-70: "A `defn` that returns `->interceptor` from its arguments → `(rf/reg-interceptor :app/with-timeout {:factory (fn [ms] {:before …})})`, and each call `(with-timeout 500)` in a chain → the ref `[:app/with-timeout 500]`." comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
New evidence from a later unit of the same downstream migration (skills retrospective pass 4; suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 0783705626.

This item covers a v1 interceptor CONSTRUCTOR: a defn that returns `->interceptor` from data arguments. A second shape has the same gap: a v1 higher-order interceptor COMBINATOR, a fn that takes another interceptor and returns a wrapped one, for example `(when-ix pred? inner-ic)`, which runs `inner-ic` only when a predicate holds. Such combinators are common in v1 shared-interceptor namespaces.

Why the constructor recipe does not cover it:

- v2 chain entries are refs only, and a `:factory` receives its ref's `arg` verbatim. `resolve-factory` in implementation/core/src/re_frame/interceptor_registry.cljc (around line 359) calls `((:factory descriptor) arg)` with no ref resolution. So `[:app/when-ix [pred :inner/ic]]` hands the factory a keyword, not an interceptor, and nothing in the migration skill says how to compose two registered interceptors.
- A fixed-string search for "combinator" in skills/re-frame-migration finds 0 hits, and "higher-order" finds none about interceptors. Control: "reg-interceptor" hits twice in references/guided-interceptors-subs.md. M-21 there (lines 154 and 163) says only "register the original body with `reg-interceptor`".

The shape the unit proposed (observed on a ~170-file app):
- Fold the combinator into the inner interceptor's own factory, and pass the gate as data: `(rf/reg-interceptor :app/audit {:factory (fn [{:keys [gate]}] {:after (fn [ctx] (if (gate-holds? gate ctx) (audit ctx) ctx))})})`, referenced as `[:app/audit {:gate :only-when-dirty}]`.
- Make the gate DATA (a keyword or map the factory interprets), not a fn value. spec/002-Frames.md:2636 requires the `arg` to be EDN-serializable wherever a ref is serialized, and override matching compares refs in canonical form, so a fn-valued arg breaks both.

Suggested addition to this item's fix: beside the constructor row, a combinator row. "A v1 fn that wraps another interceptor → give the wrapped interceptor a `:factory` and pass the combinator's parameter in its arg map (`[id {:gate …}]`). One registered id per wrapped behaviour. There is no ref-to-ref composition."

title: remove-worker-worktree.sh/.ps1 run git worktree remove without core.longpaths, so on Windows a worker tree with a path over 260 characters becomes a husk
description:
Follow-up found while working rf2-uhq5a (suggestion-grade, P3).

## What

scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh and scripts/remove-worker-worktree.ps1 run `git worktree remove` (the .sh at the `git -C "$MAYOR_ROOT" worktree remove [--force] "$WT"` calls) without `-c core.longpaths=true`, and neither script carries a long-path pre-check. A search of both files for `longpath`, `too long`, `260` and `MAX_PATH` finds nothing (grep exit 1); the control, `husk` over the same two files, finds 105 and 99 lines.

So on a Windows host whose Git for Windows has no `core.longpaths` set (this machine: `git config --show-origin core.longpaths` prints nothing), a worker tree whose deepest path exceeds 260 characters becomes a husk on removal. The scripts already classify the outcome after the fact (REMOVE_PARTIAL, exit 3, read from the remove's exit code); this item is about preventing it.

## Measured (git version 2.56.0.windows.3, Windows 11)

Throwaway repo, one worktree, one file at a 393-character path inside it:

- `git -c core.longpaths=false worktree remove --force <wt>` exits 255 with `error: failed to delete '<wt>': Filename too long` (the message names the worktree root, not the long path); the admin dir `.git/worktrees/<id>` is gone, `git worktree list` no longer lists it, the shallow file and `.git` file were deleted but the deep directories remain, `git -C <wt> status --porcelain` exits 128, and `git worktree prune -v` prints nothing.
- The same with `-c core.longpaths=true` exits 0 and the tree is fully removed.

Source: builtin/worktree.c at v2.56.0 (byte-identical in git-for-windows v2.56.0.windows.3), `remove_worktree`: `ret |= delete_git_work_tree(wt);` then the comment "continue on even if ret is non-zero, there's no going back from here." then `ret |= delete_git_dir(wt->id);`.

## Suggested change

Pass `-c core.longpaths=true` on the scripts' `git worktree remove` calls (harmless off Windows: the setting is a Git for Windows option and other builds ignore an unknown core key), in both the .sh and the .ps1, and re-run the scripts' own tests. Whether any status read the scripts make inside a worker tree needs the same flag is for the worker to check.

description:
Two prose descriptions of core's clj-kondo export still describe the reg-* family the way an older config did. Found while working rf2-phqz0, which fixed the export's `:unresolved-var` exclude list. Both files sat outside that change's write scope.

- `implementation/core/resources/clj-kondo.exports/day8/re-frame2/README.md`, under "What it does", names `reg-event-db` first among "The registration macros (`reg-event-db`, `reg-sub`, `reg-fx` and the rest of the `reg-*` family)". `reg-event-db` is no longer a macro: it is a `^:no-doc` `def` throwing stub in `re-frame.core`. The ONE event form is `reg-event`.
- The repo-root `.clj-kondo/config.edn` header comment describes core's export as "the `re-frame.core` reg-* family as `do`". The export carries no `:lint-as` entry for the family. Each registration lints as an ordinary call, with no `do` shape, which is what its own `:lint-as` comment explains.

Fix: change those two sentences so they describe the export as it is. Prose only, so no gate is affected; check links by hand if any are touched (the README's root is `implementation/`, which is `check_readme_links.py --ci` territory).

title: skill(re-frame-migration): runtime-smoke-test.md:20's injected window 'error' listener does not say it must be installed before the bundle runs; one added after load misses every boot-time throw, and no minimal CDP event set is given
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (a suggestion, not a work order). Verified at re-frame2 origin/main fd1d1565f1. Observed on a ~170-file Reagent app's boot smoke, driven by an agent over raw CDP.

## Skill file and section

skills/re-frame-migration/references/runtime-smoke-test.md, §The boot smoke-test phase, the "does it boot without throwing?" paragraph (line 20).

## What it says

runtime-smoke-test.md:20: "Steps 1 and 8 below are a **plain browser-console** job: load the dev build, watch the console for the `:rf.error/*` throws step 1 enumerates, and reload with an injected `window` `'error'` listener to capture the throwing stacks. Any CDP / devtools tool (or manual devtools) does it".

## What happened (generic)

The paragraph does not say when the listener has to be in place. A listener added from the console or a CDP evaluate after the page loads misses everything the bundle throws while it boots: registration throws at namespace load, and errors in the init events. Those are exactly the errors step 1 hunts. The worker got a complete capture only by installing it before navigation with CDP `Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument`. The capture was a `window` `'error'` listener in the capture phase, an `unhandledrejection` listener, and `console.error` / `console.warn` wrappers. An agent with no browser MCP also has to work out which CDP domains to enable, and the leaf does not list them.

## Evidence

- The worker's harness: the capture installed with `Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument` before navigation recorded the boot-time console, exceptions and failed requests. A listener added after load sees only what fires after it.
- De-dup: no item mentions installing the capture before the bundle runs. Searches for `addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument`, `evaluateOnNewDocument` and "before the bundle" hit nothing relevant.

## Suggested change

In runtime-smoke-test.md:20, say that the capture must be installed before the page's scripts run, for example CDP `Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument` or Puppeteer/Playwright `evaluateOnNewDocument` / `addInitScript`, and that one attached after load misses boot errors. Add the minimal CDP set for an agent without a browser MCP:

- `Runtime.enable` (`exceptionThrown`, `consoleAPICalled`);
- `Log.enable` (`entryAdded`);
- `Network.enable` (`loadingFailed`, responses with status >= 400).

close_reason: Landed in PR #11706 (day8/re-frame2), branch worker/smoke-boot, commit 'the boot smoke installs its error capture before the page's scripts run'. runtime-smoke-test.md's does-it-boot-without-throwing paragraph now says the capture must be installed before the page's scripts run (CDP Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument, Puppeteer evaluateOnNewDocument, Playwright addInitScript, then navigate). title: skill(re-frame2-pair): two small doc gaps: setup.md:34's external-path warning prints only when the classpath is computed (silent with a warm .cpcache), and nothing says read-sub [:rf/machine id] on a never-started machine is a plain :ok? true nil
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (a suggestion, not a work order). Verified at re-frame2 origin/main fd1d1565f1. Two minor gaps in re-frame2-pair, observed on a ~170-file app.

## 1. setup.md: the external-path warning prints only when the classpath is computed

**File and section:** skills/re-frame2-pair/references/setup.md §The preload (line 34).

**What it says:** "Not `:extra-paths ["…/preload"]`: tools.deps prints `WARNING: Use of :paths external to the project has been deprecated` for every `:paths` or `:extra-paths` entry outside the project".

**What happened:** The app still had an external `:extra-paths` entry for the preload, and a downstream checklist expected that warning. The watch printed no warning, because the CLI reused the classpath cached in `.cpcache` and never recomputed it. A checklist that expects the warning can misread its absence as "the entry is gone" or "wrong file".

**Evidence:** The worker's watch log printed no warning, with `.cpcache` warm and the entry still present in deps.edn. The closed item rf2-luo6 already relied on the same behaviour when measuring this warning ("re-run with -Sforce and .cpcache cleared, so not a cache hit"), but the skill does not say it.

**Suggested change:** Say "prints ... when the classpath is computed (a cold `.cpcache`, or `-Sforce`); a cached classpath prints nothing".

## 2. A registered machine that never started reads as a plain `nil`

**File and section:** skills/re-frame2-pair/references/recipes.md §"Inspect this machine" (lines 182-194), and the `subs/read` row in references/ops.md (line 39).

**What it says:** "Inspect this machine" step 3 reads the snapshot with `read-sub {sub: "[:rf/machine :auth]"}`. Neither it nor the ops.md row says what a never-started machine returns.

**What happened:** For a machine that is registered but never started, `read-sub [:rf/machine <id>]` returns `{:ok? true :value nil}`. That is the same as for a machine that is absent. re-frame-migration's runtime-smoke-test.md step 2 (line 26) explains the three causes of an empty snapshot, but the pair skill, which owns the read, does not.

**Suggested change:** Add one sentence to recipes.md step 3 (and the ops.md row): "a registered machine that has not started, or that finished, reads `:ok? true :value nil`. Confirm registration with `list-handlers {kind: "machine"}` and tell the cases apart from the trace (`:rf.machine/started`, `:rf.machine/destroyed`)."

De-dup: no item covers the `.cpcache` caveat for this warning, or a never-started machine's `read-sub` result.

close_reason:
Landed in PR #11710, in its first commit.

(1) setup.md §The preload now says the external-path warning prints only when the classpath is computed: a cold .cpcache, a changed deps.edn, or -Sforce. So a missing warning does not show the entry is gone.
- Source: `validate-paths` in clojure.tools.deps (deps.clj, clojure-tools 1.12.4.1618) prints the warning. It runs only during classpath computation, which the CLI skips when .cpcache is warm.
- Measured on one external :extra-paths entry: the cold run printed the warning, the warm run printed nothing, and -Sforce printed it again.

(2) recipes.md "Inspect this machine" step 3 and the ops.md subs/read row now say that read-sub [:rf/machine id] reads a plain :ok? true with :value nil for a machine with no snapshot. The step also says how to tell the cases apart: list-handlers picks out an unregistered id, and the :rf.machine/started and :rf.machine/destroyed traces separate the other two.
- Source: the :rf/machine sub is (get-in runtime-db (snapshot-path machine-id)), in implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines.cljc, and read-sub! validates only the sub-id.
- JVM probe: never started → nil, unregistered id → nil, destroyed → nil, started → :idle, finished → :done.

Correction to the bead's suggested wording: a FINISHED singleton does not read nil. It rests with its final snapshot (rest-machine in lifecycle_fx/finalize.cljc), and final_singleton_rest_test.clj pins this. The docs say so.

title: senior review: ssr: server-side rendering core
description:
SENIOR-DEVELOPER REVIEW of one slice of the tree. Part of the review sweep rf2-r5cc2, which partitions implementation/, tools/, examples/ and skills/ into slices; this bead owns exactly the slice below, and its siblings own the rest.

SLICE:
- implementation/ssr/**

FOCUS: Rendering, the hydration payload policy and its path-precise :payload permit, render-state, the emitter (Spec 011, Spec 015 §SSR). A security boundary: weight fail-closed behaviour.

PERSONA. A senior Clojure/ClojureScript developer who did not write this code, reading it as its next maintainer and as a programmer who has to use it. Judge it against the project stance (CLAUDE.md), quoted verbatim:

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every
> last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.

So record material, actionable insights only: a defect, a simplification that removes real weight, an ergonomic sharp edge a programmer (or the AI they use) will hit, a test that cannot go red, a doc or docstring that misleads. Not style preferences, not nagging diagnostics, not defensive belt-and-braces, not renames for taste.

LENSES, in priority order:
1. Correctness — error paths, concurrency, cleanup, and fail-closed behaviour on any security or privacy boundary.
2. Simplicity and clarity — dead code, duplication (within the slice or with another slice), accidental complexity, an abstraction that earns nothing.
3. Ergonomics — the API or tool as a programmer, or the AI they use, actually meets it.
4. Performance — hot spots on real paths, never at the expense of clarity.
5. Test rigour — a test that cannot fail, a gap on a branch that matters.
6. Comments and docstrings — per CLAUDE.md § Conventions & Patterns: present tense, the reason plus a spec pointer, no provenance, no restated spec.

METHOD. Read the slice's source first, then its tests, against the owning spec sections (spec/Ownership.md maps each surface to its spec). A finding is a CLAIM until checked: confirm each one at source, and confirm a behaviour claim with a quick REPL or test run where that is cheap. This is a read-only review: edit no file, and run only read-only commands and the slice's existing test lanes.

OUTPUT, recorded on THIS bead and never in a separate file: write the section to a file and append it with `bd update <this bead> --append-notes "$(cat <file>)"` (never `--notes`, which replaces). Head it `== SENIOR REVIEW FINDINGS (<datetime with zone>, trunk <short sha>)` and include:
- 0 to 15 numbered findings, most important first. Each gives: `path:line` (plus a short quote so it can be re-found by text), what is wrong, why it matters (the concrete failure or cost), the fix (a sketch is fine), size (S/M/L), confidence (verified / probable), and its lens.
- A short "looked at and sound" list, so the review's coverage is visible.
- Cross-slice findings, whose defect lives in another slice's files, in a separate list naming the owning slice. Do not act on them.

Then add the label `findings-recorded` and leave the bead OPEN: its findings become this slice's fix work, which the coordinator dispatches in clusters. If the slice needs nothing, record zero findings with the coverage list and close the bead with that as the reason.
notes:
== SENIOR REVIEW FINDINGS (2026-10-29 10:23:36 AUSEST, trunk 795c61b924) Slice: implementation/ssr/** (24 source files, 87 test files). Read against Spec 011 (§Payload scope, §:rf/app-db projection, §The render-tree → HTML emitter, §XSS at output boundaries, §Drain-time error classification) and Spec 015 §SSR and hydration are allowlist-first. The slice is byte-identical at 9657b27a5d (only a beads checkpoint landed between). Behaviour claims were checked with a JVM probe on the slice's own test classpath (clojure -M:test with the runner's main-opts overridden; exit 0) and, for react-dom parity, against the installed react-dom 19.3.0 (node, exit 0). FINDINGS (most important first) 1. on* attributes off a curated name list ride live — react-dom drops every on* name. [correctness / security boundary] S, verified. Where: implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/html_helpers.cljc:481 (event-handler-name-re "[Oo][Nn](?:[A-Z].*|-.*)"), :497 (event-handler-allowlist, ~130 names), :528 (event-handler-name?); pinned by implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_attr_filter_test.clj:28 (online="3" once="2" ... must survive). What: strip-prop? drops an on* name only if it is camel/kebab-shaped or on a hand-kept WHATWG list. react-dom 19.3.0 drops EVERY prop whose name is longer than two characters and starts o/O + n/N, on client and server alike (react-dom-client.development.js:22068, react-dom-server.node.development.js:1604: "!(2 < key.length) || ('o' !== key[0] && 'O' !== key[0]) || ('n' !== key[1] && 'N' !== key[1])"). Probe (JVM, this slice): render-to-string [:animate {:onbegin "alert(1)" :attribute-name "x" :dur "1s"}] => ; [:div {"onwebkitanimationend" "alert(1)" :onsearch "alert(2)" :online "3" :once "2"}] => all four emitted. Control: {"onclick" … :on-click …} => stripped. react-dom/server on the same props: ,
; it keeps only on (length 2) and data-on. Cost: the spec threat path (an attacker-controlled attribute KEY, Spec 011 §XSS at output boundaries) gets a live handler wherever the name is off the list — SVG onbegin/onend/onrepeat on / is a stock XSS payload, plus onwebkitanimation*/onwebkittransitionend, onsearch, onmousewheel, onscrollsnapchange…, and every future event. And online/once/only paint attributes the client never paints — the "drops fewer" direction Spec 011 calls a live vector of a roster "closed in both directions". Fix: replace the regex + list with react-dom's own rule — (and (> (count nm) 2) (#{"on"} (str/lower-case (subs nm 0 2)))) — keeping the grammar gate ahead of it for names carrying breakout characters so those still throw as Spec 011 requires. Deletes the ~70-line list; update the ssr_attr_filter_test pin (one/once/online/only now dropped, on kept), the html_helpers comments that defend keeping online/once, and optionally add the rule to a react_dom_probe fixture beside the boolean/javascript-url ones. The hyphenated custom-element path (react-dom paints string on* there; re-frame strips) is a separate, safer-direction choice — leave it. 2. project-render-exception! overwrites a buffered worse status with the render projection. [correctness] S, verified. Where: implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/error_listener.cljc:308 "(apply-error-projection! frame-id)" (drains, stamps worst, result discarded) then :340 "(let [public-error (apply-error-projection! frame-id trace-event)]" — the 2-arity (:248-251) stamps unconditionally and is what's returned. What: the code drains the buffer first precisely so an earlier fault "is not silently dropped", then immediately overwrites its status. Spec 011 §Drain-time error classification: "The worst buffered failure decides … a server fault anywhere … takes the error arm whatever 4xx follows it." Probe: server frame with a custom projector mapping :rf.error/ssr-render-failed → 404; a buffered :rf.error/handler-exception, then project-render-exception! => public status 404, response :status 404. Controls: the same handler fault settled alone => 500; handler fault + a buffered ssr-render-failed settled through flush-response-result! => 500 (worst wins there). Cost: only with a custom projector that maps render failures to a 4xx — exactly the pattern reg-error-projector's own docstring shows (reading [:tags :exception ex-data]). E.g. a sub that throws mid-render recovers to nil and buffers a 500, the view then throws the app's not-found ex-info → 404 served, server fault masked. The default projector maps render failures to 500, so default apps are unaffected. Fix: project the render event, combine with the drained buffer via worse-public-error, stamp once, return the worse one. 3. canonical-number paints JVM scientific notation where the client paints decimals. [correctness / hydration parity] S, verified. Where: implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/hash.cljc:76 ":else (pr-str number)", and its docstring :56-61 ("vanishingly rare … no cheap normalisation closes it"). What: any non-whole double with |x| < 1e-3 or |x| ≥ 1e7 prints JVM-style. Probe (JDK 21): 0.0005 => "5.0E-4" (client "0.0005"); 12345678.5 => "1.23456785E7" (client "12345678.5"); 1730000000.123 => "1.730000000123E9" (client "1730000000.123"); 1e21 => "1.0E21" (client "1e+21"). render-to-string [:div 0.0005] =>
5.0E-4
; a style number 12500000.5 => width:1.25000005E7px. Cost: text children diverge, which React reports as a hydration mismatch and repairs by client re-render of the root — fractional epoch seconds, large money amounts or small ratios are ordinary view values. Attribute and style numbers diverge silently (React neither patches nor reports attribute-only divergence). Fix: on JDK ≥ 19 Double.toString gives the same shortest digits as JS, so the gap is spelling only: for a finite double emit (.toPlainString (BigDecimal. (Double/toString d))) with a trailing ".0" stripped when the JS exponent is in [-7, 20], and JS's "de+n"/"de-n" form outside it. Correct the docstring's residual note. (Confirm the project's JDK floor; see NOT SETTLED.) 4. hydration-payload on a dead frame returns a payload the client is guaranteed to refuse, with a diagnostic that points away from the cause. [ergonomics] S, verified. Where: implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc:183-220 (hydration-payload; docstring: "a frame that is not live projects as fully redacted"); pinned by implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_hydration_payload_test.clj:74-78. Probe: live frame => {:rf/version 1 :rf/app-db {:articles [1 2]}}; after rf/destroy-frame! => {:rf/version 1 :rf/app-db :rf/redacted}; the client's own guard on that payload (hydrate/malformed-hydration-payload-reason) => "the :rf/hydrate payload's :rf/app-db slice is not a map (got clojure.lang.Keyword); hydration rejected". The sibling projection, render-state/project, throws :rf.error/frame-destroyed for the same frame (render_state.cljc:293-308, which records why: half-projected output for a dead frame is worse than a loud one). Cost: hydration-payload's audience is the host running its own lifecycle; "render, destroy, then build the payload" is the natural ordering slip, and it ships a page whose hydration silently fails, reported only on the client as a malformed payload. Fix: throw :rf.error/frame-destroyed at the hydration-payload door (the same liveness check render-state uses), keeping project-app-db-egress's whole-slice redaction as the inner fail-closed layer; update the pinned test. 5. project-runtime-db's 1-arity and project-routing-egress's nil-frame verbatim arm are a fail-open path only tests use. [simplicity / security boundary] S, verified. Where: implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/payload_policy.cljc:633-637 (1-arity, ambient resolve-current-frame), :493-499 + :511-513 (nil frame-id → slice rides verbatim), and the docstring at :615-621 that explains the two arms fail in opposite directions. What: every production caller passes the explicit frame — ssr.cljc:220, render_state.cljc:333, ssr-ring payload.clj:86 (grep of "project-runtime-db " over implementation/ and tools/). The 1-arity is called only from tests (ssr payload_policy_cljs_test, ssr_machine_snapshot_projection_test, ssr_route_slice_projection_test, plus resources, routing and core tests). Cost: a security-boundary projection carries an ambient-frame convenience and a classified-route-rides-raw branch, plus the prose defending them, for no production caller. Fix: drop the 1-arity and the nil verbatim arm (nil frame → project-egress, which fails closed); tests pass the frame explicitly (:rf/default where they mean it). The test edits reach the resources, routing and core slices' test files — sequence with them. 6. The JVM emitter hook-up is a dynamic require wrapped in catch Throwable for a hard dependency. [simplicity] S, verified (by reading). Where: implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/emit.cljc:1177-1182 "(try (require 're-frame.substrate.plain-atom) ((requiring-resolve …) render-to-string) (catch Throwable _ nil))". What: re-frame.substrate.plain-atom lives in core (implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/plain_atom.cljc), which ssr/deps.edn depends on unconditionally, and it requires nothing from ssr; the CLJS branch already requires it statically (emit.cljc:39, :1184-1185). Cost: a genuine load failure is swallowed and resurfaces later as :rf.error/no-hiccup-emitter-bound, far from its cause; plus a reader conditional that earns nothing. Fix: one unconditional :require of re-frame.substrate.plain-atom and a plain set-hiccup-emitter! call on both hosts. 7. edn-carryable? admits keywords and symbols whose printed form does not read back. [correctness, low] S, verified. Where: implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/wire.cljc:172-173 "(keyword? v) true / (symbol? v) true"; its docstring (:200) claims exactly (= v (read (pr-str v))). Probe: (edn-carryable? [(keyword "a b")]) => true, but it reads back as [:a b]; through the render-state wire, {:rf/app-db {(keyword "a b") 1}} serialises and deserialises as {:a 1} — a silent key rename, where the contract (render_state.cljc ns doc) promises refusal at projection, never a silent wrong value. Control: (keyword "ab") => true and round-trips. Cost: niche, but keywordised third-party JSON keys with spaces or odd characters are how such keywords arrive. Fix: for a keyword or symbol, test the printed form round-trips (or match it against the reader's token grammar). title: senior review: fresco: the re-frame-native view layer
description:
SENIOR-DEVELOPER REVIEW of one slice of the tree. Part of the review sweep rf2-r5cc2, which partitions implementation/, tools/, examples/ and skills/ into slices; this bead owns exactly the slice below, and its siblings own the rest.

SLICE:
- implementation/fresco/** (src, test, test_kit, testbed, scripts, spec, resources)

FOCUS: Fresco's view model, boundaries and HMR, its test kit and its own spec tree.

PERSONA. A senior Clojure/ClojureScript developer who did not write this code, reading it as its next maintainer and as a programmer who has to use it. Judge it against the project stance (CLAUDE.md), quoted verbatim:

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every
> last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.

So record material, actionable insights only: a defect, a simplification that removes real weight, an ergonomic sharp edge a programmer (or the AI they use) will hit, a test that cannot go red, a doc or docstring that misleads. Not style preferences, not nagging diagnostics, not defensive belt-and-braces, not renames for taste.

LENSES, in priority order:
1. Correctness — error paths, concurrency, cleanup, and fail-closed behaviour on any security or privacy boundary.
2. Simplicity and clarity — dead code, duplication (within the slice or with another slice), accidental complexity, an abstraction that earns nothing.
3. Ergonomics — the API or tool as a programmer, or the AI they use, actually meets it.
4. Performance — hot spots on real paths, never at the expense of clarity.
5. Test rigour — a test that cannot fail, a gap on a branch that matters.
6. Comments and docstrings — per CLAUDE.md § Conventions & Patterns: present tense, the reason plus a spec pointer, no provenance, no restated spec.

METHOD. Read the slice's source first, then its tests, against the owning spec sections (spec/Ownership.md maps each surface to its spec). A finding is a CLAIM until checked: confirm each one at source, and confirm a behaviour claim with a quick REPL or test run where that is cheap. This is a read-only review: edit no file, and run only read-only commands and the slice's existing test lanes.

OUTPUT, recorded on THIS bead and never in a separate file: write the section to a file and append it with `bd update <this bead> --append-notes "$(cat <file>)"` (never `--notes`, which replaces). Head it `== SENIOR REVIEW FINDINGS (<datetime with zone>, trunk <short sha>)` and include:
- 0 to 15 numbered findings, most important first. Each gives: `path:line` (plus a short quote so it can be re-found by text), what is wrong, why it matters (the concrete failure or cost), the fix (a sketch is fine), size (S/M/L), confidence (verified / probable), and its lens.
- A short "looked at and sound" list, so the review's coverage is visible.
- Cross-slice findings, whose defect lives in another slice's files, in a separate list naming the owning slice. Do not act on them.

Then add the label `findings-recorded` and leave the bead OPEN: its findings become this slice's fix work, which the coordinator dispatches in clusters. If the slice needs nothing, record zero findings with the coverage list and close the bead with that as the reason.
notes:
== ROUTED FROM rf2-r5cc2.2 (core subs/views review, trunk 89f5bbc4de) — an item this slice owns

- fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/collector.cljs:162-171 (dispose-cell!) and :319 are the consumer side of rf2-r5cc2.2 finding 4 (a teardown callback added to a shared reaction per consumer and never removed). The leftover (fn [] (invalidate-cell! cell)) closure holds the dead cell; it needs the disarm that finding 4's fix adds (that fix is in flight on worker branch core-subs-fix — read its PR if open).

== SENIOR REVIEW FINDINGS (2026-10-29 14:11:13 AUSEST, trunk aacb6a14e0)

Slice: implementation/fresco/** (src, test_kit, spec, resources, scripts, testbed, test). Read against implementation/fresco/spec/ (authoring-contract, commit-law, invariants), Spec 006 (lifetime, on-dispose hooks) and Spec 002 (frames). Paths are repo-relative under implementation/fresco/ unless they say otherwise. The slice is byte-identical between dde786b07a, where the read began, and aacb6a14e0; only beads checkpoints landed in between.

Rulings respected, not re-proposed:
- A same-id frame recreated in a LATER task leaves a mounted boundary showing the predecessor until something re-renders. This is deliberate (rf2-3x7nj.7) and pinned by test/re_frame/fresco/reincarnation_readset_dom_cljs_test.cljs (rf2-3awu).
- A hot reload remounts every view it re-mints. That is the contract.
- The per-map-key merge rule for an author's own attribute map (authoring-contract, The controlled-input door).

ROUTED ITEMS FROM rf2-r5cc2.2 (both answered)
- The consumer side of finding 4 is still open here. It is finding 1 below.
- Finding 2 (the unmount sentinel appended as an extra child) does NOT apply to Fresco. Fresco installs no :wrap-view: collector.cljs publish-view-alias! (:1278-1319) writes registrar/register! directly, and views/view-head returns a :view slot it did not build exactly as stored. A grep for wrap-view under src/ finds only that docstring. The core fix also landed (PR #11727, the Fragment-sibling shape).

FINDINGS (most important first)

1. A disposed cell leaves its disposal callback armed on the shared reaction. That is one closure per cell lifetime, without bound.
   - Where: src/re_frame/fresco/impl/collector.cljs:171, `(rf.subs/unsubscribe-if-reaction (.-frameKw cell) (.-queryV cell) r))`, in dispose-cell!. The callback is minted at :319-321 in wire-cell!, `(rf.subs/acquire-watched-reaction! ... (fn [] (invalidate-cell! cell)))`, and no handle on it is kept.
   - Defect: core's seam now pairs acquire-watched-reaction! with release-watched-reaction!. That release (core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc:2647) calls remove-on-dispose! and then unsubscribe-if-reaction. The rf2-r5cc2.2 close reason says it was added "for the Fresco seam". Fresco still releases through the bare unsubscribe-if-reaction, so the closure stays in the reaction's removable set. Nothing in implementation/ outside core's own tests and spine.cljs:3402 calls remove-on-dispose! or release-watched-reaction!.
   - Cost: the closure outlives the cell whenever another holder keeps the reaction cached. That holder can be a layer-2 sub whose input it is, or a UIx or Reagent reader on the same frame. Each time the last Fresco reader of the key unmounts, after the one-macrotask grace, one more closure is added, and it retains the dead cell: its key vector, its reader array and its reaction. Virtualised rows, route churn and popovers all grow the set. It shrinks only when the reaction finally disposes, and then every stale closure runs, each as a no-op on a disposed cell. The residue census (test_kit/src/re_frame/fresco/test/runtime.cljs, residue) counts cells and memberships only, so the leak gate cannot see this.
   - Fix: keep the closure on the cell when it is wired (for example an "onDispose" slot set in wire-cell!). In dispose-cell!, release through `(rf.subs/release-watched-reaction! frame-kw query-v r (.-onDispose cell))`. Add a test row that:
     - holds the key through a layer-2 sub;
     - churns a Fresco reader of the input N times, past the grace;
     - asserts that the input reaction's `.-rfRemovableOnDispose` size returns to its baseline. The UIx suite reads the same field (adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_use_sub_dom_cljs_test.cljs:488).
   - Size S. Lens 1 (cleanup), with a lens-5 gap. Confidence: verified by reading. dispose-cell! is the only release path, and it never touches the removable set.

2. Across a same-id frame reincarnation, a read-free boundary keeps controls pinned to the dead incarnation, while the memo docstring says this cannot happen.
   - Where:
     - src/re_frame/fresco/impl/codec.cljs:500-502, in boundary-props=: "The frame is not compared and need not be: it arrives through React context, which React propagates ahead of the comparator and through a memo".
     - spec/authoring-contract.md:417: "The successor's next render mints operations that route to it".
   - Defect: the frame context's value is the frame KEYWORD (core/src/re_frame/adapter/context.cljs:77, `#js {:value frame-kw}`). The keyword is identical across a destroy plus make-frame under the same id, so React has nothing to propagate.
     - A boundary with reads is repaired by invalidate-cell!'s microtask, which rewires the cell and marks it dirty (collector.cljs:330-364).
     - A boundary that reads nothing has no cell to invalidate, and its props compare `=`. React.memo therefore bails out on every parent re-render, and the body never runs again.
     - Every intent that body lowered keeps the predecessor's frame-dispatch, and core's capture-frame fence refuses it with :rf.error/frame-destroyed.
     - Toolbars, nav and static buttons have exactly this shape. The suite calls this transition "the ordinary one a tenant or account switch performs" (the seat! docstring in reincarnation_readset_dom_cljs_test.cljs).
   - Cost: suppose an app switches accounts by calling destroy-frame! and then make-frame under a tree that stays mounted. The page looks right, but its static controls are dead, and the refusal goes to the error channel, not the screen. rf2-3x7nj.7 ruled this class deliberate for the later-task case ("until something re-renders"). So the ask is to state the behaviour, not to change the stance. Today both texts quoted above say the opposite.
   - Fix (S):
     - Correct the boundary-props= docstring: the context carries the frame's address, not its incarnation.
     - Add one point to the incarnation rule: a mounted boundary that nothing re-renders keeps its predecessor's operations, read-free views included.
     - State the remedy there: recreating a frame under a mounted tree means remounting that tree, either by keying the frame-root's parent with a session token or by h/unmount! followed by h/render!.
     - A runtime fix is possible: stamp the lowering frame's incarnation token into the boundary element and compare it in boundary-props=. That sits close to the frame-in-props machinery rf2-6c12m.16 cut, so it needs a ruling first.
   - Size S for the docs; M if the runtime route is ruled in. Lens 1/6. Confidence: probable. Each link is verified by reading: the keyword context, the `=` memo, and the absence of a cell for a read-free body. One browser test row would settle it at runtime: a read-free view with an intent, destroy plus make-frame in one task, a click, then an assertion that the successor's app-db moved.

3. The two governing texts disagree about which entry wins at an owned slot, and the package's own components that merge owned attributes follow the weaker rule.
   - Where:
     - spec/invariants.md, row I15: "a forwarded attribute cannot replace one".
     - spec/authoring-contract.md:237-240: "The rule is per map key, not per React prop: an :onInput beside an owned :on-input lands on the same React prop in map order".
     - The merges are in src/re_frame/fresco/forms.cljs:237-246 and src/re_frame/fresco/impl/overlay.cljs:517.
       - buffered-field merges with `(merge {:type "text"} (apply dissoc props module-props) {...owned...})`, and its docstring (:225-226) says "owned wins on collision".
       - element-attrs merges with `(merge (apply dissoc props own-keys) (dissoc extra :style))`.
   - Defect: both merge by KEY, but the codec emits by SLOT. convert-entry (codec.cljs:393-395) writes the same js-name twice, and the last write wins. A forwarded entry survives the merge beside the owned kebab key whenever its spelling differs: `:onBlur`, `:onInput` or `:onKeyDown` on buffered-field, or `:onKeyDown` or `:onCancel` on a modal. The map's iteration order then picks the winner. Up to 8 entries that is insertion order; past 8 it is hash order. A buffered-field with a few ordinary attributes already has more than 8.
   - Cost: one of two things happens silently, and a hash decides which. Either the field's commit protocol on blur and Enter, or the modal's Tab wrap, is replaced by a camelCase spelling that the contract itself accepts (intent.cljs re-event-prop takes both spellings), or the caller's own handler is dropped.
   - Fix: in both components, drop every forwarded entry whose canonical slot is claimed by an owned key before merging. collector.cljs:967-989 without-authored-slots already does exactly this for annotate-root, through codec/canonical-slot, so lift it into one shared helper. Then make I15 and the contract agree; the contract's per-key rule can stay for an author's own maps.
   - Size S. Lens 1/6. Confidence: verified by reading. The merge keeps both keys because they are not `=`, and convert-entry's last write wins. Which spelling wins for a given map depends on the hash, and that was not run.
