   - Where: src/re_frame/fresco/impl/mount.cljs:481-490 says "one `:require` of it from this namespace would put the whole spine into the bundle of every Fresco application". But :32 of the same file already requires re-frame.substrate.spine, which it uses at :362, and impl/frame_boundary.cljs requires it too. Every Fresco app loads both through re-frame.fresco.
   - Defect: the require already exists, so the cost the comment says it avoids is not avoided. What the reachability gate really guards is the substrate module's load-time make-react-spine call (scripts/check_optional_module_reachability.py, the substrate row), not a require. The comment is used to justify two copies:
     - the handle trio at :557-621 copies core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:1070 make-client-root-fns, a factory that exists "so the ratom family and the React-hook family cannot drift";
     - report-recoverable-default! (:308) copies spine.cljs:1166.
   - Cost: a reader who trusts the comment keeps a copy that can drift. The next change to the shared root semantics then has to be made twice, and only the tests will say so.
   - Fix: build the trio from `(rf.substrate.spine/make-client-root-fns mount-client-root!)`, keep Fresco's per-call require-root-options! as a thin wrapper around render!, and delete the paragraph. Sharing report-recoverable-default! as well would mean making spine's copy public; that is core's file and optional.
   - Size S. Lens 2/6. Confidence: verified by reading.

LOOKED AT AND SOUND
- Commit basis and fence: impl/generation.cljs, whose four terms are all monotone, including the retired-epoch term across a same-id reincarnation; collector render-body's fence and its max-fence-retries refusal.
- impl/frames.cljs: rows pinned to an incarnation; lazy replacement as the safety mechanism; the :post-dead drop, which is for retention only.
- Collector tables:
  - cell acquire and release are symmetric (make-subscribe and its unsubscribe);
  - the two reapers: one timer per horizon, reaping on clock skew, and reset-reapers!;
  - the entry cache: an order-sensitive bucket hash and a pairwise match;
  - make-snapshot's staged term, and retire-entries-naming!;

  - with-commit re-entrancy, flush!'s deferral while a body runs, and cold-read!'s per-run probe.
- The shell: two hooks only (shell-hook-ledger); resolve-frame!; mint-view! as a pure allocation; annotate-root's author-wins, held at the slot.
- impl/intent.cljs: the event-first argument law, the closed ::h/prevent grammar, the key-map composition gate and its arm order, and carriers selected by kind.
- impl/boundary.cljs: the roster, shape and frame refusals at render; reset-key adoption in componentDidUpdate; the frame read through contextType.
- impl/mount.cljs and impl/roots.cljs: lowering before createRoot, a per-root adoption window, hydration-reporter composition, and the active-roots drain. impl/frame_boundary.cljs: lowering in the ready pass, and the hydration refusal.
- server.cljs: a frame per request, a listener keyed per invocation, and the teardown order in finally.
- Read but not exercised: impl/controlled.cljs (converge, caret measured from the end, the composition shadow), impl/presence.cljs with presence_react.cljs, the anchor claim and release in impl/overlay.cljs, impl/portal.cljs, and native.cljc.
- The test kit:

title: senior review: template and testbed-support
description:
SENIOR-DEVELOPER REVIEW of one slice of the tree. Part of the review sweep rf2-r5cc2, which partitions implementation/, tools/, examples/ and skills/ into slices; this bead owns exactly the slice below, and its siblings own the rest.

SLICE:
- tools/template/**
- tools/testbed-support/**
- top-level files under tools/

FOCUS: The project template a new user starts from (its substrate variants and registry) and the shared testbed support.

PERSONA. A senior Clojure/ClojureScript developer who did not write this code, reading it as its next maintainer and as a programmer who has to use it. Judge it against the project stance (CLAUDE.md), quoted verbatim:

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every
> last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.

So record material, actionable insights only: a defect, a simplification that removes real weight, an ergonomic sharp edge a programmer (or the AI they use) will hit, a test that cannot go red, a doc or docstring that misleads. Not style preferences, not nagging diagnostics, not defensive belt-and-braces, not renames for taste.

LENSES, in priority order:
1. Correctness — error paths, concurrency, cleanup, and fail-closed behaviour on any security or privacy boundary.
2. Simplicity and clarity — dead code, duplication (within the slice or with another slice), accidental complexity, an abstraction that earns nothing.
3. Ergonomics — the API or tool as a programmer, or the AI they use, actually meets it.
4. Performance — hot spots on real paths, never at the expense of clarity.
5. Test rigour — a test that cannot fail, a gap on a branch that matters.
6. Comments and docstrings — per CLAUDE.md § Conventions & Patterns: present tense, the reason plus a spec pointer, no provenance, no restated spec.

METHOD. Read the slice's source first, then its tests, against the owning spec sections (spec/Ownership.md maps each surface to its spec). A finding is a CLAIM until checked: confirm each one at source, and confirm a behaviour claim with a quick REPL or test run where that is cheap. This is a read-only review: edit no file, and run only read-only commands and the slice's existing test lanes.

OUTPUT, recorded on THIS bead and never in a separate file: write the section to a file and append it with `bd update <this bead> --append-notes "$(cat <file>)"` (never `--notes`, which replaces). Head it `== SENIOR REVIEW FINDINGS (<datetime with zone>, trunk <short sha>)` and include:
- 0 to 15 numbered findings, most important first. Each gives: `path:line` (plus a short quote so it can be re-found by text), what is wrong, why it matters (the concrete failure or cost), the fix (a sketch is fine), size (S/M/L), confidence (verified / probable), and its lens.
- A short "looked at and sound" list, so the review's coverage is visible.
- Cross-slice findings, whose defect lives in another slice's files, in a separate list naming the owning slice. Do not act on them.

Then add the label `findings-recorded` and leave the bead OPEN: its findings become this slice's fix work, which the coordinator dispatches in clusters. If the slice needs nothing, record zero findings with the coverage list and close the bead with that as the reason.

title: machines: should a machine's event :schema see framework-reserved :rf.machine/* lifecycle markers?
description:
From the correctness review of examples-core (rf2-lgzco.40). The login example's machine event `:schema` refuses the reserved `[:rf.machine/start]` kick. Three Story variants then fail validation and the machine never starts. rf2-k1jbu introduced the schema. The example gets a one-line fix that admits the kick. The general question stays open: should a machine's event `:schema` see framework-reserved `:rf.machine/*` lifecycle markers at all?

Coordinator's lean, under the stance (trust the programmer, low friction): the framework owns `:rf.machine/*`. The author's event schema describes the author's events, so the runtime should not validate reserved markers against it, and no author should have to whitelist them.

Check Spec 005 first, including its machine event-schema section and the reserved-event rows. If Spec 005 already says the author's schema sees reserved markers, decide whether that clause is deliberate. If it is, close this bead citing it.

Surface: `implementation/machines/**`, plus the Spec 005 sentence (a HOT ZONE). Wait until the live machines-lifecycle-fix worker's PR has merged. Gates: `clojure -M:test` in implementation/machines and `npm run test:cljs`.

== FINDING (worker machines-join-schema, 2026-10-30 03:04:15 AUSEST). The lean holds; implementing it needs a change to implementation/core, which this dispatch fenced, so it STOPPED here and the bead stays open.

SPEC 005 CHECK. No clause deliberately puts the reserved :rf.machine/* events under the author's event :schema. §reg-machine (the event-:schema arity) and §What validates machine events today say the opts :schema validates "the whole dispatched outer vector [:machine-id [:inner-event <payload>]]" at the :where :event boundary, and §Reserved synthetic events says the runtime threads its vectors "through the standard dispatch pipeline". Neither carves the reserved events in or out, so the clause is not a deliberate ruling and the coordinator's lean stands.

REACH IS WIDER THAN THE KICK. Measured on the JVM plain-atom adapter at f12e430b42, schemas artefact and Malli adapter loaded: a singleton :p registered with {:schema [:tuple [:= :p] [:tuple [:enum :go]]]}, whose :waiting state declares a :spawn with :on-done {:target :finished}. After [:p [:go]] and the child reaching its :final? state, the runtime-minted carrier [:p [:rf.machine.spawn/done [:waiting] {...} 1]] is refused at :where :event, so :on-done never runs and :p stays in :waiting for good; [:p [:rf.machine/start]] is refused as well (2 :where :event refusals in all). [:rf.machine.timer/after-elapsed ...] reaches the machine id by the same route (Spec 005 §Reserved synthetic events); that one was not measured. No author can sensibly whitelist the carrier wire shapes, so today a singleton machine with an event :schema and a :spawn (or, by the same route, an :after) hangs silently unless the schema admits any inner vector.

WHY IT IS NOT IMPLEMENTED HERE. The :where :event check is router.cljc validate-event! in implementation/core: it runs BEFORE the machine handler, against the registrar meta's :schema, and both arms pass through it (dev: the schemas artefact's :schemas/validate-event!; production: rf.spec/validate-at-boundary! for :boundary? true). The schema value is opaque to the machines artefact, so machines cannot narrow it, and moving the check into the machine handler would change the boundary's contract (a refusal before cofx delivery, :boundary? true, the meta :schema tools read). The smallest shape is one guard at the top of that router fn: skip the event-schema check when the handler meta carries :rf/machine? true and the inner event's id is in a reserved :rf.machine namespace (:rf.machine, :rf.machine.spawn, :rf.machine.timer). That is a core change, which the dispatch's fence forbade ("if one is needed, stop and report").

WHAT A DISPATCH HOLDING implementation/core DOES. The router guard plus a pin test (a singleton with a narrow event :schema starts on the kick and takes a :spawn child's :on-done); one sentence in Spec 005 §reg-machine and §What validates machine events today saying the opts :schema sees only the author's events; and examples/core/login/model.cljc drops :rf.machine/start from its sub-event enum and the comment explaining it (PR #11792 added both), so the example teaches the low-friction form. The login example is left as #11792 made it, because its whitelist is still needed until the guard lands.

- A re-registration that closes a cycle or an overlap reports :rf.error/flow-eval-exception, carrying cause :rf.error/flow-cycle and no :flow-id, where Spec 013 §Re-registration says "raising :rf.error/flow-cycle". The thrown error is that id, wrapped by the router, and flows_trace_test.clj:137-153 pins it. Wording.
- reassert-output's :output-write message says the ":derive fn RETURNED normally" (flows.cljc:128-139, reached via :166), but on a reassert :derive did not run. Message text only; the phase is right.
- A clear-flow or path-moving reg-flow from inside an fx leaves the output until the next event (the frame state is unchanged, so there is no settle). This matches Spec 013 §Re-registration "next event", and the September .18.3 contract went with the lifecycle settle.
- Flows run during a refused event's unwind and can report ahead of :rejected. This is deliberate (router.cljc:932-938).
- An unknown or typo'd metadata key (e.g. :sensitve) is accepted silently, and fn? refuses a var as :derive. Programmer misuse / ergonomics; trust the programmer.
- A departure vacates a value a handler wrote at that path in the same event. Spec-sanctioned (the next pass vacates the path); September item 12 rejected the sibling case.
- The dirty check relies on identical? over the resolved definition. It is stable across events on a live frame: flows_output_reassert_cljs_test.cljc:34-45 pins a single :derive call across equal-input events.
- Prose drift, no behaviour: flows_rollback_dirty_check_test.clj:10-12 and Spec 013 §Failure semantics rule 2 still speak of claims "added to the live elision registry" (claims now derive from named definitions plus memo rows, and the asserted outcomes hold). Spec 013 §Conformance coverage points the activation-cycle row at flows_test.clj, which holds no cycle test (flows_activation_test.clj:76-94 does). Core epoch/tool_pair.cljc:1071 (rf2-lgzco.5) still lists a "flows memo reset" in the post-write tail, and none exists.
- Re-read and sound: Kahn with the retained self-edge and closing-repeat extraction; overlap detection; vector-index vacation; publish-on-install memo; destroy teardown, including an in-drain destroy deferred to the event boundary (frame.cljc:4288-4295); settle-after-walk; the path interceptor's coeffect unwind; ambiguity totality (r5cc2.13 #1); the :images resolution binding, which covers the settle too (router.cljc:1196-1201).

NOT VERIFIED
- CLJS host: not built (no shadow-cljs, per the protocol). The implicated sites are shared .cljc with no reader conditional, so the JVM probe ran the same code; the CLJS arm is inferred.
- Finding 1 was measured for routing only. Resource and mutation roots, whose instances could first appear in a pending runtime-db, were not probed, and nor were other subsystems' mid-event traces over the pending runtime-db (out of slice).
- Finding 2 was measured with restore-epoch! only. replace-frame-state! follows the same install and is inferred. The off-box surfaces (Pair MCP) were not driven end to end; the leak shown is elide-wire-value over the live app-db, which those surfaces call.

DE-DUPLICATION
One export (`bd list --all --limit 0 --json`, 4666 records, exit 0), searched with Python regex over title, description, notes and close reason. Controls hit: "departing flow output" found 3 (rf2-3zqly among them), and "reassert-output" found 3 (rf2-r5cc2.13 among them).
- Finding 1: "pending runtime-db" near classif/redact/elid found 0; container/committed near runtime claims found 0; "elide-inputs" found 2, both closed and unrelated (rf2-kuky.5, rf2-3x7nj.18); route/flow/input proximity found 16, all read, none on this defect.
- Finding 2: restore near flow near vacate found 9, all read; the nearest is rf2-i4j03 (the opposite order, fixed). Time-travel near a cleared flow found 0.
- Finding 3: db-nil-coerced near flow found 1 (rf2-1jky4, a skill review listing the warning), not this defect.
== RULING (coordinator, 2026-10-30 04:27:58 AUSEST). Mike may override.

Finding 2: take (A), the reviewer's recommendation, in its smallest shape. A restore is a framework act, and Spec 013 already promises that "a flow leaving a frame vacates its output path", so the promise has to survive time travel.
- The epoch record carries the frame's memo DEFINITIONS (`{flow-id definition}`, no values).
- Restore and replace re-seed them as rows that force a recompute, so the next pass reconciles departures through the existing `reconcile-departures` (vacate, plus `:rf.warning/unregistered-flow`).
- `output-classification` keeps the restored output classified until that pass.
- No per-frame dead-claim set (B), and no out-of-contract carve-out (C).

Finding 1 needs no decision: elide a flow's runtime-db inputs against the PENDING runtime-db the pass read, not the committed one.

Finding 3 is in core `router.cljc`, which another worker holds this round. It moves to its own bead, filed with this ruling, so this bead can close on findings 1 and 2.

title: Mutations: a path-declared continuation reply is redacted at source, so the app's own :reply-to handler gets :rf/redacted
description:
Found while fixing rf2-acqqo (PR #11802, merged). A mutation's continuation reply with PATH declarations (`:sensitive [[...]]` on `reg-mutation`) is redacted at SOURCE, by `redact-continuation-reply`. So the app's own `:reply-to` handler receives those paths already `:rf/redacted`.

That contradicts Spec 015's model: real values flow through the application unchanged, and classification redacts only at framework-mediated observation boundaries. It is also inconsistent within the same feature:
- since #11802, a mutation's COARSE claim redacts its reply off-box only;
- a resource reply is redacted off-box only (`row-owner-redacts?` in `trace_egress`).

The existing test `execute-classifies-the-instance-and-redacts-egress-and-continuation` pins the source behaviour.

== RULING (coordinator, 2026-10-30). Mike may override. Make it consistent. A path-declared mutation reply is redacted off-box only, like the coarse claim and like a resource reply, and the app's `:reply-to` handler receives the real value. A login mutation then hands its token to its workflow whichever way the author declared it.

FIX: move the path-declaration arm of the continuation-reply redaction from source to the egress projection, reusing the coarse arm #11802 added. Update the pinning test so the app's handler sees raw and egress sees `:rf/redacted`. Amend the Spec 015 / Spec 016 mutation-carrier sentence, which #11802 wrote to say the coarse claim is off-box, so that it covers path declarations too.

Surface: `implementation/resources/**`, plus the Spec 015 / 016 mutation-carrier sentences. Gates: resources `clojure -M:test`, `npm run test:cljs`, `mkdocs build --strict`, `check_doc_slugs.py`.
